Masaai: Ore peyie eidip intamesin aatookisho, eitayio oltung'ani olgisoi le sahabu laa eoroti nabo e shekel enkiroishi, o lkataarri aare loo nkaik enyena oimu enkiroishi enye shekeli tomon e sahabu.

English: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy father's house for us to lodge in?
Masaai: Nejo, “Aatasayia tolikioki ajo ira entito e ng'ae? Ketii olgilata likirrag enkaji e papaai lino?”

English: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninye, “Ara entito e Betuel olayioni le Milka otoikio Nahor.”

English: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
Masaai: Neitoki ajoki, “Kiata sii pokira olkujita o lgilat ooirragi.”

English: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.
Masaai: Neirrug oltung'ani elukunya aserem Olaitoriani.

English: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren.
Masaai: Nejo: “Meisisi Olaitoriani Enkai olkitok lai Abraham, leitu eing'uaa enyorrata enye nauno o enchunet enye to Laitoriani lai. Ore nanu, aatorikuo Olaitoriani te nkoitoi arikoki enkaji oo lalashera lo lkitok lai.”

English: And the damsel ran, and told them of her mother's house these things.
Masaai: Neipirri ina tito aliki enkaji e ng'otonye kuna baa.

English: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the well.
Masaai: Eeta apa Rebeka olalashe oji enkarna enye Laban. Nepuku Laban akuet alo enetii ilo tung'ani te nchorro.

English: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol olgisoi o lkataarri otii inkaik e nkanashe, nening'u sii irorei le Rebeka enkanashe enye oojo, “Neija aatiaaka oltung'ani,” eshomo enetii oltung'ani; nenyorriki eitashe tembata oo ntamesin te nchorro.

English: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Tijing'u, olomayiana lo Laitoriani, ainyoo peyie intashe tiauluo: naidipa aitobira enkaji o ewueji oo ntamesin.”

English: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men's feet that were with him.
Masaai: Metaa etijing'ua ilo tung'ani atua aji, nelaku Laban ilolan too ntamesin, neisho ninye ninche endaa oo ntamesin. Neisho sii ninye enkare naisujie inkejek enyena o tenebo lelo oiriamunore.

English: And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
Masaai: Neirragakinyeki ninye endaa meinosa, kake etejo ninye; “Manya endaa o metaba anaa nairo ororei laayawua.” Nejoki Laban ninye, “Iroro.”

English: And he said, I am Abraham's servant.
Masaai: Metaa etejo ninye, “Ara nanu osinka le Abraham! Netamayiana Olaitoriani olkitok lai oleng, neitaa ninye karsis:

English: And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.
Masaai: eishoo ninye inkishu, o ntare, inkoshola o sahabu, o sinkan, o nkaisiaayiak, o ntamesin o sirkon.

English: And Sarah my master's wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
Masaai: Ore Sara, enkitok olkitok lai etoikio ninye enkayioni etaa moruo. Ore nena masaa pooki neishoo olayioni lenye.

English: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife to my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
Masaai: Aainosie olkitok lai olmumai ajoki, ‘Milo iyie ayamaki olayioni lai enkitok too ntoyie oo Lkanaan lena kop naamanya.

English: But thou shalt go unto my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.
Masaai: Kake shomo enkaji e papa lai, o ltung'ana lang torikoki olayioni lai enkitok.’

English: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.
Masaai: Najoki nanu olkitok lai, ‘Eidimayu metanya enkitok aasuju nanu.’

English: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house:
Masaai: Kake aatiaaka ninye nanu, ‘Ore Olaitoriani lalo te dukuya ninye naa keirriu olmalaika lenye tenebo iyie neitumunyan enkoitoi ino, nirikoki enkitok olayioni lai too ltung'ana lang le nkaji e papa.

English: Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee one, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
Masaai: Niking'uaa ina kata olmumai tinilo enetii iltung'ana laainei. Naa tinikimitiki ninche ninye, nimikintoki aibung iyie olmumai lai.’

English: And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:
Masaai: “Nalotu duoo nanu e nchorro najo, ‘Oi Olaitoriani Enkai olkitok lai Abraham, tenaa aitumunyana tena kata enkoitoi naim aitorioo,

English: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw water, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;
Masaai: ing'ura aitashe nanu te mbata enchorro e nkare, inchoo entito nalotu aoku enkare naa tenajoki, “Aatoomono inchooki te moti ino; enkiti are naok.”

English: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom the LORD hath appointed out for my master's son.
Masaai: Naajoki nanu, “Tooko naa kaokoki sii intamesin inono,” inchoo metaa ninye enkitok nategeleka Olaitoriani olayioni lo olkitok lai.’

English: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the well, and drew water: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
Masaai: “Ore sii ake eitu aishu enkiroroto oltau lai, ng'ura, nelotu Rebeka enapita emoti e nkare to loililai, nedoiki enchorro aoku enkare. Najoki ninye, ‘Aatoomono inchooki matooko.’

English: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
Masaai: Nesioki aitadou emoti enye to loililai lenye nejo; ‘Tooko, naa kaisho sii ninche ntamesin inono.’ Neaku atooko nanu neisho sii nena tamesin enkare.

English: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
Masaai: Naitoki aikilikuan ninye ajoki: ‘Ira entito e ng'ae?’ nejo, ‘Entito e Betuel olayioni le Nahor otoikio ninye Milka.’ Napik olgisoi enkume enye olkataarri inkaik enyena.

English: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter unto his son.
Masaai: Nairrug elukunya aserem Olaitoriani, naisis Olaitoriani Enkai o lkitok lai Abraham, ilo laatorikoyie te nkoitoi nasipa matoriko entito o lalashe lo lkitok lai arikoki olayioni lenye.

English: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, tenaa aiyasiasa esupatisho o esipata to lkitok lai entolikioki nanu, naa tinimiasiasa entolikioki nanu peyie atum aibelekenyakinoyu enkaina e tatene arashu kedienye.”

English: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD: we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.
Masaai: Newal Laban o Betuel aajo, “Ore ena bae naa Olaitoriani eing'uaa. Mikindiim aatiaaki iyie entorrono anaa esidai.

English: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master's son's wife, as the LORD hath spoken.
Masaai: Ing'ura neina Rebeka natii dukuya iyie, toriko ninye shomo metaa ninye enkitok olayioni lo lkitok lino anaa enairoro Olaitoriani.”

English: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
Masaai: Ore peyie ening olaisiaayiani le Abraham irorei lenye neirrugo abaiki enkop te dukuya Olaitoriani.

English: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
Masaai: Neyau ilo aisiaayiani intokitin naagol enkinyiang'a o enkosholai o sahabu o nkilani neisho ninche Rebeka. Eishoo sii ninye olalashe lenye tenebo ng'otonye intokitin naagol enkinyang'a.

English: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.
Masaai: Ore ninye o lelo tung'ana apa ootii tenebo ninye, nedaa neokisho, neirrag ine. Ore pee einyototo ninche tadekenya, nejo ninye, “Entushukoki enetii olkitok lai.”

English: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
Masaai: Nejo olalashe tenebo ng'otonye, “Enchoo entito eng'as aton tenebo iyiook inkuti olong'i, anaa napaji inkolong'i tomon, ore peyie eishunye neidim ashomo.”

English: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.
Masaai: Kake etiaka ninye ninche, “Mikintokiki ailitilit, anaa enaidipa Olaitoriani aitumunyana enkoitoi ai, enchooki mashomo enetii olkitok lai.”

English: And they said, We will call the damsel, and enquire at her mouth.
Masaai: Nejo ninche; “Aikimpot entito aaikilikuan enajo.

English: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
Masaai: Neipot ninche Rebeka, nejoki ninye, “Amaa airiamariyie ele tung'ani?” Newal ajo, “Ekalo.”

English: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
Masaai: Neaku eishoo ninche Rebeka enkanashe enye meshomo tenebo enkaisiaayiani enye, o sinka le Abraham tenebo iltung'ana lenyena.

English: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.
Masaai: Nemayian ninche Rebeka ejoki: “Enkanashe ang taa iyie ng'otonye oo nkalifuni, oo nkalifuni tomon, naa inchoo metujung'o eishoi ino kishomi elelo ooiba ninche.”

English: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
Masaai: Nedumunye Rebeka tenebo inkaisiaayiak enyena, neked ntamesin neirukurukore ilo tung'ani, neaku etoriko ilo aisiayani Rabeka, nelo enkop enye.

English: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi; for he dwelt in the south country.
Masaai: Eewuo apa Isaak ina kata eing'uaa Beer-lahai-roi nelotu abik te Negeb.

English: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
Masaai: Nepuku Isaak alo ong'ata adamisho teipa, neraposhu inkonyek enyena, ngura nedol intamesin naapuonu.

English: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel.
Masaai: Neraposhu Rebeka inkonyek enyena nedol Isaak, ore peyie edol ninye nedou te ntames,

English: For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.
Masaai: nejoki ilo aisiaayiani, “Kalo tung'ani lido olotu ti ong'ota anang'are iyiook?” Nejoki ilo aisiaayiani, “Olkitok lai.” Neitayu enkarasha aitoip kewan.

English: And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
Masaai: Neinosaki ilo aisiaayiani Isaak imbaa pooki naataasate.

English: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
Masaai: Nerik Isaak ninye atua olng'obor. Neya Rebeka neaku ninye enkitok enye, nenyorru ninye. Neaku eitagoloki apa Isaak te nkeeya e ng'otonye.

English: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
Masaai: Neyam Abraham ae kitok naji enkarna enye Ketura.

English: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
Masaai: Neiki ninye Simran, o Yokshan, o Medan, o Midian, o Ishbak, o Shua,

English: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
Masaai: ore apa Tokshan naa ninye menye le Sheba, o Dedon. Ore ilayiok le Dedan, naa Asshurim, o Letushim, o Leumim.

English: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Midian naa Epa, o Eper, o Hanok o Abida, o Eldaa. Ore apa kulo naa nkera e ketura.

English: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.
Masaai: Neisho Abraham pooki toki naata Isaak.

English: But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.
Masaai: Kake eishoo Abraham ilayiok loo nkapiak enyena inkishorot, ore eton eishu, neidurrie ninche aitung'uaa olayioni lenye Isaak meshomo enkop oloosaen.

English: And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.
Masaai: Kuna inkolong'i oo larin le nkishui e Abraham, ilarin iip o ntomoni naapishana o imiet,

English: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.
Masaai: neye Abraham etaa olpayian kitok etamorua amitunye, nepiki ninye eneiturrurrorre olorere lenye.

English: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;
Masaai: nenukaa ninye ilayiok lenyena Isaak o Ishmael te nkapune e Makpela te nkurma e Efron olayioni le Soha loo Lhiti.

English: The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.
Masaai: To loo saen le Mamre, te nkurma nainyiang'ua apa Abraham too Lhiti. Metaa te ine apa etunukayioki Abraham tenebo enkitok enye Sara.

English: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahairoi.
Masaai: Ore peyie eidip Abraham atua, etamayiana Enkai Isaak olayioni lenye. Nebik Isaak te Beelarahoi.

English: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
Masaai: Kulo ninche ile ishoi e Ishmael olayioni le Abraham otoikio ninye Hagar e Misiri naa enkaisiaayiani apa e Sara.

English: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
Masaai: Kuna ninche nkarn oo layiok le Ishmael anaa enaikunakino te inoto enye: Nebaiot aa ninye olkikau le Ishmael o Kedar, o Adbeel, o Mibsam,

English: And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Masaai: Mishma, o Duma, o Masa,

English: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
Masaai: o Hadad, o Tema, o Yetur, o Napish, o Kedema.

English: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Ishmael naa kuna inkarn enye, too nkangitie enye o too lngoborri lenye. Ilkituaak tomon o are anaa iloshon lenye.

English: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.
Masaai: (Kulo ninche ilarin le nkishui e Ishmael ilarin iip o tomoni uni o naapishana, neitianya aye, neiturrurrokino ninye olorere lenye.)

English: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: and he died in the presence of all his brethren.
Masaai: Nemany ebaiki Hafila o meshomo Shur, natii enkalo o loosaen le Misiri te nkalo e Asiria. Etamanya apa ninye enetalakinore olikae orere pooki lenye.

English: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac:
Masaai: Kulo ninche ile ishoi e Isaak olayioni le Abraham: ore apa Abraham naa ninye menye le Isaak.

English: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
Masaai: Ore apa Isaak naa oloo larin artam peyie eyam enkitok enye Rebeka, ina tito e Betuel le Aramean te Padan-aram, ina anashe e Laban le Aramean.

English: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
Masaai: Neomon Isaak Olaitoriani tenkaraki enkitok enye, amu koolupi apa ninye, newal Enkai enkomono enye, neiroshiu Rebeka enkitok enye.

English: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD.
Masaai: Nepupung'a nkera tiatua enkoshoke enye, nejo ninye, “Amaa tenaa inji etiu, ainyoo doi peyie aishu? Nelo ninye aikilikuan Olaitoriani ina bae.”

English: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani ninye, “Etii iloshon aare atua enkoshoke ino, naa ore lelo tung'ana pookira liiu, naa ekeori; ekegolu obo aalang olikae, ore olbotor naa keisiaai oloti.”

English: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
Masaai: Ore peyie ebau inkolong'i enyena peyie ejing aji, ng'ura! eeta ilmao te nkoshoke enye.

English: And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
Masaai: Ore olotang'asunye naa kenyokie, naa keju osesen lenye pooki anaa ilpapit le nkila, neipot ninye aajo enkarna Esau.

English: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.
Masaai: Neitoki olalashe lenye asuju, ore enkaina enye eibung'ita entutunyo e Esau, neipot ninye aajo Yakobo ore apa Isaak naa oloo larin ntomoni ile peyie eiki Rebeka ninye lelo mao.

English: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
Masaai: Ore peyie ebulu lelo ayiok, neaku Esau olang'oroni padan naa oltung'ani sii liong'ota. Ore Yakobo, naa oltung'ani obor ogira aton too lng'oborri.

English: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
Masaai: Kenyor apa Isaak Esau tenkaraki nkiri oo ng'uesi naayaki ninye. Ore Rebeka nenyor Yakobo.

English: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
Masaai: Ore nabo olong egira Yakobo ayier imotori oo nkaitubulu enkurma enye, nebau Esau eing'uaa ong'ota neeta esumash oleng.

English: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
Masaai: Nejoki Esau Yakobo; “Etaa kaye te sumash, inchooki mainosa ina toki nayiera natii emoti. Ore enkaraki ina, neji enkarna enye Edom.”

English: And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
Masaai: Newaliki Yakobo ninye ajoki “Tang'asa timirakaki esipata e kikauisho ino.”

English: And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
Masaai: Nejo Esau, “Etaa kaye, kenenyoo tipat naata esipata e kikausho te nanu?”

English: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo, “Tang'asa inosakaki olmumai.” Neinos ninye olmumai, nemiraki ninye Yakobo esipata enye e kikausho.

English: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
Masaai: Neaku neisho Yakobo Esau emukate tenebo nena motori, nenya neok sii, neinyototo alo. Neaku etemenayie Esau esipata enye e kikausho.

English: And there was a famine in the land, beside the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went unto Abimelech king of the Philistines unto Gerar.
Masaai: Enyaaka olameyu ajing enkop leme olapa ameyu le nkata e Abraham. Nelo Isaak Gera enetii Abimelek olaiguanani loo Lfilisti.

English: And the LORD appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of:
Masaai: Neipang'aki Olaitoriani ninye ejoki, “Midoyio alo Misiri, totona tamanya enkop naaliki.

English: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;
Masaai: Indurrudurra tena kop, naa kaaku nanu tenebo iyie, naa kaamayian, amu iyie tenebo iishoritin inono aisho kuna kuapi pooki, naitabaya olmumai lainosie papaai lino Abraham.

English: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
Masaai: Kaponaa eishoi ino metotiwuo anaa ilakir le nkeper, naisho eishoi ino ena kop pooki naa te ishoi ino emayian iloshon le nkop pooki ate.

English: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
Masaai: Ore amu etoning'o Abraham oltoilo lai, neibung enkikoo ai, o nkitanapat aainei pooki.”

English: And Isaac dwelt in Gerar:
Masaai: Neaku etamanya apa Isaak Gera.

English: And the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, She is my wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she was fair to look upon.
Masaai: Ore peyie eikilikuan ilewa leine imbaa naipirta enkitok enye, etejo ninye “Enkanashe ai ninye.” Amu eturia ninye ejo, “Enkitok ai” edamu ajo, “keidim ilewa leine ataar ninye metua tenkaraki Rebeka,” amu aisidai ninye oleng te nidol.

English: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
Masaai: Ore peyie ebik ninye teine enkata naado eturumishe te lusie Abimelek olaiguanani loo Lfilisti, nedol Isaak eirrapirap Rebeka enkitok enye.

English: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy wife: and how saidst thou, She is my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die for her.
Masaai: Metaa eipoto Abimelek Isaak nejoki, “Nyorriki ime enkitok ino, kaji inkuna peyie itejo ‘Enkanashe ai ninye’?” Nejoki Isaak ninye, “Amu atadamua ajo, ‘peyie maye tenkaraki ninye,’ ”

English: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
Masaai: Nejo Abimelek, “Ainyoo ena nintaasa iyiook? Eidim obo loo ltung'ana ashomo enetii enkitok ino, nipik iyiook entaboi te sunkureisho.”

English: And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
Masaai: Metaa eikoo Abimelek iltung'ana pooki ejoki, “Ore pooki ng'ae oiseyie ele tung'ani anaa enkitok enye naa keari metua.”

English: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him.
Masaai: Neunisho Isaak teina kop ilo ari, netum enkisampuare iip nabore. Nemayian Olaitoriani ninye.

English: And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great:
Masaai: Neaku apa ilo tung'ani karsis neponari imasaa oleng oleng, ometaa tetia.

English: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store of servants: and the Philistines envied him.
Masaai: Eeta apa ntare kumok o luaat oo nkishu, olmarei sapuk ometaa etoduakita Ilfilisti olom.

English: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
Masaai: Nenuk Ilfilisti nchorroi pooki te nterit apa naatuturo ilaisiaayiak le menye aa Abraham.

English: And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than we.
Masaai: Nejoki Abimelek Isaak, “Shomo tung'uai iyiook, amu ira magilani aleng iyiook.”

English: And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
Masaai: Neaku eidurra apa Isaak teine, nelo apik olng'obor lenye o erata le Gera nebik teine.

English: And Isaac digged again the wells of water, which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
Masaai: Neitoki Isaak atur nena shorroi oonkariak naatuturoki apa too nkolong'i e Papaai lenye, Abraham, amu etapalaitie Ilfilisti ninche peyie eye Abraham. Neisho sii inkarn apa naishoo menye.

English: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
Masaai: Kake ore peyie eidip ilaisiaayiak le Isaak aatuturisho te yarrata netum teine enchorro e nkare naijirrijirru,

English: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying, The water is ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him.
Masaai: neishankarrarre ilchekuti le Gera ilchekuti le Isaak ejoki, “Enaang ena are.” Neaku eipoto ina shorro enkare ajo Esek, amu eishankarrarre ninche ninye.

English: And they digged another well, and strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.
Masaai: Neitoki ninche aatur ae shorro, neitoki ake aishankarrarre ninye teina aaigil neaku eipoto enkarna enye ajo Sitina.

English: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
Masaai: Neidur teine atur ae shorro, neitu ejing enchankar ina, neaku eipoto enkarna eina Rehobot ejo, “Ore tena kata eitaikia iyiook Olaitoriani ewueji nelala, naa aikibul te nkop.”

English: And he went up from thence to Beersheba.
Masaai: Nepuku teine ailep alo Beer-sheba.

English: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.
Masaai: Neipang'aki Olaitoriani ninye ina kewarie nejoki, “Ara nanu Enkai e Abraham papaai lino, miureishoyu amu atii tenebo iyie, naa kaamayian iyie naitubul eishoi ino tenkaraki osinka lai Abraham.”

English: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the Lord, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac's servants digged a well.
Masaai: Neaku etesheta olperere lo lasar teine neipot enkarna Olaitoriani, neun olng'obor lenye teine, Netur ilaisiaayiak le Isaak enchorro enkare teine.

English: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
Masaai: Neitoki adumunye Abimelek alo enetii ninye eing'uaa Gera tenebo Ahusa olautaroni lenye tenebo Fikol olkitok lenye le njore,

English: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?
Masaai: nejoki Isaak ninche, “Ainyoo peyie ietuo enatii nadolita ajo aikimbaba intae nanu, nikitaaraitie aitung'uaa ate?”

English: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Kidolita metii olng'ash aajo etii Olaitoriani tenebo iyie metaa kitejo, inchoo maitayu olmumai terishata ino o iyiook naa maitayu sii olning'o o iyie,

English: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of the LORD.
Masaai: inchere mintaas iyiook intorrok anaa eneitu kiseyie iyie neitu kintaas iyie entorroni meteleku eseriani ake nikincho iyie shomo te seriani. Ira taata iyie olomayiana lo Laitoriani.”

English: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.
Masaai: Metaa eitobiraka ninye ninche osirua, nedaa neokisho.

English: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
Masaai: Ore peyie ekenyu, enyeito ninche enasirie aainos pooki olmumai, neisho Isaak ninche meshomo, nepuo aaing'uaa ninye to sotua.

English: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.
Masaai: Ore ake teina olong eetuo ilaisiaayiak le Isaak aaliki ninye enchorro e nkare natuturo ejoki ninye,

English: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city is Beersheba unto this day.
Masaai: “Kinotito enkare.” Neisho enkarna ine aajo shiba, metaa ore enkarna eina anasa naa keji Beer-sheba o metabaiki ena olong.

English: And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
Masaai: Ore peyie eaku Esau oloo larin artam, eyama Yudit entito e Beeri loo Lhiti tenebo Basemat entito e Elon oo Lhiti.

English: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.
Masaai: Nepik emion enkishui e Isaak o Rebeka.

English: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, here am I.
Masaai: Ore apa peyie eaku Isaak moruo oleng metaa eiliilaitie inkonyek metaa meekure edolisho neipotu Esau olkikau lenye, nejoki ninye, “Enkerai ai” neng'amaa menye ajoki, “Nele nanu.”

English: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ing'ura, atamorua nemayiolo enkolong naye.

English: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison;
Masaai: Tudumu imasaa inono, emootian ino tenebo enkawuo ino, nilo ong'ota pee kilo ang'oroki eng'ues.

English: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
Masaai: Nikintobiraki endaa namelok, anaa enoshi nanyor, nikiyaki mainosa peyie aatum atamayiana eton eitu aye.

English: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
Masaai: Ore apa Rebeka, einining'ito Isaak olayioni lenye Esau. Metaa ore peyie edumunye Esau alo ong'ata ang'or eng'ues, nayau

English: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,
Masaai: nejoki Rebeka olayioni lenye Yakobo “Atoning'o papaai lino eirorie olalashe lino Esau ejoki,

English: Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death.
Masaai: ‘Iyakaki eng'ues nikilotu aitobiraki endaa sidai. Natum ainosa naamayian iyie te dukuya Olaitoriani eton eitu aye.’

English: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee.
Masaai: Ore naa tena kata olayioni lai, toning'o ororei lai anaa enaaitanap ajoki.

English: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth:
Masaai: Shomo intare, niking'uraki ilbalelon aare sidain, peyie aitobirie endaa namelok sidai naaijo enoshi nanyor papaai lino.

English: And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
Masaai: Niyaki ninye papaai lino meinosa peyie kitum atamayiana eton eitu eye.”

English: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yakobo Rebeka ng'otonye, “Ng'ura ajo ore Esau olalashe lai naa oltung'ani oju, nara nanu oltung'ani osipa.

English: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
Masaai: Eidimayu naairrapirrap papa nanu, natiu nanu anaa oltung'ani olej ninye, nayaki kewan oldeket ajo emayianata aing'oru.”

English: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.
Masaai: Nejoki ng'otonye ninye, “Inchoo oldeket lino elotu shumata nanu enkerai ai, toning'o ake iyie ororei lai nikilo aing'uraki ilbalelon.”

English: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo ayau ninche ayaki ng'otonye, neitobir ng'otonye endaa sidai namelok naaijo enoshi nanyor.

English: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son:
Masaai: Neishopoki Rebeka inkilani sidan e Esau olkikau lenye, naata tiaji, olayioni lenye oti Yakobo, neripaki indapan oo lbalelon inkaik enyena tenebo emurt enye nasipa. Neisho ninye endaa sidai namelok tenebo emukate naitobira olayioni lenye Yakobo.

English: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
Masaai: Ore nena dapan oo lbalelon nepik inkaik enyena o ine wueji nesipa te murt enye;

English: And she gave the savoury meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
Masaai: neisho ninye endaa sidai namelok tenebo emukate naitobiraka epik inkaik o layioni lenye Yakobo.

English: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?
Masaai: Metaa eshomo ninye ajingaki menye nejoki, “Papa”. Neng'amaa ajoki, “Nele nanu, ira ng'ae enkerai ai?”

English: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo menye, “Nanu doi Esau olkikau lino. Aidipa ataasa anaa enikitiaka. Inyo totona inosa inkiri oo ng'uesi aainei peyie kitum atamayiana.”

English: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought it to me.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Isaak olayioni lenye, “Kaji doi inkuna peyie itasioko taata atum olayioni lai?” Newal ajoki, “Amu aaishoo Olaitoriani Enkai ina dupoto.”

English: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Isaak Yakobo, “Wou tinyiku, peyie atum airrapirrapa ajur enkerai ai, matayiolo katukul metii olng'ash ajo ira olayioni lai Esau anaa aimira.”

English: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Masaai: Neaku neigutaki Yakobo Isaak papaai lenye. Neirrapirrap ninye nejo, “Ore oltoilo naa oltoilo le Yakobo, kake ore inkaik naa ine Esau.”

English: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him.
Masaai: Neitu eyiolou ninye amu ore inkaik enyena naa keju anaa ino lalashe lenye Esau, neaku etamayiana ninye.

English: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Aira hoo doi olayioni lai Esau?” Newal ajo, “Ekara.”

English: And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo, “Iyakaki nanu peyie atum ainosa inkiri oo ng'uesi o layioni lai naatum atamayiana.” Neaku eyaua ninye ayaki ninye, nenya ninye; neyaki ninye enaisho oo sabibu neok ninye.

English: And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Isaak olayioni lenye, “wou tinyikakaki tung'ututaki olayioni lai.”

English: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:
Masaai: Metaa etinyikua ninye neng'utut ninye neing'uaya olng'usil too nkilani enyena, nemayian ninye ejo, “Ing'ura olng'usil lo layioni lai otiu anaa olng'usil liong'ata otamayiana Olaitoriani.

English: Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:
Masaai: Mikinchoo Enkai enkolielio e keper, tenebo empiron e nkop, tenebo enkisampuare sapuk o enaisho oo sabibu.

English: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.
Masaai: inchoo kisiaai iyie iloreren, nikigilaki kung iyie iloshon. Taa olkitok too lalashera linono, naa inchoo ilayiok le ng'utunyi kirrugokino iyie. Metedeki pooki ng'ae likidek, nemayiani pooki ng'ae likimayian iyie!”

English: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
Masaai: Ore ake enaidipie Isaak atamayiana Yakobo, ore ake enaipangie Yakobo aing'uaa ine netii Isaak Papaai lenye, nejingu olalashe lenye Esau eing'uaa engorore.

English: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.
Masaai: Neitobir sii ninye endaa sidai namelok, neyau ayaki papaai lenye. Nejoki menye “Inchoo papa lai edumunye aton ainos inkiri e ng'ues pee kitum atamayiana.”

English: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.
Masaai: Neng'amaa papaai lenye Isaak ajoki ninye, “Ira doi ng'ae?” Newal ajoki, “Nanu doi olayioni lino, olkikau lino Esau.”

English: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.
Masaai: Netum Isaak olokirikiri sapuk le ng'oro nejo ninye; “Aing'ae doi naaji otang'oro eng'ues naayaki nanu, nainosa pooki eton eitu ibau, naidipa atamayiana ninye? Nesipa Ee, naa kemayiana ninye.”

English: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
Masaai: Ore peyie ening Esau irorei le papaai lenye neishir abuaku to ltoilo sapuk o te mion, nejoki papaai lenye, “Oi tamayianaki sii nanu, nchooki sii nanu emayianata ino, papaai lai!”

English: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.
Masaai: Kake etiaka, “Eewuo olalashe lino to losek, neewa emayianata ino.”

English: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?
Masaai: Nejo Esau, “Aime keji doi te sipata etejoki enkarna enye Yakobo? Naaeseka ninye nanu kuna katitin are. Ewa apa ninye esipata ai e kikausho, naa ng'ura ake ajo enyaaka tena kata aya emayianata ai.” Ina peyie ejoki “Keitu hoo ninye kilekaki nanu emayianata?”

English: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?
Masaai: Newaliki Isaak Esau ejo, “Ing'ura ajo aitaa ninye olkitok lino, naa ore ilalashera lenyena, aishoo ninye meitaa isinkan, naa too lpaek tenebo enaisho oo sabibu aitotio ninye. Kaa naa taata aaitaas enkerai ai?”

English: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
Masaai: Nejoki Esau papaai lenye, “Ke mayianata nabo duoo ake iata papaai lai? Oi tamayianaki sii nanu, nchooki sii nanu emayianata ino, papaai lai!” Neilepie Esau oltoilo lenye neishir.

English: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;
Masaai: Newaliki Isaak papaai lenye ajoki, “ng'ura, iyaku ololamita empiron enkop te manyisho ino, niaku sii ololamita enkoliolio e keper e shumata.

English: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
Masaai: Keaku olalem lino ninye inchuyie, niaku oloisiaai olalashe lino, naa tinigelunye te nkitoria enye, nigil enchata oo lmong'i natii emurt ino.”

English: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
Masaai: Ore ina kata, neibayu Esau Yakobo enkaraki emayianata natamayiana papaai lenye ninye. Nejo Esau to ltau lenye. “Etabautua inkolong'i naishiraki papaai, ore peyie eishunye natum ataara metua olalashe lai Yakobo.”

English: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.
Masaai: Kake ore irorei le Esau ilo ayioni lenye botor etolikioki Rebeka; metaa eirriwayie Rebeka lkiliku meipoti ilo ayioni lenye oti, Yakobo nejoki ninye, “Ingura, ore olalashe lino Esau, eitagolito kewan oshoke pee kitum atara tua.

English: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
Masaai: Metaa ore tena kata enkerai ai toning'o oltoilo lai tudumunye isikaki enetii Laban olalashe lai otii Haran,

English: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;
Masaai: niton tenebo ninye te nkiti rishata, ometaba anaa neyagaa engoro napi olalashe lino;

English: Until thy brother's anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
Masaai: o metaba anaa nerrinyo engoro olalashe lino. Nerikino enintaasa ninye, naa kairriu olkilikuai mikitorikuni te ine. Ainyoo peyie aiturraa intae pookira te keeya te nkolong nabo?”

English: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Rebeka Isaak, “Enaure enkishui ai tenkaraki kuna kituaak oo Lhiti. Teneyam sii ninye Yakobo nabo o nkituaak oo Lhiti naaijo kuna, nabo oo nkituaak ena kop, kainyoo tipat enkishui te nanu?”

English: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
Masaai: Neitoki Isaak aipot Yakobo, nemayian ninye, neitanap ejoki, “Mayieu niyam hoo nabo oo nkituaak oo Lkanaan.

English: Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.
Masaai: Inyo tudumunye shomo Padan-aram enkaji e Betuel laa ninye otoiwuo yeyioo lino, niyau aitaa enkitok teine entito nabo e Laban olalashe yieyioo lino.

English: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;
Masaai: Mikitamayiana Enkai Magilani, nikintubul aponaa, metaa iaku olorere kumok too ltung'ana.

English: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.
Masaai: Mikinchoo ninye iyie emayianata e Abraham o tenebo eishoi ino, niaku oloya enkop nitaa iyie omoni naishoo Enkai Abraham!”

English: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padanaram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.
Masaai: Neisho Isaak Yakobo meshomo. Nelo Padan-aram enetii Laban olayioni le Betuel le Aram, naa olalashe le Rebeka ng'otonye Yakobo o tenebo Esau.

English: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padanaram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
Masaai: Etodua apa Esau ajo etamayiana Isaak Yakobo neisho ninye meshomo Padan-aram meing'oru enkitok teine netamayiana sii neitanap ejoki, “Mayieu niyam enkitok hoo nabo oo Lkanaan,”

English: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padanaram;
Masaai: netoning'o Yakobo menye o yieyio lenye nelo Padan-aram.

English: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
Masaai: Metaa ore peyie edol Esau ajo eitu eitiship nena kituaak oo Lkanaan papaai lenye Isaak;

English: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.
Masaai: nelo Esau enetii Ishmael, neyam aitaa enkitok, aponaa te nena kituaak naata, Mahalat entito e Ishmael, olayioni le Abraham; enkanashe e Naboiot.

English: And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
Masaai: Neing'uaa Yakobo Beer-sheba alo enkalo e Haran.

English: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
Masaai: Nelotu ewueji neje neirrag ine ina kewarie, amu etadoyie enkolong nedumu osoit obo teine airishunye elukunya enye neirrag teine airura.

English: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
Masaai: Ore eirura, netum enkidetidet naitodolu olkedet ororita enkop ore enchumata enye nebaiki keper, naa ng'ura! ilmalaika le Nkai oodou neilep te ilo kedet!

English: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;
Masaai: naa ng'ura eitashe Olaitoriani te nchumata ninye, nejo ninye, “Ara nanu Olaitoriani, Enkai e Abraham papaai lino, nara sii Enkai e Isaak, naa ore ena kop naa ninye irragie, ekaaisho nanu iyie tenebo o eishoi ino.

English: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
Masaai: Naa kebayu eishoi ino anaa enterit enkop naa aiponari aibulaa aidapashakino enkop te nkalo o loontoluo, o tenkalo o loosaen, o te nkalo e moikuape o te nkalo e kopikop; naa te iyie tenebo eishoi ino emayian iloshon le nkop pooki ate.

English: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
Masaai: Ing'ura atii nanu te nebo iyie naa kaarrip iyie te pooki wueji naba anaa enilo, naaitoki arrinyu ena kop, amu maaing'uaa nanu iyie o metaba anaa naas ina naatolikio.”

English: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
Masaai: Neinyototo Yakobo too njo enyena nejo, “Esipa etii Olaitoriani ene wueji, neitu duoo ayiolou.”

English: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
Masaai: Neureishoyu oleng nejo, “Kebaa eitureisho ene wueji! Meeta duoo inchere paa dikae ene wueji neme enkaji e Nkai, naa enkishomi (enkiimata najing'ieki) keper, ena.”

English: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
Masaai: Neaku einyo Yakobo tadekenya enasirie, neya oladuo soit oirishunye elukunya enye neitasheyie aitaa eng'ape nebukoki eilata shumata ninye.

English: And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.
Masaai: Neipot enkarna eine wueji ajo Betel, kake keji apa enkarna e ina anasa Lus te dukuya.

English: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
Masaai: Neinos Yakobo olmumai ejo, “Tenaa keaku Enkai tenebo nanu, naarrip nanu tena lototo, naaisho sii endaa nanya o nkilani naishop

English: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
Masaai: metaa anyaaka arrinyunye enkaji e papa lai te seriani, naa keaku Olaitoriani Enkai ai.

English: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
Masaai: Ore ele soit laitasheyie aitaa eng'ape, naa keaku enkaji Enkai, ore pooki nikincho nanu naa kaaisho iyie ematua e tomon.”

English: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.
Masaai: Nedumunye Yakobo aibung enkoitoi alo, nebau enkop oo ltung'ana oomanya oloosaen.

English: And he looked, and behold a well in the field, and, lo, there were three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone was upon the well's mouth.
Masaai: Ore eing'orisho, etoduaa enchorro ti ong'ata, ore ake sii, etodua iluaat uni oo nkishu o nkerrai eirrag te mbata eina shorro amu teina shorro eokokinyieki enkare naok. Netii osoit sapuk enkutuk enchorro.

English: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth in his place.
Masaai: Naa tenereuni nkerrai pooki meirraga teine, neibeleleng'oo ilchekuti ilo soit te nkutuk enchorro peyie etum aishoo ntare enye enkare. Ore ake peyie eidip aaitooko pooki, neitoki aapising enchoro teilo soit aapik enkutuk enchorro.

English: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence be ye? And they said, Of Haran are we.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo ninche, “Ilalashera laainei, kaji doi ing'uaa?” Nejo ninche, “King'uaa Haran.”

English: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Amaa iyiololo Laban olayioni le Nahor?” Nejo ninche, “Aikiyiolo ninye.”

English: And he said unto them, Is he well? And they said, He is well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo ninche “Aisupat ninye?” Neng'amaa aajo, “Ee aisupat, naa ore entito enye Raheli elotu ereuta ntare!” Nejo Yakobo,

English: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go and feed them.
Masaai: “Ing'ura, eton aa enaipirie enkolong, eton menkata naiturrurri nkerrai aaokoki enkare peyie etum aashom aatadaata.”

English: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and till they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.
Masaai: Kake etejo, “Mikintook omeiturrurroto nkerrai pooki tenebo, nikimbeleleng'oo osoit te nkutuk e nchorro nikitum aaitooko inkerrai.”

English: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep: for she kept them.
Masaai: Ore eton eirorie ninche, nebau Raheli ereuta ntare e papaai lenye aa ninye nairritita.

English: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Yakobo Raheli entito e Laban olalashe ng'otonye tenebo nkerrai e Laban olalashe ng'otonye nelo Yakobo aibeleleng'oo osoit te nkutuk enchorro, neitook inkerrai e Laban, olalashe ng'otonye.

English: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
Masaai: Neng'utut Yakobo Raheli eishir abuaku te nchipai.

English: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.
Masaai: Neliki Yakobo Raheli ajoki ole sotua, naa olayioni le Rebeka. Neipirri Raheli ang alo aliki menye.

English: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
Masaai: Ore peyie ening Laban ilomon le Yakobo olayioni le nkanashe, neipirri alo anang'are ninye, neitamuat ninye inkaik neng'utut neriku ninye enkaji enye. Neliki Yakobo Laban kuna baa pooki,

English: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.
Masaai: neaku etiaka Laban ninye, “Esipa tukul ajo ira oloito lai nira sii osesen lai!” Neton aboitare ninye olapa.

English: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?
Masaai: Neitoki Laban ajoki Yakobo, “Ore amu ira ole sotua, aikisiaai iyie nanu pesho? Tolikioki ajo ainyoo elaata niyieu naalaaki?”

English: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
Masaai: Eeta apa Laban ntoyie are, neji entito botor Lea neji entito kiti Raheli.

English: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.
Masaai: Aitorrok apa nkonyek e Lea ore Raheli naa aisidai neikishiaan.

English: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
Masaai: Nenyorru Yakobo Raheli, o metejo “Ekaaisiaai iyie ilarin oopishana tenkaraki Raheli ina tito ino kiti.”

English: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
Masaai: Nejo Laban, “Enaikash te naaisho iyie alang te naisho ninye likae lee; totona tenebo nanu.”

English: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
Masaai: Neaku eisiaayia apa Yakobo ninye ilarin oopishana tenkaraki Raheli, netiu lelo arin anaa inkolong'i kuti tenkaraki enyorrata sapuk naata te ninye.

English: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
Masaai: Neitoki Yakobo ajoki Laban, “Inchooki nanu enkitok ai peyie alo ayiolou ninye, amu aitabayie enkata ai.”

English: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
Masaai: Neiturrurru Laban iltung'ana pooki leine, neitayu osirua

English: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.
Masaai: kake ore teipa ewa entito enye Leah ayaki ninye Yakobo; neboitare Yakobo ninye ina kewarie.

English: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid for an handmaid.
Masaai: (Eishooyie Laban enkaisiaayiani enye Silpa, aisho Lea entito enye metaa enkaisiaayiani enye.)

English: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?
Masaai: Ore peyie ekenyu, ng'ura, Leah ngole eishooki Yakobo, Nejoki Yakobo Laban, “Ainyoo ena nikintaasa nanu? Aime enaji Raheli doi apa aaisiayie? Ainyoo naa peyie kiteleja iyie nanu?”

English: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.
Masaai: Neng'amaa Laban ejo, “Measi oshi neijia te nkop ang, aaishooyo entito kiti eton eitu eishoori enkikau.

English: Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.
Masaai: Iishu e wiki ena, naa aikintoki aaisho iyie enkae tinikisiaai kulikae arin oopishana.”

English: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week: and he gave him Rachel his daughter to wife also.
Masaai: Neas Jakobo ina, neishu ewiki enye; neaku neishoo Laban ninye Raheli ina tito enye meitaa enkitok.

English: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her maid.
Masaai: (Eishooyie Laban enkaisiaayiani enye Bilha, aisho Raheli entito enye metaa enkaisiaayiani enye.)

English: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.
Masaai: Neaku enyaaka sii Yakobo alo ayiolou Raheli nenyorru Raheli oleng aitalang enanyor Lea neisiaai Laban kulikae arin oopishana.

English: And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Olaitoriani ajo keibai Lea, nebol eng'uset enye, kake ore apa Raheli naa koolupi.

English: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; now therefore my husband will love me.
Masaai: Nenutayu Lea neiu enkayioni neipot ninye enkarna ajo Ruben, amu etejo, “Enkaraki natoduaa Olaitoriani enkisilisiloto ai, nesipa taata ajo ekaanyoru olpayian lai.”

English: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.
Masaai: Neitoki ake anutayu, neiu enkayioni, nejo, “Enkaraki natoningo Olaitoriani ajo kaaibai naaisho ena ayioni aigil.” Neipot enkarna enye ajo Simon.

English: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.
Masaai: Neitoki ake anutayu neiu enkayioni nejo, “Ore taata naa kaibung'are olpayian lai, amu atoikio ninye ilayiok okuni.” Ina peyie eipot enkarna enye ajo Lawi.

English: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah; and left bearing.
Masaai: Neitoki anutayu neiu enkayioni nejo “Ore taata naa kaisis Olaitoriani,” metaa eipoto ninye enkarna ajo Yuda, ina pee edung eishoi.

English: And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Raheli ajo eitu eiki Yakobo inkera, netum olom te nkanashe enye oleng, nejoki ninye Yakobo, “Nchooki nanu nkera ashu aye!”

English: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
Masaai: Negorokino Yakobo Raheli nejoki ninye, “Katii nanu ewueji Enkai nikitomitikio eishoi enguset ino?”

English: And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; and she shall bear upon my knees that I may also have children by her.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo Raheli, “Neina enkaisiaayiani ai Bilha; shomo enetii peyie aaiki nanu nkera.”

English: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife: and Jacob went in unto her.
Masaai: Metaa eishoo ninye Yakobo enkaisiaayiani enye Bilha meitaa enkitok. Nelo Yakobo ayiolou ninye.

English: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.
Masaai: Neiroshiu Bilhah neiki Yakobo olayioni.

English: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo Raheli, “Aatudungoko Enkai enkiguana, netoning'o sii oltoilo lai naaisho nanu enkayioni.” Neaku eipoto enkarna enye ajo Dan.

English: And Bilhah Rachel's maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.
Masaai: Neitoki errindik e Raheli anutayu neiki Yakobo olayioni le are.

English: And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo Raheli, “Te nkesha nagol atigilunore enkanashe ai natimirishe;” neipot enkarna enye ajo Naftali.

English: When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her maid, and gave her Jacob to wife.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Lea ajo etudunge meekure eisho, neisho sii ninye enkaisiaayiani enye Silpa Yakobo meitaa enkitok.

English: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a son.
Masaai: Neiki ina rrindik e Lea naji Silpa Yakobo olayioni.

English: And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.
Masaai: Nejo Lea, “Atumunyana!” metaa eishoo enkarna enye ajo Gad.

English: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a second son.
Masaai: Neigil ake errindik e Lea naji Silpa aiki Yakobo ae ayioni e are.

English: And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed: and she called his name Asher.
Masaai: Ina pee ejo Lea, “Ashipa nanu! amu kaaipot nanu inkituaak aajo nashipa.” Ina pee eipot enkarna enye ajo Asheri.

English: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.
Masaai: Ore too nkolong'i enkisampuare e nkano eshomo Ruben olokeri neinepu nkaitubulu naaji tunkuja tiongota, neyaki ng'otonye Lea. Ina peyie ejoki Raheli Lea “Inchooki aatasayia embata oonkaitubulu e tukuja e nkayioni ino.”

English: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night for thy son's mandrakes.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Lea ninye, “Ijo doi kembae kiti tinikioru olpayian lai? Iyieu sii nintoki aya tunkuja olayioni lai?” Nejo Raheli, “Inchoo naa meirraga enitii ena kewarie te nkaraki tunkuja olayioni lino.”

English: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.
Masaai: Ore peyie eshukunye Yakobo tiong'ata teipa, eshomo Lea anang'are ninye nejoki ninye, “Meeta inchere peyie mikilotu taata ayiolou, amu ainyiang'ua iyie te tunkuja olayioni lai.” Metaa etaboitare ninye ina kewarie.

English: And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob the fifth son.
Masaai: Nening Enkai Lea, nenutayu neiki Yakobo olayioni le imiet.

English: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
Masaai: Nejo Lea, “Aishoo Enkai elaakinoto ai amu aishooyie errindik ai aisho olpayian lai;” neipot enkarna ajo Isachar.

English: And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.
Masaai: Neitoki Lea anutayu, neiki Yakobo enkayioni e ile,

English: And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
Masaai: ina peyie ejo Lea, “Aaishoo Olaitoriani enkishoroto sapuk; ekaayanyitu taata olpayian lai, amu atoikio ninye ilayiok ile;” neipot enkarna enye Sebulon.

English: And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
Masaai: Neitoki ake te siadi aiu entito neipot enkarna enye ajo Dina.

English: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.
Masaai: Neitoki Enkai adamu Raheli, nening Enkai ninye nebol eng'uset.

English: And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach:
Masaai: Nenutayu neiu enkayioni nejo, “Eiwuangie Enkai esulare ai,”

English: And she called his name Joseph; and said, The LORD shall add to me another son.
Masaai: neipot enkarna enye ajo Yosef ejo, “Maatoponiki Olaitoriani ae ayioni.”

English: And it came to pass, when Rachel had born Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, Send me away, that I may go unto mine own place, and to my country.
Masaai: Ore peyie eiki Raheli Yakobo Yosef, etiaaka ninye Laban, “Inchooki nanu mashomo, pee atum ashomo enkang ai o enkop ai.

English: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest my service which I have done thee.
Masaai: Inchooki inkituaak aainei tenebo nkera aainei nena naisiaayua te iyie nikincho mashomo amu iyiolo esiaai naataasaka.”

English: And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Laban ninye, “Tenaa aikincho matejo ena, atayiolo te limunoto olaitumusumusoni inchere aatamayiana Olaitoriani tenkaraki iyie.

English: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.
Masaai: Tolimu elaakinoto ino naa kaishoru.”

English: And he said unto him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how thy cattle was with me.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo ninye, “Iyiolo iyie openy enaikuna tenaaisiaai, niyiolo sii eneikuna inkishu inono peyie eponari te nanu.

English: For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased unto a multitude; and the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also?
Masaai: Amu aikuti apa imasaa inono enalotunye, netoponari aaku kumok, nikitamayiana iyie Olaitoriani te pooki wueji naibelekenyakine. Paa amaa kanu kenya nanu agolie olmarei lai makewan?”

English: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing: if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed and keep thy flock:
Masaai: Nejo Laban, “Ainyoo iyieu naaisho?” Nejo Yakobo, “Meeta entoki nikinchoo tini kintaas ena, ekaitoki ake aaku oloirrita naramat aing'or intare inono.

English: I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.
Masaai: “Nchooki matijing'a atua intare inono ena olong aitayu tiatua pooki ker naata oltipoto anaa nairimo o pooki kuo le ker orok, tenebo pooki kine oirimo tiatua inkineji; neaku nena elaakinoto ai.

English: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.
Masaai: Metaa esipata ai ninye naawalaki te siadi, tinilotu aing'or elaakinoto ai te iyie. Ore pooki nemeeta oltipoto nemeirrimo sii tiatua inkineji, nerok sii tiatua lkuoo le kerra metaa tenelo netumi te nanu, neikenari aajo kepurruno.”

English: And Laban said, Behold, I would it might be according to thy word.
Masaai: Nejo Laban, “Aisidai! inchoo etiu anaa enitejo.”

English: And he removed that day the he goats that were ringstraked and spotted, and all the she goats that were speckled and spotted, and every one that had some white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
Masaai: Kake ore ina olong, eitayio Laban iloroi pooki o otipo neirrimo tenebo inkineji pooki netipo neirrimo pooki ake ninye naata eneibor, o pooki sitima lo ker orok, neisho ilayiok lenyena metaramata.

English: And he set three days' journey betwixt himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flocks.
Masaai: Nelo Laban alamari elakuani oo nkolong'i uni elototo terishata enye o Yakobo; neirrita Yakobo kulie tare pooki e Laban.

English: And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree; and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
Masaai: Neitayu Yakobo ing'usidin naashal too lkeek oonyaanyukie olporokuai, o seki o siteti nekinyu nkopit e oriong te nena keek metaa kelio ing'udisin eibor.

English: And he set the rods which he had pilled before the flocks in the gutters in the watering troughs when the flocks came to drink, that they should conceive when they came to drink.
Masaai: Nepik nena ngudisin naatikinya te dukuya ntare too mpeuti aa taa, ine neokishoreki, ine nepuonu ntare aaokie enkare. Amu kesesh etonie ilmeregeshi anaa iloroi intare teine.

English: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
Masaai: Neraposhoyu intare te dukuya nena ngudisin metaa etoiwutuo ilbalelon oo rasha, o loo tipo, o loonkererin.

English: And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban; and he put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not unto Laban's cattle.
Masaai: Negelaa Yakobo isitiman, neing'orie inkomomi oo ntare enkalo natii inaarasha tenebo inaarook pooki naatii tiatua intare e Laban; neitalamaa inenyena, neitu eitushulaki ine Laban.

English: And it came to pass, whensoever the stronger cattle did conceive, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the cattle in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods.
Masaai: Ore enkata pooki natonie ilmeregeshi anaa iloroi intare biot, neirragie Yakobo ing'udisin too mpeuti te dukuya ninche peyie etum aatotonie intare te nena ng'udisin,

English: But when the cattle were feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's.
Masaai: kake ore nena sasin too ntare, eitu eirragie ing'udisin teine; metaa ore nena sasin neaku ine Laban ore inaapir neaku ine Yakobo.

English: And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses.
Masaai: Metaa etaa Yakobo karsis oleng, netum intare luaat kumok, o nkaisiaayiak o ilaisiaayiak o intamesin o sirkon.

English: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's; and of that which was our father's hath he gotten all this glory.
Masaai: Etoning'o apa Yakobo ilayiok le Laban ejo, “Ewa Yakobo pooki apa naara ine papa lang; ore sii te nena pooki apa naara ine papa lang, nenoto ninye ena arsisisho.”

English: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.
Masaai: Nedol Yakobo ajo meekure enyor Laban ninye anaa apa te dukuya.

English: And the LORD said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Olaitoriani Yakobo, “Torrinyoyu enkop oo loo papaai lino, tushukokinoyu iltung'ana linono naa kaaku nanu tenebo iyie.”

English: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,
Masaai: Neirriwaa Yakobo olkilikuai aipotu Raheli tenebo Lea meetu ina ong'ata natii ntare enyena,

English: And said unto them, I see your father's countenance, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father hath been with me.
Masaai: nejoki ninche, “Adolita taata ajo meekure aanyor papaai linyi anaa apa. Kake etii Enkai e papaai lai tenebo nanu.

English: And ye know that with all my power I have served your father.
Masaai: Iyiololo aajo aisiaaiyia papaai linyi te ngolon ai pooki;

English: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.
Masaai: ore ake eyia, aateleja papaai linyi aibelekeny olekoisiaayio lai katitin tomon, kake eitu eisho Enkai ninye maaitamio.

English: If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy wages; then all the cattle bare speckled: and if he said thus, The ringstraked shall be thy hire; then bare all the cattle ringstraked.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo, ‘Ore pooki naatipo naa keaku olekoisiaayio lino,’ ina pee eiu intare pooki inaata iltipot; naa tenejo, ninye, ‘Naata nkererin naaku olekoisiaayio lino,’ neiu intare pooki naata nkererin.

English: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me.
Masaai: Metaa neijia eikuna Enkai aya inkishu e papaai linyi naaisho ninche nanu.

English: And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled.
Masaai: Ore te nkata nadumu iloroi anaa ilmaregeshi intare, atejo araposhu inkonyek aainei nadol te nkidetidet inchere ore iloroi pooki oo oodumu intare naa iloota nkererin o iltipot nerasha neirrimo.

English: And the angel of God spake unto me in a dream, saying, Jacob: And I said, Here am I.
Masaai: Ina peyie aajoki olmalaika le Nkai te nkidetidet, ‘Yakobo,’ nang'amaa ajo, ‘Nele nanu!’

English: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle are ringstraked, speckled, and grisled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.
Masaai: nejo ninye, ‘Taraposhu inkonyek inono ing'orisho, ore inkineji pooki naaitigiran tiaatua intare naa keeta nkererin, neeta iltipot nerasha; amu atoduaa nena pooki nikintaasa Laban iyie.

English: I am the God of Bethel, where thou anointedst the pillar, and where thou vowedst a vow unto me: now arise, get thee out from this land, and return unto the land of thy kindred.
Masaai: Ara nanu Enkai e Betel, ine wueji apa nintisinyie eng'ape abukoki e ilata nikinosaki sii olmumai. Ore tena kata inyo shomo tung'uai ena kop nirrinyo alo enkop apa nikitoinyieki.’ ”

English: And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?
Masaai: Ina pee ewalaki Raheli o Lea aajoki ninye, “Ketii ae rubata arashu enjung'ore natung'ueikiaki iyiook te nkaji e papa lang?

English: Are we not counted of him strangers? for he hath sold us, and hath quite devoured also our money.
Masaai: Amaa taata iyiook emeitaa iyiook ilomon? Amu etimira iyiook, netaasishore impisai naaishoruaki te nkaraki iyiook.

English: For all the riches which God hath taken from our father, that is ours, and our children's: now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.
Masaai: Ore nena masaa pooki naawa Enkai aitung'uaa papaai lang eishoo metaa inkunaang o nkera ang, ore tena kata, ore pooki nikijoki Enkai iyie, taasa.”

English: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels;
Masaai: Neinyototo Yakobo neitaked ilayiok lenyena o nkituaak enyena intamesin,

English: And he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, the cattle of his getting, which he had gotten in Padanaram, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: nereu ninye aidurrie inkishu enyena pooki, tenebo imasaa enyena pooki naanoto, inkishu enyena naanoto te Padan-aram, pee epuo enkop e Kanaan enetii papaai lenye Isaak.

English: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's.
Masaai: Eshomo apa Laban adung ilpapit loo nkerra enyena, ore Raheli nepurroo inkaitin enkaji e papaai lenye.

English: And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.
Masaai: Neluaya Yakobo eitu eliki Laban le Aram, ajoki ekeisikita alo.

English: So he fled with all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the river, and set his face toward the mount Gilead.
Masaai: Neisik ninye o nena masaa pooki naata, neinyototo alang olkeju le Frati, neitoriokino oldoinyo le Gilead.

English: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled.
Masaai: Ore peyie elikini Laban te enkolong e uni inchere eisika Yakobo,

English: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead.
Masaai: nerik iltung'ana lenyena le sotua, nepuo aasuj ninye inkolong'i naapishana esuj aigutaki ninye oleng toldoinyo le Gilead.

English: And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said unto him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
Masaai: Kake eewuo Enkai enetii Laban le Aram te nkidetidet kewarie nejoki ninye, “Toduaa ake kewan mijoki Yakobo ororei hoo obo sidai arashu oltorrono.”

English: Then Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mount: and Laban with his brethren pitched in the mount of Gilead.
Masaai: Neinepu Laban Yakobo. Ore ina kata eidipa Yakobo atuuno olng'obor lenye te nkop ooldoinyo, ore Laban, o ltungana lenyena le sotua, etuuno ilng'oborri too ldoinyo le Gilead.

English: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters, as captives taken with the sword?
Masaai: Nejoki Laban Yakobo, “Kaa ena nikintaasa peyie kilotu alej aiko nji, niya intoyie aainei anaa iyarunot o lalem?

English: Wherefore didst thou flee away secretly, and steal away from me; and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee away with mirth, and with songs, with tabret, and with harp?
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie isika apurrorri, nikilej nanu, neitu kiliki nanu, metaa anaata aaishoo iyie shomo te nchipai o too sinkolioitin, o te ntampuri o to lwulul loo usin?

English: And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? thou hast now done foolishly in so doing.
Masaai: Naa kainyoo peyie eitu kincho matung'ututa ilayiok laainei o ntoyie aainei aisho olesere? Itaasa tukul ene emodai.

English: It is in the power of my hand to do you hurt: but the God of your father spake unto me yesternight, saying, Take thou heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
Masaai: Ekaata engolon naitameyie kake aairorie Enkai e papaai lino ena kewarie aajoki, ‘Toduaa kewan ake mijoki Yakobo ororei hoo obo sidai arashu oltorrono.’

English: And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father's house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
Masaai: Ore taata ishomo aidur enkaraki niyieu oleng to ltau enkaji e papaai lino, kake ainyoo peyie itupurroyie inkaitin aainei?”

English: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid: for I said, Peradventure thou wouldest take by force thy daughters from me.
Masaai: Newaliki Yakobo Laban ajoki, “Amu atureishe, atadamua ajo aikindim atooru intoyie inono te ngolon.

English: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
Masaai: Ore ake ninye oltung'ani litum eeta inkaitin inono nemeitoki abik eishu. Ore te dukuya iltung'ana lang le sotua imbalunye entoki ino pooki naata pee iya.” Eitu eyiolou Yakobo ajo Raheli ninye natupurroyie nena aitin.

English: And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the two maidservants' tents; but he found them not. Then went he out of Leah's tent, and entered into Rachel's tent.
Masaai: Metaa etijing'a Laban olng'obor le Yakobo, neitoki alo olng'obor le, Lea neitoki oloo nkaisiaayiak enyena pokira, neitu etum ninche katukul. Nepuku aing'uaa olng'obor le Lea, nejing olng'obor le Raheli.

English: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
Masaai: Ore ina kata earr Laban ilng'oborri naa Raheli apa naawa inkaitin enkaji e Papaai lenye nepik abori olorika otonieki te ntames, netonie ninche. Near Laban olng'obor pooki, kake eitu etum ninche.

English: And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
