Masaai: Nejoki Raheli Papaai, lenye, “Mincho olkitok lai egoro amu maidim aitasho te dukuya iyie, amu kaata empukunoto oo nkituaak.” Metaa etuturuo aing'oru oleng neitu etum inkaitin enkaji enye tukul.

English: And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my trespass? what is my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?
Masaai: Neaku etagore Yakobo oleng oleng metaa keitarriki Laban; nejoki Yakobo Laban, “Ainyoo doi enkitarruorroto ai? Ainyoo eng'oki ai pee kitusujua te ngoro sapuk?

English: Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? set it here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us both.
Masaai: Ore hoo nitijing'a aisiamput intokitin aainei, ainyoo inoto tiatua naara imasaa nkaji ino? Iyau irragie tene te dukuya iltung'ana laaine le sotua o te dukuya iltung'ana linono le sotua pee etum aatirrish iyiook pokira.

English: This twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.
Masaai: Kitaboitate tenebo iyie kulo arin tikitam; netiu aikata eibiru isupeni e kerra inono anaa inkineji inono, neitu ainos ilmeregeshi loo ntare inono.

English: That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, whether stolen by day, or stolen by night.
Masaai: Ore nena naanya ing'uesi etim eitu ayaki, nanu onoto enyamali makewan; anaa aiyieu pooki too nkaik aainei; anaa enapurrorri dama anaa kewarie.

English: Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.
Masaai: Metaa neijia apa atiu aanya enkolong naa neijia etiu enkewarie, nemeekure apa atumoki aimula nkonyek airurayu.

English: Thus have I been twenty years in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.
Masaai: Ore te kulo arin tikitam natotona te nkaji ino; naataasaka esiaai ilarin tomon oong'uan te nkaraki intoyie inono pokira are, naataasaka esiaai ilarin ile too ntare inono, nimbelekenya olekoisiaayio lai katitin tomon.

English: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely thou hadst sent me away now empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesternight.
Masaai: Tenaa aime Enkai duoo e papaai lai Enkai e Abraham tenebo olturiaki le Isaak ootii enkalo ai, esipa katukul inchere anaata kinchoo mashomo too nkaik naarook. Etoduaa Enkai osina lai tenebo esiaai oo nkaik aainei, nikisikong ng'ole kewarie.”

English: And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and these cattle are my cattle, and all that thou seest is mine: and what can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children which they have born?
Masaai: Ina peyie ewalu Laban ajoki Yakobo, “Ore kuna toyie naa inaainei, ore kuna kera naa inaainei, ore kuna tare naa inaainei, naa ore pooki nidolita naa inaainei. Kake kaa naa aitaas kuna toyie aainei ena olong arashu inkera enye naatoiutuo ninche? Wou taata maitayu olning'o terishata ai o iyie;

English: Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.
Masaai: ore iyie o nanu; naa inchoo metijing'a shakeni erishata ang.”

English: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
Masaai: Ina peyie eyau Yakobo osoit, neitasheyie aitaa eng'ape.

English: And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made an heap: and they did eat there upon the heap.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo iltung'ana lenyena le sotua, “Entasotu isoito,” neyau pooki isoito neitayu osototi; neinos endaa te mbata e ilo sototi loo soito.

English: And Laban called it Jegarsahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.
Masaai: Neipot Laban ine ajo Yegarsahaduta: nejo ninye Yakobo ajo Gilead.

English: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;
Masaai: Nejo Laban, “Ore ele sototi loo soito naa shakeni terishata ino o nanu tena olong.”

English: And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.
Masaai: Metaa eipoto ine ajo Gilead, ore engape nejo Mispa, ketejo, “Inchoo meing'ura Olaitoriani erishata ai o enino, tinikipuo aalama,

English: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, God is witness betwixt me and thee.
Masaai: Tinintanyamal intoyie aainei, anaa tiniyam kulie kituaak neme intoyie aainei, ore hoo nemetii likae lee ine oyiolo, tadamu, ajo, Enkai ninye shakeni terishata ai o iyie.”

English: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Laban Yakobo, “Ing ura ele sototi loo soito tenebo eng'ape naitasheyie ena olong te dukuya iyie o nanu.

English: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.
Masaai: Ore ele sototi naa shakeni naa neijia etiu eng'ape, inchere migiru ele sototi loo soito, nimilang'u sii iyie ele sototi loo soito kilang'aki, neijia eitiu eng'ape kilotu aitame nanu.

English: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob sware by the fear of his father Isaac.
Masaai: Ore Enkai e Abraham, oe Nkai e Nahor oe Nkai oo papaai lenye inchoo metirisha iyiook.” Ina peyie einos Yakobo olmumai te uriata e papaai lenye, Isaak.

English: Then Jacob offered sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mount.
Masaai: Neitayu Yakobo olasar to ldoinyo neipoti iltung'ana lenyena le sotua meinosa endaa, nenya endaa netoni enkewarie pooki te ilo doinyo.

English: And early in the morning Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban departed, and returned unto his place.
Masaai: Ore tadekenya enasirie, einyo Laban ayooki ang'utut inoo nkakuyiaa enyena tenebo intoyie enyena nemayian ninche; nerrinyo alo enkang enye.

English: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
Masaai: Nedumunye Yakobo alo arrinyo enkop enye, nenang'are ilmalaika le Nkai ninye.

English: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is God's host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Yakobo ninche, etejo, “Enjore e Nkai ena!” Neipot enkarna eine ajo Mahanaim.

English: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Yakobo ilkiliku meituruko aapuo enetii olalashe lenye Esau te nkop e Seir, natii enkop e Edom,

English: And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye speak unto my lord Esau; Thy servant Jacob saith thus, I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed there until now:
Masaai: neitaarriyian ninche ejoki, “Inji intae enchom entiaaki olkitok lai Esau inji ejo olaisiaayiani lino Yakobo, ‘Ataboitare Laban o taata,

English: And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and menservants, and womenservants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.
Masaai: naata ilmong'i, o sirkon, o ntare o laisiaayiak lewa, o nkaisiaayiak ng'oruo nairriwua olkilikuai aliki olkitok lai, pee atum anoto omom too nkonyek inono.’ ”

English: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and also he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
Masaai: Nerrinyunye lelo kiliku enetii Yakobo nejoki, “Kitabaikitia olalashe lino Esau, naa elotu ninye peyie kinang'are iyie nerikito ilewa iip ong'uan.”

English: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands;
Masaai: Neureishoyu Yakobo oleng oleng netum enkiputukuny, oleng, Neor lelo tung'ana apa ooboitare, neor inkishu o ntamesin, neitainye pooki ntukusi are edamu ejo,

English: And said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the other company which is left shall escape.
Masaai: “Tenelotu Esau aidaikie entukus nabo, neaku ore entukus natelekua neidim aisika.”

English: And Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the LORD which saidst unto me, Return unto thy country, and to thy kindred, and I will deal well with thee:
Masaai: Nejo Yakobo, “Na Ai Enkai e papa lai Abraham naa Enkai e papa lai Isaak, Lo Aitoriani, ilo apa laatiaaka nanu, ‘Torrinyoyu shomo enkop ino enetii olorere lino le sotua, naa kaitaas iyie esidai,’

English: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast shewed unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands.
Masaai: maaishaakino nanu katukul ina nyorrata ino nauno, tenebo ina kisiligata nintodua iyie osinka lino, amu te ng'udi ai ake atalang'a ele keju le Yordan; nataa taata iltimito oare.

English: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.
Masaai: Tokorduaki nanu, aatoomono iyie, te nkaina olalashe lai, te nkaina e Esau, amu kaure nanu ninye melotu ake aar iyiook pooki matuata, nkera o noo ngotonye.

English: And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
Masaai: Kake itejo, ‘Ekaaitaas iyie esidai, naisho eishoi ino metaba anaa osinyai le naiposha, nemeikenayu te nkumoi.’ ”

English: And he lodged there that same night; and took of that which came to his hand a present for Esau his brother;
Masaai: Metaa eirraga ine ina kewarie, neitayu te nena naata ninye enkishooroto naisho olalashe lenye Esau.

English: Two hundred she goats, and twenty he goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams,
Masaai: Inkineji iip are, o oloroi tikitam, o supeni e kerra iip are tenebo ilmeregeshi tikitam,

English: Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty kine, and ten bulls, twenty she asses, and ten foals.
Masaai: Intamesin naalepo tomoni uni o nkurrarrun enye o nkishu artam tenebo iloing'ok tomon, o sirkon lipong'a tikitam, o lamuyeishi tomon.

English: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.
Masaai: Neitarasaa kuna too nkaik oo laisiaayiak lenyena, meeta ake ineitu erewi te luaata enye maate, ejoki sinkan lenyena, “Enchom enturuko ninchosho metaa ketii erishata eluaata ake o eluaata.”

English: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?
Masaai: Neitaarriyian olorikito pooki ajoki, “Ore te nenang'are intae Esau olalashe lai, nikinkilikuan ajoki, ‘Ira iyie oleng'ae? Kaji iloito? Naa einkuneng'ae kuna nireutata?’

English: Then thou shalt say, They be thy servant Jacob's; it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, also he is behind us.
Masaai: Naa ijoki ninye, ‘Ino sinka lino Yakobo naa enkishooroto nairriwaka olkitok lai Esau; ore ake sii, elotu ninye te siadi ang.’ ”

English: And so commanded he the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying, On this manner shall ye speak unto Esau, when ye find him.
Masaai: Neitaarriyian ake sii ilo liare o ilo liokuni o lelo pooki ooreuta nena masaa ejoki, “Entiaaki Esau ina bae tininang'arere, ninye.

English: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.
Masaai: Naa ijokiki intae, ‘Ore ake elotu osinka lino Yakobo te siadi.’ ” Amu etadamua ajo, “Kaidim aitoborro ninye too nkishorot naashomo te dukuya nanu, ore esuju ina naidim atoduaa enkomom enye; ebaiki naaidim atang'amai nanu.”

English: So went the present over before him: and himself lodged that night in the company.
Masaai: Metaa neitogirori ninye enkishooroto ore ina kewarie eirraga ninye olng'obor.

English: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two womenservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok.
Masaai: Ore ake ina kewarie nedumunye ninye arik inkituaak enyena pokira are, o nkaisiaayiak enyena pokira are tenebo inkera enyena tomon oobo nelang te lang'ata e Yabok.

English: And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that he had.
Masaai: neya ninche aitalang enkare, tenebo pooki toki naba anaa enaata,

English: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.
Masaai: neing'uari Yakobo aa ninye ake; ore ina kewarie etii oltung'ani otupupungare enkewarie pooki o metamanai e sirua.

English: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol ilo tung'ani ajo eitu eidimu Yakobo, neibung emorloo enkupes; nepuku enkupes e Yakobo terubata oloudo ina kata epupung'are ilo tung'ani.

English: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo oltung'ani, “Inchooki mashomo, amu ekenyua.” Kake etiaka Yakobo, “Maaisho hoo ilo o metaba anaa nikimayian.”

English: And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Aikiji ng'ae enkarna?” Nejo, “Yakobo.”

English: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki “Mikintokini aekata aajo Yakobo, kake Israel, amu itekeshare Enkai tenebo iltung'ana nisulie.”

English: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.
Masaai: Neitoki Yakobo aikilikuan ninye ajoki, “Tolikioki aatasayia enkarna ino.” Kake etiaaka, “Ainyoo doi peyie inkilikuanu enkarna ai?” Nemayian ninye teine.

English: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
Masaai: Neipot enkarna ine wueji ajo Peniel ejoito, “Amu kitoduaate o Enkai too nkomomi, ore ake eyia neton aishu.”

English: And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.
Masaai: Neilepaki enkolong egiroo Penuel, neitong'ojinari te nkaraki enkupes enye.

English: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh in the sinew that shrank.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina ebaiki ina olong; meinos Isiraeli emorloo o loudo; naatii enkong'u oloudo, tenkaraki naibung'a apa ninye enkong'u oloudo le Yakobo o emorloo enye.

English: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.
Masaai: Neraposhu Yakobo inkonyek enyena aing'orisho, ng'ura, elotu Esau nerikito iltung'ana iip ong'uan. Metaa etooro inkera aoriki Lea o Raheli o nkaisiaayiak enyena.

English: And he put the handmaids and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindermost.
Masaai: Nepik inkaisiaayiak tenebo inkera enye dukuya, ore Lea o nkera enyena, o Raheli o Yosef nepuonu te siadi,

English: And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
Masaai: ore ninye makewan neituruk te dukuya ninche, neirrugo abaiki enkop katitin naapishana, o metaba anaa nenyiku olalashe lenye.

English: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
Masaai: Kake ekuetua Esau alo anang'are ninye, neng'utut ninye, nebatatakino emurt enye ang'utut, neishir pokira.

English: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, Who are those with thee? And he said, The children which God hath graciously given thy servant.
Masaai: Ore peyie eraposhu Esau nkonyek enyena, etodua inkituaak o nkera, nejo ninye, “Kakua kuna nikiboitare?” Nejo Yakobo, “Inkera naaishoo Enkai to lng'ur osinka lino.”

English: Then the handmaidens came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves.
Masaai: Neitoki nena aisiaayiak aanyiku, ninche tenebo inkera enye, neirrugo aabaiki enkop;

English: And Leah also with her children came near, and bowed themselves: and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they bowed themselves.
Masaai: neitoki Lea tenebo inkera enyena aabau aanyiku neirrugo aabaiki enkop; ore te bayie e pooki nenyiku Yosef o Raheli, neirrugokino aabaiki enkop.

English: And he said, What meanest thou by all this drove which I met? And he said, These are to find grace in the sight of my lord.
Masaai: Nejo Esau, “Ainyoo eutu ele orora pooki lainepua?” Newal Yakobo ajo, “Pee atum omom te dukuya nkonyek olkitok lai.”

English: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself.
Masaai: Kake etejo Esau, “Ekaata inaabaiki, olalashe lai; intaa pooki niata ininono.”

English: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand: for therefore I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God, and thou wast pleased with me.
Masaai: Nejo Yakobo, “A'a, aatasayia, tenaa kanoto omom too nkonyek inono, neaku tang'amai naa enkishoroto ai too nkaik aainei; amu esipa tenajo ore enduaata natoduaa enkomom ino netiu anaa enduaata natoduaa enkomom e Nkai amu te nyorrata natiu neijia kitang'amua nanu.

English: Take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took it.
Masaai: Tang'amai, aatasayia ina kishoroto ai nikiyakaki iyie, amu aaing'urrie Enkai oleng, naa kaata sii inaabaiki.” Ina peyie earaki ninye meewa, neya ninye.

English: And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before thee.
Masaai: Neitoki Esau ajo, “Emaibung'a enkoitoi aapuo, naa kaituruk te dukuya iyie.”

English: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender, and the flocks and herds with young are with me: and if men should overdrive them one day, all the flock will die.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yakobo ninye, “Eyiolo olkitok lai ajo ore kuna ng'aturran naa kenana, naa nanu ogolie intare o nkishu tenebo ilasho lenye, naa te nerewi oleng enkolong nabo, naa keye imasaa pooki.

English: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant: and I will lead on softly, according as the cattle that goeth before me and the children be able to endure, until I come unto my lord unto Seir.
Masaai: Inchoo olkitok lai egiroo osinka lenye, pee ariku ninche maakutiti te risioroto e lototo oo nkishu naatii dukuya nanu o te risioroto e lototo oo inkera, omatabau enetii olkitok lai te Seir.”

English: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the folk that are with me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find grace in the sight of my lord.
Masaai: Neaku etejo Esau, “Inchooki maatung'ueiki embata oo ltung'ana laainei laata tene.” Kake etejo, “Meeta tipat ning'uarie. Ayieu ake duoo natum omom te dukuya enkomom ino olkitok lai.”

English: So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.
Masaai: Metaa etorrinye Esau ina olong alo Seir.

English: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him an house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
Masaai: Kake eshomo Yakobo Sukot, neshetaki kewan enkaji neitayu ninye ilngoborri loo nkishu enyena, metaa keji enkarna e ine wueji Sukot!

English: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padanaram; and pitched his tent before the city.
Masaai: Nelotu Yakobo te Seriani o metabaiki enkanasa naji Shekem, natii ina kop e Kanaan einguaa Padan-aram, neun ilngoborri te mbata enkanasa.

English: And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money.
Masaai: Neinyang'u too layiok le Hamor, aa papaai le Shekem too mpisai iip nabo e seshati enkop naa ninye etuunie ilngoborri lenyena.

English: And he erected there an altar, and called it Elelohe-Israel.
Masaai: Neshetu teine olperere lo lasar nedung'oki enkarna ine ajo El-Elohe Israel.

English: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
Masaai: Nedumunye Dina entito e Lea natoikio ninye Yakobo alo aparan inkituaak eina kop;

English: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.
Masaai: ore peyie edol Shekem olayioni le Hamor le Hifi ilo kitok leina kop, neibung ninye te ng'olon aikony nesul ninye.

English: And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.
Masaai: Neng'uar ninye Dina oleng to ltau lenye ina tito e Yakobo; nenyorru ninye ina tito, neirorie ninye too rorei oobor.

English: And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo Shekem airorie papai lenye Hamor ajoki: “Ing'urakaki ena tito maitaa enkitok.”

English: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter: now his sons were with his cattle in the field: and Jacob held his peace until they were come.
Masaai: Nening apa Yakobo ajo einyala shekem entito enye Dina; netii apa ilayiok lenyena nkishu ti ong'ota, negira Yakobo eitu ejo ae o metaba anaa nepuonu ninche.

English: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob to commune with him.
Masaai: Nelotu Hamor menye le Shekem enetii Yakobo airorie ninye.

English: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter; which thing ought not to be done.
Masaai: Nejing'u ilayiok le Yakobo eing'uaa ong'ota peyie ening ilo omoni; negoro ninche oleng pee ening ina bae amu etaasa Shekem ina nayaua esulare atua Israel aikony entito e Yakobo, amu ore embae neeijo ena nemeishaakino neasi.

English: And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you give her him to wife.
Masaai: Kake eirorie Hamor ninche ejoki, “Etayiewua naleng oltau lo layioni lai Shekem entito ino; aatasayia, enchoo ninye meyama.

English: And make ye marriages with us, and give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.
Masaai: Emayamata maate, enchoo iyiook intoyie inyi; niyaya sii intae intoyie ang.

English: And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.
Masaai: Nikishula aaku elatia, ore enkop neaku kebolokino intae, entamany nikintawal imasaa nitumutumu imasaa kumok.”

English: And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find grace in your eyes, and what ye shall say unto me I will give.
Masaai: Nejoki ake sii ninye Shekem menye ina tito tenebo ilalashera lenyena, “Nchooki manoto omom te dukuya inkonyek inyi, naa ore pooki nikijokiki intae naa kaishoru.

English: Ask me never so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to wife.
Masaai: Inkilikuanu te nanu imasaa pooki naaba anaa niyieu too nkishorot, naa kaishoru te risioroto eina nikijokiki nanu, kake intabai ake ena naata to ltau, inchooki ake ninye nanu ena tito metaa enkitok ai.”

English: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister:
Masaai: Newaliki ilayiok le Yakobo Shekem tenebo papaai lenye Hamor te nkeleekisho enkaraki nainyala enkanashe enye Dina.

English: And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us:
Masaai: Etiakita ninche ninche, “Mikiindim iyiook aataas ena bae, aaisho enkanashe ang oltung'ani lememurata, amu keaku ina esulare te iyiook.

English: But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised;
Masaai: Pooki ake pee kinyorraa tiniasiasa ena: Tiniakuku ake anaa iyiook ore pooki lee linyi nemurati.

English: Then will we give our daughters unto you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
Masaai: Ina peyie kinyorraa aaisho intae intoyie ang, nikiya sii iyiook intoyie inyi, nikiparana tenebo aaku olorere obo.

English: But if ye will not hearken unto us, to be circumcised; then will we take our daughter, and we will be gone.
Masaai: Naa tinimining'ining'i iyiook ninchosho metumurati intae, neaku aikiya entito ang', nikipuo aaidur.”

English: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor's son.
Masaai: Neitiship irorei lenye Hamor olayioni lenye Shekem.

English: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob's daughter: and he was more honourable than all the house of his father.
Masaai: Neaku eitu eitoki ilo barnoti aitumutiki ina bae, amu etonyorra ninye ina tito e Yakobo. Naa ninye apa enyorri oleng aaitulus to lmarei pooki.

English: And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate of their city, and communed with the men of their city, saying,
Masaai: Metaa eshomo Hamor tenebo olayioni lenye Shekem kishomi enkanasa enye neirorie ilewa le nkanasa enye ejoki,

English: These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for the land, behold, it is large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.
Masaai: “Ore kulo tung'ana naa iltung'ana supati, enchoo etoni tena kop nikimirakino intokitin, amu ing'ura ekelala enkop oleng te ninche, emayama intoyie enye nikincho sii ninche meyama intoyie ang.

English: Only herein will the men consent unto us for to dwell with us, to be one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Masaai: Tena bae ake eidim kulo tung'ana aatonyorrai aatotoni tiatua iyiook, nikiaku olorere obo: pee emurati pooki lee tiatua iyiook anaa pee emurata ninche.

English: Shall not their cattle and their substance and every beast of theirs be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.
Masaai: Aimeaku inkishu enye, o ntokitin enye o ng'uesi enye pooki inkunaang? Ematonyorrai ake duoo ina nayieu, naa kemany ninche atua iyiook.”

English: And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.
Masaai: Ore lelo pooki oimutua kishomi enkanasa enye, etonyorraitie nena pooki naatejo Hamor o Shekem metaa etumurataki pooki lee, o pooki ooimutua kishomi eina anasa.

English: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni, aa enamuratieki neton emueyiaa, nedumunye ilayiok aare le Yakobo, Simon o Lawi oong'arie kina Dina, neya ilalema lenye aarasaki e nkanasa meyiolo, near lelo lewa pooki metuata.

English: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out.
Masaai: Near Hamor metua tenebo olayioni lenye Shekem to lalem neitayu Dina aitung'uaa enkaji e Shekem, nepuo aaing'uaa.

English: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister.
Masaai: Nedoiki ilayiok le Yakobo aar enkanasa, near iltung'ana metuata neya ntokitin te nkanasa amu einyalaki enkanashe enye.

English: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field,
Masaai: Neya intare enye o nkishu enye o sirkon lenye o pooki toki ake ninye natii atua enkanasa o naatii nkurman.

English: And all their wealth, and all their little ones, and their wives took they captive, and spoiled even all that was in the house.
Masaai: Neya pooki toki naata tipat, o nkera enye pooki tenebo inkituaak enye, o pooki toki natii atua inkajijik neibung aaisardakie ninche.

English: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yakobo Simon o Lawi, “Kiyakita nanu enyamali amu kintong'ueita nanu tiatua olorere lena kop, too Ilkanaani o Ilperesi; aikuti iltungana laainei, naa tenelo neibung'a aaitoriokino aarare nanu, naa kaamuti nanu tenebo enkaji ai pooki.”

English: And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?
Masaai: Kake etejo ninche, “Keishaakino ninye neitaa enkanashe ang e mulayoi?”

English: And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
Masaai: Nejoki Enkai Yakobo, “Tudumunye ilepa shomo Betel, nilo amany ine; nintobir teine olperere lo lasar, aitaiki Enkai ina nikimpang'aka ina kata apa peyie ilo ailany olalashe lino Esau.”

English: Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
Masaai: Metaa etiaka Yakobo Enkaji enye o lelo pooki apa ootii tenebo ninye, “Ewuangie kulie aitin oo loreren naatii atua intae, nintisinyinyi ate, nimbelekenyenye inkilani inyi;

English: And let us arise, and go up to Bethel; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
Masaai: ematudumunye aailep aapuo Betel, peyie atum aitayu teine olperere lo lasar aitaiki Enkai ina naatawalikia nanu te nkata osina, naataboitare te pooki wueji nashomo.”

English: And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and all their earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
Masaai: Ina peyie eisho Yakobo nena aitin oo loreren pooki naata, tenebo ilgiso ootii inkiyiaa enye; neisudoo Yakobo nena pooki te ntonata olchani onyaanyukie olngaboli otii embata Shekem.

English: And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
Masaai: Ore eidur ninche nedoiki enkuretisho naing'uaa Enkai inkanas naamanita ninche, metaa eitu esujaa ninche ilayiok le Yakobo.

English: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Bethel, he and all the people that were with him.
Masaai: Nelotu Yakobo Lus (aa ninye Betel), aa ninye natii enkop e Kanaan, ore ninye tenebo olorere pooki oboitare,

English: And he built there an altar, and called the place Elbethel: because there God appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
Masaai: neshet olperere lo lasar teine, nejo ine wueji El-betel, amu ine apa eibalakinye Enkai kewan ninye ina kata naisik alo aing'uaa olalashe lenye.

English: But Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Bethel under an oak: and the name of it was called Allonbachuth.
Masaai: Neye Debora enkaisiaayiani, teine nenukari te ntonata olchani onyaanyuuki olng'aboli tiabori Betel, metaa etejoki enkarna e ine Al'lonbakut.

English: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came out of Padanaram, and blessed him.
Masaai: Neitoki ake Enkai aipang'aki Yakobo aigil, ina kata pee elotu aing'uaa Padan-aram, nemayian ninye.

English: And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.
Masaai: Nejoki Enkai ninye, “Aikiji enkarna ino Yakobo; meitokini aajo enkarna ino Yakobo, kake keji Israel, enkarna ino.” Metaa eipotoki enkarna enye aajo Israel.

English: And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;
Masaai: Nejoki Enkai ninye, “Ara Enkai magilani; entoisho entoponari, epuku te iyie olorere o lorora loo loreren, nepuku ilaiguanak te iyie.

English: And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.
Masaai: Ore ina kop apa naishoo Abraham o Isaak naa kaaisho iyie, naa kaisho ina kop eishoi ino nikisuju.”

English: And God went up from him in the place where he talked with him.
Masaai: Nelo Enkai aig'uaa ninye teine neirorie ninche.

English: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he talked with him, even a pillar of stone: and he poured a drink offering thereon, and he poured oil thereon.
Masaai: Neitasheyie Yakobo eng'ape teine apa neirorie Enkai o ninye eng'ape osoit; nebukoki olasar opikuni enchumata enye, nebukoki eilata shumata enye.

English: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spake with him, Bethel.
Masaai: Metaa eishoo enkarna ine wueji neirorie Enkai ajo Betel.

English: And they journeyed from Bethel; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.
Masaai: Neitoki ninche aaidur aapuo te Betel; ore eton elakuaniki Efrat, nesaisayu Raheli, near enkop oleng.

English: And it came to pass, when she was in hard labour, that the midwife said unto her, Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.
Masaai: Ore eitanyamal emion oleng', etiaka enkaitoyioni ninye, “Miureishoyu amu itum ae ayioni.”

English: And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Benoni: but his father called him Benjamin.
Masaai: Ore ena kata edung'o tau (amu etua), neipot enkarna enye ajo Benoni; kake eipoto menye enkarna enye ajo Benchamen.

English: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
Masaai: Metaa etua Raheli, nenukari te nkoitoi epuoi Efrat, (aa ninye Betlehem),

English: And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of Rachel's grave unto this day.
Masaai: neitasheyie Yakobo eng'ape te nchumata enkurare e Raheli; naa eng'ape ina enkurare e Raheli, netii ina ng'ape o taata.

English: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar.
Masaai: Neidur Israel alo, neun olng'obor lenye te dukuya oltalet le Eder.

English: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
Masaai: Ore emanya Israel ina kop, nejing'aki Ruben aboitare Bilhah ina apiani e papaai lenye nening Israel ina bae.

English: The sons of Leah; Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun:
Masaai: Nera ina kata ilayiok le Yakobo tomon aare. Ore ilayiok le Lea naa: Ruben, (olkikau le Yakobo), o Simion, o Lawi, o Yuda, o Isaakar o Sebulon.

English: The sons of Rachel; Joseph, and Benjamin:
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Raheli naa: Yosef o Benchamen.

English: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid; Dan, and Naphtali:
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Bilhah enkaisiaayiani e Raheli naa: Dan o Naftali.

English: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid; Gad, and Asher: these are the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Padanaram.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Silpa enkaisiaayiani e Lea naa Gad o Asheri. Kulo apa ilayiok le Yakobo ootoikioki ninye te Padan-aram.

English: And Jacob came unto Isaac his father unto Mamre, unto the city of Arbah, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
Masaai: Nelotu Yakobo enetii Isaak papaai lenye te wueji neji Mamre, aashu Kiriat-tarba (aa ninye taa eji Hebron), ine apa etamanya Abraham o Isaak.

English: And the days of Isaac were an hundred and fourscore years.
Masaai: Etabaitie ina kata inkolong'i e Isaak ilarin iip o ntomoni isiet.

English: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
Masaai: Neye ninye, nelo eneiturrurrorre iltung'ana lenyena apa ootuata, etaa oltung'ani moruo oiputakinote nkolong'i, ore ilayiok lenyena Esau o Yakobo nenukaa ninye.

English: Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ile ishoi e Esau (aa ninye Edom),

English: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
Masaai: etasayia Esau inkituaak enyena too lkanaani; Ada entito e Elon oo Lhiti, o Oholibama entito e Akna olayioni le Sibeon loo Lhifi,

English: And Bashemath Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebajoth.
Masaai: o Basemat entito e Ishmael enkanashe e Nebaiot.

English: And Adah bare to Esau Eliphaz; and Bashemath bare Reuel;
Masaai: Neiki Adah Esau, Elifas; neiu Basemat Reul;

English: And Aholibamah bare Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: these are the sons of Esau, which were born unto him in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: neiu Oholibama Yeush o Yalam o Kora. Kulo ninche Ilayiok le Esau ootoikioki ninye te nkop e Kanaan.

English: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance, which he had got in the land of Canaan; and went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob.
Masaai: Neya Esau inkituaak enyena o layiok lenyena, o ntoyie enyena o ltung'ana pooki lo lmarei lenye, o nkishu enyena, o ng'uesi pooki enyena, o ntokitin enyena pooki e tipat naanoto te nkop e Kanaan; nelo enkop nalakua alam olalashe lenye Yakobo.

English: For their riches were more than that they might dwell together; and the land wherein they were strangers could not bear them because of their cattle.
Masaai: Amu ore imasaa enye naa aikumok apa oleng nemeidim aatamany nebo; ore enkop apa naidurrakita ninche meekure eishaa tenkaraki enkumoi oo nkishu enye.

English: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo Esau amany enkop oo ldoinyo e Seir. Esau aa ninye Edom.

English: And these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir:
Masaai: Kulo ninche ile ishoi e Esau menye loo le Edom teina kop ooldoinyo e Seir.

English: These are the names of Esau's sons; Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, Reuel the son of Bashemath the wife of Esau.
Masaai: Kuna ninche inkarn oo layiok le Esau: Elifas olayioni le Ada enkitok e Esau, Reul olayioni le Basement enkitok e Esau,

English: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
Masaai: ore ilayiok le Elisfas naa Teman, o Omar, o Sefo, o Gatam o Kenas

English: And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau's son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau's wife.
Masaai: (ore apa Timna naa enkapiani e Elifas, olayioni le Esau; neiki Elidas Amalek. Kulo ilayiok le Ada, enkitok e Esau.

English: And these are the sons of Reuel; Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these were the sons of Bashemath Esau's wife.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Reul: Nahat, o Sera, o Shamma, o Misa, kulo ninche ilayiok le Basemat, enkitok e Esau.

English: And these were the sons of Aholibamah, the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon, Esau's wife: and she bare to Esau Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Oholibama entito e Ana olayioni le Sibeon, enkitok e Esau: Etoikio ninche Esau Yeush, o Yalam o Kora.

English: These were dukes of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn son of Esau; duke Teman, duke Omar, duke Zepho, duke Kenaz,
Masaai: Kulo ilarikok loo layiok le Esau. Ilayiok le Elifas olkikau le Esau: ilarikok ooji Teman, o Omar, o Sefo,

English: Duke Korah, duke Gatam, and duke Amalek: these are the dukes that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these were the sons of Adah.
Masaai: o Kenas, o Kora, o Gatam o Amalek; kulo ilarikok le Elifas te nkop e Edom; Naa ilayiok le Ada.

English: And these are the sons of Reuel Esau's son; duke Nahath, duke Zerah, duke Shammah, duke Mizzah: these are the dukes that came of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Bashemath Esau's wife.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Reul olayioni le Esau; ore ilarikok naa Natan, o Sera, o Shama, o Misa; kulo ninche ilarikok le Reul te nkop e Edom; naa ninche ilayiok le Basement, enkitok e Esau.

English: And these are the sons of Aholibamah Esau's wife; duke Jeush, duke Jaalam, duke Korah: these were the dukes that came of Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau's wife.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Oholibama, enkitok e Esau: ilarikok le Yeush, o Yalam o Kora; lelo ilarikok ootoikioki Oholibama entito e Ana, enkitok e Esau.

English: These are the sons of Esau, who is Edom, and these are their dukes.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Esau (aa ninye Edom) naa kulo ilarikok lenye.

English: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Seir loo le Hori iloopeny enkop: Lotan, o Shobal, o Sibeon, o Ana,

English: And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
Masaai: o Dishon, o Eser, o Sisham; kulo apa ilarikok lo Lhori ilayiok le Seir te nkop e Edom.

English: And the children of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
Masaai: Ore apa ilayiok le Lotan naa Hori, o Heman; ore apa enkanashe e Lotan naa Timna.

English: And the children of Shobal were these; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
Masaai: Kulo ilayiok le Shobal: Alfan, o Manahat, o Ebal, o Shefo o Onom.

English: And these are the children of Zibeon; both Ajah, and Anah: this was that Anah that found the mules in the wilderness, as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Sibeon: Ayia, o Ana, Ana apa ilo onoto inchorroi nairowua tiong'ota, eirrita isirkon le Sibeon papaai lenye.

English: And the children of Anah were these; Dishon, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah.
Masaai: Kuna ninche inkera e Ana, Dishon o Oholibama entito e Ana.

English: And these are the children of Dishon; Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Dishon: Hemdan, o Eshban, o Itran o Keran.

English: The children of Ezer are these; Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Eser; o Bilham, o Saafan o Akan.

English: The children of Dishan are these; Uz, and Aran.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilayiok le Dishan: Usi o Aran.

English: These are the dukes that came of the Horites; duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah,
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilarikok le Hori: ore lelo arikok naa Lotan, o Shobal, o Sibeon o Ana,

English: Duke Dishon, duke Ezer, duke Dishan: these are the dukes that came of Hori, among their dukes in the land of Seir.
Masaai: o Dishon, o Eser, o Dishan: kulo ninche ilarikok le Hori te risioroto oo ilgilat lenye te nkop e Seir.

English: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
Masaai: Kulo ninche ilaiguanak apa oitoreisho te nkop e Edom, eton eitu etumi hoo likae aiguanani oitoreisho too Siraeli.

English: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Masaai: Eitoria Bela olayioni le Beori enkop e Edom, neji enkarna enkanasa enye Dinhaban.

English: And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Neye Bela, neitoreisho Yobab olayioni le sera le Bosra te rishata enye.

English: And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Neye Yobab neitoreisho Husham le nkop e Ltemani te rishata enye.

English: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.
Masaai: Neye Husham neitoreisho Hadad olayioni le Bedad, laa ninye apa otimira ile Midian te nkop e Moab te rishata enye, neji enkarna e nkanasa enye Afiti.

English: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Neye Hadad, neitoreisho Samla le Masreka te rishata enye.

English: And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Neye Samla, neitoreisho Shaul le Rehobot to lkeju le Frati te rishata enye.

English: And Saul died, and Baalhanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Neye Shaul, neitoreisho Baalhanan olayioni le Akbor te rishata enye.

English: And Baalhanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
Masaai: Neye Baalhanan olayioni le Akbor neitoreisho Hadar te rishata enye, ore enkarna e nkanasa enye neji Pau; neji apa enkarna enkitok enye Mehetabel, ina tito e Matred, entito e Mesahab.

English: And these are the names of the dukes that came of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names; duke Timnah, duke Alvah, duke Jetheth,
Masaai: Kuna ninche inkarn oo larikok Le Esau, te risioroto oo ilmareita lenye o manyishoritin enye anaa enatiu inkarn enye; ore ilarikok naa Timna, o Alifa o Yelet,

English: Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,
Masaai: o Oholibama, o Ela, o Pinon,

English: Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar,
Masaai: o Kenas, o Tenan, o Mibsar,

English: Duke Magdiel, duke Iram: these be the dukes of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession: he is Esau the father of the Edomites.
Masaai: o Magdiel, o Imran. Kulo ninche ilarikok le Edom (aa ninye eji Esau, menye le Edom), te risioroto oo manyishoritin enye teina kop nataa enenye.

English: And Jacob dwelt in the land wherein his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: Nebik Yakobo teina kop apa naidurraka papaai lenyena te ina kop e Kanaan.

English: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives: and Joseph brought unto his father their evil report.
Masaai: Ena enkatini o lmarei le Yakobo. Ore aa oloo larin tomon oopishana Yosef, neirritita apa intare tenebo ilalashera lenyena; ore apa aa enkayioni ninye netii apa tenebo ilayiok le Bilha o Silpa nena kituaak e Papaai lenye, neyaki Yosef papaai lenye ilomon torrok ooipirta ilalashera lenyena.

English: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
Masaai: Kenyor apa Israel Yosef oleng aitalang inkera enyena pooki, amu etoikioki ninye etaa kitok oleng, neitobiraki ninye olkila oodo loo inkaik adoru.

English: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol ilalashera lenyena aajo kenyor menye ninye aitalang ilalashera lenyena pooki, neibayu ninche ninye oleng, neaku meyieu neirorie ninye te supatisho.

English: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.
Masaai: Netum Yosef enkidetidet, ore peyie eliki ilalashera lenyena neibayu ninche ninye oleng'.

English: And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Entoning ena kidetidet naidetidetua.

English: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.
Masaai: Ng'ura, kigira iyiook aaen irridat le enkano tiatua enkurma naa ng'ura, ore orridati lai etudumunye aitashe, aitoriori naa ng'ura, ore irridat linyi pooki eetuo pooki aiturrurrokino aaman ninye, neirrugokino pooki orridati lai.”

English: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.
Masaai: Nejoki ilalashera lenyena ninye, “Kesipa iyaku oloitore iyiook? Arashu iyaku oloota enkitoo te iyiook pooki?” Neaku eibaitie ninche ninye oleng too nkidetidetat enyena o too rorei lenyena.

English: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
Masaai: Neitoki ake atum ae kidetidet, neliki ilalashera lenyena nejo, “Ng'ura anyaaka aidetidet ae kidetidet; naa ng'ura, ore enkolong o lapa o lakir tomon oobo neaku kaapuonu aairrugokino.”

English: And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?
Masaai: Kake ore ake peyie eliki menye neliki sii ilalashera eisikong'a menye nejoki ninye, “Kainyoo doi ena kidetidet nindetidetu? Metaa kaalotu nanu tenebo yieyioo lino o lalashera linono aairrugo aabaiki enkop te dukuya iyie?”

English: And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
Masaai: Netum ilalashera lenyena olom te nkaraki ninye, kake etushuma menye ina kiroroto to ltau.

English: And his brethren went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.
Masaai: Nedumunye ilalashera lenyena aapuo airrita intare e menye te mbata e Shekem.

English: And Israel said unto Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed the flock in Shechem? come, and I will send thee unto them. And he said to him, Here am I.
Masaai: Nejoki Israel Yosef, “Aimegira ilalashera linono aairrita intare te Shekem? Wou maairriwai enetii ninche.” Nejoki Yosef ninye, “Nele nanu.” Ina peyie ejoki ninye,

English: And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see whether it be well with thy brethren, and well with the flocks; and bring me word again. So he sent him out of the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
Masaai: “Shomo tena kata taleenoi tenaa keserian ilalashera linono, o ntare, nikintoki ayaki olomoni.” Neaku eirriwayie ninye to erata le Hebron, nelo Shekem.

English: And a certain man found him, and, behold, he was wandering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
Masaai: Neinepu oltung'ani ninye egira alilita too nkong'at; neikilikuan ilo tung'ani ninye ajoki, “Ainyoo doi ing'oru?”

English: And he said, I seek my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they feed their flocks.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Agira aing'oru ilalashera laainei, tolikioki sii ake aatasayia, kaji doi etii aairritayie intare.”

English: And the man said, They are departed hence; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo tung'ani, “Eshomo aaidurraki dikae, amu atoning'o ninche ejo, ‘Maape Dotan.’ ” Metaa eshomo Yosef asujaa ilalashera lenyena, netum ninche te Dotan.

English: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.
Masaai: Nedolu ninche ninye elakua ore eton eitu elotu anyikaki ninche, neinos ninche enkiguana peyie ear ninye metua.

English: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
Masaai: Nejokino maate, “Nelido oloshi aidetidetani olotu.

English: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
Masaai: Wootu taata, emataar ninye metua nikinang'aki ninye engumoto nabo te kuna, nikipuo aajo eng'ues entim ninye nainosa ninye, nikianyu aadol enaaku inkidetidetat enyena.”

English: And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.
Masaai: Kake ore peyie ening Ruben ina, neitajeu ninye too nkaik enye nejoki, “Mikiar ninye metua.”

English: And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.
Masaai: Nejoki Ruben ninche, “Emimbukoo osarge; entanang'aki ninye atua ena gumoto tene tiong'ota, kake eminteleiki ninye enkaina aar metua,” peyie etum aitajeu ninye aitung'ai enkaina enye, arrinyoki ninye papaai lenye.

English: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him;
Masaai: Metaa ore peyie elotu Yosef enetii ilalashera lenyena, neng'as aaoru ninye olkila lenye, ilo kila oodo oota inkaik adoru oishopito;

English: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.
Masaai: neya ninye aanang'aki eng'umoto, ore ina gumoto nemetii toki, metii enkare atua.

English: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.
Masaai: Netoni ninche te nkop aanya endaa, nejo mataraposhu nkonyek enye nedol encholiek oolamirak le Ishmael epuonu aaing'uaa Gilead, ereuta intamesin enye, enapita neeta intokitin naaji ubani*, o Seu*, o emanoo etii enkoitoi edoyio aapuo Misiri.

English: And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yuda ilalashera lenyena, “Ainyoo taa doi kitum tinikiar olalashe lang metua, nikituroo osarge lenye?

English: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.
Masaai: Wootu, ematimir ninye aamiraki kulo tungana le Ishmael, nimikincho inkaik ang ebaiki ninye, amu olalashe lang ninye, olo sarge lang.” Nenyorraa ilalashera ina natejo.

English: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
Masaai: Ore peyie epuonu ilbiasharani le Midian aaim ine: neyietu Yosef aaitayu te ng'umoto, nemiraki ninye lelo tungana le Ishmael te shekeli tikitam e nkosholai; neya ninche Yosef Misiri.

English: And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.
Masaai: Ore pee eshukunye Ruben enaduoo gumoto nedol ajo meekure etii ine, nepolos inkilani enyena tosina sapuk,

English: And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, whither shall I go?
Masaai: nerrinyo enetii ilalashera lenyena nejoki: “Metii enkayioni ine kaji taata alo nanu?”

English: And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood;
Masaai: Neya olkila le Yosef, neyieng enkine, neitadoiki ilo kila osarge.

English: And they sent the coat of many colours, and they brought it to their father; and said, This have we found: know now whether it be thy son's coat or no.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ilo kila adoru inkaik meyakini menye, nejo, “Nele olkila likinotito, ng'ura sii iyie tujurru tenaa kolkila lo layioni lino anaa aimeninye.”

English: And he knew it, and said, It is my son's coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.
Masaai: Neyiolou nabo kata ninye, nejo, “Olkila lo layioni lai; einosa eng'ues entim ninye; maing'ash tukul ajo etumuta Yosef ing'uesi.”

English: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
Masaai: Nepolos Yakobo inkilani enyena to sina nerreten olkuniyia te mpolos enye. Neishiraki olayioni lenye inkolong'i kumok.

English: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.
Masaai: Neinyototo ilayiok pooki lenyena tenebo intoyie enyena pooki aaibung ninye aitagol; kake etanya ninye tukul eitagoli, nejo, “A-a ekalo abori enemeneng'a enetii olayioni lai, aishirita.” Metaa eishiraka menye ninye oleng.

English: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh's, and captain of the guard.
Masaai: Ore ina rishata eidipa Ilmidian aatimir ninye te Misiri aamiraki Potifa, obo loo laitoriak le Farao, aa ninye olkitok loo larripok le wueji netii Farao.

English: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
Masaai: Ore te nena olong'i, etadoyie Yuda alo aing'uaa ilalashera nelo aitaa elatia oltung'ani obo le Adullam oji enkarna enye Hira.

English: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her.
Masaai: Ore etii ine nedol Yuda entito e likae tung'ani loo Lkanaan neji enkarna enye Shua; neyam ninye nelo aboitare.

English: And she conceived, and bare a son; and he called his name Er.
Masaai: Neiroshiu neiu enkayioni, nedung'oki ninye enkarna ajo Eri.

English: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and she called his name Onan.
Masaai: Neitoki ake anutayu neiu enkayioni, nedungoki ninye enkarna enye ajo Onan.

English: And she yet again conceived, and bare a son; and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bare him.
Masaai: Neitoki ake aigil aiu enkayioni, neisho ng'otonye enkarna enye ajo Shela. Naa Kesib apa etii peyie eiu Shela.

English: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
Masaai: Neyamaki Yuda olayioni lenye kikau Eri enkitok, naji enkarna enye Tamar.

English: And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him.
Masaai: Kake ore apa ilo kikau lenye oji Eri, naa oltung'ani apa arruoni oleng te dukuya Olaitoriani; near Olaitoriani ninye metua.

English: And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yuda Onan, “Shomo tijing'aki ina kitok oliai o lalashe lino tayiolo ninye, pee etum olalashe lino nkera te iyie.”

English: And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.
Masaai: Kake eyiolo Onan ajo ore inkera naaiu nemeaku inenyena, neaku ore ake peyie elo ayiolou enkitok olalashe lenye, nebukoki enkare e le waisho enkop pee meisho ake inkera olalashe lenye.

English: And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also.
Masaai: Ore ina nataasa, eitu katukul eitiship Olaitoriani, near sii ninye metua.

English: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter in law, Remain a widow at thy father's house, till Shelah my son be grown: for he said, Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren did. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yuda Tamar ina kitok o layioni lenye. “Totona ira enkoliai te nkaji e papaai lino, o metaba anaa nebulu olayioni lai Shela.” Amu etureishe ajo keidim sii ninye atua anaa ilalashera lenyena. Metaa eshomo Tamar enkaji e menye.

English: And in process of time the daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheepshearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
Masaai: Ore etulusoyie enkiti rishata neye enkitok e Yuda, entito e Shua. Ore peyie eitagoli Yuda, nelo ninye tenebo olchore lenye Hira le Adulam ewueji neji Timna, ewueji negirae aabarnie intare enyena.

English: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold thy father in law goeth up to Timnath to shear his sheep.
Masaai: Ore peyie elikini Tamar aajoki, “Ekeloito olaputani lino Timna abarn intare enyena.”

English: And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.
Masaai: Neitayu to sesen lenye inkilani enyena e nkoliai, nepika enkarasha aitoipie elukunya enye peyie medoli enkomom, nelotu aton te kishomi e Enaim, natii enkoitoi nalala nalo Timna; amu etodua ajo etubulua Shela, neitu eishori ninye meyama.

English: When Judah saw her, he thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Yuda ninye, nedamu ninye ejo inoshi kituaak naibor onyek, amu eitoipo ninye enkomom enye.

English: And he turned unto her by the way, and said, Go to, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee; (for he knew not that she was his daughter in law.) And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?
Masaai: Nelo ninye enetii te mbata enkoitoi nalala nejoki ninye, “Wou inchooki maatayiolo,” amu eitu eyiolou ninye ajo entito olayioni lenye. Nejo ninye, “Ainyoo naa kincho peyie kitum atayiolo?”

English: And he said, I will send thee a kid from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?
Masaai: Newal ajo, “Ekaairriwaki olkuoo too ntare aainei.” Nejo Tamar, “Amaa aikincho entoki ino naibung naarreshunye o terewakaki ilo kuo?”

English: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
Masaai: Nejo, “Ainyoo iyieu naaisho?” Newal ajo, “Inchooki olgisoi lino o enkeene ino, o ina ng'udi ino nimbung'ita te nkaina ino.” Neaku eishooyie ninye ninche nelo ayiolou ninye neiroshiu ninye.

English: And she arose, and went away, and laid by her vail from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
Masaai: Neinyototo alo; neitayu enkarasha te nkomom neishop inkilani enyena e nkolia.

English: And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive his pledge from the woman's hand: but he found her not.
Masaai: Ore peyie eirriu Yuda olkuoo eyau olchore lenye le Adullam, peyie etum enaduoo kitok aishoru intokitin naata e Yuda nelotu alau ninye te naduoo wueji.

English: Then he asked the men of that place, saying, Where is the harlot, that was openly by the way side? And they said, There was no harlot in this place.
Masaai: Neikilikuan ninye iltung'ana ootii ine ajoki, “Koree ake enkitok mulayoi natii naaji embata enkoitoi nalala e Naim aton?” Nejo ninche, “Meetae emulayoi natii ene.”

English: And he returned to Judah, and said, I cannot find her; and also the men of the place said, that there was no harlot in this place.
Masaai: Neaku etushukokine Yuda nejoki, “Eitu alo atum, netejo sii iltung'ana le ine, ‘Metii emulayoi natii ine.’ ”

English: And Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
Masaai: Newal Yuda ajo, “Inchoo ninye eya nena tokitin aitaa inenyena, peyie mekueniyieki ake iyiook; idol ajo airriwaka ele kuo, neitu ilo ainepu ninye.”

English: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.
Masaai: Ore peyie eishunye ilapaitin okuni, nelikini Yuda aajoki, “Ore Tamar enkitok o layioni lino, etaa emulayoi, ore ake sii eiroishi te nkerai e mulayaisho.” Nejo Yuda, “Entoriku entupuku boo peyie kipuo aapejoo ninye.”

English: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff.
Masaai: Ore eitupukuni boo, neirriwaa olkilikuai airriwaki olaputani lenye ejo, “Olopeny kuna tokitin anotie enkerai.” Nejo, “Ing'ura tujurru, aatasayia, ainkuneng'ae, kuna tokitin o lgisoi, o enkeene, o eng'udi.”

English: And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
Masaai: Nenyorraa Yuda ninche nejo, “Aisinyati ninye peyie aalang, anaa keitu apa aitabaya ororei lai aisho ninye olayioni lai Shela meyama.” Neitu eitoki aikata ayiolou ninye.

English: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.
Masaai: Ore peyie ebau enkata najing aji neiu ilmao te ishoi.

English: And it came to pass, when she travailed, that the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
Masaai: Ore earita enkop, neitayu obo enkaina aitupuku neng'amaa enkaitoiyioni neeniki ina aina enkopito pile, ejoito, “Ele otang'asunye.”

English: And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, How hast thou broken forth? this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.
Masaai: Kake ore erriny enkaina enye, ng'ura, nepuku olalashe, nejo enkaitoiyioni, “Metaa inji doi inkununye tinipuku!” Nedungokini ninye enkarna enye aajo Peres.

English: And afterward came out his brother, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name was called Zarah.
Masaai: Ore te siadi nepuku olalashe lenye eeta enaduoo opito pile eenikino enkaina enye; neipoti enkarna enye aajo Serah.

English: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.
Masaai: Ewaki apa ina kata Yosef Misiri, ore Potifa laa obo loo lkituaak le Farao, olkitok le rripore, naa olmisiri sii, einyiang'ua Potifa ninye too ltung'ana le Ishmael laa ninche ooyautua ninye ina kop.

English: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
Masaai: Etii apa Olaitoriani tenebo Yosef, neaku oltung'ani otudupe oleng', netii enkaji olkitok lenye ilo Misiri,

English: And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
Masaai: nedol olkitok lenye ajo etii Olaitoriani tenebo ninye, ore pooki naata neisho Olaitoriani metubula too nkaik enyena.

English: And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
Masaai: Metaa enoto Yosef omom too nkonyek enyena, neisho ninye metaa oloitasheikinoni le nkaji enye pooki neaku ninye oitore pooki toki naata.

English: And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the LORD was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
Masaai: Ore ebaiki ina kata neitaa ninye olaitasheikinoni le nkaji enye o pooki toki naata etamayiana Olaitoriani enkaji e ilo Misiri tenkaraki Yosef, ore emayianata Enkai nejing pooki toki naata, tiaji o te nkurma.

English: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.
Masaai: Metaa etungueikia apa pooki naata metaa Yosef oitasheiki; neaku ore eeta ninye, eitu eitoki anyamaliki ae toki meteleku endaa ake nanya ninye. Ore apa Yosef naa oltung'ani sidai te nking'urata.

English: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
Masaai: Ore etulusoyie enkata, nekurraki enkitok olkitok lenye inkonyek enyena ang'uar Yosef, nejoki, “Irraga tenebo nanu.”

English: But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
Masaai: Kake etanya ninye nejoki enkitok olkitok lenye, “Ing'ura, ore atii ene meekure enyamalaki olkitok lai ae toki tena aji, netipika pooki toki naata atua enkaina ai;

English: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
Masaai: Meekure aa kitok tena aji pee aalang nanu; nemeeta hoo ae toki naatirishie nanu meteleku iyie ake, amu ira iyie enkitok enye; kaji taa pasa aiko peyie aas enkarrueisho naba inji, naas eng'oki te dukuya Enkai?”

English: And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
Masaai: Ore hoo duoo ninye neirorie Yosef anaake neitu ening Yosef ninye, peyie eirrag tenebo ninye, arashu eisiritore ninye.

English: And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
Masaai: Kake ore nabo olong', eshomo Yosef atua enkaji aas esiaai enye nemeetae likae lee otii atua aji,

English: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
Masaai: neibung enkila enye ejoki, “Irraga tenebo nanu.” Kake etung'uayie ninye enkila enye te nkaina enye, neilanyisho aisik aipang te nkaji.

English: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,
Masaai: Ore peyie edol ina kitok ajo etung'uayie enkila enye te nkaina enye eibung'ita, neisik alo aing'uaa enkaji,

English: That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
Masaai: neipot ilewa le nkaji enye nejoki ninche, “Eng'ura, eyaka ninye iyiook Iheburaniai meeu amor iyiook; aaewuo ajing'aki ajo aboitare, naishir oleng to ltoilo sapuk;

English: And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and got him out.
Masaai: ore peyie ening ajo ailepie oltoilo lai aishir oleng', neing'uaa enkila enye te nkaina ai neilanyisho aipirri aipung boo.”

English: And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
Masaai: Neirragie ninye ina kila enye tembata enye o meeu olkitok lenye ang'.

English: And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
Masaai: Neliki ninye ina bae ake ajoki, “Ore ilo sinka loo Lhebrania, ilo liyaua atua iyiook, aaewuo ajing'aki amor;

English: And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled out.
Masaai: kake ore ake peyie ailepie oltoilo lai aishir, neing'uaa enkila enye aata neilanyisho aisik apuku te nkaji.”

English: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
Masaai: Ore peyie ening olkitok lenye lelo rorei o oiroro enkitok enye, “Neijia aaikuna osinka lino.” Neiyupuyup engoro enye.

English: And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
Masaai: Neya olkitok le Yosef ninye apik korokoroni, ine wueji nepiki ilmapuusuni lo laiguanani. Nepiki ninye korokoroni.

English: But the LORD was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
Masaai: Kake etii apa Olaitoriani tenebo Yosef neitodol ninye enyorrata nauno, neisho ninye omom too nkonyek olaitasheikinoni le korokoroni.

English: And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.
Masaai: Ore ilo aitasheikinoni, nepik Yosef aitaa ninye oitasheiki lelo pooki ooikenoro te korokoroni neaku ore pooki naasi naa ninye oas.

English: The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the LORD was with him, and that which he did, the LORD made it to prosper.
Masaai: Ore ilo kitok le korokoroni eitu eitoki aitanyamaluo te pooki toki natipika inkaik e Yosef, amu etii Olaitoriani tenebo ninye; neaku ore pooki nataasa, neisho Olaitoriani meitobirari.

English: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.
Masaai: Ore etulusoyie enkata, neyooki olaitasheikinoni le naisho oo sabibu lo laiguanani le Misiri tenebo olapejoni loo mukateni o laiguanani, aaitagor olkitok lenye ilo aiguanani le Misiri.

English: And Pharaoh was wroth against two of his officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.
Masaai: Negoro Farao te nkaraki lelo aitasheikinok lenyena pokira, olaitasheikimoni kitok le naisho oo sabibu tenebo olapejoni kitok loo mukateni.

English: And he put them in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
Masaai: Nepik ninche enkaji narripieki iltung'ana arruok natii enkaji olkitok le rripore, teina korokoroni naikenorieki Yosef.

English: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he served them: and they continued a season in ward.
Masaai: Ore ilo kitok le rripore neitanap Yosef meing'ura, neisaiai ninche. Netoni inkolong'i naaikash teina aji oo larruok.

English: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.
Masaai: Ore enkewarie nabo, eidetideta pokira, olaitasheikinoni kitok le naisho oo sabibu tenebo olapejoni loo mukateni lo lkitok le Misiri, eikenoro te Korokoroni. Meeta ake oleitu eidetidet enkidetidet enye, nemeeta ake enkidetidet nemeeta enautu.

English: And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they were sad.
Masaai: Ore peyie eyooki Yosef ninche enasirie, nedol ninche, nenyorriki ajo kenyamal oleng pokira.

English: And he asked Pharaoh's officers that were with him in the ward of his lord's house, saying, Wherefore look ye so sadly to day?
Masaai: Neaku eikilikuana ilaitasheikinok le Farao ootii tenebo te nkaji naenishoreki te enkaji olkitok lenye ajoki, “Ainyoo doi anaaijo kesoto taata intae inkomomi?”

English: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “Kindetideta duo, nemeeta hoo oltung'ani oidim aibelekenyaki iyiook atoliki aibalakinye.” Nejoki Yosef ninche, “Amaa doi enkibelekenyata aime ene Nkai? Entolikioki atasayia intae.”

English: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;
Masaai: Ore ilo aitasheikinoni kitok le naisho oo sabibu, neliki Yosef enkidetidet enye nejoki ninye, “Ore te nkidetidet ai etii duoo o sabibu dukuya nanu,

English: And in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:
Masaai: ore te nchumata eilo sabibu, etii ilng'osil okuni; ore ake peyie eitapuku, nelioyu esidano enye, neku enkimarrati aaku osabibu.

English: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
Masaai: Netii duoo enkikompe e Farao enkaina ai, naitayu ilng'anayio loo sabibu, naironyaki enkare enye ina kikompe, napik ina kikompe e Farao inkaik e Farao.”

English: And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days:
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yosef ninye, “Ena enkibelekenyata ena kidetidet: ore ilng'osil okuni naa inkolong'i uni,

English: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.
Masaai: ore too nkolong'i uni naa aikidumu Farao endukuya ino nikinyaaki esiaai ino, neaku aipikaki Farao enkaina enye enkikompe enye anaa apake te dukuya aa olaitasheikinoni le naisho oo sabibu.

English: But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
Masaai: Kake tadamuaki tenilo nitum eseriani, nikintaas sii nanu esupatisho peyie kimbalie sii nanu te dukuya Farao, pee kintayu nanu tena aji.

English: For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
Masaai: Amu kesipa tukul ajo kapurruno te nkop oo Lhebrania; ore sii tene natii maata enataasa peyie aatipikaki atua ewueji e korokoroni.”

English: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head:
Masaai: Ore peyie edol olapejoni loo mukateni ajo ore enkibelekenyata naibelekenya Yosef ajo ekening'unoyu, etiaka sii ninye Yosef “Aidetideta sii nanu, etii nkikapuni uni oo mukateni elukunya ai,

English: And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.
Masaai: ore enkikapu natii shumata inkulie netii indaiki oo mpukunot pooki naapejuno e Farao, neinosita imotonyi nena daiki naatii enkikapu natii endukuya ai.”

English: And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three days:
Masaai: Newal Yosef ajoki, “Ena enkibelekenyata enye: Ore inkikapuni uni naa inkolong'i uni;

English: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
Masaai: ore too nkolong'i uni, naa kedumu Farao endukuya ino nikintung'uaa iyie! nikilili iyie to lchani, ore imotonyi naa keinos inkiri osesen lino.”

English: And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni, aa enkolong apa natoinyieki Farao, neitaiki ilaisiaayiak lenyena pooki o sirua nedumu endukuya olaitookoni kitok tenebo endukuya olayierani kitok tiatua ilaisiaayiak lenyena.

English: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand:
Masaai: Neshukoki olaitasheikinoni kitok le naisho oo sabibu, nepik enkikompe inkaik e Farao,

English: But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
Masaai: kake eililio ilo apejoni kitok loo mukateni, anaa enatolikio apa Yosef ninche.

English: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
Masaai: Ore ake eyia, eitu edamu ilo kitok le naisho oo sabibu Yosef, etorikine ninye.

English: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.
Masaai: Ore peyie eishunye ilarin oare oolulung'a, neidetidet Farao enkidetidet natoduaa kewan eitashe te mbata olkeju le Nail.

English: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura etupukutuo aailepu to lkeju le Nail inkishu naapishana sidain naapir, nenya ilo alaa otii embata olkeju.

English: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, eetuo kulie kishu naapishana sasin, naaikinyoot aailepu to lkeju le Nail aasuju ninche, neitashe te mbata oo nkulie te nkiyopata olkeju le Nail.
