English: And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.
Masaai: Ore nena kishu sasin naaikinyoot, einosa nena kishu sidain naapir. Neputunye Farao te nkidetidet.

English: And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good.
Masaai: Neitoki airora neitoki aidetidet eniare; naa ng'ura, ilkiyiaa oopishana loo lpaek oopir naa sidain ebulu to lpaeki obo.

English: And, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.
Masaai: Ng'ura ore ake peyie eitalioo inkiyiaa pokira naapishana, neitoki kulie kiyiaa naapishana aaliooyu naa sasin naaitoiyito enkijape naing'uaa enkalo oloosaen.

English: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.
Masaai: Ore lelo kiyiaa sasin le ntapa etoijoitie ilkiyiaa oopishana sidain oopir. Neputunye Farao, naa ng'ura enkidetidet duoo ake ina.

English: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.
Masaai: Metaa ore peyie ekenyu etanyamala oleng to oltau lenye; neirriwaa olkilikuai meipoti ilasakutok o ltung'ana le Misiri o olang'eni pooki; neliki Farao ninche ina kidetidet enye pooki, neitu etumi obo te ninche oidim aibelekenya ina kidetidet aliki Farao.

English: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
Masaai: Nejoki olaitasheikinoni kitok le naisho oo sabibu e Farao, “Atadamua taata inkitarruorrot aainei.

English: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in ward in the captain of the guard's house, both me and the chief baker:
Masaai: Ore apa peyie egorokino Farao ilaisiaayiak lenyena, naapik nanu tenebo olapejoni kitok loomukateni enkaji narripieki iltung'ana arruok natii enkaji olkitok le rripore,

English: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
Masaai: nikindetidet pokira ina kewarie, ore iyiook pokira meeta oleitu eidetidet enkidetidet enye naata e utunoto enye.

English: And there was there with us a young man, an Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.
Masaai: Netii apa oloti barnoti loo Lhebrania oboitare iyiook teine, olaisiaayiani lo lkitok le rripore, ore peyie kiliki ninye nena kidetidetat eibelekenyaka iyiook ninche, eisho ake enkipirta enkidetidet pooki ng'ae anaa enatiu enkidetidet enye.

English: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.
Masaai: Naa ore peyie eliki iyiook, nelotu aaku ina natolimuo, naashukokini esiaai ai, ore olapejoni kitok loo mukateni nepuoi aailili.

English: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Farao olkilikuai meipoti Yosef, neyauni ninye aaitasieku aaitung'uaa korokoroni ore peyie eidip atabarnoyu neibelekeny sii inkilani enyena nelotu atua aitashe te dukuya Farao.

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.
Masaai: Nejoki Farao Yosef, “Anoto det enkidetidet, nemeetae likae tung'ani laaidim aibelekenyaki ninye, natoning'o eji ore peyie ining enkidetidet naa indim aibelekenya.”

English: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
Masaai: Newaliki Yosef ajoki, “Ime, nanu etii ewalata keisho Enkai Farao ewalata sidai naitiship.”

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river:
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Farao Yosef, “Ng'ura, ore te nkidetdet ai, aitashe apa te nkiyopata olkeju le Nail,

English: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
Masaai: nepuonu inkishu naapishana naapir naa sidain aailepu to lkeju le Nail, nedaa aadaa tiatua olalaa,

English: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill favoured and leanfleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:
Masaai: nepuonu kulie kishu naapishana enetii, naa ore ninche naa sasin neikinyoot ineitu aikata adol te nkop e Misiri.

English: And the lean and the ill favoured kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:
Masaai: Ore nena kishu sasin naaikinyoot, neinos nena kishu e dukuya naapishana

English: And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill favoured, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
Masaai: kake ore peyie eidip ainosa ninche, meetae hoo obo otayiolo ajo einosa ninche, meetae hoo obo otayiolo ajo einosa ninche inkulie amu eton ake emueyiaa naa sasin anaa enatiu te nkiterunoto. Ina peyie aputunye.

English: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up in one stalk, full and good:
Masaai: Anyaaka ake sii te nkidetidet ai adol ilkiyiaa oopishana oobulu to lpaeki, obo oobore naa sidain.

English: And, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:
Masaai: Ore kulie kiyiaa naapishana, netoito, naa sasin, neitoi olkutati lo loo saen.

English: And the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told this unto the magicians; but there was none that could declare it to me.
Masaai: Etubulakita ninche, ore lelo kiyiaa sasin lo lpaek etoijoitie lelo kiyiaa oopishana sidan. Natolikio nanu nena kidetidetat ilasakutok kake metii hoo obo laaidima atoliki ina kidetidet.”

English: And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: God hath shewed Pharaoh what he is about to do.
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Yosef Farao, “Ore enkidetidet e Farao naa nabo; eitoduaa Enkai Farao enataa kejo pee eas.

English: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.
Masaai: Ore inkishu naapishana sidain naapir, naa ilarin oopishana, ore ilkiyaa oopishana sidain naa ilarin oopishana; ore enkidetidet naa nabo.

English: And the seven thin and ill favoured kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
Masaai: Ore inkishu sasin naaikinyoot naapishana, naaetuo aasuju ninche naa ilarin oopishana, ore ilkiyiaa lemeeta toki oopishana ooitoyio olkutati lo loo saen naa ilarin lo lameyu oopishana.

English: This is the thing which I have spoken unto Pharaoh: What God is about to do he sheweth unto Pharaoh.
Masaai: Eketiu anaa enatiaaka Farao, eitoduaa Enkai Farao enataa kejo pee eas.

English: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
Masaai: Kepuonu ilarin oopishana ootumieki endaa sapuk te nkop pooki e Misiri,

English: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
Masaai: kake ore ake peyie eishunye lelo arin, nepuonu ilarin oopishana lo lameyu sapuk, ore lelo arin pooki le ndaa sapuk nerikinisho te nkop pooki e Misiri, nemut olameyu ena kop,

English: And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine following; for it shall be very grievous.
Masaai: neaku meitokini ninye aadamu enapa naatae sapuk te nkaraki ilo ameyu osuju, amu ekeaku torrono oleng'.

English: And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
Masaai: Ore nkigilata enkidetidet e Farao, eitodolu inchere ore ina siaai naa Enkai natipika, naa keyau Enkai aitaa te nkata nemelakua.

English: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Inchoo naa tena kata Farao egelu oltung'ani oisiligayu neeta sii eng'eno neisho ninye meitasheiki enkop e Misiri.

English: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.
Masaai: Shomo dukuya tegelu ilaitashekinok tena kop niya e matua e imiet e pooki daa naiu enkop e Misiri te kulo arin oopishana le ndaa sapuk.

English: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.
Masaai: Nincho ninche metasoto endaa pooki e kulo arin sidain oopuonu, neiteng'eli ilpaek tiabori enkitoria e Farao pee eaku endaa too nkanas, nincho ninche meiteng'ela.

English: And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.
Masaai: Ekeaku ina daa enashumi te nkaraki enkop te lelo arin oopishana lo lameyu oopuonu ena kop e Misiri, pee meidak enkop teina rishata o lameyu.”

English: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
Masaai: Ore ina bae naa sidai apa oleng te Farao o too laisiaayiak lenyena pooki.

English: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?
Masaai: Nejoki Farao ilaisiaayiak lenyena, “Aikindim aanoto oltung'ani laijo ele, otii enkiyang'et e Nkai atua ninye?”

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:
Masaai: Ina peyie ejoki Farao Yosef, “Ore amu kintoduaa Enkai kuna pooki, meetae likae arriyia naa ng'en laijo iyie;

English: Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.
Masaai: iyaku olaitasheiki enkaji ai ore iltung'ana laainei pooki ekeaku ilooning ina nintanap; meteleku tolorika le nkitoo ake aaku nanu kitok te iyie.”

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Nejoki Farao Yosef, “Ng'ura ajo aaitasheyie iyie ing'ura enkop pooki e Misiri.”

English: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
Masaai: Neitayu Farao olgisoi lenye lo lmishire te nkaina enye, nepik enkaina e Yosef; neishopoki ninye ilkilani le kitani napuyiapuy, nepik olpisiai le saabu emurt enye,

English: And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: neisho ninye meshomo ekedito engarri enye e are oo mbartan, neishir ninche te dukuya ninye ejo, “Entigil kung!” Neijia eikuna apik ninye meitasheiki ina kop pooki e Misiri.

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Ore ake sii, etiaka Farao Yosef, “Ekara Farao, naa ore teneitu inchoru orusa, meetae oltung'ani odumu enkaina anaa enkeju te nkop pooki e Misiri.”

English: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Neisho Farao Yosef enkarna oo Lmisiri ajo Safenatapanea; neisho ninye meyama Asenat, ina tito e Potifera olapolosani le Oni. Metaa eshomo Yosef enkop e Misiri.

English: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Oloo larin tomoni uni apa Yosef peyie ejing enkisiaayiare e Farao olaiguanani le Misiri. Nelo Yosef aing'uaa Farao, nelo aman enkop pooki e Misiri.

English: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.
Masaai: Ore te lelo arin oopishana lo lari sapuk, enoto enkop eishoi sapuk,

English: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same.
Masaai: neiturrurru indaiki pooki oo larin oopishana eton eetae endaa sapuk te nkop e Misiri, neshum endaa pooki too nkanas, etushuma te pooki anasa ina daa naing'uaa nkurman naamanita.

English: And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.
Masaai: Neshum Yosef entapa te nkumoi naba anaa osinyai le naiposha, o metaa meekure eyiolo eneba ndaiki te nkumoi amu aimeekure etemayu.

English: And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bare unto him.
Masaai: Ore eton eitu elotu olari lo lameyu, eeta Yosef ina rishata ilayiok aare, ootoikio Asenata entito e Potifera olapolosani le Oni.

English: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For God, said he, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.
Masaai: Nedung'oki Yosef ilo kikau lenye enkarna ajo Manase, amu etejo, “Aishoo Enkai maatorikinoto ingolikinot aainei pooki, o enkaji e papaai lai pooki.”

English: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.
Masaai: Neipot enkarna oliare ajo Efraim, “Amu aitaa Enkai olotubula tena kop enyamali ai.”

English: And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.
Masaai: Nebau enkiting'oto oo larin oopishana le nkumoi;

English: And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
Masaai: neiteru ilarin oopishana lo lameyu aabau, anaa enatejo apa Yosef. Neaku olameyu sapuk too nkuapi pooki; kake ore te nkop pooki e Misiri, netii endaa ina rishata.

English: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.
Masaai: Ore peyie eishunye indaiki te nkop e Misiri to lorere, neishiraki olorere Farao meishoo endaa; nejoki Farao iltung'ana pooki le Misiri, “Enchom enetii Yosef; ore pooki najoki intae, entaas.”

English: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Metaa ore peyie eibulu olameyu ina kop pooki, nebol Yosef inkajijik naashumishoreki, nemiraki ninye Ilmisiri, amu etaa torrono olameyu oleng te nkop e Misiri.

English: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn; because that the famine was so sore in all lands.
Masaai: Ore ake sii, eetuo iloreren pooki le nkop Misiri enetii Yosef aainyiang'u ilpaek, amu aitorrono apa olameyu te nkop pooki nalulung'a.

English: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
Masaai: Ore peyie ening Yakobo ajo keetae entapa te Misiri, etiaka ilayiok lenyena, “Ainyoo doi peyie itonini aaing'ura maate tene?”

English: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.
Masaai: Nejo, “Ng'ura, atoning'o ajo keetae ilpaek te Misiri; enchom ina kop enyang'u ilpaek einyiang'aki iyiook teine, peyie kibikoo eitu kiye.”

English: And Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo ilalashera le Yosef tomon aainyiang'u ilpaek te Misiri.

English: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure mischief befall him.
Masaai: Kake eitu eirriwaa Yakobo Benchamen, olalashe le Yosef tenebo ilalashera lenyena, amu keure ajo ketum enyamali.

English: And the sons of Israel came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: Neaku eetuo apa ilayiok le Israel aainyiang'isho anaa olikae orere oetuo, amu etijing'a apa olameyu enkop e Kanaan.

English: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.
Masaai: Ore apa ina kata naa Yosef olbalusui leina kop naa ninye enkorrok apa omiraki ilpaek olorere pooki le nkop. Nepuonu ilalashera le Yosef, neirrugo ninche te dukuya ninye aaitabaiki inkomomi enye enkop.

English: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them; and he said unto them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.
Masaai: Nedol Yosef ilalashera lenyena, neyiolou ninye ninche, kake eitaasa ninye ninche anaa lomon neirorie ninche te nkisikong'ata ejoki, “Kaji doi ing'uaa?” Nejo ninche, “Enkop e Kanaan king'uaa kietuo ainyiang'u endaa.”

English: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.
Masaai: Metaa etayiolo Yosef ilalashera lenyena, kake eitu eyiolou ninche ninye.

English: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
Masaai: Nedamu Yosef inapa kidetidetat naaidetideta naipirta ninche; nejoki ninche, “Irara ilaikitalak, iyietuo aajur enchalan oo itung'ana lena kop.”

English: And they said unto him, Nay, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “A-a olkitok lang, kake kietuo ainyiang'u endaa, ina pee eetuo isinkan linono.

English: We are all one man's sons; we are true men, thy servants are no spies.
Masaai: Aikira pooki ilayiok lo lpayian obo, nikira iltung'ana ooisiligayu, ore isinkan linono neme ilaikitalak.”

English: And he said unto them, Nay, but to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “A-a, iyetuo aajur enchalan oo ltung'ana lena kop.”

English: And they said, Thy servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and, behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Ore iyiook isinkan linono, kira ilalashera tomon aare, ilayiok lo lpayian obo te nkop e Kanaan; naa ng'ura, ore oloti te iyiook eboitare ena olong papaai lang, ore obo nemeekure eetae.”

English: And Joseph said unto them, That is it that I spake unto you, saying, Ye are spies:
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yosef ninche, “Etiu taa anaa enatiaaka intae inchere irara ilaikitalak.

English: Hereby ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.
Masaai: Ore tenkaraki ina naa ketemi intae; ore te nkishui e Farao, mipuopuo aing'uaa ene wueji ometaba anaa nelotu olalashe linyi oti ene.

English: Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether there be any truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye are spies.
Masaai: Erriwai obo linyi olo ayau olalashe linyi, ore intae nianyunyu te Korokoroni pee etumi aatujur irorei linyi, tenaa ketii esipata atua intae, arashu anaa te nkishui e Farao, esipa irara ilaikitalak.”

English: And he put them all together into ward three days.
Masaai: Nepik pooki tenebo Korokoroni too nkolong'i uni.

English: And Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live; for I fear God:
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni nejoki Yosef ninche, “Entaas ena peyie inchushu, amu kaure Enkai:

English: If ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses:
Masaai: tenaa irara iltung'ana loo sipat, enchoo olalashe linyi obo eing'uari eikenoro teine neikenorieki intae, nepuo ilkulikae aaya entapa tenkaraki olameyu loo lmareita linyi,

English: But bring your youngest brother unto me; so shall your words be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.
Masaai: nikiyakiki olalashe linyi, oti; pee etumi aatonyorrai irorei linyi, nimiyeye.” Neas ninche ina.

English: And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
Masaai: Nejokino maate, “Ore taa te sipata einepua iyiook entorroni o lapa alashe lang, amu kitoduaa enyamali oltau lenye, ina kata peyie esai iyiook neitu kinining ninye katukul, neaku ena pee eewuoena nyamali atua iyiook.”

English: And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.
Masaai: Newal Ruben ajo, “Ekeitu apa ajoki intae emintaas entorrono enkayioni? Neitu kinining'ining'i. Metaa ore taata etabawua naa elaata osarge lenye.”

English: And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spake unto them by an interpreter.
Masaai: Eitu ninche eyiolou aajo etoning'o Yosef irorei lenye pooki, amu etii apa olaibelekenyani erishata enye.

English: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
Masaai: Nepuku ninye aing'uaa ninche alo aishir; neshukunye airorie ninche. Neitayu ninye Simon tiatua ninche neen ninye te dukuya ninche.

English: Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks with corn, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus did he unto them.
Masaai: Neiitanapisho Yosef meiputi ilbenia lenye te ntapa, neshukokini pooki bene impisai nayautua ninche, neishori sii endaa nainosaa te nkoitoi. Neitaasi ninche ina.

English: And they laded their asses with the corn, and departed thence.
Masaai: Neirot isirkon lenye too lpaek nedumunye aapuo.

English: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money; for, behold, it was in his sack's mouth.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo obo lenye abol olbene lenye pee eisho osikiria lenye endaa te wueji neirraga, etodua impisai enyena te nkutuk olbene lenyena;

English: And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that God hath done unto us?
Masaai: nejoki ilalashera lenye; “Aatushukokoki nanu impisai aainei, noona naatii enkutuk olbene lai!” Ore ake pee ening ina neikirikira tolkirutoto nerrinyokino maate ejokino, “Kaa bae ena naitaasa iyiook Enkai?”

English: And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell unto them; saying,
Masaai: Ore pee epuonu enetii Yakobo; papaai lenye, te nkop e Kanaan, neliki nena pooki naanoto ninche, ejoki,

English: The man, who is the lord of the land, spake roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.
Masaai: “Ore ilo tung'ani, ilo kitok leina kop, eirorie iyiook te nkisikong'ata, neiko iyiook anaa aikira ilaikitalak leina kop.

English: And we said unto him, We are true men; we are no spies:
Masaai: Kake kitiakita ninye, ‘Aikira iltung'ana ooisiligayu, mikira ilaikitalak;

English: We be twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: kira iyiook ilalashera tomon aare, ilayiok le papa lang; nemeekure eishu obo lang, ore oloti neboitare ena olong papaai te nkop e Kanaan.’

English: And the man, the lord of the country, said unto us, Hereby shall I know that ye are true men; leave one of your brethren here with me, and take food for the famine of your households, and be gone:
Masaai: Ina peyie ejo ilo tung'ani, ilo kitok leina kop ajoki iyiook, ‘Tena ayiolou ajo irara iltung'ana asipak; entunguai olalashe linyi obo entung'ueikiaki, niyaya ilpaek aayaki olorere tenkaraki olameyu lo lmareita linyi, nipuopuo aarrinyo.

English: And bring your youngest brother unto me: then shall I know that ye are no spies, but that ye are true men: so will I deliver you your brother, and ye shall traffick in the land.
Masaai: Entorikokoki, olalashe linyi oti, pee atum atayiolo ajo mirara ilaikitalak kake iltung'ana ooisiligayu, naa kalaaki intae olalashe linyi, nindimidimi aataar biashara tena kop.’ ”

English: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack: and when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.
Masaai: Ore eitayu ntokitin too lbenia lenye, ng'ura, meeta ake oltung'ani lemeeta orridati loo mpisai enyena to lbene; ore pee edol ninche tenebo menye irridat loo mpisai, neirut oleng.

English: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo papaai lenye ninche, “Kinchirie intae to sina sapuk aaiturrarrie inkera aainei: Meekure eetae Yosef, nemeekure eetae Simon, ore tena kata naa intokiki aaya Benchamen, ore kuna pooki naa inaanoto nanu.”

English: And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Reuben menye, “Taara ilayiok laainei aare metuata tenemayau ninye ashuku enitii; tipika ninye inkaik aainei naa kashuku ninye enitii.”

English: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
Masaai: Kake etejo, “Melo olayioni lai airiamarie intae, amu etua olalashe lenye, naa ninye ake taata etung'uayioki. Tenelo netum bata te nkoitoi ina kata ipuopuo, ataa nanu oltung'ani kitok oibor lukuya, ore osina likiyakiki nanu naa kaar nanu matua.”

English: And the famine was sore in the land.
Masaai: Etaa apa olameyu sapuk oleng te nkop.

English: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the corn which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.
Masaai: Ore pee emut ina tapa nayautua te Misiri, nejoki papaai lenye ninche, “Enyaaki enchom, enyang'aki iyiook enkiti daa.”

English: And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yuda ninye, “Eitanapa apa iyiook ilo tung'ani ejoki iyiook, ‘Midolidolo enkomom ai, arashu tenaa ketii olalashe linyi tenebo intae.’

English: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:
Masaai: Tinirriwaa olalashe lang tenebo iyiook, naa aikipuo ainyang'aki iyie endaa teine,

English: But if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
Masaai: kake tinimirriwaa ninye nimikipuo ine, amu etiaka apa iyiook, ilo tung'ani, ‘Midolidolo enkomom ai tukul, arashu tinirikitoto ake olalashe linyi.’ ”

English: And Israel said, Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?
Masaai: Nejo Israel, “Ainyoo doi pee kinkuna inji aitamuoi aaliki ilo tung'ani aajoki iatata likae alashe?”

English: And they said, The man asked us straitly of our state, and of our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?
Masaai: Newal aajo, “Ore ilo tung'ani, eikilikuanishore iyiook te nkarriyiano aikilikuanu imbaa naaipirta iyiook olmarei lang ejoki iyiook, ‘Keton eishu papaai linyi? Iyatata likae alashe?’ Ore nena nikitiakita naa iwalat e nena kikilikuanat; ijo duoo aikinteiki aajo kejoki iyiook, ‘Eayau olalashe linyi ene?’ ”

English: And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.
Masaai: Nejoki Yuda Israel, Papaai lenye, “Inchoo enkayioni elo tenebo nanu, nikidumunye aapuo, pee kinchu eitu kiye, iyiook o iyie o tenebo inkera ang.

English: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:
Masaai: Aitayio enkishui ai tenkaraki ninye metaa te nanu ing'oru ninye. Teneitu ashuku ninye enitii naitasheyie ninye te dukuya iyie, neaku entorroni ai intarasi.

English: For except we had lingered, surely now we had returned this second time.
Masaai: Amu teneitu taa doi apa kimutie anaata taata kindipa aashom ine katitin are nikishukunye.”

English: And their father Israel said unto them, If it must be so now, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:
Masaai: Nejoki papaai lenye Israel ninche, “Tenaa neijia etiu, entaas ena: ewaita embata oo lnganayio gelunot lena kop too lbenia linyi, niyakiki ilo tung'ani enkishooroto, enkiti ilata narropil, o enkiti aisho, o emanoo, o enkorropil, o lng'anayio lo lchani onyaanyukie oseki.

English: And take double money in your hand; and the money that was brought again in the mouth of your sacks, carry it again in your hand; peradventure it was an oversight:
Masaai: Niyiaya impisai kat are ipuopuo, nirrinyirrinyi inapa pisai naatushukokoki intae too nkutukie oo lbenia linyi; amu ebaiki apa naa keitu edoli.

English: Take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:
Masaai: Entorik sii ninye olalashe linyi nidumunyenye aapuo, nishukokinono enetii ilo tung'ani;

English: And God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.
Masaai: meishoo intae Enkai Magilani olng'ur te dukuya ilo tung'ani, pee etum aishoo intae entushuku olikae alashe linyi o Benchamen. Tenaa apa kaiturraa inkera aainei, inchoo aiturraa.”

English: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
Masaai: Neaku ewaita iltung'ana inkishorot, neya irridat maare loo mpisai tenebo ninche tenebo Benchamen; nedumunye aadoyio aapuo enkop e Misiri neitashe te dukuya Yosef.

English: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring these men home, and slay, and make ready; for these men shall dine with me at noon.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yosef Benchamen tenebo ninche, nejoki ilo aitasheikinoni le nkaji enye, “Toriku lelo tung'ana atua aji niyieng'aki, amu keinos ninche taata endaa tenebo nanu teneipir enkolong.”

English: And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
Masaai: Neas ilo sinka anaa enaitanapa Yosef ninye, nerik lelo tung'ana enkaji e Yosef.

English: And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph's house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.
Masaai: Neureishoi iltung'ana amu eyauaki ninche enkaji e Yosef, nejo, “Enkaraki taa inapa pisai naatipikaki ilbenia lang te nkata e dukuya, ina pee etum anoto enaitaas iyiook nebaiki iyiook aitaa iyiook irrindiki neibung isirkon lang.”

English: And they came near to the steward of Joseph's house, and they communed with him at the door of the house,
Masaai: Metaa eshomo ninche enetii olaitasheikinoni le nkaji e Yosef, neirorie ninye te kutuk e nkaji ejo,

English: And said, O sir, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food:
Masaai: “Oi olkitok lang, kietuo apa enkata e dukuya ainyiang'u endaa;

English: And it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.
Masaai: ore kipuo te nkoitoi, ore ewueji nikirraga nikibol ilbenia lang, nemeeta olbene hoo obo lemetii irridat loo mpisai enkutuk olbene lenye, eba ake impisai anaa apake; neaku kitorrinyutuo pooki,

English: And other money have we brought down in our hands to buy food: we cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.
Masaai: nikiyautua sii too nkaik ang kulie pisai nikinosie endaa. Mikiyiolo aajo aing'ae otorrinyoko impisai ang ilbenia lang.”

English: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them.
Masaai: Nejoki olaitasheikinoni ninche, “Entotoni miatata enkuretisho; ore Enkai inyi o Enkai oo loo papaai linyi ninye natipika ilo shumati atua ilbenia linyi apikaki intae; atang'amayie impisai inyi.” Neriku ninye Simon enetii ninche.

English: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
Masaai: Ore pee eriku ilo tung'ani lelo tung'ana atua enkaji e Yosef, neishoo ninche enkare, neisuja inkejek enye, neidipa sii aishoo isirkon lenye olkujita onya.

English: And they made ready the present against Joseph came at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.
Masaai: Nerretena aanyu elotunoto e Yosef enaipirie enkolong, amu etoning'o aajo kenya endaa tenebo teine.

English: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Yosef ang', eyautua atua enkaji enye inkishorot naata, neirrugokino ninche ninye aabaiki enkop.

English: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?
Masaai: Neikilikuan ninye ninche ilomon le seriani ejo, “Aisupat papaai linyi, ilo apa payian kitok liimakiita? Keton eishu?”

English: And they answered, Thy servant our father is in good health, he is yet alive. And they bowed down their heads, and made obeisance.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Ore osinka lino, papaai lang naa aisupat neton eishu.” Neirrug ilukuny enye te dukuya ninye te nkanyit sapuk.

English: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, God be gracious unto thee, my son.
Masaai: Nedumu inkonyek enyena nedol olalashe lenye Benchamen, olayioni le ng'otonye nejo, “Kele doi olalashe linyi oti ilo apa likitolikitio? Miking'urrie iyie Enkai enkayioni ai!”

English: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.
Masaai: Neisarrisar Yosef amu etayiewua oltau lenye olalashe lenye te nkirimo sapuk, nelo aing'oru ewueji nelo aishirie. Nejing atua olgilata, nelo aishir teine.

English: And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip aishira, neituku enkomom enye nepuku; neitagol kewan nejo, “Enchoo endaa eyauni.”

English: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.
Masaai: Neng'asi aaisho ninye eton openy, neitokini aisho ninche etoni oopeny, ore Ilmisiri ootoni oopeny neishori sii ninche aa ninche ake, amu ebaiki nemeng'ar Ilmisiri endaa tenebo Ilhebrania, amu entoki ina naa enturuj too Lmisiri.

English: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.
Masaai: Netoni pooki te dukuya ninye anaa enaikunari te mbotoro eiteru to lbotor te inoto ometabaiki oloti te inoto anaa kitisho enye; neing'or iltung'ana ate te nking'asia sapuk.

English: And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.
Masaai: Neyakini pooki endaa naing'uaa emesa e Yosef, kake ore ene Benchamen naa katitin imiet te sapuko elusoo too nkulie. Metaa etookishote ninche neshipa tenebo ninye.

English: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth.
Masaai: Ina pee eitanap olaitasheikinoni lenye le nkaji enye ajoki, “Imputa ilbenia le lelo tung'ana endaa, tipika enaba anaa enaidim ake ninche aatanap, nipik impisai e pooki tungani enkutuk olbene lenye.

English: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
Masaai: Nipik enkikompe ai ina kikompe enkosholai enkutuk olbene lo loti tenebo impisai enyena naainosie ilpaek.”

English: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.
Masaai: Neas anaa enaitanapa Yosef ninye. Ore ake pee ekenyu, neishori iltung'ana epuo aareu isirkon lenye.

English: And when they were gone out of the city, and not yet far off, Joseph said unto his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?
Masaai: Ore ake pee epuo aalamari penyo aalam enkanasa, nejoki Yosef olaitasheikinoni le nkaji, enye, “Inyo, tusuja lelo tung'ana, ore ake pee inepu, tiaaki ninche, ‘Ainyoo pee itushukutuo entorrono te sidai? Ainyo pee itupurroitie enkikompe ai enkosholai?

English: Is not this it in which my lord drinketh, and whereby indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.
Masaai: Aime ena kikompe oshi eokishore olkitok lai, naa te ninye eibonisho? Itaasa entorroni teina nitaasa.’ ”

English: And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these same words.
Masaai: Ore ake pee einepu ninche, neirorie ninche lelo rorei.

English: And they said unto him, Wherefore saith my lord these words? God forbid that thy servants should do according to this thing:
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “Ainyoo pee eiro olkitok lang irorei laijo kulo? Metalama isinkan linono ina aaku keidim aataas embae naijo ina!

English: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again unto thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lord's house silver or gold?
Masaai: Ing'ura, ore inapa pisai nikinotito too nkutukie oo lbenia lang, kitushukutuo aashukoki iyie king'ua enkop e Kanaan; kaji naa kinko siake tinikipurroo enkosholai arashu sahabu te nkaji olkitok lino?

English: With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, both let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen.
Masaai: Inchoo ake obo lang too sinkan linono otumi eeta, enchoo eye, nikiaku sii iyiook pooki irrindiki lo lkitok lang.”

English: And he said, Now also let it be according unto your words: he with whom it is found shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Enchoo naa eaku anaa enitejo; ore ake olotumi eeta neaku orrindik lai, ore ilkulikae linyi pooki neaku meeta entioto.”

English: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
Masaai: Nesioki pooki ng'ae aitadou olbene lenye enkop, nebol pooki tung'ani olbene lenye.

English: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
Masaai: Neing'oru te pooki eiteru to lbotor neitabayie to loti; netumi enkikompe to lbene le Benchamen.

English: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
Masaai: Nepolos pooki inkilani enye, neirot pooki ng'ae esikiria enye, nerrinyo aapuo enkanasa.

English: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph's house; for he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Yuda o lalashera lenyena enkaji e Yosef, eton ake etii Yosef ine; nebatata te dukuya ninye aabatatakino enkop.

English: And Joseph said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? wot ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine?
Masaai: Nejoki Yosef ninche, “Kaa bae ena nikintaasa? Aimiyiololo aajo ore oltung'ani laijo nanu naa kaidim aibonisho?”

English: And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord's servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.
Masaai: Nejo Yuda, “Kaa taa kijoki olkitok lang? Ainyoo taa kiro aajo? Anaa kaji kinko tinikilaku ate? Enoto Enkai entorroni oo sinkan linono; ng'ura, kira iyiook irrindiki lo lkitok lang, iyiook pooki ometabaiki lido duoo linotie enkikompe.”

English: And he said, God forbid that I should do so: but the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant; and as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.
Masaai: Kake etejo, “Meidimayu te nanu mataasa ina! Oltung'ani ake onotieki enkikompe ninye ake oaku orrindik lai; kake ore intae, enchom te seriani enetii papaai linyi.”

English: Then Judah came near unto him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant: for thou art even as Pharaoh.
Masaai: Ina pee elo Yuda enetii ninye nejoki, “Oi olkitok lang, inchoo osinka lino eiro, aatasayia, kaliki ororei enkiok o lkitok lai, nimincho engoro ino eyupuyup to sinka lino; amu itiu doi iyie anaa Farao enkorrok.

English: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
Masaai: Eikilikuana apa olkitok lai isinkan lenyena ajoki, ‘Iyatata papaai linyi anaa likae alashe?’

English: And we said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.
Masaai: Nikiwal apa aajoki olkitok lang, ‘Kiata papa, naa olpayian kitok oleng, nikiata sii olalashe lang, oti olotioiwuoki te moruao enye, netua apa olalashe lenye, neaku ninye ake etung'uayioki too nkera e ng'otonye; naa kenyor menye ninye oleng.’

English: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.
Masaai: Nintoki ajoki isinkan linono, ‘Eyau ninye ene natii, pee adol ninye too nkonyek aainei.’

English: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.
Masaai: Nikijoki olkitok lang, ‘Meidim enkayioni atung'uai menye, amu tenelo aing'uaa menye, naa keye menye.’

English: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.
Masaai: Ina pee ijoki isinkan linono, ‘Pooki ake pee intokiki aadol enkomom ai, tenelotu olalashe linyi oti tenebo intae.’

English: And it came to pass when we came up unto thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
Masaai: “Ore pee kirrinyo enetii osinka lino, aa papa, nikiliki irorei lo lkitok lang.

English: And our father said, Go again, and buy us a little food.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo papaai lang, ‘Enchom enyaaki enyang'aki iyiook enkiti daa;’

English: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down: for we may not see the man's face, except our youngest brother be with us.
Masaai: nikijo, ‘Mikipuo katukul. Tenaa keiriamariyie iyiook olalashe lang oti naa aikipuo; amu mikindim katukul aatodol enkomom eilo tung'ani arashu ake kiata olalashe lang oti tenebo iyiook.’

English: And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons:
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki iyiook osinka lino papaai lang, ‘Iyiololo apa aajo aatoikio enkitok ai ilayiok oare;

English: And the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since:
Masaai: ore obo naatung'uayie nanu, ina pee ajo, esipa etumutaki apa aaitaa ndung'udung'ot, neitu aekata aitoki adol ninye.

English: And if ye take this also from me, and mischief befall him, ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
Masaai: Tinintokiki sii taata aaya ele aaitung'uaa nanu nelo netum enyamali e nkitamioto niyauu ilpapit laainei ooibor to sina enemeneng'a.’

English: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad be not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life;
Masaai: Ore naa taata, ore tenalotu enetii osinka lino papaai lang, nemetii enkayioni tenebo iyiook, neaku ore enkishui enye neibung'are ena ayioni,

English: It shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants shall bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to the grave.
Masaai: ore pee edol ajo metii enkayioni tenebo iyiook, neye ninye, neyau isinkan linono ilpapit ooibor lo sinka lino papaai lang to sina enemeneng'a.

English: For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.
Masaai: Amu etaa osinka lino oloitasheiki enkishui enkayioni, te papaai lang ejoki. ‘Teneitu ashuku ninye enitii, naaku oloota entorroni te dukuya papaai te nkishui ai pooki,’

English: Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.
Masaai: metaa, ore naa taata, inchoo osinka lino, aatasayia, ejing erishata enkayioni aaku orrindik lo lkitok lai; nincho enkayioni eshuko tenebo ilalashera.

English: For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me? lest peradventure I see the evil that shall come on my father.
Masaai: Amu kaji naa aikunari tenarrinyokino papaai lai marikito enkayioni? Ekaure doi ninye ajo atoduaa intorrok naajing'aki papaai lai.”

English: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren.
Masaai: Neaku meekure eidim Yosef aibooi kewan te dukuya lelo pooki ooitashe te dukuya ninye; neishir ejo, “Enchoo pooki ng'ae otii ene aaipung aing'uaa.” Metaa meetae hoo oltung'ani obo otii ine ina kata eibalakinye Yosef kewan ilalashera lenyena.

English: And he wept aloud: and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard.
Masaai: Nebuaku aishir ometoning'o Ilmisiri ninye, nening sii enkaji pooki e Farao.

English: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.
Masaai: Nejoki Yosef ilalashera lenyena, “Ekara doi Yosef; keton eishu papaai?” Kake eitu eidim ilalashera lenyena aatawaliki ninye, amu eiputukunyo oleng te dukuya ninye.

English: And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Yosef ilalashera lenyena, “Wootu entinyiku enatii atasayia intae.” Nepuonu aanyiku. Nejoki ninye, “Ekara olalashe linyi Yosef, ilo apa litimirakita enkop e Misiri.

English: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
Masaai: Naa ore naa taata emiureishoyu, anaa igororo maate, te nkaraki nikitimirakita apa ena kop; amu Enkai apa naaiturukunye nanu maeu aitopok enkishui.

English: For these two years hath the famine been in the land: and yet there are five years, in the which there shall neither be earing nor harvest.
Masaai: Amu etijing'a olameyu enkop te kulo arin pokira aare; neton aa kepuonu kulikae arin imiet laa metumi enturore anaa enkisampuare.

English: And God sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
Masaai: Naairriu apa Enkai ene pee aituruku te ntae, pee alotu aitajeu ilekunot te nkop naitasheyie tenkaraki intae pee meye ilkumok.

English: So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Metaa mme intae apa likirriutua ene kake Enkai; naaeuo aaitaa menye le Farao, naaku olkitok le nkaji enye pooki o loitore e nkop pooki e Misiri.

English: Haste ye, and go up to my father, and say unto him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt: come down unto me, tarry not:
Masaai: “Entasiooi esarisara enchom enetii papaai nijokiki ninye, ‘Inji ejo olayioni lino Yosef, aitaa Enkai olkitok le nkop pooki e Misiri; wou ene natii, mayieu nimutie.

English: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy children, and thy children's children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:
Masaai: Ilotu amany enkop e Goshen nikilotu anyikaki iyie tenebo inkera inono o nkera oo nkera inono, o ntare inono, o nkishu inono, o pooki toki niata.

English: And there will I nourish thee; for yet there are five years of famine; lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, come to poverty.
Masaai: Ore itii ine naaisho pooki toki niyieu, amu eton eetae kulikae arin imiet leton epuonu lo lameyu; pee mikiya iyie osina o lmarei lino pooki o pooki toki niata.’

English: And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you.
Masaai: “Idolitata too nkonyek inyi, nedolita nkonyek o lalashe lai Benchamen inchere enkutuk ai nairorie intae.

English: And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen; and ye shall haste and bring down my father hither.
Masaai: Enchom entoliki papaai esikar pooki naata tene te Misiri, o pooki toki nitodua tene. Entasiooi eyau papaai ene.”

English: And he fell upon his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
Masaai: Ina pee emuataki inkaik olalashe lenye Benchamen aishiraki; neishirakino pokira.

English: Moreover he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.
Masaai: Neng'utut ilalashera lenyena pooki neishiraki ninye ninche; ore pee eidip ina neiteru ilalashera aairorie ninye.

English: And the fame thereof was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, Joseph's brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
Masaai: Ore pee ening'i olomoni te nkaji e Farao, eji, “Eetuo ilalashera le Yosef,” neitiship ina Farao o ilaisiaayiak lenyena.

English: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Say unto thy brethren, This do ye; lade your beasts, and go, get you unto the land of Canaan;
Masaai: Nejoki Farao Yosef, “Tiaki ilalashera linono, entaas ena ‘Eroto isirkon linyi nipuopuo aarrinyo enkop e Kanaan;

English: And take your father and your households, and come unto me: and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.
Masaai: nirikuku papaai linyi o pooki tung'ani loo lmareita linyi, nipuonunu enatii, naa kaisho nanu intae enkop naisul ena kop e Misiri te sidano, naa ainyanya empiron ena kop.’

English: Now thou art commanded, this do ye; take you wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
Masaai: Intanapa ake sii ninche tiaki, ‘Entaas ena: entereu ingarrin tena kop e Misiri pee enapunyeki inkera inyi o nkituaak inyi, niyauu papaai linyi nipuonunu.

English: Also regard not your stuff; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
Masaai: Niminkenaa aajo kitung'uaitie imasaa ang e tipat teine amu ore inaaisul enkop pooki e Misiri naa inkuninyi.’ ”

English: And the children of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
Masaai: Neas ilayiok le Israel ina; neisho Yosef ninche ingarrin te risioroto eina naitanapishe Farao, neisho sii ninche endaa nainosaa epuo te nkoitoi o epuonu.

English: To all of them he gave each man changes of raiment; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment.
Masaai: Meeta ake sii oleitu eisho te pooki lenye inkilani ng'ejuko kake eishoo Benchamen shekeli iip uni e nkosholai o nkilani imiet ng'ejuko.

English: And to his father he sent after this manner; ten asses laden with the good things of Egypt, and ten she asses laden with corn and bread and meat for his father by the way.
Masaai: Ore papaai lenye, neirriwaki kuna; isirkon tomon naairoto too ntokitin sidain e Misiri, o lipong'a tomon oo sirkon naanapita entapa, o imukateni, o ntokitin naanya papaai lenye te nkoitoi.

English: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said unto them, See that ye fall not out by the way.
Masaai: Ina pee eisho ilalashera meshomo, ejoki ninche, “Mayieu ake ninchankarrarra te nkoitoi.”

English: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan unto Jacob their father,
Masaai: Metaa etudumunye aapuo aaing'uaa Misiri nebau Kanaan enetii papaai lenye, Yakobo.

English: And told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob's heart fainted, for he believed them not.
Masaai: Neliki ninye lelo omon, ejoki, “Eton doi ake eishu Yosef, naa ninye oitore enkop pooki e Misiri!” Neiterre Yakobo, amu eitu eiruk ninye ninche.

English: And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:
Masaai: Kake ore pee eliki ninche irorei pooki le Yosef, lelo apa ootiaka ninye ninche, ore ake sii pee edol ingarrin naaetuo pee enap ninye neitoki oltau le Yakobo papaai lenye apok;

English: And Israel said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.
Masaai: nejo Israel eidipe eton doi eishu olayioni lai Yosef; ekalo adol ninye eton eitu aye.

English: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac.
Masaai: Metaa etudumunye Yakobo alo o pooki toki naata, nepuonu Beer-sheba, neitayu ilasarri aaitaiki Enkai e papaai lenye Isaak.

English: And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I.
Masaai: Neirorie Enkai Israel too nkitoduat e kewarie nejoki ninye, “Yakobo, Yakobo,” nejo ninye, “Nele nanu.”

English: And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki, “Ara nanu Enkai, Enkai e papaai lino; miureishoyu ilo Misiri; amu kaalo aitaa olosho sapuk teine.

English: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.
Masaai: Ekaairiamariyie iyie Misiri, naa kaaitoki ashuku ene, neaku inkaik e Yosef ilo airurare.”

English: And Jacob rose up from Beersheba: and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
Masaai: Ina pee epuku Yakobo aing'uaa Beer-sheba, nenap ilayiok le Israel Yakobo papaai lenye, o nkera enye, o nkituaak enye too ngarrin naairriwua Farao metanapa ninye.

English: And they took their cattle, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him:
Masaai: Eterewa sii inkishu enye o masaa enye, naanoto te nkop e Kanaan, nepuonu enkop e Misiri, Yakobo o eishoi enye pooki,

English: His sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed brought he with him into Egypt.
Masaai: ilayiok lenyena, o layiok loo layiok lenyena tenebo ninye, o ntoyie enyena, o ntoyie oo layiok lenyena, o eishoi enye pooki eyaua ninye pooki tenebo ninye Misiri.

English: And these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn.
Masaai: Kuna ninche inkarn e ishoi e Israel, naaetuo atua Misiri, Yakobo o layiok lenyena, Ruben, olkikau le Yakobo.

English: And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Ruben, naa: Hanok, o Palu, o Hesron, o Karmi.

English: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Simon naa: Yemuel, o Yamin, o Ohal, o Yakin, o Sohar o Saul, aa layiok le nkitok oo Lkanaani.

English: And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Lawi naa: Gershon, o Kohat, o Merari.

English: And the sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zarah: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Yuda naa: Eri, o Onan, o Shela, o Peres, o Sera (kake ore Eri o Onan netuata te nkop e Kanaan): ore ilayiok le Peres naa: Hesron, o Hamul.

English: And the sons of Issachar; Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Isaakar naa: Tola, o Pufa, o Yob, o Shimron.

English: And the sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Sebulon naa: Sered, o Elon o Yahaleel

English: These be the sons of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob in Padanaram, with his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty and three.
Masaai: (kulo apa ilayiok le Lea ootoikio ninye Yakobo te Padan-aram, tenebo entito enye Dina; neaku pooki ilayiok o ntoyie enyena iltung'ana tomoni uni o kuni).

English: And the sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Gad naa: Sifion, o Haggi, o Shuni, o Esbon, o Eri, o Arod, o Areli.

English: And the sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister: and the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Asheri naa: Imna, o Ishfa, o Ishfi, o Beria, tenebo Sera enkanashe enye. Ore ilayiok le Beria naa: Heber o Malkiel

English: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and these she bare unto Jacob, even sixteen souls.
Masaai: (kulo ninche ilayiok le Silpa oishoo Laban Lea entito enye; neaku kulo etoikio Yakobo - iltung'ana tomon o ile).

English: The sons of Rachel Jacob's wife; Joseph, and Benjamin.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Raheli, enkitok e Yakobo naa: Yosef o Benchamen.

English: And unto Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, which Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On bare unto him.
Masaai: Neikini Yosef te nkop e Misiri Manaseh o Efraim, laa ninche etoikio Asenat entito e Potifera olapolosani le Oni.

English: And the sons of Benjamin were Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Benchamen naa: Bela, o Becher, o Ashbel, o Gera, o Naaman, o Ehi o Rosh, o Mupin, o Huppin o Ard

English: These are the sons of Rachel, which were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
Masaai: (kulo ninche ilayiok le Raheli ootoikioki Yakobo - iltung'ana tomon oong'uan pooki.)

English: And the sons of Dan; Hushim.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Dan naa: Hushim.

English: And the sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok le Naftali naa: Yahseel, o Guni, o Yeser, o Shilem,

English: These are the sons of Bilhah, which Laban gave unto Rachel his daughter, and she bare these unto Jacob: all the souls were seven.
Masaai: (kulo ninche ilayiok le Bilha, ooishoo Laban Raheli entito enye, neaku kulo ninye etoikio Yakobo - iltung'ana oopishana pooki.)

English: All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, which came out of his loins, besides Jacob's sons' wives, all the souls were threescore and six;
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana pooki le Yakobo ooetuo atua Misiri, laa ile ishoi enye enkorrok, nemeikenaro ilayiok loo nkituaak oo layiok lenyena naa iltung'ana intomoni ile o ile pooki;

English: And the sons of Joseph, which were born him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.
Masaai: o layiok aare le Yosef ootoikioki ninye te Misiri; neaku ore olorere pooki le nkaji e Yakobo oetuo atua Misiri naa iltung'ana intomoni naapishana.

English: And he sent Judah before him unto Joseph, to direct his face unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ninye Yuda meituruko alo enetii Yosef ajoki ninye menotore ninye te Goshen; nepuonu ninche enkop e Goshen.

English: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
Masaai: Neirot Yosef engarri enye oo mbartan nelo anang'are papaai lenye Israel te Goshen; nekuetik Yosef papaai lenye nemuataki inkaik enyena emurt, aishir te murt enye te nkata naado.

English: And Israel said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.
Masaai: Nejoki Israel Yosef, “Etaa taa nchooki matua amu aatoduaa enkomom nayiolo ajo eton ake inchu.”

English: And Joseph said unto his brethren, and unto his father's house, I will go up, and shew Pharaoh, and say unto him, My brethren, and my father's house, which were in the land of Canaan, are come unto me;
Masaai: Nejoki Yosef ilalashera lenyena o enkaji e menye pooki; “Ekalo ainosaki Farao, naa kajoki ninye, ‘Ore ilalashera laainei o enkaji e papa pooki, otii apa enkop e Kanaan, eetuo enatii.

English: And the men are shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.
Masaai: Ore lelo tung'ana naa ilairritak, amu ilaramatak loo nkishu, neyautua intare enye, o nkishu enye o pooki toki naata.’

English: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your occupation?
Masaai: Ore teneipot intae nejoki intae: ‘Ainyoo esaiai inyi niasiasa?’

English: That ye shall say, Thy servants' trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.
Masaai: Enchom entejo, ore isinkan linono naa ilaramatak loo nkishu eiteru te keraisho o metabaiki ena kata, iyiook tenebo iloo papa lang; pee itumutumu aatamany enkop e Goshen; Amu ore pooki aramatani loo ntare naa olminong too Lmisiri.”

English: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo Yosef ajing'aki Farao te nkaji, nejoki: “Ore papaai lai o lalashera laainei, tenebo intare enye o nkishu enye o pooki toki naata, eetuo aaing'uaa enkop e Kanaan. Netii taata ninche ina kop e Goshen.”

English: And he took some of his brethren, even five men, and presented them unto Pharaoh.
Masaai: Neriku too lalashera lenyena ltung'ana imiet arikoki Farao.

English: And Pharaoh said unto his brethren, What is your occupation? And they said unto Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.
Masaai: Nejoki Farao ilalashera lenyena. “Ainyoo oshi esaiai inyi niasiasa?” Nejoki ninche Farao, “Ore isinkan linono naa ilaramatak, anaa enatiu apa iloo papa lang.”

English: They said moreover unto Pharaoh, For to sojourn in the land are we come; for thy servants have no pasture for their flocks; for the famine is sore in the land of Canaan: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche Farao, “Kietuo iyiook aamany ena kop, amu meeta indaat oo ntare isinkan linono, amu etaa olameyu sapuk te nkop e Kanaan; naa ore taata, kiomon iyie inchoo isinkan linono emany enkop e Goshen.”

English: And Pharaoh spake unto Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come unto thee:
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Farao Yosef, “Eewuo papaai lino o lalashera enitii.

English: The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.
Masaai: Neina enkop e Misiri natii dukuya iyie, intamanya papaai lino o lalashera linono ine wueji sidai aisul tena kop, inchoo emany enkop e Goshen naa tiniyiolo iltung'ana airritak supati te ninche tipika ninche meitasheiki inkishu aainei.”

English: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Masaai: Ina peyie eitijing'u Yosef Yakobo papaai lenye neitoton te dukuya Farao, nemayian Yakobo Farao.

English: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob, How old art thou?
Masaai: Nejoki Farao Yakobo, “Kaja inkolong'i oo larin le nkishui ino.”

English: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years: few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo Farao, “Ore inkolong'i oo larin laainei lenkidurrudur ai naa ilarin iip o tomoni uni; kuti naa torrok inkolong'i oo larin le nkishui ai, neitu ebaiki inkolong'i oo larin le nkishui oo loo papa too nkolong'i enkidurrudur enye.”

English: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
Masaai: Nemayian Yakobo Farao nepuku alo aing'uaa Farao.

English: And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Masaai: Neaku eitamanya Yosef ilalashera lenyena, neisho ninye ninche enkop metaa enenye te Misiri, ewueji neisul te ina kop e Rameses, anaa enaitanapishe Farao.

English: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread, according to their families.
Masaai: Neisho Yosef papaai lenye, tenebo ilalashera lenyena, o lmarei lenye pooki endaa, terisioroto esiana ooltung'ana lenye.

English: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very sore, so that the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
Masaai: Etaa meekure apa eetae endaa teina kop pooki; amu etasapuka olameyu oleng', metaa etaa enkop e Misiri o enkop e Kanaan enaisumash te nkaraki olameyu.

English: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.
Masaai: Nesotu Yosef impisai pooki naanotoki te nkop e Misiri o te nkop e Kanaan, te ntapa nainyiang'utua; neyau Yosef nena pisai aya enkaji e Farao.

English: And when money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came unto Joseph, and said, Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money faileth.
Masaai: Neaku ore pee emiri aaishu impisai pooki te nkop e Misiri o te nkop e Kanaan, eetuo Ilmisiri pooki enetii Yosef nejoki ninye, “Inchoo iyiook endaa; ainyoo pee kiye te dukuya nkonyek inyi?

English: And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money fail.
Masaai: Amu kiishutua impisai ang'.” Newal Yosef ajo, “Enchoru inkishu inyi, naa kaisho intae endaa awalunye nkishu inyi tenetaa eishunye impisai inyi.”

English: And they brought their cattle unto Joseph: and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flocks, and for the cattle of the herds, and for the asses: and he fed them with bread for all their cattle for that year.
Masaai: Metaa nerewaki inkishu enye Yosef; neisho Yosef ninche endaa awalunye imbartan enye, o intare, o nkishu, o sirkon: neisho ninye ninche endaa awalunye nkishu enye pooki teilo ari.

English: When that year was ended, they came unto him the second year, and said unto him, We will not hide it from my lord, how that our money is spent; my lord also hath our herds of cattle; there is not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:
Masaai: Ore pee eishunye ilo ari, neitoki aapuonu to likae ari nejoki ninye, “Mikisudorie ate olkitok lang inchere eishunye impisai ang pooki, ore iluaat oo nkishu naa ino lkitok lang; metii ae toki natung'uayioki te dukuya olkitok lang meteleku iseseni lang ake o enkop ang'.

English: Wherefore shall we die before thine eyes, both we and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh: and give us seed, that we may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate.
Masaai: Ainyoo pee kiye te dukuya inkonyek inono, iyiook tenebo enkop ang'? Inyang'u iyiook tenebo enkop ang te ndaa; ore iyiook tenebo enkop ang nikiaku irrindiki le Farao; nincho iyiook ilanterera pee kinchu nimikiye, neaku ena kop pooki mitil.”

English: And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them: so the land became Pharaoh's.
Masaai: Metaa einyiang'ua Yosef enkop pooki e Misiri ainyang'aki Farao, amu etimira Ilmisiri inkurman enye amu ketarasua olameyu oleng te ninche. Neaku enkop pooki ene Farao;

English: And as for the people, he removed them to cities from one end of the borders of Egypt even to the other end thereof.
Masaai: ore iltung'ana neaku, irrindiki pooki eiteru te nkiting'oto nabo e Misiri o metabaiki enkae kiting'oto.

English: Only the land of the priests bought he not; for the priests had a portion assigned them of Pharaoh, and did eat their portion which Pharaoh gave them: wherefore they sold not their lands.
Masaai: Enkop ake oo lapolosak eitu einyang'u; amu keeta apa ilapolosak emborei enye nauno naing'uaaa Farao, neishunyie ina borei enye naishoo Farao ninche; metaa eitu ninche emir enkop enye.

English: Then Joseph said unto the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you, and ye shall sow the land.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Yosef iltung'ana, “Ing'ura ainyiang'ua intae ena olong tenebo enkop inyi aitaa ene Farao. Ore naa, noolo ilanterera linyi, naa entuun enkop.

English: And it shall come to pass in the increase, that ye shall give the fifth part unto Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
Masaai: Ore te nkata e nkisampuare ninchosho ematua e imiet Farao, ore ematua e ong'uan neaku inkuninyi ilanterera le nkop, neaku sii endaa inyi o lmarei linyi, o ndaiki naanya inkera inyi.”

English: And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Intajeuo enkishui ang; inchoo eitiship ena olkitok lang', aikiaaku iyiook irrindiki le Farao.”

English: And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth part; except the land of the priests only, which became not Pharaoh's.
Masaai: Metaa eitobirua Yosef nkiguanat naaipirta enkop e Misiri, neitashe nena kiguanat o taata, inchere etum Farao ematua e imiet; enkop ake oo lapolosak neitu eaku ene Farao.

English: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen; and they had possessions therein, and grew, and multiplied exceedingly.
Masaai: Metaa etamanya Israel Enkop e Misiri ina kop e Goshen; netum imasaa kumok teine, neisho oleng nebul te nkumoi.

English: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole age of Jacob was an hundred forty and seven years.
Masaai: Neton Yakobo te nkop e Misiri ilarin tomon o oopishana; metaa ore inkolong'i oo larin le nkishui e Yakobo naa iip o artam oopishana.

English: And the time drew nigh that Israel must die: and he called his son Joseph, and said unto him, If now I have found grace in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt:
Masaai: Ore pee enyiku inkolong'i pee eaku enkata nairura Israel, eipoto olayioni lenye Yosef nejoki ninye, “Tenetaa taata anoto omom too nkonyek inono, tipika enkaina ino abori enkupes ai nikisiligie ajo aikintaas nanu enkanyit o esipata.

English: But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace. And he said, I will do as thou hast said.
Masaai: Mayieu nikinukaa nanu te Misiri, kake tunukayioki nanu tiatua inkuraren oo loo papa; tanapaki nanu intung'uayioki Misiri nikilo aturoo nanu te wueji enye neturorie olorere.” Newal ninye ajo, “Ekaas anaa enitejo.”

English: And he said, Swear unto me. And he sware unto him. And Israel bowed himself upon the bed's head.
Masaai: Nejo, “Inosa olmumai te nanu.” Neinos ninye olmumai. Ina pee eirrug Israel endukuya enye te ndukuya e ndapash enye.

English: And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
Masaai: Ore pee elusoo nena, nelikini Yosef aajoki, “Ing'ura kemuoi papaai lino;” metaa etoriko ninye ilayiok lenyena aare, Manase o Efraim.

English: And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh unto thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
Masaai: Nelikini Yakobo aajoki:, “Eewuo olayioni lino Yosef enitii;” neitagoluo Israel nenyok ainyototo aton te ndapash.

English: And Jacob said unto Joseph, God Almighty appeared unto me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
Masaai: Nejoki Yakobo Yosef, “Aaipang'aka Enkai magilani nanu te Lus te nkop e Kanaan naamayian nanu,

English: And said unto me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a multitude of people; and will give this land to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.
Masaai: naajoki nanu, ‘Ng'ura kaaisho iyie tubula, naa kaaponaa iyie, naaitaa iyie olorora loo ltung'ana kumok, naa kaisho ena kop eishoi ino nikisuju metaa enenye intarasi.’

English: And now thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, which were born unto thee in the land of Egypt before I came unto thee into Egypt, are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.
Masaai: “Ore ilayiok linono pokira aare likitoikioki te nkop e Misiri eton eitu alotu enitii tene te Misiri; naa ilaainei; Efraim o Manase eaku ilaanei anaa paa ilaainei Ruben o Simon.

English: And thy issue, which thou begettest after them, shall be thine, and shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.
Masaai: Ore eishoi nitum tesiadi ninche naa keaku ilinono; naa keipotieki ninche enkarna oo lalashera te njung'ore enye.

English: And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan in the way, when yet there was but a little way to come unto Ephrath: and I buried her there in the way of Ephrath; the same is Bethlehem.
Masaai: Amu ore apa pee alotu te Padan-aram aainepua osina etua Raheli te nkop e Kanaan te nkoitoi, eton elakua elototo pee ebau Efrat. Naturoo ninye teine te nkotoi alotito Efrat (aa ninye Betlehem).”

English: And Israel beheld Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?
Masaai: Ore pee edol Israel ilayiok le Yosef, etejo “Kakua doi kulo?”

English: And Joseph said unto his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.
Masaai: Nejoki Yosef papaai lenye, “Ilayiok laainei ninche, lelo apa laaishoo Enkai tene.” Nejo Israel, “Toriku ninche ene natii, aatasayia pee atum atamayiana ninche.”

English: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
Masaai: Ore ina kata, eiliilaitie nkonyek e Israel te moruao, metaa meidim ninye atisipu. Neaku eyaua Yosef ninche aitinyiaki ninye; neng'utut ninche neitamuat inkaik enyena.

English: And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed.
Masaai: Nejoki Israel Yosef, “Majo apa kaaitoki adol enkomom ino; naa ng'ura, aaishoo Enkai matoduaa sii inkera inono.”

English: And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
Masaai: Metaa eiwuangie Yosef ninche too nkung enyena, neirrugo ninye makewan abaiki enkop.

English: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near unto him.
Masaai: Nerik Yosef ninche pokira, etii Efraim enkaina enye e tatene eitorioki enkaina e kedienye e Israel, netii Manase enkaina enye e kedienye eitorioki ninye enkaina e tatene e Israel, neriku ninche aitinyikaki ninye.

English: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn.
Masaai: Neitorioo Israel enkaina enye e tatene neiteleiki ninye endukuya e Efraim, laa ninye oloti, ore enkaina enye e kedienye eiteleikia endukuya e Manase, eitapaash inkaik, amu ore Manase naa ninye olbotor.

English: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day,
Masaai: Nemayian ninye Yosef ejo; “Ore ina Ai naisiaayia iloo Papa te dukuya enye, Abraham o Isaak, ina Ai naatorikoyie te nkishui ai pooki o metabaiki ena olong,

English: The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.
Masaai: Ilo malaika laaitajeuo nanu te pooki torroni, tamayiana kuna ayiok; Naa te ninche inchoo enkarna ai meipoti, tenebo enkarna oo loo papa Abraham o Isaak; Naa inchoo ninche ebulu aaku ilororani tiatua ena kop pooki.”

English: And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Manasseh's head.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yosef ajo eiteleikia menye enkaina e tatene shumata endukuya e Efraim neitu eitiship ninye, nedumu enkaina e menye aitayu aitung'uaa endukuya e Efraim apik ene Manase.

English: And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head.
Masaai: Nejoki Yosef papaai lenye, “Ime neijia etiu papaai, amu ore ilo naa ninye olkikau; tipika enkaina ino e tatene shumata endukuya enye.”

English: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.
Masaai: Kake etanya menye tukul nejo, “Ekayiolo olayioni lai, ekayiolo; ekeaku sii ninye kitok; kake ore ake eyia, ekeaku olalashe lenye oti kitok te ninye, ore eishoi enye naa keaku olorere kumok.”

English: And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Masaai: Metaa etamayiana ninye ninche ina olong ejoki, “Te iyie elo Israel aibalie imayianat ejo, ‘Mikintotiwuo Enkai anaa Efraim o Manase;’ ” neaku neija eikuna aitojool Efraim Manase.

English: And Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die: but God shall be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki Israel Yosef, “Ng'ura, etataana enkata pee aye, kake keaku Enkai tenebo iyie, naa aikintoki ayau iyie ina kop o loo papaai lino.

English: Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.
Masaai: Ore ake sii aaishoo iyie neitu aisho ilalashera linono Shekem enkiyopata o ldoinyo, ine wueji nepir naawa too nkaik oo Lamori to lalem lai o te nkawuo ai.”

English: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.
