English: And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh, who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
Masaai: Nejo Yesero, “Meisisi Olaitoriani, laa ninye oitajeu intae aitung'uaa enkaina oo Lmisiri neitung'uaa enkaina e Farao.

English: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.
Masaai: Ayiolo taata ajo eikitok Olaitoriani alang nkaitin pooki, amu eyaua iltung'ana aitung'uaa abori enkaina oo Lmisiri ina kata apa eisikong ninche.”

English: And Jethro, Moses' father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father in law before God.
Masaai: Neitayu Yesero, olaputani le Musa, enkishoroto olasar opejori o nkishorot naapolosakini Enkai, nelotu Aron te nebo ilpayiani pooki loo Siraeli aanya endaa te nebo olaputani le Musa te dukuya Enkai.

English: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood by Moses from the morning unto the evening.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ekenyu neton Musa arish iltung'ana, neitashe iltung'ana aaman Musa ebaiki tadekenya o metaa teipa.

English: And when Moses' father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even?
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol olaputani le Musa nena pooki naasita te nkaraki iltung'ana, nejo, “Kainyoo ena niasita te nkaraki iltung'ana? Kainyoo pee iton openy, nikintashe aaman iltung'ana pooki ebaiki tadekenya o metaa teipa?”

English: And Moses said unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to enquire of God:
Masaai: Nejoki Musa olaputani lenye, “Enkaraki napuonu iltung'ana enatii aaikilikuan mbaa e Nkai;

English: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.
Masaai: ore te neeta enchankar, nepuonu enatii narish nanu oltung'ani o ilo le latia enye, naitayiolo nanu ninche nkitanapat e Nkai o nena naatejo ninye.”

English: And Moses' father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.
Masaai: Nejoki olaputani le Musa ninye, “Ore ena niasita ne me sidai.

English: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
Masaai: Ore iyie o ltung'ana liboitare iariara ate, amu keiroishi ena te iyie; nimindim ataasa openy.

English: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God:
Masaai: Toning'o naa enaajoki amu kaaikok, naa, keaku Enkai te nebo iyie! Taa itii dukuya Enkai;

English: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.
Masaai: ninteng'en ninche nkitanapat o naatejo, nintayiolo ninche enkoitoi napuoyie o enaishiaakino neas.

English: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:
Masaai: Ore ake tegelu iltung'ana oata enkidimata too ltung'ana pooki, lelo ooure Enkai, iltung'ana ooisiligayu neiba eropare; nipik kulo payiani shumata iltung'ana aitaa ilarikok loo nkalifuni, loo maa iip, loo moo onom o loo maa tomon.

English: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.
Masaai: Nincho ninche meiguenare iltung'ana nkatitin pooki; ore pooki bae sapuk neyau enitii kake ore embae kiti nedung oopeny, pee eleleku te iyie nenap sii ninche olola te nebo iyie.

English: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.
Masaai: Te nias ena, anaa enikirikoo Enkai, naa ina kata ibikoo, nepuo sii kulo tung'ana pooki ewueji enye te seriani.”

English: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.
Masaai: Nening Musa enkikoo o laputani lenye neas nena pooki naatejo ninye.

English: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Masaai: Negelu Musa iltung'ana oata enkidimata ti atua Siraeli pooki, neitaa ninche ilukuny oo ltung'ana, ilaitoriak loo nkalifuni, loo maa iip, loo moo onom o loo maa tomon.

English: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.
Masaai: Neiguenare ninche iltung'ana nkatitin pooki; ore ilomon oogol neyaki ninche Musa, kake ore embae pooki kiti nedung oopeny.

English: And Moses let his father in law depart; and he went his way into his own land.
Masaai: Neisho Musa olaputani lenye meshomo, neibung ninye enkoitoi alo enkop enye.

English: In the third month, when the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e dukuya olapa li okuni anaa pee epuo iltung'ana loo Siraeli te nkop e Misiri, ore ina olong nepuonu olpurkel le Sinai.

English: For they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the desert of Sinai, and had pitched in the wilderness; and there Israel camped before the mount.
Masaai: Ore pee edumunye te Refidim aapuonu olpurkel le Sinai neitayu ilng'oborri to lpurkel; ore te ine nepik Isiraeli ilng'oborri dukuya o ldoinyo.

English: And Moses went up unto God, and the LORD called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel;
Masaai: Neked Musa alo enetii Enkai, neipot ninye Olaitoriani to ldoinyo, ejo, “Ena iyie ilo ajoki enkaji e Yakobo, niliki iltung'ana loo Siraeli: ajoki,

English: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto myself.
Masaai: Itoduaa intae enaikuna Ilmisiri, ina natanapa nanu intae too naipuko o lkurragos nayaki intae kewan ai.

English: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
Masaai: Ore naa taata tinining'ining'i oltoilo lai nimbung'ubung'u nkitanapat o sotua lai, niaakuku iltung'ana laainei tukul ti atua iltung'ana pooki; amu ore enkop pooki naa enaai,

English: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.
Masaai: naa iakuku intae te nanu enkitoria oo lapolosak o losho osinya. Kulo ninche irorei lilo ajoki nkera e Israel.”

English: And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and laid before their faces all these words which the LORD commanded him.
Masaai: Nelotu Musa neipot lelo payiani loo ltung'ana, neibalie te dukuya ninche kulo rorei pooki ooitanapa Olaitoriani ninye.

English: And all the people answered together, and said, All that the LORD hath spoken we will do. And Moses returned the words of the people unto the LORD.
Masaai: Newal iltung'ana pooki te nebo nejo, “Ore nena pooki naatejo Olaitoriani eikiaas.” Nelikioo Musa irorei loo ltung'ana to Laitoriani.

English: And the LORD said unto Moses, Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and believe thee for ever. And Moses told the words of the people unto the LORD.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa, “Ng'ura, kalotu nanu te nkatampoi nairrusha, pee etum iltung'ana aatoning te naairorie iyie, pee kitum sii aairuko ntarasi.” Neitoki Musa aliki Olaitoriani irorei loo ltung'ana.

English: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go unto the people, and sanctify them to day and to morrow, and let them wash their clothes,
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa, “Shomo enetii iltung'ana nintisiny ninche taata o taisere, nincho ninche meisuja inkilani enye,

English: And be ready against the third day: for the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.
Masaai: nerretena te nkolong e uni; amu ore te nkolong e uni nelotu Olaitoriani adou enchumata o ldoinyo le Sinai metoduaa iltung'ana.

English: And thou shalt set bounds unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, that ye go not up into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death:
Masaai: Nipikaki iltung'ana olpolosie aitamanaa, ijo, ‘Entodol ake mipuopuo shumata o ldoinyo arashu iseyieyie olpolosie lenye; ore pooki ng'ae ororo oldoinyo neari metua.

English: There shall not an hand touch it, but he shall surely be stoned, or shot through; whether it be beast or man, it shall not live: when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.
Masaai: Nemeetae enkaina naiseyie ninye kake kenang'i too soito arashu eng'ori, aa eng'ues arashu oltung'ani, melo ninye eishu.’ Ore pee eru entarumpeta ayiataa, naa keilepu ninche aapuonu oldoinyo.”

English: And Moses went down from the mount unto the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their clothes.
Masaai: Nedou Musa to ldoinyo alotu enetii iltung'ana, neitisiny ninye iltung'ana neisuj ninche inkilani enye.

English: And he said unto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not at your wives.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye iltung'ana, “Enterretenata te nkolong e uni, nimipuopuo aanyikaki nkituaak.

English: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.
Masaai: Ore takedenya te nkolong e uni, netii ndarat o nkiwuang'at, o enkatampoi nairrusha e nchumata oldoinyio, o endarata sapuk e ntarumpeta, o metaa einkirikirate iltung'ana pooki ootii ilng'oborri.

English: And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.
Masaai: Neyau Musa iltung'ana aitung'uaa ilng'oborri meetu aatumore Enkai; neitashe ninche te ntonata o ldoinyo.

English: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.
Masaai: Neimulumul oldoinyo le Sinai empuruo, amu etadoikio Olaitoriani enchumata enye te nkima, neilep empuruo enye anaa empuruo o lkokuet, neikirikira oldoinyo pooki oleng.

English: And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.
Masaai: Naa ore anaa enadaru embuakunoto e ntarumpeta aponari, neiro Musa, newaliki ninye Enkai te ndarata.

English: And the LORD came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the LORD called Moses up to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.
Masaai: Nelotu Olaitoriani adoiki oldoinyo le Sinai, entopij o ldoinyo; neipot Olaitoriani Musa meshomo entopij o ldoinyo, neilep Musa alo.

English: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go down, charge the people, lest they break through unto the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa, “Tadoi shomo inkoo iltung'ana, melang'u ake olpolosie memuta ake ilkumok lenye.

English: And let the priests also, which come near to the LORD, sanctify themselves, lest the LORD break forth upon them.
Masaai: Nchoo sii lelo apolosak oonyikaki Olaitoriani eitisiny ate, pee maitame ake ninche.”

English: And Moses said unto the LORD, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou chargedst us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.
Masaai: Nejoki Musa Olaitoriani, “Mepuonu iltung'ana aailepu oldoinyo le Sinai; amu iyie enkorrok ino oitanapa iyiook, ajo, ‘Entayu ilpolosien to ldoinyo, nintisinyinyi ninye.’ ”

English: And the LORD said unto him, Away, get thee down, and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up unto the LORD, lest he break forth upon them.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani ninye “Tadoi shomo pee ilepu ayau Aron te nebo iyie; kake mincho ilapolosak o ltung'ana elang'u olpolosie aailepu enetii Olaitoriani menang'are ake Olaitoriani ninche.”

English: So Moses went down unto the people, and spake unto them.
Masaai: Nelo Musa adoyio enetii iltung'ana neliki ninche.

English: And God spake all these words, saying,
Masaai: Neiro Olaitoriani kulo rorei pooki ajo,

English: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Masaai: “Ara nanu Olaitoriani Enkai ino, ilo likiyau aitung'uaa enkop e Misiri, aitung'uaa enkaji e sinkaisho.

English: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Masaai: Miaata ake kulie aitin te dukuya nanu.

English: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:
Masaai: Mintobiraki kewan enkitanyaanyukoto nagueta, arashu ae nanyaanyukie ae toki te shumata te keper arashu enatii abori enkop, arashu enatii atua tiabori enkop.

English: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;
Masaai: Mirrugokino ninche arashu isiaai ninche; amu ore nanu Olaitoriani Enkai ino ara Enkai olom, naitusuj nkera nkitarruorrot oo loo menye o metabaiki eishoi e uni o eni ong'uan e lelo laaiba nanu,

English: And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.
Masaai: kake kaitodolu enyorrata nauno too nkalifuni e lelo laanyor nanu neibung nkitanapat aainei.

English: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
Masaai: “Mimpot aasishore enkarna o Laitoriani Enkai ino pesho amu meikenaa Olaitoriani ajo meeta enkitarruoroto ilo oipot enkarna enye pesho.

English: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Masaai: “Tadamu enkolong e Sabato, inchoo eaku sinyati.

English: Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:
Masaai: Too nkolong'i ile taasisho, nias isiaaitin inono pooki;

English: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
Masaai: kake ore te nkolong e naapishana naa sabato to Laitoriani Enkai ino; ore te ina olong nimiaas hoo ae siaai, iyie arashu olayioni lino, arashu entito ino, o sinka lino lee, arashu esinka ino, arashu inkishu inono, arashu olomoni otii atua enkang ino.

English: For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
Masaai: Amu too nkolong'i ile eitobira Olaitoriani shumata o enkop, o enaiposha, o nena pooki naatii atua ninche, neyeng'iyeng'a te nkolong e naapishana. Metaa etamayiana Olaitoriani enkolong e naapishana neitaa sinyati.

English: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
Masaai: “Iyanyita minyi o ng'utunyi pee eaku inkolong'i inono kumok te ina kop nikincho Olaitoriani Enkai ino.

English: Thou shalt not kill.
Masaai: “Miar metua.

English: Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Masaai: “Miloloito.

English: Thou shalt not steal.
Masaai: “Mipurrisho.

English: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
Masaai: “Minteeniki ilo le latia ino elejare.

English: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.
Masaai: “Ming'uar enkaji e ilo le latia ino; ming'uar enkitok e ilo le latia ino, arashu osinka lenye, arashu esinka enye, arashu olkiteng lenye, arashu osikiria lenye, arashu hoo ae toki ole latia ino.”

English: And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they removed, and stood afar off.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening iltung'ana pooki ndarat nedol inkiwuang'at, o embuakunoto e ntarumpeta o empuruo to ldoinyo, neirut iltung'ana neikirikira, nelamari aaitashe tenelakua.

English: And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche Musa, “Irorie iyie iyiook, amu eikining; kake nchoo metaa mme Enkai nairorie iyiook, mikiye ake.”

English: And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not.
Masaai: Nejoki Musa iltung'ana, “Emiureshoyu, amu keewuo ake Enkai atem intae, pee aa ore euriata enye nelotu dukuya nkonyek inyi, pee miasiasa ake ing'ok.”

English: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.
Masaai: Nelamari iltung'ana aaitashe te nelakua, etaa kenyikaki Musa ina aimin nairrusha te ine netii Enkai.

English: And the LORD said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa, “Ena tiaaki iltung'ana loo Siraeli: ‘Itoduaakita ntae ate nchere airorie nanu intae atii keper.

English: Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold.
Masaai: Mintayuyu nkaitin e nkosholai pee eaku te nebo nanu, nimintaikiki sii ate nkaitin e sahabu.

English: An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in all places where I record my name I will come unto thee, and I will bless thee.
Masaai: Olperere le nkulupuoni ninye kintaikiki nanu nikipolosakiki te nchumata enye ilasarri linyi oo pejori o lasarri linyi le seriani; enker inyi o lkiteng linyi. Ore pooki wueji nagelu metadamunyeki enkarna ai naa kalotu enitii namayian intae.

English: And if thou wilt make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stone: for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.
Masaai: Naa ti nikintaikiki intae nanu olperere lo lasar loo soito, mishetutu too soito oogueta, amu ti niguetiguete te ntolu nisarkionienie.

English: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon.
Masaai: Nimikedikede too nkedeta olperere lai lo lasar, pee mimbalayuyu nchere michopopo.’

English: Now these are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.
Masaai: “Kuna ninche nkitanapat nipik dukuya ninche.

English: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.
Masaai: Ti ninyiang'u orrindik loo Lhebrania, neasisho ninye ilarin ile, ore to lari liopishana neipang ninye alo elakuno, nemelak toki.

English: If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he were married, then his wife shall go out with him.
Masaai: Tenaa keewuo apa aa ninye ake, nelo ninye aa ninye ake; te neewuo apa eyamishe nelo enkitok enye te nebo ninye.

English: If his master have given him a wife, and she have born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out by himself.
Masaai: Te neishoo apa olkitok lenye enkitok neiki ninye ilayiok arashu ntoyie, neaku enkitok o nkera enyena ino lkitok lenye nelo ninye openy.

English: And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free:
Masaai: Kake te neibalunye orrindik ajo, ‘Kanyor olkitok lai, o enkitok ai, o nkera aainei; malo nanu alakunoyu,’

English: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.
Masaai: neyau olkitok lenye enetii Enkai, neyau ninye kutuk aji arashu ntaloishin e kutuk aji neud olkitok lenye enkiok enye to ltidu; neisiaai ninye te nkishui pooki.

English: And if a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.
Masaai: “Te nemir oltung'ani entito enye aitaa errindik nemelo ae kata anaa enapuo irrindiki lewa.

English: If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.
Masaai: Te nemeitiship olkitok lenye, laa ninye otisiraka kewan, neisho ninye meinyiang'uni ninye, meeta ninye esipata namirakinye iltung'ana loo loreren amu etonyorra apa ninye te sunkureisho.

English: And if he have betrothed her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.
Masaai: Te nesiraki oltung'ani olayioni lenye entito rrindik neiko ninye anaa entito enye.

English: If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.
Masaai: Te neyamaki kewan enkitok e are nemeitong'or endaa enye, o nkilani enyena o enjung'ore e ina kitok botor.

English: And if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money.
Masaai: Naa te nemeitaas olee ninye kuna pokira uni, nelo ninye aing'uaa ninye pesho, metii elaata oo mpisai.

English: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae oosh oltung'ani near metua, neari metua.

English: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.
Masaai: Kake te neitu eirrag arreshu ninye, kake Enkai ake natorikoyie metabatatakinoyu inkaik enyena, naa kegelaki intae ewueji naa ninye eisikaki.

English: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
Masaai: Kake te neotiki oltung'ani aitirraki olikae pee ear metua, ewaita intae ninye aaitung'uaa olperere lai pee eye.

English: And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae oosh menye arashu ng'otonye neari metua.

English: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae opurroo oltung'ani, pee emir arashu etumi ninye ti atua imasaa enyena, neari metua.

English: And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae odek menye arashu ng'otonye neari metua.

English: And if men strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keepeth his bed:
Masaai: “Te neishankarra iltung'ana neosh obo olikae to soit arashu te nkaina neitu eye oltung'ani eirraga te rruat,

English: If he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.
Masaai: ore pee edumunye ilo nelo te ntirma, ore ilo otoosho ninye nelakuni; kake elak ina kata naiturrayie neing'or ninye o meishiu alaari.

English: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall be surely punished.
Masaai: “Te nedumu oltung'ani eng'udi neosh orrindik lenye, aa olee arashu enkitok, neye orrindik te ine, neitamei ilo tung'ani.

English: Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.
Masaai: Kake te neitu eye orrindik te nkolong nabo arashu too nkolong'i are, nemeitamei amu ore orrindik naa impisai enyena.

English: If men strive, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart from her, and yet no mischief follow: he shall be surely punished, according as the woman's husband will lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.
Masaai: “Te neara iltung'ana nepik entuaa olbae o metapololoyu, nemetii ae torroni natusuja, ore ilo otipika ninye olbae neitalaki te risioroto e nkitalakunoto naitalak ninye olpayian le ina kitok; nelak anaa enanyorraa iladung'ok le nkiguana.

English: And if any mischief follow, then thou shalt give life for life,
Masaai: Te nesuju ae torroni neitalakuni enkishui te nkishui,

English: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
Masaai: enkong'u te nkong'u, olalae to lalae, enkaina te nkaina, enkeju te nkeju,

English: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
Masaai: enkinosata e nkima te nkinosata e nkima, olbae to lbae, olkordata to lkordata.

English: And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, that it perish; he shall let him go free for his eye's sake.
Masaai: “Te neosh oltung'ani enkong'u o rrindik lenye, olee arashu enkitok, neitarruoo, neisho ninye ilo rrindik meshomo te nkaraki enkong'u.

English: And if he smite out his manservant's tooth, or his maidservant's tooth; he shall let him go free for his tooth's sake.
Masaai: Te neitayu olalae lo rrindik lenye, olee arashu enkitok, nelo ilo rrindik te nkaraki olalae.

English: If an ox gore a man or a woman, that they die: then the ox shall be surely stoned, and his flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be quit.
Masaai: “Te near olkiteng oltung'ani lee arashu enkitok metua, neari ilo kiteng too soito metua; nemenyae inkiri enyena; ore olopeny ilo kiteng nelakuni.

English: But if the ox were wont to push with his horn in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, but that he hath killed a man or a woman; the ox shall be stoned, and his owner also shall be put to death.
Masaai: Kake te netamoo ilo kiteng ear iltung'ana, neikooki olopeny neany ening, near ilo kiteng metua olee arashu enkitok, neari ilo kiteng too soito metua, neari sii olopeny metua.

English: If there be laid on him a sum of money, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatsoever is laid upon him.
Masaai: Naa te neigeroki metawalu enkishui enye nelak ninye meitajeu enkishui enye esiana pooki naba anaa enatudung'okoki.

English: Whether he have gored a son, or have gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done unto him.
Masaai: Te near olkiteng olayioni le likae tung'ani arashu entito, neiguanareki olopeny te risioroto ena kitanapata nabo.

English: If the ox shall push a manservant or a maidservant; he shall give unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
Masaai: “Te near olkiteng orrindik metua, olee arashu enkitok, neisho olopeny olkitok le ilo rrindiki shekeli tomoni uni e nkosholai. Neari ilo kiteng too soito metua.

English: And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit, and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein;
Masaai: “Te neing'uaa oltung'ani engumoto menuka arashu te netur oltung'ani engumoto nemenuk, nedoiki olkiteng arashu osikiria atua,

English: The owner of the pit shall make it good, and give money unto the owner of them; and the dead beast shall be his.
Masaai: neitobir olopeny ina gumoto neisho impisai olopeny o lkiteng o sikiria neaku ina natua enenye.

English: And if one man's ox hurt another's, that he die; then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the money of it; and the dead ox also they shall divide.
Masaai: “Te near olkiteng le likae tung'ani olkiteng le likae metua nemir ninche ilo kiteng oishu neor impisai enyena. Neor sii ina ng'ues natua.

English: Or if it be known that the ox hath used to push in time past, and his owner hath not kept him in; he shall surely pay ox for ox; and the dead shall be his own.
Masaai: Naa te neyioloi aajo etamoo oshi ilo kiteng earisho neitu eing'or olopeny, nelak ninye olkiteng to lkiteng neaku ina ng'ues natua enenye.

English: If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
Masaai: “Te nepurroo oltung'ani olkiteng arashu enker, neyieng arashu emir, nelak ninye ilmong'i imiet to lkiteng obo, o nkerra ong'uan te nker nabo.

English: If a thief be found breaking up, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed for him.
Masaai: Meeta nchere melak ninye ina toki natupurroyie. Te nemeeta ninye toki, nemiri ninye anaa orrindik, pee elak ina natupurroyie.

English: If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
Masaai: Te netumi ina ng'ues natupurroyie ninye ti atua imasaa enyena, aa enkiteng, osikiria arashu enker nelak ninye are te nabo.

English: If the theft be certainly found in his hand alive, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep; he shall restore double.
Masaai: Te neibung'i olapurroni egilita enkaji kewarie neari metua; ore ilo otaara ninye metua nemeeta iloikop. Kake tenaa dama ekenyua neeta ninye iloikop.

English: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feed in another man's field; of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.
Masaai: “Te neisho oltung'ani inkishu edaa te nkurma anaa te nkurma oo sabibu anaa epalaa enkiteng meshomo ainos enkurma e likae tung'ani meeta nchere pee meitalakuni teina naisul naing'uaa enkurma enye oo sabibu.

English: If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field, be consumed therewith; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
Masaai: Te nenya enkima enkop, neibung ilkiku o metaa ore enkanasa nateenaki arashu enkano naitashe arashu enkurma nabulu einosa enkima, ore ilo oinua enkima nelak pooki.

English: If a man shall deliver unto his neighbour money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man's house; if the thief be found, let him pay double.
Masaai: “Te neisho oltung'ani ole latia enye impisai arashu ntokitin metushuma, nepurrorri te nkaji enye, ore te netumi olapurroni, nelak ninye katitin are.

English: If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall be brought unto the judges, to see whether he have put his hand unto his neighbour's goods.
Masaai: Te neitu etumi olapurroni, ore ilo openy e nkaji nelotu ataaniki Enkai, aitodolu tenaa ketipika ninye enkaina enye atua intokitin ole latia enye arashu eitu epik.

English: For all manner of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing, which another challengeth to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double unto his neighbour.
Masaai: “Ore olomoni pooki opong'oreki, tenaa te nkaraki olkiteng anaa, enkaraki osikiria, anaa enkaraki enker, anaa enkaraki nkilani, arashu pooki toki naimina najoyie oltung'ani, ‘Ninye ena’, neyauni enchankar oo nkaloli pokira dukuya Enkai; ore ilo odung'oki Enkai enkiguana nelaaki katitin are ilo le latia enye.

English: If a man deliver unto his neighbour an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, no man seeing it:
Masaai: “Te neisho oltung'ani ole latia enye osikiria arashu olkiteng, arashu enker, arashu ae ng'ues pooki meing'ura, neye, arashu etum olbae, arashu eyae, eitu eduaaya hoo ng'ae,

English: Then shall an oath of the LORD be between them both, that he hath not put his hand unto his neighbour's goods; and the owner of it shall accept thereof, and he shall not make it good.
Masaai: neaku olmumai to Laitoriani erishata enye pokira pee edoli tenaa ketipika ninye enkaina enye atua imasaa e ilo le latia enye. Nenyorraa olopeny olmumai nemeitalaku enyamu.

English: And if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.
Masaai: Naa tenaa ketupurroyioki too nkaik enyena, nelaaki naa ninye olopeny.

English: If it be torn in pieces, then let him bring it for witness, and he shall not make good that which was torn.
Masaai: Tenaa ing'uesi e ntim naatara nchoo ninye eyau shakenisho; nemelak ninye enyamu te ina nataara ing'uesi e ntim.

English: And if a man borrow ought of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof being not with it, he shall surely make it good.
Masaai: “Te neisilenoo oltung'ani ae toki to le latia enye, netum olbae arashu eye metii olopeny, nelak enyamu pooki.

English: But if the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be an hired thing, it came for his hire.
Masaai: Naa te netii olopeny te nebo ina kiteng nemelak. Tenaa entoki apa naisilenuoki aasishore nelakieki enatoning'oteki.

English: And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.
Masaai: “Te neirorie oltung'ani entito neitu eyami, neboitare ninye, neishoru ninye ntokitin e nkaputi te nkaraki ninye, neitaa ninye enkitok enye.

English: If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
Masaai: Te neany menye eisho ninye meyama, nelaaki impisai naarisiore ine nkiyama oo ntoyie neitu ae kata eyiolou olee.

English: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
Masaai: “Taara metua enkasakutoni.

English: Whosoever lieth with a beast shall surely be put to death.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae ololoitore eng'ues neari metua.

English: He that sacrificeth unto any god, save unto the LORD only, he shall be utterly destroyed.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae opolosaki kulie aitin neme Olaitoriani ake neitarruorri tukul.

English: Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Masaai: “Eminyal olomoni arashu imbooki ninye enkop, amu irara sii apa intae ilomon te nkop e Misiri.

English: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.
Masaai: Minosie osina enkoliai arashu enkerai okishi.

English: If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry;
Masaai: Naa ti ninosie ninche osina naaishiraki ninche nanu, naa kaning nanu olkiyioi lenye,

English: And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
Masaai: neyupuyup engoro ai, naar nanu intae to lalem, neaku inkituaak inyi inkolia, neaku inkera inyi okishin.

English: If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.
Masaai: “Ti nisilenoki impisai obo loo ltung'ana laainei otii atua intae ora aisinani, mitiu te ninye anaa oloitalaku esile niming'oru dupoto te ninye.

English: If thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, thou shalt deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down:
Masaai: Te nelo niya olkila le ilo le latia ino pee intalakunye esile tushukoki ninye eitu edoyio enkolong,

English: For that is his covering only, it is his raiment for his skin: wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.
Masaai: amu ninye ake eitoipore, ninye enkitoipet to sesen lenye; kainyoo naa eitoipore? Naa te naaishiraki ninye nanu, naning amu kara oloata olng'ur.

English: Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.
Masaai: “Misukeny Enkai nimidek olarikoni loo ltung'ana linono.

English: Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.
Masaai: “Mimutie te nkishorunoto e nkiputakinoto e nkisampuare ino o te mborei nadooyo e naisho oo sabibu. “Ore olkikau loo layiok linono nikincho nanu.

English: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.
Masaai: Ninko sii neijia too lmong'i o too ntare; nchoo eboitare ng'otonye too nkolong'i naapishana; ore te nkolong' e naapishana nikincho nanu.

English: And ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.
Masaai: “Iakuku intae iltung'ana ooitisinyaki te nkaraki nanu; metaa eminyanya inkiri oo ng'uesi naatara lowuarak, enchoo ildiein.

English: Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
Masaai: “Mintayuyu intae ilomon le lejare. Mimbung'arere oltung'ani torrono aaitayu enchakenisho e lejare.

English: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:
Masaai: Mirubarere esiamo aas intorrok, nimintayuyu shakenisho te nkiguana aarubare esiamo pee inturraa esipata.

English: Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.
Masaai: Nimintodolu olkep to ltung'ani aisinani te nkiguana enye.

English: If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.
Masaai: “Ti ninang'arere enkiteng arashu osikiria lo lmanga'tinta lino eimina tushukoki ninye.

English: If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.
Masaai: Ti nidol osikiria li obo likimba etepetikia olola enkop, nimilo aing'uaa, taretoki ninye metudumu olola.

English: Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause.
Masaai: “Mintapong'oo esipata naipirakinore ilo aisinani te nkiguana enye.

English: Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.
Masaai: Talama enkitang'oroto e lejare, nimiar metua ole meeta entioto o lasipani, amu maikenaki nanu esipata olarruoni.

English: And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.
Masaai: Niming'amu entoki e ropare, amu ore eropare naa keitamodok ilkituaak neinyal erishata e lelo loo sipat.

English: Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger: for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Masaai: “Misoruru olomoni, iyiololo oltau lo lomoni, amu irara apa intae ilomon te nkop e Misiri.

English: And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the fruits thereof:
Masaai: “Too larin ile entuun nisampumpu nkurman inyi;

English: But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.
Masaai: kake ore to lari li opishana nipalipala nimisampumpu hoo ae toki nabulu. Pee enya ilaisinak le lelo tung'ana linyi; ore inaaleku nenya ing'uesi e ntim. Ninkoko neijia too sabibu linyi o too lng'anayio linyi.

English: Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed.
Masaai: “Entaas esiaai inyi too nkolong'i ile, kake ore te nkolong e naapishana niyeng'iyeng'a pee etum olkiteng lino o sikiria lino enkiyeng'iyengata, negolu olayioni le rrindik ino o ilo dokunoti.

English: And in all things that I have said unto you be circumspect: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.
Masaai: Embung'a nena pooki natiaaka intae, nimimpotipoto ake nkarn e kulie aitin arashu minchosho metoning'i eimu nkutukie inyi.

English: Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.
Masaai: “Katitin uni to lari kintobiraki nanu osirua.

English: Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Abib; for in it thou camest out from Egypt: and none shall appear before me empty:)
Masaai: Imbung'a osirua loo mukateni neitu eisuijieki, anaa apa enaaitanapa, ninya imukateni neitu eisuijieki too nkolong'i naapishana te nkolong natudung'oki olapa le Abibu amu te ninye apa itupukutuo aaing'uaa Misiri. Meetae oltung'ani olotu dukuya nanu too nkaik naarook.

English: And the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou hast sown in the field: and the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.
Masaai: Imbung'a osirua le nkisampuare, oo lng'anayio le dukuya le siaai ino, te nena nintera aun ti atua enkurma, imbung'a osirua le nkiturrurrorre te nkiting'oto o lari, ti ninturrur te nkurma lelo ng'anayio le siaai ino.

English: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord GOD.
Masaai: Katitin uni to lari epuonu ilewa linyi pooki dukuya o Laitoriani Enkai.

English: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning.
Masaai: “Mintayu osarge lo lasar lai te nebo imukateni naaisuijieki arashu inchosho eilata o sirua lai eirrag o mekenyu.

English: The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the LORD thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.
Masaai: “Ore ilng'anayio ooituruku le lelo le dukuya le nkop ino iyau enkaji o Laitoriani Enkai ino. Miyierie, olkuoo kule e ng'otonye.

English: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.
Masaai: “Ng'ura, airriwaa olmalaika dukuya iyie, pee kirrip iyie te nkoitoi, nikiyau iyie ewueji naidipa aitobira.

English: Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
Masaai: Toning'o ninye nias enajo, migolong'aki ninye, amu mikipalaki ninye enkitarruoroto ino; amu etii enkarna ai atua ninye.

English: But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.
Masaai: “Kake ti nining asipu oltoilo lenye nias nena pooki najo, naaku nanu olmang'atinta loo lmang'ati linono nagilunore lelo likigilunore iyie.

English: For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.
Masaai: “Te nelo olmalaika lai dukuya intae, neyau intae atua Ilamori, o Ilhiti, o Ilperesi, o Ilkanaani, o Ilhifi, o Ilyebusi, te najutu nanu ninche, (aishu),

English: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.
Masaai: nimirrugokino iyie inkaitin enye, arashu aisiaai ninche, arashu aas anaa enaishiaakino isiaatin enye, kake tusulai ninche tukul nibel ing'apeta enye metaa mbelat.

English: And ye shall serve the LORD your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.
Masaai: Olaitoriani Enkai ino isiayia, naa kamayian nanu emukate ino o enkare ino; naiwuang'ie emueyian ti atua intae.

English: There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I will fulfil.
Masaai: Ore te nkop ino nemetii enkitok naibiru arashu enkolupi. Kaaisho nanu iyie enkishui naado.

English: I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.
Masaai: Kairriu nanu olkirutoto lai meshomo te dukuya ntae napik enkiuyiaui iltung'ana pooki likiarare naisho ilmang'ati linono pooki mikimbelekenyata aailany.

English: And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
Masaai: Kapik nanu ilmang'ati linono enkuretisho, naaraa Ilhifi, o Ilkanaani o Ilhiti mikishomo aaing'uaa.

English: I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee.
Masaai: Maaraa nanu ninche meshomo te dukuya iyie to lari obo, pee meaku ake enkop ailitani neponari ilowuarak le ntim nikintanyamal.

English: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.
Masaai: Maakutiti maa kutiti aaraa ninche meshomo te dukuya iyie, metaba anaa niponari nimbung enkop.

English: And I will set thy bounds from the Red sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand; and thou shalt drive them out before thee.
Masaai: Napik nanu olpolosie lino ebaiki Enaiposha Nanyokie o metabaiki enaiposha oo Lfilisti, o ebaiki olpurkel o metabaiki olkeju le Frati; amu kayau lelo oomanya enkop apik enkaina ino, niaraa iyie ninche te dukuya iyie.

English: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
Masaai: Mining'ore aitayunye osotua ninche arashu te nebo nkaitin enye.

English: They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.
Masaai: Metoni ninche te nkop ino, pee mikipik ake easata oo ng'ok ti alo nanu; amu ti nisiaai nkaitin enye meeta nchere pee meaku ina orreshet te iyie.”

English: And he said unto Moses, Come up unto the LORD, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship ye afar off.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye Musa, “Ilepu wou enetii Olaitoriani, iyie o Aron, o Nadabu, o Abihu o lpayiani ntomoni naapishana loo Siraeli, enteserem te nelakua.

English: And Moses alone shall come near the LORD: but they shall not come nigh; neither shall the people go up with him.
Masaai: Musa ake olotu ataaniki Olaitoriani, kake mepuonu ilkulikae aanyiku, nemeilepu iltung'ana te nebo ninye.”

English: And Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD, and all the judgments: and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which the LORD hath said will we do.
Masaai: Nelotu Musa, neliki iltung'ana irorei pooki lo Laitoriani o nkitanapat pooki; newalu iltung'ana pooki to ltoilo obo nejo, “Ore irorei pooki ooiroro Olaitoriani naa eikiaas.”

English: And Moses wrote all the words of the LORD, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the hill, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
Masaai: Neiger Musa irorei pooki lo Laitoriani. Nedumunye ayooki tadekenya neshet olperere lo lasar te ntonata o ldoinyo, o ng'apeta tomon o are aitorisioki iloshon tomon o are loo Siraeli.

English: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, which offered burnt offerings, and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen unto the LORD.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ilbarnot loo ltung'ana loo Siraeli, ooitaituo nkishorot oo ilasarri oopejori nepolosaki Olaitoriani nkishorot, ilasarri le seriani oo lmong'i.

English: And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basons; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
Masaai: Nedumu Musa olpisiai lo sarge nepik ingirran, ore olikae pisiai lo sarge nebukoki olperere.

English: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient.
Masaai: Neitoki adumu embuku osotua neisomaki iltung'ana metoning'o; nejo ninche, “Ore nena pooki naatejo Olaitoriani naa eikiaas, naa eikining'ishoyu iyiook.”

English: And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you concerning all these words.
Masaai: Nedumu Musa osarge neisuaaki iltung'ana nejo, “Eng'ura osarge lo sotua oitobira Olaitoriani o ntae te risioroto e kulo rorei pooki.”

English: Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel:
Masaai: Neitoki Musa o Aron, o Nadabu o Abihu o lpayiani ntomoni naapishana loo Siraeli aailep,

English: And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.
Masaai: nedol ninche Enkai oo Siraeli, netii abori nkejek enyena entoki neeijo oltiren oitobiraki too soito sidain, ooikununo anaa keper te mua.

English: And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: also they saw God, and did eat and drink.
Masaai: Neitu ninye eiteleiki enkaina enye lelo arikok loo ltung'ana loo Siraeli; nedol ninche Enkai, neokisho nedaa.

English: And the LORD said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa, “Ilepu wou enatii to ldoinyo, nianyisho te ine; naa kaaisho nanu isoito dapashi, te nebo nkitanapat, naigero nanu te nkaraki enkiteng'enare enye.”

English: And Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua: and Moses went up into the mount of God.
Masaai: Nedumunye Musa te nebo osinka lenye Yoshua, neilep Musa alo atua oldoinyo le Nkai.

English: And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until we come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: if any man have any matters to do, let him come unto them.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilpayiani, “Entaanyu iyiook tene o metaba anaa nikintoki aapuonu enitii, naa ng'ura, etii Aron o Huri te nebo intae; ore pooki ng'ae oata enyamali nchoo elo enetii ninche.”

English: And Moses went up into the mount, and a cloud covered the mount.
Masaai: Neilep Musa alo oldoinyo, neitoip enkatampoi oldoinyo,

English: And the glory of the LORD abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
Masaai: neton enkitoo e Nkai to ldoinyo le Sinai neitoip enkatampoi inkolong'i ile; ore te nkolong e naapishana neipot ninye Musa ti atua ina atampoi.

English: And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel.
Masaai: Ore eloito e nkitoo o Laitoriani neikununo anaa enkima nayupuyup te nchumata o ldoinyo te dukuya iltung'ana loo Siraeli.

English: And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and gat him up into the mount: and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.
Masaai: Nejing Musa atua enkatampoi neilepaki oldoinyo. Netii apa Musa oldoinyo nkolong'i artam o nkewaritin artam.

English: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Musa,

English: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me an offering: of every man that giveth it willingly with his heart ye shall take my offering.
Masaai: “Irorie iltung'ana loo Siraeli, pee aaitaiki enkishoroto. Tang'amu enkishoroto te rishata ai te pooki tung'ani otonyorra aishoru to lpela, ning'amu iyie enkishoroto te nkaraki nanu.

English: And this is the offering which ye shall take of them; gold, and silver, and brass,
Masaai: Naa ena enkishoroto ning'amu te ninche: sahabu, o enkosholai, o suyai,

English: And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair,
Masaai: nkarash pusi o sinteti, o naanyokie, o katani napuyiapui o lpapit loo nkineji,

English: And rams' skins dyed red, and badgers' skins, and shittim wood,
Masaai: ndapan naanota oo lmeregeshi, o ndapan oo nkineji, imbaoi oo lera,

English: Oil for the light, spices for anointing oil, and for sweet incense,
Masaai: eilata oo ltaai, o enkorropil o te ilata naaputishoreki o te rropili o lbani,

English: Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.
Masaai: o soito barrikon ooji oniks o lkulikae soito oopiki olkila lo lapolosani kitok o ina bene enye o lgoo.

English: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.
Masaai: Nchoo ninche aaitobiraki nanu ewueji nesinya, pee atum atotona ti atua ninche.

English: According to all that I shew thee, after the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the instruments thereof, even so shall ye make it.
Masaai: Anaa nena pooki naaitodol iyie naaipirta olchetei to lng'obor lo Laitoriani o masaa enyena pooki, neaku intobir aiko neijia.

English: And they shall make an ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
Masaai: “Naa keitobir ninche osanduku too nkeek o lerai; intemat are o lpisiai enkadoro, entemata nabo o lpisiai endapasho, naa entemata nabo o lpisiai enkilepata.

English: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, within and without shalt thou overlay it, and shalt make upon it a crown of gold round about.
Masaai: Nimur ninye te sahabu nasila, nintoip oriong o atua, nipik enkamanaa e sahabu aitaman ninye.

English: And thou shalt cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in the four corners thereof; and two rings shall be in the one side of it, and two rings in the other side of it.
Masaai: Nipik ilgiso oong'uan le sahabu oonapieki, nipik ninche nkejek enyena pokira ong'uan, ilgiso oare te nchoto enye nabo, o lgiso oare te nkae shoto enye.

English: And thou shalt make staves of shittim wood, and overlay them with gold.
Masaai: Nintayu ing'apeta oo nkeek o lchani oji olerai, nimur ninche te sahabu.

English: And thou shalt put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, that the ark may be borne with them.
Masaai: Nipik nena bokishi atua lelo giso too mbat o sanduku pee enapieki ilo sanduku.

English: The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.
Masaai: Netoni nena keek, ti atua lelo giso too mbat o sanduku pee enapieki ilo sanduku; nemeitayuni aaitung'uaa ninye.

English: And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee.
Masaai: Nipik atua osanduku ina shakenisho naaishoo nanu iyie.

English: And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
Masaai: Nintoki aitayu olorika lo lng'ur le sahabu nasila; laa intemat are o lpisiai enkadoro naa entemata nabo o lpisiai endapasho.

English: And thou shalt make two cherubims of gold, of beaten work shalt thou make them, in the two ends of the mercy seat.
Masaai: Nipik ilmalaika oare ooji ilkerubi le sahabu; te nkidong'ore intobir ninche, too nkaloli pokira are e ilo orika lo lng'ur.

English: And make one cherub on the one end, and the other cherub on the other end: even of the mercy seat shall ye make the cherubims on the two ends thereof.
Masaai: Intayu olkerubi obo te nkalo nabo nintayu olikae te nkae shoto; te ntoki nabo intobira lelo kerubi o ilo orika lo lng'ur too nkaloli enyena pokira are.

English: And the cherubims shall stretch forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall look one to another; toward the mercy seat shall the faces of the cherubims be.
Masaai: Nelak lelo kerubi inaipuko enye aaitushur olorika lo lng'ur too naipuko enye, neipira nkomomi enye eing'orita lkerubi ilo sanduku.

English: And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.
Masaai: Naa eipik ilo orika lo lng'ur enchumata o sanduku; ore atua ilo sanduku nipik ina shakenisho naaisho nanu.

English: And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.
Masaai: Te ine nanu aalotu atumore, naa te shumata olorika lo lng'ur o te rishata e lelo kerubi ootii enchumata o sanduku le nchakenisho, aairorie nanu iyie ti alo nena pooki naaisho nanu iyie too nkitanapat te nkaraki itung'ana loo Siraeli.

English: Thou shalt also make a table of shittim wood: two cubits shall be the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
Masaai: “Naa ntobira emesa oo nkeek olerai ntemat are enkadoro, naa entemata nabo endapasho, naa entemata nabo o lpisiai enkilepata.

English: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, and make thereto a crown of gold round about.
Masaai: Imulumula te sahabu nasila nipik enkamanaa e sahabu.

English: And thou shalt make unto it a border of an hand breadth round about, and thou shalt make a golden crown to the border thereof round about.
Masaai: Nipik aitaman enkamanaa e ntemata e ndapasho endap

English: And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that are on the four feet thereof.
Masaai: naa ntobiraki ilgiso oo ng'uan le sahabu nieniki lelo giso ilpijat pokira oong'uan too nkejek enyena pokira ong'uan.

English: Over against the border shall the rings be for places of the staves to bear the table.
Masaai: Neirrag lelo giso te mbata e nkamanaa pee eimieki nena bokishi naanapieki emesa.

English: And thou shalt make the staves of shittim wood, and overlay them with gold, that the table may be borne with them.
Masaai: Nintayuyu mbokishi o lerai nimur te sahabu naa kuna enapieki emesa.

English: And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and spoons thereof, and covers thereof, and bowls thereof, to cover withal: of pure gold shalt thou make them.
Masaai: Naa intobir isaanini enyena e nkorropil o masaa enyena naapikunyeki olasar opikuni te sahabu nasila ntobir ninche.

English: And thou shalt set upon the table shewbread before me alway.
Masaai: Nipik emukate e Nkitaduaaroto emesa dukuya nanu anaake.

English: And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same.
Masaai: “Naa intobir enkitashet e sahabu nasila napiki iltaai. Ore entonata o empolos enye neitobiri te siaai e nkidong'ore; ore nkikompeni enyena, o neeigululu enyena, o ntapuka enyena neitaae pooki nabo o enkitashet.

English: And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side:
Masaai: Nepiki ilng'osil ile ooiipang too nkaloli enyena, ilng'osil okuni te nkibung'et te nkalo nabo o lng'osil okuni te nkibung'et te nkae alo enye;

English: Three bowls made like unto almonds, with a knop and a flower in one branch; and three bowls made like almonds in the other branch, with a knop and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick.
Masaai: netii ake nkikompeni uni naikunuaki anaa intapuka o lgulului, eeta ake nabo eneigululu o entapukai, to lng'osila obo, o nkikompeni uni naikunuaki anaa ntapuka o lgulului, meetae ake ene meeta eneigululu o entapukai, to likae ng'osila, netiu neijia pokira ile ooipang'u te ina kibung'et.

English: And in the candlestick shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers.
Masaai: Ore te nkitashet kewan netii inkikompeni ong'uan naikunuaki anaa ilgululu, eeta ineigululu o ntapuka,

English: And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick.
Masaai: netii ake eneigululu nabo abori ilng'osil oare o oiriamari te lelo ngosil ile le ina kitashet.

English: Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold.
Masaai: Ore nena kiyiaa enye oo ntapuka o lng'osil lenye neitaa entoki nabo o ninye; neaku pooki entoki nabo e siaai naidong'uoki te sahabu nasila.

English: And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.
Masaai: Nintaiki iltaai oopishana, nepiki iltaai pee eitawang'aki dukuya enye.

English: And the tongs thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, shall be of pure gold.
Masaai: Ore intokitin naarieki iltaai o neeiteleikini naa ile sahabu nasila.

English: Of a talent of pure gold shall he make it, with all these vessels.
Masaai: Te ntalanta nabo e sahabu eitobiri te nebo kuna masaa pooki.

English: And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.
Masaai: Ning'or nchere, intobira te nkitanyaanyukoto enye, apa nikintoduaaki to ldoinyo.

English: Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: with cherubims of cunning work shalt thou make them.
Masaai: “Ore ake tenebo nena intobira, olng'obor le Nkai too lkarash le katani napuyiapui tomon, pusi, o lmorijo o lpilei, neripakini ilkerubi te nkarriayiano oleng.

English: The length of one curtain shall be eight and twenty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and every one of the curtains shall have one measure.
Masaai: Ore enkadoro, e pooki karasha nchoo eaku intemat tikitam o isiet enkadoro, ore endapasho e pooki karasha naa intemat ong'uan endapasho. Nerisioroyu ilkarash pooki.

English: The five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.
Masaai: Nchoo eripi ilkarash imiet aaibung'ie te nebo, neitokini aarip aaibung'ie ilkarash imiet te nebo.

English: And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likewise shalt thou make in the uttermost edge of another curtain, in the coupling of the second.
Masaai: Intayu ilgoso le nkopito pusi loo nkarash te matua e oriong e lelo karash te ntukus e dukuya. Nintoki ake aiko neijia, aitayu ilkiintani pusi loo nkarash te matua e oriong e ina tukus e are.

English: Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the coupling of the second; that the loops may take hold one of another.
Masaai: Ilkiintani onom intayu te ntukus nabo oo lkarash, nintoki aitayu ilkiintani onom te matua e oriong e ina tukus e are oo lkarash; ore lelo goso nchoo eipira.

English: And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains together with the taches: and it shall be one tabernacle.
Masaai: Intayu ilala onom le sahabu oololo paa ninche intutumie entukus oo lkarash o enkae pee eaku enkaji e Nkai entoki nabo.

English: And thou shalt make curtains of goats' hair to be a covering upon the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make.
Masaai: “Intobira sii nkilani oo lpapit loo nkineji naaitushur olng'obor; ntobira nkilani tomon o obo.

English: The length of one curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and the eleven curtains shall be all of one measure.
Masaai: Ore enkadoro e pooki kila naa intemat tomoni uni enkadoro naa intemat ong'uan e ndapasho; ore nena kilani pokira tomon o obo nerisioroyu.

English: And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.
Masaai: Nintutum ilkarash imiet te nebo, o nkilani ile te nebo, ore enkila e ile nipud te shumata te mbata e njing'et o lng'obor.

English: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops in the edge of the curtain which coupleth the second.
Masaai: Nintayu ilkiintani onom te matua e nkila ti oriong e ntukus nabo, o lkiintani onom te matua e oriong e ntukus e are e nkila.

English: And thou shalt make fifty taches of brass, and put the taches into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
Masaai: “Nintayu iltidii ooriwuo lo suyai onom, nipik lelo tidii atua lelo kiintani nintutum olng'obor te nebo metaa entoki nabo.

English: And the remnant that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the backside of the tabernacle.
Masaai: Ore ina shoto naleku too lkarash o lng'obor, ilo pisiai lo lkarasha, neisiong'a ti oriong o lng'obor.

English: And a cubit on the one side, and a cubit on the other side of that which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, it shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
Masaai: Ore ina matua naleku te nchoto nabo, o ematua naleku te nkae shoto, te nkadoro oo nkilani o lng'obor.

English: And thou shalt make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering above of badgers' skins.
Masaai: Neisiong'a too mbat o lng'obor enkikenet oo ndapan naanota oo lmeregeshi o noo nkineji.

English: And thou shalt make boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up.
Masaai: “Ntobira intorioi irubat oo sunta o lng'obor too nkeek o lerai.

English: Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half shall be the breadth of one board.
Masaai: Ore ake erubata e suntai naa intemat tomon enkadoro o entemata nabo o lpisiai e ndapasho.

English: Two tenons shall there be in one board, set in order one against another: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
Masaai: Netii ake erubata nabo ilng'amat oare pee etumi aairuburubie te nebo; ninko neijia too rubat pooki

English: And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards on the south side southward.
Masaai: ntobira nkeek o lng'obor, irubat tikitam e nkosholai te nkalo e kopikop.

English: And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for his two tenons, and two sockets under another board for his two tenons.
Masaai: Nkitotoneta artam e nkosholai ti abori nena rubat tikitam oo sunta, nkitotoneta are ti abori erubata nabo too lng'amat lenyena pokira oare, o nkitotoneta are te rubata nabo too lng'amat lenyenapokira oare.

English: And for the second side of the tabernacle on the north side there shall be twenty boards:
Masaai: Ore te nchoto e are o lng'obor, te nkalo e moikuape irubat tikitam oo sunta.

English: And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
Masaai: O nkitotoneta enye tikitam e nkosholai, nkitotoneta are ti abori erubata nabo o nkitotoneta are ti abori enkae rubata.

English: And for the sides of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.
Masaai: Ore ti oriong o lng'obor te nkalo o loo ntoluo nintayu irubat ile oo sunta.

English: And two boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the two sides.
Masaai: Nintayu irubat are too lpijat lo lng'obor ti oriong;

English: And they shall be coupled together beneath, and they shall be coupled together above the head of it unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.
Masaai: nepaasha ninche te kop kake nchoo eibung'a te shumata, to lgisoi le dukuya, netiu inji te pokira are; neitayu ilpijat pokira are.

English: And they shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
Masaai: Naa keaku irubat isiet, tenebo nkitotoneta enye e nkosholai, nkitotoneta tomon o ile, o nkitotoneta are tiabori erubata nabo, o nkitotoneta are tiabori enkae rubata.

English: And thou shalt make bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
Masaai: “Nintayu iloom lo lerai, imiet too rubat e nkalo nabo olng'obor,

English: And five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the two sides westward.
Masaai: o loom imiet too rubat enkae alo o lng'obor, o loom imiet too rubat o lng'bor te nkalo e oriong te nkalo o loo ntoluo.

English: And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall reach from end to end.
Masaai: Ore ilo loomi le mpolos oitorit nena rubat neng'ung'ur ebaiki enkiting'oto o metabaiki enkiting'oto.

English: And thou shalt overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars with gold.
Masaai: Nimulumul irubat te sahabu, nintayu ilgiso lenye le sahabu pee eibung iloom, nimur iloom te sahabu.

English: And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount.
Masaai: Nishetu olng'obor te nkitanyaanyukoto apa anaa enikintoduaaki to ldoinyo.

English: And thou shalt make a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen of cunning work: with cherubims shall it be made:
Masaai: “Nintobir oliaatua too ntokitin pusi o sinteti o mpilei o nkarash e katani napuiyiapui. Neitobir te siaai e nkarriayiano neripakini ilkerubi.

English: And thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold: their hooks shall be of gold, upon the four sockets of silver.
Masaai: Neisiong ninche too ng'apeta o lerai nemur te sahabu, neeta ilala oo lolo le sahabu, too nkitotoneta ong'uan e nkosholai.

English: And thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches, that thou mayest bring in thither within the vail the ark of the testimony: and the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy.
Masaai: Niik oliatua te lelo ala oo lolo, niyau osanduku le nchakenisho atua oliaatua; nikirishaki ilo liaatua ewueji sinyati o ine nesinya oleng.

English: And thou shalt put the mercy seat upon the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.
Masaai: Nipik ilo orika lo lng'ur shumata ilo sanduku le nchakenisho ine wueji nesinya oleng.

English: And thou shalt set the table without the vail, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.
Masaai: Nipik ina mesa oriong o liaatua, nipik enkitashet o ltaa enkalo e kopikop o lng'obor neipirakinore emesa; nipik emesa enkalo e moikuape.

English: And thou shalt make an hanging for the door of the tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, wrought with needlework.
Masaai: “Ore kutuk aji o lng'obor nintayu olkarasha pus o olmorijoi, o lpile, oitobiruno te kitani napuyiapui napiyaya, neikodi to ltidu.

English: And thou shalt make for the hanging five pillars of shittim wood, and overlay them with gold, and their hooks shall be of gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.
Masaai: Nintaiki lelo karash ing'apeta imiet o lerai nimur te sahabu, ore ilala lenye oololo naa ile sahabu nintaiki nkitotoneta imiet o suyai.

English: And thou shalt make an altar of shittim wood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height thereof shall be three cubits.
Masaai: “Ntobira olperere too nkeek o lerai intemat imiet enkadoro naa intemat imiet endapasho; nerisioro olperere too nkaloli pooki. Ore enkilepata enye naa intemat uni.

English: And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof: his horns shall be of the same: and thou shalt overlay it with brass.
Masaai: Nipik imowuarak lelo pijat lenyena pokira oong'uan; neaku nena mowuarak entoki nabo o ninye. Nimur to suyai.

English: And thou shalt make his pans to receive his ashes, and his shovels, and his basons, and his fleshhooks, and his firepans: all the vessels thereof thou shalt make of brass.
Masaai: Nintayu imotioo enyena naaiwouo nkuruon, o ilkijikoni o ngirran o ntokitin naaitobirieki enkima; ore ntokitin enyena pooki naasishoreki nintobir to suyai.

English: And thou shalt make for it a grate of network of brass; and upon the net shalt thou make four brasen rings in the four corners thereof.
Masaai: Nintaiki sii ngesherreta naashetuno to suyai; ore nena ngesherreta nipik ilgiso oong'uan lo suyai ilpijat lenyena pokira oong'uan.

English: And thou shalt put it under the compass of the altar beneath, that the net may be even to the midst of the altar.
Masaai: Tipika ina ng'esherrie abori emanaroto o lperere pee eitorit ina ng'esherrie o lperere ti abori.

English: And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of shittim wood, and overlay them with brass.
Masaai: Nintayu imbokishi o lperere, imbokishi o lerai nimur ninche to suyai;

English: And the staves shall be put into the rings, and the staves shall be upon the two sides of the altar, to bear it.
Masaai: nepiki nena bokishi aaimie lelo giso metaa ketii imbokishi nchot pokira o lperere te nenapi.

English: Hollow with boards shalt thou make it: as it was shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it.
Masaai: Intobira too nkeek, nintugum anaa apa enikintoduaaki to ldoinyo, neitobirunye atiu neijia.

English: And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen of an hundred cubits long for one side:
Masaai: “Intobira endung'oroto olng'obor le Nkai. Ore te nkalo e kopikop nepiki endung'oroto olkarasha oisiong'a sidai oshetuno too usin naapiyaya loo intemat iip enkadoro te nkalo nabo.

English: And the twenty pillars thereof and their twenty sockets shall be of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.
Masaai: Ore ing'apeta enye naa tikitam, ore nkitotoneta enye naa tikitam, lo suyai, kake ore ilala oololo loo ng'apeta, o olgoso lenye naa ine nkosholai.

English: And likewise for the north side in length there shall be hangings of an hundred cubits long, and his twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets of silver.
Masaai: Neijia sii etiu enkadoro enye te nkalo e moikuape, tipika nkisiong'at oo ilkarash loo ntemat iip. Nera ing'apeta enye tikitam nera nkitotoneta enye tikitam naa ino suyai, kake ore lelo ala oololo loo lgoso lenye naa ile nkosholai.

English: And for the breadth of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits: their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
Masaai: Ore te nkalo e ndoyioroto e nkolong tipika ilkarash onom te nkadoro o ng'apeta tomon o nkitotoneta tomon.

English: And the breadth of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.
Masaai: Ore endapasho e ndung'oroto te nkalo najing'ieki te nkilepunoto e nkolong naa intemat onom.

English: The hangings of one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits: their pillars three, and their sockets three.
Masaai: Ore ilkarash te nkalo nabo e kishomi naa intemat tomon o imiet, o ng'apeta uni o nkitotoneta uni.

English: And on the other side shall be hangings fifteen cubits: their pillars three, and their sockets three.
Masaai: Ore te nkae shoto naa intemat tomon o imiet, o ng'apeta uni o nkitotoneta uni.

English: And for the gate of the court shall be an hanging of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, wrought with needlework: and their pillars shall be four, and their sockets four.
Masaai: Ore enkishomi e ndung'oroto nipik aitolok olkarasha loo ntemat tikitam te nkadoro oata emua pus o emorijoi o empile nashetuno te nkarasha sidai napuyiapui. Neikodoki te ripare o ltidu; nepiki ing'apeta ong'uan o nkitotoneta ong'uan.

English: All the pillars round about the court shall be filleted with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of brass.
Masaai: Ore ing'apeta pooki naamanita endung'oroto neitutumi te nkeene e nkosholai, ore lala lenye oololo naa ile nkosholai, ore nkitotoneta enye naa ino suyai.

English: The length of the court shall be an hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every where, and the height five cubits of fine twined linen, and their sockets of brass.
Masaai: Ore enkadoro e ndung'oroto naa intemat imiet. Netii ilkarash ooluaa sidain oopuyiapui o nkitotoneta o suyai.

English: All the vessels of the tabernacle in all the service thereof, and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.
Masaai: Ore imasaa pooki e ilo ng'obor e pooki siaai, o ncheito enyena pooki endung'oroto naa ino suyai.

English: And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always.
Masaai: “Nintanap iltung'ana loo Siraeli pee kiyaki ninche eilata naironyuno nasila oo loirienito te nkaraki ewang'an, pee eiki oltaa meiyupuyupo enkata pooki.

English: In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the LORD: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.
Masaai: Ore te ilo ng'obor o tumoreki, ti oriong ilo liatua otii dukuya enchakenisho, neitobir Aron o layiok lenyena ebaiki teipa o metabaiki tadekenya te dukuya Olaitoriani. Neaku enkitanapata ntarasi naibung'i ti atua iishoritin enye iltung'ana loo Siraeli.

English: And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.
Masaai: “Niyau iyie aitinyiku Aron, olalashe lino, o layiok lenyena te nebo ninye, laa ninche ti atua iltung'ana loo Siraeli laaisiaai anaa ilapolosak. Aron o layiok lenyena, Nadab o Abihu o Eliesa o Isamar.

English: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.
Masaai: Nintaiki Aron olalashe lino ilkilani oosinya, te nkitoo o te sidano.

English: And thou shalt speak unto all that are wise hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron's garments to consecrate him, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.
Masaai: Nirorie lelo pooki oata enkidimata, lelo laishoo eng'eno, pee eitobir ilkilani le Aron, pee eitisinyi te mpolosare ai.

English: And these are the garments which they shall make; a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.
Masaai: Kuna inkilani naaitobir ninche, enkila o lgoo, enkila dorrop, olkila oado, enkila e oriong naikodo o enkarasha e lukunya, o enkimeita; neitobir ninche nkilani naasinya te nkaraki Aron olalashe lino o layiok lenyena pee aaisiaai ninche anaa ilapolosak.

English: And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.
Masaai: “Neng'amu ninche sahabu o nkarash pusi o morijo o mpilei o enkatani napuyiapui napiyaya.

English: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and of purple, of scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cunning work.
Masaai: Neitobir ninche enkila dorrop te sahabu, too usin pusi, o too morijo, o too mpilei o te katani napuyiapui napiyaya te nkarriayiano.

English: It shall have the two shoulderpieces thereof joined at the two edges thereof; and so it shall be joined together.
Masaai: Neeta inkeenta are ooronyi too lpijat lenyena pee eitutumieki te nebo.

English: And the curious girdle of the ephod, which is upon it, shall be of the same, according to the work thereof; even of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
Masaai: O enkimeita naitobiruno te nkarriyiano te nena tokitin, pee eenieki; te sahabu o too usin pusi o sinteti o naanyokie, o naaibor sidain.

English: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:
Masaai: Niya isoito are barrikon naaji oniks niguetaki asiraki ninche nkarn oo layiok le Israel,

English: Six of their names on one stone, and the other six names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth.
Masaai: nkarn enye ile to soit obo, ore nkulie ile naaleku ning'eroki olikae soit, too inot enye.

English: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold.
Masaai: Anaa enkarriyiano olaguetani omishir isoito, neijia sii iyie inkuna eng'uetakinoto e lelo soito oare nkarn oo layiok le Israel; nipik nena nitaguetua te sahabu.
