English: And they cried unto the children of Dan. And they turned their faces, and said unto Micah, What aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company?
Masaai: Nebuaaki ninche lelo tung'ana le Dan, ooibelekenyunye nejoki Mika, “Kainyoo nikinosita anaijo itorikuo olorere kitok obanji?”

English: And he said, Ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? and what is this that ye say unto me, What aileth thee?
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Iwaita intae nkaitin aainei naitayio nanu, o lapolosani, nipuopuo, kainyoo naa aatung'ueikiaki? Kainyoo naa pee kijokiki intae nanu, ‘Eji kainyoo nikinosita?’ ”

English: And the children of Dan said unto him, Let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy life, with the lives of thy household.
Masaai: Nejoki lelo tung'ana le Dan ninye, “Mincho iyie oltoilo lino metoning'i ti atua iyiook, pee mikidoiki iltung'ana ootagorote, niminie enkishui ino o nena tokitin e nkaji ino.”

English: And the children of Dan went their way: and when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back unto his house.
Masaai: Nepuo lelo tung'ana le Dan aaibung enkoitoi enye; ore ake pee edol Mika nchere kegol ninche oleng aalang ninye, neibelekenya neshuko alo enkang enye.

English: And they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest which he had, and came unto Laish, unto a people that were at quiet and secure: and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.
Masaai: Neyau ninche nena tokitin apa naaitobirua Mika, o ilo apolosani apa ora olenye, nepuonu lelo tung'ana le Dan Laish, enetii iltung'ana oobor lememuso, nesesekuan ninche te nepi o lalem, nepejoo ina anasa te nkima.

English: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Zidon, and they had no business with any man; and it was in the valley that lieth by Bethrehob. And they built a city, and dwelt therein.
Masaai: Nemeetae apa olakordunoni amu kelakuaniki apa ninye Sidon, nemetii apa kulikae tung'ana ooata enabaikinore ninche. Etii atua oerata le Bet-rehob. Neitoki apa ninche aashet ina anasa nemany atua.

English: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.
Masaai: Neisho apa ina anasa enkarna aajo Dan, aaipotie nkakuyiaa lenye, apa otoiuo Israel; amu keji apa enkarna e ina anasa te dukuya Laish.

English: And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
Masaai: Neitasheikinye apa lelo tung'ana le Dan ate ina kitanyaanyukoto naguetuno; naa Yonasan ilo ayioni le Geshom, olayioni le Musa, o layiok lenyena apa ilapolosak lo losho le Dan o metabau ina olong apa natarayoki ilo osho.

English: And they set them up Micah's graven image, which he made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.
Masaai: Neaku eitasheyie apa ninche ina kitanyaanyukoto e Mika naguetuno, naitayio ninye ina kata pooki apa natii enkaji e Nkai te Shilo.

English: And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim, who took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah.
Masaai: Ore apa te nena olong'i, eton meetae olaiguanani ti atua Israel, netii Olawi obo otii nena rishat naaliyio e ina kop oo ndoinyo e Efraim, apa oyaka kewan enkapiani e Betlehem ti atua Yuda.

English: And his concubine played the whore against him, and went away from him unto her father's house to Bethlehemjudah, and was there four whole months.
Masaai: Ore ina apiani negorokino ninye, nelo enkaji e menye te Betlehem ti atua Yuda aing'uaa ilo Lawi, neton ninye te ine too lapaitin oong'uan.

English: And her husband arose, and went after her, to speak friendly unto her, and to bring her again, having his servant with him, and a couple of asses: and she brought him into her father's house: and when the father of the damsel saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
Masaai: Nedumunye ilo moruo lenye nelo asujaa, pee elo ailejilej ninye neshuku ninye ayau. Netii apa te nebo ninye osinka lenye o sirkon aare. Nelotu apa ninye enkaji e papaai lenye; ore ake pee edolmenye ina tito ninye, nelotu te nchipai anang'are ninye.

English: And his father in law, the damsel's father, retained him; and he abode with him three days: so they did eat and drink, and lodged there.
Masaai: Neibok ninye olaputani, menye ina tito, neton ninye te nebo ninye nkolong'i uni; neaku etadaate ninche neokisho neirrag ine.

English: And it came to pass on the fourth day, when they arose early in the morning, that he rose up to depart: and the damsel's father said unto his son in law, Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward go your way.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e ong'uan nedumunye ninche tadekenya nenapa ninye pee elo; kake etiaaka menye ina tito olaputani lenye, “Ntagolo kewan inosa endaa, ore te siadi ina nitum taa ashomo.”

English: And they sat down, and did eat and drink both of them together: for the damsel's father had said unto the man, Be content, I pray thee, and tarry all night, and let thine heart be merry.
Masaai: Netoni lelo lewa pokira oare aadaa neokisho te nebo; nejoki menye ina tito ilo tung'ani, “Tobiko tishipayu niyeng'iyeng'a.”

English: And when the man rose up to depart, his father in law urged him: therefore he lodged there again.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edumunye ilo tung'ani ajo alo, neitirrishaki olaputani ninye, o menyaaki aigil aairrag ine.

English: And he arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart: and the damsel's father said, Comfort thine heart, I pray thee. And they tarried until afternoon, and they did eat both of them.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e imiet nedumunye ninye tadekenya enasirie pee elo; nejoki menye ina tito, “Ntagolo kewan, totona o metigilayu enkolong.” Nedaa ninche pokira oare.

English: And when the man rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his servant, his father in law, the damsel's father, said unto him, Behold, now the day draweth toward evening, I pray you tarry all night: behold, the day groweth to an end, lodge here, that thine heart may be merry; and to morrow get you early on your way, that thou mayest go home.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edumunye ilo tung'ani o ina apiani enye o laisiaayiani lenye pee epuo, nejoki ninye olaputani lenye menye ina tito, “Ng'ura, etinyikaiyie endama aaku teipa; totona siaake kewarie pooki, ng'ura etinyikua endama; irraga ene nchoo oltau lino eng'ida; ore taisere nidumunye tadekenya enasirie te nkaraki elototo ino, pee ilo ang.”

English: But the man would not tarry that night, but he rose up and departed, and came over against Jebus, which is Jerusalem; and there were with him two asses saddled, his concubine also was with him.
Masaai: Kake etanya apa ilo tung'ani eirrag ina kewarie etudumunye ninye alo, nelo abaya enkipirakinoto e Yebus (aa taa Yerusalem). Neeta apa te nebo ninye isirkon oare ooitobiraki pee ekedi, netii apa ina apiani te nebo ninye.

English: And when they were by Jebus, the day was far spent; and the servant said unto his master, Come, I pray thee, and let us turn in into this city of the Jebusites, and lodge in it.
Masaai: Ore ake pee etaaniki ninche Yebus, netinyikayie endama, nejoki olaisiaayiani olkitok lenye, “Wou taata maibelekenyakinoto iyiook ena anasa oo Lyebusi, pee kirrag ena kewarie.”

English: And his master said unto him, We will not turn aside hither into the city of a stranger, that is not of the children of Israel; we will pass over to Gibeah.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo kitok ninye, “Mikimbelekenya iyiook aajing atua enkanasa oo ltung'ana leeiking'a leme iltung'ana le Israel ninche; kake eikigiroo iyiook aapuo Gibea.”

English: And he said unto his servant, Come, and let us draw near to one of these places to lodge all night, in Gibeah, or in Ramah.
Masaai: Neitoki ninye ajoki ilo sinka lenye, “Wou matataaniki iyiook nabo e kuna wuejitin pee kirrag ena kewarie Gibea aashu Rama.”

English: And they passed on and went their way; and the sun went down upon them when they were by Gibeah, which belongeth to Benjamin.
Masaai: Negiroo ninche nepuo aaibung enkoitoi enye; nedoyio enkolong etii ninche embata e Gibea, nara ninye ene Benchamen,

English: And they turned aside thither, to go in and to lodge in Gibeah: and when he went in, he sat him down in a street of the city: for there was no man that took them into his house to lodging.
Masaai: neibelekenya ninche te ine, aapuo aairrag ina kewarie Gibea. Nelo ninye aton te nkoitoi kitok e ina anasa; amu meetae oltung'ani otoriko ninche atua enkaji enye meirraga ina kewarie.

English: And, behold, there came an old man from his work out of the field at even, which was also of mount Ephraim; and he sojourned in Gibeah: but the men of the place were Benjamites.
Masaai: Ng'ura, nelotu apa olpayian kitok eing'uaa esiaai enye ti atua enkurma teipa; ore apa ilo tung'ani naa o leina kop oo ndoinyo e Efraim, neidurraka apa Gibea amany; ore apa iltung'ana le ine wueji naa ile Benchamen.

English: And when he had lifted up his eyes, he saw a wayfaring man in the street of the city: and the old man said, Whither goest thou? and whence comest thou?
Masaai: Neshumu ninye nkonyek enyena nedol ilo tung'ani elotu to losinko leina anasa nejo ilo payian kitok, “Kaji iyie iloito? Naa kaji ing'uaa?”

English: And he said unto him, We are passing from Bethlehemjudah toward the side of mount Ephraim; from thence am I: and I went to Bethlehemjudah, but I am now going to the house of the LORD; and there is no man that receiveth me to house.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilo payian kitok, “Kipuoito iyiook aagiroo Betlehem ti atua Yuda, aapuo nekua rishat naabayie e ina kop oo ndoinyo e Efraim, naa ninye aing'uaa nanu. Ashomo apa Betlehem ti atua Yuda, naloito taata enkang ai, nemetii hoo ng'ae laatoriko nanu atua enkaji enye.

English: Yet there is both straw and provender for our asses; and there is bread and wine also for me, and for thy handmaid, and for the young man which is with thy servants: there is no want of any thing.
Masaai: Kiaata iyiook endaa o lkujita loo sirkon lang, o mukateni o enaisho te nkaraki nanu o ena sinka ino, o ele barnoti otii te nebo isinkan linono; eitu eng'oriki iyiook toki.”

English: And the old man said, Peace be with thee; howsoever let all thy wants lie upon me; only lodge not in the street.
Masaai: Nejo ilo payian kitok, “Meeu eseriani enitii; kagolie nanu iyieunot inono pooki; kake mirrag ena kewarie to losinko.”

English: So he brought him into his house, and gave provender unto the asses: and they washed their feet, and did eat and drink.
Masaai: Neaku etorikuo apa ninye atua enkaji enye, neisho lelo sirkon lenyena olkujita, neisuj ninche nkejek enye, nedaa ninche neokisho.

English: Now as they were making their hearts merry, behold, the men of the city, certain sons of Belial, beset the house round about, and beat at the door, and spake to the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him.
Masaai: Ore apa ina kata etishipate ninche iltauja lenye, ng'ura, ore iltung'ana le ina anasa, iltung'ana arruok neng'adu ina aji aaman, eosh kutuk e nkaji nejoki ninche ilo payian kitok, ilo openy e nkaji, “Mpang'unye ilo tung'ani duo oewuo atua enkaji ino, pee kitum iyiook aatayiolo ninye.”

English: And the man, the master of the house, went out unto them, and said unto them, Nay, my brethren, nay, I pray you, do not so wickedly; seeing that this man is come into mine house, do not this folly.
Masaai: Ore ilo payian, olopeny ina aji, neipang'aki ninche nejoki ninche, “A-a, ilalashera laainei, emiaas intae ena torroni; itoduaa aajo eewuo ele tung'ani atua enkaji ai, emiaas intae ena bae suuji.

English: Behold, here is my daughter a maiden, and his concubine; them I will bring out now, and humble ye them, and do with them what seemeth good unto you: but unto this man do not so vile a thing.
Masaai: Ng'ura, etii ene entito selenkei neitu eyiolou olee o enkapiani enye; ntasho maipang'unye nanu ninche. Embung'a ninche nintaasiasa ninche anaa enidolidolo eishiaakino te intae; kake ore ti alo ele tung'ani emintaas ena bae suuji.”

English: But the men would not hearken to him: so the man took his concubine, and brought her forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning: and when the day began to spring, they let her go.
Masaai: Kake mening lelo tung'ana ninye. Neaku eibung'a apa ilo payian enkapiani enye neipung'ie ninye boo mewaita ninche; neyiolou ninche ninye, neinyal enkewarie pooki o mekenyu. Ore ake pee emanaa enkakenya neisho meshomo.

English: Then came the woman in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was, till it was light.
Masaai: Ore pee ekenyu, nelotu ina kitok nebatata te kutuk aji e nkaji e ilo payian apa naa ninye etii olkitok lenye, neirrag o metawang'a.

English: And her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way: and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, and her hands were upon the threshold.
Masaai: Nedumunye olkitok lenye tadekenya; ore ake pee ebol kutuk aji e ina aji neipang alo, ng'ura, eirragita enkapiani enye te kutuk aji e ina aji, eibung'ita too nkaik enyena ntaloishin e kutukaji.

English: And he said unto her, Up, and let us be going. But none answered. Then the man took her up upon an ass, and the man rose up, and gat him unto his place.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Tudumunye maape.” Kake eitu ewalikini ninye. Nepik ilo tung'ani ninye enkoriong o sikiria lenye; nedumunye ilo lee nelo enkang enye.

English: And when he was come into his house, he took a knife, and laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejing ninye enkaji enye, neyau enkalem, neibung ina apiani enye neorrior ninye erubata o erubata aitaa irubat tomon o are, neirriwaa ninye nkuapi pooki e Israel.

English: And it was so, that all that saw it said, There was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds.
Masaai: Ore pooki ootoduaa ina nejo, “Eitu ae kata easayu embae neeijo ena aashu edoli ebaiki enkolong apa naileputua iltung'ana le Israel aapuku te nkop e Misiri o metabaiki ena olong; embirribirra enguanare niwaliwala.”

English: Then all the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh.
Masaai: Nepuonu iltung'ana pooki le Israel, ebaiki Dan o metabaiki Beer-sheba te nebo enkop e Gilead; ore ina umata neiturrurro anaa oltung'ani obo te dukuya Olaitoriani te Mispa.

English: And the chief of all the people, even of all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword.
Masaai: Ore laiguanak le lelo tung'ana pooki, too loshon pooki le Israel neyau ate atua ilo turrur loo ltung'ana le Nkai, naa nkalifuni iip ong'uan apa iltung'ana oopuo too nkejek ooata lalema.

English: (Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh.) Then said the children of Israel, Tell us, how was this wickedness?
Masaai: Nening apa iltung'ana le Benchamen nchere eilepa iltung'ana le Israel aapuo Mispa. Nejo iltung'ana le Israel, “Entoliki iyiook, kaji apa eikununye ena torroni?”

English: And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered and said, I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.
Masaai: Ore ilo Lawi, ilo moruo apa le ina kitok nataraki metua, newal ajo, “Aewuo apa nanu Gibea, ina nara ene Benchamen, nanu o enkapiani ai, pee kirrag ina kewarie.

English: And the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me: and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead.
Masaai: Naadumakino nanu ilewa le Gibea, neman aang'adu ina aji natii kewarie; keyieu apa ninche naar nanu matua, neikony enkapiani ai, netua ninye.

English: And I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the country of the inheritance of Israel: for they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel.
Masaai: Naya nanu ina apiani ai nadung nanu aitaa ndung'udung'ot, nairriwaa nanu ninye aibulunye enkop pooki enjung'ore e Israel, amu etaasa apa ninche embae torrono naa olminong sapuk entorroni ti atua Israel.

English: Behold, ye are all children of Israel; give here your advice and counsel.
Masaai: Eng'ura, intae iltung'ana le Israel, intae pooki, enchoru enkikoo inyi o eutaroto inyi tene.”

English: And all the people arose as one man, saying, We will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house.
Masaai: Nedumunye iltung'ana pooki le Israel anaa oltung'ani obo, ejo, “Mikipuo iyiook hoo obo lang olng'obor lenye, nemeetae olalang orrinyo alo enkaji enye.

English: But now this shall be the thing which we will do to Gibeah; we will go up by lot against it;
Masaai: Kake ore taata ena iyiook kintaas Gibea: eikipuo iyiook aarare ninye te oshoto e nkukuo,

English: And we will take ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and an hundred of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to fetch victual for the people, that they may do, when they come to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly that they have wrought in Israel.
Masaai: nikiya iltung'ana tomon te iip ti atua iloshon pooki le Israel, o iip ti atua enkalifu, o enkalifu too nkalifuni tomon, pee eyaki iltung'ana ndaiki, paa te nepuonu ninche netum aaitalaa Gibea e Benchamen elap, te ina taboi pooki entorroni nataasa ninche ti atua Israel.”

English: So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.
Masaai: Neaku eiturrurrote apa iltung'ana le Israel aaipirakinore ina anasa etaa oltung'ani obo.

English: And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What wickedness is this that is done among you?
Masaai: Neirriwaa iloshon le Israel iltung'ana meshomo atua olosho pooki le Benchamen, ejo, “Kaa torroni ena nataase ti atua intae?

English: Now therefore deliver us the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel:
Masaai: Ore naa taata entayu lelo tung'ana, lelo arruok le Gibea, pee kitum iyiook aataar ninche metuata, nikiwuang'ie entorroni te Israel.” Kake mening Ibenchamen oltoilo loo lalashera lenye, lelo tung'ana le Israel.

English: But the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children of Israel.
Masaai: Neiturrurrunye ile Benchamen te nebo aaipang'u too nkanas aapuonu Gibea, pee epuo olarrabal aarare iltung'ana le Israel.

English: And the children of Benjamin were numbered at that time out of the cities twenty and six thousand men that drew sword, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, which were numbered seven hundred chosen men.
Masaai: Neiturrurro ile Benchamen ina olong too nkanas enye iltung'ana nkalifuni tikitam o ile ooata lalema, te nebo lelo oomanya Gibea ooiturrurro iltung'ana iip naapishana gelunot.

English: Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.
Masaai: Ore ti atua kulo pooki netii iltung'ana iip naapishana gelunot kedienyiaa; laa keidim ake pooki lenye atanang'a oleinyuaa to soit le nkopito nemediak.

English: And the men of Israel, beside Benjamin, were numbered four hundred thousand men that drew sword: all these were men of war.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana le Israel metii Benchamen neiturrur iltung'ana nkalifuni iip ong'uan oata ilalema; ore kulo pooki naa iltung'ana lo larrabal.

English: And the children of Israel arose, and went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God, and said, Which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first.
Masaai: Nedumunye iltung'ana le Israel neilep aapuo Betel, neikilikuanishore Enkai, “Kalo lang oituruk alo aarare ile Benchamen?” Nejoki Olaitoriani, “Yuda ong'as alo.”

English: And the children of Israel rose up in the morning, and encamped against Gibeah.
Masaai: Nedumunye iltung'ana le Israel tadekenya nepuo aaitayu ilng'oborri te nkipirakinoto e Gibea.

English: And the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin; and the men of Israel put themselves in array to fight against them at Gibeah.
Masaai: Neilep iltung'ana le Israel aapuo olarrabal aarare Benchamen; neitoluakino iltung'ana le Israel ninche te Gibea.

English: And the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah, and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men.
Masaai: Neipang ile Benchamen te Gibea neirragieki te nkop ina olong iltung'ana nkalifuni tikitam o are oo le Israel.

English: And the people the men of Israel encouraged themselves, and set their battle again in array in the place where they put themselves in array the first day.
Masaai: Kake ore lelo tung'ana, lelo lewa le Israel eitagoluote, neitoki aaluaakino olarrabal te ine wueji netoluare te nkolong e dukuya.

English: (And the children of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked counsel of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, Go up against him.)
Masaai: Nepuo iltung'ana le Israel aaishir te dukuya Olaitoriani o metaa teipa; neikilikuanishore Olaitoriani, “Eikingil iyiook aaluakino olarrabal aarare ilalashera lang lelo le Benchamen?” Nejo Olaitoriani, “Elepa enchom entaarare ninche.”

English: And the children of Israel came near against the children of Benjamin the second day.
Masaai: Neigutu iltung'ana le Israel aapuonu aarare lelo le Benchamen te nkolong e are.

English: And Benjamin went forth against them out of Gibeah the second day, and destroyed down to the ground of the children of Israel again eighteen thousand men; all these drew the sword.
Masaai: Nelo Benchamen aarare ninche te Gibea te nkolong e are, nebatata te nkop iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon o isiet oo ltung'ana le Israel; ore kulo pooki naa iltung'ana loo lalema.

English: Then all the children of Israel, and all the people, went up, and came unto the house of God, and wept, and sat there before the LORD, and fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
Masaai: Neitoki iltung'ana pooki le Israel, enjore pooki, aailep aapuo Betel neishir; netoni ninche te ine te dukuya Olaitoriani, neen ate aaitupukoo ina olong o metaa teipa, neitayu ilasarri oopejori o lasarri le seriani te dukuya Olaitoriani.

English: And the children of Israel enquired of the LORD, (for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,
Masaai: Neikilikuanishore iltung'ana le Israel Olaitoriani (amu ore apa osanduku lo sotua le Nkai naa ine apa etii te nena olong'i,

English: And Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days,) saying, Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, Go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand.
Masaai: ore Finehas olayioni le Eliesa, olayioni le Aron, neisiaaisho te dukuya ilo sanduku apa te nena olong'i), ejo, “Eikingil iyiook aapuo olarrabal aarare lelo alashera lang lelo le Benchamen, anaa eikintirring'a?” Nejo Olaitoriani, “Elepa enchom; amu ore taisere kaishoru nanu ninche apik atua nkaik inyi.”

English: And Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah.
Masaai: Neaku eirriwayie Isiraeli iltung'ana meshomo aajing ilnukat aaman Gibea.

English: And the children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and put themselves in array against Gibeah, as at other times.
Masaai: Nepuo iltung'ana loo Siraeli aarare ile Benchamen te nkolong e uni, neitobirakino olarrabal pee earare Gibea, anaa enaikuna too nkulie katitin.

English: And the children of Benjamin went out against the people, and were drawn away from the city; and they began to smite of the people, and kill, as at other times, in the highways, of which one goeth up to the house of God, and the other to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men of Israel.
Masaai: Neipang iltung'ana le Benchamen aapuo aarare lelo tung'ana nerrumori aaitalam enkanasa. Ore anaa oshi too nkulie katitin neiteru aaoshisho near embata oo ltung'ana metuata, too nkoitoi, aa ore enkoitoi nabo nalala naa enailep alo Betel, nelo enkae Gibea. Ore te ina kisiajata near iltung'ana oobaya tomoni uni o are loo Siraeli.

English: And the children of Benjamin said, They are smitten down before us, as at the first. But the children of Israel said, Let us flee, and draw them from the city unto the highways.
Masaai: Nejo lelo tung'ana le Benchamen, “Ekueta ninche te dukuya iyiook anaa apa te dukuya.” Kake etejo iltung'ana loo Siraeli, “Maisika iyiook nikintalamaa ninche te nkanasa aarik nkoitoi kituaak.”

English: And all the men of Israel rose up out of their place, and put themselves in array at Baaltamar: and the liers in wait of Israel came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah.
Masaai: Nedumunye iltung'ana pooki loo Siraeli too wuejitin enye, neitobirakino olarrabal te Baal-tamar; ore lelo tung'ana loo Siraeli ootii olnukata neisarrisar too wuejitin enye aapuo enkalo o loo ntoluo le Geba.

English: And there came against Gibeah ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the battle was sore: but they knew not that evil was near them.
Masaai: Nepuonu aaimu enkalo e Gibea iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon oogeluno ti atua Israel pooki. Negolu olarrabal oleng. Neitu apa eyiolou iltung'ana le Benchamen aajo etataanikia ninche enkidaata.

English: And the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: and the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men: all these drew the sword.
Masaai: Nemir Olaitoriani Benchamen te dukuya Isirael. Neidaikie iltung'ana le Israel iltung'ana nkalifuni tikitam o imiet o iip nabo oo ltung'ana le Benchamen te ina olong; ore kulo pooki naa iltung'ana loo lalema.

English: So the children of Benjamin saw that they were smitten: for the men of Israel gave place to the Benjamites, because they trusted unto the liers in wait which they had set beside Gibeah.
Masaai: Neaku etoduaa ile Benchamen ina olong aajo etimiraki. Ekueta apa iltung'ana le Israel aailany ile Benchamen, amu eisiliga apa ninche lelo tung'ana ootii olnukata, otii embata e Gibea.

English: And the liers in wait hasted, and rushed upon Gibeah; and the liers in wait drew themselves along, and smote all the city with the edge of the sword.
Masaai: Nedumunye lelo tung'ana apa ootii olnukata, neisarisaru aakuetiki Gibea, nepuo lelo tung'ana ootii olnukata aar enkanasa tenepi o lalam.

English: Now there was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city.
Masaai: Ore apa olmonekie otoning'oteki te rishata oo ltung'ana le Israel o ltung'ana ootii olnukata, naa nchere, teneitayu enkatampoi sapuk e mpuruo naailep shumata, te nkanasa,

English: And when the men of Israel retired in the battle, Benjamin began to smite and kill of the men of Israel about thirty persons: for they said, Surely they are smitten down before us, as in the first battle.
Masaai: neibelekenyakino iltung'ana le Israel olarrabal. Neiterua apa Benchamen aar metuata iltung'ana loo Siraeli oobaya tomoni uni nejo ninche, “Esipa etooshoki ninche aanang'ie enkop te dukuya iyiook, anaa apa to larrabal le dukuya.”

English: But when the flame began to arise up out of the city with a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and, behold, the flame of the city ascended up to heaven.
Masaai: Kake ore pee eiter ailepu ilo monekie te nkanasa, te mpuruo nairrusha, neing'or ile Benchamen siadi, naa ng'ura, etaa duoo enkanasa pooki empuruo naijukujuku alo keper.

English: And when the men of Israel turned again, the men of Benjamin were amazed: for they saw that evil was come upon them.
Masaai: Neibelekenyuni taa iltung'ana loo Siraeli, neidang iltung'ana le Benchamen, amu etoduaa ninche aajo etataanikia ninche enkidaata.

English: Therefore they turned their backs before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness; but the battle overtook them; and them which came out of the cities they destroyed in the midst of them.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina neibelekenya ninche te dukuya iltung'ana le Israel aaipirri ong'ata; kake einepuaki ninche ore lelo ooipang'u ti atua nkanas nemut ninche te rishata enye.

English: Thus they inclosed the Benjamites round about, and chased them, and trode them down with ease over against Gibeah toward the sunrising.
Masaai: Nedung'oo iltung'ana le Benchamen, nemir aasujaa ninche neitunyoo ninche ebaiki Noha o meitabaiki enkipirakinoto Gibea te nkalo o loosaen.

English: And there fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand men; all these were men of valour.
Masaai: Nebatata ile Benchamen nkalifuni tomon o isiet, ore pooki naa iltung'ana yiolot.

English: And they turned and fled toward the wilderness unto the rock of Rimmon: and they gleaned of them in the highways five thousand men; and pursued hard after them unto Gidom, and slew two thousand men of them.
Masaai: Neibelekenya ninche neisikaki enkalo e ong'ata aapuo endapidapoi e Rimon; neari metuata iltung'ana nkalifuni imiet too nkoitoi kituaak, neitirrishakini aasujaa o meitabaikini Gibom, nesesekuani iltung'ana nkalifuni are te ine.

English: So that all which fell that day of Benjamin were twenty and five thousand men that drew the sword; all these were men of valour.
Masaai: Neaku ore lelo pooki le Benchamen ootabatate te ina olong naa nkalifuni tikitam o imiet le lelo ooenita ilalema, ore pooki naa iltung'ana yiolot.

English: But six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months.
Masaai: Kake eibelekenyate iltung'ana iip ile neisik aapuo ong'ata enkalo e ndapidapoi e Rimon, nebik ninche te ina dapidapoi e Rimon ilapaitin oong'uan.

English: And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they came to.
Masaai: Neitoki iltung'ana le Israel aaibelekenyakino iltung'ana le Benchamen neshurt ninche te nepi olalem, iltung'ana o ng'uesi o pooki naanoto ninche. Ore nkanas enye apa pooki naaitobira nepejoo te nkima.

English: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpeh, saying, There shall not any of us give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife.
Masaai: Einosa apa iltung'ana le Israel olmumai te Mispa, nejo, “Meetae hoo obo te iyiook oisho entito enye meyama iltung'ana le Benchamen.”

English: And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;
Masaai: Nepuonu iltung'ana Betel netoni teine te dukuya Enkai ometaa teipa, neyietu aaishir te mion.

English: And said, O LORD God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Olaitoriani Enkai e Israel, kainyoo pee eewuo ena atiu nji tiatua Israel, eji metaa keetae taata olosho obo lemeetae te Israel?”

English: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people rose early, and built there an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Masaai: Ore taisere neyooki iltung'ana aadumunye enasirie, neshet olperere lo lasar teine, neitayu ilasarri oopejori o lasarri le seriani.

English: And the children of Israel said, Who is there among all the tribes of Israel that came not up with the congregation unto the LORD? For they had made a great oath concerning him that came not up to the LORD to Mizpeh, saying, He shall surely be put to death.
Masaai: Nejo iltung'ana le Israel, “Kalo osho too loshon le Israel leitu elotu ena umata o Laitoriani?” Amu einosa apa ninche olmumai kitok tenkaraki ilo osho leitu elotu eumata o Laitoriani te Mispa, ejo, “Keari ninye metua.”

English: And the children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, and said, There is one tribe cut off from Israel this day.
Masaai: Eeta apa iltung'ana le Israel olng'ur te nkaraki Benchamen olalashe lenye, nejo ninche, “Eiwuang'ieki olosho obo aaitung'uaa Israel ena olong.

English: How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the LORD that we will not give them of our daughters to wives?
Masaai: Kaji kinko tenikincho nkituaak lelo ootelekutua, nikinosa apa olmumai to Laitoriani nchere, mikincho ninche hoo nabo oo ntoyie ang meyama.”

English: And they said, What one is there of the tribes of Israel that came not up to Mizpeh to the LORD? And, behold, there came none to the camp from  Jabeshgilead to the assembly.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Kalo osho ilo too loshon le Israel leitu elotu enetii Olaitoriani te Mispa?” Naa ng'ura, meetae hoo obo ebaiki Yabesh-gilead oshomo ina umata.

English: For the people were numbered, and, behold, there were none of the inhabitants of  Jabeshgilead there.
Masaai: Amu ore ina kata eipotitoi iltung'ana nkarn, meetae hoo obo le lelo oomanya Yabesh-gilead oirukishe.

English: And the congregation sent thither twelve thousand men of the valiantest, and commanded them, saying, Go and smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the children.
Masaai: Neaku eirriwayie apa ina umata iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon oare oopi, neitanap aajoki, “Enchom entaar metuata lelo oomanya Yabesh-gilead to lalem, o nkituaak o nkera.

English: And this is the thing that ye shall do, Ye shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman that hath lain by man.
Masaai: Ena intae enchom entaas. Ore pooki lee o pooki ngoruoi naatayiolounote endaikie ninche tukul.”

English: And they found among the inhabitants of  Jabeshgilead four hundred young virgins, that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
Masaai: Netum ninche tiatua lelo oomanya Yabesh-gilead iselenken iip ong'uan nemeyiolo olee, neriku ninche ilng'oborri te Shilo, naa enkop e Kanaan etii.

English: And the whole congregation sent some to speak to the children of Benjamin that were in the rock Rimmon, and to call peaceably unto them.
Masaai: Neitoki ina umata pooki aairriwaki olkilikuai ile Benchamen apa ooti endapidapoi e Rimon, neibalakinye ninche eseriani.

English: And Benjamin came again at that time; and they gave them wives which they had saved alive of the women of Jabesh-gilead: and yet so they sufficed them not.
Masaai: Nerrinyunye Benchamen neisho ninche ile Benchamen nena kituaak apa neitu eari metuata te Yabesh-gilead, kake eitu eidip ninche.

English: And the people repented them for Benjamin, because that the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
Masaai: Neing'urrie apa iltung'ana Benchamen enkaraki natipika Olaitoriani elusie iloshon le Israel.

English: Then the elders of the congregation said, How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing the women are destroyed out of Benjamin?
Masaai: Neitoki ilpayiani leina umata aajo, “Kaa iyiook kiaas tenkaraki nkituaak e lelo ootelekutua, neidaikieki apa ing'oruo aaishie te Benchamen?”

English: And they said, There must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Meeta nchere metumi enjung'ore te lelo ootelekutua le Benchamen, pee meimin ake ilo osho te Israel.

English: Howbeit we may not give them wives of our daughters: for the children of Israel have sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin.
Masaai: Ore ake eyia, mikindim iyiook aaishoo ninche ntoyie ang meyama.” Amu einosa olmumai iltung'ana le Israel nchere, “Etediaaki ilo oisho Benchamen enkitok.”

English: Then they said, Behold, there is a feast of the LORD in Shiloh yearly in a place which is on the north side of Bethel, on the east side of the highway that goeth up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.
Masaai: Neaku etejo ninche, “Ng'ura eetae anaake to lari osirua lo Laitoriani te Shilo, aa taa moikuape e Betel, te nkalo o loo saen e nkoitoi kitok nalo te Betel ometabaiki Shekem, o kopikop e Lebona.”

English: Therefore they commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in wait in the vineyards;
Masaai: Neitanap ninche ile Benchamen ejo, “Enchom erraga to lnukata tiatua nkurman oo sabibu,

English: And see, and, behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances, then come ye out of the vineyards, and catch you every man his wife of the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
Masaai: ning'orishosho, naa tenepuonu ntoyie e Shilo aaranyisho to sinkolio, nimpang'ung'u tiatua enkurma oo sabibu, neibung ake pooki lee enkitok enye aya, te nena toyie e Shilo, nelo enkop e Benchamen.

English: And it shall be, when their fathers or their brethren come unto us to complain, that we will say unto them, Be favourable unto them for our sakes: because we reserved not to each man his wife in the war: for ye did not give unto them at this time, that ye should be guilty.
Masaai: Naa tenepuonu loo menye anaa ilalashera lenye aailepilepaki iyiook, nikijoki iyiook ninche, ‘Enchoo iyiook mawaita ninche te mpiris, amu eitu iyiook kiya ninche aaitaa nkituaak ang to larrabal, neitu sii intae inchosho iyiook, anaa naa eaku eninyi entorroni.’ ”

English: And the children of Benjamin did so, and took them wives, according to their number, of them that danced, whom they caught: and they went and returned unto their inheritance, and repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.
Masaai: Neas ile Benchamen ina, neya nkituaak enye terisioroto esiana enye te nena toyie apa naaranyisho naaibung'a ninche aaya. Neitoki ninche aapuo aarrinyokino enjung'ore enye, neshet inkang'itie nemany.

English: And the children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe and to his family, and they went out from thence every man to his inheritance.
Masaai: Neitoki iltung'ana le Israel aadumunye. Nelo ake oltung'ani olosho lenye, o lmarei lenye, neipang aapuo teine, nelo ake pooki ng'ae enjung'ore enye.

English: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
Masaai: Ore apa te nena olong'i nemeetae olaiguanani te Israel; etaasa ake pooki tung'ani enaishiaakino too nkonyek enyena.

English: Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
Masaai: Ore apa te nena olong'i naaitoreisho ilarishak, netii olameyu enkop, ore oltung'ani obo le Betlehem ti atua enkop e Yuda nelo amany enkop e Moab. Eshomo ninye te nebo enkitok enye o layiok lenyena oare.

English: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.
Masaai: Ore apa enkarna e ilo tung'ani naa Elimelek, ore enkarna e nkitok enye naa Naomi. Ore nkarn oo layiok lenyena pokira oare naa Mahalon o Kilion. Ile Frati apa ninche ooing'uaa Betlehem ti atua enkop e Yuda. Eshomo apa ninche enkop e Moab nepuo aabik te ine.

English: And Elimelech Naomi's husband died; and she was left, and her two sons.
Masaai: Kake etua apa Elimelek ilo moruo le Naomi, neing'uari aa ninye ake o layiok lenyena pokira oare.

English: And they took them wives of the women of Moab; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth: and they dwelled there about ten years.
Masaai: Ore kulo pokira neyam ntoyie oo Lmoabu; ore apa enkarna e nabo naa Orpa ore enkarna e nkae naa Rusi. Etobiko apa ninche te ine ilarin oobaya tomon.

English: And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them; and the woman was left of her two sons and her husband.
Masaai: Ore Mahalon o Kilion neye sii ninche, neaku ore ina kitok enoto olkiyioi lo lmoruo lenye o loo layiok lenyena.

English: Then she arose with her daughters in law, that she might return from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab how that the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread.
Masaai: Nedumunye ninye o nena toyie oo layiok lenyena pee errinyo te ina kop e Moab, amu etoning'o apa ninye te ina kop e Moab nchere etumutana Olaitoriani iltung'ana lenyena neisho ninche endaa.

English: Wherefore she went forth out of the place where she was, and her two daughters in law with her; and they went on the way to return unto the land of Judah.
Masaai: Nedumunye teine aapuo teine wueji netii ninye te nebo ntoyie are oo layiok lenyena, neibung enkoitoi aapuo enkop e Yuda.

English: And Naomi said unto her two daughters in law, Go, return each to her mother's house: the LORD deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me.
Masaai: Kake enyaaka Naomi ajoki nena toyie are oo layiok lenyena, “Enchom entorrinyoto, shomo ake oltung'ani enkaji e ngotonye. Naa meitaasa intae Olaitoriani isupati, anaa apa enintaasa intae ilootuata o nanu.

English: The LORD grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. Then she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice, and wept.
Masaai: Meidimie intae Olaitoriani enoto nkang'itie, oltung'ani ake te intae netum olmoruo!” Neitoki ang'utut ninche, neyietu ninche aaishir.

English: And they said unto her, Surely we will return with thee unto thy people.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “A-a, eikirrinyo iyiook te nebo aapuo enetii iltung'ana linono.”

English: And Naomi said, Turn again, my daughters: why will ye go with me? are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
Masaai: Kake etejo Naomi, “Entorrinyoto enchom ntoyie aainei, kainyoo pee kiriamariyieyie nanu? Keton nanu aata ilayiok te nkoshoke ai eji pee eyooki aayam intae?

English: Turn again, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have an husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should have an husband also to night, and should also bear sons;
Masaai: Entorrinyoto enchom, ntoyie aainei, shomo ake oltung'ani enkoitoi enye, amu atamorua nanu meekure atum olmoruo. Amaa naaji ninye te najo kaata osiligi, anaa napaji ninye tenaa katum olmoruo ena kewarie naiu ilayiok,

English: Would ye tarry for them till they were grown? would ye stay for them from having husbands? nay, my daughters; for it grieveth me much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD is gone out against me.
Masaai: iyanyunyu naa o metubulu? Eipalipala intae meyami intae. A-a, ntoyie aainei, amu keme oleng te nanu te nkaraki intae, nchere aatigilunore nanu enkaina o Laitoriani.”

English: And they lifted up their voice, and wept again: and Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her.
Masaai: Neitoki ninche aayietu aaishir, neng'utut Orpa enkaputani enye kake etamuatakine Rusi ninye.

English: And she said, Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods: return thou after thy sister in law.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Ng'ura, esintani ino eshomo olorere lenye nelo enetii nkaitin enyena; torrinyoyu tusuja esintani ino.”

English: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
Masaai: Kake etejo Rusi, “Mikisai nanu maatung'uai iyie arashu pee arrinyo eitu aasuj iyie; amu ore ewueji nilo ninye nanu alo, ore ewueji nirrag naa ninye nanu airrag; ore iltung'ana linono naa keaku iltung'ana laainei, neaku Enkai ino Enkai ai;

English: Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the LORD do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me.
Masaai: ore ewueji ninang ninye nanu anang, naa te ine aanukari nanu. Maaitaasa nanu Olaitoriani ena aitulus tenaa ninye kaarishie keeya iyie.”

English: When she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, then she left speaking unto her.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Naomi ajo eteenikine asuj ninye, neitu eitoki ajo ae.

English: So they two went until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they were come to Bethlehem, that all the city was moved about them, and they said, Is this Naomi?
Masaai: Neaku eshomo ninche pokira are ometabai Betlehem. Ore ake pee ebau Betlehem neing'asia enkang pooki te nkaraki ninche; nejo nkituaak, “Ai Naomi ena?”

English: And she said unto them, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Emikimpot nanu aajo Naomi, entejoki nanu Mara, amu aaitaasa nanu Olmagilani mbaa e mion.

English: I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?
Masaai: Ashomo apa nanu abore, naatorrinyuo nanu Olaitoriani arok. Kainyoo pee kimpotipoto nanu aajo Naomi, aaisilisilo nanu Olaitoriani neyaua Olmagilani entaboi shumata nanu?”

English: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter in law, with her, which returned out of the country of Moab: and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
Masaai: Neaku etorrinyunye Naomi o Rusi ina oo Lmoabu nara entito o layioni lenye. Etorrinyunye ninche eing'uaa enkop e Moab. Nepuonu ninche Betlehem te nkiterunoto e nkisampuare e shairi.

English: And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name was Boaz.
Masaai: Eeta apa Naomi oltung'ani le sotua lo lmarei lo lmoruo lenye, o ltung'ani karsis, lo lmarei le Elimelek, oji enkarna enye Boas.

English: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
Masaai: Ore Rusi ina oo Lmoabu nejoki Naomi, “Nchooki nanu mashomo enkurma ang'osilu ilng'osil le nkano te siadi ilo latumie nanu ninye omom.” Nejoki Naomi ninye, “Shomo entito ai.”

English: And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
Masaai: Neaku etudumunye Rusi alo asotisho ti atua enkurma asuj lelo ooisampu, nelotu apa ninye ewueji enkurma e Boas laa olo lmarei le Elimelek.

English: And, behold Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said unto the reapers, The LORD be with you. And they answered him, The LORD bless thee.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, eewuo Boas eing'uaa Betlehem, nejoki lelo ooisampu enkurma, “Metaa Olaitoriani te nebo intae!” Newal ninche aajo, “Mikitamayiana Olaitoriani.”

English: Then said Boaz unto his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose damsel is this?
Masaai: Neitoki Boas ajoki ilo aisiaayiani lenye oitasheiki lelo ooisampu, “Keneng'ae ena sila?”

English: And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab:
Masaai: Nejoki ilo sinka aitasheikinoni, “Entito oo Lmoabu apa nairiamunore Naomi te nkop e Moab.

English: And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves: so she came, and hath continued even from the morning until now, that she tarried a little in the house.
Masaai: Netejo ninye, ‘Aatasayia nchooki nanu matasotu naiturrur tiatua irridat le shairi o le nkano te siadi ilooisampu.’ Neaku eewuo ninye, netasotishe ebaiki tadekenya o metabaiki ena kata, eitu ninye eyagie te nkiti rishata.”

English: Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:
Masaai: Neitoki Boas ajoki Rusi, “Ore taata, toning'o, entito ai, milo asotisho ti ai kurma, nimilo aing'uaa ena, kake tataaniki ntoyie aainei.

English: Let thine eyes be on the field that they do reap, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? and when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.
Masaai: Ing'ura iyie ewueji nepuo ninche aaisampishore, nilo iyie asujaa ninche. Keitu nanu aitanap ilbarnot pee mikintanyamal ninche iyie? Naa te niata enkure shomo enetii motioo tooko ina natookutuo ilbarnot.”

English: Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?
Masaai: Negilaki kung neirugokino enkop nejoki ninye, “Kainyoo nanu pee anoto omom too nkonyek inono, eji nikitishilayie hoo nara enkomoni?”

English: And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband: and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people which thou knewest not heretofore.
Masaai: Kake etawalikia Boas ninye ajoki, “Ore nena pooki nintaasa enkaputani ino ebaiki keeya o lmoruo lino aatolikioki nanu aaitobiraki, o ina apa nitung'uayie papaai lino o yieyioo lino o enkop inyi nilotu enkop oo ltung'ana apa limiyiolo.

English: The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
Masaai: Mikitalaaki Olaitoriani ina apa nitaasa, nikincho Olaitoriani olerrinyore te nkiputakinoto Enkai oo Siraeli, naa abori inaipuko enyena iewuo asaru!”

English: Then she said, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.
Masaai: Neitoki Rusi ajo, “Kimpirisie iyie nanu, olkitok lai, amu kintagolo nanu oshoke nirorie esinka ino te supatisho, hoo ninye nemara nanu nabo oo nkaisiayiak inono.”

English: And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
Masaai: Ore te nkata nainosi endaa nejoki Boas, “Wou ene, pee inos endaa nintadoiki oldung'oti lino engirra atua enaisho oo sabibu.” Neaku etotona ninye te nebo nena aisampuak, neitarasaki ninye emukate natapejoki; neinos ninye o metaraposhoyu, neleku.

English: And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not:
Masaai: Ore pee edumunye ninye alo asotisho, neiguan Boas ilbarnot lenyena ajoki, “Enchoo ninye metasotisho ninye tiatua o metong'osilu irridat, nimibuakiki ninye.

English: And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
Masaai: Ore sii entaiki ninye kulie naatii irridat, ning'ueikiki ninye metasotu, nimimbuakiki ninye.”

English: So she gleaned in the field until even, and beat out that she had gleaned: and it was about an ephah of barley.
Masaai: Neaku etasotishe ninye ti atua enkurma o metaa teipa; neitoki aidong nena naatasotuo ninye, neaku efa nabo e ntapa naji shairi.

English: And she took it up, and went into the city: and her mother in law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth, and gave to her that she had reserved after she was sufficed.
Masaai: Nedumu ninye aya nelo atua enkanasa; neitodol enkaputani enye entoki natasotuo ninye, neyaua sii aisho ninye endaa duoo natelekua ninye etaraposhe.

English: And her mother in law said unto her, Where hast thou gleaned to day? and where wroughtest thou? blessed be he that did take knowledge of thee. And she shewed her mother in law with whom she had wrought, and said, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz.
Masaai: Nejoki enkaputani enye ninye, “Kaji duo taata ishomo asotishore? Naa kaji itaasishore? Metamayiani ilo tung'ani likitisirua iyie.” Neaku etolikio ninye enkaputani oltung'ani duo oshomo aaisiaai, nejoki, “Ore enkarna e ilo tung'ani duo lashomo aaisiaai naa keji Boas.”

English: And Naomi said unto her daughter in law, Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said unto her, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.
Masaai: Nejoki Naomi ina tito o layioni lenye, “Metamayiana Olaitoriani ilo leitu eing'uaa esupatisho enye ilo oishu aashu iloo tuata!” Neitoki sii Naomi ajoki ninye, “Olo lmarei lang ilo tung'ani, obo le ntaloishi ang.”

English: And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said unto me also, Thou shalt keep fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.
Masaai: Nejo Rusi, ina tito oo Lmoabu, “Ore te nebo nena, aatiaaka ninye, ‘Tataaniki ilaisiayiak laainei, o metaba anaa neidip enkisampuare.’ ”

English: And Naomi said unto Ruth her daughter in law, It is good, my daughter, that thou go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field.
Masaai: Neitoki Naomi ajoki Rusi, ina tito o layioni lenye, “Keishiaakino entito ai te nilo iyie te nebo nkaisiayiak enyena, pee mikintanyamali ake ti ae kurma.”

English: So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and dwelt with her mother in law.
Masaai: Neaku etataanikia apa ninye nkaisiayiak e Boas, esotisho o metabau enkiting'oto e nkisampuare e shairi o enkano; neton ninye te nebo enkaputani.

English: Then Naomi her mother in law said unto her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?
Masaai: Neitoki Naomi enkaputani enye ajoki ninye, “Entito ai, aimaaing'uraki nanu iyie ang, pee itum aitirring'ayu?

English: And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to night in the threshingfloor.
Masaai: Amaa, Boas, aime olol lgilata lang, naa atua nkaisiayiak enyena itii? Ng'ura eitobir ade shairi kewarie te wueji neidong'ishoreki.

English: Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment upon thee, and get thee down to the floor: but make not thyself known unto the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.
Masaai: Ntukuoyu naa niyela te ilata ninchop ilkilani sidain nidoyio alo ewueji neidong'ishoreki; kake mincho kidol ilo tung'ani o metaba anaa neidip ainosa endaa neokisho.

English: And it shall be, when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the place where he shall lie, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet, and lay thee down; and he will tell thee what thou shalt do.
Masaai: Kake te nelo ninye airrag, tisipu ewueji neirragie ninye; nilo taa abolu nkejek enyena nirrag te ine; naa eikiliki ninye enias.”

English: And she said unto her, All that thou sayest unto me I will do.
Masaai: Newal ninye ajo, “Ore pooki nijo kalo nanu aas.”

English: And she went down unto the floor, and did according to all that her mother in law bade her.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo ninye ewueji neidong'ishoreki neas anaa enaitanapa enkaputani ninye.

English: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn: and she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.
Masaai: Ore eidipa Boas ainosa endaa neokisho netishipe oltau lenye nelo ninye airrag te bayie o sototi le nkurma. Nelotu Rusi akiti nebolu nkejek enyena, neirrag.

English: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself: and, behold, a woman lay at his feet.
Masaai: Ore te mpolos e kewarie neipirriu ilo tung'ani, neibelekenya, naa ng'ura, eirragita enkitok too nkejek enyena!

English: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Ira ng'ae?” Newal ninye ajo, “Ara nanu Rusi, enkaisiaayiani ino; isalaasha olkila lino ntoipo enkaisiaayiani ino amu iyie olo lgilata lang o taana.”

English: And he said, Blessed be thou of the LORD, my daughter: for thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Mikitamayiana Olaitoriani, entito ai; inyaaka aitasapuk ena supatisho aitulusoo tene dukuya, nchere eitu iyie ilo asujaa ilbarnot, aa karsisi o aa aisinak.

English: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.
Masaai: Ore naa taata entito ai, miureishoyu, kaaitaas nanu nena pooki niomonu, amu eyiolo pooki lena ang nchere ira enkitok e tipat.

English: And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I.
Masaai: Naa kesipa nchere ara nanu olo lgilata linyi linyikare, ore ake eyia etii olo lgilata linyikare alang nanu.

English: Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman's part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the LORD liveth: lie down until the morning.
Masaai: Totona ena kewarie, ore tadekenya, ti nikintaas ninye te rishat o ltung'ani lo lgilata, naa sidai; nchoo ninye eas ina. Kake te nemeyieu ninye neas ina rishata o ltung'ani lo lgilata te iyie, ore anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, nalo nanu aas erishata o ltung'ani lo lgilata te iyie. Irraga mekenyu.”

English: And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose up before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor.
Masaai: Neaku eirraga ninye too nkejek enyena o mekenyu, kake etudumunye ninye enasirie; nejoki Boas, “Mincho ake eyiolouni aajo eewuo enkitok ewueji neidong'ishoreki.”

English: Also he said, Bring the vail that thou hast upon thee, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her: and she went into the city.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Iyau ilo karasha linchopito toluaa.” Neaku etoluaa ninye, nepik ninye mboreitin ile e shairi neitanap ninye; nelo ninye atua enkanasa.

English: And when she came to her mother in law, she said, Who art thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.
Masaai: Ore pee elo ninye enetii enkaputani, nejoki ninye, “Kaji eikunari mbaa, entito ai?” Neliki Rusi nena pooki naaitaasa ilo tung'ani,

English: And she said, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty unto thy mother in law.
Masaai: ejo, “Ore kuna boreitin ile e shairi ninye laaishoo, amu etejo ninye, ‘Milo too nkaik naarook enetii nkaputani ino.’ ”

English: Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest, until he have finished the thing this day.
Masaai: Newalu Naomi ajo, “Taanyisho entito ai o metaba anaa niyiolou enetiu ena bae, amu meitirring'a ilo tung'ani, kake kelo taata aitabaya ena bae.”

English: Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spake came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
Masaai: Neilep Boas alo kishomi neton te ine; naa ng'ura ore oladuoo lo lgilata lenye onyikare oimaka Boas nelotu agiroo. Neaku etiaaka Boas, “Mbelekenyunye olchore, totona tene;” neibelekenyunye ninye neton.

English: And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sat down.
Masaai: Neyau ninye ilpayiani tomon le ina anasa nejo, “Entotoni tene;” netoni ninche.

English: And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's:
Masaai: Neitoki ninye ajoki lelo lo lgilata lenye, “Ore Naomi enoshi natorrinyunye te nkop e Moab, nemirita enkiti wueji e nkop apa o ltung'ani lo lgilata lang oji Elimelek.

English: And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it beside thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.
Masaai: Neaku atejo nanu kaaliki iyie, naajoki, Inyang'u te dukuya kulo ootoni tene, o te dukuya kulo payiani lo lorere lang. Tenaa iyie inyang'u; kake te niminyang'u, tolikioki nanu, pee atum atayiolo, amu meetae likae likidutieki pee inyang'u, naa nanu laaitoki asuju.” Nejoki ninye, “Kainyang'u nanu.”

English: Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
Masaai: Neitoki Boas ajoki, “Ore akenya enkolong ninyang'u enkurma te nkaina e Naomi, ninyang'u sii ninye Rusi, ina tito oo Lmoabu, ina oliai olapa lemeishu pee errinyokini enkarna e ilo lemeishu enjung'ore enye.”

English: And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.
Masaai: Neitoki ilo tung'ani lo lgilata lenye ajo, “Maidim nanu ainyang'u te nkaraki kewan ai, pee mainyal ake enjung'ore ai. Iwa iyie erishata ai metaa enino makewan, amu maidim nanu atalaku.”

English: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel.
Masaai: Ele apa olkerreti too le Israel too nkolong'i e apa, too mbaa naaipirta elakunoto o ewalunoto; ore pee eitisipi enkinyiang'a neitayu oltung'ani enamuke neisho olikae, naa ena pukunoto apa enkitabaroto too Siraeli.

English: Therefore the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee. So he drew off his shoe.
Masaai: Neaku ore ake pee ejoki ilo tung'ani lo lgilata lenye Boas, “Inyang'u iyie,” nedotu ninye enamuke.

English: And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi.
Masaai: Neitoki Boas ajoki lelo payiani o ltung'ana pooki, “Irara intae ilchakenini ena olong nchere ainyang'ua nanu te nkaina e Naomi nena pooki apa naara ine Elimelek, o pooki naara ine Kilion o Mahalon.

English: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.
Masaai: O Rusi sii ina tito oo Lmoabu ina, oliai e Mahalon, ainyang'ua nanu ninye metaa enkitok ai, pee eitudupari enkarna e ilo otua te njung'ore enye, pee meiminieki enkarna e ilo lemeishu too lalashera lenyena, o te kishomi e wueji enye; irara intae ilchakenini ena olong.”

English: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. The LORD make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel: and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Bethlehem:
Masaai: Nejo lelo tung'ana pooki ootii kishomi, o lpayiani, “Kira iyiook ilchakenini. Meitotiuo Olaitoriani ina kitok nalotu atua enkaji ino anaa Raheli o Lea, naa ninche pokira naatesheta enkaji e Israel. Tubulu iyie te Efrata nining'oyu te Betlehem;

English: And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the LORD shall give thee of this young woman.
Masaai: naa metotiuo enkaji ino anaa enkaji e Peres, laa ninye etoikio Tamar Yuda, te nkaraki nkera nikincho iyie Olaitoriani tena siankiki.”

English: So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son.
Masaai: Neaku eewa Boas Rusi neitaa enkitok enye; nelo aboitare ninye, neisho Olaitoriani metunutayu, neiu enkayioni.

English: And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel.
Masaai: Nejoki inkituaak Naomi, “Meisisi Olaitoriani, laa ninye leitu kipalaa iyie ena olong miata oltung'ani lo lgilata, naa metoning'oyu enkarna enye te Israel!

English: And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.
Masaai: Keaku ina kerai olikirrinyoki enkishui nikintagol te moruao ino; amu ore ina tito o layioni lino nikinyor iyie, nelang ninye ilayiok oopishana, netoiuo ninye.”

English: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.
Masaai: Kaae nedumu Naomi ina kerai neirragie to lgoo lenye, neaku ninye enkaing'urani enye.

English: And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Masaai: Nedung'oki nkituaak e latia e nkarna, ejo, “Etoikioki Naomi olayioni.” Neisho ninche ninye enkarna aajo Obed; ninye apa menye le Yese, menye le Daudi.

English: Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez begat Hezron,
Masaai: Ena ninye eishoi e Peres: Peres apa menye le Hesron,

English: And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,
Masaai: neiu Hesron Raam, Neiu Raam Aminadab,

English: And Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
Masaai: Neiu Aminadab Nashon, neiu Nashon Salmon,

English: And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
Masaai: neiu Salmon Boas, neiu Boas Obed,

English: And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
Masaai: Neiu Obed Yese, neiu Yese Daudi.

English: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite:
Masaai: Etii apa oltung'ani obo le Ramataim, le ina kop oo ldoinyo e Efraim, oji enkarna enye Elkana olayioni le Yeroham, olayioni le Elihu, olayioni le Tohu, olayioni le Sufi ilo le Efraim.

English: And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
Masaai: Neeta apa ninye nkituaak are; ore enkarna e ina e dukuya naa Hana, ore enkarna e nkae naa Penina. Neeta apa Penina nkera kake meeta apa Hana nkera.

English: And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there.
Masaai: Naa keilep apa ele tung'ani to lari ake o to lari ailep te nkanasa enye alo aserem nepolosaki Olaitoriani loo lororani te Shilo, te ine apa nerayie ilayiok pokira oare le Eli, Hofni o Finehas ilapolosak lo Laitoriani.

English: And when the time was that Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions:
Masaai: Ore apa te ina olong napolosisho Elkana, neisho ninye irubat Penina, enkitok enye o layiok lenyena pooki o ntoyie enyena;

English: But unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion; for he loved Hannah: but the LORD had shut up her womb.
Masaai: naa, ore hoo nenyor apa Hana neisho ninye erubata nabo ake, amu eikeno Olaitoriani enguset enye.

English: And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
Masaai: Ore apa Penina naitayunore ninye naa keitagor ninye oleng neinosie osina, te nkaraki naikeno Olaitoriani enguset enye.

English: And as he did so year by year, when she went up to the house of the LORD, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and did not eat.
Masaai: Neikunari neijia to lari ake, o to lari. Ore anaake te nelo ninye enkaji o Laitoriani neitagor apa ina aini enye ninye. Ore enkaraki ina neishir Hana ometaa menya endaa.

English: Then said Elkanah her husband to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?
Masaai: Ore Elkana ilo payian lenye, nejoki ninye, “Hana, kainyoo peyie inchir? Naa kainyoo pee minya endaa? Naa kainyoo pee eeta oltau lino osina? Aimalusoo too ilayiok tomon te iyie?”

English: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip ninche aainosa endaa, neokisho te Shilo nedumunye Hana. Netonita apa ina kata Eli ilo apolosani to ltonet te mbata e ng'ape e kutukaji e ina aji o Laitoriani.

English: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore.
Masaai: Neeta apa ninye Hana emion sapuk to ltau neomon Olaitoriani, neishir te mion.

English: And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.
Masaai: Nenya ninye olmumai nejo, “Olaitoriani loo lororani, tenaa eing'or iyie te sipata osina le sinka ino, nikidamu nanu, nimincho kirikino esinka ino, kake nincho esinka ino olayioni, naisho nanuninye Olaitoriani inkolong'i pooki e nkishui enye, nemeetae olmurunya oiseyie endukuya enye.”

English: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli marked her mouth.
Masaai: Ore eomonito ninye te dukuya Olaitoriani, neing'or Eli enkutuk enye.

English: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.
Masaai: Eirorita apa Hana to ltau lenye, nchonito enyena e nkutuk ake naaiseuseu nemening'o oltoilo lenye; ore enkaraki ina nejo Eli tenaa kenkitok natemere.

English: And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.
Masaai: Nejoki Eli ninye, “Imera ade o anu? Intalamai ina aisho ino.”

English: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.
Masaai: Kake etawala Hana ajo, “A-a, Olkitok lai, ara nanu enkitok naata emion to ltau; eitu nanu aok enaisho naitemerisho, agira nanu abukoki Olaitoriani enyamali oltau lai.

English: Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.
Masaai: Minko naa esinka ino aitaa enkitok e pesho, amu ore ena rishata pooki kagira alikioo eyieunoto ai o sina lai.”

English: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.
Masaai: Neitoki Eli awaliki, “Shomo te seriani, mikinchoo Enkai oo Siraeli nena nitasayua te dukuya ninye.”

English: And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Nchoo esinka ino menoto omom too nkonyek inono.” Nelo ina kitok te nkoitoi enye nenya endaa, neitu ninye eitoki aisinanuo.

English: And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.
Masaai: Neinyototo ninche aayooki tadekenya neserem Olaitoriani; neitoki aashuko aapuo enkang enye te Rama. Neyiolou Elkana Hana ina kitok enye, nedamu Olaitoriani ninye;

English: Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.
Masaai: ore pee ebaya enkata nenutayu Hana neiu ninye enkayioni, nejo ninye enkarna enye Samuel, amu etejo ninye, “Atoomonuo nanu ninye to Laitoriani.”

English: And the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the LORD the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani oji Elkana o enkaji enye pooki neilep aapuo aaitaiki Olaitoriani olasar te pooki ari, nelak ninye olmumai lenye.

English: But Hannah went not up; for she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD, and there abide for ever.
Masaai: Kake eitu ninye eilep Hana alo, amu etiaaka ninye olpayian lenye, “Te neoruni enkerai lke, nayau nanu ninye, pee etum ataliooyu te dukuya Olaitoriani, neton te ine ntarasi.”

English: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only the LORD establish his word. So the woman abode, and gave her son suck until she weaned him.
Masaai: Nejoki Elkana ilo payian lenye, “Taasa ina naa ninye sidai te iyie; totona ometaba anaa neoruni ninye lke; meibung'a ake duoo ninye Olaitoriani ororei lenye.” Neton ina kitok neing'or aitubulu olayioni lenye, ometaba anaa neere ninye.

English: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the LORD in Shiloh: and the child was young.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eoruni ilke neya ninye ailepie te nebo ninye, oloing'oni loo larin okuni, o entemet nabo e nkurma o olbene lo lchoni le naisho oo sabibu, neyau ninye enkerai ina aji o Laitoriani natii Shilo; naa ei kiti ina kerai.

English: And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.
Masaai: Neyieng' ninche ilo oing'oni, neitoki ninche aayau ina kerai enetii Eli.

English: And she said, Oh my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the LORD.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Olkitok lai! Ore anaa eninchu, Olkitok lai, ara nanu ina kitok apa naitashe tene te dukuya iyie, eomonito Olaitoriani.

English: For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him:
Masaai: Atoomonuo naaishori ena kerai, naaishoo nanu Olaitoriani eomonunoto ai apa natoomono ninye.

English: Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD. And he worshipped the LORD there.
Masaai: Metaa aishoo nanu ninye Olaitoriani. Ore anaa neishu ninye naa keaku olo Laitoriani.” Neserem ninche Olaitoriani te ine.

English: And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.
Masaai: Neitoki Hana aomon nejo, “Keshipakino oltau lai Olaitoriani; eitaaki kitok engolon ai to Laitoriani. Etaboloki enkutuk ai, matakueniki ilmang'ati laainei, amu kang'idakino nanu enjeunoto ino.

English: There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.
Masaai: “Metii likae sinyati anaa Olaitoriani. Metii likae leme iyie, metii endapidapoi nanyaanyukie, Enkai ang.

English: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
Masaai: Emintoki aairo aabuaku to lwuasa, emincho enkitokoos eimu nkutukie inyi; amu ore Olaitoriani naa Enkai e ng'eno, naa te ninye eineneng'i iasat.

English: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.
Masaai: Etigilate nkaik e lelo magil. Kake eitagoloki lelo ooshal.

English: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry ceased: so that the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.
Masaai: Ore lelo apa ooiputakinote neisilenoitie ate pee etum endaa, kake ore lelo apa ooisumash nemeekure eisumash. Etoiuo ina apa olupi nkera naapishana, kake ore ina apa naata nkera kumok nemeekure eeta.

English: The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.
Masaai: Olaitoriani oar metua naa ninye oitopiu. Eitadou ninye aya enemeneng'a neilepunye.

English: The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.
Masaai: Olaitoriani oitaa aisinani naa ninye oitaa karsis. Ninye oitadou, ninye sii oilepie.

English: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S, and he hath set the world upon them.
Masaai: Ninye odumu olaisinani aitung'uaa enterit. nedumu ilaisinak aitung'uaa olchala loo nkuruon. Neitoton ninche te nebo lelo kituaak nejung olorika le nkanyit. Amu ore ing'apeta e nkop naa ino Laitoriani naa shumata ninche eiteleikia enkop.

English: He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.
Masaai: “Kerrip ninye nkejek e lelo ooisiligayu lenyena. Kake keiturrarri lelo arruok tiatua enaimin; amu mme te magilanisho eisulu oltung'ani.

English: The adversaries of the LORD shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.
Masaai: Ore lelo mang'ati lo Laitoriani naa kegiligili aaitaa mbelibelat, kegilunore ninche naa kedaraki ninche te keper. Kedung'oki Olaitoriani enkiguana ineeiting'ie enkop, neisho ninye engolon ilo aiguanani lenye, neilepie ninye engolon eilo lenye otubukokoki eilata aaput.”

English: And Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child did minister unto the LORD before Eli the priest.
Masaai: Nelo Elkana ang te Rama. Neisiaai ina ayioni Olaitoriani te ine netii Eli ilo apolosani.

English: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD.
Masaai: Ore apa lelo ayiok le Eli naa iltung'ana le pesho; meshilaa apa ninche Olaitoriani.

English: And the priests' custom with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand;
Masaai: Ore apa olkuaak loo lapolosak loo ltung'ana naa nchere te neitayu pooki ng'ae olasar, nelotu osinka lo lapolosani, eton eitokitok inkiri, eeta enkisuret oo lala okuni te nkaina enye,

English: And he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.
Masaai: neisuroki ina kisuret atua entereet arashu ene eng'irra arashu emoti oo nkulukuok, arashu ae toki; ore ina pooki nayau ina kisuret neya olapolosani makewan. Neas ninche ina te Shilo too Siraeli apa ooetuo ine.

English: Also before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.
Masaai: Ore ake sii, eton eitu epeji eilata, nelotu osinka lo lapolosani nejoki ilo tung'ani oitayuto olasar, “Nchoru nkiri o lapolosani naapeji. Amu meng'amaa ninye nkiri naayiera te iyie, kake inaajon.”

English: And if any man said unto him, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would answer him, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.
