English: And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.
Masaai: Nemir Yonatan oltim loo Lfilisti apa otii Geba; nening Ilfilisti ina. Neosh Saul emowuo te nkop pooki; ejo, “Nchoo Lhebrania metoning'o.”

English: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel also was had in abomination with the Philistines. And the people were called together after Saul to Gilgal.
Masaai: Nening Isiraeli pooki eji nchere etimira Saul oltim loo Lfilisti, o sii etaa Israeli ilmang'ati too Lfilisti. Neipoti iltung'ana meetu aaibung'are Saul te Gilgal.

English: And the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude: and they came up, and pitched in Michmash, eastward from Beth-aven.
Masaai: Neiturrurro lfilisti pee eitayu olarrabal o Israel, ngarrin oo mbartan nkalifuni ntomoni uni, o lakedok loo mbartan nkalifuni ile, o sikerin ooba anaa osinyai le mbata enaiposha te nkumoi; nepuonu aailepu nepik ilng'oborri lenye Mikmash, natii enkalo oloo saen e Beshafen.

English: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, (for the people were distressed,) then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol iltung'ana le Israel aajo etaa emiri (amu earitae apa iltung'ana oleng) neisudoo iltung'ana ate too nkapuniaa o too ngumot o too ndapidapo o too nkuraren o too lchorroi,

English: And some of the Hebrews went over Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
Masaai: arashu eim ilang'at e Yordan aapuo e nkop e Gad o Gilead. Neton apa etii Saul Gilgal, nesujaa iltung'ana pooki ninye eikirikira.

English: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
Masaai: Neanyisho ninye nkolong'i naapishana, enkata apa natudung'o Samuel; kake eitu elotu Samuel Gilgal, naa kegira iltung'ana aaidapasha aaing'uaa ninye.

English: And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
Masaai: Neaku etejo Saul, “Eyautu ilo asar opejori ene natii, o ilo asar le seriani.” Neitayu ninye olasar opejori.

English: And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.
Masaai: Ore enaidipie enkitayunoto o lasar opejori, ng'ura, nelotu Samuel; neipang Saul alo anang'are ninye neng'asaki ninye.

English: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
Masaai: Nejo Samuel, “Kaa iyie itaasa?” Nejo Saul, “Ore ake pee adol nchere kaaidapashari iltung'ana aaing'uaa, neitu sii ilotu too nkolong'i nikitudung'okinote neiturrurrote sii Lfilisti te Mikmash,

English: Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the LORD: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.
Masaai: najo nanu, ‘Kaapuonu taata Ilfilisti aadoiki te Gilgal, neton eitu aing'oru omom to Laitoriani’; neaku ataaraka kewan, naitayu olasar opejori.”

English: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel Saul, “Itaasa te modai; eitu iyie imbung enkitanapata o Laitoriani Enkai ino, apa nikintanapa; amu ore taata anaata eitubulayie Olaitoriani enkitoria ino te Israel intarasi.

English: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the LORD commanded thee.
Masaai: Kake ore taata mebikoo enkitoria ino; eing'orua Olaitoriani oltung'ani onyor oltau lenye; netegelua ninye Olaitoriani pee eaku olkitok too ltung'ana lenyena, enkaraki neitu iyie imbung ina nikintanapa Olaitoriani.”

English: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
Masaai: Nedumunye Samuel, neilep te Gilgal alo Gibea e Benchamen. Neiken Saul iltung'ana apa ootii te nebo ninye, naa iltung'ana oobaya iip ile.

English: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, abode in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
Masaai: Ore Saul o Yonatan, olayioni lenye, o lelo tung'ana apa ootii te nebo ninche netoni te Geba e Benchamen; kake etuuno Lfilisti ilng'oborri te Mikmash.

English: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned unto the way that leadeth to Ophrah, unto the land of Shual:
Masaai: Ore lelo oarisho neipang'u aaing'uaa ilng'oborri loo Lfilisti too lturrurri okuni; neibelekenya olturrur obo aing'or Ofra, alo enkop e Shual;

English: And another company turned the way to Bethhoron: and another company turned to the way of the border that looketh to the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
Masaai: ore olikae turrur neibelekenya aing'or enkalo e Bet-horon, ore olikae turrur neibelekenya aing'or ilo polosie oing'orita oerata le Sebuim te nkalo o lpurkel.

English: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
Masaai: Nemetumi apa olkunoni hoo obo te nkop pooki e Israel; amu etejo Ilfilisti, “Pee meitobiraki ate Ilhebrania ilalema arashu iremeta.”

English: But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.
Masaai: Kake ore pooki ng'ae loo Siraeli nedoyio alo enetii Ilfilisti pee eii enchempe enye, o osururu, o entolu enye, o empanka enye nariuo nadung'ieki enkano;

English: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.
Masaai: ore apa elaata naa esenti nabo kiti te nkiiyioto oo nchempei o too munton, naa erubata e shekel te nkiiyioto oo ntoluo o te mpikata oo nkeek.

English: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
Masaai: Neaku te ina olong apa o larrabal nemetumi olalem arashu empere te nkaina e likae tung'ani obo le lelo tung'ana apa ootii te nebo Saul o Yonatan; kake eeta apa Saul o Yonatan, olayioni lenye.

English: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash.
Masaai: Neipang oltim loo Lfilisti aapuo empaash e Mikmash.

English: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines' garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.
Masaai: Nejoki nabo olong Yonatan olayioni le Saul olbarnoti apa onap imasaa enyena o larrabal, “Wou, maape iyiook enetii oltim loo Lfilisti te lido kekun.” Kake eitu ninye eliki menye.

English: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
Masaai: Netonita apa Saul te netaaniki Gibea ti abori olchani otii Migron; ore iltung'ana apa ootii te nebo ninye nebaya iip ile,

English: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD'S priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.
Masaai: o Ahija olayioni le Ahitab, ilo alashe le Ikabod olayioni le Finehas, olayioni le Eli, ilo apolosani lo Laitoriani te Shilo eishop enkila dorrop. Neitu eyiolou iltung'ana aajo eshomo Yonatan.

English: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines' garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
Masaai: Ore te mpaash te ine apa neim Yonatan elo oltim loo Lfilisti netii apa emarti enchoto nabo o emarti te nkae shoto; neji nabo Boses neji enkae Sene.

English: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
Masaai: Ore emarti nabo neitashe te moikuape te dukuya Mikmash ore enkae te kopikop te dukuya Geba.

English: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
Masaai: Nejoki Yonatan ilo barnoti apa onapita imasaa enyena o larrabal, “Wou, maape iyiook enetii oltim le kulo lememurata; eidimayu pee eret Olaitoriani iyiook; amu meetae ae toki naidim aibooi Olaitoriani amitiki eitajeusho too lkumok arashu too lkuti.”

English: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo onapita imasaa enyena olarrabal ninye, “Taasa anaa eniyieu niaas; ng'ura, atii nanu te nebo iyie, anaa enatiu ndamunot inono neijia etiu inaainei.”

English: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
Masaai: Nejo ninye Yonatan, “Ng'ura, eikilang iyiook aapuo enetii ilewa, nikintodol ate ninche.

English: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.
Masaai: Ore pee ejoki iyiook, ‘Entaanyisho o maetu iyiook enitii intae;’ nikintashe iyiook aaitirring'a te wueji ang, nimikilep iyiook aapuo enetii ninche.

English: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.
Masaai: Kake te nejo ninche, ‘Wootu elepu enikitii,’ nikilep iyiook aapuo; amu eishorua Olaitoriani ninche apik enkaina ang. Neaku ele olmonekie te iyiook.”

English: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
Masaai: Neitoduaaya pokira oare ate to ltim loo Lfilisti; nejo Ilfilisti, “Eng'ura, epuonu Ilhebrania aaipang'u too ngumot te nenen apa neisudorie ate.”

English: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
Masaai: Neipotu lelo tung'ana lo ltim, Yonatan o ilo anapani loo masaa enyena olarrabal nejo, “Elepu wootu enikitii, naa eikintodol intae entoki.” Nejoki Yonatan ilo anapani lenye, “Ilepu wou tusujuaki amu eishoo ninche Olaitoriani metijing'a atua enkaina e Israel.”

English: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
Masaai: Neked Yonatan ailep too nkaik enyena o too nkejek, nesuju olanapani lenye. Nebatata ninche te dukuya Yonatan near ilo anapani ninche metuata te siadi ninye.

English: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.
Masaai: Ore lelo meneng'a le dukuya, ooitayutuo Yonatan o ilo anapani lenye, nebaya iltung'ana tikitam te rishata naba anaa olpisiai le eka.

English: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
Masaai: Nejing enkuretisho ilng'oborri, o ong'ata, o atua iltung'ana; ore oltim o lelo oarisho neikirikira; neikirikira enkop neaku olkirutoto kitok.

English: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.
Masaai: Neing'or ilarripok le Saul te Gibea e Benchamen; naa ng'ura, eidapashari olorora idie o idie.

English: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul lelo tung'ana ootii te nebo ninye, “Enkenisho eng'urai kaing'ae oshomo ti atua iyiook.” Ore ake pee eidip aaikenisho, ng'ura, metii Yonatan o lanapani lenye loo masaa olarrabal ine.

English: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Ahija, “Iyau ene ilo Sanduku le Nkai.” Amu kelo apa ilo Sanduku le Nkai ina kata te nebo iltung'ana le Israel.

English: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.
Masaai: Ore egira Saul airorie olapolosani, neponari olodoo too lng'oborri loo Lfilisti oleng oleng; nejoki Saul ilo apolosani, “Tushuko enkaina ino.”

English: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.
Masaai: Ore Saul o lelo tung'ana pooki apa ootii te nebo ninye neipirri aapuo olarrabal; naa ng'ura, ore ake olalem lo ltung'ani near olikae, netii apa olmilo kitok oleng.

English: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.
Masaai: Ore ina kata Ilhebrania apa ootii te nebo Ilfilisti te dukuya ina kata, lelo ooshomo aailep atua ilng'oborri, eibelekenyate aaku te nebo Israeli apa ootii te nebo Saul o Yonatan.

English: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
Masaai: Neijia eikununo, ore iltung'ana pooki le Israel apa ooisudoitie ate te ina kop oo ldoinyo e Efraim nening nchere eisikita Ilfilisti; nesuju sii ninche te ngolon epuo enjore.

English: So the LORD saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Bethaven.
Masaai: Neaku etokordua Olaitoriani Israel ina olong; ore olarrabal negiroo te idiaalo Bes-afen.

English: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
Masaai: Nenyamalu iltung'ana le Israel ina olong; amu einosie Saul iltung'ana olmumai, ejo, “Ediaa ilo tung'ani onya endaa o metaba anaa neaku teipa aitalakua too lmang'ati laainei.” Neaku meetae obo too ltung'ana oishamishama endaa.

English: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.
Masaai: Nepuonu iltung'ana pooki atua entim; netii apa enaisho enkop.

English: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejing iltung'ana entim, ng'ura, eitong'ita olkenkei le naisho, kake meetae oltung'ani otipika enkaina enkutuk; amu etureita iltung'ana ilo mumai.

English: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
Masaai: Kake eitu ening Yonatan eitanap papaai lenye iltung'ana ilo mumai; neaku eisuroko eng'udi apa natii enkaina, nepik atua lukuny oo naishi nepik enkaina enkutuk; newang'u nkonyek enyena.

English: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.
Masaai: Nejo obo loo ltung'ana, “Eitanapa papaai lino iltung'ana akurraki to lmumai, ejo, ‘Ediaa ilo tung'ani onya endaa ena olong.’ ” Netanaurate iltung'ana.

English: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
Masaai: Nejo Yonatan, “Eitanyamala papaai enkop; ng'ura ajo etawang'ita nkonyek aainei enkaraki naishamishama enkiti ena aisho.

English: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
Masaai: Kebaa na eikash tenaa keinosa iltung'ana ena olong nena yarunot oo lmang'ati lenye naaineputua ninche. Amu ore taata earata olalem too Lfilisti neme kitok.

English: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
Masaai: Near ninche Ilfilisti ina olong ebaiki Mikmash o metabaiki Aijalon. Neaku etanaurate iltung'ana,

English: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.
Masaai: nekuetiki iltung'ana nena tokitin apa naataarutua, neya ninche nkerra o lmong'i o lasho, neyieng te nkop nenya iltung'ana ninche te nebo osarge.

English: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche Saul, “Ng'ura, easita iltung'ana eng'oki to Laitoriani, aanya nkiri te nebo osarge.” Nejo ninye, “Itaasa te nkaldaroto; embeleleng'u osoit sapuk ene natii nanu.”

English: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Endapashaki ate atua olorere, nijokiki ninche, ‘Nchoo pooki tung'ani meyau olkiteng lenye arashu enker enye, neyieng ninche tene, nenya; nimiasiasa eng'oki to Laitoriani aanya nkiri te nebo osarge.’ ” Neaku eyaua pooki tung'ani olkiteng lenye te nebo ninye ina kewarie apa, neyieng ninche te ine.

English: And Saul built an altar unto the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built unto the LORD.
Masaai: Neshetu Saul olperere lo lasar lo Laitoriani; naa olperere lo lasar le dukuya oitera Saul ashetaki Olaitoriani.

English: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Matadoi aapuo aasujaa Ilfilisti nikimbung, nikiya ntokitin enye nikiar kewarie ninche o mekenyu; miking'uaa iyiook oltung'ani obo te ninche.” Nejo ninche, “Taasa enaba anaa enidol aa sidai te iyie.” Kake etejo olapolosani, “Maigutu iyiook aanyikaki Olaitoriani tene.”

English: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
Masaai: Neikilikuanishore Saul Enkai, “Amaa, kalo nanu adoyio asujaa Ilfilisti? Amaa nchoru ninche apik atua enkaina e Israel?” Kake eitu ninye ewaliki ninye ina olong.

English: And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Wootu ene, intae ilarikok pooki loo ltung'ana; entayiolo nidolidolo eneikununye ena ng'oki taata.

English: For, as the LORD liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
Masaai: Amu ore anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, ilo oitajeu Israel, hoo tenaa atua Yonatan, olayioni lai etii meeta nchere meye ninye.” Kake metii apa oltung'ani ti atua iltung'ana pooki otawalikia ninye.

English: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.
Masaai: Neitoki ninye ajoki Israel pooki, “Entijing intae enkalo nabo, ore nanu o Yonatan, olayioni lai, nikijing enkae shoto.” Nejoki iltung'ana Saul, “Taasa ina nidol aa sidai te iyie.”

English: Therefore Saul said unto the LORD God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped.
Masaai: Neaku etejo Saul, “Olaitoriani Enkai oo Siraeli, kainyoo pee eitu iwaliki osinka lino ena olong? Tenaa atua nanu etii ena torroni arashu atua Yonatan, olayioni lai, Olaitoriani Enkai oo Siraeli, nchoru Urim; kake tenaa atua iltung'ana linono Israel etii ena torroni, nchoru Tummin.” Neyae Yonatan o Saul, nepok iltung'ana.

English: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Entoosh enkukuo te rishata nanu o layioni lai Yonatan.” Neyae Yonatan.

English: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Yonatan, “Tolikioki nanu ina nitaasa.” Neliki Yonatan ninye, “Ainyorrinyorra nanu enkiti aisho te ndukuya e ng'udi apa natii enkaina ai; nele nanu, naa kaye.”

English: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.
Masaai: Nejo Saul, “Metaasa Enkai ena te nanu neitulus; meeta nchere pee miye iyie, Yonatan.”

English: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
Masaai: Nejoki iltung'ana Saul, “Keye Yonatan laa ninye oisula te nkisulata sapuk e Israel? Ekelakua ina! Anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, meetae ninye olpapita le ndukuya enye odoiki enkop; amu etaasishe ninye te nebo Enkai ena olong.” Neaku eitopuaa iltung'ana Yonatan, metaa eitu eye.

English: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.
Masaai: Neilep Saul alo aing'uaa emirata oo lfilisti; nepuo Ilfilisti ewueji enye.

English: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them.
Masaai: Ore apa pee eya Saul enkiguana te Israel, nearare ninye ilmang'ati lenyena pooki te pooki shoto, etaarare Moab, o Ilamoni, o Idom o laiguanak le Soba o Lfilisti; naa ore ake eneibelekenyakine neisulu ninye.

English: And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
Masaai: Nearisho te mpijan nemir Ilmaleki, nekordu Israel aitung'uaa nkaik e lelo apa ooibung'a ninche.

English: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
Masaai: Ore apa ilayiok le Saul naa Yonatan, o Ishfi, o Malkishua; ore nkarn oo ntoyie enyena pokira are ninche kuna; eji ina kikau Merab, neji ina kiti Mikal;

English: And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
Masaai: neji enkitok e Saul Ahinoam, entito e Ahimaas. Neji olkitok lenye le Njore Abna olayioni le Ner, olenkapu le Saul;

English: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
Masaai: Kish apa menye le Saul, ore Ner menye le Abna naa olayioni apa le Abiel.

English: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.
Masaai: Eetae apa olarrabal ogol too Lfilisti too nkolong'i pooki e Saul, naa ore ake pee edol Saul oltung'ani ogol, arashu oltung'ani opi, neitinyikaki ninye kewan enye.

English: Samuel also said unto Saul, The LORD sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the LORD.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel Saul, “Olaitoriani apa laairriwua nanu maatubukoki eilata aput pee iaku olaiguanani te shumata iltung'ana lenyena Isiraeli; ore naa taata toning'o irorei lo Laitoriani.

English: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
Masaai: Inji ejo Olaitoriani loo lororani, ‘Kaitame nanu ina naitaasa Ilamaleki Israel te ina naibooitie ninche te nkoitoi, apa eilepu aaing'uaa Misiri.

English: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
Masaai: Shomo taata taara Amalek, inyala tukul nena pooki naata ninche; mileku ninche, kake taara metua oltung'ani pooki olee o enkitok, enkerai kiti o enanakita, olkiteng o enker, entames o sikiria.’ ”

English: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
Masaai: Neaku eipoto Saul iltung'ana neiken ninche te Telaim, netii apa iltung'ana oopuo too nkejek nkalifuni iip are, o nkalifuni tomon oo ltung'ana le Yuda.

English: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.
Masaai: Nelotu Saul enkanasa oo Lamaleki neirrag arresh to erata.

English: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Ilkeni, “Entudumunye, enchom entadoi enchom entung'uai Ilmaleki, mamut ake nanu intae te nebo ninche; amu intodolutua apa intae esupatisho too ltung'ana pooki le Israel apa pee epuonu aailepu aapuku aaing'uaa Misiri.” Neaku etudumunye Ilkeni aapuku ti atua Ilameleki.

English: And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, that is over against Egypt.
Masaai: Nemir Saul lelo Amaleki ebaiki Hafila o meshomo aabaiki Shur, aa ninye oloo saen le Misiri.

English: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
Masaai: Neibung Agag ilo aiguanani loo Lamaleki eishu, nemut tukul iltung'ana pooki te nepi o lalem.

English: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
Masaai: Kake etelekutua Saul o iltung'ana Agag, o nkerra sidain oleng o lmong'i o lasho o lkuoo le kerra o pooki nara sidai, neitu eyieng ninche amut; ore ina pooki apa nameni naa pesho nemut ninche tukul.

English: Then came the word of the LORD unto Samuel, saying,
Masaai: Nelotu ororei lo Laitoriani enetii Samuel ejo:

English: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night.
Masaai: “Airridua nanu nchere aitaa Saul olaiguanani; amu eibelekenye ninye ashuko aing'uaa esujata ai, neitu eas inkitanapat aainei.” Netagore apa Samuel neishiraki ninye Olaitoriani enkewarie pooki.

English: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.
Masaai: Neinyototo Samuel ayooki pee enang'are Saul tadekenya; netiaakaki apa Samuel, “Eewuo Saul Karmel, naa ng'ura eshetaki kewan esoit nadamunyeki neitoki ashuko, nelo agiroo, nedoyio alo Gilgal.”

English: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of the LORD: I have performed the commandment of the LORD.
Masaai: Nelotu Samuel enetii Saul, nejoki Saul ninye, “Mikitamayiana Olaitoriani; ataasa nanu enaaitanapa Olaitoriani.”

English: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
Masaai: Neitoki Samuel ajo, “Kainyoo naa ena orui oo nkerra too nkiyiaa aainei, o nkipurrot oo lmong'i naning'ito nanu?”

English: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.
Masaai: Nejo Saul, “Eyautua ninche too Lamaleki; amu etelekutua iltung'ana nkerra sidain o lmong'i, pee epolosaki Olaitoriani Enkai; ore nkulie nikitumuta iyiook tukul.”

English: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the LORD hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.
Masaai: Neitoki Samuel ajoki Saul, “Tigirayu! Ekaaliki nanu enaatiaaka Olaitoriani ena kewarie.” Nejoki Saul ninye “Tolimu.”

English: And Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the LORD anointed thee king over Israel?
Masaai: Nejo Samuel, “Ore hoo nira oti too nkonyek inono, aimira iyie endukuya oo loshon le Israel? Kitubukoko iyie Olaitoriani eilata aput aitaa olaiguanani le Israel.

English: And the LORD sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.
Masaai: Nikirriwayie iyie Olaitoriani esiaai, nejo, ‘Shomo, indaikie lelo aing'okok, Ilamaleki, niarare ninche o metaba anaa neishunye.’

English: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the LORD, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the LORD?
Masaai: Kainyoo naa pee eitu ining oltoilo lo Laitoriani? Kainyoo pee ikuetikia nena tokitin nitaarutua, niaas embae torrono too nkonyek o Laitoriani.”

English: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Samuel, “Atoning'o oltoilo lo Laitoriani, ashomo nanu esiaai naa ninye aairriwayie Olaitoriani, ayaua Agag olaiguanani le Amalek, natumuta aidaikie Ilmaleki.

English: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God in Gilgal.
Masaai: Kake eyautua iltung'ana nena tokitin naataarutua, nkerra o lmong'i, nena tokitin sidain apa naatejoki keidaikieki pee epolosaki Olaitoriani Enkai ino te Gilgal.”

English: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
Masaai: Nejo Samuel, “Amaa keeta Olaitoriani enchipai sapuk too lasarri oopejori o nkishorot, anaa te nening'i oltoilo lo Laitoriani? Ng'ura eisidai ening'oto alang olasar, o enkinining'oto alang ilmeregeshi oopir.

English: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
Masaai: Amu etiu empaasharoto anaa esakutore, ore engolon e nkong'u naa esuujisho anaa eseremata oo ntokitin neme Enkai. Ore enkaraki nitanya ororei lo Laitoriani, kitanya sii ninye iyie pee miaku olaiguanani.”

English: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Samuel, “Ataasa nanu eng'oki; amu atigila nanu enkitanapata o Laitoriani o rorei linono, amu aturia nanu iltung'ana naning oltoilo lenye.

English: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, aatoomono nanu, tapalakaki eng'oki ai, nirrinyo te nebo nanu, pee atum nanu ateserema Olaitoriani.”

English: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel Saul, “Marrinyo nanu te nebo iyie; amu itanya iyie ororei lo Laitoriani, nikitanya iyie Olaitoriani pee miaku olaiguanani te Israel.”

English: And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.
Masaai: Ore eshuko Samuel alo aing'uaa, neibung Saul olcholoi lo lkila lenye, nepolosa.

English: And Samuel said unto him, The LORD hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel ninye, “Etopolosayie Olaitoriani enkitoria e Israel te iyie ena olong, neishoo ninye olelatia ino, laa ninye supat likilang iyie.

English: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.
Masaai: Ore sii Ilo ora Enkitoo e Israel nemelejisho arashu eirridu; amu mme oltung'ani ninye, metaa keirridu.”

English: Then he said, I have sinned: yet honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD thy God.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Ataasa nanu eng'oki; ore eyia; iyanyitaki taata te dukuya ilpayiani loo ltung'ana laainei o te dukuya Israel, nirrinyo te nebo nanu, pee atum nanu ateserema Olaitoriani Enkai ino.”

English: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped the LORD.
Masaai: Nerrinyo Samuel asuj Saul; neserem Saul Olaitoriani.

English: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
Masaai: Neitoki Samuel ajo, “Iyau ene natii nanu Agag, ilo aiguanani loo Lamaleki.” Nelotu Agag enetii ninye eshipa. nejo Agag, “Esipa etulusoyie emion e keeya.”

English: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
Masaai: Nejo Samuel, “Ore anaa enatooruo olalem lino nkituaak inkera, keaku sii ninye taata ngutunyi enemeeta enkerai ti atua nkituaak.” nedung Samuel Agag aitaa ndung'ot te dukuya Olaitoriani te Gilgal.

English: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
Masaai: Neitoki Samuel alo Rama; nelo Saul enkaji enye te Gibea e Saul.

English: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul: and the LORD repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.
Masaai: Neitu ae kata eitoki Samuel adol Saul o metabau enkolong e keeya enye, kake eishiraka Samuel Saul. Neirridu Olaitoriani nchere eitaa Saul olaiguanani le Israel.

English: And the LORD said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Bethlehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Samuel, “Nchiraki akenya Saul o anu, idolita ajo atanya nanu ninye pee meaku olaiguanani te Israel? Imputa ina mouo eilata nilo; kaairriwaa nanu iyie enetii Yese, ilo Betlehemi, amu aing'uraka nanu kewan ai olaiguanani ti atua ilayiok lenyena.”

English: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And the LORD said, Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the LORD.
Masaai: Nejo Samuel, “Kaji nanu aiko te nalo? Te nening Saul ina naar nanu matua.” Nejo Olaitoriani, “Iwa enkashe te nebo iyie nijo, ‘Aewuo pee apolosaki Olaitoriani olasar.’

English: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will shew thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.
Masaai: Nintoomon Yese meeu olasar, naa kaaitadol eniaas; nibukoki iyie eilata aput ilo laaipotoki enkarna enye.”

English: And Samuel did that which the LORD spake, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?
Masaai: Neas Samuel ina naitanapa Olaitoriani, nelotu Betlehem. Nepuonu ilpayiani le nkanasa eikirikira aanang'are ninye nejo, “Ilotu iyie te seriani?”

English: And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice unto the LORD: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Te seriani; aewuo nanu apolosaki Olaitoriani; entisinya ate, nipuonunu te nebo nanu olasar.” Neitisiny ninye Yese o layiok lenyena, neitoomon ninche to lasar.

English: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the LORD'S anointed is before him.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau ninche, neing'or ninye Eliab, nedamu ajo, “Esipa etii ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aput dukuya.”

English: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Olaitoriani Samuel, “Ming'or enaikununo ninye arashu enkadoro enye o lkitashei lenye, amu atanya nanu ninye; amu meing'or Olaitoriani anaa enaing'or tung'ani; eing'or tung'ani enaikununo oriong, kake oltau eing'or Olaitoriani.”

English: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.
Masaai: Neitoki Yese aipot Abinadab, neisho ninye metogiroi te dukuya Samuel. Nejo ninye, “Eitu sii egelu Olaitoriani ele.”

English: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.
Masaai: Neitoki Yese aisho Shamas metogiroi. Nejo ninye, “Eitu sii egelu Olaitoriani ele.”

English: Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The LORD hath not chosen these.
Masaai: Neisho Yese ilayiok lenyena pokira oopishana metogiroi te dukuya Samuel. Nejoki Samuel Yese, “Eitu egelu Olaitoriani kulo.”

English: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel Yese, “Ketii ilayiok linono pooki ene?” Nejo ninye, “Etiooyo ilo oti, kake ng'ura, etii ntare.” Nejoki Samuel Yese, “Irriwai olkilikuai metorikuni ninye; amu mikitoni iyiook o metaba anaa nelotu ninye ene.”

English: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ninye olkilikuai, nerikuni ninye aaitijing'u. Naa kenyokie apa ninye newang nkonyek enyena, neikishiaan. Nejo Olaitoriani, “Tudumunye, tubukoki ninye eilata; amu ninye ele.”

English: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
Masaai: Neya Samuel emowuo e ilata nebukoki ninye eilata aput te mpolos oo lalashera lenyena; nelotu Enkiyang'et o Laitoriani te ngolon shumata Daudi ebaiki ina olong neito dukuya. Nedumunye Samuel nelo Rama.

English: But the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.
Masaai: Nelo Enkiyang'et e Nkai aing'uaa Saul, nelotu enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Olaitoriani aitanyamal aisomit ninye.

English: And Saul's servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul isinkan lenyena, “Ng'ura taata, kintanyamalita iyie enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Olaitoriani.

English: Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
Masaai: Nchoo taata olkitok lang eitanap isinkan linono ootii dukuya iyie, pee eing'oru oltung'ani oyiolo atoosho enkawuo oo sinkolioitin; ore ake pee eitoki atii shumata iyie enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Enkai, nerany ninye te ina auo oo sinkolioitin, naa inchiu iyie.”

English: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.
Masaai: Neaku etiaaka Saul isinkan lenyena, “Entorikokoki nanu oltung'ani oyiolo ataranya oleng, nirikuku ninye ene natii.”

English: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the LORD is with him.
Masaai: Newal obo loo lbarnot ajo, “Ng'ura, atoduaa nanu olayioni le Yese le Betlehem, laa kaarriyia te ranyare, oltung'ani opi, naa oltung'ani lo larrabal, arriyia te nkiroroto naa oltung'ani le nkishaa sidai; netii Olaitoriani te nebo ninye.”

English: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.
Masaai: Neaku eirriwayie Saul ilkiliku enetii Yese nejo, “Irriwakaki nanu Daudi, olayioni lino, laa ninye otii ntare.”

English: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.
Masaai: Neitayu Yese olkurrarruu onap imukateni, olbene lo lchoni le naisho, o lkuoo le kine, neirriwaa ninche te Daudi, olayioni lenye, airriwaki Saul.

English: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.
Masaai: Nelotu Daudi enetii Saul, nejing enkisiaayiare enye. nenyorru Saul ninye oleng; neaku ninye olanapani lenye loo masaa o larrabal.

English: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.
Masaai: Neirriwaki Saul olkilikuai Yese, ejo, “Nchoo Daudi eton te nkisiaayiare ai, amu enoto ninye omom too nkonyek aainei.”

English: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
Masaai: Naa ore ake pee elotu enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Enkai shumata Saul, nedumu Daudi enkawuo oo sinkolioitin neosh te nkaina enye; neaku eitagoloki apa Saul, nesupatu, neing'uaa ninye ina kiyang'et torrono.

English: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle, and were gathered together at Shochoh, which belongeth to Judah, and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.
Masaai: Neiturrur apa Ilfilisti ilororani lenye le njore te nkaraki olarrabal. Neiturrurrote apa ninche te Soko, naa ene Yuda, nepik ilng'oborri erishata e Soko o Aseka, te Efes-damim.

English: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
Masaai: Ore Saul o iltung'ana le Israel neiturrurrote, nepik ilng'oborri oerata le Ela, neluaa too lkererin lo larrabal pee earare Ilfilisti.

English: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
Masaai: Neitashe Ilfilisti te nchumata oldoinyo te nkalo nabo, neitashe Isiraeli te nchumata oldoinyo te nkae shoto, etii oerata erishata ninche.

English: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
Masaai: Neipang'u apuku too lng'oborri loo Lfilisti oloing'oni oji Goliat, le Gas, laa ore enkadoro enye negiroo ntemat e nkaina ile,

English: And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
Masaai: neeta apa ninye emaupe o suyai neishopito olkila lo lgoo lo suyai le shekeli nkalifuni imiet.

English: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.
Masaai: Neeta apa nkitushureta o suyai too nkejek enyena. Ore eremet o suyai neika te rishata oo ronyi lenyena.

English: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver's beam; and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
Masaai: Neba enchata e remet enye anaa enauner ore esipil e ina remet enye naa irratilini tomon o imiet; ore ilo onap elong'o enye nelo te dukuya ninye.

English: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
Masaai: Neitashe ninye nebuaaki enjore oo Siraeli ejo, “Kainyoo pee impang'utua intae aapuonu aataaniki olarrabal? Ae mara nanu Olfilisti, nirara intae isinkan le Saul? Entegelaki ate oltung'ani, ninchosho ninye edou alotu ene natii.

English: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
Masaai: Te naidim ninye ataarare nanu naar nanu matua, nikiaku iyiook isinkan linyi; kake te naisulu nanu te ninye naar ninye metua, niakuku intae isinkan lang, nisiaayiayia iyiook.”

English: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
Masaai: Nejo ilo Filisti, “Atamoro nanu iltimito le njore e Israel ena olong; enchooki nanu oltung'ani pee kitum aatarata te nebo.”

English: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening Saul o Siraeli pooki kulo omon lo Lfilisti neing'aeng'ae ninche neirut oleng.

English: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men for an old man in the days of Saul.
Masaai: Naa olayioni lo Lframiti apa Daudi le Betlehem e Yuda, oji Yese, oata apa ilayiok isiet. Ore apa too nkolong'i e Saul netamorua ilo tung'ani oleng neaku oloo larin kumok.

English: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
Masaai: Ore lelo ayiok okuni botoro le Yese netusuja apa Saul aapuo enjore; ore nkarn e lelo ayiok lenyena ooshomo enjore naa Eliab ilo kikau, ore olosujita ninye naa Abinadab, ore oliokuni naa Shama.

English: And David was the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.
Masaai: Daudi apa oloti te pooki; ore lelo okuni botoro netusuja Saul,

English: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
Masaai: kake eshomo apa, Daudi ailoiki enetii, o Betlehem alo airrita ntare e menye.

English: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
Masaai: Too nkolong'i artam apa eewuo ilo Filisti dukuya neitashe te nkitashoto enye, tadekenya o teipa.

English: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched corn, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren;
Masaai: Nejoki Yese Daudi olayioni lenye, “Iyaki ilalashera linono ena efa enkano napejo, o kuna mukateni tomon, ninap aitasiooyo aya ilng'oborri enetii ilalashera linono;

English: And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.
Masaai: niyaki sii kulo belat tomon le ng'orno naitoyioki olkitok le nkalifu enye. Toduaa eneikununo ilalashera linono, nishoru iyie entoki naitodolu ajo itoduaa ninche naa eisupati.”

English: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
Masaai: Ore apa Saul, o ninche, o ltung'ana pooki le Israel, netii atua oerata le Ela, eara o lelo Filisti.

English: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the trench, as the host was going forth to the fight, and shouted for the battle.
Masaai: Neinyototo Daudi ayooki tadekenya, neing'uaa nkerra te nebo olaing'urani, neya endaa, nelo anaa enaitanapa Yese ninye; nelotu lelo ng'oborri egira olorora alo dukuya too lkererin lo larrabal te wueji niarareki; ebuaku to lkiyioi lo larrabal.

English: For Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.
Masaai: Ore Isiraeli o Lfilisti nenyikakino pee eara, enjore earare njore.

English: And David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage, and ran into the army, and came and saluted his brethren.
Masaai: Neing'ueiki Daudi intokitin olaing'urani loo lolan, neipirri alo enetii iltimito, nelo neiroroki ilalashera lenyena.

English: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.
Masaai: Ore eirorie ninche, ng'ura, ore ilo oing'oni ilo Filisti le Gas, oji Goliat neilepu apuku ti atua iltimito loo Lfilisti; neiro lelo rorei anaa apa. nening Daudi ninye.

English: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana pooki le Israel, pee edol ilo tung'ani, neipirri aailany ninye, neirut ninche oleng.

English: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel.
Masaai: Nejo iltung'ana le Israel, “Itoduaa iyie ele tung'ani oilepua? Esipa eewuo ninye ailepu pee emor Israel; ore oltung'ani oar ninye metua, neitaaa ninye olaiguanani karsis te nkarsisisho kitok, neisho ninye entito enye neitaa enkaji e papaai lenye metalakunoyu te Israel.”

English: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi lelo tung'ana apa ooitashe te mbata enye, “Kaa eitaasi oltung'ani oar ele Filisti metua, neitayu emoroto te Israel? Amu kaing'ae ninye ele Filisti lememurata, metaa keidim atamoro njoreitin e Nkai naishu?”

English: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.
Masaai: Newaliki ninye iltung'ana neijia inchere, “Ina eitaasi oltung'ani oar ninye metua.”

English: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab's anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.
Masaai: Nening Eliab, ilo alashe lenye botor, eirorie iltung'ana; neyupuyup engoro e Eliab te nkaraki Daudi, nejo ninye, “Kainyoo iyie pee itadouo ene? Naa kaing'ae itung'ueikia nekua kuti kerra naatii ong'ota? Ayiolo nanu enkitokoos ino, o entorroni o ltau lino; amu iewuo adou aing'or olarrabal.”

English: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Kaa taata ataasa? Aime ororei ake?”

English: And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.
Masaai: Neibelekenya aing'uaa ninye alo enetii olikae, neiro te ina oitoi; neitoki iltung'ana aawaliki ninye anaa duoo ake te dukuya.

English: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul: and he sent for him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening'i lelo rorei ooiroro Daudi, neigil ninche aalimu te dukuya Saul; neirriwaa ninye olkilikuai aipotu ninye.

English: And David said to Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Saul, “Emincho oltung'ani hoo obo epalari te nkaraki ninye; kelo osinka lino aarare ele Filisti.”

English: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Daudi, “Mindim iyie ashomo ataarare ele Filisti; amu ira iyie olbarnoti ake, naa oltung'ani apa ninye lo larrabal ebaiki kitisho enye.”

English: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Daudi Saul, “Keing'or apa osinka lino nkerra e papaai lenye; naa tenelotu olng'atuny arashu olng'arurumi, neya olkuoo ti atua eluaata,

English: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.
Masaai: nalo nanu asujaa naar ninye naitayu nanu olkuoo te nkutuk enye; naa te nelo naadumakino nanu, naibung olmunyei lenye naar metua.

English: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
Masaai: Etaara osinka lino metuata ilng'atunyo o lng'arurumi; ore ele Filisti lememurata naa ketiu anaa obo te ninche, amu etamoro injoreitin e Nkai naishu.”

English: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Ore ilo Aitoriani laaitajeuo nanu too loisotok lo lng'atuny o te nkaina o lng'arurumi naa kaaitajeu te nkaina ele Filisti.” Nejoki Saul Daudi, “Shomo, neaku Olaitoriani te nebo iyie.”

English: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.
Masaai: Neishopoki Saul Daudi iruparen enyena e njore; nepik emaupe o suyai e ndukuya enye, neishopoki olkila lo lgoo lo larrabal.

English: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.
Masaai: Nerreten Daudi olalem lenye ti oriong olkila lenye lo larrabal, nejo pesho ajo alo, amu eitu apa emoku ninche. neitoki Daudi ajoki Saul, “Maidim nanu ashomo te kuna; amu eitu nanu amoku ninche.” Neitayu Daudi ninche airragie.

English: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
Masaai: Neya ninye eng'udi enye te nkaina, negelu isoito imiet oosipa to lkeju, nepik atua ilo bene lenye lo lairritani loo ntare, netii enkopito enye enkaina, nelo anyikaki ilo Filisti.

English: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.
Masaai: Nelotu ilo Filisti anyikaki Daudi, etii ilo anapani le long'o enye dukuya ninye.

English: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eing'or ilo Filisti, nedol Daudi; nemenaa ninye, amu olbarnoti apa ninye onyokie neikishiaan te nking'urata.

English: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo Filisti Daudi, “Kara nanu oldia, pee ilotu enatii too ng'udisin?” Nedek ilo Filisti Daudi too nkaitin enyena.

English: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo Filisti Daudi, “Wou enatii, naa kaisho nanu nkiri o sesen lino imotonyi o loing'ang'e o ng'uesi e ong'ata.”

English: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi ajoki ilo Filisti, “Ilotu iyie enatii to lalem o te mpere, o te nkae pere naado; kake alotu nanu enitii iyie te nkarna o Laitoriani loo lororani, ina Ai oo njoreitin e Israel, naa ninye iyie itamoro.

English: This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
Masaai: Ore ena olong eikipik iyie Olaitoriani atua enkaina ai, naar abatat, nadung'oo endukuya ino, naisho nanu impopong'i oo lororani oo tuata loo Lfilisti ena olong imotonyi o loing'ang'e o ilowuarak le ntim pee etum enkop pooki atayiolo nchere etii Enkai atua israel,

English: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands.
Masaai: neyiolou sii ele turrur pooki nchere keitajeu Olaitoriani neme to lalem o te remet; amu olo Laitoriani ele arrabal naa eikinchoru ninye apik iyie atua enkaina ang.”

English: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edumunye ilo Filisti nelotu pee enang'are Daudi, neipirri Daudi asiooyo alo ilo kereri lo larrabal anang'are ilo Filisti.

English: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
Masaai: Nepik Daudi enkaina atua olbene lenye neitayu osoit, nepik enkopito, neyuk ninye, nenang ilo Filisti olpura le nkomom enye; neimis ilo soit ti atua olpura le nkomom enye, nebatata ninye te nkomom enye aosh enkop.

English: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
Masaai: Neaku eisula Daudi ilo Filisti te nkopito o to soit, neosh ilo Filisti, near ninye metua; nemetii apa olalem enkaina e Daudi.

English: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
Masaai: Neipirri Daudi neitashe te nchumata e ilo Filisti, neya olalem lenye, neyietu ashurtu te nchashur enye, near ninye metua, nedung'orie endukuya enye. Ore ake pee edol Ilfilisti aajo etua oloing'oni lenye neisik.

English: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana le Israel o Yuda nedumunye te mbuakunoto nesuj Ilfilisti o metabai Gas o nchomito e Ekron neaku ore lelo Filisti loo lbaa nebatata ebaiki She-ara-im o metabaiki Gas o Ekron.

English: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.
Masaai: Nepuonu Israeli aashukunye te mirata oo Lfilisti neya intokitin too lng'oborri lenye.

English: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.
Masaai: Neyau Daudi endukuya eilo Filisti Yerusalem, kake etipika imasaa enyena o larrabal atua olngobor lenye.

English: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Saul Daudi elo aarare ilo Filisti, nejoki ninye Abna, olkitok le njore, “Abna, kole ng'ae ele barnoti?” Nejo Abna, “Anaa enaishu oltau lino, olaiguanani, maaidim nanu atolimu.”

English: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling is.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Inkilikuanu kole ng'ae ele ayioni.”

English: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
Masaai: Ore eshukunye Daudi aing'uaa enkirragata e ilo Filisti, neya Abna ninye, neyau ninye dukuya Saul eeta elukunya e ilo Filisti te nkaina enye.

English: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul ninye, “Ira iyie ole ng'ae, lo barnoti?” Newal Daudi ajo, “Ara nanu olo sinka lino Yese le Betlehem.

English: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eidip airorie Saul, neibung'a oltau le Yonatan oltau le Daudi, nenyorru Yonatan ninye anaa oltau lenye kewan.

English: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father's house.
Masaai: Nerik Saul ninye ina olong, nemeisho ninye metushukoyu alo enkang enye.

English: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
Masaai: Nenya Yonatan olmumai lo sotua te nebo Daudi, enkaraki apa nanyor ninye anaa oltau lenye kewan.

English: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
Masaai: Neitayu Yonatan olkila apa oishopito neisho Daudi, o masaa enyena, o lalem lenye o enkawuo o enkimeita enye.

English: And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul's servants.
Masaai: Naa ore ake te neipang Daudi alo eneba anaa eneirriwayie Saul nedupoyu; neaku etipika ninye Saul shumata iltung'ana le njore. Naa eisidai apa ina too nkonyek oo ltung'ana pooki o too nkonyek sii oo sinkan le Saul.

English: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.
Masaai: Ore egira aapuonu ang, ina kata pee eshukunye Daudi eing'uaa esesekuanata e ilo Filisti, neipang'u nkituaak aapuonu too nkanas pooki e Israel, eranyisho neiguran pee enang'are olaiguanani Saul, too ntampurini, o too sinkolioitin le ng'ida, o too nkinantani oo sinkolioitin.

English: And the women answered one another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
Masaai: Neranyakino nkituaak maate eraposhoki ejo, “Etasesekuana Saul nkalifuni enyena, nesesekuan Daudi nkalifuni tomon enyena.”

English: And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him; and he said, They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?
Masaai: Negoro Saul oleng, ore ena kiroroto neitu eitiship ninye; nejo ninye, “Eterrepakitia ninche Daudi nkalifuni tomon, ore nanu naaterrepakitia nkalifuni; kainyoo ae naitoki ninye aata meteleku enkitoria?

English: And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.
Masaai: Neduaaki Saul Daudi olom ebaiki ina olong neito dukuya.

English: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house: and David played with his hand, as at other times: and there was a javelin in Saul's hand.
Masaai: Ore pee ekenyu nelotu enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Enkai nejing atua Saul, neiyiang'iyiang ninye ti atua enkaji enye, eoshito Daudi enkawuo oo sinkolioitin, anaa ake. Neeta apa Saul empere te nkaina enye;

English: And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.
Masaai: nengoroo Saul empere amu etejo ninye, “Apudaki nanu Daudi esuntai.” Kake etapaashare Daudi ninye katitin are.

English: And Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him, and was departed from Saul.
Masaai: Keure apa Saul Daudi, amu etii Olaitoriani te nebo ninye kake etung'uayie Saul.

English: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
Masaai: Neaku eiwuang'ie Saul ninye te ine netii, neitaa ninye olkitok le nkalifu neipang alo nelo dukuya iltung'ana.

English: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the LORD was with him.
Masaai: Netum Daudi dupoto te nena pooki apa naataasa; amu etii Olaitoriani te nebo ninye.

English: Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Saul nchere enoto ninye dupoto sapuk, neureyu ninye.

English: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.
Masaai: Kake ore Israel pooki o Yuda pooki naa kenyor apa Daudi amu eshomo apa ninye aipang nejing'u atua te dukuya ninche.

English: And Saul said to David, Behold my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight the LORD'S battles. For Saul said, Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Daudi, “Nena entito ai botor Merab; kaaisho nanu iyie pee intaa enkitok; kake tudupayu te nanu niarisho too larrabali lo Laitoriani.” Amu etejo Saul, “Mincho enkaina ai eaku shumata ninye, kake nchoo enkaina oo Lfilisti eaku shumata ninye.”

English: And David said unto Saul, Who am I? and what is my life, or my father's family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king?
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Saul, “Kara nanu ng'ae, naa kainyoo olmarei lai, olmarei le papaai te Israel, metaa kaaku nanu olaputani lo laiguanani?”

English: But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul's daughter should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.
Masaai: Kake te nkata apa nataa keishori Merab, entito e Saul, Daudi, neishori ninye Adriel ilo Meholati meitaa enkitok.

English: And Michal Saul's daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.
Masaai: Nenyor apa entito e Saul, Mikal, Daudi; neliki ninche Saul, neitiship ina toki ninye.

English: And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son in law in the one of the twain.
Masaai: Nejo Saul, “Ntasho maishoo nanu ninye, pee etum ataa orreshet te ninye, pee etum sii enkaina oo Lfilisti ataarare ninye.” Metaa etiaaka Saul Daudi te nkata e are, “Iaku taata iyie olaputani lai.”

English: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, Commune with David secretly, and say, Behold, the king hath delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: now therefore be the king's son in law.
Masaai: Neitanap Saul isinkan lenyena ejo, “Erorie Daudi too nkurrat nijokiki, ‘Ng'ura, eikishipakino iyie olaiguanani, naa eikinyor isinkan lenyena pooki; ore naa taata taa olaputani lo laiguanani.’ ”

English: And Saul's servants spake those words in the ears of David. And David said, Seemeth it to you a light thing to be a king's son in law, seeing that I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?
Masaai: Neiro isinkan le Saul lelo rorei too nkiyiaa e Daudi. Nejo Daudi, “Idolidolo intae aa entoki kiti te neaku oltung'ani olaputani lo laiguanani, idolitata aajo ara nanu oltung'ani aiterani lemening'o?”

English: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye isinkan le Saul, “Inji o nji eiroro Daudi.”

English: And Saul said, Thus shall ye say to David, The king desireth not any dowry, but an hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king's enemies. But Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Entoliki Daudi ijokiki, ‘Meyieu olaiguanani entoki e nkaputi meteleku isuaaten iip oo Lfilisti pee etum aitalaku elap too lmang'ati lo laiguanani.’ ” Naa kejo apa Saul pee eisho Daudi metua te nkaina oo Lfilisti.

English: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king's son in law: and the days were not expired.
Masaai: Ore ake eliki isinkan lenyena Daudi kulo rorei, neitiship Daudi ina neaku olaputani lo laiguanani. Ore eton eitu eishunye enkata,

English: Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king's son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.
Masaai: nedumunye Daudi nelo, te nebo iltung'ana lenyena, near metuata Ilfilisti iip are; neyau Daudi isuaaten enye, naaishooki apa te siana nalulung'a olaiguanani, pee etum ninye ataa olaputani lo laiguanani. Neisho Saul ninye ina tito enye Mikal meitaa enkitok.

English: And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal Saul's daughter loved him.
Masaai: Kake ore ake pee edol Saul neyiolou ajo etii Olaitoriani te nebo Daudi, o nchere kenyor Isiraeli pooki ninye,

English: And Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul became David's enemy continually.
Masaai: neponari Saul aureyu Daudi oleng. Neaku etaa apa Saul olmang'atinta le Daudi anaake.

English: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, after they went forth, that David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by.
Masaai: Neitoki ilkituaak loo Lfilisti aaipang'u aapuonu olarrabal, naa ore ake anaa te nepuonu netum Daudi dupoto sapuk alang isinkan pooki le Saul; neaku ore apa enkarna enye naa kejukari oleng.

English: And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.
Masaai: Neirorie Saul Yonatan, olayioni lenye, o lelo sinkan lenyena pooki, nchere pee ear ninche Daudi metua. Kake ore Yonatan, olayioni le Saul, keshipakino apa Daudi oleng.

English: But Jonathan Saul's son delighted much in David: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:
Masaai: Nejoki Yonatan Daudi, “Ore Saul, papaai lai, naa eiking'oru iyie aar tua; neaku tagolie kewan tadekenya, totona te wueji misil isudoi kewan;

English: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou art, and I will commune with my father of thee; and what I see, that I will tell thee.
Masaai: naa kalo nanu aipang aitashe atashare papaai lai te ine wueji nitii, nairorie nanu papaai lai mbaa inono; naa te nayiolou nanu pooki toki naaliki iyie.”

English: And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works have been to thee-ward very good:
Masaai: Neiro Yonatan mbaa sidain ti alo Daudi te Saul, papaai lenye, nejoki ninye, “Mincho olaiguanani eas eng'oki ti alo osinka lenye Daudi; amu eitu ninye eas eng'oki tialo iyie, amu ore nkiaasin enyena naa ine nkisiaayiare sidain apa te iyie;

English: For he did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and the LORD wrought a great salvation for all Israel: thou sawest it, and didst rejoice: wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?
Masaai: amu etipika ninye enkishui enye nkaik enyena nesesekuan ninye ilo Filisti, neyaki Olaitoriani Israel pooki emirata kitok. Itoduaa apa iyie, ning'idayu; kainyoo naa pee ias eng'oki to sarge lemeeta entioto aar Daudi metua meeta emporeet?”

English: And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As the LORD liveth, he shall not be slain.
Masaai: Nening Saul oltoilo le Yonatan; nenya Saul olmumai ajo, “Anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, meari ninye metua.”

English: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan shewed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as in times past.
Masaai: Neipotu Yonatan Daudi, neitodol Yonatan ninye kuna baa pooki. Neriku Yonatan Daudi enetii Saul, netii apa ninye ine netii ninye anaa apa te dukuya.

English: And there was war again: and David went out, and fought with the Philistines, and slew them with a great slaughter; and they fled from him.
Masaai: Neitoki olarrabal apuku; neipang Daudi alo nearare Ilfilisti, neitayu esesekuanare sapuk ti atua ninche, neaku eipirritio te dukuya ninye.

English: And the evil spirit from the LORD was upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand: and David played with his hand.
Masaai: Neitoki enkiyang'et torrono naing'uaa Olaitoriani alotu shumata Saul, etonita ti atua enkaji enye eeta empere enye te nkaina enye; neoshito Daudi enkawuo oo sinkolioitin.

English: And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the javelin; but he slipped away out of Saul's presence, and he smote the javelin into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.
Masaai: Nejo Saul apudaki Daudi esuntai te mpere; kake etapaashare Daudi Saul, neaku eibitaka empere esuntai. neisik Daudi, neimisho.

English: Saul also sent messengers unto David's house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal David's wife told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.
Masaai: Ore ina kewarie neirriwaa Saul ilkiliku enkaji e Daudi metaleeno ninye, pee etum ataara ninye metua tadekenya. Kake etiaaka ninye Mikal, enkitok e Daudi, “Ti nimintajeu enkishui ino ena kewarie, ore taisere niye.”

English: So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.
Masaai: Neaku eitadoyie Mikal Daudi aimie elusie nelo ninye aisik neimisho.

English: And Michal took an image, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats' hair for his bolster, and covered it with a cloth.
Masaai: Neya Mikal enkitanyaanyukoto neirragie ninye te ndapash nepik entoki nairishunyeki endukuya oo lpapit loo ntare elukunya enye, neimulumul too nkarash.

English: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eirriwaa Saul ilkiliku meshomo aaya Daudi, nejo ninye, “Kemuei ninye.”

English: And Saul sent the messengers again to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Saul ilkiliku meshomo aadol Daudi, ejo, “Eyakaki nanu ti atua endapash, pee atum nanu ataara ninye metua.”

English: And when the messengers were come in, behold, there was an image in the bed, with a pillow of goats' hair for his bolster.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejing'u lelo kipaareta, ng'ura, etii ina kitanyaanyukoto endapash, o ina toki nairishunyeki endukuya oo lpapit loo nkineji te ndukuya enye.

English: And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; why should I kill thee?
Masaai: Nejoki Saul Mikal “Kainyoo pee kiteleja aikonji, nincho olmang'atinta lai meshomo neaku etajeuo ninye?” Newaliki Mikal Saul, “Aatiaaka ninye nanu, ‘Ntasho mashomo; kainyoo pee aar nanu iyie tua?’ ”

English: So David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.
Masaai: Neisik Daudi neimisho nelotu apa ninye enetii Samuel te Rama, neliki nena pooki naaitaasa Saul ninye. Ore ninye o Samuel nepuo aabik te Naios.

English: And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.
Masaai: Netiaakaki apa Saul, “Ng'ura, etii Daudi Naios te Rama.”

English: And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the Spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul airriwaa ilkiliku meyau Daudi; ore ake pee edol ninche olturrur loo loibonok le Nkai eibonisho, o Samuel aa olarikoni te shumata ninche, nelotu enkiyang'et e Nkai shumata lelo kipaareta le Saul, neibonisho sii ninche.

English: And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elikini Saul, neirriwaa ninye kulikae kipaareta, neibonisho sii ninche. Neitoki Saul airriwaa ilkiliku te nkata e uni, neibonisho ake sii ninche.

English: Then went he also to Ramah, and came to a great well that is in Sechu: and he asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And one said, Behold, they be at Naioth in Ramah.
Masaai: Neitoki ninye makewan alo Rama, nelotu ilo shorro sapuk apa otii Seku; neikilikuanu ajo, “Kaji etii Samuel o Daudi?” Nejo obo, “Ng'ura, etii ninche Naios te Rama.”

English: And he went thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on, and prophesied, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
Masaai: Nelo ninye teine Naios te Rama; nelotu enkiyang'et e Nkai shumata ninye, ore eloito neibonisho ninye, o metaba anaa nelotu ninye Naios e Rama.

English: And he stripped off his clothes also, and prophesied before Samuel in like manner, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets?
Masaai: Neshurtu sii ninye nkilani enyena, neibonisho sii ninye te dukuya Samuel, neirrag meeta enkila ina olong pooki o ina kewarie pooki. Neaku etejoki, “Ketii sii ninye Saul atua iloibonok le Nkai?”

English: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what is mine iniquity? and what is my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi aisik aing'uaa Naios te Rama, nelotu ajoki Yonatan, “Kainyoo nanu ataasa? Kainyoo entorroni ai? Naa kainyoo eng'oki ai te dukuya papaai lino, metaa keing'oru ninye enkishui ai?”

English: And he said unto him, God forbid; thou shalt not die: behold, my father will do nothing either great or small, but that he will shew it me: and why should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.
Masaai: Nejoki Yonatan ninye, “Metalakuana ina! Miye iyie. Ng'ura, meas papaai toki aa kitok o aa kiti eitu aaimakinye nanu; naa kainyoo naa pee aamikinye nanu papaai ena? Mme neijia etiu.”

English: And David sware moreover, and said, Thy father certainly knoweth that I have found grace in thine eyes; and he saith, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved: but truly as the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step between me and death.
Masaai: Kake etawala Daudi ajo, “Eyiolo papaai lino oleng nchere anoto nanu omom too nkonyek inono; nejo ninye, ‘Mincho Yonatan eyiolou ena, pee megoro ake.’ Kake esipa, anaa enaishu Olaitoriani o anaa enaishu oltau lino, eroruata nabo ake natii erishata nanu o keeya.”
