English: Then said Jonathan unto David, Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I will even do it for thee.
Masaai: Neitoki Yonatan ajoki Daudi, “Ore pooki nijo, naaitaas nanu iyie.”

English: And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Yonatan, “Ng'ura, olapa ng'ejuk taisere, nemajoyio nanu eitu aton te mesa te nebo olaiguanani, kake nchooki nanu mashomo, pee atum aisudoi kewan ti ong'ata o metabau enkolong e uni teipa.

English: If thy father at all miss me, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Bethlehem his city: for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.
Masaai: Te naalau nanu papaai lino tukul, nijoki, ‘Etasaishe Daudi aomonu pee ekuet alo Betlehem, enkanasa enye; amu etii ine olasar anaake to lari to lmarei pooki.’

English: If he say thus, It is well; thy servant shall have peace: but if he be very wroth, then be sure that evil is determined by him.
Masaai: Te nejo ninye, ‘Sidai!’ nesidanu to sinka lino; kake te negoro ninye, nitum atayiolo ajo eitobirita ninye entorroni.

English: Therefore thou shalt deal kindly with thy servant; for thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of the LORD with thee: notwithstanding, if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why shouldest thou bring me to thy father?
Masaai: Neaku intaasa osinka lino te supatisho, amu iyaua osinka lino atua olmumai osinya lo sotua te nebo iyie. Kake te netii entorroni atua nanu, taaraki iyie nanu; amu kainyoo paa papaai lino kiyaki?”

English: And Jonathan said, Far be it from thee: for if I knew certainly that evil were determined by my father to come upon thee, then would not I tell it thee?
Masaai: Nejo Yonatan, “Mikitalama kuna! Amaa naaji tenaa kayiolo nchere eitobirita papaai entorroni pee elotu shumata iyie, aimaaliki nanu iyie?”

English: Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me? or what if thy father answer thee roughly?
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi ajoki Yonatan, “Kaing'ae laaliki nanu tenaa eikiwaliki papaai lino te nkisikong'ota?”

English: And Jonathan said unto David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they went out both of them into the field.
Masaai: Nejoki Yonatan Daudi, “Wou, maipang'a aapuo ong'ota.” Neaku eipang'a pokira oare aapuo ong'ota.

English: And Jonathan said unto David, O LORD God of Israel, when I have sounded my father about to morrow any time, or the third day, and, behold, if there be good toward David, and I then send not unto thee, and shew it thee;
Masaai: Nejoki Yonatan Daudi, “Metaa Olaitoriani, Enkai oo Siraeli shakeni! Te naimakinye nanu papaai lai tena rishata taisere, arashu te nkolong e uni, ng'ura, tenaa esidai ninye ti alo iyie, aimairriu nanu olkilikuai pee aaitayiolo iyie.

English: The LORD do so and much more to Jonathan: but if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will shew it thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace: and the LORD be with thee, as he hath been with my father.
Masaai: Kake te nelo neaku keitiship papaai lai pee kintaas iyie entorrono, metaasa sii Olaitoriani ina te Yonatan, neitulusoo sii te nemaaitayiolo nanu, areu iyie shomo, pee itum ashomo te seriani. Metaa Olaitoriani te nebo iyie, anaa enataa te nebo papaai lai.

English: And thou shalt not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of the LORD, that I die not:
Masaai: Te neton nanu aishu, ntoduaaki nanu enyorrata nemeibelekenya o Laitoriani, pee maye nanu;

English: But also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever: no, not when the LORD hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.
Masaai: nimidung esupatisho ino aitung'uaa enkaji ai ntarasi. Te neiwuang'ie Olaitoriani adung'oo pooki ng'ae loo lmang'ati le Daudi aiwuang'ie ti oriong e nkop,

English: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let the LORD even require it at the hand of David's enemies.
Masaai: mincho enkarna e Yonatan edung'ori aaitung'uaa enkaji e Daudi. Naa meitalaku Olaitoriani elap too lmang'ati le Daudi.”

English: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
Masaai: Neitoki Yonatan ainosie Daudi olmumai aigil ti alo enyorrata enye te ninye; amu kenyor apa ninye anaa enanyor oltau lenye.

English: Then Jonathan said to David, To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.
Masaai: Neitoki Yonatan ajoki ninye, “Ore taisere naa olapa ng'ejuk; naa eikilai iyie, enkaraki nemetii toki olorika lino.

English: And when thou hast stayed three days, then thou shalt go down quickly, and come to the place where thou didst hide thyself when the business was in hand, and shalt remain by the stone Ezel.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni naa eikilai iyie oleng; neaku shomo ewueji apa nisudoriyie kewan aa torrok mbaa, niton te mbata oo soito oosoto.

English: And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.
Masaai: Naa kang'oroo nanu mbaa uni embata enye anaa duoo kaata entoki nang'orito.

English: And, behold, I will send a lad, saying, Go, find out the arrows. If I expressly say unto the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee, take them; then come thou: for there is peace to thee, and no hurt; as the LORD liveth.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, kairriu nanu enkerai, ajoki, ‘Shomo, ing'oru mbaa.’ Ore ake pee ajoki enkerai, ‘Ng'ura ena shoto ino etii mbaa, iyau ninche’; nilotu iyie, amu, ore anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, keserian te iyie nemetii embatisho.

English: But if I say thus unto the young man, Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way: for the LORD hath sent thee away.
Masaai: Kake te najoki nanu ilo barnoti, ‘Ng'ura etii mbaa te idia alo iyie;’ shomo, amu Olaitoriani likirriwayie iyie shomo.

English: And as touching the matter which thou and I have spoken of, behold, the LORD be between thee and me for ever.
Masaai: Ore ti alo ina bae nikiimakitia nanu o iyie, ng'ura, etii Olaitoriani erishata iyie o nanu ntarasi.”

English: So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat him down to eat meat.
Masaai: Neaku eisudoyie Daudi kewan ti atua enkurma; ore ake pee elotu olapa ng'ejuk, neton olaiguanani anya endaa.

English: And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, even upon a seat by the wall: and Jonathan arose, and Abner sat by Saul's side, and David's place was empty.
Masaai: Neton olaiguanani to lorika lenye, anaa too nkulie katitin, to lorika otii embata e suntai; neton Yonatan aipirakinore, neton Abna atashare Saul kake keisiu ewueji e Daudi.

English: Nevertheless Saul spake not any thing that day: for he thought, Something hath befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean.
Masaai: Ore eyia eitu ejo Saul ae ina olong; amu etejo ninye, “Eeta ake naanoto ninye; mesinya ninye, esipa mesinya ninye.”

English: And it came to pass on the morrow, which was the second day of the month, that David's place was empty: and Saul said unto Jonathan his son, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to day?
Masaai: Kake ore te nkolong e are, taisere e tulusoyie olapa ng'ejuk, neisiu ake ewueji e Daudi. Nejoki Saul Yonatan, olayioni lenye, “Kainyoo pee eitu elotu olayioni le Yese anya endaa, ng'ole arashu taata?”

English: And Jonathan answered Saul, David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Bethlehem:
Masaai: Newaliki Yonatan Saul ajoki, “Aatasayia nanu Daudi aomonu pee elo Betlehem;

English: And he said, Let me go, I pray thee; for our family hath a sacrifice in the city; and my brother, he hath commanded me to be there: and now, if I have found favour in thine eyes, let me get away, I pray thee, and see my brethren. Therefore he cometh not unto the king's table.
Masaai: etejo ninye, ‘Nchooki nanu mashomo; amu eeta olmarei lang olasar ti atua enkang, naaitanapa nanu olalashe lai pee atii ine. Neaku taata, te nanoto nanu omom too nkonyek inono, nchooki mashomo, pee adol ilalashera laainei.’ Te nkaraki ena eitu ninye elotu emesa o laiguanani.”

English: Then Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, Thou son of the perverse rebellious woman, do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own confusion, and unto the confusion of thy mother's nakedness?
Masaai: Neyupuyup engoro e Saul tialo Yonatan, nejoki ninye Yonatan “Iyie olayioni le nkitok modai nemening'isho, aimayiolo nanu ajo itegelua iyie olayioni le Yese te nkurruna ino makewan, o te nkurruna e masipaisho e ng'utunyi?

English: For as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. Wherefore now send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die.
Masaai: Amu ore anaa enaishu olayioni le Yese ti oriong kop, mibul iyie nemebul enkitoria ino. Metaa irriwai olkilikuai niyau ninye enatii, amu esipa eye ake.”

English: And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said unto him, Wherefore shall he be slain? what hath he done?
Masaai: Neitoki Yonatan awaliki Saul, papaai lenye ajoki, “Kainyoo pee eari ninye metua? Kainyoo etaasa ninye?”

English: And Saul cast a javelin at him to smite him: whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David.
Masaai: Kake etang'oroyie Saul empere enye ajo ang'or ninye; neaku etayiolo Yonatan nchere enyokita apa papaai lenye ajo aar Daudi metua.

English: So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did eat no meat the second day of the month: for he was grieved for David, because his father had done him shame.
Masaai: Nedumunye Yonatan aing'uaa emesa te ngoro napi neitu enya endaa te nkolong e are o lapa, amu eishirieki te nkaraki Daudi, te nkaraki naitukurrua papaai lenye ninye.

English: And it came to pass in the morning, that Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little lad with him.
Masaai: Ore tadekenya neipang Yonatan alo atua enkurma ewueji netoning'okinote o Daudi, nelo te nebo ninye enkiti ayioni.

English: And he said unto his lad, Run, find out now the arrows which I shoot. And as the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye enkerai enye, “Kueta ing'oru nena baa natang'oroyie nanu.” Ore ekuet enkayioni nengoroo embae te idia alo ninye.

English: And when the lad was come to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the lad, and said, Is not the arrow beyond thee?
Masaai: Ore ake elotu enkayioni ewueji netii ina bae natang'oroyie Yonatan, neipot Yonatan enkayioni nejoki,

English: And Jonathan cried after the lad, Make speed, haste, stay not. And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.
Masaai: “Aimetii embae te idia alo iyie?” Neipot Yonatan enkayioni, “Tasiooi, isarisara, miton.” Neaku etasotuo enkayioni e Yonatan mbaa, nelotu enetii olkitok lenye.

English: But the lad knew not any thing: only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
Masaai: Kake meyiolo apa ina ayioni toki; Yonatan ake o Daudi ooyiolo ina bae.

English: And Jonathan gave his artillery unto his lad, and said unto him, Go, carry them to the city.
Masaai: Neisho Yonatan imasaa enyena olarrabal ina ayioni nejoki ninye, “Shomo iwa ninche enkanasa.”

English: And as soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times: and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.
Masaai: Ore ake eshomo ina ayioni nedumunye Daudi te mbata oo soito oorupa, nebatata ninye te nkomom enye abaiki enkop, neirrugo katitin uni; neng'ututa maate, neishirakino maate, o metaba anaa neyagaa Daudi.

English: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.
Masaai: Neitoki Yonatan ajoki Daudi, “Shomo te seriani, amu ore anaa enikinosa olmumai iyiook pokira te nkarna o Laitoriani, kijo, Olaitoriani otii erishata nanu o iyie, o erishata e ishoi ai o eshoi ino, intarasi.” Nedumunye ninye nelo; nelo Yonatan ajing enkanasa.

English: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David, and said unto him, Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?
Masaai: Nelotu Daudi Nob enetii Ahimelek olapolosani; nelotu Ahimelek anang'are Daudi eikirikira, nejoki ninye, “Kainyoo paa iyie openy, nemetii hoo obo te nebo iyie?”

English: And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know any thing of the business whereabout I send thee, and what I have commanded thee: and I have appointed my servants to such and such a place.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Ahimelek ilo apolosani, “Aairriwayie nanu olaiguanani te mbae naje, naajoki nanu, ‘Mincho ake hoo ng'ae eyiolou ae toki ena bae naa ninye aairriwarie, naa ninye aaitanapa iyie.’ Aata nanu ndung'eta oo lbarnot te wueji neje.

English: Now therefore what is under thine hand? give me five loaves of bread in mine hand, or what there is present.
Masaai: Ore naa, kainyoo iata? Nchooki nanu imukateni imiet, arashu entoki naba anaa enatii ene.”

English: And the priest answered David, and said, There is no common bread under mine hand, but there is hallowed bread; if the young men have kept themselves at least from women.
Masaai: Newaliki ilo apolosani Daudi ajo, “Maata nanu imukateni e oshi ake tene, kake etii imukateni naasinya, te neitalama ake duoo ninche ilbarnot ate nkituaak.”

English: And David answered the priest, and said unto him, Of a truth women have been kept from us about these three days, since I came out, and the vessels of the young men are holy, and the bread is in a manner common, yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel.
Masaai: Newaliki Daudi ilo apolosani ajo, “Ore te sipata eitalamayioki apa nkituaak te iyiook anaa oshi ake te nalo te nkisiaayiare eisinyat imasaa oo lbarnot, hoo duoo ninye tenaa elototo e oshi ake; kebaa naa taata aa sinyat imasaa enye?”

English: So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the LORD, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
Masaai: Neaku eishoo olapolosani ninye emukate nasinya, amu metii apa emukate ine meteleku ake ina mukate enkitoduaaroto, naa ninche eiwuang'ieki aaitung'uaa dukuya o Laitoriani, pee eitapaashikini imukateni naairowua ina olong naawaki.

English: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
Masaai: Netii apa oltung'ani oje loo sinkan le Saul ine ina olong, oikenoyioki te dukuya o Laitoriani; ore apa enkarna enye naa Doeg le Edom, olkitok loo lchekuti le Saul.

English: And David said unto Ahimelech, And is there not here under thine hand spear or sword? for I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business required haste.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Ahimelek, “Amaa aimiaata iyie empere arashu olalem tene? Amu eitu duoo ayau olalem lai arashu empere ai te nebo nanu, enkaraki naa ore enkisiaayiare o laiguanani neyieu enkisarrisar.”

English: And the priest said, The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest in the valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod: if thou wilt take that, take it: for there is no other save that here. And David said, There is none like that; give it me.
Masaai: Nejo olapolosani, “Ore olalem le Goliat ilo Filisti litara apa to oerata le Ela, ng'ura, etii ene eirina te nkarasha ti oriong enkila dorrop; tenaa iya ilo, iwa, amu metii likae kake ele ake.” Nejo Daudi, “Meetae likae laaijo ilo; nchooki nanu.”

English: And David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
Masaai: Nedumunye Daudi neisik ina olong ailany Saul, nelo enetii Akish olaiguanani le Gas.

English: And the servants of Achish said unto him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
Masaai: Nejoki ninye isinkan le Akish, “Aime Daudi ele olaiguanani le nkop? Keitu ninche eranyakino maate ti alo ninye too sinkolioitin ejo: ‘Etasesekuana Saul nkalifuni enyena, Ore Daudi naa nkalifuni tomon enyena?’ ”

English: And David laid up these words in his heart, and was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
Masaai: Neya Daudi kulo rorei to ltau, neureyu oleng Akish ilo aiguanani le Gas.

English: And he changed his behaviour before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down upon his beard.
Masaai: Neaku eibelekenya ninye olkuaak lenye te dukuya ninche, neitaakuno koltung'ani omoda, too nkaik enyena, nekord mbaoi oo milankoni e kishomi, neisho nkamulak edou aapuo olmunyei lenye.

English: Then said Achish unto his servants, Lo, ye see the man is mad: wherefore then have ye brought him to me?
Masaai: Nejoki Akish isinkan lenyena, “Eng'ura aajo kemoda ele tung'ani; kainyoo naa pee iyautua intae enatii?

English: Have I need of mad men, that ye have brought this fellow to play the mad man in my presence? shall this fellow come into my house?
Masaai: Ai maata nanu iltung'ana oomoda, pee iyautua ele tung'ani metaasa emodaisho te dukuya nanu? Kelotu ele tung'ani atua enkaji ai?”

English: David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave Adullam: and when his brethren and all his father's house heard it, they went down thither to him.
Masaai: Nedumunye Daudi te ine neisik alo enkapune e Adulam; ore ake pee ening ilalashera lenyena o enkaji e papaai lenye pooki, nedoyio aapuo enetii ninye.

English: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae oata osina, o pooki ng'ae oata esile, o pooki ng'ae leton emonira neiturrurrukino ninye, neaku ninye olarikoni lenye. Netii apa te nebo ninye iltung'ana oobaya iip ong'uan.

English: And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said unto the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come forth, and be with you, till I know what God will do for me.
Masaai: Nelo Daudi teine Mispe e Moab; nejoki ninye olaiguanani le Moab, “Aatoomono nchoo sii ake papaai o yieyio etoni te nebo iyie, o metaba anaa nayiolou enaas Enkai te nanu.”

English: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the hold.
Masaai: Neing'uaa ninye ninche te nebo olaiguanani le Moab, netoni ninche te nebo ninye ina kata pooki etii Daudi enkapune.

English: And the prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the hold; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth.
Masaai: Nejoki oloiboni le Nkai Daudi, “Mintoki aton to lnukata, shomo enkop e Yuda.” Neaku etudumunye Daudi nelo atua entim e Heres.

English: When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul abode in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;)
Masaai: Nening apa Saul nchere enotoki Daudi, o lelo tung'ana apa ootii te nebo ninye. Netonita apa Saul te Gibea ti abori olchani oji olkuaju te wueji neika, eeta empere enye te nkaina enye neitashe isinkan lenyena pooki aaman ninye.

English: Then Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, ye Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;
Masaai: Nejoki Saul lelo sinkan lenyena oomanita ninye, “Entoning taata, intae ile Benchamen; amaa keisho ole Yese pooki ng'ae te intae inkurman o nkurman oo sabibu, keitaa ninye intae pooki ilkituaak loo nkalifuni o ilkituaak le maaip,

English: That all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that sheweth me that my son hath made a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or sheweth unto me that my son hath stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Masaai: pee kitarresho intae pooki nanu? Meetae hoo obo laaliki nanu enkata naibung'are olayioni lai olayioni le Yese, meetae obo te intae laaing'urrie nanu arashu aaliki nanu nchere eisisa olayioni lai osinka lai maataara nanu, maatarresho, anaa enatiu ena olong.”

English: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
Masaai: Newal Doeg le Edom, apa oitasho te mbata oo sinkan le Saul ejo, “Ataduaa nanu olayioni le Yese elotu Nob, enetii Ahimelek, olayioni le Ahitab,

English: And he enquired of the LORD for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
Masaai: neikilikuanishore ninye Olaitoriani te nkaraki ninye, neisho ninye ndaiki, neisho ninye olalem le Goliat ilo Filisti.”

English: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father's house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani airriwaa olkilikuai aipotu Ahimelek olapolosani, olayioni le Ahitab, o enkaji e papaai lenye pooki, lelo apolosak apa ootii Nob; nepuonu ninche pooki enetii olaiguanani.

English: And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.
Masaai: Nejo Saul, “Toning'o taata, olayioni le Ahitab.” Newalu ninye, “Nele nanu, olkitok lai.”

English: And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Masaai: Nejoki Saul ninye, “Kainyoo pee kitarresho nanu, iyie o layioni le Yese, te ina ninchoo ninye imukateni o olalem, ninkilikuanishore Enkai te nkaraki ninye, neaku aatudumakine ninye nanu naairrag arresh, anaa enatiu ena olong?”

English: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king's son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?
Masaai: Newaliki Ahimelek olaiguanani ajo, “Naa kaing'ae ti atua isinkan linono pooki oisiligayu oleng alang Daudi, kaing'ae olaputani lo laiguanani, olkitok oitasheiki lelo likirrip iyie, neyanyiti ti atua enkaji ino?

English: Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
Masaai: Ae taata enkata e dukuya naikilikuanishore nanu Enkai te nkaraki ninye? A-a! Mincho olaiguanani eomonu ae toki to sinka lenye arashu te nkaji pooki e papaai lai; amu eitu eyiolou osinka lino ae toki te kuna pooki, te sapuk arashu te nkiti.”

English: And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father's house.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Esipa, iye ake, Ahimelek, iyie o enkaji e papaai lino.”

English: And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani lelo arripok oomanita ninye, “Embelekenyata entaar ilapolosak lo Laitoriani metuata; amu etii sii enkaina enye te nebo Daudi, neyiolo apa aajo eisika ninye, neitu ninche aaliki nanu.” Kake ore isinkan lo laiguanani nemeidim aatudumu enkaina enye aaiteleiki lelo apolosak lo Laitoriani.

English: And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani ajoki Doeg, “Imbelekenyayu iyie tusulakinoyu ilapolosak.” Neibelekenya Doeg le Edom nedoiki lelo apolosak, near ninye ina olong iltung'ana ntomoni isiet o imiet ooishopito enkila dorrop sidai.

English: And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
Masaai: Ore Nob ina ang oo lapolosak, near ninye to lalem; ilewa o nkituaak, nkera o naanakita, ilmong'i, isirkon o nkerra, near to lalem.

English: And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
Masaai: Kake ore obo loo layiok le Ahimelek ole Ahitab, oji Abiata, neisudori neisik asujaa Daudi.

English: And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the LORD'S priests.
Masaai: Neliki Abiata Daudi nchere etaara Saul ilapolosak lo Laitoriani metuata.

English: And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father's house.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Abiata, “Atayiolo apa te ina olong, etii Doeg ilo Edometi ine, inchere esipa keliki ninye Saul. Ayaua nanu ina keeya oo ltung'ana pooki le nkaji e papaai lino.

English: Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.
Masaai: Totona te nebo nanu, miureisho; amu ore ilo oing'oru enkishui ai neing'oru enkishui ino; ore te nebo nanu niton te wueji neserian.”

English: Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines fight against Keilah, and they rob the threshingfloors.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche Daudi, “Ng'ura, earita Ilfilisti Keila nepurrito nenen neeitobirieki enkurma.”

English: Therefore David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And the LORD said unto David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.
Masaai: Neaku eikilikuanishore Daudi Olaitoriani, “Kalo nanu aar kulo Filisti?” Nejoki Olaitoriani Daudi, “Shomo taara pee intajeu Keila.”

English: And David's men said unto him, Behold, we be afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
Masaai: Kake etiaakitia iltung'ana le Daudi ninye, “Ng'ura, eikiureisho iyiook tene te Yuda; kebaa naa naaji ti nikipuo Keila aarare injorin oo Lfilisti?”

English: Then David enquired of the LORD yet again. And the LORD answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand.
Masaai: Neitoki ake Daudi aikilikuanishore Olaitoriani. Newaliki Olaitoriani ninye ajo, “Tudumunye, tadoi shomo Keila; amu kaishoru nanu Ilfilisti apik atua nkaik inono.”

English: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
Masaai: Nelo Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena Keila, nearare Ilfilisti, neyau nchoo enye, near iltung'ana kumok metuata tiatua ninche. Neaku etokordua Daudi lelo oomanya Keila.

English: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.
Masaai: Ore apa pee eisik Abiata olayioni le Ahimelek alo enetii Daudi te Keila, nedou ninye alotu eeta enkila dorrop te nkaina enye.

English: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, God hath delivered him into mine hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a town that hath gates and bars.
Masaai: Netiaakaki apa Saul nchere eewuo Daudi Keila. Nejo Saul, “Eishorua Enkai ninye apik atua nkaik aainei amu eikenoyie ninye kewan ajing enkanasa naata nchomito oo sekenke.”

English: And Saul called all the people together to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
Masaai: Neipotu Saul iltung'ana pooki meetu olarrabal, metadoi aapuo Keila, pee eng'adu Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena.

English: And David knew that Saul secretly practised mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring hither the ephod.
Masaai: Neyiolou Daudi ajo eitobirita Saul entorroni te nkaraki ninye; nejoki ninye Abiata ilo apolosani, “Iyau ina kila dorrop ene.”

English: Then said David, O LORD God of Israel, thy servant hath certainly heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Olaitoriani, Enkai e Israel, etoning'o osinka lino asipu nchere keing'oru Saul pee elotu Keila pee eidaikie enkang te nkaraki nanu.

English: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? O LORD God of Israel, I beseech thee, tell thy servant. And the LORD said, He will come down.
Masaai: Amaa, kaaishooyo nanu iltung'ana le Keila aapik atua enkaina enye? Kedou Saul alotu, anaa enatoning'o osinka lino? Olaitoriani, Enkai e Israel, aatasayia iyie, toliki osinka lino.” Nejo Olaitoriani, “Kedou ninye alotu.”

English: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And the LORD said, They will deliver thee up.
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi ajo, “Amaa, kaishooyo nanu iltung'ana le Keila iltung'ana laainei aapik atua enkaina e Saul?” Nejo Olaitoriani, “Eikinchooyo ninche.”

English: Then David and his men, which were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.
Masaai: Nedumunye Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena, oobaya iip ile neing'uaa Keila, nepuo ninche eneba anaa eneidim aashom. Ore ake pee elikini Saul nchere eisika Daudi nepal elototo.

English: And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.
Masaai: Neton Daudi ti atua ilnukat ti ong'ota, te ina kop oo ldoinyo lo lpurkel le Sif. Neing'oru Saul ninye nkolong'i pooki, kake eitu epik ninye Enkai atua enkaina enye.

English: And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.
Masaai: Neiruto apa Daudi enkaraki naipang'u Saul alo aing'oru enkishui enye. Netii apa Daudi ong'ata e Sif te Horesh.

English: And Jonathan Saul's son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.
Masaai: Nedumunye Yonatan, olayioni le Saul, nelo enetii Daudi te Horesh, neitagol enkaina enye te Nkai.

English: And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Miureisho amu ore enkaina e Saul, papaai lai, mikitum iyie; iaku iyie olaiguanani te Israel, naaku nanu oliare te iyie; eyiolo sii Saul papaai lai ena.”

English: And they two made a covenant before the LORD: and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.
Masaai: Nenya pokira oare olmumai lo sotua te dukuya Olaitoriani; neton Daudi te Horesh, nelo Yonatan ang.

English: Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
Masaai: Nepuo Ilsifi enetii Saul te Gibea, ejo, “Aimeisudori Daudi ti atua iyiook too lnukat te Horesh, ldoinyo le Hakila, le kopikop e Yesimon?

English: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand.
Masaai: Tadou naa wou, olaiguanani, te risioroto e yieunoto o ltau lino pooki pee idou alotu; ore erishata ang naa pee kinchoru ninye aapik atua enkaina o laiguanani.”

English: And Saul said, Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me.
Masaai: Nejo Saul, “Metamayiana intae Olaitoriani; amu inotito intae olng'ur te nanu.

English: Go, I pray you, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who hath seen him there: for it is told me that he dealeth very subtilly.
Masaai: Enchom, enyaaki entisipa oleng; entayiolo nidolidolo eneisudoriyie, naa kaing'ae otodua ninye te ine; amu aatiaakaki nchere eikalamas ninye oleng.

English: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hideth himself, and come ye again to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah.
Masaai: Entodol naa, nijurrurru iwuejitin oshi neeisudoriyie, o neerreshishore, nishukunyenye enatii iatata olomoni osipa, pee alo nanu te nebo intae; naa te netii ninye ina kop, naing'oru nanu ninye ti atua nkalifuni pooki e Yuda.”

English: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.
Masaai: Nedumunye ninche, nepuo Sif aaituruk te Saul. Netii apa Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena ong'ata e Maon, ti atua Araba te nkalo e kopikop e Yesimon.

English: Saul also and his men went to seek him. And they told David: wherefore he came down into a rock, and abode in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.
Masaai: Nelo Saul o ltung'ana lenyena aaing'oru ninye. Nelikini Daudi; neaku etadoyie alo endapidapoi natii ong'ata e Moan. Ore ake pee ening Saul ina, nesujaa Daudi ti ong'ata e Moan.

English: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.
Masaai: Nelo Saul enchoto nabo o ldoinyo, nelo Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena te nkai shoto o ldoinyo, neisarisarita apa Daudi pee eilany Saul, ore etinyikutua Saul o ltung'ana lenyena aapunyaki Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena pee eibung ninche,

English: But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come; for the Philistines have invaded the land.
Masaai: nelotu olkipaaret enetii Saul, ejo, “Isarisaru wou; amu etaara Ilfilisti enkop.”

English: Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Selahammahlekoth.
Masaai: Neaku etushuke Saul eitu eitoki asujaa Daudi, nelo aarare Ilfilisti; neaku etejoki apa ine wueji Endapidapoi e nkisikata.

English: And David went up from thence, and dwelt in strong holds at Engedi.
Masaai: Neilep Daudi alo te ine, nebik too lnukat le En-gedi.

English: And it came to pass, when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi.
Masaai: Ore pee eshukunye Saul eing'uaa esujata oo Lfilisti, nejokini, “Ng'ura, etii Daudi ong'ata e En-gedi.”

English: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.
Masaai: Neya Saul iltung'ana nkalifuni uni oogeluno ti atua Israel pooki, nepuo aaing'oru Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena te dukuya ndapidapo oo nkineji oo soito.

English: And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.
Masaai: Nelotu ninye imuatat oo nkerra e mbata e nkoitoi, ine apa netii enkapune, nelo Saul atua pee eyeng'iyeng'ie kewan. Ore apa Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena netonita teneiting'ie enkapune ti atua.

English: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily.
Masaai: Nejoki iltung'ana le Daudi ninye, “Nena enkolong naa ninye kitiaaka iyie Olaitoriani, ‘Ng'ura, kapik nanu olmang'atinta lino atua enkaina ino, naa intaas ninye anaa enidol aa sidai.’ ” Neinyototo Daudi neiseleejari alo adung'oo olcholoi lo lkila le Saul.

English: And it came to pass afterward, that David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's skirt.
Masaai: Ore te siadi neitanyamal Daudi oltau lenye, enkaraki natudung'oyie ninye olcholoi lo lkila le Saul.

English: And he said unto his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD'S anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the LORD.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye iltung'ana lenyena, “Maatomitiki nanu Olaitoriani pee maitaas nanu ena olkitok lai, ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aput aitorioo enkaina ai agilunore ninye adolita ajo olotuputo Olaitoriani ninye.”

English: So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
Masaai: Neaku eilejileja Daudi iltung'ana lenyena te kulo rorei, neitu eisho ninche metarasaki Saul. Nedumunye Saul neing'uaa enkapune, nelo te nkoitoi enye.

English: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.
Masaai: Ore te siadi nedumunye sii ninye Daudi, neipang'u ti atua enkapune, neipotu Saul, “Olkitok lai, olaiguanani!” Ore ake pee enang Saul silig, neirrugo Daudi o metabaiki enkop te nkomom enye, neserem ninye.

English: And David said to Saul, Wherefore hearest thou men's words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Saul, “Kainyoo iyie pee ining irorei loo ltung'ana oojo, ‘Ng'ura, eing'oru Daudi enkitamioto ino?’

English: Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that the LORD had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee: but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the LORD'S anointed.
Masaai: Dol, ore ena olong etoduaa nkonyek inono aajo kitipika taata iyie Olaitoriani atua enkaina ai ti atua enkapune; naajoki nanu ilkulikae maataara iyie tua, kake aatapala nanu. Najo, ‘Maitorioo enkaina ai aar olkitok lai; amu olotubukokoki eilata aaput lo Laitoriani ninye!’

English: Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it.
Masaai: Toduaa, papaai lai, toduaa ajo etii olcholoi lo lkila lino enkaina ai; amu ore te sipata nchere atudung'oyie olcholoi lo lkila lino, neitu aar iyie tua, indim atayiolo nidol nchere metii entorroni e nkibelekenyata arashu enkitoria atua nkaik aainei. Eitu aas eng'oki ti alo iyie, hoo nirresh enkishui ai pee intayu.

English: The LORD judge between me and thee, and the LORD avenge me of thee: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.
Masaai: Metaa Olaitoriani orish erishata ai o iyie, maaitalaa nanu Olaitoriani te iyie; kake mikiarare iyie enkaina ai.

English: As saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.
Masaai: Anaa enajo endung'et e rashe e apa moitie, ‘Atua ilo torrono epukunye entorroni.’ Kake mikiarare iyie enkaina ai.

English: After whom is the king of Israel come out? after whom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.
Masaai: Kaing'ae eipang'u olaiguanani le Israel asujaa? Kaing'ae isujita iyie? Koldia otua isujita iyie! Kolpidilai isujita!

English: The LORD therefore be judge, and judge between me and thee, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thine hand.
Masaai: Metaa naa Olaitoriani orish nedung'oki enkiguana te rishata ai o iyie, neingor ninye, naamitu nanu, naakordu nanu te nkaina ino.”

English: And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eidip Daudi airorie kulo rorei Saul, nejo Saul, “Koltoilo lino ele, enkerai ai Daudi?” Neyietu Saul aishir.

English: And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye Daudi, “Iyie asipani alang nanu, amu kitalaaka nanu esidai aa entorroni nanu aatalaaka.

English: And thou hast shewed this day how that thou hast dealt well with me: forasmuch as when the LORD had delivered me into thine hand, thou killedst me not.
Masaai: Nimbalunye iyie ena olong ina nikintaasa nanu esidai, te ina neitu kiar matua ina kata pee aapik nanu Olaitoriani atua nkaik inono.

English: For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away? wherefore the LORD reward thee good for that thou hast done unto me this day.
Masaai: Amu amaa te netum oltung'ani olmang'atinta lenye, keisho ninye meshomo ninye eserian? Neaku mikitalaaki Olaitoriani te sidai te ina nikintaasa iyie nanu ena olong.

English: And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.
Masaai: Ore taata, ng'ura, ayiolo nanu ajo esipa iaku iyie olaiguanani, neitubulari enkitoria e Israel te nkaina ino.

English: Swear now therefore unto me by the LORD, that thou wilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou wilt not destroy my name out of my father's house.
Masaai: Inosieki olmumai to Laitoriani nchere midung'oo iyie eishoi ai te siadi nanu, o nchere mindaikie iyie enkarna ai aitayu te nkaji e papaai lai.”

English: And David sware unto Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men gat them up unto the hold.
Masaai: Nenya Daudi ele mumai te nkaraki Saul. Nelo Saul ang; kake eshomo Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena atua olnukata.

English: And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
Masaai: Neye apa Samuel, neiturrurro Israel pooki aaishiraki ninye, nenukaa ninche ninye te nkaji enye te Rama. Nedumunye Daudi nedoyio alo ong'ata e Paran.

English: And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
Masaai: Netii apa oltung'ani otii Maon, otii esiaai enye Karmel. Eikarsis apa ilo tung'ani oleng; eeta apa ninye nkerra nkalifuni uni o nkineji enkalifu nabo. Nebarnu apa ninye ilpapit loo nkerra enyena te Karmel.

English: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
Masaai: Ore apa enkarna e ilo tung'ani naa Nabal, ore enkarna e nkitok enye naa Abigail. Naa ng'en apa ina kitok neikishiaan kake kemoda apa olee naa torrono olkuaak; naa ole ntipat e Kaleb apa.

English: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal did shear his sheep.
Masaai: Nening Daudi ti ong'ata nchere ebarnita Nabal nkerra enyena.

English: And David sent out ten young men, and David said unto the young men, Get you up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:
Masaai: Neaku eirriwayie Daudi ilbarnot tomon; nejoki Daudi lelo barnot, “Elepa enchom Karmel, nipuopuo enetii Nabal, nirorokiki ninye te nkarna ai.

English: And thus shall ye say to him that liveth in prosperity, Peace be both to thee, and peace be to thine house, and peace be unto all that thou hast.
Masaai: Naa nji enkuna te nirorokiki ninye: ‘Metaa enino eseriani, metaa eseriani ene nkaji ino, metaa eseriani ene lelo pooki liata iyie.

English: And now I have heard that thou hast shearers: now thy shepherds which were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there ought missing unto them, all the while they were in Carmel.
Masaai: Aning nanu nchere iata iyie ilabarnok; etii oshi ilchekuti linono te nebo iyiook, neitu iyiook kintaas ninche entorrono, neitu ninche elau toki, ina kata pooki etii Karmel.

English: Ask thy young men, and they will shew thee. Wherefore let the young men find favour in thine eyes: for we come in a good day: give, I pray thee, whatsoever cometh to thine hand unto thy servants, and to thy son David.
Masaai: Nkilikuana ilbarnot linono, amu eikiliki ninche. Metaa nchoo ilbarnot laainei etum omom too nkonyek inono; amu kipuonu iyiook te nkolong o sirua. Kitoomono iyie, nchoo pooki toki niaata isinkan linono o olayioni lino Daudi.’ ”

English: And when David's young men came, they spake to Nabal according to all those words in the name of David, and ceased.
Masaai: Ore ake pee epuonu ilbarnot le Daudi, nejoki ninche nena pooki Nabal te nkarna e Daudi; netoni aanyisho.

English: And Nabal answered David's servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master.
Masaai: Newaliki Nabal isinkan le Daudi nejo, “Kaing'ae Daudi? Kaing'ae olayioni le Yese? Etii oshi taata kuna olong'i isinkan kumok oopuo aaing'uaa ilkituaak lenye.

English: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men, whom I know not whence they be?
Masaai: Kaitayu nanu endaa ai o enkare ai o enkiring'o ai nateyieng'uo te nkaraki ilabarnok laainei, aisho iltung'ana ooing'uaa ewueji nemayiolo nanu ajo kaji eing'uaa?”

English: So David's young men turned their way, and went again, and came and told him all those sayings.
Masaai: Neaku eibelekenyate lelo barnot le Daudi aapuo, neshuko neliki ninye ina.

English: And David said unto his men, Gird ye on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the stuff.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi iltung'ana lenyena, “Teena pooki ng'ae olalem lenye!” Ore pooki ng'ae te ninche neen olalem lenye; neen sii ninye Daudi olalem lenye; nepuo iltung'ana oobaya iip ong'uan aasujaa Daudi, netoni iltung'ana iip are aarrip ilolan.

English: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.
Masaai: Kake etiaaka obo loo lbarnot Abigail, enkitok e Nabal, “Ng'ura, Eirriwua Daudi ilkiliku ooing'uaa ong'ata meetu aairoroki olkitok lang, kake etamoro ninche.

English: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:
Masaai: Ore eyia, eisupati apa lelo tung'ana te iyiook, neitu iyiook kitum entorroni, neitu iyiook kilau toki apa kitii ong'ota, te nkata naba anaa enikishomo te nebo ninche;

English: They were a wall unto us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
Masaai: esuntai apa ninche te iyiook te nkewarie o te ndama, te ina kata pooki apa nikitii iyiook te nebo ninche king'orita nkerra.

English: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a son of Belial, that a man cannot speak to him.
Masaai: Ore naa taata tayiolo ena nidamu eniaas; amu eitobirakitia olkitok lang entorroni o enkaji enye pooki, naa kegogong ninye oleng meetae oltung'ani oidim airorie ninye.”

English: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
Masaai: Kaae neisarrisar Abigail, neya imukateni iip are, o lbenia oare loo lonito le naisho oo sabibu o nkerra imiet naayieng'a, o ntemat imiet enkurma napejo o rridat iip loo sabibu, o mukateni iip are oo lng'abolo, neirragie ninche te nchumata oo sirkon.

English: And she said unto her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye lelo barnot lenye, “Enchom enturuko te dukuya nanu; ng'ura, kalotu nanu asuju intae.” Kake eitu ninye eliki olpayian lenye Nabal.

English: And it was so, as she rode on the ass, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down against her; and she met them.
Masaai: Ore eloito ninye ekedito osikiria nedou alotu abori olmelil lo ldoinyo, ng'ura, nelotu Daudi, o ltung'ana lenyena aadou aanang'are ninye; nenang'are ninye ninche.

English: Now David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow hath in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained unto him: and he hath requited me evil for good.
Masaai: Netejo apa Daudi, “Esipa pesho apa nanu atorripo nena pooki naata ele tung'ani ti ong'ata neaku meetae entoki natalaki te nena pooki naara nkunenyena; naatushukoko ninye nanu entorroni te sidano.

English: So and more also do God unto the enemies of David, if I leave of all that pertain to him by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.
Masaai: Metaasa Enkai ena te Daudi, neitulusoo sii, te natung'uayie nanu tadekenya obo lee le lelo pooki oora ilenyena.”

English: And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Abigail Daudi, neisarrisar ninye, nedou to sikiria, nebatata ninye te dukuya Daudi te nkomom enye, neirrugo abaiki enkop.

English: And fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: and let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine audience, and hear the words of thine handmaid.
Masaai: Nebatata ninye too nkejek enyena nejo, “Shumata nanu ake, olkitok lai, nchoo elotu entorroni; aatoomono nchoo esinka ino eiro too nkiyiaa inono, nining irorei le sinka ino.

English: Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thine handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.
Masaai: Mincho olkitok lai eshilaa ele tung'ani le ntorroni, Nabal; amu ore anaa enatiu enkarna enye, neijia etiu ninye, Nabal enkarna enye, netii emodai te nebo ninye; kake ore nanu esinka ino eitu adol lelo barnot lo lkitok lai, laa ninche iyie irriwua,

English: Now therefore, my lord, as the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing the LORD hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
Masaai: ore naa taata, olkitok lai, anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, o anaa enaishu oltau lino, idolita ajo kimbooyie iyie Olaitoriani aitung'uaa enkibukoroto o sarge, o enkitalakunoto e lap te nkaina ino makewan, ore naa taata nchoo ilmang'ati linono o lelo ooing'oru aaitaas entorroni olkitok lai etiu anaa Nabal.

English: And now this blessing which thine handmaid hath brought unto my lord, let it even be given unto the young men that follow my lord.
Masaai: Ore taata ena kishoroto naa ninye eyaka esinka ino olkitok lai inchoo meishori lelo barnot oosuj olkitok lai.

English: I pray thee, forgive the trespass of thine handmaid: for the LORD will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of the LORD, and evil hath not been found in thee all thy days.
Masaai: Aatoomono tapalakaki engolong'akinoto e sinka ino; amu esipa keitaa Olaitoriani olkitok lai enkaji nauno, amu ilarrabali lo Laitoriani etii olkitok lai; nemetumi entorroni te iyie anaa ninchu.

English: Yet a man is risen to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul: but the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the LORD thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as out of the middle of a sling.
Masaai: Te nedumunye iltung'ana pee kisujaa iyie pee eing'oru enkishui ino, ore enkishui o lkitok lai naa keenari to rridata loo looishu te nking'urata o Laitoriani Enkai ino; ore enkishui oo lmang'ati linono nenang'aa ninye anaa osoit onang'ari te nkopito.

English: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel;
Masaai: Ore ake pee eidip Olaitoriani aitaasa olkitok lai te risioroto e nena pooki sidain naairoro ninye ti alo iyie, nikitegelua ninye taa olkitok te shumata Israel,

English: That this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood causeless, or that my lord hath avenged himself: but when the LORD shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thine handmaid.
Masaai: metum olkitok lai enaitagor arashu enyamali o ltau, te nkibukoroto o sarge metii emporeet, arashu to lkitok lai eitalaku elap makewan. Ore ake pee kindip Olaitoriani aitaasa olkitok lai esidai, nidamu naa esinka ino.”

English: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me:
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Abigail, “Meisisi Olaitoriani, Enkai e Israel, laa ninye nikirriua iyie ena olong pee kinang'are nanu!

English: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.
Masaai: Metamayiani eng'eno ino, naa mikitamayiani iyie, aa iyie nikimbooyie nanu ena olong te nkibukoroto o sarge o te nkitalakunoto elap te nkaina ai makewan!

English: For in very deed, as the LORD God of Israel liveth, which hath kept me back from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.
Masaai: Amu ore te sipata anaa enaishu Olaitoriani Enkai e Israel, laa ninye laaibooyie nanu eitu aaitame iyie, te neme eisarisarua iyie nikilotu anang'are nanu, esipa ore tadekenya anaata eitu ninye elekakini Nabal hoo ninye olee obo.”

English: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.
Masaai: Neng'amu Daudi too nkaik eina kitok ina nayaka ninye ninye; nejoki ninye, “Ilepa shomo te seriani enkaji ino; ing'ura, atoning'o nanu oltoilo lino, naishorua nanu ina omonunoto ino.”

English: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
Masaai: Nelotu Abigail enetii Nabal; naa, ng'ura eeta apa ninye osirua ti atua enkaji enye, anaa osirua lo laiguanani. Neng'ida apa oltau le Nabal ti atua ninye, amu etemere apa oleng; neaku eitu eliki ninye toki tukul o metaba anaa nekenyu awang'u.

English: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
Masaai: Ore te nkakenya eishunye emerai te Nabal, neliki ninye enkitok enye kuna baa, neye oltau lenye ti atua ninye, netiu ninye anaa osoit.

English: And it came to pass about ten days after, that the LORD smote Nabal, that he died.
Masaai: Ore too nkolong'i naabaya tomon te siadi neosh Olaitoriani Nabal; neye ninye.

English: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the LORD, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the LORD hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Daudi nchere etua Nabal, nejo ninye, “Metamayiani Olaitoriani laa ninye oitalakua ina moroto apa natang'amua nanu te nkaina e Nabal, neibooyie ninye osinka lenye aitung'uaa entorroni; etushukoko Olaitoriani ina kiaas torrono enchumata endukuya enye makewan.” Neirriwaa Daudi iltung'ana pee esir Abigail aitaa ninye enkitok enye.

English: And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to Carmel, they spake unto her, saying, David sent us unto thee, to take thee to him to wife.
Masaai: Ore ake pee epuonu isinkan le Daudi enetii Abigail te Karmel, nejoki ninche ninye, “Eirriua Daudi iyiook enitii pee kintaa iyie te ninye anaa enkitok enye.”

English: And she arose, and bowed herself on her face to the earth, and said, Behold, let thine handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
Masaai: Nedumunye ninye neirrugo te nkomom enye o metabaiki enkop, nejo, “Ng'ura, ore esinka ino naa enkaisaayiani naituku nkejek oo sinkan lo lkitok lai.”

English: And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
Masaai: Neisarrisar Abigail, nedumunye neked osikiria, neisiaai ninye nkaisiaayiak enyena imiet; nesujaa ninye lelo kiliku le Daudi, neaku enkitok enye.

English: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives.
Masaai: Neitoki sii Daudi aya Ahinoam e Yesreel; neaku ninche pokira are nkituaak enyena.

English: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.
Masaai: Neishoo apa Saul Mikal, entito enye, ina kitok e Daudi, Palti olayioni le Laish, laa olayioni le Galim apa ninye.

English: And the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?
Masaai: Nepuonu Ilsifi enetii Saul te Gibea, nejo, “Aimeisudori Daudi to ldoinyo le Hikila, otii enkalo o loo saen le Yeshimon?”

English: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
Masaai: Neaku etudumunye Saul nedoyio alo ong'ata e Sif, te nebo iltung'ana nkalifuni uni oogeluno le Israel, pee eing'oru Daudi ti ong'ata e Sif.

English: And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
Masaai: Neitayu Saul olg'obor to ldoinyo le Hikila, otii embata enkoitoi nalala te nkalo o loo saen le Yesimon. Kake etotona Daudi to lpurkel; ore ake pee edol ajo eewuo Saul asuju ninye atua olpurkel,

English: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.
Masaai: neirriwaa Daudi ilaikitalak, pee eyiolou aasipu nchere eewuo Saul.

English: And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.
Masaai: Nedumunye Daudi nelotu ine wueji apa netipika Saul olg'obor, nedol Daudi ine wueji neirragie Saul, te nebo Abna olayioni le Ner, olkitok le njore enye; neirragita apa Saul ti atua olng'obor nemanita enjore pooki ninye.

English: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with thee.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Ahimelek ilo Hitati; o lalashe le Yoab Abishai olayioni le Seruiya, “Kaing'ae odoyio alo te nebo nanu atua olng'obor enetii Saul?” Nejo Abishai, “Kadoyio nanu alo te nebo iyie.”

English: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo Daudi o Abishai enetii ina jore kewarie; neirragita Saul te ine airura ti atua olng'obor, neunokino empere enye enkop te mbata e ndukuya enye; ore Abna o enjore neirrag aaman ninye.

English: Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.
Masaai: Nejoki Abishai Daudi, “Eishorua Enkai olmang'atinta lino apik atua enkaina ino ena olong; ore naa nchooki nanu matupudaki ninye enkop te remoto nabo e mpere, nemaitoki nanu arem ninye kat are.”

English: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD'S anointed, and be guiltless?
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Daudi Abishai, “Minyal ninye, amu kaing'ae oidim aitorioi enkaina enye metaarare ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aaput, neaku meeta entioto?”

English: David said furthermore, As the LORD liveth, the LORD shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, kear Olaitoriani ninye; arashu elotu enkolong enye pee eye; arashu elo ninye atua olarrabal neari metua.

English: The LORD forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the LORD'S anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
Masaai: Metomito Olaitoriani nchere kadumu nanu enkaina ai aar ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aput; kake iwa taata ina pere natii embata endukuya enye, o ina moti e nkare, pee kipuo iyiook.”

English: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.
Masaai: Neaku ewa Daudi empere o emoti e nkare aitung'uaa endukuya e Saul, nepuo ninche. Metii oltung'ani otoduaa ina, arashu otayiolo ina, arashu einyo hoo likae; amu keirura apa pooki, te nkaraki eetuo njo naairoishi naaing'uaa Olaitoriani shumata ninche.

English: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space being between them:
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi alang alo lido kekun, neitashe te nelakua te nchumata o ldoinyo, etii erishata sapuk erishata enye.

English: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest thou not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who art thou that criest to the king?
Masaai: Neipot ina jore, o Abna olayioni le Ner, ejo, “Aimiwal iyie, Abna?” Newal Abna, “Ira ng'ae ilo oipot olaiguanani?”

English: And David said to Abner, Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Abna, “Aimira iyie olee? Kaing'ae likinyaanyukie iyie ti atua Israel? Kainyoo naa pee eitu iyie irrip olkitok lino olaiguanani? Amu eewuo obo loo ltung'ana atua pee eidaikie olaiguanani olkitok lino.

English: This thing is not good that thou hast done. As the LORD liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the LORD'S anointed. And now see where the king's spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.
Masaai: Ore ena toki nitaasa iyie neme sidai. Anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, kinchiaakinore iyie niye, enkaraki neitu iyie irrip olkitok ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aput. Naa ore taata ing'ura enetii empere o laiguanani, o ina moti e nkare duoo natii embata endukuya enye.”

English: And Saul knew David's voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
Masaai: Neyiolou Saul oltoilo le Daudi, nejo, “Koltoilo lino ele, enkerai ai, Daudi?” Nejo Daudi, “Oltoilo lai, olkitok lai, olaiguanani.”

English: And he said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Kainyoo pee esuj olkitok lai osinka lenye? Amu kainyoo nanu ataasa? Kaa torroni natii nkaik aainei?

English: Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the LORD; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, Go, serve other gods.
Masaai: Ore naa taata nchoo olkitok lai olaiguanani ening irorei lo sinka lenye. Tenaa Olaitoriani likituputuo iyie taaraki nanu, metang'amu ninye olasar; kake tenaa iltung'ana, metaa kediaa ninche te dukuya Olaitoriani, amu aataaraitie ninche aaipang'ie ena olong pee matum nanu eng'arata e njung'ore o Laitoriani, ejo, ‘Shomo isiaayia kulie aitin.’

English: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the LORD: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.
Masaai: Ore naa, mincho osarge lai ebukokino enkop te nelakuaniki ine netii Olaitoriani; amu eipang'ua olaiguanani le Israel alotu aing'oru enkishui ai, anaa oltung'ani orresh enkurle too ldoinyo.”

English: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajo, “Ataasa nanu entorrono; tushukunye, enkerai ai, Daudi, amu maaitoki nanu aitaas iyie entorrono, amu keeta enkishui ai tipat ena olong too nkonyek inono.”

English: And David answered and said, Behold the king's spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi awalu ajo, “Nena empere o laiguanani! Nchoo obo loo lbarnot elang'u alotu aya.

English: The LORD render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the LORD delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the LORD'S anointed.
Masaai: Ekelaaki Olaitoriani pooki tung'ani te supatisho enye o te nkisiligata enye; amu kinchorua iyie Olaitoriani apik atua enkaina ai taata, nemadumu nanu enkaina ai aarare ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata aaput.

English: And, behold, as thy life was much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the LORD, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
Masaai: Ng'ura, anaa enaata enkishui ino tipat ena olong too nkonyek aainei, neaku metaa enkishui ai ene tipat too nkonyek o Laitoriani, naa maatokordu ninye aitayu ti atua isinaitin pooki.”

English: Then Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great things, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajoki Daudi, “Mikitamayiani iyie, enkerai ai, Daudi! Ias iyie mbaa kumok naa idupoyu te pooki.” Neaku eshomo Daudi enkoitoi enye neshuko Saul alo ewueji enye.

English: And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel: so shall I escape out of his hand.
Masaai: Nejo Daudi to ltau lenye, “Kaye nanu nabo olong te nkaina e Saul; metii entoki sidai te nanu alang te naisikaki enkop oo Lfilisti; pee etum Saul atapalari aaing'oru nanu too lpolosien le Israel, naluaya nanu apuku te nkaina enye.”

English: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
Masaai: Neaku etudumunye Daudi nelang alo, ninye o lelo tung'ana iip ile apa ootii te nebo ninye, aapuo enetii Akish olayioni le Moak, olaiguanani le Gas.

English: And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, even David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife.
Masaai: Nebik Daudi te nebo Akish te Gas, ninye o ltung'ana lenyena, pooki tung'ani te nebo enkaji enye o Daudi te nebo nkituaak enyena pokira are, Ahinoam e Yesreel, o Abigail e Karmel, enkoliai e Nabal.

English: And it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejokini Saul nchere eshomo Daudi Gas, neitu ninye eitoki aing'oru ninye.

English: And David said unto Achish, If I have now found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee?
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi ajoki Akish, “Tenaa kanoto nanu omom too nkonyek inono, nchoo maaishori nanu ewueji ti atua nabo oo nkang'itie ena kop pee atum nanu atobiko te ine; amu kainyoo pee eton osinka lino te nkanasa e nkitoo te nebo iyie?”

English: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.
Masaai: Neaku eishoo Akish ninye ina olong Siklag; metaa etaa Siklag enoo laiguanak le Yuda o metabaiki ena olong.

English: And the time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.
Masaai: Ore esiana oo nkolong'i naatobiko Daudi te nkop oo Lfilisti naa olari o lapaitin oong'uan.

English: And David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt.
Masaai: Neilep Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena nerasaki Ilgeshuri, Ilgirsi, o Lamaleki; amu kulo apa emanya enkop ti apa, o Shuri, o metabaiki enkop e Misiri.

English: And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.
Masaai: Near Daudi enkop, neitu eing'uaa olee arashu enkitok eishu, kake eewa nkerra, o lmong'i, o isirkon, o intamesin, o nkilani, neshukunye alotu enetii Akish.

English: And Achish said, Whither have ye made a road to day? And David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites.
Masaai: Ore pee eikilikuan Akish ajo, “Kakua duoo taata itaara?” Nejo Daudi, “Ilnegeb le Yuda,” arashu, “Ilnegeb le Ijerame,” arashu, “Kitaarare Ilnegeb le Keni.”

English: And David saved neither man nor woman alive, to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, So did David, and so will be his manner all the while he dwelleth in the country of the Philistines.
Masaai: Neitu eing'uaa Daudi olee arashu enkitok eishu, pee etum ayau olomoni Gas, ejo, “Pee melikioo ake ninche iyiook, nejo, ‘Ena etaasa Daudi.’ ” Ele apa olkuaak lenye ina kata pooki apa ebikito te nkop oo Lfilisti.

English: And Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.
Masaai: Neisilig apa Akish Daudi edamu ajo, “Eibaitie tukul iltung'ana lenyena Israeli; metaa keaku ninye osinka lai anaake.”

English: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said unto David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.
Masaai: Ore apa te nena olong'i neiturrur Ilfilisti njorin enye te nkaraki olarrabal, pee earare Israel. Nejoki Akish Daudi, “Tayiolo nchere ore iyie o ltung'ana linono naa impang'ipang'a aapuo te nebo nanu ti atua enjore.”

English: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of mine head for ever.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Akish, “Sidai oleng, iyiolou iyie enaidim osinka lino ataasa.” Nejoki Akish Daudi, “Sidai oleng, kaaitaa nanu iyie olarriponi lai te nkishui pooki.”

English: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.
Masaai: Netua apa Samuel neidipa Israel pooki aaishiraki ninye nenukaa ninye te Rama, te nkanasa enye kewan. Netaarayie apa Saul lelo aisi le yiolounoto o lasakutok meshomo te ina kop.

English: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.
Masaai: Neiturrurro Ilfilisti nepuonu aaitayu olng'obor te Shunem; neiturrur Saul Israel pooki, neitayu ninche olng'obor te Gilboa.

English: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Saul enjore oo Lfilisti, neureishoyu neikirikira oltau lenye oleng.

English: And when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.
Masaai: Ore pee eikilikuanishore Saul Olaitoriani, neitu ewaliki Olaitoriani ninye, aa te nkidetidet arashu te Urim, arashu too loibonok.

English: Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at Endor.
Masaai: Neitoki Saul ajoki isinkan lenyena, “Eng'urakaki nanu enkitok nadolisho te naibon, pee atum nanu ashomo enetii ninye naikilikuanishore ninye.” Nejoki isinkan lenyena ninye, “Etii enkaisi nadolisho te naibon Endor.”

English: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.
Masaai: Neibelekeny Saul kewan nepika kulikae kilani, nelo, ninye o ltung'ana oare te nebo ninye; nepuonu ninche enetii ina kitok kewarie. Nejo ninye, “Mbonokoki nanu te nkiyang'et, nikilepakinye nanu oltung'ani abo laaipotoki enkarna enye.”

English: And the woman said unto him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
Masaai: Nejoki ina kitok ninye, “Esipa iyiolo ina nataasa Saul, ina naitaasa ninye iloibonok oodolisho, o lasakutok aipang'ie tena kop. Kainyoo naa pee kirragakinye nanu orreshet te nkaraki enkishui ai pee iyau keeya ai?”

English: And Saul sware to her by the LORD, saying, As the LORD liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.
Masaai: Kake einosaka Saul ninye olmumai to Laitoriani ejo, “Anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, melotu enkitamioto shumata iyie tena bae.”

English: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
Masaai: Neitoki ina kitok ajo, “Kaing'ae aayaki ailepakinye?” Nejo ninye, “Iyau ilepakinyeki nanu Samuel.”

English: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol ina kitok Samuel neyietu aishir to ltoilo sapuk; nejoki ina kitok Saul, “Kainyoo iyie pee kiteleja nanu? Ira iyie Saul.”

English: And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Miureshoyu iyie; kainyoo iyie idolita?” Nejoki ina kitok Saul, “Adolita nanu enkai eilepu apuku te nkop.”

English: And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninye, “Kainyoo eliooto enye?” Nejo ninye, “Olpayian moruo oilepu alotu; neirina ninye to lkila.” Neyiolou Saul inchere Samuel ninye, neirrugo ninye te nkomom enye o metabaiki enkop, neserem.

English: And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.
Masaai: Nejoki Samuel Saul, “Kainyoo pee kintanyamal ailepunye nanu?” Newal Saul ajo, “Atii nanu atua osina sapuk, amu aaitirrishakitia nanu Ilfilisti aarare, naaibelekenye Enkai aing'uaa nemeekure aawaliki, aa too loibonok arashu te nkidetidet, neaku aaipoto iyie pee kiliki enaas.”

English: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?
Masaai: Neitoki Samuel ajo, “Kainyoo naa pee kinkilikuan nanu, aa Olaitoriani likimbelekenye aing'uaa neaku ninye olmang'atinta lino?

English: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the LORD hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David:
Masaai: Kintaasa iyie Olaitoriani anaa apa enairoro te nanu; amu etopolosayie Olaitoriani enkitoria aitung'uaa enkaina ino, neisho ilo le latia ino Daudi.

English: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the LORD, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing unto thee this day.
Masaai: Enkaraki neitu iyie ining oltoilo lo Laitoriani, neitu intabaya ina goro enye napi aarare Amalek, neaku kintaasa iyie Olaitoriani ena bae ena olong.

English: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
Masaai: Ore ake sii keishooyo sii Olaitoriani Israel te nebo iyie apik atua enkaina oo Lfilisti; ore taisere iyie o layiok linono niakuku te nebo nanu; naa kelo aishoru Olaitoriani enjore e israel apik atua enkaina oo Lfilisti.”

English: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.
Masaai: Nebatata Saul nabo kata te nkop aitorriori eiputa enkuretisho te nkaraki irorei le Samuel; nemeekure apa etii engolon atua ninye, amu eitu ninye enya toki endama pooki o enkewarie pooki.

English: And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thine handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy words which thou spakest unto me.
Masaai: Nelotu ina kitok enetii Saul, ore ake pee edol ajo eiputukunyo, nejoki ninye, “Ng'ura, kitoning'o iyie esinka ino; aitayio nanu enkishui ai te nkaina ai natoning'o ina nikitiaaka iyie nanu.

English: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thine handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, toning'o sii iyie esinka ino; nchooki nanu mairragie embelati e mukate te dukuya iyie; pee inya, pee itum engolon te nilo te nkoitoi ino.”

English: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.
Masaai: Neany ninye nejo, “Manya nanu endaa.” Kake etasayia isinkan lenyena ninye te nebo ina kitok, nening irorei lenye. Neaku neinyototo ninye te nkop neton te rruat.

English: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:
Masaai: Neeta apa ina kitok olashe opir ti aji, neyieng ninye asioki, neitayu enkurma, neipurjupurj nepeju imukateni neitu eisuijeki,

English: And she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.
Masaai: nepik dukuya Saul o laisiaayiak lenyena; neya. Nedumunye ninche nepuo ina kewarie.

English: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which is in Jezreel.
Masaai: Neiturrurro apa Ilfilisti injoreitin enye pooki te Afek; ore Israeli neitayutuo apa ninche ilng'oborri te mbata e nkong'u natii atua Yesreel.
