English: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
Masaai: Ore ebaiki Beta ometabaiki Berotai, nkanas e Hadadesa, neya olaiguanani Daudi isuyan kumok.

English: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening Toi olaiguanani le Hamat nchere etimira Daudi enjore pooki e Hadadesa,

English: Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
Masaai: neirriwaa Toi olayioni lenye Yoram enetii olaiguanani Daudi, pee eisho ninye enchunet, o pee eisho ninye enchunet enkaraki nataarare Hadadesa nemir ninye; amu kesej apa eeta Hadadesa olarrabal o Toi. Neyau Yoram te nebo ninye ntokitin e nkosholai, o sahabu, o no suyai.

English: Which also king David did dedicate unto the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
Masaai: Ore sii kuna neitisiny olaiguanani Daudi to Laitoriani, te nebo ina osholai o sahabu apa naaitisinya naaing'uaa iloreren pooki apa ootimira ninye,

English: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
Masaai: ebaiki Edom, o Moab, o Ilamoni, o Ilfilisti, o Amaleki, o naaing'uaa iyarunot e Hadadesa olayioni le Rehob, olaiguanani le Soba.

English: And David gat him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, being eighteen thousand men.
Masaai: Neishur enkarna e Daudi. Ore pee eshukunye ninye, nesesekuan Iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon o isiet ti atua Oerata le Munyan.

English: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
Masaai: Nepik ninye iltimito Edom; ore atua Edom pooki nepik iltimito, lelo le Edom pooki isinkan le Daudi. Neishoo Olaitoriani Daudi metimirisho te pooki wueji neba anaa eneshomo.

English: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.
Masaai: Neaku eitoria apa Daudi Israel pooki; neisiaisho Daudi te sipata o te risioroto too ltung'ana lenyena pooki.

English: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
Masaai: Naa Yoab olayioni le Seruiya apa oitore enjore, naa Yehoshafat olayioni le Ahilud apa olaigeroni.

English: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;
Masaai: Naa Sadok apa olayioni le Ahitab o Ahimelek olayioni le Abiata ninche ilapolosak; naa Seraia apa olasirani;

English: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.
Masaai: naa Benaia olayioni le Yehoida apa otii shumata lelo Kereti o lelo le Peleti ore ilayiok le Daudi naa ilapolosak.

English: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan's sake?
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Keton etii oltung'ani obo otelekua te nkaji e Saul, pee atum nanu aitoduaa ninye esupatisho te nkaraki Yonatan?”

English: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
Masaai: Netii apa osinka le nkaji e Saul oji Siba, neipotu ninche ninye enetii Daudi; nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Ira iyie Siba?” Nejo ninye, “Ore osinka lino naa ninye ilo.”

English: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Aimeton etii likae obo le nkaji e Saul, pee atum nanu aitoduaa ninye esupatisho e Nkai?” Nejoki Siba olaiguanani, “Eton etii olayioni le Yonatan; olmaima ninye tarrushi nkejek enyena.”

English: And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Koree ninye?” Nejoki Siba olaiguanani, “Etii atua enkaji e Makir olayioni le Amiel te Lo-debar.”

English: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.
Masaai: Kaae neirriwaa olaiguanani meyauni ninye aaitung'uaa enkaji e Makir ole Amiel, te Lo-debar.

English: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
Masaai: Nelotu Mefiboshet, olayioni le Yonatan ole Saul enetii Daudi, nebatata te nkomom enye neserem. Nejo Daudi, “Mefiboshet!” Newal ninye, “Ng'ura, osinka lino.”

English: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi ninye, “Miureisho; amu kaaitodol nanu esupatisho te nkaraki papaai lino Yonatan, naa kaashukoki iyie enkop pooki e Saul papaai lino; nidaa iyie te mesa ai anaake.”

English: And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
Masaai: Neserem ninye, nejo, “Kainyoo ninye osinka lino, metaa ing'or iyie oldia otua anaa nanu?”

English: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master's son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.
Masaai: Neipotu olaiguanani Siba, ilo sinka le Saul, nejoki ninye, “Ore nena pooki apa naara ine Saul o ne nkaji enye pooki aishoo nanu olayioni lo lkitok lino.

English: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master's son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
Masaai: Ore iyie o layiok linono o sinkan linono niturokiki ninye enkurma niyauu atua nena nintayuyu, pee etum olayioni lo lkitok lino endaa nanya; kake ore Mefiboshet olayioni lo lkitok lino nedaa anaake te mesa ai.” Neeta apa Siba ilayiok tomon o imiet o sinkan tikitam.

English: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.
Masaai: Nejoki Siba olaiguanani, “Ore te risioroto e nena pooki, naaitanap olkitok lai olaiguanani osinka lenye, neaku ina eas osinka lino.” Neaku etadee Mefiboshet te mesa e Daudi, anaa obo loo layiok lo laiguanani.

English: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
Masaai: Neeta apa mefiboshet olayioni oti oji enkarna Mika. Ore pooki ootobiko te nkaji e Siba neaku isinkan le Mefiboshet.

English: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king's table; and was lame on both his feet.
Masaai: Neaku etobiko Mefiboshet te Yerusalem; amu kedaa apa ninye anaake te mesa o laiguanani. Naa olmaima apa too nkejek enyena pokira are.

English: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena neye olaiguanani loo Lamoni neitoreisho Hanan olayioni lenye te rishata enye.

English: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
Masaai: Nejo Daudi, “Kaitodol nanu esupatisho Hanan olayioni le Nashash, anaa apa enaaitaasa papaai lenye nanu te supatisho.” Neaku eirriwayie Daudi isinkan lenyena pee eitigir ninye ti alo papaai lenye. Nepuonu isinkan le Daudi atua enkop oo Lamori.

English: And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David rather sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
Masaai: Kake etiaakitia lelo lkituaak loo Lamoni Hanan olkitok lenye, “Ijo iyie ore enkaraki nikirriwaka iyie Daudi iltung'ana likintagol naa keyanyitita papaai lino? Keitu ninye eirriu Daudi isinkan lenyena enitii iyie pee eing'or enkanasa, neikeern ninye, nenang'aa ninye?”

English: Wherefore Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.
Masaai: Neaku eewa Hanan isinkan le Daudi, nebarn ake enchoto o lmunyei lo ltung'ani nedung nkilani enye too mpolosi enye neisho ninche meshomo.

English: When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elikini Daudi, neirriwaa iltung'ana metanang'are ninche, amu etukurrutua apa lelo tung'ana oleng. Nejo olaiguanani, “Entotoni te Yeriko o metaba anaa nebulu ilmunyo linyi, pee intokiki aashukunye.”

English: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Bethrehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ishtob twelve thousand men.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol lelo tung'ana le Amoni aajo etaa ilmang'ati te Daudi, neirriwaa lelo tung'ana le Amoni ilkiliku aaisho esiaai Isiria le Beterehob, o Isiria le Soba, isikarini nkalifuni tikitam oopuo too nkejek, o laiguanani le Maaka te nebo iltung'ana enkalifu, o ltung'ana le Tob, iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon o are.

English: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening Daudi ina, neirriwaa Yoab o lorora pooki lo ltung'ana magil.

English: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
Masaai: Nepuonu Ilamoni aaipang'u neluaa to larrabal te kishomi; ore lelo Siria le Soba o le Rehob, o ltung'ana le Tob o Maaka netii ninche maate enkop naisiaja.

English: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yoab inchere eirragieki olarrabal aarare ninye te dukuya o te siadi, negelu ninye embata oo ltung'ana gelunot le Israel, neitobiraki ninche metaarare Isiria;

English: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put them in array against the children of Ammon.
Masaai: ore ilkulikae pooki loo ltung'ana lenyena nepik ninye atua enkitoria e Abishai olalashe lenye, neitobiraki ninche metaarare Ilamoni.

English: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Tenaa kegol oleng Isiria te nanu, naa eikiretu iyie nanu; kake tenaa kegol oleng Ilamoni te iyie naa kaalotu nanu aretu iyie.

English: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.
Masaai: Ntagoluoyu, naa maikuna anaa lewa te nkaraki iltung'ana lang, o too nkanas e Nkai ang; naa nchoo metaasa Olaitoriani ina nadol aa sidai te ninye.”

English: And Joab drew nigh, and the people that were with him, unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
Masaai: Neaku etupunyakitia Yoab o lelo tung'ana apa ootii te nebo ninye olarrabal aarare Isiria; neipirri aailanyisho ninche te dukuya ninye.

English: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Ilamoni aajo eilanyishote Isiria, neiko sii ninche neijia aailanyisho te dukuya Abishai, nejing atua enkanasa. Kaae neshukunye Yoab aing'uaa olarrabal loo Lamoni, nelotu Yerusalem.

English: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
Masaai: Kake ore ake pee edol Isiria aajo etimira ninche Israel, neiturrurro maate te nebo.

English: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Hadadesa olkilikuai, neyau aitupuku lelo Siria apa ootii te idia alo Frati; nepuonu ninche Helam, te nebo Shobak olkitok le njore e Hadadesa te dukuya ninche.

English: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elikini Daudi, neiturrur ninye Israeli pooki te nebo, nelang Yordan, nepuonu Helam. Neitobira Isiria maate aarare Daudi, neitayu olarrabal te nebo ninye.

English: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew the men of seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.
Masaai: Neipirri Isiria aailanyisho te dukuya Israel, near Daudi metuata too ltung'ana le Siria iip naapishana loo ngarrin, o lakedok loo mbartan nkalifuni artam, nepik olbae Shobak ilo kitok le njore enye, neaku etua ninye te ine.

English: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
Masaai: Ore pee edol lelo aiguanak pooki apa laa isinkan le Hadadesa ninche etimira Israel neitayu ninche osotua te nebo Israel, neaku isinkan te ninche. Neaku etureita Isiria eitoki aaretu Ilamoni.

English: And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore te nkiterunoto o lari, ina kata apa napuoie ilaiguanak olarrabal, neirriwaa Daudi Yoab, o sinkan lenyena te nebo ninye, o Israel pooki, neitalaku ninche elap too ltung'ana le Amoni neman aamuat Raba. Kake etotona Daudi te Yerusalem.

English: And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
Masaai: Ore nabo olong, etigile enkolong, ore pee edumunye Daudi te ndapash enye, neloolo ninye te nchumata oltapeet le nkaji o laiguanani, nedol ninye te nchumata olperere enkitok eitukuo; naa eisidai ina kitok oleng.

English: And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
Masaai: Neirriwaa Daudi olkilikuai aikilikuanu ina kitok. Nejo obo, “Aime Betsheba ena, entito e Eliam, enkitok e Uria Olhiti?”

English: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
Masaai: Neaku eirriwayie Daudi ilkiliku, neya ninye; nelotu ninye enetii, neboitare ninye ninye. (Naa keitobira apa ninye kewan te nkiduruk enye.) Neitoki ashuko alo enkaji enye.

English: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
Masaai: Nenutayu ina kitok; neirriwaa ninye olkilikuai nejoki Daudi, “Atunute.”

English: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
Masaai: Neirriwaki Daudi Yoab olomoni, ejo, “Irriwakaki nanu Uria loo Lhiti.” Neirriwaa Yoab Uria enetii Daudi.

English: And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Uria enetii ninye, neikilikuanu Daudi enaasita Yoab o eneikununo iltung'ana, o eneikunari olarrabal.

English: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Uria, “Tadoi shomo enkaji ino, pee intuku nkejek inono.” Neipang Uria alo te nkaji o laiguanani, nesujaa ninye enkishooroto naing'uaa olaiguanani.

English: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
Masaai: Kake eirure Uria te kutukaji e nkaji o laiguanani te nebo isinkan pooki lo lkitok lenye, neitu elo enkaji enye.

English: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down unto thine house?
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejoki ninche Daudi, “Eitu edoyio Uria alo enkaji enye,” nejoki Daudi Uria, “Keitu iyie ilotu aing'uaa enkop naado kainyoo pee eitu idoyio alo enkaji ino?”

English: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
Masaai: Nejoki Uria Daudi, “Ore osanduku le Nkai, e Israel o Yuda nebikito too lng'oborri; ore olkitok lai Yoab o sinkan lo lkitok lai netii ilng'oborri ti ong'ata naisiaja; kalo naa nanu enkaji ai, adaa naokisho, nairrag te nebo enkitok ai? Anaa eninchu, o anaa enaishu oltau lino, maas nanu ena bae.”

English: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi ajoki Uria, “Totona ake sii taata tene, ore taaisere naaisho iyie shomo.” Neaku etotona Uria te Yerusalem ina olong o pee ekenyu.

English: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
Masaai: Neitoomon Daudi ninye, nedaa ninye te dukuya ninye neokisho, neaku eitemera ninye; ore te nteipa neipang ninye alo airrag te ndapash enye te nebo isinkan lo lkitok lenye, kake eitu ninye edoyio alo enkaji enye.

English: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
Masaai: Ore tadekenya neigeroki Daudi Yoab empalai, neirriwaa te nkaina e Uria.

English: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
Masaai: Ore ti atua empalai neiger ajo, “Tipika Uria enkomom o larrabal ogol, paa intokiki aaitiakunye aaing'uaa ninye, pee etumi aatar metua.

English: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.
Masaai: Ore emanita Yoab enkanasa neisho ninye Uria ewueji neyiolo ajo ketii iltung'ana oopi.

English: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Masaai: Neipang'u iltung'ana le nkanasa aapuonu aarare Yoab, ore embata oo ltung'ana le Daudi ti atua iltung'ana neurori. Ore Uria ilo Hiti nesesekuani sii ninye.

English: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
Masaai: Neirriwaa Yoab olkilikuai aliki Daudi ilomon pooki lo larrabal.

English: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
Masaai: Neitanap ninye ilo kilikuai, ejo, “Ore ake pee indip ainosaki ilomon pooki lo larrabal olaiguanani,

English: And if so be that the king's wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
Masaai: ore ake pee eilep, engoro o laiguanani, ore ake pee kijoki iyie, ‘Kainyoo intae pee ishomo aataaniki enkang oleng to larrabal? Keitu intae iyiolouu aajo kengorisho te suntai.

English: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
Masaai: Kaing'ae apa natara Abimelek olayioni le Yerubeshet metua? Aime enkitok natanang'ua osoit oidong'ishoreki aitadoiki te suntai, neaku etua ninye te Tebes. Kainyoo intae pee ishomo oleng aanyikaki esuntai?’ Nijo iyie, ‘Ore sii osinka lino Uria Olhiti etua sii ninye.’ ”

English: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.
Masaai: Kaae nelo ilo kilikuai, nelotu neliki Daudi nena pooki naairriwua Yoab ninye metoliki.

English: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo tung'ani lo lkilikuai Daudi, “Enotokitio iyiook iltung'ana, neipang'u aapuonu aarare iyiook ti ong'ata; kake kiterewa aashukoki enejing'ieki kishomi.

English: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king's servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
Masaai: Neng'or iltung'ana loo mbaa isinkan linono te suntai; netuata embata oo sinkan lo laiguanani; ore osinka lino Uria Olhiti netua sii ninye.”

English: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi ilo kilikuai, “Nji iyie shomo tiaaki Yoab, ‘Mincho iyie ena bae kintanyamal, amu ear olalem obo taata near taata olikae; ntirrisha erasakinoto ino, enkanasa nimbung ninye.’ Nintagol ninye oshoke.”

English: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
Masaai: Ore pee ening enkitok e Uria nchere etua Uria olmoruo lenye, neishir ninye olkiyioi lo Sina enkaraki olmoruo lenye.

English: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
Masaai: Ore pee eishunye olkiyioi, neirriwaa Daudi olkilikuai neyau ninye enkaji enye, neaku ninye enkitok enye, neiki ninye olayioni. Kake ore ina bae nataasa Daudi neitu eitiship Olaitoriani.

English: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Olaitoriani Natan enetii Daudi. Nelotu ninye enetii ninye nejoki ninye, “Etii apa iltung'ana oare enkang naje, naa karsis obo naa aisinani olikae.

English: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani karsis neeta nkerrai kumok o nchoo;

English: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
Masaai: kake ore ilo tung'ani aisinani nemeeta toki meteleku ake enkiti supen e ker, apa nainyiang'ua ninye. Neoroo ninye, nebulu ninye te nebo ninye o te nebo nkera enyena; naa keng'arie apa ninye endaa enye, neokisho te nkikompe enye, neirrag to lgoo lenye, netiu apa ninye anaa entito te ninye.

English: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
Masaai: Nelotu apa olalotoni enetii ilo tung'ani karsis, nemeyieu apa ninye neya too nkerrai enyena arashu too nchoo pee eitobiraki ilo otudung'uo enkop oewuo enetii ninye, kake eewa ninye olkuoo le ilo aisinani, neitobiraki ilo tung'ani apa oewuo enetii ninye.”

English: And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
Masaai: Neyupuyup oleng engoro e Daudi te nkaraki ilo tung'ani; nejoki ninye Natan, “Ore anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, ore ilo tung'ani otaasa ena eishiaakino neye;

English: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Masaai: nelak ilo kuoo katitin ong'uan, enkaraki ena bae, o enkaraki nemeeta olng'ur.”

English: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
Masaai: Nejoki Natan Daudi, “Iyie ilo tung'ani. Nji ejo Olaitoriani, Enkai e Israel, ‘Aatubukoko iyie eilata aput aitaa olaiguanani te shumata Israel naatokordua iyie aitayu te nkaina e Saul;

English: And I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.
Masaai: naaisho nanu iyie enkaji o lkitok lino, o nkituaak o lkitok lino to lgoo lino, naaisho iyie enkaji e Israel o ene Yuda; naa tenaa ae kiti ena, naaponiki nanu iyie nkumok oleng.

English: Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
Masaai: Kainyoo iyie pee itemenayie ororei lo Laitoriani, pee ias ina suuji too nkonyek enyena? Itasesekuana iyie Uria ilo Hiti to lalem, niya enkitok enye metaa enkitok ino, nitara ninye to lalem loo Lamori.

English: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
Masaai: Ore naa taata meiwuang'a ae kata olalem te nkaji ino amu kitemena nanu, niya enkitok e Uria ilo Hiti metaa enkitok ino.’

English: Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
Masaai: Nji ejo Olaitoriani, ‘Ng'ura, kadumu nanu entorroni nikiarare iyie ti atua enkaji ino makewan; naya nanu nkituaak inono te dukuya nkonyek inono, naisho nanu ninche olelatia ino, neirrag ninye te nebo inkituaak inono dama ena olong.

English: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
Masaai: Amu itaasa iyie too nkisudorot kake kaas nanu ena te dukuya Israel pooki, naas nanu dama.’ ”

English: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Natan, “Ataasa nanu eng'oki to Laitoriani.” Nejoki Natan Daudi, “Eiwuang'ie sii ninye Olaitoriani eng'oki ino; miye iyie.

English: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
Masaai: Ore eyia, enkaraki ore tena yasata nintorioko iyie amor Olaitoriani, keye ina kerai nikitoikioki iyie.” Nelo Natan enkaji enye.

English: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
Masaai: Neosh Olaitoriani ina kerai apa natoikio enkitok e Uria Daudi, nemueyu ninye.

English: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
Masaai: Nesai Daudi Enkai te nkaraki ina kerai; nepukoo Daudi, nelo atua neirrag enkewarie te nkop.

English: And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
Masaai: Ore ilpayiani le nkaji enye neitashe te mbata ninye, pee edumu ninye aaitung'uaa enkop; kake medumunye ninye, nemenya ninye endaa te nebo ninche.

English: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e naapishana neye ina kerai. Neureyu isinkan le Daudi eliki ninye nchere etua enkerai; amu etejo ninche, “Ng'ura ore apa eton eishu enkerai, nikirorie iyiook ninye, neitu ninye ening iyiook; kaji naa kinko ti nikijoki ninye inchere etua enkerai? Eidim ninye aitaasa kewan ae torrono.”

English: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
Masaai: Kake ore pee edol Daudi nchere keing'oming'omakino isinkan lenyena, nemuso Daudi nchere etua enkerai; nejoki Daudi isinkan lenyena, “Ketua enkerai?” Nejo ninche, “Etua ninye.”

English: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
Masaai: Kaae nedumunye Daudi te nkop, neitukuo, neel kewan te ilata, neibelekeny nkilani enyena nelo ninye atua enkaji o Laitoriani, neserem; neitoki ninye alo enkaji enye kewan; ore pee eikilikuanu, neirragieki endaa te dukuya ninye, nenya ninye.

English: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
Masaai: Nejoki isinkan lenyena, “Kainyoo ena bae nitaasa iyie? Itupukoyie ninchiraki eton eishu; kake ore ake pee eye enkerai nidumunye ninya endaa.”

English: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Ore apa eton eishu enkerai, napukoo naishir; amu atejo nanu, ‘Kaing'ae oyiolo tenaa kaaing'urrie nanu Olaitoriani, pee epok enkerai?’

English: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
Masaai: Kake ore taata etua; kainyoo naa pee apukoo nanu? Kaidim anyaaki atushuku ninye? Kalo nanu enetii ninye, kake meshukunye ninye enatii nanu.”

English: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
Masaai: Neilejilej Daudi enkitok enye, Bet-sheba, nelo enetii ninye, neirrag te nebo ninye, neiu ninye olayioni, nejo enkarna enye Solomon. Naa kenyor apa ninye Olaitoriani.

English: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
Masaai: Naa kenyor apa Olaitoriani ninye neirriwaa olkilikuai te Natan ilo oiboni, neaku etejo ninye enkarna enye Yedidia, te nkaraki Olaitoriani.

English: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
Masaai: Nearare Yoab Raba loo Lamoni, neya ina ang e nkitoo.

English: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Yoab ilkiliku enetii Daudi, nejo, “Ataarare nanu Raba, ore sii, aawa nanu ina anasa oo nkariak.

English: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, nturrurro tenebo ilkulikae tung'ana, nintayuyu ilng'oborri aaipirakinore enkanasa, niyaya ninye, pee maya ake nanu ina anasa, neaku te nkarna ai eipoti.”

English: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
Masaai: Neaku eiturrurro Daudi iltung'ana pooki tenebo nepuo Raba, nearare ninye neya ninye.

English: And he took their king's crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
Masaai: Neya ninye olmarisian le nkitoo lo laiguanani lenye te lukunya enye, ore apa enkiroishi enye naa entalanta e sahabu, netii atua ninye osoit ogol e nkinyang'a; nepiki ninye endukuya e Daudi. Neya ninye nena yarunot e ina anasa ntokitin kumok oleng.

English: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
Masaai: Neyau ninye lelo tung'ana apa ootii atua enkanasa, nepik ninche enkisiaayiare too musumenoni, o sururuni o ntoluo, neisho ninche meteekenyata te mpejoto oo lmatofali naa nji eikuna ninye too nkanas pooki oo Lamoni. Kaae neitoki Daudi o ltung'ana pooki aashuko Yerusalem.

English: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
Masaai: Ore apa Absalom, olayioni le Daudi, neeta enkanashe sidai naji enkarna Tamar; ore pee elusoo enkata, nenyorru ninye Amnon, olayioni le Daudi.

English: And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
Masaai: Neisomita oleng Amnon o metaba anaa nemueyu te nkaraki enkanashe enye Tamar; amu eselenkei apa nemeyiolo olee neaku etaliee ajo meidimayu te Amnon pee eitaas ninye ae.

English: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother: and Jonadab was a very subtil man.
Masaai: Kake eeta apa Amnon olchore, oji enkarna Yonadab, olayioni le Shimea, olalashe le Daudi; ore apa Yonadab naa oltung'ani kalamas oleng.

English: And he said unto him, Why art thou, being the king's son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninye, “Olayioni lo laiguanani, kainyoo pee igira asasu anaake? Aimikiliki iyie nanu?” Nejoki Amnon ninye, “Kanyor nanu Tamar, enkanashe o lalashe lai Absalom.”

English: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it at her hand.
Masaai: Nejoki Yonadab ninye, “Irraga te ndapash ino, nintaakuno eimuei; ore ake pee kilotu papaai lino adol, tiaaki ninye, ‘Nchoo enkanashe ai Tamar aalotu aisho endaa nanya, neitobir endaa te dukuya nanu, pee atum nanu atoduaa ina daa, nanya nanu te nkaina enye.’ ”

English: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
Masaai: Neaku eirraga Amnon, neitaakuno kemuei; ore ake pee elotu olaiguanani adol ninye, nejoki Amnon olaiguanani, “Nchoo siaake enkanashe ai Tamar elotu aitobir inkuti mukateni te dukuya nanu, pee aatum ninye aishoo endaa.”

English: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon's house, and dress him meat.
Masaai: Neirriwaa Daudi olkilikuai enetii Tamar ejoki, “Shomo enkaji olalashe lino Amnon, intobiraki ninye endaa.”

English: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo Tamar enkaji o lalashe lenye Amnon, ine apa neirragie. Neya ninye enkurma, neipurj, neitobir imukateni too nkonyek enyena, nepej imukateni.

English: And she took a pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.
Masaai: Neitayu ninye enkarae oo mukateni neitayu imukateni aisho te dukuya ninye, kake etanya ninye enya. Nejo Amnon, “Taarai pooki tung'ani maashomo aaing'uaa nanu.” Neipang pooki ng'ae alo aing'uaa ninye.

English: And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
Masaai: Nejoki Amnon Tamar, “Iyau endaa atua olgilata, pee atum nanu ainosa te nkaina ino.” Neya Tamar nena mukateni naaitobira, neyau ninche atua olgilata enetii Amnon olalashe lenye.

English: And when she had brought them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.
Masaai: Kake ore ake pee eyau ninche aitinyikaki ninye meinosa, neibung ninye, nejoki, “Wou, irraga te nebo nanu, enkanashe ai.”

English: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
Masaai: Newaliki ninye, “A-a, olalashe lai, mikiaraki nanu; amu measi ena te Israel; mias ena torroni emodai.

English: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.
Masaai: Amaa te nanu, kaji aya enkurruna ai? Amaa te iyie, nitiu iyie anaa obo loo larruok oomoda too Siraeli. Ore naa taata, aatasayia iyie, irorie olaiguanani, amu maamitiki ninye iyie.”

English: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.
Masaai: Kake eitu ening, naa ore amu ninye ogol alang ninye, nearaki ninye, neirag ninye te nebo ninye.

English: Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.
Masaai: Neitoki Amnon aibayu ninye te nkiba sapuk; neaku ore enkiba naiba ninye naa eisapuk alang enyorrata apa natonyorra ninye. Nejoki Amnon ninye, “Tudumunye, shomo.”

English: And she said unto him, There is no cause: this evil in sending me away is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.
Masaai: Kake etiaka ninye, “A-a, olalashe lai, amu ore ena kitarruoroto nikiararie nanu naa eikitok alang ina ae nikintaasa nanu.” Kake meinining ninye ninye.

English: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
Masaai: Neipotu ninye olbarnoti apa oisiaaita ninye nejoki, “Iwuang'ie ena kitok tene natii nanu, ninken kutukaji te siadi ninye.”

English: And she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
Masaai: Neishopito apa ninye olkila oado adoru nkaik; amu nji apa eiko iselenken o laiguanani nemeyiolo olee te neishopo. Neaku eitayio osinka lenye ninye boo, neiken kutukaji te siadi ninye.

English: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.
Masaai: Nepik Tamar nkuruon endukuya enye nepolos ilo kila oado apa oishopito; neiteleiki nkaik enyena endukuya enye, nelo, neyietu aishir eloito.

English: And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house.
Masaai: Nejoki olalashe lenye Absalom ninye, “Ketii duoo Amnon olalashe lino te nebo iyie? Tigirayu naa taata, enkanashe ai; olalashe lino ninye; mipik ena oltau.” Nebik Tamar, anaa enkitok naliyio, ti atua enkaji o lalashe lenye Absalom.

English: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Olaiguanani Daudi kuna baa pooki, negoro ninye oleng.

English: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
Masaai: Kake eitu eirorie Absalom Amnon aa esidai aa entorrono; amu eibayie apa Absalom Amnon, enkaraki naikonya enkanashe enye Tamar.

English: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ilarin oare oolulung'a neeta apa Absalom ilabarnok loo nkerra te Baal-haso, naa ninye nataaniki Efraim, neitoomon Absalom ilayiok pooki lo laiguanani.

English: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.
Masaai: Nelotu Absalom enetii olaiguanani, nejo, “Ng'ura, eeta osinka lino ilabarnok loo nkerra; aatasayia nchoo olaiguanani o sinkan lenyena epuo te nebo osinka lino.”

English: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.
Masaai: Kake etiaka olaiguanani Absalom, “A-a, olayioni lai, mincho iyiook kipuo pooki, mikiaku ake iyiook olola te iyie.” Neitirrishaki ninye, kake meyieu ninye nelo kake eishoo ninye emayianata enye.

English: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?
Masaai: Nejo Absalom, “Ti nimilo, aatoomono nchoo olalashe lai Amnon elo te nebo iyiook.” Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kainyoo pee elo ninye te nebo intae?”

English: But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.
Masaai: Kake eitirrishaka Absalom ninye o metaba anaa neisho ninye Amnon o layiok pooki lo laiguanani meshomo te nebo ninye.

English: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.
Masaai: Neitanap Absalom isinkan lenyena, ejo, “Entujurru ore ake pee emera Amnon te naisho oo sabibu, ore ake pee ajoki intae, ‘Entoosh Amnon,’ niariara intae ninye metua. Emiureisho; aime nanu oitanapa intae? Entipijuoto niarriyianunu.”

English: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.
Masaai: Neaku eitaasa isinkan le Absalom Amnon anaa enaitanapishe Absalom. Nedumunye ilayiok lo laiguanani pooki, neked ake oltung'ani enyumpu enye neisik.

English: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left.
Masaai: Ore epuoito ninche te nkoitoi, nepuonu ilomon enetii Daudi, nejo “Etaara Absalom ilayiok lo laiguanani pooki, metuata neitu ninye eing'uari obo.”

English: Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.
Masaai: Nedumunye olaiguanani, nepolos ilkilani lenyena, neirrag te nkop; ore isinkan lenyena pooki apa ooitashe te mbata nepolos ilkilani lenye.

English: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men the king's sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
Masaai: Kake etejo Yonadab olayioni le Shimea, ilo alashe le Daudi, “Mincho olkitok lai ejo ketaara ninche metuata lelo barnot pooki, lelo ayiok lo laiguanani, amu Amnon ake otua, amu te nkitanapata e Absalom etaasaki ena ebaiki apa enkolong naikonya ninye enkanashe enye Tamar.

English: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king's sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, mincho olkitok lai olaiguanani epik oltau adamu ajo etuata ilayiok pooki lo laiguanani; amu Amnon ake otua.”

English: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill side behind him.
Masaai: Kake eisika Absalom. Ore apa olbarnoti orripisho nedumu nkonyek enyena, neing'orisho, naa ng'ura, epuonu iltung'ana aaimu enkoitoi e Horonaim emurte o ldoinyo.

English: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king's sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.
Masaai: Nejoki Yonadab olaiguanani, “Ng'ura, eetuo ilayiok lo laiguanani; anaa enatejo osinka lino, metaa etaa ina.”

English: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.
Masaai: Ore ake enaidipie airoro, ng'ura, nepuonu ilayiok lo laiguanani, neilepie oltoilo neishir; ore olaiguanani o sinkan lenyena pooki neishir te mion oleng.

English: But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
Masaai: Kake eisika Absalom, nelo enetii Talmai olayioni le Amihud, olaiguanani le Geshur. Neishir Daudi te nkaraki olayioni lenye anaake.

English: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
Masaai: Neaku eisika Absalom, nelo enetii Geshur, netii apa ine ilarin okuni.

English: And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.
Masaai: Neyieu oltau lo laiguanani nelo enetii Absalom; amu eitigiraki ti alo Amnon, etodua ajo etua ninye.

English: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom.
Masaai: Ore apa Yoab olayioni le Seruiya nemusu ajo Absalom edamu oltau lo laiguanani.

English: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
Masaai: Neirriwaa Yoab olkilikuai meshomo Tekoa, meyau te ine enkitok ng'en, nejoki ninye, “Ntaakunoyu ira enkaishirani, nipika ilkilani lo lkiyioi; nimiel kewan te ilata, kake taasa anaa enkitok naishirita too nkolong'i kumok te nkaraki o lotua;

English: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.
Masaai: nilo enetii olaiguanani, niro aiko nji te ninye.” Neaku etipika Yoab irorei enkutuk enye.

English: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu ina kitok e Tekoa enetii olaiguanani, nebatata te nkomom enye o metabaiki enkop, nesai, nejo, “Taretuoki, Olaiguanani.”

English: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kainyoo enyamali ino?” Newal ninye ajo, “Ng'ura ara nanu enkoliai; etua olmoruo lai.

English: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.
Masaai: Neeta esinka ino ilayiok oare, neitarrikino ninche maate ti ong'ata; nemetii apa oltung'ani orish ninche, neosh obo olikae near ninye metua.

English: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the earth.
Masaai: Ore taata netudumakine olmarei pooki esinka ino, nejo ninche, ‘Nchoru ilo tung'ani otara olalashe lenye, pee kitum iyiook aataar ninye metua te nkaraki olalashe lenye apa otasesekuana’; neaku keinyal sii ninye olajung'oni. Neiko neijia aar enkukuo ai natung'uayioki, nemeing'ueiki olmoruo lai enkarna arashu olpisiai ti oriong enkop.”

English: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ina kitok, “Shomo enkaji ino, naa kaishoru nanu nkitanapat ti alo iyie.”

English: And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father's house: and the king and his throne be guiltless.
Masaai: Nejoki ina kitok e Tekoa olaiguanani, “Nchoo eaku shumata nanu etii enkitarruoroto, Olaitoriani lai olaiguanani, o shumata enkaji e papa lai; nchoo olaiguanani o lorika lenye le nkitoo eaku meeta entioto.”

English: And the king said, Whosoever saith ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Ti nikijoki oltung'ani ae toki, iyau ninye enatii nanu, nimikingil ae kata ninye aibung.”

English: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Aatoomono nchoo olaiguanani eipot Olaitoriani Enkai ino, paa ore ilo oitalaku elap to sarge nemeitoki ae kata asesekuanisho, ore olayioni lai nemeari metua.” Nejo ninye, “Anaaenaishu Olaitoriani, medoiki ninye olpapita obo lo layioni lino enkop.”

English: Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak one word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
Masaai: Neitoki ina kitok ajo, “Aatasayia nchoo esinka ino eiro ororei to lkitok lai olaiguanani.” Nejo ninye, “Iroro.”

English: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.
Masaai: Nejo ina kitok, “Kainyoo naa iyie pee intobira embae naaijo ena aarare iltung'ana le Nkai? Amu ore te nkishorunoto ena walata neen olaiguanani kewan, te ina nemeyau olaiguanani ilo lenye oararo nerrinyunye ang.

English: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
Masaai: Meeta nchere mikiye pooki, kitiu iyiook anaa enkare naisuaakaki enkop, nemeitoki asotunoyu; kake meitayu Enkai enkishui e ilo oing'oru nkoitoi pee mepal ilo lenye oararo metaa oloiturrayioki.

English: Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
Masaai: Aewuo nanu ajo ena to lkitok lai olaiguanani amu aaitaa nanu iltung'ana kuret; nedamu apa esinka ino, ajo, ‘Kairorie nanu olaiguanani; eidimayu pee eas olaiguanani eomonunoto e sinka enye.

English: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
Masaai: Amu kening olaiguanani, nekordu esinka enye aitung'uaa enkaina o ltung'ani laaidim ainyala nanu o layioni lai te nebo aitung'uaa enjung'ore e Nkai.’

English: Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.
Masaai: Nedamu esinka ino ajo, ‘Ore ororei lo lkitok lai olaiguanani naa kaayeng'iyeng'ie nanu’; amu ore olkitok lai olaiguanani netiu anaa olmalaika le Nkai te nerish esidai o entorrono. Metaa Olaitoriani Enkai ino te nebo iyie!”

English: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani awaliki ina kitok nejo, “Mikisudorie nanu pooki toki naba anaa enaaikilikuan iyie.” Nejo ina kitok, “Nchoo olkitok lai olaiguanani eiro.”

English: And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Ketii enkaina e Yoab te nebo iyie te kuna pooki?” Newal ina kitok nejo, “Esipa ore anaa eninchu iyie, olkitok lai olaiguanani, meidim oltung'ani aibelekenyayu enkaina e tatene arashu enkaina e kedienye te pooki bae natejo olkitok lai olaiguanani. Osinka lino Yoab laaiguanaka nanu; ninye otipika kulo rorei pooki enkutuk e sinka ino.

English: To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.
Masaai: Etaasa osinka lino Yoab ena pee etum aibelekenya kuna baa. Kake ore olkitok lai neeta eng'eno anaa olmalaika le Nkai ayiolou mbaa pooki naatii enkop.”

English: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Yoab, “Ng'ura taata, aishorua ena; shomo tushuku ilo barnoti Absalom.”

English: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
Masaai: Nebatata Yoab te nkomom enye abaiki enkop, nesai, nemayian olaiguanani, nejo Yoab, “Ore taata etayiolo osinka lino nchere anoto omom too nkonyek inono, olkitok lai olaiguanani, te ina naishorua olaiguanani eomonunoto osinka lenye.”

English: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Neaku etudumunye Yoab nelo Geshur, nelo ariku Absalom Yerusalem.

English: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king's face.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Nchoo ninye eton openy ti atua enkaji enye makewan; melotu ninye enatii nanu.” Neaku etotona Absalom openy te enkaji enye makewan, neitu elotu enetii Olaiguanani.

English: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
Masaai: Ore apa ti atua Israel pooki nemetii oltung'ani orrepi te nkishaa enye anaa Absalom; ore ebaiki endap e nkeju enye o metabaiki endukuya enye nemeetae eleyiata te ninye.

English: And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year's end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.
Masaai: Naa te nedung ninye ilpapit le ndukuya enye (amu kedung apa te nkiting'oto e pooki ari; te neiroshiu oleng te ninye, nedung) neipim ninye ilpapit le ndukuya enye, naa shekeli iip are te ntemata o laiguanani.

English: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
Masaai: Netoikioki apa Absalom ilayiok okuni o entito nabo naji Tamar; naa enkitok sidai apa ninye.

English: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king's face.
Masaai: Neaku etobiko Absalom ilarin oare oolulung'a te Yerusalem, eitu elotu enetii olaiguanani.

English: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
Masaai: Neirriwaki Absalom ilkiliku Yoab pee eirriwaa ninye enetii olaiguanani; kake etanya elotu Yoab enetii ninye. Neirriwaa eniare, kake melotu Yoab.

English: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab's field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye isinkan lenyena, “Eng'ura aajo ore enkurma e Yoab netashare enaai, neeta enkano te ine; enchom entipik enkima.” Neaku eshomo aapej enkurma.

English: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
Masaai: Nedumunye Yoab nelo enetii Absalom te nkaji enye, nejoki ninye, “Kainyoo pee etapejo isinkan linono enkurma ai?”

English: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king's face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
Masaai: Newaliki Absalom Yoab nejo, “Ng'ura aairriwaka iyie olomoni, ‘Wou ene, pee aatum airriwaki olaiguanani, pee aikilikuan ajoki, “Kainyoo nanu pee aewuo aing'uaa Geshur? Enaikash te nanu te neton atii ine.” Ore naa taata nchooki nanu alo enetii olaiguanani; naa te naata enkitarruoroto, nchoo ninye maatara nanu matua.’ ”

English: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
Masaai: Kaae nelo Yoab enetii olaiguanani, neliki ninye; neipotu ninye Absalom. Neaku eewuo ninye enetii olaiguanani, neirrug kewan te nkomom enye o metabaiki enkop te dukuya olaiguanani; neng'utut olaiguanani Absalom.

English: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena neing'uraki Absalom kewan engarri oo mbartan o ltung'ana onom ookuet te dukuya ninye.

English: And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
Masaai: Naa keinyototo apa Absalom ayooki neitashe te mbata enkoitoi e kishomi; ore te neeta oltung'ani enkiguana nayau dukuya olaiguanani pee eiguanareki, neipotu Absalom ninye, nejo, “Kaa anasa ing'uaa iyie?” Ore ake pee ejo, “Ore osinka lino naa olosho oje te Israel,”

English: And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
Masaai: nejoki Absalom ninye, “Ng'ura, kesipa neishiaakino ena niyieu; kake metii oltung'ani otegelua olaiguanani likining iyie.”

English: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!
Masaai: Nepon Absalom ajo, “Oi naaji aa kara oladung'oni le nkiguana tena kop! Neaku ore pooki tung'ani oata enkiguana arashu enaikilikuanu neidim aeu enatii, naisho nanu ninye esipata.”

English: And it was so, that when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
Masaai: Naa ore ake pee ejo oltung'ani anyiku alotu aserem ninye, neitorioo enkaina enye neibung ninye, neng'utut ninye.

English: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
Masaai: Neiko neijia Absalom too ltung'ana loo Israeli oopuonu enetii olaiguanani metundung'okini enkiguana; neaku etupurroyie Absalom iltauja loo ltung'ana le Israel.

English: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.
Masaai: Ore te nkiting'oto oo larin oong'uan nejoki Absalom olaiguanani, “Aatasayia nchooki nanu mashomo alak olmumai apa lainosa to Laitoriani, te Hebron.

English: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.
Masaai: Amu einosa apa osinka lino olmumai atii Geshur natii Aram, najo, ‘Esipa te naaitoki nanu Olaitoriani ashuku Yerusalem, naitayu nanu eseremata to Laitoriani.’ ”

English: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Shomo te seriani.” Neaku etudumunye ninye nelo Hebron.

English: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
Masaai: Kake eirriwayie Absalom ilkiliku te nkisudoroto atua Israel pooki, ejo, “Ore ake pee ining'ining'i oltoilo le mowuo, entejo, ‘Absalom olaiguanani te Hebron!’ ”

English: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.
Masaai: Nepuo te nebo Absalom iltung'ana iip are ooing'uaa Yerusalem aa ilomon apa ooitoomonoki, nepuo ninche meeta ae too ltauja neitu eyiolou toki.

English: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
Masaai: Ore eitayu Absalom olasar, neirriwaki olkilikuai meipotuni Ahitofel ilo le Gilom olaikooni le Daudi meeu te nkanasa enye Gilo. Neponari enkarruoisho e Absalom ore iltung'ana ootii te nebo Absalom neponari.

English: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.
Masaai: Nelotu olkilikuai enetii Daudi, ejo, “Eshomo iltauja loo ltung'ana le Israel aasujaa Absalom.”

English: And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi iltung'ana lenyena pooki apa ootii te nebo ninye te Yerusalem, “Entudumunye, emaisika iyiook, arashu eaku mikiata iyiook enikisikaki aailany Absalom; enchom entasiooi meinepu akeninye iyiook asioki, neyau entorroni aitadoiki shumata iyiook, neshurt ena anasa te nepi o lalem.”

English: And the king's servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.
Masaai: Nejoki isinkan lo laiguanani olaiguanani, “Ng'ura, eanyita isinkan linono pee eas enaba anaa enadung'u olkitok lai olaiguanani.”

English: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, which were concubines, to keep the house.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo olaiguanani, ore enkaji enye pooki nesujaa ninye. Neing'uaa olaiguanani nkapiak tomon pee eing'or enkaji.

English: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.
Masaai: Nelo olaiguanani nesujaa iltung'ana pooki ninye; neitashe ninche te nkaji nabayie.

English: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Masaai: Negiroo isinkan lenyena pooki ninye; o Lkereti pooki, o Lpeleti, o lelo iip ile le Giti apa ootusujaitie ninye ebaiki Gas, negiroo aaim dukuya olaiguanani.

English: Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou art a stranger, and also an exile.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Itai ilo le Giti, “Kainyoo sii pee ilo iyie te nebo iyiook? Tushukoyu shomo, pee ilo aton te nebo olaiguanani; amu ira iyie olomoni, nira sii oloisikua aing'uaa enkang ino.

English: Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth be with thee.
Masaai: Ng'ole ake iewuo iyie, naa kaaisho nanu iyie taata tamanai te nebo iyiook, idolita aloito, nemayiolo enalo? Tushukoyu shomo, nirik ilalashera linono te nebo iyie; naa mikintoduaa iyie Olaitoriani enyorrata nauno o enkisiligata.”

English: And Ittai answered the king, and said, As the LORD liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.
Masaai: Kake etawalikia Itai olaiguanani ajoki, “Ore anaa enaishu Olaitoriani, naa ore enaishu olkitok lai olaiguanani, ore eneba enaa enetii olkitok lai olaiguanani, aa te keeya arashu te nkishui, ine sii ninye etii osinka lino.”

English: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Itai, “Shomo naa, tulusoi.” Neaku eshomo Itai ilo le Giti agiroo, te nebo iltung'ana lenyena pooki o nena kutiti pooki apa naatii te nebo ninye.

English: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.
Masaai: Neishir enkop pooki ayietu egiroo iltung'ana pooki, nelang olaiguanani oerata le Kidron, negiroo iltung'ana pooki aing'or enkalo o lpurkel.

English: And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
Masaai: Neilepu Abiata, naa ng'ura, eewuo sii Sadok, te nebo Ilawi pooki, enapita osanduku lo sotua le Nkai; neirragie ninche ilo sanduku le Nkai, o metaba anaa negiroo iltung'ana pooki ti oriong enkanasa.

English: And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Sadok, “Entanap osanduku le Nkai entorriny tiaatua enkanasa. Te natum nanu kirotetisho too nkonyek o Laitoriani, naa kaashuku ninye naaisho ninye matodua ninye o emanyisho enye;

English: But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
Masaai: kake te nejo ninye, ‘Maashipakino nanu iyie,’ ng'ura, nele nanu, nchoo ninye maaitaasa ina nadol aa sidai te ninye.”

English: The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
Masaai: Neitoki ake sii olaiguanani ajoki Sadok olapolosani, “Ng'ura, tushukoyu shomo enkanasa te seriani, iyie o Abiata, te nebo ilayiok linyi pokira oare, Ahimasi olayioni lino, o Yonatan olayioni le Abiata.

English: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
Masaai: Ng'ura, kaanyu nanu iyie too lang'at o lpurkel, o metaba anaa nelotu olomoni oing'uaa enitii pee aaitayiolo nanu.”

English: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.
Masaai: Neaku etanapa Sadok o Abiata osanduku le Nkai aashuk Yerusalem; nebik ninche te ine.

English: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
Masaai: Kake eilepa Daudi alo enchumata o ldoinyo loo loirienito, neishiraa eloito, meeta namuka neimulumula endukuya enye; ore lelo tung'ana pooki ootii te nebo ninye neimulumul ilukuny enye, neilep ninche aapuo, neishiraa epuoito.

English: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
Masaai: Nejokini apa Daudi, “Etii Ahitofel atua lelo arruok te nebo Absalom.” Nejo Daudi, “Olaitoriani, aatoomono nanu iyie, mbelekenya enkiguana e Ahitofel metaa emodai.”

English: And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
Masaai: Ore ake pee elotu Daudi entopij o ldoinyo ine apa neseremieki Enkai, ng'ura, nelotu Hushai ilo Akiti anang'are ninye epolosa olkila lenye lioriong netii enterit endukuya enye.

English: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi ninye, “Ti nilo iyie te nebo nanu niaku iyie olola te nanu.

English: But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father's servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
Masaai: Kake ti nishuko iyie alo enkanasa, nijoki Absalom, ‘Kaaku nanu osinka lino, iyie olaiguanani, naa ore apa anaa enara nanu osinka le papaai lino te nkata natulusoyie, neijia sii taata etiu kaaku nanu osinka lino,’ niaku intashal iyie te nkaraki nanu enkiguana e Ahitofel.

English: And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king's house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Masaai: Ai metii Sadok o Abiata ilapolosak te nebo iyie te idie? Metaa ore enaba anaa enining te nkaji o laiguanani, toliki Sadok o Abiata ilapolosak.

English: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok's son, and Jonathan Abiathar's son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
Masaai: Ng'ura etii ilayiok lenye pokira oare te nebo ninche te ine, Ahima-as, olayioni le Sadok, o Yonatan, olayioni le Abiata; naa te ninche kirriwaki nanu pooki toki nining.”

English: So Hushai David's friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
Masaai: Neaku eewuo Hushai, olchore le Daudi atua enkanasa, ina kata apa ejing'ita Absalom Yerusalem.

English: And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
Masaai: Ore ake pee egiroo Daudi enchumata o ldoinyo peno, netumore ninye Siba osinka le Mofiboshet, o sirkon are naairotoki, enapita imukateni iip are, o rridat iip loo sabibu ooitoyioki, o rridat iip loo lng'anayio le nkolong, o lbene lo lchoni le naisho oo sabibu.

English: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Siba, “Kainyoo iyie pee iyaua kuna?” Newal Siba ajo, “Ore kulo sirkon laa ile nkaji o laiguanani pee eked alotie, ore imukateni o lng'anayio naa inoo lbarnot naanya, ore enaisho oo sabibu naa ene lelo ooiterre to lpurkel pee eok.”

English: And the king said, And where is thy master's son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Paa koree olayioni lo lkitok lino?” Nejoki Siba olaiguanani, “Ng'ura, etotona te Yerusalem; amu etejo ninye, ‘Taata aaisho nanu enkaji e Israel aashukoki enkitoria e papa lai.’ ”

English: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani ajoki Siba, “Ng'ura, ore nena apa pooki naara ine Mefiboshet naa nkuninono taata.” Nejo Siba, “Kaasai nanu; nchooki nanu manoto omom too nkonyek inono, olkitok lai olaiguanani.”

English: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Olaiguanani Daudi Bahurim, neipang'u te ine oltung'ani lo lmarei le nkaji e Saul, oji enkarna enye Shimei, olayioni le Gera; naa ore elotu neidikidik adekisho.

English: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
Masaai: Nenang Daudi too soito; nenang sii isinkan pooki lo laiguanani Daudi, o ltung'ana pooki, o ltung'ana pooki kituaak ootii enkaina enye e tatene o ene kedienye.

English: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:
Masaai: Nejo Shimei ina kata edekisho, “Shomo, shomo, iyie oltung'ani lo sarge, iyie oltung'ani le pesho!

English: The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.
Masaai: Eitalakua Olaitoriani te iyie osarge pooki le nkaji e Saul, laa te wueji enye intoreishe; neishooyie Olaitoriani enkitoria apik atua enkaina o layioni Absalom. Toduaa ajo etii emutata ino shumata ino; amu ira oltung'ani lo sarge.”

English: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
Masaai: Neitoki Abishai olayioni le Seruiya ajoki olaiguanani, “Kainyoo pee edek ele dia otua olkitok lai olaiguanani? Nchooki nanu mashomo adungu endukuya enye.”

English: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
Masaai: Kake etejo olaiguanani, “Kaa nanu aabaikinore iyie, olayioni le Seruiya? Te nedekisho ninye te nkaraki natiaaka ninye Olaitoriani, ‘Tediaa Daudi,’ kaing'ae naa ojo, ‘Kainyoo pee itaasa iyie ena?’ ”

English: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Abishai o sinkan lenyena pooki, “Ng'ura, olayioni lai kewan oing'oru enkishui ai; kebaa elusoo ele tung'ani le Benchamen! Tung'uai ninye, naa nchoo ninye edekisho; amu Olaitoriani oishoo ninye.

English: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.
Masaai: Eidimayu pee eing'or Olaitoriani osina lai, naa kaalaaki nanu Olaitoriani too supati tele deket lena olong.”

English: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill's side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo Daudi o ltung'ana lenyena te nkoitoi, ina kata eloito Shimei te murte o ldoinyo eipirakinore ninye, nedekisho eloito, nenang ninye too soito neisuaaki enterit.

English: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
Masaai: Ore olaiguanani, o ltung'ana pooki apa ootii te nebo ninye, nebau enaurate Yordan; neyeng'iyeng'a ninye te ine.

English: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
Masaai: Ore apa Absalom o ltung'ana pooki, ilewa le Israel nepuonu Yerusalem, o Ahitofel te nebo ninye.

English: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elotu Hushai, lo losho le Akito ilo shore le Daudi, enetii Absalom, nejoki Hushai Absalom, “Tobikoi olaiguanani! Tobikoi olaiguanani!”

English: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
Masaai: Nejoki Absalom Hushai, “Kena enkanyit ino to lchore lino? Kainyoo pee eitu ilo te nebo olchore lino?”

English: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
Masaai: Nejoki Hushai Absalom, “A-a; amu ore ilo otegelua Olaitoriani o kulo tung'ana o lewa pooki le Israel, olenye aaku nanu, naa te nebo ninye nanu abik.

English: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father's presence, so will I be in thy presence.
Masaai: Ore ake sii, kaing'ae nanu aisiaai? Aime ilo ayioni lenye? Ore apa anaa enaisiaayia papaai lino, kaaisiaai sii nanu iyie.”

English: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
Masaai: Nejoki Absalom Ahitofel, “Nchoru enkikoo ino; kaa iyiook kias?”

English: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father's concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
Masaai: Nejoki Ahitofel Absalom, “Shomo iyie atua enetii nkapiak e papaai lino, apa naatung'uayie ninye meing'ura enkaji; pee ening Israel pooki nchere intaa kewan olmang'atinta te papaai lino, ore inkaik e lelo pooki ootii te nebo iyie neitagoli.”

English: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
Masaai: Neaku etuunokito ninche Absalom olng'obor te nchumata enkaji; nelo Absalom atua enetii nkapiak e papaai lenye edolita Israel pooki.

English: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
Masaai: Ore apa te nena olong'i eutaroto naishoru Ahitofel neikununo ake duoo anaa ororei le Nkai eikilikuanishoreki; keyanyiti apa oleng enkikoo e Ahitofel, Daudi o Absalom, pokira are.

English: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
Masaai: Neponaa Ahitofel ajoki Absalom, “Nchooki nanu mategelu iltung'ana nkalifuni tomon o are, pee aipang nanu amir Daudi kewarie.

English: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
Masaai: Naa kalotu nanu enetii ninye etanaure netashala, nanang'aki ninye atua enkiputukuny; ore iltung'ana ootii te nebo ninye neisik. Naar nanu olaiguanani ake,

English: And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
Masaai: naayaki nanu iltung'ana pooki enitii anaa esiankiki narikuni ang aarikoki olpayian lenye. Aing'oru iyie enkishui o ltung'ani obo ake, ore iltung'ana pooki neserianu.”

English: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
Masaai: Neitiship ina kikoo Absalom o lpayiani pooki le Israel.

English: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
Masaai: Neitoki Absalom ajo, “Empoto sii ninye Hushai ilo Alkiti, pee kining iyiook enajo ninye.”

English: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Hushai enetii Absalom, nejoki Absalom ninye, “Nji eiroro Ahitofel ajo; amaa aikias iyiook anaa enautu ninye? Tinimikias iroro naa iyie.”

English: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.
