Masaai: Nejoki Hushai Absalom, “Ore tena kata enkikoo naishorua Ahitofel neme sidai.”

English: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
Masaai: Nejo Hushai, “Ore ake, iyiolo nchere ore papaai lino o ltungana lenyena naa ltung'ana magil netarasutua sii, anaa olng'arurumi otooruoki nkera enyena ti ong'ata. Ore etii ina, kaarriyia papaai lino to larrabal; meirura ninye kewarie te nebo iltung'ana.

English: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
Masaai: Ng'ura, ore ninye taata eisudoyie ninye kewan te ngumoto nabo, arashu ti ae wueji. Naa ore ake pee ebatata embata oo ltung'ana te rasakinoto e dukuya, ore pooki ng'ae oning nejo, ‘Etii enkidaaroto atua lelo tung'ana oosujita Absalom.’

English: And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
Masaai: Neaku ore ninye oltung'ani opi, oikununo oltau anaa oltau lo lng'atuny, nelepori tukul te nkuretisho; amu eyiolo Israel pooki nchere ore papaai lino naa oltung'ani magilani, naa ore lekua ootii te nebo ninye naa iltung'ana oopi.

English: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.
Masaai: Kake ore eutaroto ai naa nchere pee kinturrurrokino iyie Israel pooki, ebaiki Dan o metabaiki Beer-sheba, eba anaa osinyai le naiposha te nkumoi naa nchere, mirikoo iyie makewan olarrabal.

English: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
Masaai: Neaku eikipuonu iyiook shumata ninye ti atua ewueji neba anaa enetumieki ninye, paa eikidoiki iyiook ninye te wueji neba anaa enetumieki nikidoiki iyiook ninye anaa enadoiki enkoileelio enkop; ore te ninye o ltung'ana pooki ootii te nebo ninye meing'uari ninye obo.

English: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
Masaai: Naa tenelo ninye ajing atua enkanasa, neyau Isiraeli pooki nkeenta ina ang, nikinkurtutaa iyiook ina ang atua oerata o metaba anaa neaku metumi ninye osoit obo te ine.”

English: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.
Masaai: Ore Absalom o ltung'ana pooki le Israel nejo, “Ore enkikoo e Hushai Olakiti naa eisidai alang enkikoo e Ahitofel.” Amu etegelua Olaitoriani pee emir enkikoo sidai e Ahitofel, pee etum Olaitoriani ayau entorroni shumata Absalom.

English: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
Masaai: Nejoki Hushai Sadok o Abiata lelo apolosak, “Nji o nji eikoo Ahitofel Absalom o lpayiani le Israel; naa nji o nji nanu aikoo.

English: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
Masaai: Ore naa taata erriwai ilkiliku entasioki entiaki Daudi, ‘Mirura taata iyie kewarie too lang'eta oo lkejek to lpurkel, kake togiroi tukul; meijori ake olaiguanani o ltung'ana pooki ootii te nebo ninye.’ ”

English: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
Masaai: Ore apa Yonatan o Ahima-aa neanyisho ninche te En-rogel; nelo apa enkaisiaayiani aliki ninche, nepuo ninche aaliki olaiguanani Daudi; amu meeta nchere pee etoduaki ninche ejing enkanasa.

English: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man's house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
Masaai: Kake etoduaa ninche enkayioni, neliki Absalom; neaku eshomo ninche pokira are aasiooyo, nepuonu enkaji o ltung'ani te Bahurim, apa oata enchorro ti oriong e nkaji enye; nedoiki ninche atua.

English: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
Masaai: Neya enkitok neimulumul enjing'et enchorro, neidapashaki enkano shumata enye; neaku meyiolounoyu toki.

English: And when Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee epuonu isinkan le Absalom enetii ina kitok ti aji, nejo ninche, “Koree Ahima-as o Yonatan?” Nejoki ina kitok ninche, “Eshomo ninche aalang ereyiet.” Ore ake pee esujaa ninche neitu einepu ninche, neshukunye ninche aapuonu Yerusalem.

English: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip ninche aatulusoi, neilepu lelo tung'ana te nchorro, nepuo aaliki Olaiguanani Daudi. Nejoki ninche Daudi, “Tudumunye, nilo asiooyo alang enkare; amu nji o nji eikoo Ahitofel te iyie.”

English: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.
Masaai: Nedumunye Daudi, o ltung'ana pooki apa ootii te nebo ninye, nelang ninche Yordan; ore enasirie eitu eleku obo leitu elang Yordan.

English: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol Ahitofel ajo eitu esuji enkikoo enye, neirot osikiria lenye, nelo ninye ang enkanasa enye makewan. Neitobir mbaa e nkaji enye, negor kewan; neye ninye, nenukari te nkurare e papaai lenye.

English: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
Masaai: Neitoki Daudi alotu Mahanaim. Nelang Absalom Yordan te nebo iltung'ana pooki loo Siraeli.

English: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man's son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab's mother.
Masaai: Netipika apa Absalom Amasa shumata enjore te rishata e Yoab. Ore apa Amasa naa olayioni lo ltung'ani oji Itra le Ishimail, apa oyama Abigail entito e Nahash, enkanashe e Seruiya, ng'otonye Yoab.

English: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.
Masaai: Ore israel o Absalom neitayu ilng'oborri te nkop o Gilead.

English: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Daudi Mahanaim, ore Shobi olayioni le Nahash oing'uaa Raba oo lamori, o Makir olayioni le Amiel oing'uaa Lo-deba, o Barsilai o Lgiliadi ooing'uaa Rogelim,

English: Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
Masaai: neyau ndapashi, o ngirran, o motioo oo nkulukuok, o enkano, o shairi, o enkurma, naidong'o, o mpoosho, o ndaiki oo mpukunot pooki,

English: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
Masaai: o enaisho, o engorno, o nkerra naaitung'uari eluaata te nkaraki Daudi o ltung'ana ootii te nebo ninye pee enya; amu etejo ninche, “Eeta iltung'ana esumash nenaura nenoto enkure ti ong'ata.”

English: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
Masaai: Neiturrur Daudi eiken iltung'ana pooki apa ootii te nebo ninye, nepik shumata ninche ilarikok loo nkalifuni o larikok loo maa iip.

English: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
Masaai: Neya Daudi enjore ematua nabo e uni ti abori erikore e Yoab, ematua nabo e uni ti abori erikore e Abishai olayioni le Seruiya, olalashe le Yoab, o ematua nabo e uni ti abori erikore e Itai Olgiladi. Nejoki olaiguanani lelo tung'ana, “Kalo sii nanu makewan aipang te nebo intae.”

English: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.
Masaai: Kake etejo lelo lewa, “Mimpang iyie alo. Amu ti nikisik iyiook nemeshilaa ninche iyiook. Te neye olpisiai lang nemeshilaa ninche iyiook. Kake inyaanyukie iyie iip tomon katitin tomon lang. Metaa enaikash tinirriwaki iyie iyiook eretoto te nkanasa.”

English: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninche, “Ore enaba anaa enidolidolo aa sidai te intae naas nanu.” Neaku eitashe olaiguanani te mbata e kishomi, ina kata eruko enjore pooki aapuo too maa iip o too nkalifuni.

English: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
Masaai: Neitanap olaiguanani Yoab o Abishai o Itai, ajoki, “Emintaas entorrono te nkaraki nanu ilo barnoti Absalom.” Nening iltung'ana pooki eisho olaiguanani nkitanapat lelo arikok pooki le njore tiaalo Absalom.

English: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
Masaai: Neaku eipang'a enjore alo ong'ata aarare Israel; neitayuni olarrabal tiaatua entim e Efraim.

English: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
Masaai: Nemiri iltung'ana le Israel teine isinkan le Daudi nesapuku enkidaaroto teine ina olong, iltung'ana nkalifuni tikitam.

English: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
Masaai: Neidapashakino olarrabal oriong enkop pooki; neinos entim iltung'ana kumok ina olong alang olalem.

English: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
Masaai: Nediding Absalom isinkan le Daudi. Nekedito apa Absalom enyumpu enye, nelo enyumpu aim abori ilng'osil sapuki lo lchani neng'amari endukuya too lng'osil, neing'uari ninye eililio to lgam; ore ina nyumpu apa natii abori ninye nelo.

English: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
Masaai: Nedol oltung'ani obo, neliki Yoab, “Ng'ura, atoduaa nanu Absalom eisiong'a to lchani.”

English: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.
Masaai: Nejoki Yoab ilo tung'ani otiaka ninye, “Kainyoo itoduaa iyie ninye! Kainyoo naa pee eitu iosh ninye teine asulaki enkop? Anaata naaji ashipa nanu naaisho iyie mpisai tomon e nkosholai o enkimeita.”

English: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
Masaai: Kake etiaka ilo tung'ani Yoab, “Ore naaji ninye hoo te naning nanu te nkaina ai enkiroishi oo mpisai nkalifuni tomon e nkosholai, maitorioo nanu enkaina ai aar olayioni lo laiguanani; amu ore te ning'oto ang nikintanapa iyie olaiguanani o Abishai o Itai, ejo, ‘Ore te nkaraki nanu entomitu ilo barnoti Absalom.’

English: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
Masaai: Ore sii enkae, tenaa naaji kaitaasa nanu enkishui enye entorrono (nemetii entoki naisudoro to laiguanani) anaata indim iyie makewan atekepari.”

English: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
Masaai: Nejo Yoab, “Maitoki nanu aiturraa enkata aiko nji te nebo iyie.” Neyau ninye iremeta uni te nkaina enye neibitaki ninche oltau le Absalom, eton eishu to lchani.

English: And ten young men that bare Joab's armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
Masaai: Ore ilbarnot tomon anapak loo masaa o larrabal e Yoab, neman ninche Absalom neosh ninye near ninye metua.

English: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
Masaai: Neosh Yoab emowuo nepuonu iltimito aashukunye te mirata oo Siraeli amu etomitikio Yoab ninche.

English: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
Masaai: Neitayu ninche Absalom, nenang'aki ninye atua engumoto sapuk ti atua entim, nesot te shumata ninye osototi sapuk loo soito, neisik Israel pooki, pooki ng'ae alo enkang enye.

English: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king's dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom's place.
Masaai: Ore apa Absalom eton eishu neitobiraka kewan eng'ape osoit natii atua oerata lo Laiguanani, amu etejo ninye, “Maata nanu olayioni oshum enkarna ai metadamuni.” Neipotie ina ng'ape kewan, naa keji enadamunyeki Absalom o metabaiki ena olong.

English: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.
Masaai: Nejo Ahimaas olayioni le Sadok, “Nchooki nanu maipirrio, pee aya ilomon sidain enetii olaiguanani nchere etalakua Olaitoriani ninye aitung'uaa engolon oo lmang'ati lenyena.”

English: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead.
Masaai: Nejoki Yoab ninye, “Miya iyie ilomon taata; indim iyie aawa lomon ae olong, kake ore taata miya iyie lomon, amu etua olayioni lo laiguanani.”

English: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab ajoki ilo tung'ani le Kushi, “Shomo tiaaki olaiguanani ina nitoduaa.” Neirrugo Olkushi te dukuya Yoab, nekuet.

English: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?
Masaai: Neitoki Ahimaas olayioni le Sadok ajoki Yoab, “Nchoo etiu enatiu, nchooki sii nanu maipirrio asujaa Olkushi.” Nejoki Yoab, “Kainyoo iyie pee impirri, olayioni lai, idolita ajo mitum iyie olerrinyore too lomon?”

English: But howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Nchoo eaku enaaku, aipirri ake.” Neaku etiaka ninye, “Mpirrio.” Neipirri Ahimaas te nkoitoi e nkisiajata negiroo ilo Kushi.

English: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
Masaai: Netonita apa Daudi te rishata oo nchomito are; neilep olarriponi alo shumata enkishomi te mbata e suntai, ore ake pee eshumu nkonyek enyena neing'orisho, nedol oltung'ani oipirri openy.

English: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
Masaai: Neipotisho olarriponi neliki olaiguanani. Nejo olaiguanani, “Tenaa ninye ake, netii ilomon sidain enkutuk enye.” Nelotu ninye anyiku netaanu.

English: And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
Masaai: Nedol olarriponi likae tung'ani ekuetu; neipotisho olarriponi te nkishomi nejo, “Ng'ura ekuetu likae tung'ani openy!” Nejo olaiguanani, “Ilomon sidain sii ninye eyau.”

English: And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.
Masaai: Nejo olarriponi, “Amen ajo ore enkuetata ole dukuya naa kenyaanyukie enkuetata e Ahimaas olayioni le Sadok.” Nejo olaiguanani, “Oltung'ani supat ninye naa kelotu ayau ilomon sidain.”

English: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
Masaai: Neishiraki Ahimaas olaiguanani ajo, “Eseriani.” Neirrugo ninye te dukuya olaiguanani nebaiki enkomom enye enkop, nejo, “Meisisi Olaitoriani Enkai ino, laa ninye oishooyie lelo tung'ana ootekepari aarare olkitok lai olaiguanani!”

English: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Eisidain mbaa ti alo ilo barnoti Absalom?” Newalu Ahimaas ejo, “Ore pee eirriwaa Yoab osinka lino, nadol enking'oling'ol sapuk, kake mayiolo nanu ajo kainyoo.”

English: And the king said unto him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Mbelekenyau, ntasho tene.” Neaku eitasho ninye te mbata, neitashe aitirring'a.

English: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, nelotu Olkushiti; nejo ilo Kushiti, “Ilomon sidain to lkitok lai olaiguanani! Amu kitokordua iyie Olaitoriani ena olong aitung'uaa engolon e pooki apa likitudumakinote iyie.”

English: And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Olkushiti, “Eisidain mbaa ti alo ilo barnoti Absalom?” Newal ilo Kushiti ajo, “Metaa ilmang'ati lo lkitok lai olaiguanani, o pooki likidumakino aarare iyie te ntorroni, etiu anaa ilo barnoti.”

English: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
Masaai: Nenyamalu olaiguanani oleng, neilep alo olgilata otii shumata kishomi neishir; naa ore eloito, nejo ninye, “Oi olayioni lai Absalom, olayioni lai, olayioni lai Absalom! Enyor naa katua nanu te rishata ino, Absalom, olayioni lai, olayioni lai!”

English: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
Masaai: Netiaakaki apa Yoab, “Ng'ura, eishirita olaiguanani neisina te nkaraki Absalom.”

English: And the victory that day was turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.
Masaai: Neaku eibelekenyaki enkishuroto e njore ina olong metaa olkiyioi too ltung'ana pooki; amu etoning'o iltung'ana ina olong, “Eisinanuo olaiguanani te nkaraki olayioni lenye.”

English: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
Masaai: Nepurrokino iltung'ana ina olong anaa enapurrokino iltung'ana atua ootukurrutua ekueta to larrabal.

English: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!
Masaai: Neimulumul olaiguanani enkomom enye, neishir olaiguanani to ltoilo sapuk, “Oi olayioni lai Absalom, Oi Absalom, olayioni lai, olayioni lai.”

English: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;
Masaai: Nelotu Yoab atua aji enetii olaiguanani, nejo, “Imulumula iyie taata te nkurruna nkomomi oo sinkan linono pooki, laa ninche ooitajeutuo ena olong enkishui ino, o enkishui oo layiok linono o ntoyie inono, o enkishui oo nkituaak inono o nkapiak inono,

English: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.
Masaai: te nkaraki ninyor iyie lelo likimba iyie nimba lelo likinyor iyie. Amu imbalunye iyie taata nchere, ore larikok le njore o sinkan naa pesho te iyie; amu ore taata adol nanu ajo, tenaa naaji keishu Absalom nikituata iyiook pooki taata, anaata ishipa iyie.

English: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.
Masaai: Ore naa taata tudumunye, shomo auluo irorie te supato isinkan linono; amu anya nanu olmumai to Laitoriani, ti nimilo iyie, meton ninye oltung'ani obo te nebo iyie ena kewarie; naa keaku ena torrono oleng te iyie alang entorroni apa naewuo shumata iyie ebaiki kitisho ino o metabaiki taata.”

English: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.
Masaai: Nedumunye olaiguanani, netonie olorika lenye te kishomi. Nelikini iltung'ana pooki aajoki, “Ng'ura, etonita olaiguanani te kishomi”; nepuonu iltung'ana pooki dukuya olaiguanani. Ore apa Israel neisika pooki tung'ani alo enkang enye.

English: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana pooki neing'oling'ola ti atua iloshon pooki loo Siraeli ejo, “Etokordua iyiook olaiguanani aitung'uaa enkaina oo lmang'ati lang, neitajeuo iyiook aitung'uaa enkaina oo Lfilisti; ore taata neisika alo te nkop aing'uaa Absalom.

English: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?
Masaai: Kake ore Absalom, laa ninye kitubukokitio eilata aaput meitoria iyiook, netua to larrabal. Ore naa taata kainyoo pee mijojo intae ae ti alo enchukunoto o laiguanani?”

English: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, even to his house.
Masaai: Neirriwaa olaiguanani Daudi olkilikuai lenye enetii Sadok o Abiata lelo apolosak nejo, “Entiaaki ilpayiani le Yuda, ‘Kainyoo pee iakuku ile bayie te nchukokinoto o laiguanani enkaji enye, eidipa ororei le Israel pooki aeu enetii olaiguanani?

English: Ye are my brethren, ye are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
Masaai: Irara intae iltung'ana laainei, irara intae o loito lai o sesen lai; kainyoo pee iakuku ile siadi te nchukunoto o laiguanani?’

English: And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
Masaai: Naa tiaaki Amasa, ‘Aimira iyie oltoilo lai o sesen lai? Nchoo eiko neijia Enkai te nanu, neitulusoo sii, ti nimira iyie olkitok le njore ai ebaiki taata te rishata e Yoab.’ ”

English: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.
Masaai: Neibelekeny ninye oltau loo ltung'ana le Yuda netiu anaa oltung'ani obo; neaku eirriwaitie ninche ororei enetii olaiguanani ejo, “Tushukunye, o sinkan linono pooki.”

English: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.
Masaai: Neaku etushukunye olaiguanani alotu Yordan; nelotu Yuda Gilgal anang'are olaiguanani neriku olaiguanani aaitalang'u Yordan.

English: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
Masaai: Ore Shimei olayioni le Gera, ilo lo losho le Benchamen, oing'uaa Bahurim, neisarisaru adou te nebo iltung'ana le Yuda pee enang'are olaiguanani Daudi;

English: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
Masaai: ore te nebo ninye netii iltung'ana enkalifu ooing'uaa Benchamen. Ore Siba osinka le nkaji e Saul, te nebo ilayiok lenyena tomon o imiet, o sinkan lenyena tikitam, nekuet aadoyio aapuo Yordan dukuya olaiguanani,

English: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;
Masaai: nelang ninche te lang'ata aariku enkaji o laiguanani, neas ninche ina nayieu ninye. Ore Shimei olayioni le Gera nebatata te dukuya olaiguanani, etaa kejo ninye pee elang Yordan,

English: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
Masaai: nejoki olaiguanani, “Mincho olkitok lai aaibung nanu te ntorroni arashu edamu eneikuna osinka lino pee eas entorrono ina olong apa naing'uaa olkitok lai olaiguanani Yerusalem; mincho olaiguanani enap too ndamunot enyena.

English: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
Masaai: Amu eyiolo osinka lino nchere ataasa nanu eng'oki; metaa, ng'ura, aewuo nanu ena olong, ole dukuya te nkaji pooki e Yosef otadowuo alotu anang'are olkitok lai olaiguanani.”

English: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD'S anointed?
Masaai: Newaliki Abishai olayioni le Seruiya ajoki, “Aimeari Shimei metua tena, enkaraki netediaa ninye ilo otubukoko Olaitoriani eilata?”

English: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?
Masaai: Kake etejo Daudi, “Kaa nanu aaporoki intae, intae ilayiok le Seruiya, nchere itiuu intae ena olong anaa ilmang'ati te nanu? Keari pooki ng'ae metua te Israel ena olong? Amu aimayiolo nanu nchere ara nanu ena olong olaiguanani le Israel?”

English: Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Shimei, “Miye iyie.” Neisho olaiguanani ninye olmumai lenye.

English: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace.
Masaai: Ore Mefiboshet olayioni le Saul nedou alotu anang'are olaiguanani; neitu ninye eituku nkejek enyena, arashu eitobir olmunyei lenye, arashu eituku nkilani enyena, ebaiki enkolong apa nashomo olaiguanani o metabaiki enkolong naewuo ninye ashukunye te seriani.

English: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?
Masaai: Ore pee elotu ninye aing'uaa Yerusalem anang'are olaiguanani, nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kainyoo pee eitu ilo te nebo nanu Mefiboshet?”

English: And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant is lame.
Masaai: Newal ninye ajo, “Olkitok lai, olaiguanani, aateleja apa nanu osinka lai; amu etiaka osinka lino ninye, ‘Irotokoki nanu osikiria, pee atum atakedo nalo te nebo olaiguanani.’ Amu olmaima osinka lino.

English: And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in thine eyes.
Masaai: Etakaldayie ninye osinka lino to lkitok lai olaiguanani. Kake ore olkitok lai olaiguanani netiu anaa olmalaika le Nkai; taasa naa ina nidol aa sidai te iyie.

English: For all of my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?
Masaai: Amu ore enkaji pooki e papa lai netaa ninche iltung'ana ooishiaakino keeya te dukuya olkitok lai olaiguanani; kake itipika apa iyie osinka lino atua lelo oodaa te mesa ino. Kainyoo naa ai sipata naata nanu, naa, pee aishiraki olaiguanani?”

English: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kainyoo pee iro oleng mbaa inono? Atudung'o nanu; ore iyie o Siba naa iorioro enkop.”

English: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.
Masaai: Nejoki Mefiboshet olaiguanani, “Oi nchoo ninye eya pooki, etaa eewuo olkitok lai olaiguanani ang te seriani.”

English: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
Masaai: Ore apa Barsilai le Giliad netadowuo alotu aing'uaa Rogelim; nelo ninye te nebo olaiguanani Yordan, pee eitarioo ninye aitalang Yordan.

English: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
Masaai: Ore apa Barsilai naa oltung'ani otamorua oleng, ilarin ntomoni isiet; te moruao neishoo apa ninye olaiguanani endaa eton etonita te Mahanaim; amu oltung'ani apa karsis ninye.

English: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Barsilai, “Wou talang'u te nebo nanu, naa kaagolie nanu iyie te nebo nanu te Yerusalem.”

English: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?
Masaai: Kake etiaka Barsilai olaiguanani, “Kailarin aja nanu eton aishu, metaa kailep nanu alo te nebo olaiguanani Yerusalem?

English: I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
Masaai: Ara nanu ena olong oloo larin ntomoni isiet; kaidim nanu atayiolo ajo kainyoo sidai naa kainyoo neme sidai? Keidim osinka lino aishamisham ina nanya ninye arashu enaok ninye? Keton nanu aidim ainining'o oltoilo loo lewa ooranyisho o nkituaak naaranyisho? Kainyoo naa pee eaku osinka lino olola oponari tolkitok lai olaiguanani?

English: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
Masaai: Kelo osinka lino enkiti wueji te nkoitoi te lido kekun Yordan te nebo olaiguanani. Kainyoo pee aalaaki nanu olaiguanani to lerrinyore oba nji?

English: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
Masaai: Aatasayia nchoo osinka lino eshuko, pee atum nanu atua ti atua enkanasa ai makewan, te netaaniki enkurare e papa lai o yieyio lai. Kake nele osinka lino Kimham; nchoo ninye elo te nebo olkitok lai olaiguanani; nintaas ninye enaba anaa enidol aa sidai te iyie.”

English: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
Masaai: Newaliki olaiguanani ajoki, “Kelo Kimham te nebo nanu, naa kaitaas nanu ninye enaba enaa enidol aa sidai te iyie; ore nena pooki niyieu iyie te nanu naaitaas nanu iyie.”

English: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
Masaai: Nepuo iltung'ana pooki aalang Yordan, nelo olaiguanani alang; neng'utut olaiguanani Barsilai nemayian ninye, neshuko ninye alo enkang enye kewan.

English: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.
Masaai: Nelo olaiguanani dukuya o meshomo Gilgal, nelo Kimham te nebo ninye; ore iltung'ana pooki le Yuda o lpisiai sii loo ltung'ana loo Siraeli, neriku olaiguanani te nkoitoi enye.

English: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David's men with him, over Jordan?
Masaai: Nepuonu iltung'ana pooki loo Siraeli enetii olaiguanani, nejoki olaiguanani, “Kainyoo pee kitupurroitie iyie ilalashera lang iltung'ana le Yuda, neyau olaiguanani o enkaji enye aaitalang'u Yordan, o ltung'ana pooki le Daudi te nebo ninye?”

English: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king's cost? or hath he given us any gift?
Masaai: Newaliki iltung'ana pooki le Yuda lelo tung'ana loo Siraeli ejo, “Enkaraki naa olo lgilata onyikita iyiook. Kainyoo naa pee igoro tena bae? Eikitadaate iyiook pooki te nkinyang'a olaiguanani? Anaa tenaa keishoo ninye iyiook ae enkishoroto?”

English: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
Masaai: Newaliki iltung'ana loo Siraeli iltung'ana le Yuda nejo, “Kiata iyiook irubat tomon to laiguanani, ore sii te Daudi nikiata iyiook nkumok aitulusoo intae. Kainyoo naa pee itemena intae iyiook? Aimikira iyiook ile dukuya ooiroro pee eshukuni olaiguanani?” Kake ore apa rorei loo ltung'ana le Yuda naa kepe alang irorei loo ltung'ana loo Siraeli.

English: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
Masaai: Ore apa, netumi oltung'ani lemeeta tipat, oji enkarna enye Sheba, olayioni le Bikiri, lo losho le Benchamen neosh ninye emowuo nejo, “Mikiata iyiook erubata te Daudi nimikiata iyiook enjung'ore to layioni le Yese; shomo pooki tung'ani olng'obor lino, iyie Israel!”

English: So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Neaku etung'uaitie iltung'ana pooki loo Siraeli Daudi, nesuj Sheba olayioni le Bikiri; kake etusuja iltung'ana le Yuda olaiguanani lenye aakurraki ebaiki Yordan o metabaiki Yerusalem.

English: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.
Masaai: Nelotu Daudi enkaji enye te Yerusalem; neya olaiguanani nkapiak tomon apa naatung'uayie meing'ura enkaji, nepik ninche atua enkaji narripitoi, neitoti ninche, kake eitu elo atua enetii ninche. Neaku eikenoyioki ninche o metabaiki enkolong e keeya enye, etoni anaa nkolia.

English: Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Amasa, “Mpoto iltung'ana le Yuda te nebo meetu enatii ti atua nkolong'i uni, nitii iyie ene makewan.”

English: So Amasa went to assemble the men of Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
Masaai: Neaku eshomo Amasa aipot Yuda; kake eimutie ninye aitogiroo enkata apa natudung'okoki apa nategelakaki ninye.

English: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Abishai, “Ore taata keitaas iyiook Sheba olayioni le Bikiri entorrono alang Absalom; iwa isinkan lo lkitok lino tusujai ninye, meisho ake kewan nkanas naasheta isunta too soito nepik iyiook enyamali.”

English: And there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
Masaai: Neipang aapuo aasujaa Abishai, Yoab o lelo Sheriti o lelo Peleti, o lelo tung'ana pooki magil; neipang ninche aapuo aaing'uaa Yerusalem aasujaa Sheba olayioni le Bikiri.

English: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab's garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
Masaai: Ore etii ninche osoit sapuk otii Gibeon, nelotu Amasa anang'are ninche. Neishopito apa Yoab olkila lo ltung'ani le njore, ore ti oriong ninye netii enkimeita te nebo olalem ti atua enchashur eteenaki aakurraki te mpolos enye; ore eloito ninye dukuya nedoyio.

English: And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
Masaai: Nejoki Yoab Amasa, “Iserian iyie, olalashe lai?” Neibung Yoab Amasa olmunyei lenye te nkaina enye e tatene pee eng'utut ninye.

English: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab's hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
Masaai: Kake eitu edol Amasa olalem otii enkaina e Yoab; neaku ninye etaremie Yoab ninye enkoshoke, nebuloki imonyit enyena enkop, neye ninye eitu eigilieki ai oshoto. Ore Yoab o Abishai olalashe lenye nesujaa Sheba olayioni le Bikiri.

English: And one of Joab's men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab.
Masaai: Ore obo loo ltungana le Yoab, neitashe te mbata e Amasa nejo, “Ore olonyor Yoab anaa ole nkalo e Daudi, nchoo ninye esujaa Yoab.”

English: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.
Masaai: Ore Amasa neirrag akurro tiaatua o sarge lenye te mpolos enkoitoi. Ore pooki ng'ae ogiroo, nedol ninye, neitashe; ore pee edol ilo tung'ani ajo eitasheito iltung'ana pooki, nenap ninye Amasa aitung'uaa enkoitoi apik ong'ata, nenang'aki enkila shumata ninye.

English: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eyae aaitung'uaa enkoitoi, nepuo iltung'ana pooki aasuj Yoab esujaa olayioni le Bikiri.

English: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Bethmaachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.
Masaai: Neim Sheba atua iloshon pooki loo Isiraeli o meshomo Abel e Bet-maka, ore lelo Bikiri pooki neiturrurro, nesujaa ninye atua.

English: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
Masaai: Ore lelo tung'ana pooki apa ootii te nebo Yoab nepuonu aang'adu ninye ti atua Abel e Bet-maka; neitayu ninche olkiu te mbata e nkang, neitashe ninye aipirakinore esuntai; neoshito apa ninche esuntai pee euroo.

English: Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
Masaai: Neipotisho enkitok ang'eni ti atua enkanasa ejo, “Entoning! Entoning! Entiaaki Yoab, ‘Wou ene, pee aatum nanu airorie iyie.’ ”

English: And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
Masaai: Nelotu ninye ataaniki ninye; nejo ina kitok, “Ira iyie Yoab?” Newaliki ninye, “Ara nanu.” Neitoki ajoki ninye, “Toning'o irorei le sinka ino.” Newaliki ninye, “Aning'ito nanu.”

English: Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.
Masaai: Neitoki ninye ajo, “Ore apa naa keji, ‘Nchoo ninche eikilikuanu enkoo te Abel’; neidip ninche olomoni.

English: I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?
Masaai: Ara nanu nabo e nekua nemeetayie olomang'ati neisiligayu too Siraeli amaa ing'oru iyie aidaikie enkanasa naa ninye ng'otonye ti atua Israel; kainyoo pee iijoo iyie ina jung'ore o Laitoriani?”

English: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.
Masaai: Newal Yoab, “Kikoino maatalama ena nchere kaijoo nanu arashu aidaikie!

English: The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.
Masaai: Mesipa ina. Kake oltung'ani le nkop oo ldoinyo e Efraim, oji Sheba olayioni le Bikiri, oilepie enkaina enye aarare olaiguanani Daudi; enchoru ninye ake, naa kalo nanu aing'uaa enkanasa.” Nejoki ina kitok Yoab, “Ng'ura, eikinang'akini iyie endukuya enye aaitadooki te suntai.”

English: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
Masaai: Nelo ina kitok enetii iltung'ana pooki te ng'eno enye. Nedung'u ninche endukuya e Sheba olayioni le Bikiri nenang'u auluo enetii Yoab. Neosh ninye emowuo, neidapasha ninche aaing'uaa enkanasa, oltung'ani ake nelo enkang enye. Nerrinyo Yoab alo Yerusalem enetii olaiguanani.

English: Now Joab was over all the host of Israel: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites:
Masaai: Naa Yoab apa olkitok le njore pooki e Israel; ore Benaia olayioni le Yehoida naa ninye olkitok loo Lkereti o Lpelesi;

English: And Adoram was over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder:
Masaai: naa Adoram oitasheiki esiaai oo nkaik; naa Yehoshafat olayioni le Ahilud apa olaigeroni;

English: And Sheva was scribe: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:
Masaai: naa Shefa olasirani; naa Sadok o Abiata apa ilapolosak;

English: And Ira also the Jairite was a chief ruler about David.
Masaai: ore apa Ira ilo Yairiti naa olapolosani sii ninye le Daudi.

English: Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the LORD. And the LORD answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.
Masaai: Netii apa olameyu too nkolong'i e Daudi too larin okuni, to lari ake o to lari, neing'oru Daudi enkomom o Laitoriani. Nejo Olaitoriani, “Etii entorroni o sarge shumata Saul o shumata enkaji enye, enkaraki natara Ilgibioni metuata.”

English: And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
Masaai: Neaku eipoto olaiguanani Ilgibioni. Ore apa Ilgibioni neme iloo ltung'ana le Israel, kake ilo lpisiai loo Lamori; hoo neinosa iltung'ana le Israel olmumai pee eleku ninche, etonyuaa Saul ear ninche metuata te ina nyuata enye te nkaraki iltung'ana le Israel o Yuda.

English: Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the LORD?
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi lelo Gibioni, “Kaa nanu aitaas intae? Naa kaji nanu aikunu enkipooto, pee itumutumu intae aatamayian enjung'ore o Laitoriani?”

English: And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.
Masaai: Nejoki ilgibioni ninye, “Mme mbae e nkosholai arashu sahabu erishata ang o Saul arashu enkaji enye; neme enaang pee kiar oltung'ani metua te Israel.” Nejo ninye, “Ijojo intae pee aitaas aa nanu intae?”

English: And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,
Masaai: Nejoki ninche olaiguanani, “Ore ilo tung'ani apa otumuta iyiook neitobir pee eidaikie iyiook, metaa mikitum iyiook ewueji ti atua enkop pooki oo Siraeli.

English: Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the LORD in Gibeah of Saul, whom the LORD did choose. And the king said, I will give them.
Masaai: Nchoo meishori ilayiok lenyena oopishana pee kisiong iyiook ninche te dukuya Olaitoriani te Gibeon to ldoinyo lo Laitoriani.” Nejo olaiguanani, “Kaishoru nanu ninche.”

English: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD'S oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
Masaai: Kake etelekua olaiguanani Mefiboshet, olayioni lo layioni le Saul, Yonatan, te nkaraki olmumai lo Laitoriani apa otii erishata ninche, o erishata e Daudi, o Yonatan olayioni le Saul.

English: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:
Masaai: Neya olaiguanani ilayiok oare le Rispa entito e Aia apa naa ninye etoikio Saul, Armon o Mefiboshet; o layiok imiet le Merab entito e Saul laa ninche etoikio Adriel olayioni le Barsilai ilo Meholati;

English: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the LORD: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.
Masaai: neishooyo ninche apik atua nkaik oo Lgibioni; neilili ninche teilo doinyo te dukuya Olaitoriani, ore ninche pokira oopishana neidak te nebo. Neari ninche metuata too nkolong'i e dukuya e nkisampuare, te nkiterunoto e nkisampuare e shairi.

English: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
Masaai: Neitoki Rispa entito e Aia aya ilkuniyiani neisalaashaki te ndapidapoi ebaiki enkiterunoto e nkisampuare o metaba anaa neshaiki enchan ninche eing'uaa shumata; neitu ninye eisho imotonyi o loing'ang'e epuonu aadoiki ninche te ndama, arashu ing'uesi e ong'ata te nkewarie.

English: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elikini Daudi enataasa Rispa entito e Aia ina apiani e Saul,

English: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of  Jabeshgilead, which had stolen them from the street of Bethshan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
Masaai: nelo Daudi aitayu iloik le Saul o loik lo layioni lenye Yonatan ti atua iltung'ana le Yabesh-gilead, apa ootupurroitie ninche to lkurroto otumoreki te Bet-shan, te ine apa neililiyie Ilfilisti ninche, te ina olong apa nataara Ilfilisti Saul metua te Gilboa;

English: And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
Masaai: neyau ninye ailepunye te ine iloik le Saul o loik lo layioni lenye Yonatan; neiturrur ninche iloik le lelo apa oo lilioki.

English: And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.
Masaai: Nenukaa ninche iloik le Saul o layioni lenye Yonatan te nkop e Benchamen te Sela, ti atua enkurare e Kish papaai lenye; neas ninche nena pooki naaitanapishe olaiguanani. Ore te siadi ina nening Enkai eomonokinoto te nkaraki enkop.

English: Moreover the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.
Masaai: Nenyaakitia apa Ilfilisti aata olarrabal o Israel, nedoyio Daudi alo te nebo isinkan lenyena nearare ninche Ilfilisti; neilepunye Daudi.

English: And Ishbibenob, which was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.
Masaai: Ore Ishbi-benob, obo apa le ishoi e lelo tung'ana sapuki laa shekeli iip o suyai enkirroishi e mpere enye, oenita olalem ng'ejuk, neing'oru pee ear Daudi metua.

English: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.
Masaai: Kake eewuo Abishai olayioni le Seruiya aretu, nerasaki ilo Filisti near ninye metua. Neitirrishaki iltung'ana le Daudi ninye aajoki, “Mintoki aekata iyie aipang alo te nebo iyiook olarrabal, pee miar ake olkilang'ilang'et le Israel.”

English: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was of the sons of the giant.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena neitoki atii olarrabal apa o Lfilisti te Gob; neari metua Sibekai ol Husati Saf, laa ninye apa obo le ishoi e lelo tung'ana sapuki.

English: And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
Masaai: Neetae ake sii apa olarrabal o Lfilisti te Gob; neari Elhanan olayioni le Yaareoregim, le Betlehem near metua Goliat le Giti oba enchata e mpere enye anaa embokishi o lashetani.

English: And there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.
Masaai: Neetae sii apa olarrabal te Gas, teine apa netii oltung'ani sapuk oado oata lkimojik ile te pooki aina, o nkimojik ile te pooki keju, tikitam o ong'uan esiana e pooki; naa ole ishoi sii apa ninye e lelo tung'ana sapuki.

English: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea the brother of David slew him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edek ninye Israel near ninye metua Yonatan olayioni le Shimei, ilo alashe le Daudi.

English: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
Masaai: Ore kulo oong'uan naa ile ishoi e lelo tung'ana apa sapuki ootii Gas; near Daudi te nkaina enye o te nkaina oo sinkan lenyena metuata.

English: And David spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day that the LORD had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:
Masaai: Neirorie Daudi Olaitoriani irorei lele sinkolio ina olong natalakua ninye Olaitoriani aitung'uaa enkaina oo lmang'ati lenyena pooki, neitung'uaa enkaina e Saul.

English: And he said, The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Olaitoriani endapidapoi ai, naa osempewuet lai,

English: The God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.
Masaai: Enkai ai, endapidapoi ai, laa ninye esarunoto ai elong'o ai o emowuo enjeunoto ai, oltim lai o enkisudoroto ai, Olaitajeunoni lai; kintajeu iyie nanu aitung'uaa entorroni.

English: I will call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
Masaai: Aipoto nanu Olaitoriani, laa ninye eishiaakino nerrepi, naaitajeuoki nanu too lmang'ati laainei.

English: When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid;
Masaai: “Amu aamanita nanu ilopir le keeya, naapik nanu indoorot e ntorroni enkuretisho.

English: The sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;
Masaai: Aarrueshita nanu nkeenta e nemeneng'a, naaluaakino nanu irresheta le keeya.

English: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my God: and he did hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry did enter into his ears.
Masaai: “Ore ti atua osina lai aipoto nanu Olaitoriani; Enkai ai nanu aipoto. Te nkaji enye etoning'o ninye oltoilo lai, nelotu enkishirata ai nkiyiaa enyena.

English: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of heaven moved and shook, because he was wroth.
Masaai: “Kaae neikirikira enkop neigirigiro; ore ilkitamanyunot le shumata, neigirigiro, enkaraki natagore ninye.

English: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it.
Masaai: Neilep empuruo alo keper eing'uaa nkumeishin enyena, nepuku enkima nanyaisho te nkutuk enye; nkuk naaishu naayupuyup epuku te ninye.

English: He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under his feet.
Masaai: Neirrugu ninye shumata, nelotu adou; netii emisimisi nairrusha abori nkejek enyena.

English: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
Masaai: Etakedo ninye enchumata olkerubi, nelo tiaai; etoduaaki ninye te nchumata oo naipuko osiwuo.

English: And he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies.
Masaai: Eishoo enaimin metamana ninye, neman ninye nkatampo naairrusha o nkariak naaiturrurro.

English: Through the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled.
Masaai: Nepuku te ina wang'an natii dukuya ninye nkuk e nkima naayupuyup.

English: The LORD thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.
Masaai: Etadara Olaitoriani te shumata, ore ilo otii shumata oleng neitayu oltoilo lenye.

English: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ninye mbaa, neidapash ninche; te nkiwuang'ata eterewa ninche.

English: And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
Masaai: Nedoli kop e naiposha, neirragieki ilkitamanyunot le nkop meirraga aaibalayu, te nkisikong'ata o Laitoriani, te nkutata e nkiyang'et oo nkumeishin enyena.

English: He sent from above, he took me; he drew me out of many waters;
Masaai: “Neitoriou ninye te shumata naaya ninye nanu, naaitayu ti atua nkariak kumok.

English: He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
Masaai: Aatokordua te nkaina o lmang'atinta lai ogol, aitung'uaa lelo apa laaiba nanu; amu kegol apa oleng te nanu.

English: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.
Masaai: Eetuo ninche shumata nanu te nkolong ai e nyamali; kake etaa Olaitoriani enkigarakinoto ai.

English: He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Masaai: Aayaua ninye nanu atua ewueji nelala; aatokordua amu kaashipakino ninye nanu.

English: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
Masaai: “Aaitaasa nanu Olaitoriani te risioroto e supatisho ai; te risioroto e ina nemeiduruk nkaik aainei aaitaasa ninye.

English: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
Masaai: Amu aibung'a nkoitoi o Laitoriani, neitu nanu te ntorroni aing'uaa Enkai ai.

English: For all his judgments were before me: and as for his statutes, I did not depart from them.
Masaai: Amu ore nkitanapat enyena pooki netii dukuya nanu, ore too nkitanapat enyena neitu nanu aibelekenya.

English: I was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity.
Masaai: Maata apa nanu eleyiata te dukuya ninye, narrip nanu kewan te ntorroni.

English: Therefore the LORD hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.
Masaai: Metaa aaitaasa nanu Olaitoriani te risioroto e supatisho ai, te risioroto e ina nemaiduruk nanu too nkonyek enyena.

English: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, and with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright.
Masaai: “Ore te ilo oisiligayu nintodol kewan ajo isiligayu; ore to ltung'ani le meeta eleyiata nintodol kewan ajo miata eleyiata;

English: With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury.
Masaai: Ore te ilo shaat nintodol iyie kewan ajo ira sii iyie shaat, ore ilo lemeitoriori nintodol iyie ajo ira olo larrabal.

English: And the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.
Masaai: Ikordu iyie iltung'ana oobor, kake etii nkonyek inono shumata iloowuasa pee intadou ninche.

English: For thou art my lamp, O LORD: and the LORD will lighten my darkness.
Masaai: Ee, ira iyie oltaa lai, Olaitoriani, naa keitawang Enkai ai enaimin ai.

English: For by thee I have run through a troop: by my God have I leaped over a wall.
Masaai: Ee, te iyie aidim nanu aidaikie oltim, naa te Nkai ai nanu aidim aida esuntai.

English: As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him.
Masaai: Ore ena Ai - kesipa enkoitoi enye; ore enkisiligata o Laitoriani naa keibalayu ajo kesipa; elong'o ninye te pooki ooing'oru enkisudoroto te ninye.

English: For who is God, save the LORD? and who is a rock, save our God?
Masaai: “Amu kaing'ae Enkai, neme Olaitoriani? Naa kaing'ae endapidapoi, neme Enkai ang?

English: God is my strength and power: and he maketh my way perfect.
Masaai: Ore ena Ai naa enkisudoroto ai nagol, netaseriana ninye enkoitoi ai.

English: He maketh my feet like hinds' feet: and setteth me upon my high places.
Masaai: Neitagol ninye nkejek aainei anaa entarakuet, naagolie ninye mabatata too neeika.

English: He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.
Masaai: Neiteng'en ninye nkaik aainei to larrabal, metaa keriu nkaik aainei enkawuo osuyai.

English: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.
Masaai: Kinchoo iyie nanu elong'o e njeunoto ino, naaitaa nanu eretoto ino kitok.

English: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip.
Masaai: Kinchoo iyie nanu ewueji nelala too roruat aainei ti abori nanu, neitu eideketari nkejek aainei;

English: I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; and turned not again until I had consumed them.
Masaai: atusujayie nanu ilmang'ati laainei naidaikie ninche, neitu ashukunye o metaba anaa neishunye ninche.

English: And I have consumed them, and wounded them, that they could not arise: yea, they are fallen under my feet.
Masaai: Aishua nanu ninche; ataremo nanu ninche aipang'ie, metaa eitu ninche edumunye; etabatatate ti abori nkejek aainei.

English: For thou hast girded me with strength to battle: them that rose up against me hast thou subdued under me.
Masaai: Amu kiterretena nanu te ngolon te nkaraki olarrabal; nincho iyie ilmang'ati laainei meimiso ti abori nanu.

English: Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
Masaai: Inchoo iyie ilmang'ati laainei maaibelekenyaki nkoriong'i enye, lelo laaiba nanu, naidaikie nanu ninche.

English: They looked, but there was none to save; even unto the LORD, but he answered them not.
Masaai: Neing'orisho, kake metii hoo obo oitajeu ninche; eishirakitia ninche Olaitoriani, kake eitu ninye ewaliki ninche.

English: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, and did spread them abroad.
Masaai: Aidong'o nanu ninche naitunyoki ninche enkop anaa esarng'ab e nkoitoi.

English: Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me.
Masaai: “Kintajeuo iyie nanu te lelo tung'ana ootekepari aakeshisho; kitipika nanu mataa endukuya oo loreren; ore apa iltung'ana leitu nanu ayiolou naaisiaai nanu.

English: Strangers shall submit themselves unto me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me.
Masaai: Nepuonu iloo loreren naairr ugokino nanu; ore ake pee aaning'oo nanu, naairuk ninche nanu.

English: Strangers shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their close places.
Masaai: Etapalari iloo loreren, nepuonu eikirikira aaipang'u too nkisudorot enye.

English: The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
Masaai: “Ekeishu Olaitoriani! Meisisi endapidapoi ai! Naa meitubulari enkitoo e Nkai ai, endapidapoi e njeunoto ai.

English: It is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me,
Masaai: Ina Ai naaitalaaka nanu elap neitadou iltung'ana apik abori nanu,

English: And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: thou also hast lifted me up on high above them that rose up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.
Masaai: laa ninye laaitayio nanu aitung'uaa ilmang'ati laainei; naailepie nanu te shumata ilmang'ati laainei, nikikordu iyie nanu aitung'uaa iltung'ana arruok.

English: Therefore I will give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and I will sing praises unto thy name.
Masaai: “Ore tena kaaisis nanu iyie, Olaitoriani, ti atua iloreren, naa karanyaki irrepat e nkarna ino.

English: He is the tower of salvation for his king: and sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore.
Masaai: Nkisulat sapuki eisho ninye olaiguanani lenye, neitodolu enyorrata nauno te ilo lenye obukokino eilata, Daudi o eishoi enye ntarasi.”

English: Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
Masaai: Ore taata kulo ilomon le nkiting'oto le Daudi: Enkitanapata e Daudi, olayioni le Yese, enkitanapata e ilo tung'ani oilepieki aaya shumata, ilo obukokino eilata te Nkai e Yakobo, ilo oranyu isinkolioitin oomelok le Israel:

English: The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
Masaai: “Eirorita enkiyang'et o Laitoriani te nanu, etii ororei lenye olng'ejep lai.

English: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
Masaai: Eiroro Enkai e Israel, aatiaka endapidapoi e Israel: Te neitore oltung'ani te sipata iltung'ana, neitore te uriata e Nkai,

English: And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
Masaai: neitawang'aki ninche anaa ewang'an e nkakenya, anaa enkolong nawang'u tadekenya metii nkatampo, anaa enchan naisho nkujit metubulu te nkop.

English: Although my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.
Masaai: Ee, aimeitashe enkaji ai aiko neijia te Nkai? Amu eitobira ninye te nebo nanu osotua loo ntarasi, eishiaakino too ntokitin pooki netagolieki. Amu aimeidimie ninye metubula eretoto ai pooki o eyieunoto ai?

English: But the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
Masaai: Kake ore iltung'ana lemeeta Enkai, netiu pooki anaa ilkiku ootanang'ayioki; amu meidimi aawaita te nkaina;

English: But the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place.
Masaai: kake ore ilo tung'ani oibung ninche neeta esekenkei o enchata e mpere, nemuti ninche tukul te nkima.”

English: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.
Masaai: Kuna nkarn oo ltung'ana magil apa oata Daudi: Yosheb-bashebet Oltakenoni; kitok apa ninye te lelo okuni, eilepie ninye empere enye aarare iltung'ana iip isiet ootasesekuana ninye te nkata nabo.

English: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
Masaai: Ore oliare te ninye ti atua iltung'ana okuni magil naa Eliesa olayioni le Dodo olayioni le Ahohi. Etii apa ninye te nebo Daudi ina kata pee eiturrurro Ilfilisti to larrabal, neshuko iltung'ana le Israel.

English: He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the LORD wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.
Masaai: Nedumunye ninye near Ilfilisti o meteekunye enkaina enye, neibung'are enkaina enye o lalem lenye; neyau Olaitoriani enkisulata kitok ina olong; nerrinyunye iltung'ana aasujaa ninye pee epur lelo ootasesekuanaki.

English: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines.
Masaai: Ore olosujita ninye naa Shama, olayioni le Agee Olharari. Eiturrurrote Ilfilisti te nebo te Lehi, te ine wueji apa nebore endaa nauno; neisik iltung'ana aailany Ilfilisti.

English: But he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the LORD wrought a great victory.
Masaai: Kake etune ninye aitashe te mpolos e ine, nengoroo ine, nesesekuan Ilfilisti; neyau Olaitoriani enkisulata kitok.

English: And three of the thirty chief went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam: and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
Masaai: Ore okuni loo ltung'ana tomoni uni gelunot nedoyio aapuo, nepuonu enetii Daudi etinyikua enkata e nkisampuare te nkapune e Adulam, ina kata apa etii oltim loo Lfilisti oerata le Refaim.

English: And David was then in an hold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
Masaai: Netii apa Daudi ina kata atua enkisudoroto; ore oltim loo Lfilisti netii Betlehem.

English: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!
Masaai: Nejo te yieunoto, “Oi naaji aaisho nanu oltung'ani enkare naok naing'uaa olchorro le Betlehem otii embata kishomi!”

English: And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the LORD.
Masaai: Neim lelo tung'ana okuni magil atua ilng'oborri loo Lfilisti; neoku enkare te ilo shorro le Betlehem apa otii embata e kishomi, neyaki Daudi. Kake eitu eok; eibukoyie ninye abukoki Olaitoriani,

English: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
Masaai: nejo, “Metalakuana te nanu, Olaitoriani, tenaa kaas nanu ena. Kaok nanu osarge loo ltung'ana ooshomo te mbatisho e nkishui enye?” Neaku meok ninye. Kuna baa etaasa lelo tung'ana okuni magil.

English: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred, and slew them, and had the name among three.
Masaai: Ore apa Abishai, olalashe le Yoab, olayioni le Seruiya, naa ninye olarikoni le tomoni uni. Neilepie ninye enkaina enye aarare iltung'ana iip uni nesesekuan ninche, neisulie enkarna te lelo okuni.

English: Was he not most honourable of three? therefore he was their captain: howbeit he attained not unto the first three.
Masaai: Ninye apa eyioloi oleng te lelo tomoni uni, neaku olarikoni lenye; kake eitu eaku te lelo okuni.

English: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow:
Masaai: Ore apa Benaia olayioni le Yohoida naa oltung'ani opi oleng le Kabseel, olaasani loo nkiasin sapuki; etara ntiamasini are e Moab. Eshomo sii apa adoyio near olng'atuny ti atua engumoto ina kata apa etadowuo empaso e nkirobi.

English: And he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
Masaai: Nesesekuan olmisiri, oltung'ani le nkishaa. Eeta apa ilo Misiri empere te nkaina enye; kake eshomo Benaia enetii ninye te ng'udi enye, newuapaa empere te nkaina o Lmisiri, nesesekuan ninye tempere enye kewan.

English: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty men.
Masaai: Kuna baa etaasa Benaia olayioni le Yehoida, netum enkarna ti atua lelo tung'ana okuni magil.

English: He was more honourable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.
Masaai: Keyioloi apa oleng ti atua lelo tomoni uni, kake eitu elusoo te pokira okuni. Nepik apa Daudi ninye meitasheiki ilarripok lenyena.

English: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Masaai: Ore apa Asahel olalashe le Yoab naa obo le lelo tomoni uni; Elhanan olayioni le Dodo le Betlehem,

English: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Masaai: Shama le Harod, Elika le Harod,

English: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
Masaai: Heles o Lpalti, Ira olayioni le Ikesh le Tekoa,

English: Abiezer the Anethothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Masaai: Abiesa le Anatot, o Mebunai Olhushati,

English: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
Masaai: Salmon Olhohi, o Maharai le Netofa,

English: Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
Masaai: o Heleb olayioni le Baana le Netofa, Itai olayioni le Ribai le Gibea loo Lbenchamen,

English: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
Masaai: Benaia le Piraton, Hidai loo nong'ot e Gaash,

English: Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Masaai: Abilabon le Lbati, Asmafet le Bahurim,

English: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Masaai: Eliaba le Shaalbon, olayioni le Yashen, Yonatan,

English: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
Masaai: Shama Olharari, Ahiam olayioni le Sharar Olharari;

English: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Masaai: Elifelet olayioni le Ahasbai le Maaka, Eliam olayioni le Ahitofel le Gilo,

English: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
Masaai: Hesro le Karmel, Paarai Olabi,

English: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Masaai: Igal olayioni le Natan le Soba, Bani Olgadi,

English: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Masaai: Selek Olamori; Naharai le Be-erot, olanapani loo masaa o larrabal le Yoab olayioni le Seruiya,

English: Ira an Ithrite, Gareb an Ithrite,
Masaai: Ira ilo Tiriti; Gareb ilo Tiriti; Uria ilo Hiti:

English: Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.
Masaai: tomoni uni o opishana pooki.

English: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.
Masaai: Neitoki engoro o Laitoriani ayupuyup te nkaraki Israel, nepik Daudi endamunoto te nkaraki ninche, ejo, “Shomo nkena Israel o Yuda.”

English: For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.
Masaai: Neaku etiaka olaiguanani Yoab o lkituaak le njore, apa ootii te nebo ninye, “Enchom atua iloshon pooki le Israel, ebaiki Dan o metabaiki Beer-sheba, ninkenikene iltung'ana, pee atum atayiolo esiana oo ltung'ana.”

English: And Joab said unto the king, Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yoab olaiguanani, “Metoponai Olaitoriani Enkai ino iltung'ana katitin iip aa kumok anaa enaba, eton edolita nkonyek o lkitok lai olaiguanani; kake kainyoo pee eshipakino olkitok lai olaiguanani ena bae?”

English: Notwithstanding the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
Masaai: Kake etune ororei lo laiguanani te Yoab o too lkituaak le njore. Neaku eshomo Yoab o lkituaak le njore te ine netii olaiguanani aapuo aaiken iltung'ana.

English: And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:
Masaai: Nelang ninche Yordan, neiteru abaiki Aroer, o ebaiki ina anasa natii atua empolos o erata, te nkalo e Gad nelo Yaser.

English: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtimhodshi; and they came to Danjaan, and about to Zidon,
Masaai: Neitoki aapuonu Gilead, o Kadesh ti atua enkop oo Lhiti; nepuonu ninche Dan, nepuo te Dan nemanaa aapuo Sidon,

English: And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah, even to Beersheba.
Masaai: nepuonu enkisudoroto e Turo o nkang'itie oo Lhafi o Lkanaani; neipang ninche aapuo Negeb e Yuda te Beer-sheba.

English: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
Masaai: Neaku ore ake pee eidip ninche aashom enkop pooki, nepuonu ninche Yerusalem te nkiting'oto oo lapaitin ooudo o nkolong'i tikitam.

English: And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.
Masaai: Neisho Yoab esiana e nkikenata oo ltung'ana olaiguanani: ore ti atua Israel netii nkalifuni iip isiet oopi oo tushututua ilalema, ore iltung'ana le Yuda naa nkalifuni iip imiet.

English: And David's heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O LORD, take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
Masaai: Neitanyamal Daudi oltau lenye ena kata eidipa aikena iltung'ana. Nejoki Daudi Olaitoriani, “Ataasa nanu eng'oki sapuk tena nataasa. Kake ore taata, Olaitoriani, aatoomono nanu iyie, iwuang'ie entorroni to sinka lino; amu ataasa nanu te modai.”

English: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,
Masaai: Ore ake pee einyototo Daudi tadekenya, nelotu ororei lo Laitoriani enetii oloiboni oji Gad, ilo aduani le Daudi, ejo,

English: Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.
Masaai: “Shomo tiaaki Daudi, ‘Nji ejo Olaitoriani, ntokitin uni nanu aaisho; tegelu nabo te ninche, pee aatum aitaasa iyie.’ ”

English: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days' pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
Masaai: Neaku eewuo Gad enetii Daudi neliki ninye, nejoki ninye, “Kailarin okuni lo lameyu oopuonu atua enkop ino. Arashu impirri iyie ilapaitin okuni te dukuya ilmang'ati linono kisujita ninche? Arashu te neaku nkolong'i uni ino lmeitai ti atua enkop ino? Nguanare taata, nidut ewalata nashukoki nanu ilo laairiwua.”

English: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.
Masaai: Nejoki Daudi Gad, “Atii nanu atua osina sapuk; matabatatakinoto iyiook enkaina o Laitoriani, amu kitok olng'ur lenye, kake mikincho abatatakino enkaina e tungani.”
