English: What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?
Masaai: Nejoki, “Amaa te risioroto oo nkitanapat kaa eitaasi Fashiti amu eitu eas enaitanapa olaiguanani Serser natolikitio lelo sunaishi oogelema?”

English: And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the people that are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.
Masaai: Nejoki Memukan te dukuya olaiguanani o lelo kituaak, “Mme ake olaiguanani eitaasa Fashiti entorrono, kake eitaasa sii ilkituaak pooki o ltung'ana pooki ootii iloshon pooki lo laiguanani Serser.

English: For this deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.
Masaai: Amu ore ena yasata e ina kitok o laiguanani naa keyiolou nkituaak pooki, nemenu ilpayiani lenye, te neimakini aajo eitanapishe olaiguanani Serser ajo meyauni Fashiti dukuya enye, neany elotu.

English: Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king's princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus shall there arise too much contempt and wrath.
Masaai: Ore ninye taata ena olong ntomonok e Parsia o Media naaidipa aatoning olkuak le nkitok o laiguanani naa keliki ilkituaak pooki lo laiguanani, neaku sapuk olmena o engoro.

English: If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she.
Masaai: Tenaa keitiship ena olaiguanani, nchoo epukunye ninye enkitanapata, neigeri too nkitanapat oo Lpasia o Lmedia pee meibelekenyi, nchere meitoki ae kata Fashiti alotu dukuya Serser, naa nchoo eisho olaiguanani erishata enye e nkitoo esupat alang ninye.

English: And when the king's decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.
Masaai: Ore ake pee einosuni aaibalunye ina kitanapata o laiguanani ti atua enkitoo enye pooki, aa sapuk anaa enatiu, pee eisho nkituaak enkanyit ilpayiani lenye, lkituaak o looti.”

English: And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan:
Masaai: Neitiship ena utaroto olaiguanani, o lkituaak, neas olaiguanani anaa enatolimuo Memukan.

English: For he sent letters into all the king's provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that it should be published according to the language of every people.
Masaai: Neirriwaa mpala iloshon pooki le nkitoria enye, olosho ake too lkigeroto lenye o te nkutuk enkiroroto enye, nchere pee eaku olee ake ninye pooki olaitoriani le nkaji enye, neiro te risioroto enkutuk o lorere lenye.

English: After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.
Masaai: Ore te siadi kuna baa, ina kata pee eyagaa engoro o laiguanani Serser, nedamu Fashiti ina nataasa o ina naidipaki aatejo enkaraki ninye.

English: Then said the king's servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:
Masaai: Nejoki isinkan lo laiguanani ooisiaita ninye, “Nchoo meing'orakini olaiguanani ntoyie sidain.

English: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women unto the custody of Hege the king's chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them:
Masaai: Negelu olaiguanani ilaitasheikinok too loshon pooki le nkitoria enye, pee eiturrurru ntoyie pooki sidain meshomo enkaji oo nkituaak te Susa te ina ang kitok netoni ti abori enkirrita e Hegai ilo sunash ogelema lo laiguanani laa ninye olaing'urani loo nkituaak; nchoo meishori ninche iila enye.

English: And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
Masaai: Ore entito naitiship olaiguanani nchoo eaku ninye enkitok enye te rishata e Fashiti.” Neitiship ina olaiguanani, neiko neijia.

English: Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite;
Masaai: Netii apa Olyahudi otii Susa ina ang kitok oji enkarna enye Mordekai, olayioni le Yair, olayioni le Shimei olayioni le Kish Olbenchamini,

English: Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.
Masaai: otarayioki apa te Yerusalem te nebo lelo ootarayioki te nebo Yekonia olaiguanani le Yuda, otaarayie Nebukadnesa olaiguanani le Babilon.

English: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
Masaai: Neitubulu Hadasa, aa taa Esta, entito o lenkapu lenye amu meeta apa menye aashu ng'otonye. Entito apa ninye sidai naa supat, ore ake pee eye menye o ng'otonye, neya Mordekai netiu anaa enkerai enye keon.

English: So it came to pass, when the king's commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the king's house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eibulaa enkitanapata o laiguanani, neiturrurri ntoyie kumok te Susa te ina aji naitasheiki Hegai, neyae sii ninye Esta atua enkaji o laiguanani nepiki abori enkirrita e Hegai laa ninye olaing'urani loo nkituaak.

English: And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, which were meet to be given her, out of the king's house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best place of the house of the women.
Masaai: Neitiship ina tito ninye nenyorru ninye neisho ninye asioki ntokitin naakusore, o eoroti enye e ndaa, o sinkan naapishana gelunot naaing'ua enkaji o laiguanani, neisho ninye o nena sinkan enyena ewueji sidai te nkaji oo nkituaak.

English: Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew it.
Masaai: Eitu ninye elimu Esta iltung'ana lenye o lorere lenye amu eitanapa Mordekai pee melimu.

English: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women's house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.
Masaai: Naa ore nkolong'i pooki nelo Mordekai te dukuya ina aji oo nkituaak pee eiyiolou Esta eneikununo, tenaa keserian.

English: Now when every maid's turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished, to wit, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odours, and with other things for the purifying of the women;)
Masaai: Ore ake pee elotu enkata pee elo ake pooki tito enetii Serser, te siadi ilapaitin tomon ti abori nkitanapat oo nkituaak, aa taa ena apa enkata enye naisikarrare, ilapaitin ile te ilata o manemane, o lapaitin ile loo sonkoyoni naarropil oo nkituaak.

English: Then thus came every maiden unto the king; whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king's house.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elo entito atua ine netii olaiguanani tena oitoi, neishori pooki toki naba anaa enayieu neya eing'uaa enkaji oo nkituaak o meshomo enkaji o laiguanani.

English: In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king's chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name.
Masaai: Elo ninye teipa, ore tadekenya neshukunye alo olgilata li are te nkaji e Sha-ashgas ilo apa sunash ogelema lo laiguanani oing'or nkapiak; eitu eitoki alo enetii olaiguanani, meteleku te netishipe olaiguanani te ninye naa keipoti te nkarna.

English: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau erishata e Esta entito e Abihail nkapu e Mordekai, oowa apa ninye aitaa entito enye, pee elo atua ine netii olaiguanani, eitu eikilikuanu toki meteleku ake ina natiaaka Hegai, ilo sunash ogelema lo laiguanani laa ninye oitasheiki nkituaak. Neitiship Esta nkonyek e lelo pooki ootodua ninye.

English: So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eyae Esta enetii olaiguanani Serser, ti atua enkaji enye e nkitoo to lapa le tomon, laa ninye olapa le Tebes to lari li opishana le nkitoria enye,

English: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Masaai: nenyorru olaiguanani Esta aitalang nkituaak pooki, neitiship Esta nkonyek enyena alang nkulie toyie pooki, neaku etipika emaupe e nkitoria endukuya enye nepik ninye erishata e Fashiti.

English: Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esther's feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani aisho osiriua sapuk ilkituaak lenyena pooki o sinkan; osirua le Esta. Neitoki sii aishoru empalakinoto e kodi too lkerenketi neishori nkishorot te risioroto e nkarsisisho e nkitoria.

English: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king's gate.
Masaai: Ore pee eitokini aiturrur nena toyie eniare, etonita Mordekai te nkishomi o laiguanani.

English: Esther had not yet shewed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.
Masaai: Neitu elimu Esta olmarei lenye arashu iltung'ana lenye, anaa enaitanapa Mordekai; amu kening apa Esta Mordekai ebaiki apa pee eitubulu ninye.

English: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
Masaai: Naa ore nena olong'i, anaa enatonita Mordekai te kishomi o laiguanani, negoro oare le lelo sunaishi oogelema lo laiguanani Bigsan o Teres neing'oru eneiko pee epik nkaik enye olaiguanani Serser.

English: And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai's name.
Masaai: Neyiolou Mordekai ina bae, neliki ninye Esta enkitok o laiguanani, neliki Esta olaiguanani te nkarna e Mordekai.

English: And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ejurruni ina bae nenyorrikini aajo neijia etiu, neilili lelo tung'ana pokira oare te nchumata olchani. Neigeri nena baa te mbuku oo nkatitin te dukuya olaiguanani.

English: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
Masaai: Ore te siadi kuna baa, neilepie olaiguanani Serser Haman le Agag, olayioni le Hamedata, neisho ninye enkitoo nepik olorika lenye shumata ile lelo kituaak ooboitare ninye.

English: And all the king's servants, that were in the king's gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.
Masaai: Ore laisiaayiak pooki lo laiguanani ootii kishomi neirrugo aaisho Haman enkanyit; amu neijia apa eitanapishe olaiguanani ajo. Kake eitu eirrugo Mordekai arashu aitodolu enkanyit.

English: Then the king's servants, which were in the king's gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king's commandment?
Masaai: Nejoki lelo aisiaayiak lo laiguanani ootii kishomi Mordekai, “Kainyoo pee igil enkitanapata o laiguanani?”

English: Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
Masaai: Ore pee eirorie ninche ninye anaake neany ening ninche, neliki ninche Haman, ejo pee edol tenaa kepal Mordekai nena, amu etiaaka ninye ninche nchere Olyahudi ninye.

English: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Haman ajo eitu eirrugo Mordekai arashu eitodolu enkanyit negoro oleng.

English: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.
Masaai: Kake eitu ejo aar Mordekai aa ninye ake. Amu eitayioloki ninye iltung'ana pooki le Mordekai, neing'oru Haman pee ear Ilyahudi pooki, iltung'ana le Mordekai, te nkitoria pooki e Serser.

English: In the first month, that is, the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar.
Masaai: Ore to lapa le dukuya, laa ninye olapa le Nisan, to lari le tomon oare lo laiguanani Serser, neosh ninche Pura nchere enkukuo te dukuya Haman nkolong'i pooki; neosh too lapaitin pooki o metabaiki olapa le tomon oare, laa ninye olapa le Adar.

English: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king's laws: therefore it is not for the king's profit to suffer them.
Masaai: Neitoki Haman ajoki olaiguanani Serser, “Etii iltung'ana moobo ooisardakari aaorikino atua iltung'ana loo loshon pooki le nkitoria ino; ore nkitanapat enye nepaashare inoo lkulikae tung'ana pooki, nemeibung nkitanapat o laiguanani, metaa metumie olaiguanani dupoto te nepalaa ninche.

English: If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring it into the king's treasuries.
Masaai: Te neishiaakino to laiguanani nchoo meigeri enkitanapata pee emuti ninche, naa kalak nanu ntalantani nkalifuni tomon oo mpisai apik nkaik e lelo ooitasheiki esiaai o laiguanani pee eyau aapik atua masaa o laiguanani.”

English: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews' enemy.
Masaai: Neitayu olaiguanani olgisoi ashurtu te nkaina enye neisho Haman le Agag ole Hamedata, olmang'atinta loo Lyahudi.

English: And the king said unto Haman, The silver is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Haman, “Kinchooki mpisai, o ltung'ana sii, pee intaas ninche anaa enaishiaakino te iyie.”

English: Then were the king's scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king's lieutenants, and to the governors that were over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the king's ring.
Masaai: Neipoti ilaigerok lo laiguanani te nkolong e tomon ookuni o lapa le dukuya, neigeri anaa enaitanapishe Haman neigerokini lelo ang'eni o lelo kituaak ooitasheiki iloshon, o laitasheikinok pooki loo ltung'ana, olosho ake to rorei lenye o ltung'ana te nkutuk enye; neigeroki apa te nkarna e Serser nepiki olmishire te ilo gisoi lo laiguanani.

English: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.
Masaai: Neirriwari mpala too nkaik e lelo ooirriwari meshomo ilkerenketi pooki lo laiguanani, pee eidaikie, neari metuata, neiwuang'ieki Ilyahudi pooki ooti o lbotoro, inkituaak o nkera, te nkolong nabo, te nkolong e tomon ookuni o lapa le tomon oare, laa ninye olapa le Adar, neya imasaa enye.

English: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, that they should be ready against that day.
Masaai: Naa keirriwari empalai e ilo kigeroto iloshon pooki pee eitanapi metolikini iltung'ana pooki meterretenata te ina olong.

English: The posts went out, being hastened by the king's commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.
Masaai: Nepuo lelo ooirriwari aaya mpala te nkisarrisar te nkitanapata o laiguanani, neitayuni ina kitanapata te Susa teina ang kitok. Netoni olaiguanani o Haman aaokisho, kake ore ina ang anasa e Susa neaku enking'asia.

English: When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;
Masaai: Ore pee eyiolou Mordekai nena pooki naataasaki, nepolos Mordekai nkilani enyena neishop ilkuniyiani neelare nkuruon, neipang alo empolos e nkanasa, eyietu to ltoilo sapuk o te mion aishir;

English: And came even before the king's gate: for none might enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth.
Masaai: nelo ninye o metabaiki dukuya e nkishomi o laiguanani, amu meetae hoo abo oidim atijing'a enkishomi o laiguanani eishopito ilkuniyiani.

English: And in every province, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
Masaai: Ore pooki kerenket otabaikia enkitanapata o laiguanani o nkiguanat enyena, naa eisapuk olkiyioi loo Lyahudi, neen ate aaitupukuo, neyietu aaishir, nepetaa ilkumok lenye ilkuniyiani o nkuruon.

English: So Esther's maids and her chamberlains came and told it her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he received it not.
Masaai: Ore ake pee epuo nkaisiaayiak e Esta o lelo sunaishi oogelema aainosaki, neisina oleng ina kitok o laiguanani: Neirriwaa nkilani aishop Mordekai, pee etum aitayu ilkuniyiani, kake menyorraa ang'amaa nena kilani.

English: Then called Esther for Hatach, one of the king's chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to know what it was, and why it was.
Masaai: Neitoki Esta aipot Hatak, obo le lelo sunaishi oogelema lo laiguanani, laa ninye etegeluaki pee eisiaai ninye, neirriwaa ninye meshomo enetii Mordekai pee eyiolou ajo kaa ena naa ae tenkaraki nyoo pee etotiuo neijia.

English: So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which was before the king's gate.
Masaai: Neipang Hatak alo enetii Mordekai teilo kurroto otumoreki le nkanasa te dukuya enkishomi o laiguanani.

English: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
Masaai: Neliki Mordekai nena pooki naataasate, o esiana oo mpisai naatonyorrayie Haman alak apik olchumati lo laiguanani te mutata oo Lyahudi.

English: Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given at Shushan to destroy them, to shew it unto Esther, and to declare it unto her, and to charge her that she should go in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him for her people.
Masaai: Neitoki Mordekai aisho emboitati e mpalai e ina kitanapata naitayioki te Susa te nkaraki emutata enye, pee elo aitodol Esta, neinosaki ninye ilomon, neitanap meshomo enetii olaiguanani pee eomon nesai te nkaraki iltung'ana lenyena.

English: And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
Masaai: Nelo Hatak aliki Esta ina natejo Mordekai.

English: Again Esther spake unto Hatach, and gave him commandment unto Mordecai;
Masaai: Neitoki Esta airorie Hatak neisho ninye olkilikuai oyaki Mordekai ejo,

English: All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
Masaai: “Ore laisiaayiak pooki lo laiguanani o ltung'ana loo lkerenketi pooki lo laiguanani neyiolo aajo te nelo olee arashu enkitok ajing'aki olaiguanani ti atua ine netonie eitu eipoti, naa enkitanapata nabo ake natii, ore pooki te risioroto naa keari metuata meteleku ilo oitorioki olaiguanani eng'udi enye e sahabu pee epok. Naa eitu nanu aaipoti maeu atua enetii olaiguanani kuna olong'i tomoni uni.”

English: And they told to Mordecai Esther's words.
Masaai: Neliki ninche Mordekai ina natejo Esta.

English: Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews.
Masaai: Neitoki Mordekai ajoki ninche metushuku ewalata enetii Esta, “Mijo taa ore ti atua enkaji o laiguanani niserian alang ilkulikae Yahudi pooki.

English: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Masaai: Amu te nigira te nkata natiu anaa ena, naa kelotu eretoto o enjeunoto ti ae oitoi, kake ore iyie o enkaji e papaai lino nindaayaya. Naa eing'ae oyiolo tenaa ieuo ena kitoo te nkaraki enkata anaa ena?”

English: Then Esther bade them return Mordecai this answer,
Masaai: Neitoki Esta ajoki ninche metawaliki Mordekai,

English: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
Masaai: “Shomo, inturrurro Ilyahudi pooki ootii Susa nieniene ate aaitupukoo te rishata ai niminyanya endaa arashu iokioko too nkolong'i uni dama o kewarie. Ore nanu o nkaisiaayiak aainei nikien sii iyiook ate aaitupukoo anaa intae. alo enetii olaiguanani, hoo tenaa kengilata oo nkitanapat ina naa tenaa kaye nanu naye.”

English: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.
Masaai: Nelo Mordekai neas pooki toki anaa enaitanapa Esta ninye.

English: Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner court of the king's house, over against the king's house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni neishop Esta nkilani enyena e nkitoo neitashe ti atua olgoriet le nkaji o laiguanani, oipirakinore ina aji o laiguanani. Neton olaiguanani to lorika lenye le nkitoo ti atua enkaji e nkitoo aipirakinore kutukaji e nkaji e nkitoo,

English: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol olaiguanani Esta eitashe to lgoriet, netum ninye Esta omom too nkonyek enyena neitarasaki ninye Esta ina ng'udi e sahabu apa naata te nkaina enye. Nelotu Esta ayiaya neibung endukuya e ina ng'udi.

English: Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kainyoo Esta? Kainyoo eomonunoto ino? Eikinchori iyie, o metabaiki olpisiai le nkitoria ai.”

English: And Esther answered, If it seem good unto the king, let the king and Haman come this day unto the banquet that I have prepared for him.
Masaai: Nejo Esta, “Tenaa keishiaakino to laiguanani, nchoo olaiguanani o Haman epuonu osirua taata laitobiraka nanu olaiguanani.

English: Then the king said, Cause Haman to make haste, that he may do as Esther hath said. So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Eyau Haman entasieku, pee kitum aataas anaa enayieu Esta.” Nelotu olaiguanani o Haman ilo sirua oitobira Esta.

English: And the king said unto Esther at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.
Masaai: Ore eokito enaisho oo sabibu, nejoki olaiguanani Esta, “Kainyoo olkiyioi lino? Eikinchori iyie. Naa kainyoo eomonunoto ino? Tenaa duoo ninye kolpisiai le nkitoria ai, naa keitabari ake.”

English: Then answered Esther, and said, My petition and my request is;
Masaai: Kake etejo Esta, “Ore enkolat ai o eomonunoto ai naa;

English: If I have found favour in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition, and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I will do to morrow as the king hath said.
Masaai: tenaa kanoto nanu omom too nkonyek o laiguanani, naa tenaa keitiship olaiguanani meishoru enkolat neitabaya eomonunoto ai, nchoo olaiguanani o Haman epuonu taisere osirua layooki aitobiraki ninche, ore taisere naas anaa enatejo olaiguanani.”

English: Then went Haman forth that day joyful and with a glad heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, that he stood not up, nor moved for him, he was full of indignation against Mordecai.
Masaai: Neipang Haman ina olong alo eng'ida neshipa to ltau. Kake ore ake pee edol Haman Mordekai te nkishomi o laiguanani, nchere eitu eitashe neitu eikirikira te dukuya ninye neiput engoro te nkaraki Mordekai.

English: Nevertheless Haman refrained himself: and when he came home, he sent and called for his friends, and Zeresh his wife.
Masaai: Ore ake eyia eibooyie Haman keon, nelo ang, neirriwaa meipoti ilchoreta lenyena o enkitok enye Seresh.

English: And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all the things wherein the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.
Masaai: Neinosaki Haman ninche esikar o enkarsisisho enye, esiana oo layiok lenyena o enkitoo pooki naishoo ninye olaiguanani o ina nailepieki ninye aaitalang ilkituaak o laisiaayiak lo laiguanani.

English: Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to morrow am I invited unto her also with the king.
Masaai: Neitoki Haman aponaa ajo, “Ore ninye Esta enkitok o laiguanani eitu eisho hoo ng'ae meeu te nebo olaiguanani ilo sirua oitobira ninye meteleku nanu ake. Naa ore sii taisere aaitoomono ninye te nebo olaiguanani.

English: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
Masaai: Ore eyia, maaitiship kuna pooki te nadol Mordekai ilo Yahudi eton te nkishomi o laiguanani.”

English: Then said Zeresh his wife and all his friends unto him, Let a gallows be made of fifty cubits high, and to morrow speak thou unto the king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily with the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he caused the gallows to be made.
Masaai: Nejoki enkitok enye Seresh o lchoreta lenyena pooki, “Nchoo eitayuni olchani ogorishoreki intemat onom enkadoro ore taisere tadekenya niliki olaiguanani pee eiki Mordekai te nchumata e ilo shani. Nijing, iyie osirua lo laiguanani te ng'ida.” Neitiship ina walata Haman, neisho meitobiri olchani ogorishoreki.

English: On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.
Masaai: Ore te ina kewarie neitu eirura olaiguanani; neitanapisho ninye pee eyauni embuku natii mbaa naadamuni, neisumi te dukuya olaiguanani.

English: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
Masaai: Netumi eigero ajo etolimuo Mordekai Bigtana o Teres, lelo oare ti atua isunaishi oogelema lo laiguanani, apa oorripito kutuk aji, neyieu sii apa nepik nkaik enye olaiguanani Serser.

English: And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the king's servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Amaa kaa anyit anaa kaa kitoo eishooki Mordekai tena bae?” Nejoki ilaisiaayiak lo laiguanani ooisiaita ninye, “Meetae enaitaasaki.”

English: And the king said, Who is in the court? Now Haman was come into the outward court of the king's house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Aing'ae otii olodung'oro, naa enalotunye Haman atua ilo odung'oro li oriong enkaji o laiguanani, pee etum airorie olaiguanani pee eiki Mordekai te nchumata ilo shani ogorishoreki oitobiraka.

English: And the king's servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.
Masaai: Neliki ilaisiaayiak lo laiguanani ninye, ejo, “Etii Haman idie, eitashe to lodung'oro.” Nejo olaiguanani, “Enchoo elotu atua aji.”

English: So Haman came in. And the king said unto him, What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour? Now Haman thought in his heart, To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?
Masaai: Nejing'u Haman atua aji, nejoki olaiguanani ninye, “Kaa eitaasi oltung'ani oshipakino olaiguanani pee eyanyit.” Nejo Haman to ltau lenye, Kaing'ae pasa oitishipa olaiguanani pee eyanyit aitalang nanu?

English: And Haman answered the king, For the man whom the king delighteth to honour,
Masaai: Neitoki Haman ajoki olaiguanani, “Ore oltung'ani oshipakino olaiguanani pee eyanyit

English: Let the royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and the crown royal which is set upon his head:
Masaai: inchoo eyauni nkilani e nkitoo naaidipa olaiguanani aishopo, o ina barta naidipa olaiguanani atakedo, neishopokoki olmarisian le nkitoo endukuya enye;

English: And let this apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man withal whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
Masaai: neishori nena kilani o ina barta eitarasakini obo loo laitasheikinok lo laiguanani oata enkitoo; nchoo ninye eishopoki ilo tung'ani oshipakino olaiguanani pee eyanyit, nerikoo ninye ekedito embarta te nkoitoi sapuk e ina ang, eitayiolo aibalunye te dukuya ninye nchere, neijia eikoni ilo tung'ani oshipakinoolaiguanani pee eyanyit.”

English: Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, and take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the king's gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani ajoki Haman, “Isarisara intayu nena kilani o ina barta, ore anaa enitejo, nintaas ina Mordekai ilo Yahudi otonita te nkishomi o laiguanani. Mintong'or ake nabo te nena duoo nitejo.”

English: Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
Masaai: Neitayu Haman inkilani o embarta neishopoki Mordekai neisho ninye metakedo embarta nerikoo ninye aimie ilo kurroto otumoreki le nkanasa eibalunye ajo, “Inji eikoni oltung'ani oshipakino olaiguanani pee eyanyit.”

English: And Mordecai came again to the king's gate. But Haman hasted to his house mourning, and having his head covered.
Masaai: Neitoki Mordekai ashuko alo kishomi o laiguanani. Kake eisarisara Haman alo enkaji enye eishirita neimulumula elukunya enye.

English: And Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends every thing that had befallen him. Then said his wise men and Zeresh his wife unto him, If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews, before whom thou hast begun to fall, thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt surely fall before him.
Masaai: Neliki Haman enkitok enye Seresh o lchoreta lenyena pooki nena baa pooki naanoto ninye. Nejoki ninye ilang'eni lenyena o enkitok enye Seresh, “Tenaa ko Lyahudi Mordekai ilo apa litang'asa adumakino mindim naa iyie ninye kake meeta nchere mibatata iyie te dukuya ninye.”

English: And while they were yet talking with him, came the king's chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.
Masaai: Ore eton eirorie ninche ninye, nebau lelo sunaishi oogelema lo laiguanani eisosion pee eya Haman ilo sirua oitobira Esta.

English: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.
Masaai: Nelo olaiguanani o Haman ilo sirua te nebo Esta enkitok o laiguanani.

English: And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e are, ina kata eokito enaisho oo sabibu, neitoki olaiguanani ajoki Esta, “Kainyoo eomonunoto ino Esta? Eikinchori iyie. Ainyoo eyieunoto ino? Tenaa ninye kolpisiai le nkitoo ai, naa keitabari.”

English: Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:
Masaai: Newaliki Esta ajoki, “Tenaa kanoto omom, too nkonyek inono, olaiguanani, naa te neitiship olaiguanani, nchoo maaishori enkishui ai te yieunoto ai, o ltung'ana laainei te nkomono ai.

English: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king's damage.
Masaai: Amu etimiraki iyiook, nanu o ltung'ana laainei, pee emuti iyiook neari matuata neimisieki iyiook. Tenaa naaji ketimiraki iyiook aaitaa irindiki, ilewa o nkituaak, anaata atigire, amu meitanyaanyukieki osina lang enkitarruorroto to laiguanani.”

English: Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Serser Esta, “Kaing'ae ilo, naa kaji etii, ilo oitieu ataasa ena?”

English: And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.
Masaai: Nejoki Esta, “Olaarani naa olmang'atinta ninye; ele arruoni Haman!” Neureishoyu Haman te dukuya olaiguanani o enkitok o laiguanani.

English: And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.
Masaai: Neinyototo olaiguanani te ilo sirua te ngoro nelo enkurma e ina aji e nkitoo; neton Haman aomonu enkishui enye te Esta enkitok o laiguanani, amu etoduaa ajo eitobirita olaiguanani entorroni naarie ninye.

English: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.
Masaai: Neshukunye olaiguanani eing'uaa ina kurma e nkaji e nkitoo elotu ewueji duoo neokie enaisho oo sabibu, ore Haman ina kata ebatata aomonu olng'ur, nebatatakino ina rruat natii Esta; nejo olaiguanani, “Keyieu neikony enkitok o laiguanani te dukuya nanu ti atua enkaji ai, Ore pee epuku ilo rorei te nkutuk o laiguanani neimulumuli enkomom e Haman.

English: And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
Masaai: Nejo Harbona obo loo sunaishi oogelema ooisiaai olaiguanani, “Ore ninye ilo shata ogorishoreki ooitobiraka Haman Mordekai, laa ororei lenye oitajeuo olaiguanani, neitasheyieki te nkaji e Haman naa intemat onom enkadoro.”

English: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified.
Masaai: Nejo olaiguanani, “Entiik elilio ninye te ilo shata.” Neilili Haman te ilo shata ogorishoreki apa oitobiraka Mordekai neyagaa engoro o laiguanani.

English: On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
Masaai: Ore teina olong neisho olaiguanani Esta enkaji e Haman, ilo mang'atinta loo lyahudi. Nelotu Mordekai dukuya olaiguanani amu etolikio Esta enabaikinore ninye;

English: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
Masaai: neshurtu olaiguanani olgisoi lenye otooruo Haman neisho Mordekai. Neisho Esta Mordekai enkaji e Haman meitoria.

English: And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.
Masaai: Neitoki Esta airorie olaiguanani, nebatata too nkejek enyena nesai ninye too lkiyio pee eiwuang'ie entorroni apa naitobira Haman Olagagi o nena naaiguanua te nkaraki Ilyahudi.

English: Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,
Masaai: Neutie olaiguanani Esta eng'udi e sahabu,

English: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the king's provinces:
Masaai: Neinyototo Esta aitashe te dukuya olaiguanani Nejo, “Tenaa keitiship olaiguanani, naa tenaa kanoto omom too nkonyek inono, naa tenaa keishiaakino ena bae te dukuya olaiguanani te naishiaakino nanu te dukuya nkonyek enyena, nchoo meigeri enkitanapata naibelekenyieki mpala e nena apa naaipirua Haman Olagagi, olayioni le Hamedata, apa naaigero pee emut Ilyahudi ootii iloshon pooki lo laiguanani.

English: For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?
Masaai: Amu kaji aiko te nangiri aing'or ina torroni nalotu atua iltung'ana laainei? Arashu kaji aiko te nangiri te nadol ina mutata o lorere lai.”

English: Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Serser Esta o Mordekai ilo Yahudi, “Eng'ura, aishoo Esta enkaji e Haman, neililio ninche ninye to lchani ogorishoreki, amu eitorioko ninye nkaik Ilyahudi.

English: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse.
Masaai: Naa indimidimi aaigero anaa eniyieuu, anaa enaishiaakino Ilyahudi, te nkarna o laiguanani, nipikipiki olmishire lo lgisoi lo laiguanani, amu ore ilkigerot ooigeroki te nkarna o laiguanani, nepiki olmishire lo lgisoi lo laiguanani meetae oltung'ani oidim aibelekenya.

English: Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.
Masaai: Neipoti ilaigerok lo laiguanani te ina kata to lapa li okuni, aa olapa le Sifan te nkolong e tikitam o okuni; neigeri enkitanapata anaa enaitanapishe Mordekai meyakini Ilyahudi pooki, o lkituaak pooki, o lbalusuni o laitasheikinok loo lkerenketi ebaiki India o metabaiki Etiopia naa iloshon iip o tikitam o opishana, pooki osho ake to lkigeroto lenye, o pooki tung'ani te nkutuk enye, o lo Lyahudi sii to lkigeroto lenye o enkutuk enye.

English: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries:
Masaai: Ore lelo kigerot naa te nkarna o laiguanani Serser nemishira to lmishire lo lgisoi lenye, neyae nena pala iltung'ana ooirriwari ookedito mbartan naaten oleng apa naasishoreki te nkisiayiare o laiguanani, naaitubuluaki ti atua boo o laiguanani.

English: Wherein the king granted the Jews which were in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil of them for a prey,
Masaai: Ore te kuna nenyorraa olaiguanani Ilyahudi ootii nkanas pooki meiturrurroto pee emitu ate, nemut near metuata, neidaikie pooki jore e pooki tung'ani o pooki osho oidim atarasaki ninche, o nkera enye o nkituaak, neya masaa enye,

English: Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, namely, upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
Masaai: nabo olong too loshon pooki lo laiguanani Serser te nkolong e tomon o okuni to lapa le tomon o are, laa olapa le Adar.

English: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
Masaai: Ore empalai e nena naaigeroki naa keishoori anaa enkitanapata te pooki osho, o te nkitayioloto oo ltung'ana pooki, nerretena Ilyahudi pee eitalaku elap enye te lelo mang'ati lenye.

English: So the posts that rode upon mules and camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.
Masaai: Neked lelo ooirriwari imbartan enye naaten apa naasishoreki te nkisiayiare o laiguanani, neipang aapuo te nkisarrisar, eitirrishakita enkitanapata o laiguanani, neitayuni enkitanapata te Susa te ina ang kitok.

English: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
Masaai: Neitoki Mordekai apuku alo te ine netii olaiguanani eishopito inkilani e nkitoo pusi o naaibor o lmarisian sapuk le nkitoo le sahabu, olkila sidai sintet, ina kata ebuaku enkang e Susa neng'ida.

English: The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.
Masaai: Netum Ilyahudi ewang'an, o enchipai, o eng'ida o enkanyit.

English: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.
Masaai: Ore te pooki osho, o te pooki ang, eneba anaa enetabaikia enkitanapata o lkilikuai lo laiguanani, netii enchipai o eng'ida atua Ilyahudi; o sirua o enkisampash. Ore ilkumok te lelo tung'ana le ina kop neibalunye ate aaitaa ate Ilyahudi amu eiputa enkuretisho oo Lyahudi atua ninche.

English: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)
Masaai: Ore to lapa le tomon o are laa olapa le Adar, te nkolong e tomon o okuni e ilo apa ina kata etinyikutua inkitanapat o laiguanani o lkilikuai lenye pee eitabari, te ina olong apa ejo ilmang'ati loo Lyahudi ketum engolon te ninche, kake eibelekenye ina, aaku enkolong natumie Ilyahudi engolon too lmang'ati lenye,

English: The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.
Masaai: neiturrurro Ilyahudi too nkanas enye ti atua loshon pooki lo laiguanani Ahasero pee epik nkaik lelo oshi ooyieu near ninche. Nemetii oltung'ani oidim airisha ninche, amu eiputa iltung'ana pooki enkuretisho eure ninche.

English: And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them.
Masaai: Ore ilkituaak pooki loo loshon o laitasheikinok, o lbalusuni o lelo pooki oata enkitoo neretu sii ninche Ilyahudi, amu etijing'a ninche enkuretisho eure Mordekai.

English: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.
Masaai: Amu eikitok apa Mordekai ti atua enkaji o laiguanani, ore ening'oi enye neidapashakino iloshon pooki; amu ore ilo tung'ani oji Mordekai netoponari oleng agolu.

English: Thus the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would unto those that hated them.
Masaai: Near Ilyahudi lelo mang'ati lenye pooki to lalem, nemut, neidaikie ninche, neas anaa enayieu te lelo pooki apa ooiba ninche.

English: And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men.
Masaai: Ore te Susa te ina ang kitok ake near Ilyahudi metuata neidaikie ilewa iip imiet,

English: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
Masaai: near sii Par-shandata o Dalfon o Aspata

English: And Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
Masaai: o Parata o Adalia o Aridata

English: And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,
Masaai: o Parmasta o Arisai o Aridai o Faisata,

English: The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand.
Masaai: ilayiok pokira tomon le Haman ole Hamedata, olmang'atinta loo Lyahudi; Kake eitu epik nkaik enye nena naataarutua.

English: On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.
Masaai: Ore ina olong ake nelikini olaiguanani esiana e lelo ootaaraki te Susa te ina ang kitok.

English: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Esta enkitok o laiguanani, “Ore te Susa te ina ang kitok etaara Ilyahudi ilewa iip imiet o layiok tomon le Haman, Kainyoo naa sii yie etaasa te lelo kerenketi le laiguanani ootelekutua! Kainyoo naa taata eyieuna ino? Eikinchori iyie. Naa kainyoo intoki aomonu? Amu keitabari.”

English: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.
Masaai: Nejo Esta, “Tenaa keitiship olaiguanani, nchoo Ilyahudi ootii Susa menyaakini aanyorraki taisere metaasa anaa ena kitanapata ena olong. Naa nchoo layiok le Haman meilili to lchani ogorishorek.”

English: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons.
Masaai: Neitanapisho olaiguanani ina metaasi; neitayuni enkitanapata te Susa, neilili ilayiok pokira tomon le Haman.

English: For the Jews that were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.
Masaai: Neitoki Ilyahudi ootii Susa aaiturrurro te nkolong e tomon o ong'uan o lapa le Adar near metuata iltung'ana iip uni te Susa; kake eitu epik nkaik enye nena naataarutua.

English: But the other Jews that were in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,
Masaai: Ore lelo kulikae Yahudi ootii atua lelo oshon lo laiguanani neiturrurro sii ninche pee emitu ate, netum ninche enkiyagata ti alo ilmang'ati lenye. Neitoki aar inkalifuni ntomoni naapishana o imiet e lelo apa ooiba ninche; kake eitu epik nkaik enye nena naataarutua.

English: On the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
Masaai: Te nkolong e tomon o ong'uan neeng'iyeng'a neitaa ina olong osirua o enchipai.

English: But the Jews that were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day thereof; and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
Masaai: Kake ore Ilyahudi ootii Susa neiturrurro te nkolong e tomon o okuni o te nkolong e tomon o ong'uan, neeng'iyeng'a te nkolong e tomon o imiet, aaitaa ina olong osirua o enchipai.

English: Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.
Masaai: Metaa ore Ilyahudi loo nkang'itie kutiti, ootoni too nkang'itie nemeeta isunta, neitaa enkolong e tomon o ong'uan olapa le Adar enkolong e nchipai, osirua o enkiyeng'iyeng, enkolong naa ninye eishorore nkishorot.

English: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
Masaai: Neiger Mordekai kuna baa, neitoki airriwaki mpala Ilyahudi pooki ootii iloshon lo laiguanani Serser, ilootaana o loolakua,

English: To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,
Masaai: aikok ninche pee edamu, enkolong e tomon oong'uan o lapa le Adar o enkolong sii e tomon o imiet to lari o to lari,

English: As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.
Masaai: aa inkolong'i naa ninche enotie Ilyahudi enkiyagata too lmang'ati lenye, naa olapa sii oibelekenyaki te ninche metaa kepuku to sina aajing enchipai nepuku to lkiyioi aajing enkiyeng'iyeng, pee etum aaitaa ninche inkolong'i o sirua o enchipai, inkolong'i naaishorore nkishorot maate neisho nkishorot ilaisinak.

English: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;
Masaai: Neiruk lelo Yahudi aas anaa ina naiterutua aas, anaa sii ina naigeroko Mordekai ninche.

English: Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;
Masaai: Amu ore Haman ilo Agag olayioni le Hamedata, olmang'atinta loo Lyahudi pooki, eitobira pee ear Ilyahudi; neidaikie ninche, netoosho Pur aa nchere enkukuo pee eparripar neidaikie ninche.

English: But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
Masaai: Kake ore ake pee elotu Esta dukuya olaiguanani, neishooyo inkitanapat too lkigerot nchere ore ina kitobirata enye torrono naitobira pee emuti Ilyahudi enyor nelotu shumata endukuya enye, ore ake sii neilili ninye o layiok lenyena to lchani ogorishoreki.

English: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,
Masaai: Neaku kejo ninche kuna olong'i Purim, aaitusuj ilo rorei oji Pur. Metaa ore te nkaraki nena pooki naaigeroki tena palai, o nena naatadua tena bae, o te nena naaetuo atua ninche.

English: The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year;
Masaai: Neitayu Ilyahudi enkitanapata neibung ninche maate o nkera enye o pooki ooibung'are ninche, nchere keibung kuna olong'i pokira are eitu eitadiak te risioroto e nena apa naaigeroki o te nkata naba anaa enageluni te pooki ari

English: And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.
Masaai: nchere keishiaakino nedamuni kuna olong'i neibung'i ti atua iishoritin pooki ishoi, te pooki marei, o losho o enkang, naa ore kuna olong'i e Purim nemeishori aekata eimin ti atua Ilyahudi, nemepali sii enkitadamunoto ti atua ishoritin pooki.

English: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim.
Masaai: Neitoki Esta, ina kitok o laiguanani, entito e Abihail o Mordekai ilo Yahudi, aaiger enkitanapata nalulung'a te nkitoria, aaitadedeyie ena palai e are naipirta Purim.

English: And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,
Masaai: Neigerokini mpala Ilyahudi pooki, ootii lelo oshon tikitam o opishana lo laiguanani Serser, too rorei le seriani o esipata,

English: To confirm these days of Purim in their times appointed, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.
Masaai: nchere ore kuna olong'i e Purim neishiaakino neibung'i too nkatitin naatudung'okoki, anaa enaitanapa Mordekai ilo Yahudi o Esta enkitok o laiguanani Ilyahudi, o ina sii nairuko aaibung ninche maate o nkera enye mbaa naaipirta eenata o enkishirata enye.

English: And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.
Masaai: Neitagol enkitanapata e Esta nena baa e Purim, neigeri te mbuku.

English: And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.
Masaai: Neitalaku olaiguanani Serser kodi te ina kop o to loomanaa loo naaiposha.

English: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
Masaai: Ore iasat enyena pooki o engolon o enkidimata, o lomon pooki le nkitoo e Mordekai, naishoo olaiguanani ninye, aimeigero kuna te mbuku oo nkoon oo laiguanak le Media o Parsia?

English: For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
Masaai: Amu Mordekai ilo Yahudi naa ninye apa osujita te nkitoo olaiguanani Serser, naa aikitok too Lyahudi nening'o to lorora loo lalashera lenyena, amu eing'orua olmabarishoi loo ltung'ana lenyena neiro eseriani too ltung'ana lenyena pooki.

English: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.
Masaai: Eetae apa oltung'ani omanya enkop e Us, oji enkarna enye Yoab. Naa ore apa ilo tung'ani nemeeta entioto naa oltung'ani oitashe too sipat, neure ninye Enkai oleng, neorunye aing'uaa intorrok.

English: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.
Masaai: Eeta apa ninye ilayiok oopishana o ntoyie uni.

English: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.
Masaai: Neeta apa ninye intare nkalifuni naapishana, o ntamesin inkalifuni uni, o lmong'i iip imiet ooyietaa enchata emurt, o sirkon lipong'a iip imiet, o sinkan kumok oleng, naa ore apa ele tung'ani meetae olkarsis olang too ltung'ana pooki lo loosaen.

English: And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
Masaai: Ore apa ilayiok lenyena naa kepuo aaitayu isiruai too lmareita lenye, meeta ake olemeeta enkolong enye. Neipotu inkanashera enye pokira uni meetu aadaa te nebo neokisho te nebo.

English: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
Masaai: Ore ake pee elusoo inkolong'i o sirua, neinyototo Yoab alo aitisiny ninche te dukuya Enkai. Naa keyooki tadekenya alo aitayu olasar opejori terishata oo layiok lenyena pooki; amu ejo apa Yoab, “Ebaiki netaasa ilayiok laainei ing'ok, nedek Enkai too ltauja lenye.” Neas Yoab ina anaake.

English: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them.
Masaai: Eetae apa enkolong naetuo ilayiok le Nkai aaitayu ate te dukuya Olaitoriani, nelotu sii ninye Shetani te nebo ni nche.

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Kaji ing'uaa iyie?” Newaliki Shetani Olaitoriani ajoki, “Aing'uaa ene o idie ti oriong e nkop, naing'uaa sii elototo ai e shumata o abori te shumata ninye.”

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Itoduaa osinka lai Yoab, olaa meetae likae laaijo ninye te enkop, oltung'ani lemeeta entioto neitashe too sipat, neure Enkai neorunye aing'uaa intorrok?”

English: Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
Masaai: Ina pee ewaliki Shetani Olaitoriani ejo, “Keure Yoab Enkai te mpesho?

English: Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
Masaai: Aa keitu doi intaman ninye enkikarrata tenebo enkaji enye o pooki toki naata too nkaloli pooki? Itamayiana esiai oo nkaik enyena, netoponari imasaa enyena aaiput ena kop.

English: But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.
Masaai: Kake intorioi sii iyie enkaina ino tenakata iseyie nena pooki naata, naa aikidek ninye aitoriokino enkomom ino.”

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Ng'ura, ore pooki naata ninye etii atua engolon ino; ninye ake enkorrok enye mintorioki enkaina ino.” Neaku eshomo Shetani aing'uaa ine netii Olaitoriani.

English: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:
Masaai: Eetae apa enkolong natotona ilayiok le Yoab o ntoyie enyena aadaa neok enaisho oo lsabibu te nkaji olalashe lenye botor;

English: And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:
Masaai: nelotu olkilikuai enetii Yoab nejoki, “Ore duoo eturito ilmong'i enkurma nedaa isirkon tembata enye;

English: And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
Masaai: nedoiki iltung'ana le Sabea, nereu ninche pooki, near isinkan ootii te nepi olalem; neaku nanu ake oisikua peyie aalotu aliki.”

English: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
Masaai: Ore eton eiro eitu eishu, nelotu likae nejo, “Etadowuo enkima Enkai te shumata nepejoo intare te nebo isinkan, neidakie ninche; neaku nanu ake oisikua peyie aalotu aliki.”

English: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
Masaai: Ore eton eirorita ilo, nejing'u likae nejo, “Eitayutuo Ilkaldayo iltimito okuni, nepuonu aarare iyiook aaikonyaa intamesin nereu, near isinkan te nepi olalem; metaa nanu ake oisikua peyie aalotu aliki.”

English: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:
Masaai: Ore eton eirorita ilo, nelotu likae nejoki, “Ore layiok linono o ntoyie edaa duoo neok enaisho oo sabibu tenebo te nkaji olalashe lenye botor;

English: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
Masaai: naa ng'ura; eewuo osiwuo sapuk odung'u olpurkel, neosh ilpijat pokira oong'uan leina aji, nesulakino lelo tung'ana lelerue, netuata pooki, metaa nanu ake openy oisikua peyie aalotu aliki.”

English: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,
Masaai: Ina pee edumunye Yoab, nepolos olkila lenye, nebarn elukunya enye, nebatatakino enkop aserem.

English: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, atupukuo apa te ng'uset e yieyio maishopo naa karrinyo alo maishopo. Olaitoriani oishorua naa ninye onyaaka aya. Meisisi enkarna o Laitoriani.

English: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
Masaai: Ore te kuna pooki neitu eas Yoab eng'oki arashu eipotoki Enkai entorroni.

English: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
Masaai: Neitokini ake aata ae olong naetuo ilayiok le Nkai aaitoduaaya ate te dukuya Olaitoriani, nelotu sii ninye Shetani te nebo ninche aitoduaaya kewan te dukuya Olaitoriani.

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Kaji doi iyie ing'uaa?” Newaliki Shetani Olaitoriani ajoki, “Aing'uaa idie o idie te nkop, nalilita te shumata o tiabori.”

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Itoduaa osinka lai Yoab, olaa meetae olonyaanyukie ninye te nkop, o lemeeta entioto naa oltung'ani oitashe too sipat, oltung'ani oure Enkai neibelekenye aing'uaa intorrok? Eton ake eibung'ita enkirukoto enye anaa apake, hoo nikiewuo arrumoki ninye mataarare, meeta ninye enataasa.”

English: And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
Masaai: Ina pee ewaliki Shetani Olaitoriani ajoki, “Olchoni to lchoni eitayu oltung'ani pooki naata te nkaraki enkishui enye.

English: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.
Masaai: Kake intorioi sii iyie enkaina ino tenakata, iseyie sii iyie oloito lenye o sesen lenye, naa aikimor ninye aitoriokino enkomom ino.”

English: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Shetani, “Ng'ura, etii ninye nkaik inono enkishui enye ake miseyie.”

English: So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
Masaai: Metaa eshomo Shetani aing'uaa enetii Olaitoriani, nelo aisilisil Yoab apik impaldakani torrok naang'u eiteru too ndapi oo nkejek enyena o metabaiki elukunya enye.

English: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
Masaai: Neya Yoab embelati e moti oo nkulukuok, nelo aton to lchala loo suut aoj kewan.

English: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.
Masaai: Ina pee ejoki enkitok enye, “Keton ake imbung akurraki enkirukoto? Ainyoo pee midek Enkai pee itum atua.”

English: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yoab ninye, “Iro iyie anaa nabo oo nkituaak naamoda. Aiking'amu esidai te nkaina Enkai, nimiking'amu intorrok?” Ore te kuna pooki eitu eas Yoab eng'oki te nkutuk enye.

English: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
Masaai: Ore ina kata pee ening ilchoreta le Yoab okuni ina torroni natijing'aka Yoab, nepuonu pooki ng'ae eing'uaa wuejitin enye, Elifas le Teman, o Bildad le Shushi o Sofar le Naamat. Negelu pooki olkekun opuonu tenebo aaitobor neitagol sii.

English: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
Masaai: Ore ake pee edol ninche ninye eton elakuaniki, eitu ninche eyiolou ninye; neyietu aaishir nepolos ilkilani lenye neisuaaki enterit ilukuny eing'or keper.

English: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
Masaai: Netoni te nebo ninye te nkop inkolong'i ile o nkewaritin enye; nemeetae hoo obo otaboloko ninye enkutuk airorie, amu etoduaa ninche aajo ore osomit lenye naa kitok oleng.

English: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena, etabolo Yoab enkutuk enye adek enapa olong natoinyeki.

English: And Job spake, and said,
Masaai: Nejo Yoab:

English: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.
Masaai: “Inchoo ina olong apa naatoinyieki eidak, te nebo ina kewarie apa natejoki, ‘Kenutae enkayioni!’

English: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.
Masaai: Inchoo ina olong eaku enaimin! Inchoo Enkai e shumata epal eitu eing'oru ninye, nemeetae ewang'an naitawang'aki ninye.

English: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
Masaai: Inchoo eaku enkolong torrono o enaimin nagut te shumata enye. Tunuka ninye too nkatampo niwuang'ie enkolong te ninye.

English: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.
Masaai: Ore ina kewarie, inchoo enaimin narok ong'u eibung ninye! Mincho ninye eshipa tiatua nena olong'i o lari. Mincho ninye elotu ajing esiana oo lapaitin.

English: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.
Masaai: Ee inchoo ina kewarie eaku olupi; emincho oltoilo le nchipai ening'i tiatua.

English: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.
Masaai: Inchoo lelo oodekisho metediaa ina olong, lelo arriyiak oodumu Lefiatan.

English: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:
Masaai: Inchoo ilakir lenyena le nkakenya emisimisu nchoo ninye eisiligu ewang'an nemetum nemedol osirua enkakenya tenewang'u.

English: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
Masaai: Ore amu eitu een ina olong eng'uset e yieyio, neitu eisudoo enyamali too nkonyek aainei.

English: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?
Masaai: “Ainyoo apa pee eitu aye te nkata e inoto, anaa pee apuku ake te ng'uset naye.

English: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?
Masaai: Aainyoo pee aaibung'a yieyio too nkejek enyena? Anaa pee aaitanaa ilke lenyena?

English: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,
Masaai: Amu anaata apa airraga nagira; anaata airure; naa anaata ayeng'iyeng'e.

English: With kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;
Masaai: Tenebo ilaiguanak o laitoriak le nkop lelo apa ooteshetakita ate inkidaarot.

English: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
Masaai: Arashu ilkituaak oota sahabu, lelo ooiput inkajijik enye enkosholai.

English: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.
Masaai: Ainyoo apa pee eitu aaisudori anaa olkibiroto anaa nkiyiotin neitu ae kata edol ewang'an?

English: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.
Masaai: Teine eishu ilarruok te nyamali, naa teine eyeng'iyeng'ieki iloonaurate.

English: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.
Masaai: Teine eyeng'iyeng'a ilooena tenebo; mening ninche ilo toilo lo loitasheiki esiai.

English: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.
Masaai: Etii ine ilooti netii sii ilkituaak, nelakuno osinka to loitore ninye.

English: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;
Masaai: “Ainyoo pee eishori ewang'an ilo otii engolikinoto, neishori enkishui ilo oata emion to ltau.

English: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;
Masaai: Ilo otayiewua to ltau keeya, nemelotu ninye, neturu ninye ninye oleng alang entoki nagol enkinyang'a naiteng'ela.

English: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
Masaai: Lelo ooshipa te nchipai sapuk oleng, neshipa tenetum ninche enkurare?

English: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie eishori ewang'an oltung'ani laa ore enkoitoi enye neisudoro, ilo oitamana Enkai olpaashe ninye.

English: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.
Masaai: Amu elotu enkiyang'ata anaa emukate ai, ore inkishirat aainei nebukunye anaa enkare.

English: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.
Masaai: Amu ore ina toki naure nanu nelotu shumata nanu, naadoiki nanu ina naitureisho.

English: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.
Masaai: Maata esidano te nkewan ai, nemaata sii engira, maata enkiyeng'iyeng; kake enyamali nalotu.”

English: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
Masaai: Ina pee ewal Elifas le Teman ajo:

English: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?
Masaai: “Amaa tenikishirraki oltung'ani airorie, igoro Naa kaing'ae oidim atigirayu eitu eiro.

English: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
Masaai: Ing'ura ituutayie lkumok, nintagolo inkaik nemeeta engolon.

English: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
Masaai: Ore irorei linono neitasheyie ilo orrorro nitipika engolon inkung naashal.

English: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
Masaai: Kake ore taata kitabaikia iyie, nimindim ating'iria; kimbung'a iyie nimimputukuny.

English: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?
Masaai: Amaa euriata ino Olaitoriani aime ninye empijan ino naa enkitashoto sidai oo nkoitoi inono ninye osiligi lino?

English: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
Masaai: “Tadamisho sii iyie, kalo ae kata ilo loo supati oidaayie? Anaa aitiaji ae kata etudung'oyioki, lelo ooitashe too sipat?

English: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.
Masaai: Ore anaa enatoduaa, ore lelo ooun entorroni; neun enyamali naa ninye ejung.

English: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.
Masaai: Ore te nkiyang'et e Nkai naa keidak, ore te ndarata e ng'oro enye neijori ninche.

English: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
Masaai: Ore ina kikurrukur o lng'atuny, o ilo toilo lo lng'atuny pushati, o lelo ala le lelo ng'atunyo ooti negili.

English: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.
Masaai: Ore ilo ng'atuny ogol neish te nkaraki natala entoki nanya, ore inkera e ng'atuny neidapashari.

English: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.
Masaai: “Aayakaki olomoni aakurraki, neng'amu enkiok ai ina king'oming'omakinoto.

English: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,
Masaai: Tiatua indamunot naaing'uaa induaat enkewarie, ina kata etijing'a injo naairoishi iltung'ana.

English: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.
Masaai: Nelotu shumata nanu enkuretisho sapuk olokirikiri ina naikirikirie iloik laainei pooki.

English: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:
Masaai: Nekut enkiyang'et enkomom ai, ore ilpapit lo sesen lai neitashe.

English: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
Masaai: Neitashe aauno kake eitu nanu amusu eneikununo. Etii apa enkitanyaanyukoto dukuya nkonyek aainei; netii engira, ina pee aning oltoilo:

English: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
Masaai: ‘Keidim oltung'ani oye ataa sinyati te dukuya Enkai? Keidim oltung'ani ataa sinyati te dukuya Olaitobirani lenye?

English: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:
Masaai: Ore doi ninye too laisiaayiak lenyena mepik ninye osiligi, ore ilmalaika lenyena neikenaki enkitadiata.

English: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?
Masaai: Kebaa elus lelo oomanya inkajijik esarng'ab laa ore olkitamanyunoto lenye netii atua enterit, lelo oorrarri anaa olasai.

English: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.
Masaai: Ore teneitoriti entadekenya o enteipa nemuti; neish ninche intarasi meeta hoo oloyiolo.

English: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.
Masaai: Nemuti aaya olng'obor lenye aimemuta ninche aaye, neton ake meeta engeno nagut?’

English: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?
Masaai: “Impotisho taata, ketii hoo obo liking'amaa iyie? Kalo obo loo sinyat imbelekenyakino iyie?

English: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.
Masaai: Esipa ore enkuretisho nalus naa kear olmodai ore olom near ilo lemeeta engeno.

English: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
Masaai: Atoduaa ilo modai enoto ntona, kake atasioko nanu adek emanyisho enye.

English: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.
Masaai: Ore ilayiok lenyena nelakuaniki eseriani, etumutaki ninche aaidaikie te kishomi, nemetii hoo obo oitajeu ninche.

English: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.
Masaai: Ore enkisampuare enye nenya lelo oota esumash, naa keya doi ninye aitayu tiatua ilkiku; ore iloota enkure neipang'ipang eing'oru enkarsisisho enye.

English: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
Masaai: Amu ore olosilisili neme enterit epukunye, ore enyamali neme te nkop ebulu.

English: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
Masaai: Kake etoikioki oltung'ani enyamali anaa enailep iltiil le nkima shumata.

English: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:
Masaai: “Ore nanu, naa kaing'oru Enkai, naa Enkai apik nanu enkoitoi ai.

English: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:
Masaai: Ilo oas isiaitin sapuki enking'asia nemejurrunoyu te nguton, intokitin kumok enking'asia nemeikenayu;

English: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:
Masaai: eisho ninye enchan metashaiki oriong enkop, neirriwaa inkariak metijing'a nkurman.

English: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.
