Masaai: Nedumu ailepie lelo oobor ore lelo ooishir nedumuni aailepakinye eneserian.

English: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
Masaai: Neitaa pesho nkitobirat e lelo loo losekin, metaa metum inkaik enye hoo dupoto.

English: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.
Masaai: Eya ninye lelo ng'eni to losek lenye maate, ore inkitobirat e lelo lo losek neiting'ie asioki.

English: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.
Masaai: Etum ninche enaimin te ndama, neirrapirrapisho enaipirie enkolong, anaa lootii atua enkewarie.

English: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
Masaai: Kake keitajeu lelo okishin too nkutukie enye; ore iloomena neitajeu te nkaina eilo magilani.

English: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
Masaai: Metaa keeta ilo aisinani osiligi, ore imbaa nemetii isipat nenuk enkutuk enye.

English: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:
Masaai: “Ing'ura, eshipa ilo tung'ani oisikong Enkai; metaa mimenaa ina kisikong'ata o eilo magilani.

English: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.
Masaai: Amu kepik ninye olbae, neitoki aen, neoshisho ninye kake aikinchiunye enkaina enye.

English: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
Masaai: Aikintajeu ninye iyie too nyamalaritin ile, ore tenaapishana nemeeta entorroni nikintoki aiseyie.

English: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.
Masaai: Ore to lameyu naa aikilaku iyie te keeya, ore to larrabal sapuk nikilaku aitung'uaa engolon eilo alem.

English: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
Masaai: Aikisudori iyie teina kirowuaj e ilo ng'ejep, nimiureyu enkidaaroto tenebau.

English: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
Masaai: Ore te mutata o to lameyu nikueni iyie, nimiureyu nena ng'uesi e nkop.

English: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
Masaai: Amu mikintanyamal isoito te wueji nitur, nimikintanyamal ing'uesi entim.

English: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.
Masaai: Iyiolou iyie ina kata ajo keserian olng'obor lino, naa ijur intare inono netii pooki elulung'a.

English: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
Masaai: Iyiolou sii ajo ore iishoritin inono naa keaku kumok, naa neijia etiu inkera eishoi ino, ebayu anaa inkujit enkop.

English: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.
Masaai: Ilo akenya enkurare ino itaa olpayian kitok, anaa enkano naku nabaiki ewueji neidong'ieki te nkata enye.

English: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
Masaai: Ng'ura, king'orutua kuna aajurru, naa kesipa. Toning'o, naa tayiolo ninye te nkaraki esidano nikiyaki.”

English: But Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo,

English: O that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!
Masaai: “Oi duoo tenaa kepiki entemet nainenengishoreki isinaitin laainei! te nebo enyamali ai pooki aaineneng.

English: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.
Masaai: Amu ina kata eaku keiroishi alang osinyai le naiposha; metaa, ekuetieki irorei laainei.

English: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
Masaai: Amu etii imbaa e ilo magilani atua nanu; neok oltau lai e sayiet enye; ore nena naaitureisho e Nkai neitoluaaki te dukuya nanu maataare.

English: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?
Masaai: Keru osikiria le ntim eeta olkujita, anaa olkiteng einosita olkujita.

English: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
Masaai: Amaa ina nemeeta entoki naishamu, keinosayu metii emunyan.

English: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.
Masaai: Maata esumash endaa naaijo ina, naa ore pooki toki nanya naaitamuoi.

English: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
Masaai: “Oi duoo tenaa katum entoki natoomonuo, naaisho Enkai eyieunoto ai,

English: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
Masaai: peyie eshipakino Enkai aapurd nanu, pee eitorioo enkaina enye, pee aadung'oo nanu aiwuang'ie.

English: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
Masaai: Ena naaku enkitagoloto ai; ekaipid doi ninye te nchipai hoo naata emion, amu eitu amiki lelo rorei Leilo Sinyati.

English: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?
Masaai: Ainyoo engolon ai metaa katon aanyu? Naa kainyoo enkiting'oto ai metaa katon ang'iri?

English: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?
Masaai: Amaa engolon ai keng'olon oo soito, arashu amaa osesen lai kolo suyai?

English: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?
Masaai: Ore te sipata maata nanu eretoto te kewan, naa ore pooki wueji natumie eretoto neterewaki aaitung'uaa enatii.

English: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
Masaai: “Ore ilo oibooyo esupatisho aitung'uaa olchore, naa keing'uaa euriata e ilo magilani.

English: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away;
Masaai: Ore lalashera laainei, neeta entorroni anaa nena ariak naatoyu neish.

English: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:
Masaai: Nena naamisimis too soito le nchan, oine neisudoriyie isoito le nchan ate.

English: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
Masaai: Ore te nkata enkirowuaj neimin. Ore teneirowuaju, neish te wueji enye.

English: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.
Masaai: Ore lelo apuayak neing'uaa inkoitoi enye, nepuo ninche olpurkel, neidak.

English: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.
Masaai: Ore lapuayak le Tema neing'oru ore lelo apuayak le Sheba neisiligu.

English: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.
Masaai: Neidang ninche amu eeta apa osiligi sapuk. Epuonu ninche ine neidang.

English: For now ye are no thing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.
Masaai: Neijia iyie itotiuo tena kata te nanu; idolita osina lai, niureishoyu.

English: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?
Masaai: Katejo doi, ‘Entaikiaki nanu enkishooroto?’ anaa, ‘Entaikiaki nanu te karsisisho inyi entoki nikiropiepie?’

English: Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?
Masaai: Aashu, ‘Tokorduaki nanu te nkaina e ilo mang'atinda lai?’ Arashu, ‘Talakuaki nanu te nkaina e ilo laaironyita?’

English: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
Masaai: “Nteng'enaki nanu naa kagira nanu; intayioloki nanu matoning'u enaikuna peyie apong'ori.

English: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?
Masaai: Kebaa enkiroishi oo rorei oosipa! Kake amaa doi ainyoo eutu eutaroto ino?

English: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?
Masaai: Idamu naaji ajo indim aiturrai irorei, aa ore ina kiroroto oltung'ani oiting'o osiligi naa enkijape?

English: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.
Masaai: Indim doi ninye atoosho enkukuo te lelo okishin nimipenyare ilamirak amir olchore lino.

English: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.
Masaai: “Kake ore taata, tishipakinoyioki niking'or nanu; amu malej enkomom ino.

English: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.
Masaai: Imbelekenyunye, aatasayia, mincho entorrono easayu, imbelekenyunye tena kata amu eiting'o osiligi lai.

English: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?
Masaai: Ketii olng'ejep lai emonkoi ake ninye pooki? Amaa enkishamisham aimemusu enyamali?

English: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?
Masaai: “Keitu etum oltung'ani esiaai nagol tioriong enkop, naa amaa inkolong'i enyena, aimetiu anaa inkolong'i oltung'ani oigero?

English: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:
Masaai: Anaa orrindik oyieu oleng oloip, anaa etiu anaa oltung'ani oigero oing'oru olekoisiayio lenye?

English: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
Masaai: Metaa ore too lapaitin pooki maata toki; naaishooki nanu inkewarieitin o sina.

English: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
Masaai: Ore tenairrag najo, ‘Kanu doi ade adumunye?’ kake ekeado enkewarie, naibelibelekenya omekenyu.

English: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.
Masaai: Ore osesen lai naairuja ilkuru o loirerio, negolu olchoni lo sesen lai, neitoki adanya.

English: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.
Masaai: Elang inkolong'i aainei erisioroto oo naipuko olkurragos, nepuonu aaiting meeta osiligi.

English: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
Masaai: “Tadamu ajo ore enkishui ai naa enkiyang'et, medol ae kata enkong'u ai esidano.

English: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
Masaai: Ore ina ong'u e ilo laadol maitoki adol ae kata; ore etii inkonyek inono shumata nanu, naa kaish.

English: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.
Masaai: Anaa enaisardaka enkatampoi neish, neijia etiu ilo olo enemeneng'a meitoki ailepu;

English: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
Masaai: meigil ae kata ninye ashukokino enkaji enye nemeitoki ewueji enye ayiolo ninye ae kata.

English: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
Masaai: “Metaa maitigir nanu enkutuk ai; ekairo te nkaraki emion oltau lai. Ekailepilep te nduaran oltau lai.

English: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?
Masaai: Kara nanu enaiposha arashu enkukuu e naiposha, metaa intobira iyie olarriponi te shumata nanu?

English: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
Masaai: Ore tenajo, ‘Ekaaitagol endapash ai, ekeitololong olorika lai enkilepilep ai’;

English: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:
Masaai: ina pee kinture nanu too nkidetidetat, nikinture nanu too nduaat.

English: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.
Masaai: Metaa kagelu engoroto o keeya aitalang iloik laainei.

English: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.
Masaai: Meekure eeta enkishui ai tipat, meekure abikoo intarasi. Entung'uayioki nanu amu ore inkolong'i aainei naa enkiyang'et.

English: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?
Masaai: Ainyoo doi oltung'ani metaa ing'orunye ninye toki, nipik endamunoto ino aitorioki ninye;

English: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?
Masaai: niparan ninye anaake tadekenya, nitem ninye pooki kata?

English: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
Masaai: Kerishata naba aa miwuang'ie enkomom ino te nanu, anaa kipal nanu matoijoi nkamulak.

English: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?
Masaai: Amaa tenaas eng'oki, kaa aaitaas iyie, iyie olaing'urani loo ltung'ana? Ainyoo peyie kitisirua nanu? Ainyoo peyie ataa olola te iyie?

English: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie mikipalaki inkitarruorrot aainei niya aitalamaa intorrok aainei? Amu ore tena kata naa kairrag tiatua enkop; aiking'oru iyie nanu nematii.

English: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Bildad le Shushi awal ajo:

English: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
Masaai: “Kerishata naba aa ijo kuna baa, ore irorei le nkutuk ino netiu anaa osiwuo kitok?

English: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
Masaai: Amaa, kemerregel Enkai esipata? Amaa kemerregel Olmagilani enasipa.

English: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
Masaai: Amaa tenetaasa inkera inono eng'oki aaitaas ninye, eitarasayie ninye ninche apik engolon oo ntorrok enye.

English: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
Masaai: Tening'oru iyie Enkai, nisai iyie ilo Magilani;

English: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
Masaai: tenaa aira sinyati nintashe too sipat, nesipa katukul inchere ekedumunye ninye te nkaraki iyie; nikilaaki ninye iyie te wueji neishaakino tinimany.

English: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
Masaai: Neaku ore hoo duoo naa kiti apa enkiterunoto ino, keaku inkolong'i inono naapuonu sapuki oleng.

English: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
Masaai: “Amu inkilikuanu, aatoomono too lporori ooshomo, nijurru ayiolou nena naanoto iloo papa;

English: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)
Masaai: amu ore iyiook nikira ile ng'ole, nimikiyiolo pito, amu ore inkolong'i ang tioriong enkop naa oloip.

English: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
Masaai: “Aimikinteng'en ninche iyie, nikiliki iyie, nelimu irorei tening'unoto enye?

English: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?
Masaai: Keidim enarau atubulu te wueji nemetii olkishakual? Keidim oseyiai atubulu tewueji nemetii enkare?

English: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.
Masaai: Ore eton aa entapukai eitu edung'i, netoyu ninche engor ae aitubului ake.

English: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:
Masaai: Neijia etiu inkoitoi e lelo pooki oorikino Enkai amu ore osiligi le lelo tung'ana lemeeta Enkai naa keidak.

English: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web.
Masaai: Ore enkirukoto osiligi lenye negila ina kata naa neijia etiu osiligi lenye le nkaji olkedi.

English: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.
Masaai: Eirishakino ninye enkaji enye nemeitashe ina aji; eibung ninye ina aji enye, kake meitashe.

English: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
Masaai: Ebulu iltung'ana torrok anaa entiati natii ewueji netii enkolong, neibulaa ilukuny aaidapashakino enkurma enye.

English: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.
Masaai: Ore intona enye neman aaen isoito, neton ninye tiatua lelo soito akurrakino.

English: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
Masaai: Naa teneari aamut ninye te wueji enye, naa kemiki ninye, ejoki ‘Eitu ae kata aadol.’

English: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.
Masaai: Ing'ura, ena enchipai enkoitoi enye; nepuku tiatua enkop kulie aabulu.

English: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:
Masaai: “Ing'ura, meany Enkai oltung'ani lemeeta entioto, nemeng'amaa enkaina oo laasak loo ntorrok.

English: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.
Masaai: Aikintoki ninye aigil aiput enkutuk ino enkuenia nepik enkutuk ino embuakunoto.

English: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.
Masaai: Ore lelo likimba iyie naa keishopokini ninche enkurruna, ore ilo ng'obor loo ltorrok, nemeitokini aata.”

English: Then Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo:

English: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?
Masaai: “Esipa kayiolo ajo neijia etiu: Kake kaji eiko oltung'ani teneaku supat te dukuya Enkai?

English: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.
Masaai: Amaa teneyieu obo nekeshare ninye, meeta obo oidim atawaliki ninye kata nabo too nkatitin enkalifu nabo.

English: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?
Masaai: Aing'en ninye to ltau, naa magilani te ngolon, aing'ae oidima aitagolo kewan ataarare ninye, nemir ninye?

English: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.
Masaai: Ilo odotu ildoinyo, nemeyiolo ninche ina, tenenang'aa ninye ninche te ng'oro enye,

English: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
Masaai: ilo oigusugusie enkop aitung'uaa ewueji enye, neikirikirie ing'apeta enyena

English: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.
Masaai: ilo oitanap enkolong, meitoki ailepu; ilo oitoip ilakir,

English: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.
Masaai: ilo laa ninye ake openy oisalaash keper, neroruaa apurd ilopir le naiposha;

English: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.
Masaai: ilo oitobirua entukus oo lakir naji olng'arurumi, o enaji orion, o enaji Pledes, o entukus oo lakir le kopikop.

English: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
Masaai: Ilo oas isiaitin sapuki nena naagiroo ening'unoto, o ntokitin enking'asia nemeeta esiana.

English: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
Masaai: Ing'ura eim embata ai, nemadol ninye; eloolo dukuya, nemaning'u ninye.

English: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?
Masaai: Ng'ura, ewuapaa ninye aiwuang'ie, aing'ae oidim aibooi ninye, Aing'ae ojoki ninye, ‘Ainyoo iyasita iyie?’

English: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.
Masaai: “Meshuk Enkai siadi engoro enye; ore tiabori ninye eirrugo ilaretok le Rahab.

English: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?
Masaai: Kaji naa aiko tenawaliki ninye, agelu irorei laainei te nebo ninye?

English: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.
Masaai: Ore hoo nemaata entorroni, mawaliki ninye; ekaomonu olng'ur to Laitang'oroni lai.

English: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.
Masaai: Tenairorie ninye naawaliki nanu, mairuk ajo keinining'ito ninye oltoilo lai.

English: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.
Masaai: Amu kaar nanu to lkutati ogol neponaa ilbaa laainei meeta emporeet.

English: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.
Masaai: Maaisho ninye nanu mayagie, kake kaaiput ninye nanu emion.

English: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?
Masaai: Ore tenaa kenkesha engolon, ng'ura ninye! Naa tenaa kembae naipirta esipata aing'ae oidim aterewa ninye meshomo?

English: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
Masaai: Ore hoo nemaata entioto, naa keiguanareki enkutuk ai; ore hoo nemaata entioto, naa kaaitaa nanu olopaashari.

English: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
Masaai: Maata nanu entioto; mang'or nanu kewan; meekure aatayie enkishui ai tipat.

English: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
Masaai: Etaa pooki nabo; metaa atejo, emut ninye ilo lemeeta entioto o lelo torrok.

English: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.
Masaai: Tenelo neyau olbuket keeya aitasieku, nekueniyie engolikinoto e ilo lemeeta entioto.

English: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?
Masaai: Eishooki enkop enkaina e ilo torrono; eimulumul inkomomi oo laiguanak lenyena. Amaa teneme ninye, aing'ae naa ninye?

English: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.
Masaai: “Eten inkolong'i aainei aalang oltung'ani oipirri; eisik aailanyisho, medol ninche esidano.

English: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.
Masaai: Eish enkishui ai anaa emeli nakuet oleng, anaa olkurragos odoiki aibung entoki nainos.

English: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:
Masaai: Tenajo, ‘Madamu nanu enking'unyung'uny ai, ekaiwuang'ie esototo enkomom ai, naaku oloota enchipai’;

English: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
Masaai: naureishoyu oleng te nkaraki inyamalaritin aainei, amu ayiolo ajo, mikintaa iyie nanu olemeeta entioto.

English: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
Masaai: Ekaaku oloiguanareki; kainyoo naa peyie aasisho te mpesho?

English: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;
Masaai: Tenaituku kewan te ntoki naibor anaa enturoto, naituku inkaik aainei to sabuni ogol.

English: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.
Masaai: Naa aikinang'aki ake iyie nanu engumoto, ore ninye inkilani aainei naaibayu nanu.

English: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.
Masaai: Amu ime oltung'ani ninye anaa nanu, metaa kaidim atawaliki ninye, metaa aikipuonu metetemi iyiook te nebo.

English: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.
Masaai: Metii olarishani erishata ang, oidim aiteleiki enkaina enye shumata iyiook.

English: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:
Masaai: Inchoo ninye eiwuang'ie eng'udi enye te shumata nanu, nimincho engoro enye aaiture nanu.

English: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
Masaai: Ina peyie aaitieu airoro imbaa enyena maata enkuretisho amu ime neijia atiu tiatua enkewan ai.

English: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
Masaai: “Aibayie enkishui ai tukul; ekaisho enkiroroto e pesho enking'unyung'uny ai; ekairo tiatua emion oltau lai.

English: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.
Masaai: Ekajoki nanu Enkai, mikidung'oki nanu enkiguana; intayioloki nanu nchere ainyoo peyie kiarare nanu.

English: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
Masaai: Idol aa sidai te iyie tinikimbooki enkop, pee imenaa esiaai oo nkaik inono, nincho omom inkitobirat e lelo torrok?

English: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?
Masaai: Iyata iyie inkonyek o sesen? Idol iyie anaa enadol tung'ani.

English: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man's days,
Masaai: Amaa inkolong'i inono ketiu anaa inkolong'i e tung'ani arashu ilarin linono ketiu anaa ilarin le tung'ani?

English: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?
Masaai: Metaa ing'oru aturu ingok aainei, nijurru ingok aainei.

English: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.
Masaai: Ore hoo duoo nayiolo ajo iyiolo ajo maata entioto, nemeetae hoo obo oidim aitajeu too nkaik inono?

English: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
Masaai: Enkaina ino naaitobirua nanu; nikinyaaka taata aibelekenyakino nanu aaidaikie.

English: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?
Masaai: Tadamu ajo kintobirua apa nanu te nterit, naa aikintoki aigil arrinyoki nanu enterit?

English: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
Masaai: Keitu iyie kibuku nanu anaa kule nikimposhu nanu anaa eng'orno?

English: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.
Masaai: Kinchopo nanu to lchoni o to sesen nikirip nanu aitutum iloik omorlooishi.

English: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
Masaai: Kinchoo nanu enkishui o enyorrata nauno; ore erripoto ino netorripo oltau lai.

English: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.
Masaai: Naa ore nena tokitin nisudoyie tiatua oltau lino; ayiolo ajo ena apa eyieuna ino.

English: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
Masaai: Tenaas eng'oki, nikiut nanu, nimikipalaki nanu entorroni ai.

English: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
Masaai: Na tenara oltorrono, oi kewan ai. Naa tenara osupat, nemashumu elukunya ai, amu aabore enkurruna, naing'or olosilisil lai.

English: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.
Masaai: Naa tenadumu kewan ailepie, niking'oru nanu anaa olng'atuny ore ake sii nias inenking'asia enkaraki nanu;

English: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.
Masaai: intang'ejuk shakenisho ino tenkaraki nanu, niponaa engoro ino aitubulu tenkaraki nanu, niyau ilororani ng'ejuko maatigilunore nanu.

English: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!
Masaai: “Ainyoo peyie kiyaua nanu aitupuku te ng'uset? Enaikash apa tenatua eitu aadol toki,

English: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
Masaai: natiu anaa aimaatae apa aekata. Aatanapaki te ng'uset aaya enkurare.

English: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
Masaai: Aimekuti inkolong'i enkishui ai? Tapalaki nanu, pee atum anoto enkiti kiyagata.

English: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
Masaai: Eton eitu alo ine nemashukunore ina kop engoro natii enaimin nagut,

English: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.
Masaai: enkop engoro o longolingoli naa ore ewang'an netiu anaa enaimin.”

English: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Sofa le Naamat awal, ajo:

English: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?
Masaai: “Keishori irorei kumok meshomo eitu ewali, neishori oltung'ani oiro oleng esipata?

English: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
Masaai: Ijo doi keitigir enkiratirat ino iltung'ana, naa tininya kutuk ajo miata entioto, aimeeta obo likintukurru iyie?

English: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
Masaai: Amu ijoito, ‘Ore enkiteng'enare ai naa kesila, nara sinyati te dukuya nkonyek e Nkai.’

English: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;
Masaai: Kake ore duoo tenaa keiro Enkai, nikiboloki ninye enkutuk enye,

English: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
Masaai: naa aikiliki ninye iyie inkisudorot eng'eno nagut! Amu kitok ening'unoto enye. Tayiolo nchere aikiririki Enkai nkuti nemeba anaa nkitarruorot inono.

English: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
Masaai: “Indim atayiolo intokitin naagut naaipirta Enkai? Indim atayiolo ineebaiki Olmagilani?

English: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?
Masaai: Ekeilep oleng aalang keper, kainyoo indim ataasa? Egut alang enemeneng'a, kainyoo indim atayiolo?

English: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
Masaai: Ore entemet enye neado alang enkop, nelala alang enaiposha.

English: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?
Masaai: Amaa teneimaa ninye enkop, neenaa olorere, neipotu adung'oki enkiguana aing'ae oidim aibooi ninye?

English: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?
Masaai: Amu eyiolo Enkai lelo tung'ana lemeeta tipat; amaa tenedol ninye entorroni, aimeshilaa ninye?

English: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass's colt.
Masaai: Kake ore oltung'ani omoda naa ketum ening'unoto; oo teneini olkurrarru le ntim aa tung'ani.

English: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;
Masaai: Tenintorioki oltau lino esipata, nilak nkaik inono aitorioki ninye.

English: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.
Masaai: Tenetii entorroni enkaina ino, iwuang'ie intalamai, nimincho intorrok emany atua ilng'oborri linono.

English: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
Masaai: Nesipayu katukul ina kata nchere idumu enkomom ino metii entioto; iyaku oloserian, nimiureishoyu.

English: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:
Masaai: Naa aikirikino osina lino; idamu ninye anaa inkariak naatulusoitie.

English: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.
Masaai: Ore enkishon ino newang'u alang enaiwulie enkolong; ore enaimin enye netiu anaa entadekenya.

English: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
Masaai: Naa aitum empijan amu etii osiligi; naa aikirripi nilo ayeng'iyeng'a te seriani.

English: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
Masaai: Irraga airura, nemeeta likae likipik enkuretisho; eomonu ilkumok omom ino.

English: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.
Masaai: Kake ore inkonyek oltorrono nemeitoki aadolisho. Ore enkoitoi pooki naaisikie naa keimin te ninche, ore osiligi lenye neyang enabayie.

English: And Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo,

English: No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
Masaai: “Meeta inchere irara iltung'ana, naa keish eng'eno nagut te intae tiniyeye.

English: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
Masaai: Kake kaata ening'unoto anaa intae; madou sii doi nanu te ntae. Aing'ae lemeyiolo intokitin naaijo kuna?

English: I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.
Masaai: Ara nanu entoki nakueniyieki too ilchoreta laainei, nanu, ilo oipoto Enkai naawaliki ninye nanu, oltung'ani supat lemeeta entioto, ataa entoki nakueniyieki.

English: He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
Masaai: Ore tiatua ndamunot oo ltung'ana lemeeta enyamali olmena te lelo ootijing'a olbuket ioshiosho oltung'ani letaa kejo pee ebatata openy.

English: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
Masaai: Ore ilng'oborri loo laikonyak neeta eseriani, ore lelo ooitagor Enkai neserian, lelo ooen Enkai enye aapik enkaina enye.

English: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:
Masaai: “Kake inkilikuana ing'uesi, naa aikinteng'en ninche iyie, ore nena motonyi o loing'ang'e, naa aikiliki ninche iyie;

English: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
Masaai: arashu inkaitubulu e nkop, naa aikinteng'en iyie; ore lelo sinkir le naiposha naa aikimbalakinye iyie.

English: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?
Masaai: Kaa te kuna pooki nemeyiolo ajo, enkaina Olaitoriani nataasa ena.

English: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.
Masaai: Etii atua enkaina enye enkishui e pooki toki naishu, netii enkiyang'et e pooki tung'ani.

English: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?
Masaai: Aimetem enkiok irorei, anaa enatem enoret endaa?

English: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.
Masaai: Etii eng'eno nagut atua emoruo, ore ening'unoto netii atua enkadori oo nkolong'i.

English: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.
Masaai: Atua Enkai etii eng'eno nagut o emagilanisho; eeta eutaroto o ening'unoto.

English: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
Masaai: Tenesulaki enkop, nemeetae oloidim atesheta; teneikenoo oltung'ani tiatua, meetae oloidim atabolo.

English: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
Masaai: Teneibooyo inkariak, netoyu pooki; teneirriwaa aipang'ie, nenum enkop.

English: With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.
Masaai: Atua ninye etii engolon o eng'eno nagut; ore ilo oleji o lolejisho naa ilenyena.

English: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.
Masaai: Eiwuang'ie ilautarok meeta toki, neitaa ilarishak ilmoda.

English: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.
Masaai: Eitadoyio ilaiguanak, neitaa ninche ilooena, neeniki impolosi enye enkimeita.

English: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.
Masaai: Etorikoyie ilapolosak meeta toki nenang'aa lelo magil.

English: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.
Masaai: Emitiki enkiroroto lelo oisiligayu neya aoru emusunoto lelo tung'ana kituaak.

English: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.
Masaai: Ebukoki enkurruna lelo kituaak, neitololong ina kimeita e ilo ogol.

English: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
Masaai: Eibalunye nena naagut e naimin, neyau enaimin nagut apik ewang'an.

English: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.
Masaai: Eitaa ninye iloreren kituaak, neitoki aidakie ninche, eitasapuk iloreren, nerikoo aiwuang'ie.

English: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
Masaai: Eya aiwuang'ie ening'unoto too laiguanak le nkop, neisho ninche metilimanata to lpurkel lemetii enkoitoi.

English: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
Masaai: Eirrapirrapisho ninche te naimin metii ewang'an neesiesari anaa olamerani.

English: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it.
Masaai: Ing'ura, etoduaa enkong'u ai kuna pooki, etoning'o enkiok ai nening'u ninye.

English: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
Masaai: Ore ina niyiolo nayiolo sii nanu, maaure iyie tukul.

English: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.
Masaai: Kake ekairorie Olmagilani, nayieu naishankarra embae ai te Nkai.

English: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
Masaai: Ore iyie, nikitumuraki te nturoto e lejare irara intae pooki ilabaak le pesho.

English: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.
Masaai: Oi duoo tenaa intirring'a agira, naa keaku ina eng'eno ino nagut!

English: Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
Masaai: Inining'u tena kata embae najo, nining'u olkiyioi oing'uaa enkutuk ai.

English: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?
Masaai: Indim airoro emonkoi aipirie Enkai niro to losek tenkaraki ninye?

English: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?
Masaai: Indim aitodolu olkep te ninye indim atoomonu ororei te ninye?

English: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?
Masaai: Kesipa aisidai te iyie tenikituru ninye iyie aing'oru? Arashu aindim ateleja ninye, anaa enalej oltung'ani olikae?

English: He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.
Masaai: Aikisikong ninye iyie katukul tenaa intodolu olkep too nkisudorot.

English: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?
Masaai: Amaa enkitoo enye aimikinture iyie, o engoro enye tinikibatatakino iyie?

English: Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.
Masaai: Ore indung'eta inono e rashe kumok netiu anaa inkuruon, ore enchankar ino netiu anaa enterit.

English: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will.
Masaai: “Nchooki nanu matigirayu, naitoki airo, naa inchoo aatum pooki naaba enaa enaatum.

English: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?
Masaai: Ekapik enkishui ai batisho, nchoo aiwuang'ie enkishui ai.

English: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo kaar ninye matua, aaiting'o osiligi kake kamitu inkoitoi aainei te dukuya enkomom enye.

English: He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.
Masaai: Ena naaku enjeunoto ai, inchere melotu oltung'ani lemeeta Enkai dukuya ninye.

English: Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.
Masaai: Inining'u tukurraki irorei laainei, nincho embae nalimu aibalie ejing'u inkiyiaa inono.

English: Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.
Masaai: Ng'ura, aitobira enkiguana ai; ayiolo ajo aata esipata.

English: Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.
Masaai: Aing'ae ilo laalotu akeshare nanu? Amu ina kata agira nanu naye.

English: Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.
Masaai: Intokitin are ake inchooki nanu, nemaitoki aisudoo kewan te nkomom ino:

English: Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.
Masaai: iwuang'ie enkaina ino intalamai te nanu, nimincho olkirutoto lino aaiture nanu.

English: Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.
Masaai: Nimpotisho iyie, naawaliki nanu, oi inchooki nanu mairoro, nikiwaliki iyie nanu.

English: How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.
Masaai: Kaja esiana oo ntorrok aainei o ng'ok aainei? Intayioloki nanu intorrok aainei o eng'oki ai.

English: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie isudoo enkomom ino, nikinkenaa nanu anaa olmang'atinta lino?

English: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
Masaai: Isujaa iyie embeneyio nayaita osiwuo, nimir errarrati natoyio?

English: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.
Masaai: Amu ingero iyie mbaa e mion te nkaraki nanu, nikintijing nanu entorroni e kitisho ai.

English: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.
Masaai: Itipika nkejek aainei ilpisia, ningor inkoitoi aainei pooki, itipika ienat ndapi oo nkejek aainei.

English: And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.
Masaai: Eidaaya tung'ani anaa entoki natong'ua anaa enkila nainosa oriri.

English: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
Masaai: Ore tung'ani otoiwuo enkitok naa oloo nkolong'i kuti, nebore enyamali.

English: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
Masaai: Epuku abulu anaa entapukai, netoyu; nelo anaa oloip, nemeitoki alo.

English: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?
Masaai: Naa aibol inkonyek inono aboloki olaaijo ilo, niyau ninye atua enkiguana ino.

English: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
Masaai: Aing'ae oidim ayau entoki naiduruk tiatua enemeiduruk?

English: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
Masaai: Ore amu etuutuaki aaibalie inkolong'i enyena, ore esiana oo lapaitin lenyena niata iyie, nituutua ineebaiki metaa meidim aima.

English: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.
Masaai: Mintoki aing'or ninye, tapala ninye inchoo ninye eshipakino enkishui enye nagol, tenaa keidim.

English: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
Masaai: Eeta olchani otudung'oki osiligi, tenedung'i, naa keitoki abulu, nemetoyu intapuka enyena.

English: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;
Masaai: Ore hoo tenemusanu intona enyena tiatua enkop, netoyu aye olchani lenye tiatua enkop.

English: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.
Masaai: Kake ore ake peyie etum enkiti are nepok; nepuku ilng'osil anaa enkiti aitubului.

English: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
Masaai: Kake keye oltung'ani, neirragieki aaitadoyio tiabori; eyang oltung'ani enabayie, naa koree ninye?

English: As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:
Masaai: Ore anaa enasulunye inkariak te naiposha, neish oreyiet netoyu.

English: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
Masaai: Neijia etiu oltung'ani eirrag nemeitoki adumunye; o metaa meetae keper, meitoki adumunye, arashu edumuni aaitung'uaa injo enyena.

English: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
Masaai: Oi naaji tenaa aikisudoo nanu te nemeneng'a, nikisudoo nanu ometogiroi engoro ino, metaa aikigelaki nanu erishata niyiolo, nikidamu nanu!

English: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
Masaai: Amaa teneye oltung'ani keitoki apiu aigil? Ore inkolong'i aainei pooki esiaai ai naa kaanyu. Ometabau elakunoto ai.

English: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.
Masaai: Impotisho iyie naa kaairuk nanu iyie, iyieu oleng esiaai oo nkaik inono.

English: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?
Masaai: Amu ina kata inken iroruat aainei, nimintoki aing'or ingok aainei;

English: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.
Masaai: ore intorrok aainei neripari aaikenoo to lbene, naa aintemoo aimulumulaa ingok aainei.

English: And surely the mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place.
Masaai: “Kake esulunye ildoinyo nerrarra aaishunye, neitayuni indapidapo too wuejitin enye.

English: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.
Masaai: Neoroo inkariak isoito, neoroo olairrag le nkare enterit, metaa iishie iyie osiligi le tung'ani.

English: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
Masaai: Itimira oltung'ani nitii shumata ninye ntarasi. Itumuguta enkomom enye nireu ninye aitalamaa.

English: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
Masaai: Epuonu ilayiok lenyena aayanyit, nemeyiolo ninye; eyawuaki ninche abori, neitu emusu aayiolou.

English: But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.
Masaai: Emion ake osesen lenye ening'ito, naa kewan ake eishiraki.”

English: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Elifas le Tema awal ajo:

English: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?
Masaai: “Amaa oltung'ani ng'en, keishaakino newal te ng'eno e nkijape, neiput kewan te nkijape oloosaen?

English: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
Masaai: Keishankarra ninye te nkiroroto nemeeta tipat, arashu too rorei lemeidim aitaasa ae sidai?

English: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.
Masaai: Kake igira aitalamaa ina uriata e Nkai, nimbooyo enkibirribirrata te dukuya Enkai.

English: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
Masaai: Amu ingok inono naaiteng'en enkutuk ino, nigelu olng'ejep le lejare.

English: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
Masaai: Enkutuk ino makewan nikidung'oki iyie enkiguana, mme nanu, nikinchakenoki iyie enkutuk ino makewan.

English: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?
Masaai: “Aiyie doi apa oltung'ani le dukuya otoiwuoki? Arashu aikiyawuaki apa eton meetae ildoinyo?

English: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?
Masaai: Inining'ishe iyie tiatua enkiguana Enkai? Naa amaa eng'eno nagut intodorrop aiririki enkorrok ino ake?

English: What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?
Masaai: Ainyoo doi iyiolo iyie nimikiyiolo iyiook? Ainyoo doi ining'u iyie nemeibala te iyiook?

English: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
Masaai: Eboitare iyiook lelo ooibor lukuny, tenebo lelo kituaak te iyiook. Ilaa kituaak ninche te papaai lino:

English: Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?
Masaai: Amaa nkilejilej e Nkai a kutiti te iyie, oo ilo rorei likirorie iyie te mborron?

English: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie incho oltau lino mikitanapa aitalamaa, naa ainyoo peyie incho inkonyek inono eirriap?

English: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?
Masaai: Nimbelekeny oltau lino aarare Enkai, nincho irorei ootiu neijia epuku te nkutuk ino?

English: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
Masaai: Ainyoo doi oltung'ani metaa keidim ataa olemeiduruk? Arashu ilo otoiwuo enkitok, metaa keidim ataa supat?

English: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.
Masaai: Ing'ura, mepik Enkai osiligi isinyat lenyena, nemesinya keper too nkonyek enyena;

English: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?
Masaai: kebaa engoroto e ilo lo lminong, naa arruoni, oltung'ani ook intorrok anaa enkare!

English: I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;
Masaai: “Ekaaitodol nanu iyie ininingoki nanu; ore ina natoduaa naa kaibalunye.

English: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:
Masaai: (Ina natolimutuo iltung'ana le ngeno nagut, neitu eisudoo iloomenye,

English: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.
Masaai: ilo laa ninye ake eishooki ina kop, nemeetae olomoni oimayie ninche.)

English: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.
Masaai: Etoyu oltung'ani torrono te mion enye too nkolong'i enyena pooki, tiatua lelo arin pooki ooirragieki, te nkaraki ilo lemeeta olng'ur.

English: A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
Masaai: Etii inkiyiaa enyena iltoiloishi ooitureisho; ore etudupe, nelotu oloidaikie shumata ninye.

English: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.
Masaai: Meiruk ninye ajo keitoki arrinyo aing'uaa enaimin. Naa olalem elo ninye aitingoki.

English: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Masaai: Elimana ninye te nkop pooki eing'oru endaa ejo, ‘Kaji etii?’ Eyiolo ajo etabawua enkolong enaimin, etabaikia ninye;

English: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
Masaai: ore osina o emion neiture ninye; nebaiki ninye anaa olaiguanani otanape pee elo olarrabal.

English: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.
Masaai: Amu eitorioyie ninye enkaina enye aarare Enkai, neyaki esarkionisho ilo Magilani.

English: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:
Masaai: Ekuetiki ninye te ngolong'akinoto aarare ninye, eibung elong'o enye nairrusha o lwuasa.

English: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.
Masaai: Amu eteijia enkomom enye te mpiron neirrag enkurriny too lairakuj lenyena.

English: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.
Masaai: Netamanya inkanas mijoonto, atua nkajijik nememanya, apa naatudung'okoki enkiguana metaa osototi loo suut;

English: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.
Masaai: meaku ninye karsis, nemebikoo karsisisho enye nemetum intona tiatua enkop.

English: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.
Masaai: Meilany ninye enaimin, ore olang'at le nkima neitoi imbenek enyena ore enkipilipil enye naa kekutaa osiwuo.

English: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.
Masaai: Mincho ninye epik osiligi lenye entoki nemeetae, alej kewan; amu ore entoki nemeetae naa keaku elaakinoto enye.

English: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.
Masaai: Ekelaki te lulung'ata eng'or enkata enye, ore olng'osila lenye nemenyoriju.

English: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.
Masaai: Keipiripiroo ninye lelo sabibu lenyena leitu eku, anaa ilo shani lenye, neiturraa adung'oo esidano enye anaa oloirien.

English: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
Masaai: Amu ore encholiek e lelo lemeeta Enkai naa koolupi. Naa keidaikie enkima ilo ng'obor lo loropisho.

English: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.
Masaai: Enutayu ninche too ntorrok, neiu ingok ore oltau lenye neitobiru elejare.

English: Then Job answered and said,
Masaai: Ina peyie ewal Yoab ejo:

English: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.
Masaai: “Atoning'o nanu intokitin kumok naatiu neija; irara pooki ilaitagolok te nkata o sina.

English: Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest?
Masaai: Amaa irorei le nkijape keeta enkiting'oto? Arashu ainyoo doi nikintagoro peyie iwalu?

English: I also could speak as ye do: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.
Masaai: Ekaidim sii nanu airoro anaa iyie, tenaa naaji itii erishata ai anaata aitulus irorei tenebo pee aagilunore naigusugusie elukunya ai te iyie.

English: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage your grief.
Masaai: Ekaaitagol iyie te nkutuk ai, ore enkitagoloto e nkiroroto ai neiwuang'ie emion ino.

English: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and though I forbear, what am I eased?
Masaai: “Tenairo nemeish emion ai, naa amaa tenangiri, kebaa emion naaing'uaa nanu?

English: But now he hath made me weary: thou hast made desolate all my company.
Masaai: Esipa taata aatalepuo Enkai tukul; eitomijoono ninye encholiek ai pooki.

English: And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face.
Masaai: Kimbung'a iyie nanu akurraki; ira iyie olmang'atinta lai. Ara nanu endapana o loik neibung'a iltung'ana ina pee eishakenoki entorroni ai.

English: He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.
Masaai: Aatopolosa ninye te ng'oro enye, naaibayu nanu; etoonyo ninye ilala te nkaraki nanu. Ore olmang'atinta lai naakurraki inkonyek enyena.

English: They have gaped upon me with their mouth; they have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully; they have gathered themselves together against me.
Masaai: Aatusurdaanya iltung'ana nanu too nkutukie enye, aatoosho ninche nanu eseder, eiturrurrote pooki peyie aarare nanu.

English: God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.
Masaai: Aaishooyie nanu Enkai aitarasaki lelo lemeure Enkai, naanang'aki nanu nkaik e lelo arruok.

English: I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.
Masaai: Atonita apa te seriani, kake aaibung'a ninye nanu olgos, naadung'udung aitaa ndung'ot. Aaitasheyie ninye nanu aitaa oloitoriokino lenye.

English: His archers compass me round about, he cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground.
Masaai: Aamanita nanu imbaa enyena naatang'oruo te pooki shoto, etangoro apolol ilairakuj laainei, nemepal nebukoki olodua lai enkop.

English: He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant.
Masaai: Aarasaki ninye naapik ilbaa katitin kumok naakuetiki ninye nanu anaa olmurrani.

English: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and defiled my horn in the dust.
Masaai: Atiripaka ilkuniyiani osesen lai, neirragie engolon ai tiatua enterit.

English: My face is foul with weeping, and my eyelids is the shadow of death;
Masaai: Etodoro enkomom ai te nkishirata, netiu inkonito aainei o nkonyek anaa enaimin nagut;

English: Not for any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure.
Masaai: ore hoo nemetii olarrabal inkaik aainei, naa kesila enkomono ai.

English: O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place.
Masaai: Na kop, minukaa osarge lai, nimincho enkishirata ai etum eneeng'iyeng'are.

English: Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high.
Masaai: Ore doi ninye tena kata ng'ura, etii olchakeni lai keper, peyie eitashe terishata ai.

English: My friends scorn me: but mine eye poureth out tears unto God.
Masaai: Kaasurdaany ilchoreta laainei; ore inkonyek aainei nebukoki Enkai ilkiyio.

English: Oh that one might plead for a man with God, as a man pleadeth for his neighbour!
Masaai: Metaa ekeitasheyie esipata e tung'ani o e Nkai, anaa ina oltung'ani tenebo ole latia enye.

English: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.
Masaai: Amu ore eetuo ilkuti arin, ekalo aim enkoitoi nemaitoki ashukunye.

English: My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me.
Masaai: “Etigile oltau lai, eishunye inkolong'i aainei, etataana enkurare te nanu.

English: Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?
Masaai: Esipa etii tenebo nanu ilasukenyak, ore inkonyek aainei netii esurdaany enye.

English: Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me?
Masaai: Irragie elakunoto ai te kewan ino; kalo likae om aishoru elakunoto te nkaraki nanu.

English: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt them.
Masaai: Ore amu inkeno indamunot enye peyie mening'u, mincho naa ninche meisula.

English: He that speaketh flattery to his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.
Masaai: Ore ilo okaldaa ilchoreta lenyena too mpisai, pee etum erubata oo masaa enye, naa kemodoku nkera enyena.

English: He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret.
Masaai: Aaitaa ninye nanu entoki naimakini too loreren; nara obo le lelo oonotaki iltung'ana.

English: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members are as a shadow.
Masaai: Eiliilaitie inkonyek aainei te nkaraki olkiyioi lo sina, ore irubat o sesen lai netiu anaa oloip.

English: Upright men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.
Masaai: Ore lelo ooitashe too sipat neing'asia tena, ore ilo lemeeta entioto neitagor kewan te lelo lemeure Enkai.

English: The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.
Masaai: Kake ore isupati nekurraki enkoitoi enye, ore ilo oota inkaik nemeiduruk nebulaa agolu.

English: But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find one wise man among you.
Masaai: Kake ore intae enyaaki wootu intae pooki, nematum nanu oltung'ani ng'en te ntae pooki.

English: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the thoughts of my heart.
Masaai: Etulusoitie inkolong'i aainei, ore nkitobirat aainei netudung'oyioki aaituraa, o nena yieunot oltau lai.

English: They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness.
Masaai: Eitaa ninche enaimin endama; ‘Ore ewang'an, anaa enajo ninche, netaaniki enaimin.’

English: If I wait, the grave is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.
Masaai: Tenaing'oru enemeneng'a aitaa enkaji ai, tenaisalaash olorika lai te naimin,

English: I have said to corruption, Thou art my father: to the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister.
Masaai: Tenajoki enkurare, ‘Ira iyie papa lai’ najoki ilo kurto, ‘Ira yeiyio lai’; arashu ‘Enkanashe ai,’

English: And where is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?
Masaai: koree naa teine osiligi lai? Aing'ae odol osiligi lai?

English: They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when our rest together is in the dust.
Masaai: Kelo ninye atua ine netii iloom le nemeneng'a? Amaa aikidoyio pokira aapuo atua enterit.

English: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Bildad le Shuhit awal, ejo:

English: How long will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.
Masaai: Kenkata nabaa iyie ing'oru irorei? Tujurru, ina peyie kiro.

English: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight?
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie eikenari iyiook anaa nkishu? Ainyoo peyie kira iyiook lmoda te dukuya iyie?

English: He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place?
Masaai: Iyie ilo opolos kewan te ngoro ino, keing'uari enkop te nkaraki iyie, arashu eiwuang'ieki endapidapoi aaitung'uaa ewueji enye?

English: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.
Masaai: Ee, ore ewang'an oo ltorrok netaaraki. Ore olang'at le nkima enye nemeitoki awang.

English: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him.
Masaai: Ore ewang'an naa kemisimis to lng'obor lenye, ore oltaa otii shumata enye neari.

English: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.
Masaai: Ore iroruat enyena naagol neitodorropi, ore inkoitoi enyena nenang'aa ninye.

English: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.
Masaai: Amu etanang'akaki atua orreshet too nkejek enyena, nelo te nkoitoi nebatatakino.

English: The gin shall take him by the heel, and the robber shall prevail against him.
Masaai: Eibung orreshet entutunyo enye, neirrag orreshet oibung ninye.

English: The snare is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.
Masaai: Eisudoro olgosoi lenye tiatua enkop, orreshet otii enkoitoi enye.

English: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet.
Masaai: Emanita ninye inaaitureisho te pooki alole, nemir ninye too nkejek enyena.

English: His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side.
Masaai: Ore engolon enye apa, netaa taata olameyu te ninye, netinyikaka ninye engolikinoto pee error.

English: It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki emuoyian netumute osesen lenye ore olkikau le keeya netumuta irubat o sesen lenye.

English: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.
Masaai: Etopolosaki ninye teilo lng'obor apa oisilig neyauni ninye aayaki ilo aiguanani oitureisho.

English: It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
Masaai: Netii olng'obor lenye ina neme enenye; ebore enkima aidapashakino emanyisho enye pooki.

English: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.
Masaai: Etoito intona enyena tiabori netoyu imbenek enyena too lukuny.

English: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.
Masaai: Neish endamunoto enye te nkop, nemeeta enkarna too nkoitoi naalala.

English: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
Masaai: Eturrumoyioki ninye te wang'an aanang'aki enaimin, nerewi aaitung'uaa enkop.

English: He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.
Masaai: Meeta ninye eishoi arashu iishoritin tiatua olorere, nemeetae oloishu teine apa nemanya.

English: They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.
Masaai: Ore lelo oomanya oloontoluo, neing'asiate teina olong enye, neibung ninche olkirutoto lo loosaen.

English: Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.
Masaai: Esipa imanyishoritin kuna e lelo lemeure Enkai, ewueji ene eilo lemeyiolo Enkai.

English: Then Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo:

English: How long will ye vex my soul, and break me in pieces with words?
Masaai: “Kenkata nabaa kisilisil iyie nanu, nikigiligil aitaa ndung'ot too rorei?

English: These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed that ye make yourselves strange to me.
Masaai: Kindipa atipika nanu enkurruna kuna katitin tomon, aimidol iyie enkurruna tenikinyal nanu?

English: And be it indeed that I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.
Masaai: Naa tenaa kesipa doi inchere aitarruoyie, etii enkinyala ai atua enkorrok ai.

English: If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach:
Masaai: Tenesipa tukul ajo intasapuk kewan kiarare nanu, nintaa emborron ai, enchankar nikiarare nanu;

English: Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net.
Masaai: tayiolo naa ajo aatipika Enkai nanu atua entorroni, naaitamana nanu orreshet lenye.

English: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but there is no judgment.
Masaai: Ng'ura, aishira abuaku ajo ‘Olarrabal!’ kake eitu aawalikini; aipotishe to ltoilo sapuk, kake metii esipata.

English: He hath fenced up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths.
Masaai: Etipika esuntai enkoitoi ai, metaa maidim aima, netipika enaimin inkoitoi aainei.

English: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
Masaai: Aatooruo ninye nanu enkitoo ai, neya te nanu enkopiyia enkitoo te ndukuya ai.

English: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am gone: and mine hope hath he removed like a tree.
Masaai: Aagiligil nanu too nkaloli pooki, netaa aisha, neitayio ninye osiligi lenye anaa olchani.

English: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as one of his enemies.
Masaai: Einuaa ninye engoro enye napi peyie aarare, naaikenaa nanu aitaa olmang'atinta lenye.

English: His troops come together, and raise up their way against me, and encamp round about my tabernacle.
Masaai: Eirriwua ninye iltimito lenyena maataarare netur ninche iloong'elu, naarresh ninche eman olng'obor lai.

English: He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are verily estranged from me.
Masaai: Eitalamayie ninye iltung'ana maatung'uai ataa olomoni te lelo pooki laayiolo nanu.

English: My kinsfolk have failed, and my familiar friends have forgotten me.
Masaai: Aatung'uaitie iltung'ana laainei le sotua tenebo ilchoreta laainei.

English: They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.
Masaai: Ore ilomon ootii enkaji ai nemaadamu ninche nanu; ore inkaisiaayiak aainei naaikenaa anaa olomoni; ataa nanu olomoni too nkonyek enye.

English: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.
Masaai: Aipoto nanu osinka lai, kake eitu ninye aawaliki; meeta nchere masai nanu ninye te nkutuk ai.

English: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children's sake of mine own body.
Masaai: Ataa kereek te nkitok ai, naatonyimo ilayiok lang'arie kina.

English: Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me.
Masaai: Ore ninye nkera kutiti naatemenaitie nanu, ore tenainyototo neimaki imbaa olmena te nanu.

English: All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.
Masaai: Ore ilchoreta laainei likinyorra oleng naaing'or ninche to lmena, ore lelo apa lanyor naaibelekenyakinote aarare.

English: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
Masaai: Ore iloik laainei netaremo olchoni lai o sesen lai, naa te mpesho nanu ailanya keeya aimisho.

English: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me.
Masaai: Eng'urrieki nanu, eng'urrieki nanu, intae lo shoreta laainei, amu aatoshoroyie nanu enkaina Enkai!

English: Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
Masaai: Kainyoo iyie pee kisujaa nanu anaa Enkai? Kainyoo iyie pee mikindip enkisilisiloto o sesen lai?

English: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!
Masaai: Oi naaji tenaa keigeroki te mbuku! nedamuni pooki aiger te mbuku.

English: That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!
Masaai: Naa tenaa keigeroki te nkalamu e sekenkei naata esipil! pee eguetakini endapidapoi ntarasi!

English: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
Masaai: Amu ayiolo ajo eishu olalakunoni lai, naa ore te siadi neitashe ti oriong enkop;

English: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
Masaai: neaku ore eidipaki aatumut osesen lai, naitoki ake adol Enkai to sesen lai,

English: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.
Masaai: ilo ladol etii enkalo ai, naa kadol too nkonyek aainei; neme too ne likae. Eiterre oltau lai tiatua nanu!

English: But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?
Masaai: Naa tinijo, ‘Kaji kinko tinikisuj ninye!’ naa ‘Ore esipata embae netumi ti atua ninye’;

English: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know there is a judgment.
Masaai: turia ilo alem, amu eyau engoro napi enkitamioto to lalem, peyie itum atayiolo inchere eetae endung'okinoto enkiguana.”

English: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Sofa le Naamat awal ajo,

English: Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for this I make haste.
Masaai: “Metaa aatawalikitia indamunot aainei nanu, tenkaraki nakuetiki imbaa te nkewan ai.

English: I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer.
Masaai: Aning'ito elap aasukenyita nanu, ore te ning'unoto ai naawaliki nanu enkiyang'et.

English: Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,
Masaai: Keitu apa iyiolou ena temusano, anaa apa peyie epiki tung'ani oriong e nkop.

English: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment?
Masaai: Inchere ore enkisulata eilo torrono naa dorrop, ore enchipai e ilo lemeeta Enkai naa enkiti kata?

English: Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds;
Masaai: Ore hoo duoo neilep aaku ildoinyo aabaiki keper enkadori enye, nebaiki elukunya enye inkatampo;

English: Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?
Masaai: keish ninye intarasi anaa inkik enyena; ore lelo ootoduaa ninye naa kejo, ‘Koree doi ninye?’

English: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.
Masaai: Ekeipid ninye alo too naipuko anaa enkidetidet, nemetumoyu; kearari ninye aitalamaa anaa enduaata e nkewarie.

English: The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.
Masaai: Ore nena onyek apa naatoduaa ninye, nemeitoki aekata aaigil aadol, nemeigil aekata ewueji enye adol ninye.

English: His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.
Masaai: Ore nkera enyena neing'oru omom teilo aisinani, ore inkaik enyena nerriny aaishooyo enkarsisisho enye.

English: His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.
Masaai: Ore iloik lenyena nebore engolon e kitisho, kake keirrag ninche tenebo ninye tiatua enterit.

English: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue;
Masaai: Ore hoo duoo nemelok intorrok te nkutuk enye, ore hoo duoo neisudoo ninye tiabori olng'ejep lenye,

English: Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:
Masaai: ore hoo nemeyieu ninye nepal, nemuk ninye te nkutuk enye,

English: Yet his meat in his bowels is turned, it is the gall of asps within him.
Masaai: kake eibelekenyi ake aaitaduar endaa enye te nkoshoke, edua naleng anaa enduaran e pooki sayiet.

English: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly.
Masaai: Eijoo ninye enkarsisisho neitoki alopu; eitayu Enkai ninche anang'aa te nkoshoke enye.

English: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper's tongue shall slay him.
Masaai: Eibibi ninye esayiet, olng'ejep le nturbubua olo aar ninye.

English: He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.
Masaai: Melo ninye aing'or lelo kejek, nena shorroi naaruko inaishi o kule.

English: That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down: according to his substance shall the restitution be, and he shall not rejoice therein.
Masaai: Kerriny ninye aaishooyo ilng'anayio le siaai enye, nemeitoki aekata ninye aijoo aitadoyio; ore dupoto e biashara enye nemetum ninye murruna.

English: Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;
Masaai: Amu etupurda ninye neing'uaa lelo aisinak, eibung'a ninye aikonyaa enkaji neitu eshet.

English: Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.
Masaai: Ore amu meeta olorok lenye enkiyagata, meleku ninye ae toki hoo nabo nashipakino.

English: There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.
Masaai: Meetae entoki natelekua eidipa ninye atadaayu; ore enkaraki ina mebikoo karsisisho enye.

English: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.
Masaai: Ore enkiputakinoto e raposhoi enye, naa osina, kelotu engolon pooki o sina shumata ninye.

English: When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.
Masaai: Neiput enkoshoke enye aitaraposh, keirriu Enkai engoro enye napi shumata ninye neitashaiki shumata ninye anaa endaa.

English: He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.
Masaai: Keisik ninye aing'uaa emasaai o larrabal e sekenkei nengor ninye embae o suyai neipang.

English: It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors are upon him.
Masaai: Etushutuaki ina bae nepuku to sesen lenye, ore ine wueji neimerlel neipang'u to lodua lenye, neibung ninye enkuretisho.

English: All darkness shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.
Masaai: Ore ilchumat lenyena pooki nepuo aajing enaimin nagut, enkima neitu einoki nalo amut ninye, ore ina natelekua to lng'obor lenye nemuti.

English: The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.
Masaai: Neibalunye keper ing'ok enyena pooki, nedumakino enkop aarare ninye.

English: The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.
Masaai: Ore imasaa enkaji enye nenapi aaya neingirtitori aaya teina olong e ngoro napi e Nkai.

English: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.
Masaai: Ena erubata oltung'ani torrono naing'uaa Enkai, enjung'ore naibalakinye ninye Enkai.

English: But Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo:

English: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.
Masaai: Inining'o tisipu irorei laainei, nincho ina eaku enkitagoloto ino.

English: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.
Masaai: Ting'iria nchooki nanu mairoro, ore peyie aidip airoro, nisurdaany.

English: As for me, is my complaint to man? and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?
Masaai: Amaa nanu, ke iltung'ana aing'unyung'unyaki? Ainyoo peyie maidim ating'iria?

English: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth.
Masaai: Ing'uraki nanu, nimimputukuny, nipik enkaina ino enkutuk ino.

English: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.
Masaai: Ore tenelo nadamu naing'asia oleng, neibung olokirikiri osesen lai.

English: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?
Masaai: Ainyoo peyie eishu lelo ooas intorrok, nebaiki moruao, nebul aaku magil te ng'olon?

English: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.
Masaai: Etubula inkera enye te dukuya ninche, netodua ninche iishoritin enye too nkonyek enye.

English: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
Masaai: Ore inkajijik enye neserian metii enkuretisho, nemeetae eng'udi Enkai natii shumata ninche.

English: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.
Masaai: Edumu iloing'ok lenye nkishu nemedung; eisho nkishu enye, nemeiturraa ilasho.

English: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
Masaai: Eiguran nkera enye anaa lkuoo le kerra, neiguran nkera enye aaipid.

English: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
Masaai: Eranyisho ninche neosh entampuri, olwulul loo usin, neshipa tenening oltoilo le ndule.

English: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.
Masaai: Etoni te nkishui oo nkolong'i enye eeta enkarsisisho nalulung'a, nedoyio aapuo enemeneng'a te seriani.

English: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
Masaai: Ejoki ninche Enkai, ‘Shomo tung'uai iyiook! Miking'uar ina ng'eno oo nkoitoi inono.

English: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
Masaai: Aing'ae doi ilo Magilani, netaa aikisiaiai ninye? Naa kainyoo kitum tinikiomon ninye?

English: Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
Masaai: Ng'ura, aimetii inkaik enye ina dupoto? Ore enkiguana oo larruok naalakuaniki nanu.

English: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
Masaai: “Keari aekata oltaa le ilo torrono? Pee edoiki entaboi enye ninche? Neitame Enkai ninche te ngoro enye.

English: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.
Masaai: Eikununo ninche anaa olkujita otoyio to lkutati, netiu anaa isuut naakutaa osiwuo?

English: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
Masaai: Ijo iyie, ‘Etushuma Enkai ing'ok enye aitaany ilayiok lenyena.’ Inchoo ninye elaaki ninche peyie etum aatayiolo.

English: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
Masaai: Inchoo inkonyek enye metoduaa enkidaata enye, naa nchoo ninche metooko ina goro e ilo Magilani.

English: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
Masaai: Amu kainyoo eshilaa ninche too nkajijik enye etulusoitie ninche eidipaki aaitodorropa esiana oo lapaitin lenye.

English: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
Masaai: Ketii obo oidim aiteng'ena Enkai engeno, idol ajo eiguanare ninye lelo ootii shumata?

English: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
Masaai: Eye obo eeta enkarsisisho nalulung'a, eidipakine neserian.

English: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
Masaai: Nebore osesen lenye empiron neruko entolit loo loik lenyena.

English: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.
Masaai: Neye likae te mion oltau, eitu aikata eishamisham esidano.

English: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.
Masaai: Neirrag ninche enyaanyuk tiatua enterit, neiruj ninche olkurto.

English: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me.
Masaai: “Ng'ura, ayiolo nanu indamunot inono, nkitobirat nikinyalie nanu.

English: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
