Masaai: Amu ijo iyie, ‘Koree enkaji olkitok? Koree ilo ng'obor otonie ilo torrono?’

English: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,
Masaai: Keitu iyie inkilikuan lelo oopuo too nkoitoi naalala, naa keitu iyie ing'amaa enchakenisho enye,

English: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
Masaai: inchere etelekuaki ilo tung'ani torrono teina olong e nyamali, inchere eitajeuoki ninye teina olong engoro napi?

English: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?
Masaai: Aing'ae oidim aibalakinye ninye enkoitoi enye? Naa aing'ae oitalaku te ninye teina nataasa.

English: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.
Masaai: Ore tenenapi ninye aaya enkurare, neing'ori aarrip enkurare enye.

English: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him.
Masaai: Esujaa ilkumok osesen lenye epuoi aanukaa, ore enterit e nkop neirrag aitirring'a aitemoo osesen lenye.

English: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?
Masaai: Kaji naa inko iyie tinikintagol nanu te mpesho narok? Meetae toki natelekua too walat inono neme elejare ake.”

English: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Elifas le Teman awal ajo:

English: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?
Masaai: “Keidim oltung'ani ataa oloota tipat te Nkai? Esipa ore ilo ng'en neeta tipat te kewan enye.

English: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him that thou makest thy ways perfect?
Masaai: Ke sikar to Lmagilani tenira asipani anaa ke dupoto te ninye tenira olemeeta eleyiata too nkoitoi inono.

English: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?
Masaai: Kenkaraki euriata niure iyie ninye peyie kisikong'a ninye, niking'uanare ninye iyie?

English: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
Masaai: Aime sapuk enkarruoisho ino? Meeta intorrok inono enkiting'oto.

English: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
Masaai: Intagolikio ilalashera linono te sile nitoning'okinote nioru ninye nkilani meshomo meishopo.

English: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
Masaai: Eitu iyie incho enkare ilo onaure, nitomitikio endaa ilo oota esumash.

English: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani ogol naa ninye oya enkop, ore ilo tung'ani onyorri nemany.

English: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
Masaai: Inchoo nkolia epuo too nkaik naarook, ore inkaik e lelo okishin nigil.

English: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina kintamanaki irresheta, nikijing aluam olkirutoto.

English: Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.
Masaai: Eitomisimisoki ewang'an ino pee midolisho, nikimulumula iyie olairrag le nkare.

English: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
Masaai: Aimetii Enkai shumata keper? Neing'or ilakir tiabori hoo naa shumata etii.

English: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?
Masaai: Metaa itejo iyie kainyoo eyiolo Enkai? Keidim ninye aiguanare enaimin narok ongu?

English: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
Masaai: Eimulumulayie ninye enkatampoi nairrusha, metaa meidim atoduaa ninye nelo ninye te rishata e keper o enkop.

English: Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?
Masaai: Iton aibung ina oitoi musana, naa ninye apa eima ilarruok?

English: Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:
Masaai: Etawuapayioki ninche aaiwuang'ie eng'or enkata enye; etooroyioki aaiwuang'ie olkitamanyunoto lenye.

English: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?
Masaai: Etiakita ninche Enkai, ‘Shomo tung'uai iyiook’ naa ‘Kaa eidim ilo Magilani aitaasa iyiook?’

English: Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
Masaai: Ore ake etiu neijia eiput ninye nkajijik enye ntokitin sidain, kake ore eutaroto e lelo torrok naalakuaniki nanu.

English: The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.
Masaai: Edol lelo supati neshipa; nekueni ilemeeta entioto tenedol ilarruok eitamei;

English: Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.
Masaai: ejo, esipa etudung'oyioki aaiwuang'ie ilmang'ati lang, ore ilekunot netumuta enkima.

English: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.
Masaai: “Toning'ore Enkai, pee itum eseriani, pee epuonu isupati enitii.

English: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.
Masaai: Tang'amai enkiteng'enare te nkutuk enye, nishum ororei lenye tiatua oltau lino.

English: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.
Masaai: Tinishukokino ilo Magilani nintobor kewan, tiniwuang'ie ntorrok pooki aitalam olng'obor lino,

English: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.
Masaai: tinirragie sahabu te nterit, aashu inang'aa sahabu naisul too lturot ootoito

English: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.
Masaai: naa teneaku ilo Magilani ninye sahabu ino, naa ninye enkosholai ino naata tipat;

English: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.
Masaai: nitum taa atishipakinoyu ilo Magilani, nidumu enkomom ino ashumaki Enkai.

English: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.
Masaai: Niomon iyie ninye naa aikining ninye iyie; nilak iyie ilmuma linono.

English: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.
Masaai: Keaku idung iyie embae alimu, netiu neija, naa kewang'u ewang'an too nkoitoi inono.

English: When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.
Masaai: Amu keitadou Enkai lelo oowuasa, neitajeu lelo oobor.

English: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.
Masaai: Eitajeu ninye ilo tung'ani lemeeta entioto; aikintajeuni iyie te nkaraki nkaik inono nemeiduruk.

English: Then Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo,

English: Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
Masaai: “Ore sii taata ena olong naa keme enking'unyung'uny ai, ekeiroshi enkaina enye hoo naigorito nanu.

English: Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat!
Masaai: Ore naaji tenaa kayiolo ewueji natumie ninye, pee elotu doi ninye olorika lenye!

English: I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
Masaai: Nairragie enkiguana ai te dukuya ninye, naiput enkutuk ai inchankarri.

English: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.
Masaai: Nayiolou ina naawaliki ninye nanu, naning'u ina naajoki ninye nanu.

English: Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.
Masaai: Kaagilunore ninye nanu te nkitoo engolon enye? A-a, ekaaning ninye nanu.

English: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani oitashe too sipat neirorie ninye, naalaku olarishani lai intarasi.

English: Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:
Masaai: Ng'ura, alotito dukuya, kake metii ninye ine; nashuko siadi, kake mamusu nanu ninye;

English: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold him: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him:
Masaai: ore te nkaina e kedienye naing'oru ninye kake madol ninye; naibelekenyakino enkalo e tatene, kake madol nanu ninye.

English: But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
Masaai: Kake eyiolo ninye enkoitoi nalo aim; ore peyie aaidip atetema nanu, nalotu apuku atotiuo anaa sahabu.

English: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.
Masaai: Etuunokinote nkejek aainei iroruat enyena; aibung'a enkoitoi enye neitu apaash.

English: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
Masaai: Eitu aing'uaa nkitanapat e nkutuk enye; atushuma tiatua oltau lai irorei le nkutuk enye.

English: But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? and what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.
Masaai: Kake meibelekenya ninye, naa aing'ae oidim aibelekenya ninye? Ore ina nayieu ninye naa ina eas.

English: For he performeth the thing that is appointed for me: and many such things are with him.
Masaai: Amu keitabaya ninye ina naategelaka nanu; ore intokitin kumok naaijo nena netii endamunoto. Netii atua endamunoto enye mbaa neeijo nena.

English: Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.
Masaai: Metaa airuto nanu te dukuya ninye, ore peyie adamu, naa kaure ninye.

English: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:
Masaai: Eiterreyie Enkai oltau lai; aaituria Olmagilani nanu;

English: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.
Masaai: amu aatiripakine enaimin, neitemoyie enaimin nairrusha enkomom ai.

English: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?
Masaai: “Ainyoo pee meiteng'el Olmagilani nkolong'i e nkiguana, naa kainyoo paa ore lelo ooyiolo ninye nemedol aekata inkolong'i enyena?

English: Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.
Masaai: Eiwuang'ie iltung'ana ilpolosien; neibung iluaat oo ntare aapurroo nepuo aaramat.

English: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge.
Masaai: Eya ninche osikiria le ilo okishi; neya olkiteng le nkoliai alakie esile enye.

English: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.
Masaai: Errumoo ninche ilo aisinani aaiwuang'ie te nkoitoi ore ilaisinak pooki le nkop neisudoo ate.

English: Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.
Masaai: Ng'ura etiu ninche anaa isirkon le ntim to lpurkel epuo te nkisiayiare enye nagol eing'oru eng'ues naibung tiong'ota, pee enya inkera enye.

English: They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.
Masaai: Eiturrurru ninche endaa enye tiong'ota, nesot isabibu too nkurman oo larruok.

English: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.
Masaai: Eirrag ninche enkewarie pooki meeta nkilani, nemeeta entoki naitoipore te nkijape.

English: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
Masaai: Keshal ninche te nchan oo ldoinyio, nepetikino endapidapoi eyieu eneshurie.

English: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.
Masaai: Etii lelo oowuapaa enkerai okishi aaoru ilki, neya pee elakie esile enye enkerai o laisinani.

English: They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry;
Masaai: Emanimanaa ninche meishopo, meeta nkilani neisumash enap irridat le nkano.

English: Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.
Masaai: Tiatua intukusi oo loirienito easisho ninche; eironyu enaisho too sabibu, neton ake eeta enkure.

English: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them.
Masaai: Tiauluo enkanasa eigor ilo oye neishiru oltau le ilo otipikaki olbae eretoto. Ore ake eyia, meshilaa Enkai ina omono.

English: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.
Masaai: “Etii lelo ooiser eiba ewang'an, lelo leitu emoku inkoitoi enyena, nemetoni too nkoitoi enyena.

English: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.
Masaai: Edumunye ilarruok te naimin, pee etum aataarr metua ilo aisinani o ilo oata osina; ore kewarie netiu anaa olapurroni.

English: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.
Masaai: Eanyu sii enkong'u e ilo ololoito metomisimiso, ejo, ‘meeta enkong'u naadol nanu’; neimulumul enkomom enye.

English: In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.
Masaai: Ore te naimin netur inkajijik; ore dama neikenoo ate, nemeyiolo ninche ewang'an.

English: For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
Masaai: Amu enaimin nagut entadekenya enye pooki; amu ilchoreta ninche lo lkirutoto le naimin nagut.

English: He is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.
Masaai: “Itejo, ‘Eitasiooyioki ninche aaya shumata nkariak; etediaaki erubata enye te nkop; meetae ololo nkurman enye oo sabibu.

English: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.
Masaai: Eshol olameyu o enkirouaj neishu aitoi enkare nataa osoit le nkirobi neijia sii eiko enemeneng'a lelo ooas ing'ok.

English: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.
Masaai: Medamuni ninche too lkurrot ootumoreki le nkanasa, meekure edamuni nkarn enye, neaku etigilaki entorroni anaa olchani.’

English: He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.
Masaai: “Edaa ninche too nkajijik oo nkituaak olupin, nemeitaas inkolia mbaa supati.

English: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.
Masaai: Ore ake eyia, eitoodor Enkai nkolong'i e ilo Magilani te ngolon enye. Edumunye ninche etapalari te nkishui.

English: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways.
Masaai: Eisho ninche erripoto neretuni sii; ore nkonyek enyena neing'or nkoitoi enye.

English: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.
Masaai: Eilepieki ninche te nkiti kata, neitoki aaish; etoyu ninche neish anaa endiati pooki edung'ori ninche anaa ilukuny entapa.

English: And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?
Masaai: Naa tenemenejia etiu, aing'ae ooidim aitisipa nchere kara olalejani, neitodolu ajo meetae esipata te pooki natejo nanu?”

English: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Bildad le Shusi awal ajo,

English: Dominion and fear are with him, he maketh peace in his high places.
Masaai: “Ene Nkai enkitoria o euriata, eitobir ninye eseriani te shumata enye e keper.

English: Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?
Masaai: Keeta enjore enye esiana? Aing'ae meilepaki ewang'an enye?

English: How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?
Masaai: Kaji naa eiko oltung'ani teneaku sinyati te dukuya Enkai? Kaji eiko ilo otoiwuo enkitok teneton meiduruk.

English: Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight.
Masaai: Ng'ura mewang doi ninye olapa nemewang'an aasila ilakir te dukuya ninye.

English: How much less man, that is a worm? and the son of man, which is a worm?
Masaai: Oo naa duoo tung'ani, laa oloti kurto, o enkerai e tung'ani laa enkurto!”

English: But Job answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Yoab awal ajo:

English: How hast thou helped him that is without power? how savest thou the arm that hath no strength?
Masaai: “Kebaa eretoto nitareto ilo lemeeta engolon. Intajewuo ina aina nemeeta engolon!

English: How hast thou counseled him that hath no wisdom? and how hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?
Masaai: Inkoo ilo lemeeta engeno nagut, nincho ninye te lengon engeno sapuk.

English: To whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee?
Masaai: Aiteretoto e ng'ae iyie iroro irorei naa ae te nkiyang'et e ng'ae etupukutuo te iyie?

English: Dead things are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.
Masaai: Eikirikira iloipi liabori, o nkariak o lelo oomanya.

English: Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.
Masaai: Meishopo enemeneng'a te dukuya Enkai, nemeeta Abadon entoki naitoipieki.

English: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.
Masaai: Eisalaash moikuape aisalaashaki olngam neik enkop aililioki olngam.

English: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them.
Masaai: Een inkariak too nkatampo naairrusha, nemepolosa inkatampo tiabori ninche.

English: He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it.
Masaai: Eitoip ninye olapa neisalaashaki ninye enkatampoi enye.

English: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end.
Masaai: Etuutua olokelel tioriong nkariak, to lpolosie le rishata ewang'an o enaimin.

English: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.
Masaai: Eikirikira ing'apeta e keper, neirut aaiputukuny te nkisikong'ata enye.

English: He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud.
Masaai: Eitigir enaiposha te ngolon enye; te ng'eno enye etoosho Rahab.

English: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.
Masaai: To lkutati lenye eitisidanaki keper; nerem enkaina enye olasurai oilanyisho.

English: Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?
Masaai: Ngura, ore kuna naa nkuti ake oo nkoitoi naa kebaa enkitisho enking'oming'om oo mbaa enyena nikitoning'o! Naa amaa endarata engolon enye, aing'ae oidim atoning'u?”

English: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki ake Yoab airo nejo:

English: As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul;
Masaai: “Ore anaa enaishu Enkai, ilo laaitung'uayie esipata ai, o ilo Magilani, ilo otipika oltau lai emion;

English: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils;
Masaai: ore ake ninye aishu, netii enkiyang'et Enkai nkumeishin aainei,

English: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.
Masaai: mairo te nkutuk ai mbaa e lejare, nemeibalie olng'ejep lai enemesipa.

English: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Masaai: Metalakuana te nanu elimunoto nchere, itisipa intae ore omatua, nemaiwuang'ie aekata enkitashoto ai e sipata.

English: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.
Masaai: Ekaibung akurraki esinyatisho ai, nemaitiak, maaitukurru oltau lai too nkolong'i aainei pooki.

English: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.
Masaai: “Inchoo olmang'atinta lai eaku oltorrono, nincho ilo laadumakino aarare eaku olarruoni.

English: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?
Masaai: Amaa kainyoo osiligi le ilo lemeure Enkai teneiwuang'ie Enkai ninye, teneiwuang'ie Enkai enkishui enye?

English: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?
Masaai: Kening Enkai enkishirata enye, tenebaiki ninye enyamali?

English: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?
Masaai: Keshipakino ninye ilo Magilani? Keipot ninye Enkai pooki kata?

English: I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
Masaai: Ekaaiteng'en nanu iyie enkipirta enkaina e Enkai; ore pooki natii atua Olmagilani nemaisudoo.

English: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?
Masaai: Ng'ura, indipa pooki aatodol maate; kainyoo naa pee itaa pooki ilooiro mbaa e pesho?

English: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty.
Masaai: “Ena erubata oltung'ani torrono te Nkai, naa ina enjung'ore nang'amu ilooitorogonyisho te ilo Magilani:

English: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
Masaai: Teneponari inkera enyena, naa kemut olalem, ore eishoi enye nemetum endaa naraposh.

English: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootelekutua neye to lmeitai ore nkolia enye nemeidim aaishira.

English: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;
Masaai: Ore hoo neiturrurr enkosholai anaa enterit, nerup inkilani anaa esarng'ab;

English: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
Masaai: eidim aiturrurro, kake lelo supati ooishop, ore lelo lemeeta entioto neor enkosholai.

English: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh.
Masaai: Ore enkaji nashet ninye netiu anaa enkaji o lkedi, anaa olng'obor oitobiru olarriponi.

English: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not.
Masaai: Elo ninye endapash aa karsis, neyooki ainyototo eisha karsisisho enye ebol inkonyek enyena, nenyorriki eshomo enkarsisisho enye.

English: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.
Masaai: Eipang'aki ninye oloputukunyi anaa olairrag le nkare; ore kewarie nenap ninye osiwuo sapuk.

English: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.
Masaai: Edumu ninye olkutati lo loo saen neya; eoroo ninye aitung'uaa ewueji enye.

English: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
Masaai: Ekekut olkutati ninye meeta olng'ur ina kata etem ninye ailany engolon enye.

English: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
Masaai: Keoshoki olkutati ninye nkaik, neiture ninye aitupuku te wueji enye.

English: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.
Masaai: Esipa etii ewueji neturunyeki enkosholai, netii ewueji nesilieki sahabu.

English: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.
Masaai: Eitayuni esekenkei te nkop, nesholuni osuyai te nterit enye.

English: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.
Masaai: Eishie iltung'ana enaimin, nelimana aaing'oru olpolosie olakua ina terit natii emisimisi te naim nagut.

English: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.
Masaai: Etur ineeimi too nong'ot nemetaaniki iltung'ana; meekure edamu ninche lelo apuayak. Eililio ninche too neelakuaniki iltung'ana neyuko inkaloli pooki.

English: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
Masaai: Enkop ninye epukunye endaa; kake ore tiabori eatua neibelekenyi aitaa enkima.

English: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.
Masaai: Ore isoito lenyena neeta ewueji oo soito sidain, neeta enterit e sahabu.

English: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen:
Masaai: “Ore ina oitoi nemetii olmotonyi oinos nkiri oyiolo, neitu edol enkong'u o lmotonyi odolisho oleng.

English: The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
Masaai: Ore ng'uesi naawuasa, eitu eitunyoo ine; neitu eim olng'atuny shumata enye.

English: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.
Masaai: “Etur iltung'ana osoit ogol oleng, neibeleleng'oo ildoinyo too ntona enye.

English: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.
Masaai: Eturu ineimi too ndapidapo, nedol enkong'u enye pooki toki sidai.

English: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.
Masaai: Een ninye inchorroi pooki pee meitoki aitong, ore entoki naisudoro neyau atua ewang'an.

English: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
Masaai: “Kake aitiaji etumi engeno nagut? Naa koree ewueji ening'unoto?

English: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.
Masaai: Meyiolo oltung'ani enkoitoi nalo ine, nemetumi ninye te nkop oo looishu.

English: The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.
Masaai: Ejo enguton, ‘ime nanu etii’; nejo enaiposha ime nanu etii.

English: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
Masaai: Metumi ninye te sahabu, nemeineneng'i enkosholai metaa elaata enye.

English: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
Masaai: Metemieki ninye e sahabu e Ofir, nemetemieki enkosholai sidai.

English: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
Masaai: Ore sahabu o enkosholai nemerisiore ninye, nemewalunyeki isoito le sahabu nasila.

English: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
Masaai: Meitasimi aatemaki isoito oogol enkinyiang'a, ore enkinyiang'a e ng'eno nagut nelang isoito oogol enkinyiang'a.

English: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
Masaai: Ore isoito oogol enkinyiang'a ooji Topas le Etiopia, nemeitanyaanyukieki ninye, nemeitanyaanyukieki ninye sahabu nasila.

English: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
Masaai: “Kaji naa doi eing'uaa engeno nagut? Naa koree ewueji ening'unoto?

English: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.
Masaai: Eisudoyioki too nkonyek e pooki toki naishu; nenukari pee medol imotonyi oloing'ang'e.

English: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
Masaai: Ejo Abadon o keeya, ‘Kitoning'o iyook olmarenke too nkiyiaa ang.’

English: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.
Masaai: “Eyiolo Enkai enkoitoi nalo ine, neyiolo ewueji enye.

English: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;
Masaai: Amu eing'or ninye inkiting'ot e nkop, nedol pooki toki natii abori keper.

English: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.
Masaai: Ore pee eisho enkijape enkiroishi enye, neyiolou eneba endapasho enaiposha.

English: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:
Masaai: Neitobiru too rorei enchan, neitobiru enkoitoi enkiwuang'ata e ndarata;

English: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.
Masaai: nedol ninye neibalie ninye; neitasheyie ninye, neing'oru ninye.

English: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye tung'ani, ‘Ng'ura, euriata Olaitoriani naa ninye engeno nagut, naa tining'uaa ntorrok naa ninye ening'unoto.’ ”

English: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki ake Yoab airo nejo:

English: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me;
Masaai: “Oi naaji tenaa katii ilapaitin liapa, anaa too nkolong'i apa naatorripo Enkai nanu;

English: When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness;
Masaai: ina kata apa eitawang'aki oltaa lenye endukuya ai, ore te wang'an enye nalo aim enaimin.

English: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle;
Masaai: Anaa apa enatiu too nkolong'i e nkiputakinoto ai, ina kata etii shoruetisho e Nkai shumata olng'obor lai.

English: When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me;
Masaai: Ina kata eton etii Olmagilani tenebo nanu ina kata aamanita nkera aainei nanu.

English: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;
Masaai: Ina kata eisuji iroruat aainei te kule, naabukoki ina dapidapoi inchorroi eilata!

English: When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!
Masaai: Tenaipang nanu alo auluo enkishomi e nkanasa, ina kata naitobir nanu olorika lai to lkurroto otumoreki.

English: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up.
Masaai: Naadol lelo barnot neilanyisho, neinyototo ilpayiani kituaak neitashe;

English: The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
Masaai: negira lelo kituaak eitu eitoki aairo, nepik inkaik enye nkutukie enye aaibung,

English: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.
Masaai: negira oltoilo le lelo yiolot nerep ilng'ejepa lenye inoreti enye.

English: When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:
Masaai: Ore te nening enkiok naaipot nanu ajo olomayiana, ore peyie edol enkong'u nenyorra ninye;

English: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
Masaai: amu aitajewuo nanu ilo aisinani oishira o ilo okishi lemeeta hoo obo oretu ninye.

English: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.
Masaai: Ore emayianata e ilo letaa keidak nelotu shumata nanu, naretu nkolia menoto eseriani.

English: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.
Masaai: Aishopoko kewan esupatisho, naaitoip ninye nanu. Ore esipata ai netiu anaa olkila o enkarasha e lukunya.

English: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.
Masaai: Ara apa nanu nkonyek tialo olmodooni, nara nkejek to lmaima.

English: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
Masaai: Ara apa nanu menye ilo aisinani, naturu aing'oru aretu ilo lemaayiolo.

English: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.
Masaai: Atigila ilala le ilo oas ing'ok, naitiakie ninye ina nainosita too lala lenyena.

English: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.
Masaai: Ina peyie adamu ajo, kaye nanu tiatua enkaji ai, naa kaponaa inkolong'i aainei aitaba anaa osinyai.

English: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.
Masaai: Epuo intona aainei aaidapashakino inkariak, netii enkoilielio enkewarie pooki ilng'osil laainei.

English: My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.
Masaai: Ore enkisisa ai naa ng'ejuk te nanu, ore enkawuo ai naa ng'ejuk anaake te nkaina ai.

English: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.
Masaai: “Aainining'o nanu iltung'ana naanyu, negira einining enkikoo ai.

English: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.
Masaai: Ore peyie aidip airoro, eitu eitoki ninche aairo, nebaiki ororei lai ninche.

English: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.
Masaai: Aataanyutua ninche nanu anaa enaanyu enchan; nebol inkutukie enye anaa enchan oloirujuruj.

English: If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.
Masaai: Aatakweniyie nanu ninche ina kata meeta enkitieunoto; ore ina wang'an enkomom ai neitagol ninche.

English: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.
Masaai: Ategelua nanu enkoitoi enye, naton anaa olautaroni, naton anaa olaiguanani tiatua oltim lenye, natiu anaa ilo oitagol lelo ooishir.

English: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
Masaai: Kake aakueniyie taata ninche nanu, iltung'ana ooti te nanu, laa ore apa loo menye, naa iltung'ana le pesho, ilaa maidim ninye aitaboitaki ildiein laainei oorrip intare.

English: Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
Masaai: Ainyoo nanu aidim anoto te ngolon oo nkaik enye, iltung'ana ooisha engolon enye?

English: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
Masaai: Ore to sina o te sumash nagol, naa kenyaal intona naatoito.

English: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
Masaai: Edung'u ninche mbenek e ntim, o ntona olpurkel aaitaa endaa.

English: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)
Masaai: Etaarayioki ninche aaitung'uaa iltung'ana, nebuaku iltung'ana emirta ninche anaa iloosujaa olapurroni.

English: To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
Masaai: Ilbaat loo ndapidapo epuo ninche aamany, ingumot enkop o olkutot loo ndapidapo.

English: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.
Masaai: Eru ninche anaa ng'uesi tiatua ntimi, neiturrurro tenebo too loipi.

English: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.
Masaai: Ilmoda ninche, le ishoi oo larruok, etaarayioki ninche aaipang'ie te nkop.

English: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
Masaai: Nataa taata osinkolio lenye meekure aata tipat te ninche.

English: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
Masaai: Aaibaitie nanu naatalama nanu; meingash ninche aanotaki tenaadol.

English: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki natalaa Enkai enkeene ai naaitobor nanu, aaibelekenyakinote ninche nanu te ngoro enye pooki.

English: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
Masaai: Ore te nkaina ai e tatene einyeito ilmang'ati, naareu ninche nanu aarrumoo, naapikaki nanu aarare inkoitoi enye e nkidaaroto.

English: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
Masaai: Einyal ninche enkoitoi ai, neitubulaa ninche engolikinoto ai, metii hoo obo omitiki ninche.

English: They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.
Masaai: Epuonu ninche anaa iloim elusie nalala naapuonu aasulakino nanu aapurd.

English: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.
Masaai: Aaibelekenyakaki nanu olkirutoto ore enkisisa ai nemirareki anaa enamirta enkijape ore karsisisho ai neisha anaa enkatampoi.

English: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
Masaai: Ore taata neiting'ieki enkishui ai te nanu; aaineputua nanu inkolong'i osina aaibung.

English: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
Masaai: Ore enkewarie pooki neme iloik laainei, ore emion naaitame nanu nemeyagaa.

English: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
Masaai: Ore to larrabal neibung ninye olkila lai, naaen nanu anunuk anaa enkila.

English: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.
Masaai: Aatanang'aka nanu Enkai atua esarng'ab, natotiwuo anaa enterit o nkuruon.

English: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.
Masaai: Aaishiraka nanu iyie neitu kiwaliki nanu, aitasho nanu nimikining iyie nanu.

English: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.
Masaai: Kimbelekenyakine nanu agorokino; te nkidimata enkaina ino kitaarare iyie nanu.

English: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.
Masaai: Kidumu iyie nanu aya shumata enkijape, nikincho iyie matakedo ninye nikimposhiposh iyie nanu te nkikurrukur olkutati.

English: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.
Masaai: Ee, ayiolo nanu ajo aikipik iyie atua keeya, o atua ina aji nategelakaki lelo pooki oishu.

English: Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
Masaai: Naa amaa obo to lturrur le nkidaata aimeitorioo enkaina enye, ore te mutata enye neishiru eretoto.

English: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?
Masaai: Keitu nanu aishiraki ilo laa ore enkolong enye netagolikio, keitu eishir oltau lai to sina te nkaraki lelo aisinak?

English: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
Masaai: Kake tenaing'oru nanu esidano, nepuonu ntorrok; naa tenaanyu ewang'an, nelotu enaimin.

English: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
Masaai: Etii oltau lai osomit, nemeitirring'a aekata, naatabaikitia inkolong'i o loisilisili nanu.

English: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.
Masaai: Aloolo aaitorokaki neme te nkolong; aitashe tiatua olturrur naishiru eretoto.

English: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
Masaai: Ataa nanu olalashe loo mbariak nataa olecholiek oo sidain.

English: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
Masaai: Eibelekenye olchoni lai aroku naaitoki aing'uaa, ore iloik laainei neyupuyup te nkirouaj.

English: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.
Masaai: Eibelekenyaki olwulul lai loo usin, metaa enkishirata o sina ore oltoilo le ndule ai neibelekenyaki metotiwuo anaa oltoilo le lelo ooishir.

English: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
Masaai: “Aitobirua olning'o too nkonyek aainei; kaji naa aiko tenaitoki aing'or eselenkei?

English: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
Masaai: Kainyoo erubata ai naing'uaa Enkai natii shumata, naa ainyoo enjung'ore ai te ilo Magilani le shumata?

English: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
Masaai: Aimedoiki ingolikinot lelo torrok, netum emutata lelo aasak loo ntorrok?

English: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
Masaai: Aimedol ninye inkoitoi aainei, neiken iroruat aainei pooki?

English: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;
Masaai: Amaa tenaa kashomo nanu tenebo iloolejisho, neisarisara enkeju ai alo alejisho.

English: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.
Masaai: (Inchoo maineneng'i te ntemet naineneng'ishoreki nemeeta emonkoi naa inchoo Enkai eyiolou enkitashoto ai!)

English: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;
Masaai: Tenaa keibelekenye eroruata apaash enkoitoi neshomo oltau lai arubare nkonyek aainei, naa teneibung'a oltipoto ake ninye pooki inkaik aainei;

English: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.
Masaai: nchoo naa aaku oloun, neinos likae; naa inchoo ina nabulu aaku enaai eturuni aaitayu.

English: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;
Masaai: “Tenetang'uarra oltau lai enkitok ole latia ai, nairraga aanyisho te kutukaji ole latia ai,

English: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.
Masaai: inchoo enkitok ai eyieraki likae lee, naa inchoo ilkulikae eirrugokino ninye.

English: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
Masaai: Amu keaku ina embae torrono oleng, neaku entorroni naiguanare neitame ilarishak.

English: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
Masaai: Amu keaku ina enkima namut pooki toki, nepejoo too ntona pooki toki ai natum.

English: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;
Masaai: Tenatanya nanu aning enyamali olaisiaayiani lai arashu enkaisiaayiani ai, ore peyie eyau olong'unyung'unyi te nkaraki nanu,

English: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
Masaai: Kaa naa alo aas teneinyototo Enkai? Amaa teneikilikuanisho, kaa nanu awaliki ninye?

English: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
Masaai: Amaa ilo laaitobirua nanu te ng'uset aimeninye oitobirua ninye? Naa aime ilo obo oitobirua iyiook te ng'uset.

English: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
Masaai: “Tenatomito nanu ae toki nayieu olaisinani, arashu tenaishirie nanu enkoliai,

English: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;
Masaai: arashu tenainosa nanu endaa ai openy eitu ang'arie likae, neitu ang'arie ilo okishi

English: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)
Masaai: (amu ore eiteru te nkitisho enye naitubulua nanu ninye anaa menye ore epuku aing'uaa enguset e ng'otonye atuutayie nanu ninye);

English: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
Masaai: tenatoduaa nanu obo lenye eidaa, te nkaraki meeta inkilani o sesen, arashu oltung'ani aisinani lemeitoipo,

English: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
Masaai: teneitu ninye aamayian nanu, naa teneitu eirowuajieki too lpapit loo ntare aainei,

English: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:
Masaai: tenatudumua enkaina ai aarare lelo okishin amu atoduaa eretoto te kishomi;

English: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
Masaai: neaku inchoo inkaik aainei epuku aing'uaa oloililai lai, naa inchoo enkaina ai eorunye terubata enye.

English: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
Masaai: Amu ara apa oloure enyamali naing'uaa Enkai nemaitieu aibelekenyakinoyu aing'ura enkitoo enye.

English: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;
Masaai: “Tenaitaa nanu sahabu osiligi lai, arashu tenetaa sahabu nasila aigarakino;

English: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;
Masaai: tenatishipe nanu enkaraki naa sapuk enkarsisisho ai, arashu enkaraki nanoto enkaina ai imasaa kumok;

English: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
Masaai: tenaing'ura nanu enkolong ewang oleng, arashu olapa elo te sidano enye,

English: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:
Masaai: neeni oltau lai too nkisudorot mayiolo, netung'ututa enkutuk ai enkaina ai;

English: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.
Masaai: ore sii ninye ena naa eng'oki naitame ilarishak amu ataa olalejani te Nkai e shumata.

English: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:
Masaai: “Tenatishipakine nanu enkidaata e ilo laaiba, arashu ashipa ina kata peyie eidimu ninye entorroni.

English: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.
Masaai: (Eitu nanu aisho enkutuk ai eas eng'oki, pee aomonu enkishui enye to ldeket);

English: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
Masaai: teneitu ejo iltung'ana lolng'obor lai, ‘Kalo otii ine leitu etum aiputakinoyu te ndaa enye?’

English: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.
Masaai: Ore ilo omoni eitu eirrag enkoitoi nalala e nkanas; ataboloko nchomito aainei lelo apuayak);

English: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:
Masaai: tenaisudoyie aitemoo enkarruoisho ai too ltung'ana anuk intorrok aainei to lgoo lai,

English: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?
Masaai: amu aitasho nanu te nkuretisho sapuk aure olturrur, naaiture nanu enkiba oo lmareita, metaa atigire neitu aipang aim inchomito.

English: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.
Masaai: Oi naaji duoo tenaa kaata obo laaning nanu! (Nena entukunyata olkimojino lai! Inchoo Olmagilani aawaliki nanu! Oi naaji tenaa kataa enesirare imbaa aainei naaigero ilo mang'atinta lai!

English: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.
Masaai: Esipa anaata nanu anap to loililai lai; anaata aeniki kewan anaa emaupe e nkitoo;

English: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.
Masaai: ekaisho nanu ninye imbaa aainei pooki oo roruat aainei; ekalo nanu enetii ninye te nkanyit naishori oltung'ani kitok.

English: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;
Masaai: “Teneishira enkop ai, te nkaraki nanu, naa teneishira ineeturo enkurma tenebo;

English: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:
Masaai: tenainosa ilng'anayio lenyena eitu alak, nayau keeya oo loopeny;

English: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
Masaai: inchoo ilkiku ebulu te rishata enkano, o endiati te rishata e shairi.” Neishunye irorei le Yoab

English: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Masaai: Metaa eitu eitoki kulo tung'ana pokira okuni aawaliki Yoab amu aisupat ninye too nkonyek enyena makewan.

English: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.
Masaai: Neitoki Elihu olayioni le Berakel le Busi lo lmarei le Ram agoro. Etagorokine ninye Yoab amu eitaa kewan olemeeta entioto neaku Enkai eiteleiki entorroni.

English: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
Masaai: Etagorokine sii lelo shoreta le Yoab pokira okuni amu eitu eitoki aatum ewalata nawaliki Yoab, hoo neibalie aajo etapong'ori Yoab.

English: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.
Masaai: Etaanyua apa Elihu peyie eirorie Yoab amu aibotoro apa ninche te ninye.

English: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.
Masaai: Ore peyie edol Elihu ajo meekure eetae ewalata te lelo lewa pokira okuni, negoro.

English: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.
Masaai: Newal Elihu olayioni le Barakel le Busi ajo, “Ara nanu oti too larin, nitamorua iyie metaa kaata duoo nanu enkuretisho aibalunye enduaata ai te iyie

English: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.
Masaai: Atejo nanu, ‘Nchoo eiro nkolong'i ore ilarin kumok neiteng'enisho eng'eno nagut.’

English: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
Masaai: Kake ina kiyang'et natii tung'ani, enkiyang'et e ilo Magilani, ninye naidimie ninye metoning'u.

English: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
Masaai: Ime lelo moruak oata engeno nagut, neme ilkituaak ooning'u esipata.

English: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.
Masaai: Metaa ajo nanu, ‘Toning'oki; nchooki sii nanu maibalie enduaata ai.’

English: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.
Masaai: “Ng'ura ataanyua nanu irorei linono, atoning'o nanu nkirorot inono eng'eno nagut, ina kata ing'oru enijo.

English: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:
Masaai: Aaishoo iyie enkiok ai, nemetii hoo nabo neitu ewalu Yoab, arashu olotawalua irorei lenyena te ntae.

English: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
Masaai: Eng'ura ake ate pee mijojo ‘Kinoto eng'eno nagut; Enkai ake naidim atawalaki Yoab amu italaikinote.’

English: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.
Masaai: Eitu ninye aaitorioki irorei lenyena agilunore nanu, nemawaliki nanu ninye too nkirorot inono.

English: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.
Masaai: “Etunumate ninche, meekure eeta enawalu; meekure ninche eeta ororei ojo.

English: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;)
Masaai: Naa katon nanu aanyisho, eji amu meiro ninche, amu eitashe ninche te ine nemeekure ewalu?

English: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.
Masaai: Ekaishoru sii nanu ewalata ai; naa kaibalie sii nanu enduaata ai.

English: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
Masaai: Amu kaabore nanu irorei naarrumito oltau lai mairoro.

English: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.
Masaai: Ng'ura etiu oltau lai anaa enaisho oo sabibu napising'a, etiu anaa olbene le naisho oo sabibu ng'ejuk, netaa kedanya.

English: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.
Masaai: Ekairo nanu peyie atum ayagie, ekabol enkutuk ai awalu.

English: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
Masaai: Maitodolu nanu oloshomitore te likae, arashu asukeny likae tung'ani,

English: For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.
Masaai: amu mayiolo nanu atusukenyisho, pee maapik ake Olaitobirani lai enkiting'oto.

English: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
Masaai: “Kake ore naa taata toning'o enkiroroto ai iyie Yoab, nining'u irorei laainei pooki.

English: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
Masaai: Ng'ura, atabolo enkutuk ai; eirorita olng'ejep le nkutuk ai.

English: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
Masaai: Eibalunye irorei laainei esupatisho oltau lai, ore nena naayiolo enkutuk ai neiro te sipata.

English: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
Masaai: Aaitobirua nanu enkiyang'et Enkai naaisho nanu enkiyang'et e ilo Magilani enkishui.

English: If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.
Masaai: Tawalikiaki nanu tinindim; intobiru irorei linono te dukuya nanu; inyo mbalie enkitashoto ino.

English: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo aitoriokine sii nanu Enkai anaa iyie; aaitobiruaki sii apa nanu te nterit.

English: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.
Masaai: Ing'ura, mincho enkuretisho ai kinture iyie mesapuku enkitirrishakinoto ai te iyie.

English: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,
Masaai: “Esipa, iroro iyie aning'ito, natoning'o nanu oltoilo loo rorei linono.

English: I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.
Masaai: Itejo, iyie ‘Kara nanu sinyati, maata enaitapong'o, maata eleyiata nemetii entorroni atua nanu.

English: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo etum ninye inkitolonyat naaisikong'ie nanu, naaikenaa nanu aitaa olmang'atinta lenye;

English: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
Masaai: etipika nkejek aainei ilpisia aen neing'or inkoitoi aainei pooki.’

English: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
Masaai: “Ng'ura ajo ore tena nimira asipani. Ekaawaliki nanu iyie, aikitok Enkai alang oltung'ani.

English: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.
Masaai: Ainyoo iyie pee ikeshare ninye; ijo, ‘Mewalu ninye hoo obo loo rorei laainei?’

English: For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.
Masaai: Amu eiro Enkai te nkoitoi nabo, o tiare hoo nememusu tung'ani ninye.

English: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
Masaai: Te nkidetidet o nduaat e kewarie, ina kata najing injo nairoishi iltung'ana ina kata eimugito too ndapashi enye,

English: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,
Masaai: nebol ninye inkiyiaa oo ltung'ana, neiture ninche too nkikoot.

English: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
Masaai: Peyie etum ninye atoboina tung'ani aitung'uai nkoitoi enyena, neiwuang'ie olwuasa te tung'ani;

English: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
Masaai: negolie oltau lenye aibooyo mejing engumoto o enkishui enye pee meidak to lalem.

English: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:
Masaai: “Eutari sii oltung'ani te nkitamioto emuoyian te ndapash enye, neponaa emion too loik lenyena.

English: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.
Masaai: Metaa meitoki enkishui enye ang'uar endaa ore enkoshoke enye nemeitoki aayieu endaa.

English: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.
Masaai: Neibibiari osesen lenye ometaa meekure elioo; ore iloik apa lemelioo nepuku aibalayu.

English: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.
Masaai: Nenyikaki oltau lenye enemeneng'a, nenyikaki enkishui enye lelo ooyau keeya.

English: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:
Masaai: Tenetii olmalaika tenebo ninye, Olaitutumoni obo te nkalifu, pee eibalakinye tung'ani enasipa te ninye;

English: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
Masaai: neeta olng'ur te ninye ejoki, ‘Intajeu ninye mincho edoyio enemeneng'a, anoto elakunoto;

English: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth:
Masaai: inchoo osesen lenye esika nejing kitisho inchoo ninye errinyokino inapa olong'i e ngolon e kitisho;’

English: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.
Masaai: eomon oltung'ani Enkai, neng'amu Enkai ninye, elotu ninye enetii Enkai te nchipai. Neliki iltung'ana enjeunoto enye,

English: He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;
Masaai: neranyisho te dukuya iltung'ana ejo: ‘Ataasa eng'oki, natokordilo ina apa nasipa, neitu apa aaitalaki nanu.

English: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
Masaai: Etalakua ninye oltau lai, pee medoyio alo atua enemeneng'a, naa kedol enkishui ai ewang'an.’

English: Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,
Masaai: “Ng'ura ajo Enkai naas kuna pooki, kat are, kat uni tenebo tung'ani.

English: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
Masaai: Pee eyau arrinyu oltau lenye aitung'uaa enemeneng'a, pee etum ninye atoduaa ewang'an e nkishui.

English: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.
Masaai: Irrugu enkiok, iyie Yoab, toning'oki; tigirayu peyie atum airoro.

English: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.
Masaai: Tiniata embae niyieu nijo, tawalikiaki; iroro amu kayieu oleng naaisho iyie esipata.

English: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
Masaai: Naa tenemeneijia, toning'oki nanu; tigirayu, amu kaaiteng'en iyie eng'eno nagut.”

English: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Elihu ajo:

English: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
Masaai: “Entoning irorei laainei, intae iltung'ana ng'eni, nikirrugokiki enkiok, intae ooyiolo;

English: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.
Masaai: amu etem enkiok irorei, anaa enkutuk te ndaa.

English: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.
Masaai: Emategelu iyiook ina nasipa; ematujurru tiatua ate ina sidai.

English: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.
Masaai: Amu etejo Yoab, ‘Maata nanu entioto, neewa Enkai esipata ai;

English: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.
Masaai: Ore hoo naata esipata aaikenayioki aajo olaimonkoni; meishiunoyou olbae lai, hoo nemaata entorroni.’

English: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?
Masaai: Kalo tung'ani onyaanyukie Yoab ook esurdaanyata anaa enkare,

English: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
Masaai: ilo olo te ncholiek oo laasak loo ntorrok, neiriamariyie iltung'ana arruok?

English: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
Masaai: Amu etejo ninye, ‘Meeta toki natum oltung'ani teneshipakino Enkai.’

English: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
Masaai: “Metaa, entoning'oki, intae iltung'ana oota ening'unoto, metalamari ina te Nkai, tenaa keas ninye enkarruoisho, metalamari to Lmagilani tenaa keas ninye entorroni.

English: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
Masaai: Amu ore te risioroto e siaai e tung'ani keitalakuni te ninye, naa ore te risioroto oo nkoitoi enyena nelaaki ninye.

English: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
Masaai: Ore te sipata meas Enkai entorroni, nemeboin Olmagilani esipata.

English: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?
Masaai: Aing'ae oishoo ninye metaa olaitasheikinoni le nkop? naa aing'ae otipika ninye meitasheiki enkop pooki?

English: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;
Masaai: Tenerriny ninye enkiyang'et enye makewan, neiturrurroki kewan enkiyang'et enye,

English: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.
Masaai: neidak iseseni pooki tenebo nerrinyo tung'ani atua enterit.

English: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
Masaai: “Tiniata eyiolounoto, toning'u ena; toning'o ina najo nanu.

English: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?
Masaai: Amaa ilo lemenyor esipata, keitoreisho? Idung'oki iyie enkiguana ilo asipani naa magilani

English: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?
Masaai: ilo ajoki olaiguanani, ‘Miata tipat’ nejoki ilkituaak, ‘Oltung'ani torrono;’

English: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.
Masaai: ilo lemeitodolu oloshomitore too lkituaak, nemeshilaa ilo karsis aitalang ilo aisinani, amu ore ninche pooki naa esiaai oo nkaik enyena?

English: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
Masaai: Ore tenkiti kata neye ninche; ore te mpolos enkewarie neari metuata ore lelo magil neyae ninche neme too nkaik e tung'ani.

English: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
Masaai: “Amu etii nkonyek enyena shumata nkoitoi e tung'ani, nedol ninye iroruat enyena pooki.

English: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
Masaai: Metii osina arashu enaimin nagut, ine neisudoriyie ilaasak loo ntorrok ate.

English: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
Masaai: Amu eitu eutu enkata te pooki tung'ani pee elo dukuya Enkai te nkiguana.

English: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
Masaai: Eiwuang'ie ninye lelo magil eitu eng'as ajurru, nepik kulikae iwuejitin enye.

English: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
Masaai: Ore amu eyiolo ninye isinaitin lenye, eibeleleng'oo ninche te nkewarie, nepurdi ninche.

English: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
Masaai: Eosh ninye ninche te nkaraki enkarruoisho enye edolita pooki tung'ani.

English: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:
Masaai: Amu eibelekenyate ninche aany esuj ninye nemeikenaa hoo enkoitoi enye nabo,

English: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
Masaai: pee etum aaishoo olkiyioi le ilo aisinani elotu enetii, netoning'o ninye enkishirata e ilo oota enyamali.

English: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:
Masaai: Amaa tenegira, aing'ae oidim aiguanare? Amaa teneisudoo enkomom enye, aing'ae oidim atoduaa ninye, aa olorere anaa tung'ani?

English: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.
Masaai: Meitoreisho iltung'ana lemeure Enkai, pee mepik iltung'ana orreshet.

English: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
Masaai: “Ketii olotiaaka Enkai, ‘Anoto enkitamioto oleng,’ maitoki aekata aitadiak.

English: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
Masaai: Inteng'enaki nanu ina nemadolita; tenataasa nanu entorroni, nemaitoki aekata aigil aas?’

English: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
Masaai: Keitobir ninye ina ninyorraa iyie, amu itanya iyie ninye? Amu meeta nchere pee meyie ogelu; neme nanu ogelu metaa imbalie ina niyiolo.

English: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.
Masaai: Ekaajoki nanu iltung'ana lening'unoto, ore lelo tung'ana ng'eni laainining'ito nanu nejo,

English: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
Masaai: ‘Ekeiro Yoab meeta eng'eno, ore irorei lenyena nemetii eng'eno nagut.’

English: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.
Masaai: Enaikash tenetemi Yoab o meiting'o, amu kewal ninye anaa iltung'ana torrok.

English: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
Masaai: Amu eponiki ninye enkiseroto ing'ok enyena, eosh inkaik enyena tiatua iyiook, neponaa irorei lenyena akeshare Enkai.”

English: Elihu spake moreover, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Elihu ajo,

English: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God's?
Masaai: “Idamu iyie ena nijo kesipata? Ijo iyie, ‘Esipata ai ena te dukuya Enkai,’

English: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
Masaai: amu inkilikuanu ajo, ‘ainyoo tipat naata nanu? Kaa sipata nanu aata alang tenataasa eng'oki?’

English: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
Masaai: Ekaawaliki nanu iyie tenebo ilchoreta linono likiboitare.

English: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.
Masaai: Ing'ura keper pee idol, naa ng'ura nena atampo, naatii shumata oleng shumata iyie.

English: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
Masaai: Amaa tinitaasa eng'oki, kainyoo indim ataasa atigilunore ninye? Naa amaa tenetoponari intorrok inono, kaa iyie intaas ninye?

English: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?
Masaai: Amaa tinira iyie asipani ainyoo inchoo ninye; arashu ainyoo doi eng'amu ninye te nkaina ino?

English: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.
Masaai: Ore intorrok inono naa oltung'ani laaijo iyie eipirta ore esupatisho ino naa enkerai e tung'ani.

English: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
Masaai: “Ore enkaraki nena kibookinot kumok e nkop e tung'ani neishir iltung'ana; eipotu ninche eretoto te nkaraki enkaina e ilo Magilani.

English: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
Masaai: Kake metii olojo, ‘Koree Enkai Olaitobirani lai, ilo oishoru isinkolioitin te nkewarie;

English: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
Masaai: ilo oiteng'en iyiook alang nena ng'uesi enkop neiteng'en iyiook aitalang imotonyi oloing'ang'e?’

English: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Masaai: Eishir ninche teidie, mewaliki ninye ninche, te nkaraki ilo wuasa loo ltung'ana torrok.

English: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
Masaai: Esipa tukul mening Enkai enkishirata e pesho, nemeshilaa ilo Magilani ninye.

English: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.
Masaai: Kebaa naa elus tenijo midolita ninye, inchere etii enkiguana dukuya ninye, naa ninye iyie iyanyu!

English: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:
Masaai: Neaku ore naa taata amu meitameisho engoro enye, nemeinining'u ninye oleng intorrok.

English: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.
Masaai: Ebol Yoab enkutuk enye tenkiroroto e pesho, eponaa irorei lemeeta eng'eno.”

English: Elihu also proceeded, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Elihu alo dukuya nejo:

English: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God's behalf.
Masaai: “Nyaaki ting'iria penyo peyie aatum aitoduaa, amu eton ake aata enajo terishata Enkai.

English: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
Masaai: Ekayau nanu eng'eno ai tenelakua, naisho esipata Olaitobirani lai.

English: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.
Masaai: Amu esipa tukul ore irorei laainei neme elejare; ore ilo oiputakine eng'eno netii tenebo iyie.

English: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
Masaai: “Ng'ura, Aimagilani Enkai, nemeeta ninye olomenaa, magilani ninye te ngolon eyiolounoto.

English: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.
Masaai: Meisho ninye lelo torrok ebikoo, kake eisho lelo ooitanyamali esipata enye.

English: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
Masaai: Meiwuang'ie ninye inkonyek te lelo supati, kake ore too laiguanak te nkitoo enye, eitasheyie ninche intarasi, nejukari ninche.

English: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;
Masaai: Naa teneeni ninche too lpisia neibung'i too lgoso le nkisilisiloto e mion,

English: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
Masaai: neibalakinye ninye ninche esiaai enye, tenebo enkarruoisho enye, inchere easita ninche mbaa o lwuasa.

English: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
Masaai: Ebol ninche inkiyiaa enye aaning enkiteng'enare, neitanapisho ajo metung'uai ninche intorrok enye.

English: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
Masaai: Tenening ninche ninye neisiaai ninye, neishu ninche inkolong'i enye te dupoto, ore ilarin lenye nebore enchipai.

English: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
Masaai: Kake tenemening ninche, naa keidak to lalem neye meeta eng'eno.

English: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
Masaai: Ore ilo lemeeta Enkai to ltau, nenyor engoro; meishiru ninche eretoto teneen ninye ninche.

English: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
Masaai: Keye ninche eton aa ooti, neiting enkishui enye te nkurruna.

English: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.
Masaai: Eitajeu ninye lelo ooitamei aitung'uaa nyamaliritin enye, nebol inkiyiaa enye too ngolikinot.

English: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.
Masaai: Aikilaku sii ninye iyie too sinaitin, nikipik ewueji nelala nemetii batisho, ore ina natipikaki emisa ino nebore olkar.

English: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.
Masaai: Kake kibore iyie enkiguana e ilo torrono, kimbung'a akurraki enkiguana o esipata.

English: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
Masaai: Todua ake mikien engoro aeniki esurdaanyare; nimincho ina sapuko elakunoto kimbelekeny.

English: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
Masaai: Amaa enkishirata ino aikindim aitayu tiatua osina, arashu engolon enkidimata ino pooki?

English: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
Masaai: Mianyu iyie enkewarie, ina kata nadung'ori iltung'ana aaiwuang'ie te wueji enye.

English: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
Masaai: Todua kewan mimbelekenyakino intorrok amu ena ninye itegelua eitu igelu olosilisili.

English: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
Masaai: Ng'ura, Eisisaki Enkai te ngolon enye; aing'ae olaiteng'enani onyaanyukie ninye.

English: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
Masaai: Aing'ae otisiraka ninye enkoitoi enye, arashu aing'ae oidim atejo, ‘itaasa iyie entorrono?’

English: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
Masaai: “Tadamu ilepie esiaai enye, ina nataranyakita iltung'ana.

English: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
Masaai: Eing'ura iltung'ana pooki ninye; neing'or oltung'ani ninye te nelakua.

English: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
Masaai: Ng'ura, aikitok Enkai, nimikiyiolo iyiook ninye; mejurrunoyu esiana oolarin lenyena.

English: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:
Masaai: Amu eitadou ninye ilkitong'at le nchan, neirriu ninye enkinuku te nkata e nchan.

English: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.
Masaai: Ina nabukunye enchan te shumata, neshaiki iltung'ana te nkumoi.

English: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
Masaai: Keidim likae atayiolo enkisalaashata oo nkatampo, o endarata e keper enye?

English: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
Masaai: Ng'ura, eidapash ninye enkiwuangata enye aitaman kewan, nenuk nkonyek oo naaiposha.

English: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.
Masaai: Amu te kuna eiguanare ninye iloreren; neishooyo endaa te lengon.

English: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.
Masaai: Eimulumul ninye inkaik enyena te nkiwang'ata, neitanap ninye metoosho ine neyieu.

English: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.
Masaai: Elimu endarata elotunoto enye, Ilo oata olom o engoro eiba entorroni.

English: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.
Masaai: “Ore ake sii tena neikirikira oltau lai, nepuku aing'uaa ewueji enye.

English: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.
Masaai: Toning'o endarata oltoilo lenye o endarata napuku te nkutuk enye.

English: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.
Masaai: Abori keper pooki eimie ninye ina darata, ore enkiwuang'ata enye, neisho meshomo ilpijat pooki le nkop.

English: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
Masaai: Ore pee elusoo neikurrukurr oltoilo lenye; nedaru ninye to ltoilo lenye le nkitoo nemeibooyo ninye inkiwuang'at tenening'i oltoilo lenye.

English: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
Masaai: Edaru Enkai te nking'asia to ltoilo lenye; eas ninye imbaa sapuki nimikindim aatoning'u.

English: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
Masaai: Amu ejoki ninye enkare nataa osoit te nkirobi, ‘tadoiki enkop;’ nejoki enkirujuruj tenebo enchan, ‘Entagol.’

English: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
Masaai: Enuk ninye inkaik e pooki tung'ani pee etum iltung'ana pooki aatayiolo esiaai enye.

English: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.
Masaai: Ina pee epuo ing'uesi entim irrumati lenye, neitirring'a too lkutot lenye.

English: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.
Masaai: Nepuku olkutati te wueji enye, o enkijape to lkutati le nkidapash.

English: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
Masaai: Te nkiyang'et Enkai eishoruni isoito le nchan, ore nkariak naalala neitaa enkare osoit.

English: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:
Masaai: Eirotoki ninye enkatampoi nairrusha enkare; ore nkatampo neidapash enkiwuang'ata enye.

English: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.
Masaai: Eipila ninche aamanaa te utaroto enye, pee etum aaitabai nena pooki naaitanapa ninche, tioriong eina kop namanyayu.

English: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.
Masaai: Enkai nairriu enchan metashaiki enkop, eidim airriu meitamio iltung'ana, anaa eitodol ninche omon enye.

English: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
Masaai: “Toning'o ena iyie Yoab; intasho ineneng'a nena siaaitin enking'asia e Nkai.

English: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?
Masaai: Iyiolo iyie eneikunaki Enkai enkitanapata enye ntokitin, neisho ina kiwuang'ata enkatampoi enye metawang'a?

English: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?
Masaai: Iyiolo iyie enkiroishi oo nkatampo, nena baa enking'asia e ilo oota eng'eno nalulung'a.

English: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?
Masaai: Iyie laa ore nkilani enyena keirowua ina kata eitirring'e enkop, te nkaraki olkutati le kopikop?

English: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?
Masaai: Indim iyie anaa ninye aisalaasha keper, aitagolo anaa enking'uret nasholuno?

English: Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.
Masaai: Inteng'ena iyiook enikipuo aajoki ninye, mikindim iyiook aayau ororei lang te nkaraki enaimin.

English: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.
Masaai: Kejokini ninye nchere ekairo nanu? Ketang'uarra ae kata oltung'ani ajo eishaakino neijori ninye?

English: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
Masaai: “Ore taata meidim iltung'ana aaing'ura ewang'an, ina kata aa sapuk ewang'an te keper ina kata eidipa olkutati aimai neor.

English: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.
Masaai: Elotu te moikuape esikar e sahabu; eishopokino Enkai enkitoo enking'asia.

English: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.
Masaai: Ore ilo Magilani, mikiindim aanoto ninye, kitok ninye te ngolon o too sipat ore esupatisho natimitunye mepal ninye.

English: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina keure iltung'ana ninye; meshilaa hoo lelo oojo aing'eni te lejare enye maate.”

English: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
Masaai: Neitoki Olaitoriani awaliki Yoab to lkutati:

English: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
Masaai: “Aing'ae ele oitomisimis enkikoo too rorei lemetii eng'eno?

English: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.
Masaai: Intasho anaa olee, kaaikilikuanishore nanu iyie, naa aikimbalakinye iyie nanu.

English: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
Masaai: “Kaji apa itii iyie ina kata napik olkitamanyunoto le nkop? Tolikioki, tiniata eyiolounoto.

English: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
Masaai: Aing'ae oibalie ntemat enyena - esipa iyiolo iyie! Arashu aing'ae oyietaa ilo gosoi aitaman ninye?

English: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;
Masaai: Ainyoo naitasheyie ng'apeta enyena, arashu aing'ae oitasheyie osoit lenye lolmairroto,

English: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Masaai: ina kata eranyisho ilakir le ntadekenya tenebo, nebuaku inkera pooki e Nkai te nchipai?

English: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?
Masaai: “Arashu aing'ae oiken ina aiposha too nkikeneta, ina kata nadanya aing'uaa eng'uset;

English: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,
Masaai: tenaitaa nanu nkatampo olkila lenye, naitaa enaimin enkimulumulet enye,

English: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,
Masaai: nautaki ninye ilpolosien, napik iloom ooikenieki nchomito,

English: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?
