English: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
Masaai: Ore doi ninye enkerai neyiolouni too yasat enyena, tenaa ore ina naas naa sinyati nesipa.

English: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.
Masaai: Ore enkiok naning'isho te nebo enkong'u nadololisho, Olaitoriani ninye oitobirua pokira.

English: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
Masaai: Minyorru injo, arashu ijing atua osina; tabolo inkonyek inono naa itum endaa sapuk.

English: It is naught, it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
Masaai: “Aitorrono, aitorrono,” ejo ilo oinyang'isho, kake te nelo aing'uaa, neaku oloisis kewan.

English: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
Masaai: Etii sahabu o soito kumok oogol enkinyang'a, kake ore enkutuk naata eng'eno naa osoit ogol enkinyang'a.

English: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
Masaai: Iwa enkila eilo tung'ani otonyorrayie aitasheiki esile olomoni, nimbung ninye tena nyorrata natonyorrayie aitasheiki esile oo lomon.

English: Bread of deceit is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
Masaai: Ore endaa nanotoki te lejare naa kemelok te tung'ani, kake ore te siadi, neiput enkutuk enye osinyai.

English: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.
Masaai: Ore nkitobirat pooki neitasheyieki te nkiguana; terikore natii eng'eno atua epuoi olarrabal.

English: He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
Masaai: Ore ilo oloolo ainosaa olmarenke, neibalie imbaa naaisudoro, metaa mintaa encholiek ilo oiro te modai.

English: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.
Masaai: Ore ilo odek menye arashu ng'otonye, netiu enkishui enye anaa oltaa otaaraki.

English: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
Masaai: Ore enjung'ore nanotoki aasioki te nkiterunoto, neaku te siadi ene memayiana.

English: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.
Masaai: Mijo ake, “Ekaitalaku intorrok,” taanyu Olaitoriani naa aikiretu ninye.

English: Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good.
Masaai: Ore isoito ooineneng'ishoreki oopaashaa naa olminong' to Laitoriani, ore intemeta e nkiroishi e lejare nemesidain.

English: Man's goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
Masaai: Ore iroruat oltung'ani naa Olaitoriani oitore; kaji naa eiko oltung'ani te nening'u enkoitoi enye?

English: It is a snare to the man who devoureth that which is holy, and after vows to make enquiry.
Masaai: Orreshet to ltung'ani te nesioki ajo, “Aisinyati Olasar”, neitoki ake asipu eidipa ainosa olmumai lenye.

English: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.
Masaai: Ore olaiguanani ng'en nesilu iltorrok nereu enkeju e ngarri aitunyoo ninche.

English: The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
Masaai: Ore enkiyang'et e tung'ani naa oltaa lo Laitoriani, ojur oleng pooki toki e atua enye.

English: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.
Masaai: Olning'o o enkanyit naasho olaiguanani metobikoi, ore enkitoria enye neitasheyieki te sipata.

English: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the grey head.
Masaai: Ore enkisisa oo lbarnot naa engolon enye, kake ore enkishiaa oo lpayiani kituaak naa ilpapit lenye ooibor.

English: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so do stripes the inward parts of the belly.
Masaai: Ore ioshot naadotisho, naa keitukuo intorrok, ore ioshot kumok e ng'udi neisuj nenen wuejitin e atua.

English: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
Masaai: Ore oltau lo laiguanani naa ereyiet e nkare tiatua enkaina o Laitoriani. Neibelekenyaki ninye pooki wueji neyieu.

English: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
Masaai: Ore pooki oitoi te tung'ani naa sidai too nkonyek enyena, kake Olaitoriani ninye oineneng' oltau.

English: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
Masaai: Easata oo supati o esipata, ninye nang'amaroyu too nkonyek o Laitoriani alang enkitayunoto o lasar.

English: An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin.
Masaai: Ore nkonyek olwuasa tenebo oltau o wuasa, oltaa loo ltorrok naa ing'ok.

English: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
Masaai: Ore nkitobirat e ilo oota enyuata osipa erikoki ninye puaan te nkumoi, kake ore pooki osioki neiting ake te yieunoto.

English: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
Masaai: Ore olchumati litum tolng'ejep olejisho, netiu anaa enkinuku nasiooyo aish naa orreshet le keeya.

English: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.
Masaai: Ore enkinyala oo ltorrok naa keoroo ninche aishu, amu etanyaita eas ina nasipa.

English: The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.
Masaai: Ore enkoitoi eilo torrono naa kekordilo, kake ore olkuaak leilo supat naa aisidai.

English: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
Masaai: Enaikash tinimany olpijata le nchumata enkaji, alang tinitii enkaji e nkitok naata ororei.

English: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
Masaai: Ore oltau leilo torrono neyieu intorrok, metum olelatia enye olng'ur too nkonyek enyena.

English: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
Masaai: Ore te neitamei oloikordodisho, neng'enu olmodai ore te neutari oltung'ani ng'en, netum eng'eno.

English: The righteous man wisely considereth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness.
Masaai: Ore isupati neing'or enkaji eilo torrono; enang'akini iltorrok enkidaaroto.

English: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
Masaai: Ore ilo oiken enkiok enye pee mening enkishirata e lelo aisinak, naa keishir sii ninye nemeetae oloning ninye.

English: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.
Masaai: Ore enkishooroto naishoruni too nkisudorot naa keshuk engoro; ore eropare oo nkishorot neitigir engoro sapuk.

English: It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.
Masaai: Ore teneasi esipata, naa enchipai too supati, naa enking'asia too laasak loo ntorrok.

English: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani olo aing'uaa enkoitoi e ning'unoto netum eneeng'iyeng'are to lturrur loo loo tuata.

English: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani onyor esikar naa keaku oltung'ani aisinani ore ilo onyor enaisho o ila nemeaku karsis.

English: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
Masaai: Ore ilo torrono naa elakunoto eilo supat, ore olemeisiligayu naa elakunoto oloitashe too sipat.

English: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
Masaai: Enaikash tiniton te nkop olpurkel natoyio, alang tiniboitare enkitok naata enchankar o lkwenyi.

English: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
Masaai: Ore imasaa naagol enkinyang'a naa kebik te nkaji eilo oota eng'eno, kake ore olmodai naa keijoo.

English: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
Masaai: Ore ilo osuj isipat o enanai e oshoke naa ketum enkishui o enkanyit.

English: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani ng'en, neyiolo enaikunakino enkanasa o logol, negil isunta naaisilig ninche.

English: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
Masaai: Ore ilo oiken enkutuk enye neibooyo olng'ejep lenye, neitapaash kewan enyamali.

English: Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
Masaai: Ore olasurdaanyani, ninye enkarna o ltung'ani owuasa neitokoos, ilo oas imbaa to lwuasa le nkitokoos enye.

English: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.
Masaai: Ore eyieunoto oltashalai naa kear ninye, metua amu keany inkaik enyena eitayu esiai.

English: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
Masaai: Eng'uarrisho iltorrok endama pooki, kake ore isupati keishooyo nememit.

English: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
Masaai: Ore olasar leilo torrono naa olminong, kebaa elusoo eitayio to ltau torrono?

English: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
Masaai: Ore olchakeni lemesipa naa keimin, kake ore ororei le ilo oning'isho naa kebikoo.

English: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but as for the upright, he directeth his way.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani torrono neitodolu enkomom empijan, kake ore oltung'ani oitashe too sipat neing'or inkoitoi enyena.

English: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
Masaai: Ore enemetii eng'eno nagut, nemetii ening'unoto nemetii enkikoo, keidim ayau eanyata Olaitoriani.

English: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
Masaai: Eitaanyuni embarta ina olong e njore, kake ore enkisulata naa eno Laitoriani.

English: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
Masaai: Enaikash te negeluni enkarna sidai, alang enkarsisisho sapuk, naa ore omom nelang enkosholai o sahabu.

English: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all.
Masaai: Ore olkarsis o ilo aisinani naa ketumo te nebo, Olaitoriani ninye olaitobirani le pooki.

English: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani ng'en naa kedolu batisho neisudoo kewan; kake ore olmodai naa kelo dukuya netum enkitamioto.

English: By humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life.
Masaai: Ore olerrinyore le mborron o euriata o Laitoriani, naa enkarsisisho o enkanyit o enkishui.

English: Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
Masaai: Etii ilkiku o rresheta enkoitoi eilo otapong'ori; ore ilo orrip kewan naa kelam ninche.

English: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Masaai: Tuutaki intamoo enkerai enkoitoi naim, ore pee eaku moruo nemeing'uaa ina oitoi.

English: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
Masaai: Ore olkarsis naa ninye oitore ilo aisinani, ore ilo oisilenu naa osinka le ilo oisilenoko.

English: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
Masaai: Ore ilo oun inemesipa naa keisampu eng'olikinoto, ore eng'udi e ngoro enye napi naa keish.

English: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani aminin naa kemayiani, amu keng'arie endaa enye ilaisinak.

English: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.
Masaai: Intupuku impang'ie ilo oimaki intorrok, naa aikipuku enchankar aing'uaa, ore olarrabal o emorore naa keish.

English: He that loveth pureness of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend.
Masaai: Ore ilo onyor esinyatisho o ltau, neeta ilomon oo melook naa keaku olchore lo laiguanani.

English: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.
Masaai: Etii nkonyek o Laitoriani shumata eng'eno, kake kenang'aa ninye lelo rorei le lelo le meeta enkirukoto.

English: The slothful man saith, There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
Masaai: Ejo olturuai, “Etii doi olng'atuny auluo: kaari matua too nkoitoi naalala e nkanasa!”

English: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
Masaai: Ore enkutuk enkitok naibor onyek naa engumoto nagut; ore ilo otagorokine Olaitoriani naa kesulakino atua ninye.

English: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
Masaai: Eenaro emodai tiatua oltau le nkerai, kake ore eng'udi enkitamioto nearaa ninye aitalamaa.

English: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
Masaai: Ore oloibooki enkop olaisinani pee eponaa enkarsisisho enye, arashu eisho lelo karsisi ake, naa kelotu ake sii ninye aaku olaisinani.

English: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
Masaai: Irrugu enkiok ino inining'u irorei lo lang'eni, nintorioki indamunot inono eng'eno ai;

English: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
Masaai: amu keaku esidano tinishum ninche tiatua iyie, te netii pooki atua enkutuk ino.

English: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.
Masaai: Pee etum osiligi lino ataa Olaitoriani etii, aaitayiolo iyie ninche taata ena olong, aa iyie taa.

English: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,
Masaai: Keitu aasiraki iyie inkirorot tomoni uni, imbaa enkikoo o ine ng'eno,

English: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?
Masaai: peyie aaitodol iyie embae naitoriori nesipa, pee itum aishoo ewalata naitoriori nesipa lelo likirriwaa iyie?

English: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
Masaai: Misim olaisinani eji amu kaaisinani, arashu irony oloota osina te kishomi;

English: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
Masaai: amu keng'or Olaitoriani ninche, neinyal enkishui e lelo ooinyal ninche.

English: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:
Masaai: Mintaa olchore oltung'ani oman nang'u, aashu iriamariyie oltung'ani osioki agoro.

English: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
Masaai: Pee miyiolou inkoitoi enyena, nipik kewan atua orreshet.

English: Be not thou one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts.
Masaai: Miaku obo le lelo ooisiligie ilkulikae imbaa, ilo oaku oloitasheiki esile.

English: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
Masaai: Tinimiata entoki nilakie, ainyoo doi pee inyorraa meewai endapash ino?

English: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.
Masaai: Midotu ake entoki naitodolu olpolosie musana ina apa natipika iloo papaai lino.

English: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
Masaai: Idol oltung'ani arriyia te siaai enye? Keitashe te dukuya ilaiguanak; meitashe te dukuya iltung'ana misili.

English: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee:
Masaai: Tenelo niton anya endaa te nebo oloitoreisho, ing'ura tisipu oleng ina natii dukuya iyie;

English: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.
Masaai: naa tenaa ira oltung'ani le nkului, nipik enkalem olgos lino.

English: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat.
Masaai: Ming'uar intokitin enyena naamelook, amu endaa ina nikipikieki olosek.

English: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
Masaai: Teng'ena miar kewan amutakino ing'oru enkarsisisho, teng'ena pee imbooyo.

English: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
Masaai: Ore pee ikurraki inkonyek inono ninye, neimin; amu ketum ninye asioki inaipuko, neilep anaa olkurragos olo te keper.

English: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
Masaai: Minya endaa oltung'ani opiak, ming'uar indaiki enyena sidain.

English: For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.
Masaai: Amu ore ninye netiu anaa ilo limikiyeu to ltau kijoki ninye, “Inosa doi niok!” Kake metii oltau lenye te nebo iyie.

English: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
Masaai: Irrugumu nena belat pooki oo mukateni nindipa ainosa, neimin lelo rorei linono oo melook.

English: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
Masaai: Miro ake te wueji nening'ie olmodai amu kemenaa irorei le ng'eno o rorei linono.

English: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
Masaai: Mintayu ake ina toki musana natii olpolosie, arashu ijing nkurman e lelo lemeeta iloomenye;

English: For their redeemer is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
Masaai: amu ore olalakunoni lenye naa kegol; naa keikilikuanu ninye te iyie.

English: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
Masaai: Intorioki endamunoto ino enkiteng'enare, nipik enkiok ino irorei le ng'eno.

English: Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
Masaai: Mimbooyo enkitamioto ererioroto te nkerai; amu tinindong ninye te ng'udi nemeye.

English: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
Masaai: Tinindong ninye te ng'udi, naa intajeu enkishui enye te nemeneng'a.

English: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
Masaai: Enkerai ai, tenaa aing'en oltau lino, naa keshipa sii ninye oltau lai;

English: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.
Masaai: naa te neiro enkutuk ino inaasipa, naa keshipa oltau lai.

English: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
Masaai: Mincho oltau lino eng'uar ilaing'okok kake shomo inkolong'i pooki tiatua euriata o Laitoriani.

English: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
Masaai: Esipa katukul etii imbaa sidain dukuya iyie, nemedung'ori osiligi lino katukul.

English: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
Masaai: Toning'o enkerai ai niaku ng'en, nintorioki endamunoto ino ina oitoi.

English: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:
Masaai: Miaku ilencholiek oo laokok le naisho, arashu ole encholiek olooisepe tenkinosata oo nkiri.

English: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.
Masaai: Amu ore olamerani oloisepe naa keaku aisinak, neaku ore elepori e merai neishopoki oltung'ani mpurdat.

English: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
Masaai: Toning'o papaai lino ilo apa likitoiwuo, nimimenaa yieyio lino te neaku moruo.

English: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
Masaai: Inyang'u esipata nimimir ake, inyang'u eng'eno nagut, e nkiteng'enare; o ening'unoto.

English: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him.
Masaai: Ore menye ilo supat naa keshipa oleng; ore ilo otoiwuo olayioni ng'en naa keshipakino ninye.

English: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
Masaai: Inchoo papaai lino o yieyioo lino eshipa, inchoo ina nikitoiwuo eshipa.

English: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
Masaai: Enkerai ai nchooki nanu oltau lino, naa inchoo inkonyek inono eing'or inkoitoi aainei.

English: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
Masaai: Amu ore enkitok naibor onyek naa engumoto nagut; ore ina tang'oroi naa enchorro napirik.

English: She also lieth in wait as for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
Masaai: Neirrag ninye aanyisho anaa olaisimani, neponaa ilewa kumok aitaa ilemeisiligayu.

English: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
Masaai: Aing'ae ilo oishir ajo wooi? Aing'ae ilo oota osomit? Aing'ae ilo oota olarrabal? Aing'ae ilo oing'unyug'uny? Kalo ilo oota ilbaa nemeeta eneyopakaki? Kalo ilo oota endoron to onkonyek enyena?

English: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
Masaai: Lelo le meirura eok enaisho, lelo oopuaya aatem enaisho naitushula.

English: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.
Masaai: Ming'or enaisho te nyokieni, ina kata eitokitoku te nkikompe, nedoyio aitobirari too lgoso.

English: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
Masaai: Ore te siadi nikiony anaa olasurai, niking'or anaa enturbubua.

English: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
Masaai: Ore inkonyek inono nedol intokitin neitu aekata edol, ore indamunot inono neimaki intokitin naaitapong'oo.

English: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
Masaai: Nitiu anaa oltung'ani oirragita te mpolos e naiposha, anaa ilo oirragita te nchumata e ng'ape e meli.

English: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
Masaai: Ilo iyie ajo, “Aatoosho ninche nanu, kake eitu aning emion; aaidong'o nanu, neitu aning emion. Kanu doi ade ainyototo? Pee alo aing'oru ae aisho naok.”

English: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
Masaai: Ming'uar lelo tung'ana torrok, niming'uar aitaa ninche encholiek.

English: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
Masaai: Amu ore indamunot enye neipiru olarrabal neiro too nkutukie enye imbaa enkarruoisho.

English: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
Masaai: Te ng'eno eshetuni enkaji naa te ning'unoto eitasheyieki.

English: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
Masaai: Te ng'eno eiputi ilgilat pooki, too ntokitin pooki sidain naagol enkinyang'a

English: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani ng'en naa kegol alang oltung'ani ogol, naa neijia etiu ilo oota eng'eno elang ilo oota eng'olon.

English: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.
Masaai: Amu te rikoto e ng'eno indim aipiru enjore, naa tiatua enkumoi oo lautarok etumi enkishuroto.

English: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
Masaai: Ore eng'eno nagut naa kelakuaniki oleng olmodai, mebol ninye enkutuk enye te kishomi.

English: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
Masaai: Ore ilo oitobiru pee eas ine nkarruoisho, naa keipoti aajo oloitobir enkarruoisho.

English: The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men.
Masaai: Ore enkipirunoto e modai naa eng'oki, naa ore ilo asukenyani naa olminong too ltung'ana.

English: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
Masaai: Ore tininterre te nkolong e nyamali, naa aikiti eng'olon ino.

English: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;
Masaai: Intajeu lelo ooyae meshomo keeya; imbooi lelo oorrorrokino keeya.

English: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
Masaai: Tinijo “Ng'ura, eitu duoo iyiook kiyiolou ena,” keitu emusu ilo oineneng oltau ina? Amaa ilo likirrip oltau aimeyiolo ninye? Naa aimelaaki ninye pooki tung'ani anaa enaikununo esiaai enye?

English: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste:
Masaai: Enkerai ai, inosa enaisho amu aisidai, ore ilkitong'at lo lkenkei naa kemelook tininchamisham;

English: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
Masaai: tayiolo naa ajo neijia etiu eng'eno nagut tiatua oltau lino; tinitum ninye naa itum eseriani too nkolong'i naapuonu, nemedung'ori osiligi lino katukul.

English: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
Masaai: Mirrag arreshisho anaa oltung'ani torrono aarare emanyisho oosupati; miarare enkang enye,

English: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
Masaai: amu ebatata oltung'ani supat kat naapishana, neitoki ake adumunye; kake kemut oltorrono eng'olikinoto.

English: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
Masaai: Mishipa te nebatata o lmang'atinta lino, nimincho oltau lino eshipa te nebatata ninye;

English: Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
Masaai: pee medol ake Olaitoriani nemeshipa, negoro, neiwuang'ie engoro aitung'uaa ninye.

English: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;
Masaai: Mintanyamal kewan tenkaraki ilaasak loo ntorrok, niming'uar ilarruok.

English: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
Masaai: Amu meeta oltung'ani torrono esidano oo nkolong'i naapuonu; amu keari oltaa loo ltorrok.

English: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
Masaai: Enkerai ai turia Olaitoriani o laiguanani, nimigolong'aki hoo obo lenye.

English: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
Masaai: Amu kedumunye emutata te ninche asieku, naa aing'ae oyiolo emutata nalotu eing'uaa pokira?

English: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
Masaai: Ore sii kuna naa nkirorot o lang'eni: ore olkep te nkiguana nemesidai.

English: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
Masaai: Ore ilo ojoki oltung'ani torrono inchere, “Miata iyie entioto,” naa kedek iloreren ninye, neibayu iloshon ninye.

English: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
Masaai: Kake ore ilo oisikong oltorrono naa ketum enchipai, naa kelotu emayianata sidai shumata ninye.

English: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.
Masaai: Ore ilo oishoru ewalata nasipa, neng'utut inkonito enkutuk.

English: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
Masaai: Intobira esiaai ino tiauluo niyau pooki toki niyieu enkurma ore pee indip ina nitum taa aitesheta enkaji.

English: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.
Masaai: Miaku olchakeni oarare olelatia ino miata eniporoki, nimilejisho te nkutuk ino.

English: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
Masaai: Mijo taa ake, “Ekaitaas ninye ina naaitaasa nanu, Ekalaaki ilo tung'ani ina naaitaasa.”

English: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
Masaai: Ashomo nanu agiroo olokeri lo ltashalai, embata enkurma oo sabibu oltung'ani lemeeta endamunoto.

English: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, etubulakita ninye ilkiku; ore enkop nebore entamejoi; ore esuntai enye o soit neturori.

English: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
Masaai: Ina pee aing'or natemaa ayiolou; aing'ura nang'amu enkiteng'enare.

English: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
Masaai: Kang'as airura penyo, kang'as aimug penyo. Kang'as anunuk inkaik penyo ayeng'iyeng'a.

English: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
Masaai: Nikijing'aki osina iyie o esumash anaa olaisimani, nikijing'aki osina anaa oltung'ani otanape.

English: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
Masaai: Ore sii kuna naa indung'eta e rashe e Solomon naatisira iltung'ana le Hesekia olaiguanani le Yuda.

English: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
Masaai: Enkitoo enkisisa te Nkai te neisudoo ninye imbaa, kake enkitoo too laiguanak, te nejurru imbaa aaibalie.

English: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
Masaai: Ore anaa eneba elakuani e keper, o eneba enguton e nkop neija etiu indamunot oo laiguanak mejurrunoyu.

English: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
Masaai: Iwuang'ie endoron ti oriong e nkosholai, netum olkunoni entoki naitainyie entoki sidai.

English: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
Masaai: Iwuang'ie lelo torrok te dukuya olaiguanani naa keitasheyieki olorika lenye le nkitoo te sipata.

English: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
Masaai: Mipik kewan dukuya ine netii olaiguanani arashu doi intashe te ine wueji olkitok.

English: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
Masaai: Amu enaikash tinikijokini, “wou ilepu ene” alang tinikintadoyiori te netii olaiguanani.

English: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
Masaai: Ore ina natoduaa inkonyek inono, misioki aisosion ayau atua enkiguana; anaa kaa ias te siadi; tinikilo ole latia ino aitukurru?

English: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
Masaai: Iimaki olomoni liyieu te nebo olelatia makewan, nimilo aboloo imbaa naaisudoro e likae;

English: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
Masaai: meyau ake ilo oning enkurruna shumata iyie, nitum enkurruna nemeeta enkiting'oto.

English: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
Masaai: Ore ororei otolimuoki aaitobiru netiu anaa olng'anayioi le sahabu oikodokino enkosholai.

English: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu olgisoi le sahabu arashu e masaai e sahabu neija etiu ilo ng'en oisikong enkiok naning'isho.

English: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
Masaai: Ore olkilikuai oisiligayu, neitagol ilo oirriwaa ninye, etiu anaa enkare nairobi, te nkirouaj enkata e nkisampuare.

English: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu inkatampo o lkutati lemeeta enchan, neija etiu ilo owuasare enkishooroto nemeyieu neishooyo.

English: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
Masaai: Te ng'iriata eidimi aailejileja olaiguanani le nkop, naa ore olng'ejep omelok naa kegil oloito.

English: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
Masaai: Tinitum enaisho inosa ake enikiririkino iyie, amu indim ainosa e sapuk nintoki alopu.

English: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
Masaai: Mimoku enkaji o lelatia ino, pee miyek ake, nikiyooki aibayu.

English: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
Masaai: Ore ilo oishakenu embae nemesipa te nkaraki ole latia enye, netiu anaa orinka lo larrabal arashu olalem, arashu embae napi.

English: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
Masaai: Ore enkisiligata oltung'ani lemeisiligayu te nkata enyamali, netiu anaa olalae oigusugus arashu enkeju naishirtitari.

English: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
Masaai: Ore ilo oranyaki osinkolio oltau oata osina, netiu anaa oltung'ani ooru kewan enkila te nkolong nairobi; netiu sii anaa tinipik enaisho naisuijo ewueji netii olbae.

English: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
Masaai: Teneeta olmang'atinta lino esumash, inchoo ninye endaa nanya, naa te neeta enkure, inchoo ninye enkare naok.

English: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
Masaai: Amu inturrurroki ninye inkuk naishu shumata endukuya enye, naa aikilaaki iyie Olaitoriani.

English: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
Masaai: Ore olkutati oing'uaa moikuape naa keyau enchan; ore olng'ejep okurrisho neyau engoro.

English: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
Masaai: Enaikash tinimany olpijata le nchumata enkaji, alang tiniboitare te e nkaji enkitok naata enchankar.

English: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu enkare nairobi to ltau oota enkure, neija etiu ilomon supati ooing'uaa enkop nalakua.

English: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu enchorro natii esarng'ab, arashu enkong'u enkare naing'ola, neijia etiu oltung'ani supat oisho kewan oltung'ani torrono.

English: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
Masaai: Mme sidai tininya enaisho sapuk, metaa mitem aing'oru enkisisa sapuk.

English: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani le meeta enkibooroto e kewan, netiu anaa enkanasa natigilaki neing'uari meeta isunta.

English: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu isoito le nkirobi te nkata enkirowuaj arashu enchan te nkata enkisampuare, neijia etiu enkanyit meishaakino olmodai.

English: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
Masaai: Mikimbung ildeketa iyie arashu te naa iyata enikiporoki, etiu anaa motonyi naapuo to loing'ang'e nemedou aekata aaitirringa.

English: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.
Masaai: Eoshieki elishie embarta, ore olgisoi nepiki enkume o sikiria, ore eng'udi naa ene nkoriong oo lmoda.

English: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
Masaai: Miwaliki olmodai te risioroto e modai enye, arashu iyaku sii iyie olonyaanyukie.

English: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
Masaai: Tawaliki olmodai te risioroto enaikununo emodai enye, pee meng'enu ake too nkonyek enyena makewan.

English: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.
Masaai: Ore ilo oirriwaa olkilikuai te nkaina olmodai, nedung'oo nkejek enyena makewan, neok enapiak.

English: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu inkejek olmaima eililio pesho, neijia etiu endung'et e rashe te nkutuk olmodai.

English: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu oltung'ani oeniki osoit enkopito, neija etiu ilo oisho olmodai enkanyit.

English: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu olkikuei ojing atua enkaina olamerani, neija etiu endung'et e rashe natii atua inkutukie oo lmoda.

English: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
Masaai: Anaa enaikununo olang'oroni le nkawuo opik ilbaa pooki ng'ae, neijia etiu ilo oisho olmodai ogiroo esiaai arashu olamerani.

English: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.
Masaai: Anaa oldia orrinyokino irrugumat enyena, neijia etiu olmodai oigil emodai enye.

English: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
Masaai: Itoduaa oltung'ani ng'en too nkonyek enyena makewan, eeta olmodai osiligi sapuk alang ninye.

English: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
Masaai: Ejo oltashalai, “Etii olng'atuny ina oitoi! Etii olng'atuny nena oitoi naalala enkanasa!”

English: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.
Masaai: Anaa kutuk aji nabolo too enat enyena, neijia sii etiu oltashalai te ndapash enye.

English: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
Masaai: Enukaa oltashalai inkaik enyena tiatua esaani; neinaur ninye te neshuku arrinyoki enkutuk enye.

English: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
Masaai: Aing'en oltashalai too nkonyek enyena makewan, alang iltung'ana oopishana ooidim aatawal te nkarriyiano.

English: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
Masaai: Ore ilo ojing'aki olarrabal lemenyikita, netiu anaa ilo olo aibung inkiyiaa o ldia ogiroo.

English: As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
Masaai: Anaa enaikununo oltung'ani lo loirirua onang'aa ilkeek le nkima ooyupuyup, o mbaa o keeya,

English: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
Masaai: neijia etiu oltung'ani olej olelatia enye, nejo, “Ekaiguran taa ake!”

English: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
Masaai: Ore pee elai ilkeek neye enkima; naa ore enemetii olaing'oming'omani neish enchankar.

English: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu inkuk tiatua olang'at le nkima o lkeek te nkima, neijia etiu oltung'ani le nchankar einuaaya enchankar aitudupaa.

English: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
Masaai: Ore irorei le nking'oming'om naa kemelook, anaa mbelat e mukate, nedoyio aapuo atua ilkutot lo sesen.

English: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu enkimerlel natumurieki emoti e nterit, neija etiu irorei sidain ooirori neme sidai oltau lo loiro.

English: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
Masaai: Ore ilo oisunkur te nkiba neiro to yieta irorei, kake eisudoo aibok elejare to ltau lenye;

English: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
Masaai: te neiro too rorei le mpiris miruk ninye, amu etii oltau lenye olminong katitin naapishana

English: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.
Masaai: ore hoo netem aitoipoo enkiba enye te nkeleekisho, ekeibalunyeki intorrok enyena to lturrur.

English: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
Masaai: Ore ilo otur engumoto naa kesulakino naa keibeleleng'okino osoit shumata ilo oitera aibeleleng'oo.

English: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
Masaai: Ore olng'ejep olejisho neiba ilmang'ati lenyena te lejare. Ore enkutuk olkordo neyau ine nkidaata.

English: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
Masaai: Miwuasa te nkaraki ine taisere, amu miyiolo inaayooki ina olong ayau.

English: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
Masaai: Inchoo likae kisis iyie kake imme enkutuk ino makewan, olomoni, neme enkutuk ino.

English: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.
Masaai: Ore osoit naa keiroishi, ore sii osinyai neiroshi, kake ore engoro olmodai neiroshi alang pokira.

English: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
Masaai: Egogong engoro napi, ore engoro nemutisho, kake aing'ae oidim aitasho te dukuya olom.

English: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
Masaai: Enaikash enkisikong'ata nikinchori naibala alang enyorrata naisudoro.

English: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
Masaai: Eisiligayu ilbaa likipik olchore, naa kumok ing'ututat olmang'atinta.

English: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
Masaai: Ore ilo oiputakine naa keany enaisho, kake ore te ilo oota esumash, edol ninye ina pooki nadua anaa kemelok.

English: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
Masaai: Anaa emotonyi nalo aing'uaa enkaji enye, neijia etiu oltung'ani olo aing'uaa enkang enye.

English: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
Masaai: Ore eilata o esonkoyo neitiship oltau, kake kepolos enyamali oltau.

English: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
Masaai: Ming'uaa olchore lino o olchore le papaai lino, nimilo enkaji olalashe lino te nkolong e ng'olikinoto ino. Enaikash olelatia lino otaana, alang olalashe lino olakua.

English: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
Masaai: Teng'ena enkerai ai nintiship oltau lai pee atum atawalaki ilo laaing'oru nanu aitukurru.

English: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani ng'en nedolu batisho neisudoo kewan; kake ore ilo omoda nelo adoiki netum enkitamioto.

English: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
Masaai: Iwa enkila oltung'ani te neitayio ajo kelak esile olomoni, nimbung ninye to rorei le nkutuk enye nchere keitasheiki olomoni te sile.

English: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
Masaai: Ore ilo omayian ole latia enye to ltoilo sapuk, einyototo ayooki enasirie, naa keikenari aajo oldeket.

English: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
Masaai: Etiu enkitok e nchankar anaa enkare naitipitipu te nkolong nasha.

English: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
Masaai: Ore tinimbok ninye netiu anaa tinimbok osiwuo arashu imbung emborei e ilata, te nkaina enye e tatene.

English: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
Masaai: Eii esekenkei aitipij esekenkei, neitipij oltung'ani o likae tung'ani.

English: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae oramat olng'aboli naa keinos ilng'anayio lenyena, naa ore ilo orrip olkitok lenye naa keyanyituni.

English: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
Masaai: Anaa enaibalunye enkare enkomom ino tining'or, neija etiu endamunoto oltung'ani eutu ilo tung'ani enatiu.

English: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
Masaai: Ore enemeneng'a o Abadon nemeraposho aekata, nemeraposho aekata inkonyek e tung'ani.

English: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
Masaai: Etemi enkosholai te moti, netemi sahabu to lkokuet, netemi oltung'ani te nkisisa enye.

English: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
Masaai: Ore hoo tinipurd te ntoki naidong'ishoreki olmodai, nindong ninye tenebo enkurma naidong'i, melo hoo emodai enye aing'uaa ninye.

English: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
Masaai: Tayiolo katukul enaikununo intare inono, niramat nena kishu inono oleng.

English: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
Masaai: Amu mebikoo taa enkarsisisho intarasi, naa kebikoo sii enkopiyia e nkitoo too ishoritin pooki?

English: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
Masaai: Ore teneishunye nkujit nebulu kulie, nesotuni nkaitubulu oo ldoinyo,

English: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
Masaai: nitum inkilani too lkuoo linono le kerra, nitumie nena kineji enkurma.

English: And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
Masaai: Ketumi kule nikibaiki too nkineji inono, neaku endaa olmarei lino pooki, o enintotiyie nkaisiaayiak inono.

English: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
Masaai: Eilanyisho lelo torrok meeta oltung'ani omirita, kake ore isupati naa kepi ninche anaa olng'atuny.

English: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
Masaai: Ore teneas enkop ng'ok, neeta ilaitoriak kumok, kake ore iltung'ana oota ening'unoto o eng'eno, naa keitasheyie ninche ninye te nkata naado.

English: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani aisinani oibooki enkop ilo aisinani, netiu anaa enchan naar endaa nemeleku.

English: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
Masaai: Ore lelo oomenaa inkitanapat neisis lelo torrok, kake ore lelo ooibung inkitanapat nearare ninche.

English: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana torrok nemening'u esipata, kake ore lelo ooing'oru Olaitoriani naa kening'u katukul.

English: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
Masaai: Enaikash oltung'ani aisinani olo te ng'eno enye, alang oltung'ani karsis laa torrok inkoitoi enyena.

English: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.
Masaai: Ore ilo oibung ena kitanapata naa enkerai ng'en, kake ore ololo aisiritore oltung'ani olubo naa keitukurru menye.

English: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.
Masaai: Teniaku karsis intalaku dupoto too ltung'ana, nelo karsisisho ino aaku, eno ltung'ani onana oshoke too laisinak.

English: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
Masaai: Tenelo neitoming'an oltung'ani enkiok enye pee mening ina kitanapata, neaku ore ninye enkomono enye naa olminong to Laitoriani.

English: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.
Masaai: Ore ilo oitapong'oo ilo supat autaki atua enkoitoi torrono, naa kesulakino engumoto enye makewan, kake ore ilo le meeta entioto naa ketum enjung'ore sidai.

English: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani karsis naa aing'en too nkonyek enyena makewan, kake ore oltung'ani aisinani oota endamunoto naa kejur ninye oleng.

English: When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
Masaai: Ore te nemirisho isupati, naa ketumi enkisisa sapuk, kake te neinyototo iltorrok, neisudoo iltung'ana ate.

English: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
Masaai: Ore ilo oisudoo ing'ok enyena nemebul, kake ore ilo oibalie neing'uaa ninche naa ketum olng'ur.

English: Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
Masaai: Emayiana ilo tung'ani oure Olaitoriani anaake; kake ore ilo oitagol oltau lenye naa kebatatakino atua ing'olikinot.

English: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu enkikurrukur o lng'atuny, arashu olng'arurumi okuetu, neijia etiu oloitoreisho torrono too ltung'ana aisinak.

English: The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
Masaai: Ore oloitoreisho le meeta ening'unoto naa olaironyani ogogong; kake ore ilo oiba imasaa naapurruno naa keitoodor inkolong'i enyena.

English: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
Masaai: Teneitanyamal oltung'ani osarge le ilo tung'ani apa otara, inchoo ninye elimana o metua naa inchoo melo ake oltung'ani hoo obo aretu ninye.

English: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
Masaai: Ore ilo olo te sipata naa keitajeuni, kake ore ilo opong'ori too monko too nkoitoi enyena naa kesulakino eng'umoto.

English: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
Masaai: Ore ilo otur enkurma enye naa ketum endaa sapuk, kake ore ilo osuj imbaa nemeeta tipat naa ketum aisinanisho sapuk.

English: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani oisiligayu naa ketum imayianat kumok. Kake ore ilo osioki aaku olkarsis nemelo eitu eitamei.

English: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress.
Masaai: Tinintodolu olkep neme sidai; kake eas oltung'ani ntorrok te neishori enkiti daa.

English: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani lo lorok neing'oru enkarsisisho nasieku, nemeyiolo ajo kelotu osina enetii ninye.

English: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.
Masaai: Ore ilo oisikong oltung'ani, ore te siadi naa keitoki atum omom, alang ilo opakas ninye too rorei lo lng'ejep lenye oopuyiapuy.

English: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae opur menye arashu ng'otonye nejo, “Imme enkitarruorroto ina katukul,” naa olencholiek e ilo tung'ani amutani.

English: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani lo lorok neinyeyie olarrabal, kake ore ilo oisilig Olaitoriani naa keitaae karsis.

English: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
Masaai: Ore ilo oisilig endamunoto enye naa olmodai, kake ore ilo olo te ng'eno nagut naa kekorduni.

English: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
Masaai: Ore ilo oleng too laisinak, nemeng'oriki toki, kake ore ilo oisudoo inkonyek enyena netum ildeketa kumok.

English: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
Masaai: Ore te nedumunye iltorrok, neisudoo iltung'ana ate, kake te neidaaya neponari iltung'ana supati.

English: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
Masaai: Tenikirerei anaake nintagol elukunya ino, niyooki nabo olong agila, nimintoki aishiu.

English: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.
Masaai: Ore te netii isupati enkitoria, naa keshipa iltung'ana, kake te neitoreisho iltorrok naa keigoroo olorere.

English: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.
Masaai: Ore ilo onyor eng'eno nagut naa keitiship menye, kake ore ilo oitaa inkituaak naaibor onyek encholiek naa keishang'itie imasaa enyena.

English: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.
Masaai: Te sipata eisho olaiguanani enkop enkitashoto, kake ore ilo oisimaa nkishorot neidaikie enkop enye.

English: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani opakas ole latia enye, naa inkejek enyena eisalaashaka orreshet.

English: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani torrono naa keibung'i too ntorrok enyena, kake ore oltung'ani supat eranyisho neshipa sii.

English: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani supat neyiolo sipat eilo aisinani; ore oltung'ani torrono nemening'u ine ng'eno.

English: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.
Masaai: Ore lelo asurdaanyak naa keinuaaki enkanasa enkima, kake kerriny iltung'ana ng'eni engoro napi.

English: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.
Masaai: Tenelo neishankarra oltung'ani ng'en o lmodai, naa kegoro ake olmodai neitoki akueni nemegira.

English: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.
Masaai: Ore iltung'ana oota enkure o sarge naa keiba ilo lemeeta entioto neingoru lelo torrok enkishui enye.

English: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.
Masaai: Ore olmodai naa keiro alimu engoro enye pooki, kake ore oltung'ani ng'en neitirring'a aibooyo.

English: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked.
Masaai: Ore te neinining olarikoni le nkop imbaa e lejare, naa keaku ilooitoreisho lenyena pooki torrok.

English: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes.
Masaai: Etumo olaisinani o ilo aironyani lenye tenebo; neisho Olaitoriani ninche pokira nkonyek enye ewang'an.

English: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
Masaai: Teneiguanare olaiguanani ilo aisinani te sipata, naa keitasheyieki enkitoria enye ntarasi.

English: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.
Masaai: Ore eng'udi tenebo enkisikong'a e nkikoo naa keyau eng'eno nagut, kake ore enkerai natapalayioki naa keyaki ng'otonye enkurruna.

English: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.
Masaai: Ore te nejing iltorrok enkitoria, naa keponari ntorrok, kake keanyu lelo supati aadolu embatatata enye.

English: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.
Masaai: Toosho tarerioi enkerai ino tuutai naa aikincho ninye enkiyeng'iyeng; naa keisho enchipai oltau lino.

English: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
Masaai: Ore ine nemetii enaibon e Nkai nebatata iltung'ana amu meeta enasujita. Kake emayiana ilo oibung enkitanapata.

English: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.
Masaai: Merere olaisiaayiani irorei ake le nkutuk, ore hoo duo nening'u, menyorraa aibung asuj.

English: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
Masaai: Itodua oltung'ani okuetiki aimaki irorei lenyena? Eeta olmodai osiligi sapuk alang ninye.

English: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.
Masaai: Ore tinincho osinka lino pooki toki nayieu te keraisho, niyiooki amaniki etaa olajung'oni lino.

English: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani le ng'oro napi naa kedumu olarrabal, naa ore oltung'ani oota engoro naa keyau ntorrok kumok.

English: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
Masaai: Keitadoyio olwuasa lo ltung'ani oltung'ani, kake ore ilo obor to ltau naa ketum enkanyit.

English: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.
Masaai: Ore ilo oitaa olapurroni encholiek naa keiba enkishui enye makewan; ening ilo deket, nemeeta entoki naibalie.

English: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
Masaai: Ore euriata e tung'ani neyau orreshet. Kake ore ilo oisilig Olaitoriani neserian.

English: Many seek the ruler's favour; but every man's judgment cometh from the LORD.
Masaai: Eing'oru ilkumok omom oloitoreisho, kake to Laitoriani etum oltung'ani esipata.

English: An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani leme asipani naa olminong te lelo supati, kake ore ilo oitoriori enkoitoi enye naa olminong' te lelo torrok.

English: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,
Masaai: Irorei kulo le Aga olayioni le Yake le Masa, etiaaka ilo tung'ani Itiel, Itiel tenebo Ukai.

English: Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.
Masaai: Esipa tukul kamoda oleng mara tung'ani. maata ening'unoto e tung'ani.

English: I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.
Masaai: Eitu aitamok kewan eng'eno nagut, arashu doi ninye aata eng'eno eilo sinyati.

English: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?
Masaai: Aing'ae oilepa alo keper neitoki adou abori? Aing'ae ilo oiturrurro osiwuo too nkaik enyena? Aing'ae ilo otununuko inkariak tiatua enkila? Aing'ae ilo oitasheyie inkiting'ot ena kop? Keji ng'ae enkarna enye, naa keji enkarna enkerai enye ng'ae? Esipa iyiolo iyie!

English: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.
Masaai: Ore pooki rorei le Nkai neibala ajo kesipa; ninye elong'o e lelo oosaru ninye.

English: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
Masaai: Mipon ake ororei lenyena anaa kisikong iyie, nikiyookini aatum aajo ira olalejani.

English: Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die:
Masaai: Intokitin are aaikilikuan iyie mikimitiki ake ninche nanu eton eitu aye:

English: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:
Masaai: Intayu te nanu intalamai mbaa e ntorroni o elejare; mikincho nanu aisinanisho arashu enkarsisisho. Intotioki te ina daa naishiaakino naata.

English: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
Masaai: Pee maraposho ake naayooki aany iyie, najo, “Aing'ae doi ilo aitoriani?” Anaa aaku aisinani, naaku olopurrisho, naisarkionie ina arna e Nkai ai.

English: Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty.
Masaai: Milo aitang'or osinka te dukuya olkitok lenye, anaa kiyooki adek iyie, niaku oloota entorroni.

English: There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
Masaai: Etii lelo oodek iloomenye, nememayian sii noo ng'otonye.

English: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness.
Masaai: Etii lelo oodol aajo meeta ntiot too nkonyek enye maate, neitu eisujari ilduruki lenye.

English: There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.
Masaai: Etii lelo oodamu aajo aisidain ninche oleng, ee, eji kejo ninche aisidain oleng'!

English: There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
Masaai: Etii lelo laa ore ilala lenye naa ilalema, ore ilala lenye naa inkalema, pee etum aainosa ilaisinak aaitung'uai ena kop, o ilo omena tiatua iltung'ana.

English: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough:
Masaai: Eeta olchutai intoyie are, naaishir aajo: “Nchooki, nchooki.” Eetae intokitin uni nemeitaraposhoyu aekata, ong'uan nemejo aekata, “Ataraposhe.”

English: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough.
Masaai: Enemeneng'a, ina kitok olupi, enkop naata anaake enkure eyieu enkare, o enkima nemejo aekata “Ataraposhe.”

English: The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.
Masaai: Ore enkong'u e ilo omen menye neany eyanyit ng'otonye, naa kedumu ilkurruki lo yerata, neinos ilkurragoso.

English: There be three things which are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:
Masaai: Etii intokitin uni naa enking'asia te nanu; ong'uan nemaning'u.

English: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid.
Masaai: Enkoitoi olkurragos to loing'ang'e, enkoitoi olasurai te ndapidapoi, enkoitoi emeli te mpolos oo naaiposha, o enkoitoi e tung'ani eboitare eselenkei.

English: Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.
Masaai: Nena enkoitoi eina naloloito: Enya ake, nejut enkutuk enye, nejo, “Eitu aas entorrono.”

English: For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:
Masaai: Ore tiabori intokitin uni eikirikira enkop; ore tiabori ong'uan nemeidim ating'iria:

English: For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat;
Masaai: osinka te neaku olaiguanani, olmodai oota pooki nanya naraposh;

English: For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
Masaai: o ina kitok naibae te netum olpayian, o enkaisiaayiani najung ewueji e ina kitok naitore ninye.

English: There be four things which are little upon the earth, but they are exceeding wise:
Masaai: Etii intokitin ong'uan enkop naa aikutiti, kake kelus oleng eng'eno enye:

English: The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
Masaai: inkalao: naa imme iltung'ana oogol, neitaiki ake ate endaa neshum te nkata enkirowuaj;

English: The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;
Masaai: ore inkijujurri: neme iltung'ana oogol ninche, kake eitobir inkang'itie enye tiatua isoito;

English: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands;
Masaai: olmaati: le meeta olaiguanani, kake epuo pooki aairiamari to lturrur obo;

English: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.
Masaai: olmokua: laa imbung too nkaik inono, kake etii ninye atua iwuejitin enkitoo oo laiguanak.

English: There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going:
Masaai: Etii intokitin ong'uan naadeenyari tenepuo olotei sidai.

English: A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;
Masaai: Olng'atuny: ogol te pooki ng'ues, nemerrinyo siadi tiae toki;

English: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up.
Masaai: olukunku, o loro, olaiguanani ele te dukuya iltung'ana lenyena.

English: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, lay thine hand upon thy mouth.
Masaai: Tinitomode aaku oloisis kewan, arashu tinitaa oloun intorrok, tipika enkaina ino enkutuk ino.

English: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.
Masaai: Amu tinimposh kule naa itum eng'orno, naa tiniosh enkume e likae nepuku osarge, naa tinironyu engoro neiu enchankar o lomang'ati.

English: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.
Masaai: Irorei kulo le Lemuel olaiguanani le Masa, ooiteng'ena ng'otonye ninye:

English: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?
Masaai: Ira iyie enkerai ai enkerai e ng'uset ai, ewalet enkomono ai, ainyoo enkerai ai?

English: Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
Masaai: Mincho engolon ino, inkituaak, o nkoitoi inono nena naainyal ilaiguanak.

English: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
Masaai: Imme enoo laiguanak, iyie Lemuel, imme enoo laiguanak eokoto enaisho, arashu too laitoriak pee eyieu enaisho napi.

English: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.
Masaai: Meokisho ake nerikino ninche nkitanapat, nemeitoki aasuj esipata e lelo oinyalaki.

English: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts.
Masaai: Inchoo enaisho napi ilo oye, o lelo ootii emion sapuk atua iltauja.

English: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
Masaai: Inchoo ninche metooko pee erikino osina lenye, nemeitoki aadamu osina lenye.

English: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
Masaai: Inchoo enkutuk ino eiro te rishata e lelo lemeyiolo aairoro, niro esipata e lelo pooki ootung'uayioki oopeny.

English: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
Masaai: Inchoo enkutuk ino eiguana anaa olarishani osipa, torripo isipat e lelo aisinak o lelo oomena.

English: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
Masaai: Aing'ae oidim anoto enkitok nadupa naishiaakino enkanyit? Amu eeta ninye tipat oleng alang isoito oogol enkinyang'a.

English: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
Masaai: Keisilig oltau lo lpayian lenye ninye, nemelau aekata ninye dupoto.

English: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
Masaai: Keitaas ninye olpayian lenye isupati neme entorrono, too nkolong'i pooki e nkishui enye.

English: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
Masaai: Neing'oru ninye aitobiru inkilani too lpapit loo ntare tenebo o enkatani neasisho too nkaik to ltau le nyorrata.

English: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
Masaai: Etiu ninye anaa melin o lamirani, eyau ninye endaa enye te nelakua.

English: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
Masaai: Einyototo ninye eton aa kewarie, neitobiraki enkaji enye pooki endaa nanya, neing'uraki inkaisiaayiak enyena esiaai naas.

English: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
Masaai: Eing'oru ninye enkurma neinyang'u; ore too lng'anayio loo nkaik enyena neun enkurma oo sabibu.

English: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
Masaai: Erreten ninye empolos enye te ngolon, neitagol nkaik enyena.

English: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
Masaai: Edol ajo ore pooki toki naitobiru amir neeta dupoto; nemeye oltaa lenye kewarie.

English: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
Masaai: Epik inkaik enyena ina toki naitobiru o lpiyayoi, neibung too nkaik enyena ina garri naripunyeki inkilani.

English: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
Masaai: Eitorioki ilaisinak nkaik enyena enyena, neitoti too nkaik enyena ilaisinak.

English: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
Masaai: Meure ninye enkata enkirobi tenebau amu ore enkaji enye pooki, neeta nkilani naairowua.

English: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
Masaai: Eitobiraki enkaji enye ilkarash le rruat; ore inkilani enyena naa ine kitani napuiyiapuy pilei.

English: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
Masaai: Eyioloi olpayian lenye too nkishomin neyioloi te neton tiatua lelo payiani le ina kop.

English: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
Masaai: Eitobir ninye nkilani naapuyiapuy e kitani nemir ninche; eisho ilamirak inkimeitani meinyang'u.

English: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
Masaai: Ore inkilani enyena naa engolon o enkanyit, nekueni too nkolong'i naapuonu e dukuya.

English: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
Masaai: Ebol ninye enkutuk enye te ng'eno, ore enkiteng'enata o esupatisho netii olng'ejep lenye.

English: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
Masaai: Eing'or ninye aramat imbaa pooki o lmarei lenye, nemenya ninye endaa neitu eisiayu.

English: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
Masaai: Einyototo inkera enyena neipot ninye aajo enamaiyiana; neija sii ejo olpayian lenye, eisis ninye ejo:

English: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
Masaai: “Etaasa inkituaak kumok imbaa sidain oleng: kake ore iyie ilang ninche pooki.”

English: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
Masaai: Ore enkaja naa kelejisho, ore enkishiaa naa enepesho, kake ore enkitok naure Olaitoriani naa ninye natum enkisisa.

English: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
Masaai: Inchoo ninye olng'anayioi loo nkaik enyena, nincho esiaai enye eisis ninye te nena shomito.

English: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
Masaai: Irorei kulo lo laikooni, olayioni le Daudi, olaiguanani te Yerusalem.

English: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
Masaai: Ine pesho, ine pesho, ejo olaikooni, ine pesho ine pesho. Ine pesho pooki.

English: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
Masaai: Ainyoo etum oltung'ani te siaai enye pooki natanaurikia, ina natanaurikia tiabori enkolong?

English: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
Masaai: Kelusoo eishoi, nelotu ae ishoi, kake ebik ake enkop intarasi.

English: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
Masaai: Eilepu enkolong neitoki adoyio, nesiooyo alo ine neilepunye.

English: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
Masaai: Ekutari olkutati alo Kopikop, nemanaa alo enkalo e moikuape; Neiulo aiulo osiwuo elo, ore teina kiuloto enye nerrinyokino eneing'uaa.

English: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
Masaai: Erukokino inchorroi pooki enaiposha, kake meboreyu ae kata enaiposha. Ometabaiki ine nerukunore nchorroi, nenena naaruko ake aaigil.

English: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
Masaai: Ebore intokitin pooki enauri, meidim tung'ani aimaki ninye; meraposho enkong'u eing'orisho, nemeiput sii enkiok mbaa naaning.

English: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
Masaai: Ore ina natii apa naa ninye naitoki atii, naa ore ina naataasaki naa ninye eitokini aas; nemeetae ae toki ng'ejuk tiabori enkolong.

English: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
Masaai: Ketii entoki natejoki, “Ing'ura, aing'ejuk ena?” Etii apake too nkatitin e moitie e dukuya ang.

English: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
Masaai: Meetae endamunoto oo ntokitin naatulusoitie, nemeitokini ae kata aata enadamunyeki, ntokitin neton etii dukuya naasayu, te lelo oopuonu te siadi.

English: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore nanu ele aikooni nataa apa olaiguanani oitasheiki Isiraeli te Yerusalem.

English: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
Masaai: Napik endamunoto ai aing'oru aturu eng'eno e nena pooki naasi tiabori keper; esiaai nemetii enchipai apa eishoo Enkai nkera oo ltung'ana metanyamaliki.

English: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Atoduaa pooki toki naasitae tiabori enkolong; nanyorriki ajo ore pooki naa ine pesho, naa enkijape ake emirareki.

English: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
Masaai: Ore ina natokordile nemeidimi aaitorioi, ore ina nemeetae nemeikenayu.

English: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
Masaai: Najoki nanu kewan, “Aing'orua nanu eng'eno sapuk nagut, nalang lelo apa pooki ooitasheikito Yerusalem te dukuya nanu; neeta endamunoto ai enkarriyiano eng'eno nagut eng'eno oo mbaa nataasa, o eyiolounoto.”

English: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Napik endamunoto ai ayiolou eng'eno nagut nayiolou olkuenyi o emodai. Nanyorriki ajo ore sii ninye ena naa enkijape ake emirareki.

English: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
Masaai: Amu ore eng'eno nagut sapuk, nepik inyamalaritin kumok oltau naa ore ilo oponaa eyiolounoto neponaa sii emion o sina.

English: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity.
Masaai: Najoki nanu kewan, “Wou taata, ekatem esidano o lkar; ntumurru, ndipakinoyu.” Kake ng'ura, ore sii ninye apa ena naa ene pesho.

English: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
Masaai: Atejo sii enkuenia “Ene modai”, ore olkar nemeeta enikintaas sidai.

English: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
Masaai: Aing'orua oleng te ndamunoto ai enaiko te naitiship osesen lai te naisho oo sabibu neton ake aarikito endamunoto ai arikoo te ng'eno nagut, o enaiko te natum aibung emodai o metaba anaa nadol ina apa naji aisidai too nkera oo ltung'ana neas tiabori keper te nena kuti olong'i e nkishui enye.

English: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:
Masaai: Ataasa isiaaitin sapuki; atesheta nkajijik, naunoki kewan inkurman oo sabibu

English: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
Masaai: naitobiraki kewan inkurman o wuejitin neeyeng'iyeng'areki, naun te ninche impukunot pooki oo lkeek loo lng'anayio.

English: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:
Masaai: Naitobiraki kewan ilturot lapikie ina tim oo lkeek nabulu enkare.

English: I got me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
Masaai: Nainyiang'ua irrindiki ilewa, o ng'oruo, naata apa irrindiki ootoiuoki te nkaji ai; naata sii apa iluaat kumok oo nkishu o ntare, alang pooki ng'ae apa otii dukuya nanu te Yerusalem.

English: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
Masaai: Atushumaka sii kewan enkosholai o sahabu o lchumati pooki loo laiguanak, loo lkirinen; anoto sii ilaranyak, ilewa o ng'oruo o nkapiak kumok oleng, inkituaak kumok naayieu olee neeta.

English: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
Masaai: Metaa ataa apa kitok oleng nagiroo pooki apa laatii te dukuya nanu te Yerusalem; naata ake sii eng'eno nagut tiatua nanu.

English: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.
Masaai: Ore pooki nang'uar inkonyek aainei neitu alau ninche; atipika oltau lai atua esikar, amu ore oltau lai nenoto esikar te ekenyata ai pooki, naa ore apa olekoisiaayio le nauri ai pooki.

English: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
Masaai: Nalotu asipu nena apa pooki naataasa nkaik aainei o eekenyata nanoto aasita ina, naa ng'ura, ore pooki naa ine pesho naa enkijape ake amirare, nemeetae hoo toki naata dupoto tiabori enkolong.

English: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.
Masaai: Metaa aibelekenyakine aineneng eng'eno nagut o olkuenyi; kainyoo eas oltung'ani olotu te siadi olaiguanani? Ina ake naidipa ataasa ninye.

English: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
Masaai: Metaa atoduaa ina ng'eno nagut ajo kelus te sidano emodai anaa enalus ewang'an te sidano te naimin.

English: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
Masaai: Eeta oltung'ani oota eng'eno nagut nkonyek enyena tiatua elukunya enye, kake ore olmodai nelo te naimin; nayiolou ake ajo etum pooki olbuket obo.

English: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
