Masaai: Ina peyie ajoki kewan, “Ore ina natum olmodai, naa katum sii nanu; ainyoo naa peyie ataa nanu olang'eni oleng?” Najoki kewan ore sii ninye ena naa empesho.

English: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.
Masaai: Meetae oltung'ani odamu ilo ng'en, nemeetae olodamu olmodai, amu ore too nkolong'i naapuonu nerikinisho pooki. Eye ake ilo ng'en anaa ilo modai!

English: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Metaa aibayie apa enkishui amu ore nena naasi tiabori enkolong naa torrok te nanu; amu ine pesho pooki naa enkijape ake emirareki.

English: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
Masaai: Ekaiba apa eekenyata ai pooki nateekenye tiabori enkolong, adol ajo kaing'ueki ninche ilo tung'ani olotu te siadi nanu,

English: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
Masaai: naa aing'ae oyiolo te naa keaku oltung'ani ng'en arashu olmodai. Naa keaku ake oloitore nena pooki natanyamalaka aasishore eng'eno ai nagut tiabori enkolong. Ore sii ninye ena naa enepesho.

English: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
Masaai: Metaa aibelekenye aisho oltau lai meiting'o osiligi too siaitin pooki aainei nataasa tiabori enkolong.

English: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
Masaai: Amu ore tiae kata ore oltung'ani otaasishe te ng'eno nagut o te yiolounoto o te nkarriyiano neing'uaa pooki metishipakinoyu ilo leitu enyamaliki ninye. Ore sii ninye ena naa empesho naa eng'oki sapuk.

English: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?
Masaai: Ainyoo eeta oltung'ani too siaitin o enauri natum easisho tiabori enkolong?

English: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
Masaai: Amu ore nkolong'i enyena pooki nebore emion, ore esiaai enye pooki naa oltau eiroshiyie; neijia ninye etiu kewarie meeng'iyeng'a indamunot enyena. Ore sii ninye ena naa ene pesho.

English: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
Masaai: Meetae entoki naikash te tung'ani alang te nenya neok netum enchipai te ekenyata enye. Atoduaa sii ena ajo nkaik Enkai eing'uaa;

English: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?
Masaai: amu teneme ninye aeng'ae oidim ainosa arashu aing'ae oidim atishipakinoyu?

English: For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Ore ilo tung'ani oitiship ninye neisho Enkai ninye eng'eno nagut o eyioulounoto o eng'ida; kake ore olaing'okoni, neisho ninye ina siaai esotore neiturrur peyie eisho ilo oitiship Enkai. Ore sii ninye ena naa empesho naa enkijape ake emirareki.

English: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
Masaai: Ore te pooki toki neetae enkata enye, neetae enkata e pooki toki tiabori keper:

English: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
Masaai: Eetae enkata naini, neetae enkata naye, neetae enkata eunore, neetae enkata nadotuni ina natuunoki;

English: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
Masaai: neetae enkata naari metua, neetae enkata naishiunyeki; neetae enkata nagili neetae enkata nasheti;

English: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
Masaai: neetae enkata naishiri, neetae enkata nakueni; neetae enkata e nkishirata o sina, neetae enkata o sinkolio

English: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
Masaai: neetae enkata nanang'ari isoito, neetae enkata naiturrurri isoito tenebo; neetae enkata naibung'i aaitamuat nkaik, neetae enkata nemeibung'i aaitamuat nkaik

English: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
Masaai: neetae enkata naing'oruni, neetae enkata naiminieki, neetae enkata nashumi, neetae enkata naiturrarri;

English: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
Masaai: neetae enkata napolosi, neetae enkata naripi neetae enkata nagirae, neetae enkata nairori

English: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
Masaai: neetae enkata e nyorrata, neetae enkata e nkiba; neetae enkata o larrabal, neetae enkata e seriani.

English: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?
Masaai: Kainyoo dupoto natum olaisiaayiani te ekenyata enye?

English: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
Masaai: Atoduaa ina siaai naishorua Enkai aisho nena kera e tung'ana metanyamaliki ninye.

English: He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
Masaai: Eitaa ninye pooki toki sidai te nkata enye; ore ake sii netipika ninye e ndamunoto e tung'ani endamunoto oo ntarasi, ore etiu neija nemeidim ninye atayiolo ina nataasa Enkai te nkiterunoto o metabaiki enkiting'oto.

English: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
Masaai: Ayiolo ajo meetae ae toki sidai te ninche alang teneitiship ate neng'ida too nkolong'i pooki naaishu ninche;

English: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.
Masaai: enkishooroto sii e Nkai to ltung'ani nchere ore pooki ng'ae neinos, neok, neisikarra te ekenyata enye pooki.

English: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.
Masaai: Ayiolo ajo ore pooki naas Enkai neitashe ntarasi; meetae ae toki naponikini ninye; nemeetae toki naiwuang'ieki te ninye; eitaa Enkai metotiwuo neija, peyie etum iltung'ana aatureita ninye.

English: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
Masaai: Ore ina natii, netii apake, ore ina naitoki atii, netii apake, neing'oru Enkai ina naterewaki aaitalamaa.

English: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
Masaai: Ore tenebo ina atoduaa ake sii tiabori enkolong teine wueji neutarieki esipata ajo etii ake sii ninye ine enkarrueisho, ore ine wueji e supatisho, netii ake sii ninye enkarrueisho.

English: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
Masaai: Najo tiatua oltau lai, ekeiguanare Enkai lelo supati neiguanare lelo torrok, amu etegelua ninye enkata tenkaraki pooki toki, o pooki siai.

English: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
Masaai: Najo to ltau lai tenena naaipirta nkera oo ltung'ana inchere Enkai natemita ninche pee eitodol ninche nchere ing'uesi ninche.

English: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
Masaai: Amu ore eneiting'oki iltung'ana naa ninye sii eiting'oki ng'uesi; ore anaa enaye nabo neye ake sii ninye enkae. Eeta pooki enkiyang'et nabo nenyanyuk, nemeeta oltung'ani enelang'ie nena ng'uesi; amu ore pooki naa empesho.

English: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Masaai: Epuo pooki ewueji nebo; amu enterit eing'uaa pooki nerrinyokino pooki enterit aaigil.

English: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?
Masaai: Aing'ae oyiolo tenaa ore enkiyang'et oltung'ani neilep alo shumata ore enkiyang'et eng'ues nelo abori atua enkop?

English: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
Masaai: Metaa atoduaa ajo metii toki naikash alang teneshipakino oltung'ani esiaai enye, amu ina doi esiaai enye; aing'ae oidim ayau ninye metoduaa imbaa naasuju ninye eidipa atua?

English: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
Masaai: Atoduaa ake sii nena baa pooki e nkitorogonyata naasitae tiabori enkolong. Naa ng'ura, ore lelo kiyio le lelo ooitorogonyitai, nemeetae hoo obo lenye oilejilej ninche! Ore te nkalo e lelo ooitorogony ninche; netii apa engolon, nemeetae hoo obo oilejilej ninche.

English: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
Masaai: Nadamu ajo ore lelo ooidipa aatuata nemunyak ninche oleng, aalang lelo leton eishu;

English: Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
Masaai: neikash oleng te pokira ilo leton eitu eini neitu edol nena baa torrok naasi tiabori enkolong.

English: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Nadol ajo ore eekenyata pooki o enkarriyiano pooki esiai nelotu aimu olom oata oltung'ani to le latia enye. Ore ake sii ninye ena naa empesho naa enkijape ake emirareki.

English: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
Masaai: Emuat olmodai inkaik enyena, neisho kewan meinosa esumash.

English: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Enaikash emborei enkaina nabo etii emborron atua alang inkaik are naabore eekenyata emirata e nkijape.

English: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
Masaai: Ore ake sii natodua empesho tiabori enkolong;

English: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
Masaai: ore oltung'ani lemeeta obo, aa taa olayioni arashu olalashe, nemeeta ake enkiting'oto iekenyat enyena pooki nemeraposho aekata nkonyek enyena te nkarsisisho, metaa meikilikuanu aekata ajo, “Aing'ae doi aekenyaki pee amitiki kewan enchipai.” Ore sii ninye ena naa empesho naa esiaai nemetii enchipai.

English: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
Masaai: Enaikash aare alang obo, amu eeta olerrinyore sidai tenkaraki eekenyata enye.

English: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
Masaai: Amu tenelo nebatata pokira, naa kedumu obo o likae; kake oi iyie ilo laa ninye ake tenelo nebatata nemeeta likae odumu ninye aitasheyie.

English: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
Masaai: Ore ake sii, teneirrag aare tenebo, naa keirowuaju; kake kaji eiko obo teineirowuaju aa ninye ake?

English: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Masaai: Ore hoo neidim oltung'ani atigilu olikae laa ninye ake, eidim aare aairisha ninye. Ore enkopito natasha uni, nemelelek edung'i.

English: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
Masaai: Enaikash olbarnoti aisinani ng'en alang olaiguanani moruo omoda, lemeekure eyieu enkikoo

English: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.
Masaai: ore hoo neshomo aing'uaa korokoroni ajing olorika le nkitoo arashu etoiwuoki te nkitoria enye aa olaisinani.

English: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
Masaai: Atoduaa nena pooki naaishu naapuo tiabori enkolong, tenebo ilo barnoti ilo apa olotu aitashe te wueji enye;

English: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: nemeetae apa enkiting'oto oo ltung'ana pooki; etii apa ninye shumata e pooki. Kake ore lelo oopuonu te siadi nemeshipakino ninye. Esipa ore sii ninye ena naa empesho naa enkijape emirareki.

English: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
Masaai: Irrita iroruat inono ina kata iloito enkaji Enkai, enaikash tininyikaki ainining alang tinintayu ilo asar loo lmoda; amu meyiolo ninche aajo entorrono easita.

English: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
Masaai: Mikuetiki airo te nkutuk ino, nimincho oltau lino ekuetiki airo irorei te dukuya Enkai, amu etii Enkai keper, nitii iyie oriong enkop; metaa inchoo irorei linono eaku kuti.

English: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice is known by multitude of words.
Masaai: Amu elotu enkidetidet too siaitin kumok, ore oltoilo lo lmodai too rorei kumok.

English: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
Masaai: Teninos olmumai te Nkai ijo intayu toki, mimutie ake eitu ilak; amu meeta ninye enchipai too lmoda. Talaa ina ninosa olmumai.

English: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Masaai: Enaikash tiniminos olmumai alang tininos nimilak.

English: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
Masaai: Mincho enkutuk ino kintadoiki atua eng'oki, nimijo ake te dukuya olkilikuai eji enkitadiata ake duo, ainyoo peyie egoro Enkai te nkaraki oltoilo lino; neinyal esiaai oo nkaik inono?

English: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.
Masaai: Amu teneponari enkidetidet, neaku irorei kumok lemeeta tipat: kake turia iyie Enkai?

English: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
Masaai: Tinidol to lkerenket lelo aisinak eitorogonyi neoruni esipata naishaakino te ng'olon, ming'asia ake teina bae; amu ore ilo kitok neing'orita likae kitok alang ninye, neetae ake sii kulikae ooilep te ninche.

English: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
Masaai: Kake ore te pooki, ore olaiguanani neisilig sii ninye inkurman naaturi.

English: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
Masaai: Ore ilo onyor iropiyiani nemeraposho ae kata too ropiyiani; neijia sii etiu ilo onyor enkarsisisho e dupoto; ore sii ninye ena naa empesho.

English: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
Masaai: Ore teneponari intokitin neponari sii lelo ooinos ninche; naa kainyoo dupoto to lopeny aime pee edol ninche too nkonyek enyena?

English: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
Masaai: Emelok injo olaisiaayiani, oi teneinosa enkiti arashu esapuk; kake ore enkuretisho e ilo karsis nemeisho eirura.

English: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
Masaai: Etii entaboi torrono natoduaa nanu tiabori enkolong; ore karsisisho nashum oltung'ani naa kewan ake eshumaki batisho.

English: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
Masaai: Neimin pooki to lbuket, nemeleku toki naisho nkera enyena.

English: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
Masaai: Ore anaa enatupukuo te ng'uset e ng'otonye neijia ake eitoki aiko elo, meishopo anaa apa pee elotu, nemeeta toki e siaai enye naya ninye anap too nkaik enyena.

English: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
Masaai: Ore sii ena naa entaboi torrono anaa apa pee elotu, neijia ake sii eikunari; neaku ainyoo dupoto nanoto ilo oekenyare enkijape.

English: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
Masaai: Neton te nkishui enye pooki tiatua enaimin, o sina sapuk, te nyamali sapuk o ltau, te moyian o te nkiba.

English: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo ore enatodua aa sidai neiririkino naa pee idaa niokisho ning'oru enchipai te ekenyata pooki naekenya oltung'ani tiabori enkolong te nena kuti olong'i enyena e nkishui enye naaishoo Enkai ninye, amu ninye erubata enye.

English: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
Masaai: Ore pooki tung'ani oishoo Enkai masaa o enkarsisisho o engolon pee eshipakino ninche, neng'amaa erubata enye netum enchipai tesiai enye. Ore ena naa enkishoroto e Nkai.

English: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
Masaai: Amu medamu oleng nena olong'i e nkishui enye amu eishoo Enkai ninye enchipai tiatua oltau lenye.

English: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
Masaai: Etii entorroni natoduaa nanu tiabori enkolong, neteeka oleng iltung'ana.

English: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani oisho Enkai enkarsisisho o masaa, o enkanyit, metaa meeta toki nalau e pooki ake naba anaa enayieu, nemeisho ake sii Enkai ninye engolon metishipakinoyu ninche, kake olomoni olotu ashipakino ninche; ore sii ena naa empesho; naa olosilisil sapuk.

English: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
Masaai: Teneiu oltung'ani nkera iip nabo, nebikoo ilarin kumok oleng, metaa ore inkolong'i oo larin lenyena naa kumok oleng, kake meshipakino ntokitin sidain e nkishui, nemetum sii enukaroto, ajo nanu enaikash olkibiroto alang ninye.

English: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
Masaai: Amu elotu atua empesho nerrinyo alo atua enaimin, neitoipori enkaina enye te naimin;

English: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
Masaai: ore ake sii, eitu doi ninye edol enkolong arashu eyiolou toki; netum ake enkiyeng'iyeng alang ninye.

English: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
Masaai: Ore hoo tenaa kebikoo ninye ilarin enkalifu aigil are, neitu ake eshipakino toki aime ewueji nebo epuo ninche pooki.

English: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
Masaai: Ore eekenyata pooki o ltung'ani naa tenkaraki enkoshoke ake, nemeraposho ake te sumash enye. Kainyoo elang'ie ilo ng'en olmodai?

English: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
Masaai: Anaa ainyoo eeta ilo tung'ani ng'en nalang'ie olaisinani otayiolo eneikunaa kewan te dukuya lelo ooishu?

English: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
Masaai: Enaikash ina duaata oo nkonyek alang ina yieunoto nemeuno; ore sii ninye naa empesho enkijape ake emirareki.

English: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
Masaai: Ore pooki naewuo aaku neidipaki apa aipoto, neyioloi enatiu tung'ani, neyioloi aajo meidim ataarare obo ogol alang ninye.

English: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
Masaai: Ore teneaku irorei kumok, neaku empesho sapuk, naa ainyoo eikashie oltung'ani?

English: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
Masaai: Anaa aing'ae oyiolo ajo ainyoo esidai te tung'ani eton eishu tenena kuti olong'i naaishu ninye te nkishui enye e pesho, nena naagiroo ninye anaa oloip? Anaa aing'ae oidim atoliki oltung'ani imbaa naaku te siadi ninye tiabori enkolong?

English: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
Masaai: Enaikash enkarna sidai alang eilata nagol enkinyang'a; neikash enkolong nitua alang enkolong apa nikitoiwoki.

English: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
Masaai: Enaikash tinilo ina aji nabore olkiyioi, alang tinilo ina aji o sirua, amu ena enkiting'oto e pooki tung'ani. Neshum lelo ooishu ina too ltauja.

English: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
Masaai: Enaikash osina alang enkuenia, amu to sina o enkiroishi oltau eitishipi oltung'ani.

English: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
Masaai: Ore oltau le ilo ng'en, netii atua ina aji, olkiyioi; kake ore ilo tau loo lmoda netii ina aji enkuenia.

English: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
Masaai: Enaikash oltung'ani oning enkisikong'ata eilo ng'en, alang tenening osinkolio loo lmoda.

English: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
Masaai: Ore anaa enadar ilkiku einosita enkima tiabori e moti, neijia etiu enkuenia e lelo moda; ore sii ninye ena naa empesho.

English: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
Masaai: Esipa ore enkitorogonyata neitomod oltung'ani ng'en, naa keinyal eropare oltung'ani e ndamunoto.

English: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Masaai: Enaikash enkiting'oto entoki alang enkiterunoto enye; neikash ilo ongiri to ltau alang ilo owuasa to ltau.

English: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
Masaai: Migoro asioki, amu ore engoro neirrag to lgoo loo lmoda.

English: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.
Masaai: Mijo ake, “Ainyoo apa pee eikash inkolong'i naatulusoitie te kuna?” Amu ime te ng'eno inkilikuanu ena.

English: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
Masaai: Eisidai eng'eno tenebo enjung'ore naa dupoto, te lelo oodol enkolong.

English: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
Masaai: Amu ore erripoto e ng'eno nagut netiu anaa erripoto oo mpisai; naa ore dupoto e yiolounoto naa ina ng'eno nagut nagolie ina kishui eilo oata.

English: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
Masaai: Tadamu esiaai e Nkai: aing'ae oidim aitorioi ina naidipa atoriwuo?

English: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
Masaai: Ore teina olong ninoto masaa, ting'idayu; ore teina olong e nyamali nidamu; Enkai naitobira obo anaa olikae, metaa metum oltung'ani ae toki nalotu asuju ninye.

English: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
Masaai: Ore te nkishui ai e pesho, natoduaa pooki toki; eetae oltung'ani supat orrorri te sipata enye, neetae oltung'ani torrono oitoodor enkishui enye te yasata enye torrono.

English: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
Masaai: Miaku supat aitulus, nimintaa sii kewan ololus te ng'eno, ainyoo peyie imut kewan ainyal?

English: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
Masaai: Miaku sii olarruoni aitulus, nimiaku sii olmodai; ainyoo pee iye iyie eng'or enkata ino?

English: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
Masaai: Enaikash tinimbung ena akurraki, ore te ina nimimuat enkaina ino; amu ore ilo oure Enkai nepuku tenena pooki.

English: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
Masaai: Eisho eng'eno engolon ilo tung'ani ng'en alang ilaiguanak tomon ootii atua enkanasa.

English: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
Masaai: Esipa meetae te nkop oltung'ani supat oas isupati nemeas aekata ng'ok.

English: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
Masaai: Mishilaa nena baa pooki naajo iltung'ana, pee meya ake nining osinka lino kidekita iyie;

English: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
Masaai: eyiolo oltau lino ajo ore too nkatitin kumok nitedia sii iyie ilkulikae.

English: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
Masaai: Atetema kuna pooki te ng'eno nagut; najo, “Ekaaku ng'en”, kake ekaalakuaniki apa nanu.

English: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
Masaai: Ore ina natii, naa kelakua oleng negut, egut oleng; aing'ae oidim anoto?

English: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
Masaai: Naibelekeny endamunoto ai ayiolou naing'oru aturu naing'oru eng'eno nagut o esiana oo ntokitin, nayiolou nena torrok e modai o ina modai aa ninye olkuenyi.

English: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
Masaai: Natum enduaran oleng alang keeya eina kitok naa ore oltau lenye naa orreshet oibung'isho, naa ore inkaik naa entoki naibung'isho; ore ilo oitiship Enkai neilany ninye, kake ore olaing'okoni neya ina kitok ninye.

English: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
Masaai: Ng'ura, ena nanu anoto, ejo olaikooni, intushulaki entoki enkae peyie itum esiana enye,

English: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
Masaai: naa ninye eing'orua endamunoto ai aigil neton ake eitu atum. Oltung'ani obo anoto tiatua enkalifu kake eitu atum enkitok te pooki.

English: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
Masaai: Ng'ura, ena ake aewuo atum, inchere eitayu Enkai oltung'ani meitasho te nkitashoto sidai, kake eing'orutua inkoitoi kumok nemesipa.

English: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
Masaai: Aing'ae otiu anaa oltung'ani ng'en? Naa aing'ae oyiolo ina kibelekenyata entoki pooki? Ore eng'eno nagut e tung'ani neitawang enkomom enye, ore ina golon enkomom enye neibelekenya.

English: I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
Masaai: Imbung'a enkitanapata o laiguanani, naa ore enkaraki olmumai sinyati miureishoyu;

English: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.
Masaai: shomo tung'uai enkomom enye; mimutie eton mesidai esiaai amu eas ninye ina nayieu pooki.

English: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
Masaai: Amu ore ilo rorei lo laiguanani naa sapuk,

English: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.
Masaai: naa aing'ae oidim atiaki ninye, “Kaa doi iasita iyie?” Ore ilo oyanyit enkitanapata nemetum enkitamioto, naa ore ina damunoto oltung'ani ng'en neyiolo e nkata neyiolo enkoitoi.

English: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.
Masaai: Amu ore pooki bae neeta erishata enye o enkoitoi enye, hoo naa ore enyamali oltung'ani naa keyek ninye.

English: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
Masaai: Amu meyiolo ninye ina nayooki aaku, anaa aing'ae oidim atoliki ninye enayooki aaku?

English: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
Masaai: Meetae oltung'ani oota engolon naibokie enkiyang'et, arashu eeta engolon naitoreyie ina olong e keeya; olarrabal ilo limikiilany, nemeitajeu intorrok lelo oishooki ninye.

English: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
Masaai: Atoduaa kuna pooki ina kata apikita endamunoto ai nena pooki naasi tiabori enkolong, enkop naata kulikae engolon, neitorogony ilkulikae ootii abori ninche.

English: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
Masaai: Nadol lelo tung'ana torrok enukari; lelo apa oojing nepuku aaing'uaa ewueji sinyati, neisisi tiatua enkanasa teine netaasie imbaa naaijo nena. Ore sii ninye ena naa empesho.

English: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Masaai: Amu medung'okini ina torroni enkiguana aasioki, ore oltau le nena kera oo ltung'ana netudung'o pee eas entorroni.

English: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
Masaai: Ore hoo neas olaing'okoni entorroni katitin iip nabo neitoodor enkishui enye, kake ayiolo ake ajo kesidanu oleng te lelo ooure Enkai, amu keureisho te dukuya ninye;

English: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
Masaai: Kake mesidanu te lelo arruok, nemeitoodor inkolong'i enyena anaa oloip, amu meeta enkuretisho te dukuya Enkai.

English: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
Masaai: Etii empesho naasi te nkop, etii iltung'ana supati laa ninche eitaasi nena siaitin naaipiru lelo torrok, netii iltung'ana torrok laa ninche eipang'aki iyasat naas lelo supati. Atejo sii ore ena naa empesho sii ninye.

English: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
Masaai: Nanyorraa nanu enkitumurrunoto, amu meeta tung'ani toki sidai tiabori enkolong kake pee edaa, neokisho neshipakino kewan, amu eiriamariyie ena eekenyata enye tiatua nena olong'i e nkishui naisho Enkai ninye tiabori enkolong.

English: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
Masaai: Ore pee apik endamunoto ai aitayiolo kewan eng'eno nagut, nadol esiaai naasitae tioriong enkop, nadol ajo metum oltung'ani injo dama arashu kewarie;

English: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
Masaai: nadol teine isiaaitin pooki e Nkai, inchere meyiolou oltung'ani ina siaai naasi tiabori enkolong. O tenaa keturu oleng oltung'ani aekenya eing'oru, metum hoo ninye pito; hoo nenya kutuk oltung'ani ng'en ajo eyiolo. Metum hoo ninye pito.

English: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them.
Masaai: Kake atushuma nanu kuna pooki to ltau, najur aineneng pooki, enetiu lelo supati o lelo ng'eni o siaitin enye etii pooki enkaina e Nkai; tenaa kenyorrata arashu enkiba meyiolo tung'ani. Ore pooki toki natii dukuya enye naa empesho,

English: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
Masaai: amu ebatatakino pooki enyamali nabo aa lelo supati o lelo torrok; lelo lemeeta oloirerio o lelo ooiduruk, ilo oitayu olasar o ilo lemeitayu olasar. Anaa enatiu to ltung'ani supat, neijia etiu olaing'okoni; anaa enatiu te ilo onya olmumai etiu anaa ilo lemenya olmumai.

English: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
Masaai: Entorroni ena te pooki naasi tiabori enkolong, nchere nebo eitingoki pooki, ore isii iltauja loo ltung'ana pooki nebore enkarruoisho, netii olkuenyi iltauja lenye eton eishu ninche. Ore te siadi ina nepuo enemeneng'a.

English: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
Masaai: Kake ore ilo oitutumokoki o lelo pooki ooishu neeta osiligi, amu enaikash oldia oishu alang olng'atuny otua.

English: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
Masaai: Amu eyiolo lelo ooishu inchere keyooki aaye, kake meyiolo ilootuata ae toki, nemeeta ae laakinoto; kake ore endamunoto enye neimin.

English: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
Masaai: Ore enyorrata enye o enkiba enye o olom lenye neidipa pooki aisha, nemeekure eetaae ntarasi erubata e pooki naasi tiabori enkolong.

English: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
Masaai: Shomo inosa endaa ino te nchipai, niok enaisho ino oo sabibu te nchipai oltau; amu eidipa Enkai atonyorrai pooki nias.

English: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.
Masaai: Inchoo ilkilani linono eiborru anaake; nimincho eilata elai te ndukuya ino.

English: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
Masaai: Tishipakinoyu enkishui tenebo enkitok ninyor, too nkolong'i pooki e nkishui ino e pesho nikinchoo ninye iyie tiabori enkolong, amu ninye erubata ino tena kishui te ekenyata niekenya tiabori enkolong.

English: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
Masaai: Ore pooki naibung enkaina ino aas, taasa ninye te ngolon ino pooki; amu metii esiaai anaa endamunoto, anaa eng'eno anaa eng'eno nagut atua enemeneng'a naa ninye ilo.

English: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
Masaai: Atoduaa ake sii tiabori enkolong ajo ore ina kesha neme ene lelo ake ooten, neme ene lelo ake oogol to larrabal, neme enoo lang'eni ake e ndaa, neme enoo lkarsisi ake eng'eno, neme ene leloake arriyiak too siaitin omon; kake eipang'aki ake erishata e munyani ninche pooki.

English: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
Masaai: Amu meyiolo oltung'ani enkata enye. Anaa isinkir ooibung'aki to rreshet torrono, anaa imotonyi naaibung'aki tiatua orreshet neija etiu nkera oo ltung'ana eibung'i to rreshet te nkata torrono, ina kata napulusokino adoiki ninche.

English: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:
Masaai: Atoduaa sii ena kitanyaanyukoto e ng'eno nagut tiabori enkolong, nelioo aa sapuk te nanu.

English: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
Masaai: Eetae apa enkiti anasa natii ilkuti tung'ana atua, nelotu olaiguanani kitok aarare ninye neman aibung, nepik iltimito aitaman agilunore ninye.

English: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
Masaai: Kake enotoki tiatua ina anasa oltung'ani aisinani ng'en, neitajeu ilo tung'ani te ng'eno enye enkanasa. Nemeetae hoo obo otadamua ilo tung'ani aisinani;

English: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
Masaai: kake ajo ake enaikash eng'eno nagut alang engolon hoo netemenaiyioki eng'eno nagut eilo aisinani neitu eshilari irorei lenyena.

English: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
Masaai: Eikash irorei lo ltung'ani ng'en ooning'i te mborron alang imbuakunot oloitoreisho tiatua ilmoda.

English: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
Masaai: Eikash eng'eno nagut alang imasaa o larrabal, kake ore olaing'okoni obo nemut intokitin sidain kumok.

English: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
Masaai: Ore ilojong'a ootuata neidim aitong'ua eilata narropil. Naa ore enkiti modai neidimu eng'eno nagut o enkanyit.

English: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.
Masaai: Ore oltau lo ltung'ani ng'en neboiniki ninye meitoriokinoyu esipata, kake ore oltau lo lmodai neboiniki entorroni.

English: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
Masaai: Ore doi ninye olmodai tenelo te nkoitoi, nemeeta endamunoto, neliki pooki ng'ae ajo olmodai.

English: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
Masaai: Tenelo ake nikidumakino engoro e ilo oitoreisho, milo ake aing'uaa ewueji ino e siai, amu ore nena torrok kindimi aatapalaki tinigira aitirring'a.

English: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
Masaai: Etii enkarrueisho natoduaa tiabori enkolong, anaa duoo enkitarruoroto napuku aing'uaa ilo oitoreisho.

English: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
Masaai: Eishori iltung'ana oomoda ilorikan le shumata; netoni lelo karsisi too wuejitin e abori.

English: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
Masaai: Atoduaa irrindiki ekedito mbartan nadol iltung'ana kituaak epuo too nkejek anaa irrindiki.

English: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
Masaai: Ore ilo otur engumoto nedoiki ninye; naa keony olasurai ilo otur elusie te suntai.

English: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
Masaai: Ore ilo oturu isoito naa kear isoito ninye; naa ore ilo oiper ileng'ot nepik kewan bata.

English: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
Masaai: Tenaa ming'ani entolu ino, neitu iii ninye, neishaakino niponaa engolon oleng; kake eng'eno nagut naretu oltung'ani meisula.

English: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
Masaai: Teneonyisho olasurai eton eitu esiri te ntaleng'oi naa keaku pesho tenesiri eidipa atoonyisho.

English: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
Masaai: Ore irorei le nkutuk eilo ng'en, neisho ninye omom, kake ore enkutuk olmodai nemut ninye.

English: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
Masaai: Ore enkiterunoto oo rorei le nkutuk enye naa emodai, naa ore enkiting'oto e nkiroroto enye naa olkuenyi torrono.

English: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
Masaai: Eponaa olmodai irorei oleng, hoo nemeeta oltung'ani oyiolo ajo ainyoo naaku, naa aing'ae oidim atoliki ninye ina naaku te siadi ninye?

English: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
Masaai: Ore eekenyata o lmodai neitanaur ninye, metaa meyiolo ninye ina oitoi nalo enkanasa.

English: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
Masaai: Oi iyie na kop, tenaa ore olaiguanani lino naa enkerai, ore ilkituaak linono nenya osirua lenye tadekenya!

English: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
Masaai: Ishipa iyie na kop, tenaa ore olaiguanani lino naa olayioni loltung'ani olakuno, ore ilkituaak linono nenya osirua te nkata naishaakino, te nkaraki eng'olon, neme tenkaraki emerai!

English: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki enturuaisho neurunye shumata enkaji, ore tenkaraki enchalan newo enkaji.

English: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
Masaai: Ore endaa neitobiraki te nkaraki enkuenia, ore enaisho oo sabibu neitiship enkishui, newal impisai pooki toki.

English: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
Masaai: Midek ake olaiguanani, too ndamunot inono, nimidek to lgilata lirrag ilo karsis, amu ore imotonyi oloing'ang'e neya oltoilo lino, arashu eboloo kulie nyaun oo naipuko ina bae.

English: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
Masaai: Nteng'ela imasaa inono too nkuapi, ore tenkata nalotu nitum dupoto.

English: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
Masaai: Tooro olchumati lino kat naapishana arashu isiet, amu miyiolo ajo kaa torroni napukoki enkop.

English: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
Masaai: Tenebore nkatampo enkare, neshaiki enkop; naa teneurokino olchani kopikop arashu moikuape, ore ine nesulakino olchani neirrag te ine.

English: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
Masaai: Ore ilo ojurru enkijape nemeunisho; naa ore ilo oisilig inkatampo nemeisampu.

English: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
Masaai: Ore anaa enimiyiolo eneikunakino enkiyang'et iloik tiatua eng'uset e nkitok nairoishi, neaku miyiolo esiaai e Nkai naitobir pooki toki.

English: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
Masaai: Tuuno tadekenya ilanterera linono, ore teipa niun ake aitoki; amu miyiolo ajo kakua oobulu, kulo ashu kuldo, arashu eidim pokira aatisidana.

English: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
Masaai: Emelok ewang'an, naa keitiship inkonyek tining'or enkolong.

English: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
Masaai: Amu tenebikoo oltung'ani ilarin kumok, inchoo ninye eshipakino pooki; kake inchoo edamu ninye ajo ore nkolong'i e naimin naa keaku kumok. Ore ina pooki nalotu naa empesho.

English: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
Masaai: Tishipayu iyie lo barnoti, tiatua kitisho ino, nincho oltau lino kinting'id iyie too nkolong'i pooki e kitisho ino; shomo too nkoitoi oltau lino o too nduaat oo nkonyek inono. Kake tayiolo ajo ore te kuna baa pooki naa aikiyau iyie Enkai atua enkiguana.

English: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
Masaai: Iwuang'ie enkuretisho too ndamunot inono, niwuang'ie aitalamaa emion to sesen lino; amu ore kitisho o enkakenya enkishui naa empesho.

English: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
Masaai: Tadamu naa ilo likintobirua too nkolong'i e kitisho ino, eton eitu epuonu inkolong'i torrok, nenyikaa ilarin oleng, ina kata nilotu ajo, “Maatayie ninche enchipai;”

English: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
Masaai: eton eitu eitomisimisi enkolong, o lapa, o lakir eton eitu esoto nkatampo aayau enchan,

English: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
Masaai: ina olong naikirikira ilarripok leina aji ore iltung'ana oogol neirrugo, neitirring'a lelo ooidong'isho amu etaa kuti, ore lelo oing'orisho too lusien neiliilaa nkonyek enye.

English: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
Masaai: Ore nkutukie oo nkajijik too nkoitoi neikeni, neyagaa oltoilo lenkidong'ore, nedumunye obo to ltoilo loo motonyi, ore ntoyie pooki o sinkolio neitadouni;

English: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
Masaai: naa keureisho sii ninche teine neika, netii enkuretisho enkoitoi; neitapuka aipilipil olchani oji olmolosi, onyaanyukie oseki, nekedoo entargeeti elo; neish eyieuna enye; amu elo oltung'ani ewueji enye nebikie intarasi, ore lelo aishirak nepuaya too nkoitoi naalala e nkanasa,

English: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
Masaai: eton eitu eitir ina opito e nkosholai arashu ebela olbakuli le sahabu ore emoti naokunyeki enkare nebela te nkong'u enkare arashu egila ina keju engarri te nchoto naokunyeki enkare nerrinyo enterit alo atua enkop anaa enatiu apa tedukuya,

English: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
Masaai: nerrinyokino enkiyang'et Enkai ina apa naishorua ninye.

English: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.
Masaai: Empesho oo mpeshoritin ejo olalikioroni; ore pooki naa empesho.

English: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
Masaai: Ore ake sii aa ng'en olaikooni netuutaka iltung'ana eng'eno, eineneng neisum neiturrurru iloyietiaa te nkarriyiano sapuk.

English: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
Masaai: Etetema olaikooni aing'oru irorei ooitishipisho; neiger aitobiraki irorei oosipa.

English: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
Masaai: Ore nkirorot e ilo ang'eni netiu anaa iltuleta neikununo anaa ilmushumaani ootooshokoki aaitagol naa ore inkirorot naatasotuoki netiu anaa olchekut obo.

English: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
Masaai: Enkerai ai, tujurru oleng pooki toki nalus te kuna. Ore enkigeroto oo mbukui kumok nemeeta eneiting'ie, naa ore enkisoma sapuk naa osesen lino eek.

English: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
Masaai: Ore enabayie tena bae, nena pooki nitoning'o. Turia Enkai, nimbung inkitanapat enyena, amu ena elulung'ata e siaai pooki e tung'ani.

English: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
Masaai: Amu eyau Enkai pooki siaai atua enkiguana, o pooki toki oo nkisudorot, aa sidai arashu torrono.

English: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
Masaai: Osinkolio loo sinkolioitin laa ole Solomon,

English: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
Masaai: Oi duoo tenaa aiking'utut too ng'ututat enkutuk ino! amu ore enyorrata ino nelang enaisho oo sabibu.

English: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
Masaai: Ore iila inono naaputishoreki naa kerropil oleng, ore enkarna ino naa eilata nabukuno; metaa aikinyor iyie intoyie.

English: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.
Masaai: Iwaki nanu tenebo iyie matasiooi aaipirri, Aayawua nanu Olaiguanani atua ilgilat lenyena, aikishipa niking'ida tenebo, nikishipakino enyorrata ino aaitalang enaisho oo sabibu, ina pee kinyor ninche pooki!

English: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
Masaai: Ara oltung'ani orok oleng, nara sii sidai, na toyie e Yerusalem, atiu anaa lelo ng'oborri le Kedar, anaa lkarash le Solomon.

English: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
Masaai: Mayieu niking'or nanu to lmena enkaraki emua ai, amu aainosa enkolong. Ore ilayiok le yieyio naatagorokinote nanu, aaitaa ninche nanu olaramatani loo sabibu; kake ore osabibu lai makewan neitu aramat!

English: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?
Masaai: Tolikioki iyie nanu, iyie ilo onyor oltau lai, Ine nirritayie imasaa inono, Ine nincho meirraga enaipirie enkolong; ainyoo peyie atiu anaa obo oloolo lemeeta enetii te mbata oo nkerrai e kulikae shekuti?

English: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.
Masaai: Tinimiyiolo iyie ira sidai tiatua nkituaak, Tusuja irrekiei le nena kerrai, nilo airrita ilkuoo linono, te mbata oo lng'oborri loo lchekuti.

English: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
Masaai: Aaitanyaanyukie nanu iyie enyorrata ai, embarta oo ngarrin e Farao.

English: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
Masaai: Aisidain ilpapit linono edou aagiroo ntakul, naa sidai emurt ino ebore imasaa.

English: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
Masaai: Aikintobiraki iyiook iyie imasaa e sahabu, naaripakino enkosholai.

English: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
Masaai: Ore apa ina kata eirrag olaiguanani to lorika lenye dapash, neitorropil esonkoyo ai ine.

English: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
Masaai: Ore olanyor lai netiu anaa embene e nkorropil te nanu, ina nairrag te mpolos oo lki laainei.

English: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
Masaai: Ore olanyor lai netiu te nanu anaa entukus oo ntapuka, tiatua enkurma oo sabibu e En-gedi.

English: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo ira iyie sidai enyorrata ai, ng'ura ajo ira sidai; ore nkonyek inono netiu anaa ine nturkulu.

English: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.
Masaai: Ng'ura, inkishiaan iyie, olanyor lai, esipa ira sidai. Ore olorika lang dapash naa kenyori.

English: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
Masaai: Ore mbokishi e nkaji ang naa iltarakua, ore irishinani naa olchani onyaanyukie oltarakuai.

English: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
Masaai: Ara nanu entapukai e Sharon, entapukai oo erat.

English: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
Masaai: Anaa entapukai natii atua ilkiku, neija etiu enyorrata ai too ntoyie.

English: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
Masaai: Anaa enatiu olchani loo lng'anayio tiatua entim, neija etiu olanyor lai tiatua iltung'ana ooti. Atotona te nchipai sapuk tiatua oloip lenye, nemelok olng'anayioi lenye te nkutuk ai.

English: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
Masaai: Aatorikuo ninye nanu enkaji o sirua, naadumaki ninye nanu aitaman oltaa le nyorrata.

English: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
Masaai: Intasheyie eng'olon ai te ndaa oo lng'anayio, nikintagol too lng'anayio; amu aata nanu emuoyian e nyorrata.

English: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
Masaai: Oi duoo tenetii enkaina enye e kedienye abori elukunya ai, ore enkaina enye e tatene naaibung!

English: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
Masaai: Esiligieki intae natoyie e Yerusalem, enosa olmumai too ntarakueti naaten inchere mipututu enyorrata ang.

English: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
Masaai: Aning'ito oltoilo lo lanyor lai, ng'ura elotu, edoku too ildoinyo, elang'u indoinyo.

English: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.
Masaai: Etiu olanyor lai anaa enkolii, arashu oloing'oni le nkolii. Ng'ura, nelido oitashe tioriong esuntai ang, eing'or atua enkaji te lusie, eing'orisho too lusien.

English: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
Masaai: Airorie nanu olanyor lai naajoki ninye, “Inyo enyorrata ai, ina nanyor aisul, naa wou tung'uai;

English: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
Masaai: Amu ng'ura, ore ina kirobi neisha eishunye enchan neshomo alusoo.

English: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
Masaai: Etubulutua ntapuka tioriong enkop, netabawua enkata eranyare, netoning'oki oltoilo loo nturkuluni te nkop ang.

English: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
Masaai: Ore olng'aboli neitayio ilng'abolo, ore osabibu neitapuka eitayu olng'usil orropil. Inyo, enyorrata ai, enaikishiaan ai wou tupuku.

English: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
Masaai: Oi iyie enturkulu ai natii atua olbaata le ndapidapoi, natii olbaata le marti, inchooki matoduaa enkomom ino, inchooki matoning'o oltoilo lino, amu ore oltoilo lino naa kemelok, naa sidai enkomom ino.

English: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
Masaai: Imbung'aki iyiook mbariak, nena bariak kutiti, nena naainyal inkurman ang oo sabibu, amu ore inkurman ang oo sabibuni neitapuka.”

English: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
Masaai: Ore olanyor lai naa olalai nara nanu enenye, eirrita ninye ntare enyena tiatua ntapuka.

English: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
Masaai: O metaba anaa nemanaa, nelusoo enkewarie imbelekenyunye olanyor lai, totiwuo anaa enkoilii arashu itiu anaa oloing'oni le nkolii te nchumata oldoinyo osur.

English: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
Masaai: Ore te nchumata erruat ai kewarie, aing'orua ilo onyor oltau lai, aing'orua nanu ninye oleng neitu atum ninye; aipotuo ninye, kake eitu aaisho ninye nanu ewalata.

English: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
Masaai: “Kadumunye alo aman enkanasa, atua inkoitoi naalala e nkanasa o lkurrot oo tumoreki, ekaing'oru nanu ilo onyor oltau lai.” Aing'orua ninye, kake eitu nanu atum ninye.

English: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
Masaai: Aanotito nanu ilarripok, ina kata emanimanaa te nkanasa. “Itoduaa intae ilo onyor oltau lai?”

English: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
Masaai: Ore aa enagirorie ninche, natum ilo apa onyor oltau lai. Naibung ninye, nemaisho ninye elo, o metaba anaa nayau ninye enkaji e yeiyio, o maitijing'a ninye ilo gilata apa le ina naatoiwuo nanu.

English: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
Masaai: Enosa olmumai intae natoyie e Yerusalem, enosa olmumai too ntarakueti o naaten, inchere mipututu enyorrata ang, ometaba anaa nenyorru openy.

English: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
Masaai: Ainyoo ina nailepu to lpurkel, natiu anaa empuruo naitorropiloki te manoo o te nkorropil, te rropili pooki e nena sonkoyoni oo lbiasharani?

English: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
Masaai: Ng'ura, enapitae Solomon to lorika lenye le nkitoo, nemanita ninye iltung'ana magil ntomoni ile magil te Israel.

English: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
Masaai: Neenita pooki ilalema, naa arriyiak to larrabal, meeta hoo obo lenye lemeenita olalem, nerripisho te nkewarie.

English: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
Masaai: Etanapaki olaiguanani Solomon to lorika le nkitoo, ilo oitobirunyeki inkeek e Lebanon.

English: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
Masaai: Eitobirua ing'apeta enyena te nkosholai, ore oriong enye naa ene sahabu, ore olorika lenye naa morijoi; neripuno atua te nkarriyiano, intoyie e Yerusalem naatiriputua te nkarriyiano.

English: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
Masaai: Enchom intae na toyie e Sion, pee ingoringoro Olaiguanani Solomon, eeta emaupe e nkitoo apa naishopoko ng'otonye. Teina olong apa enkiyama enye, teina olong enchipai oltau lenye.

English: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
Masaai: Ng'ura ajo ira iyie sidai enanyor ai, ng'ura ira iyie sidai! Ore nkonyek inono netiu anaa ine nturkulu, eiwariwaru te nkarasha naitoipieki enkomom. Ore ilpapit linono netiu anaa eluaata oo nkineji, edou abori to loshong'ishong'i le Gilead.

English: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
Masaai: Ore ilala linono neibor anaa isupeni e kerra naabarno, nena naaetuo eing'uaa enkisujata, neeta pooki ilmao, nemeetae hoo nabo natua olkuoo.

English: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
Masaai: Ore nkonito e nkutuk ino netiu anaa eusi nanyokie, naa sidai enkutuk ino. Ore ntakul inono netiu anaa indung'ot are olng'anayioi oji kukumanka, eiwariwaru te nkarasha naitoipieki enkomom.

English: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
Masaai: Etiu emurt ino anaa oltalet le Daudi, napurupurana nepuyiapui, nebore imankek naaikununo anaa ilong'oi oo lmurran enkalifu.

English: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
Masaai: Ore ilki linono pokira netiu anaa nkoliin, ilmao le nkolii oodaa too ntapuka.

English: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
Masaai: Ometamanai enkakenya nelusoo enkewarie, o te ilo doinyo oti le nkorropil.

English: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
Masaai: Ira iyie sidai oleng enanyor ai, miaata iyie oleyiata.

English: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
Masaai: Wou tenebo nanu tung'uai Lebanon, esiankiki ai; wou tenebo nanu tung'uai Lebanon. Wou tung'uai entopij oldoinyo le Aman, tung'uai entopij e Senir o Hamon, tung'uai inkapuniaa oo lng'atunyo, tung'uai lelo doinyo loo lowuarak kerin.

English: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.
Masaai: Iwa iyie oltau lai te ngolon, enkanashe ai esiankiki ai, iwa iyie oltau lai te nking'urata oo nkonyek inono, to soit obo ogol enkinyang'a le murt ino.

English: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!
Masaai: Kebaa emeloni enyorrata ino, enkanashe ai, esiankiki ai! kebaa eikash enyorrata ino alang enaisho oo sabibu ore ina rropili oo ila inono alang kulie naarropil?

English: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
Masaai: Eitong'u too inkonito e nkutuk ino enaisho namelok, esiankiki ai; etii enaisho olkenkei o kule abori olng'ejep lino; Ore olng'usil loo nkilani inono netiu anaa olng'usil le Lebanon.

English: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
Masaai: Ore enkurma naikenoro naa enkanashe ai, esiankiki ai, enkurma naikenoro enchorro naripa.

English: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
Masaai: Ore nkaitubulu inono netiu anaa enkurma olng'anayio ooji kukumanka, eeta ilng'anayio pooki gelunot, hena o nardo.

English: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
Masaai: Eeta ninye Nardo o Saparani o sinantei, o lkeek pooki oo rropil, o emanoo o sonkoyoni tenebo isonkoyoni pooki naaisul.

English: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
Masaai: Olchorro le nkurma, enchorro e nkare naishu, o nchorroi naarukunye e Lebanon.

English: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
Masaai: Inyo iyie lo kutati le moikuape! Nilotu iyie, lo kutati le kopikop. Tukuta enkurma ai, inchoo erropili enye eibulaa. Inchoo olanyor lai elotu enkurma enye, nenya ilng'anayio lenyena gelunot.

English: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
Masaai: Aewuo nanu enkurma ai, enkanashe ai, esiankiki ai, aiturrurruo nanu emanoo ai tenebo esonkoyo ai, ainosa nanu olchankaroi apudaki olkenkei le naisho, naok enaisho oo sabibu o kule. Enosa lo shoreta niokioko; entookisho oleng intae iloonyorra!

English: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
Masaai: Airure nanu kake eitu eirura oltau lai. Toning'o! eoshioshito olanyor lai kutuk aji “Taboluoki, enkanashe ai, enanyor ai, enturkulu ai, enemeeta oleyiata ai; Amu keshal elukunya ai, te nkoilielio, ore ilpapit laainei neshal te nkoilielio e nkewarie.”

English: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
Masaai: Aitayio nanu nkilani, naa kaji aiko tenaitoki aishop? Aisuja nkejek aainei, kaji aiko tenaitoki apik enterit?

English: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
Masaai: Nepik olanyor lai enkaina enye enkikenet e kutuk aji, neng'idayu oltau lai tiatua nanu.

English: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
Masaai: Nainyototo abolu olanyor lai, nebore inkaik aainei emanoo, neitong ilkimojik laainei teina manoo naruko, aibung inkikeneta e kutuk aji.

English: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
Masaai: Nabolu olanyor lai, kake eibelekenye olanyor lai nelo, neisinanuo oltau lai pee eiro ninye. Naing'oru ninye neitu atum ninye; aipotuo ninye, kake eitu aawalaki nanu.

English: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
Masaai: Naatum ilarripok nanu, ina kata emanaa te nkanasa; naar nanu, naapik nanu olbae, naaoru nanu enkila ai, lelo arripok le nena sunta.

English: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.
Masaai: Enosa olmumai intae na ntoyie e Yerusalem, tinitumutumu ake olanyor lai, nilikiki ninye aajoki ekamuoi te nyorrata.

English: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
Masaai: Ainyoo elang'ie ina ninyor ino enkae ninyor? Oi ina sidai tiatua inkituaak? Kainyoo elang'ie ilo linyor lino olikae linyor eji pee intanapa iyiook ena?

English: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
Masaai: Ore olanyor lai naa aisidai oleng negol, keibala too nkalifuni tomon.

English: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
Masaai: Ore endukuya enye naa Sahabu nasila; ore lpapit lenyena naa sidain, kerook anaa olkurruk.

English: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
Masaai: Netiu nkonyek enyena anaa ine nturkulu, te mbata oo nchorroi enkare, naaisujaki te kule, naaitobirakino entonata.

English: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
Masaai: Naa sidain intakul enyena anaa ineeitobirieki isonkoyoni neitayu olng'usil oorropil, ore nkonito enkutuk enye netiu anaa ntapuka, naitong'u emanoo naruko narropil.

English: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
Masaai: Ore nkaik enyena netiu anaa sahabu nairina, naikodoki too soito oogol enkinyang'a. Ore osesen lenye anaa ilaa ooitobiraki loo lkanchaoni, netii ninye iila naarropil oleng.

English: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
Masaai: Ore nkejek enyena netiu anaa ing'apeta e Alabata naaikodoki te sahabu. Ore teningor ninye netiu anaa iltarakua le Lebanon.

English: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore enkiroroto enye naa kemelok oleng, naa ore ninye pooki naa keng'uarrayu, olanyor lai ele naa olchore lai ele, natoyie e Yerusalem.

English: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
Masaai: Kaji eshomo ilo lino linyor, iyie enaisul inkituaak? Kaji eibelekenyakine olinyor lino alo, pee kitum iyiook aaing'oru ninye tenebo iyie?

English: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
Masaai: Etadoyie olanyor lai alo enkurma enye, ine neitobirieki isonkoyoni, alo airrita iluaat oo ntare enyena too nkurman, nesotu ntapuka.

English: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
Masaai: Ara nanu eno lanyor lai, ore olanyor lai naa olalai; eirritita ntare enyena too neetii intapuka.

English: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
Masaai: Ira iyie sidai anaa Tirsah, olanyor lai ira sidai anaa Yerusalem, keitureisho anaa enjore naata inankan.

English: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
Masaai: Imbelekenya inkonyek inono intung'uayioki, amu kaaitanyamal ninche nanu, ore ilpapit linono netiu anaa iluaat oo nkineji, naadou to loshong'ishong'i le Gilead.

English: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.
Masaai: Etiu ilala linono anaa iluaat oo supeni e kerra, nena naetuo ailepu te nkisujata, neeta pooki ilmao, meetae nabo natua olkuoo.

English: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.
Masaai: Ore ntakul inono netiu anaa isashat olng'anayioi oji kukumanka, tiatua ina arasha naimulumulieki enkomom.

English: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
Masaai: Eetae nkaiguanak ntomoni ile, neetae nkapiak intomoni isiet, o nkaisiaayiak nemeikenayu.

English: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
Masaai: Na turkulu ai, enemeeta eleyiata ai, naa nabo ake, ina nanyor ng'otonye enye, ina kirotet te ng'otonye. Etoduaa ninye nkaisiayiak neipot ninye aajo enashipa; ore nkaiguanak o nkapiak neisis sii ninche ninye.

English: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
Masaai: “Aing'ae ele otiu enduaata enye anaa entadekenya, newang anaa olapa, anaa enkolong, neitureisho anaa enjore naata inankan.

English: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
Masaai: Atadoyie alo ine netii enkurma oo lng'anayio aing'or nena tapuka naatii oerata, aing'uraa tenaa keimarrimar ilkeek loo sabibu, tenaa keitapuka ilng'anayio ooji kukumanka.

English: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
Masaai: Ore apa eton mayiolo naayau oltau lai, tiatua engarri oo mbartan tembata olkitok lai.”

English: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
Masaai: Tushukunye, tushukunye iyie lo Shulami, tushukunye tushukunye pee kitum aing'ura iyie. Ainyoo peyie ing'or iyie ilo Shulami, anaa oloipidipid aiguran te dukuya injorin are?

English: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
Masaai: Kebaa enare inamuka inkejek inono? Iyie natiu anaa esiankiki o laiguanani! Nepurupurana nkupesir inono anaa isoito oogol enkinyiang'a, esiaai oo nkaik o laitobirani arriyia.

English: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
Masaai: Ore osororua lino netiu anaa olcharaa, ilo lemelau aekata enaisho oo sabibu naitushula, ore enkoshoke ino netiu anaa osototi le nkano omanita intapuka.

English: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
Masaai: Etiu ilki linono pokira anaa ilmao le nkolii.

English: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
Masaai: Netiu emurt ino anaa oltalet lo lalae lo lkanchaoi, ore nkonyek inono netiu anaa lturot ootii Heshbon, te mbata enkishomi e Batrabbin. Etiu enkume ino anaa oltalet le Lebanon, ilo oing'or Dameski.

English: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
Masaai: Ore endukuya ino neitashe aitobiraki anaa oldoinyo le Karmel, ore nena enat inono oo lpapit naaisiong'a netiu anaa nkilani pilei, netil olaiguanani tiatua ina sidano.

English: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
Masaai: Kebaa enkishiaa o esidano niaata iyie, iyie enanyor ai, kebaa elulung'a enyorrata ino.

English: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
Masaai: Isiriri iyie anaa oltukai netiu ilki linono, anaa nkimarrat enyena.

English: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
Masaai: Atejo nanu kaked ilo tukai, naitayu ilng'anayio lenyena nchoo ilki linono metotiwuo anaa nkimarrat o sabibu, ore olng'usil le nkiyang'et ino netiu anaa olng'usil loo lng'anayio oonyaanyukie ilama.

English: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
Masaai: Ore ng'ututat inono netiu anaa enaisho sidai oo sabibu. Ina nalo adoyio aitobirari, naisotuni te nkutuk neim rishat oo lala.

English: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.
Masaai: Ara nanu eno lanyor lai, naa ore eyieunoto enye naa te nkaraki nanu.

English: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
Masaai: Wou, olanyor lai, maape nkong'at, nikirrag nena ang'itie;

English: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.
Masaai: matayooki apuo nena kurman oo sabibu, nikipuo aaing'uraa tenaa keitapuka isabibu, tenaa ketabolote intapuka oo sabibu neitapukita sii ninche kukumanka. Ore te ine naa kaaisho nanu enyorrata ai.

English: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
Masaai: Ore enkaitubului nanyaanyukie enchiliwa neitayio olng'usil orropil ore ilng'anayio pooki sidain netii embata e kutukaji, ilng'ejuko tenebo ilmusan, lelo laatushumaka nanu iyie, iyie olanyor lai.

English: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.
Masaai: Oi napaji tenaa iaku olalashe lai, ilo otanaa ilki le yieyio! Tenaainepu nanu iyie te boo, naa kaang'utut, nemeetae hoo obo laamenaa nanu.

English: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
