Masaai: ilbarnot lemeeta leyiat, shaati naa arriyiak te ng'eno pooki nagut, ooishoro eyiolounoto, o enkibung'ata e nkiteng'enata, oodupa te nkisiayiare e nkaji o laiguanani, pee eiteng'eni ninche isirat o enkutuk oo Lkaldayo.

English: And the king appointed them a daily provision of the king's meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.
Masaai: Nedung'oki olaiguanani ninche erubata e anaa ake e ndaa sidai naa ninye apa einos olaiguanani, o ene naisho oo sabibu naa ninye eok. Naa kepuoi apa aaiteng'en ninche ilarin okuni, ore te siadi ina kata nepuo ninche aaitashe te dukuya olaiguanani.

English: Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Masaai: Ore te kulo naa Daniel, o Hanania, o Mishael, o Asaria lo losho le Yuda.

English: Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abed-nego.
Masaai: Ore ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok loo sunaishi oogelema nedung'oki ninche nkarn: nejo Daniel Belteshasa, ore Hanania nejo Shadrak, ore Mishael nejo Meshak, ore Asaria nejo Abednego.

English: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Masaai: Kake etumuta Daniel nchere meyieu neisarkionie kewan te ndaa o laiguanani aashu te ina aisho oo sabibu apa naok ninye; neaku eikilikuana apa ninye ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok loo sunaishi oogelema pee enyorraa ninye, pee meisarkionie kewan.

English: Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs.
Masaai: Neisho Olaitoriani Daniel omom o lng'ur too nkonyek e ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok loo sunaishi oogelema;

English: And the prince of the eunuchs said unto Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink: for why should he see your faces worse liking than the children which are of your sort? then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king.
Masaai: nejoki ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok sunash ogelema Daniel, “Kaureisho nanu, medol ake olkitok lai olaiguanani, laa ninye likitegelaka endaa ino o entoki niok, ajo ira menati alang lelo barnot lerisiori ino. Neaku ipik iyie enkishui ai batisho ti alo olaiguanani.”

English: Then said Daniel to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
Masaai: Neitoki Daniel ajoki ilo aitasheikinoni laa ninye apa etegelua ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok sunash ogelema meing'ura Daniel, o Hanania, o Mishael o Asaria;

English: Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink.
Masaai: “Tujurro isinkan linono too nkolong'i tomon; nchoo eishori iyiook mbenek mainosa o enkare nikiok.

English: Then let our countenances be looked upon before thee, and the countenance of the children that eat of the portion of the king's meat: and as thou seest, deal with thy servants.
Masaai: Nitum taa aing'ura empukunoto ang o ene lelo barnot ooinos endaa sidai o laiguanani, naa ore te risioroto e mbae naba anaa enidol neijia ntaasa isinkan linono.”

English: So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten days.
Masaai: Neaku etoning'o apa ninye ninche tena bae, nejur ninche nkolong'i tomon.

English: And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat.
Masaai: Ore te siadi nkolong'i tomon nedoli aajo ninche oopir naa biot aalang lelo barnot pooki ooinos endaa sidai o laiguanani.

English: Thus Melzar took away the portion of their meat, and the wine that they should drink; and gave them pulse.
Masaai: Neaku eiwuang'ie ilo aitasheikinoni ina daa enye sidai o ina aisho oo sabibu apa naji pee eok ninche, neisho ninche mbenek.

English: As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Masaai: Ore kulo barnot pokira oong'uan, neisho Enkai ninche enkiteng'enata o enkarriyiano too sirat pooki o te ng'eno; neeta apa Daniel eyiolounoto too nduaat pooki o te ng'eno nagut.

English: Now at the end of the days that the king had said he should bring them in, then the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ina kata, eidipa olaiguanani aitanapisho nchere meitijing'uni ninche atua aji, neyau ilo kitok loo laitasheikinok sunaishi oogelema ninche atua aji dukuya Nebukadnesa.

English: And the king communed with them; and among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: therefore stood they before the king.
Masaai: Neirorie olaiguanani ninche, ore te ninche pooki meetae hoo obo onotoki onyaanyukie Daniel, o Hanania, o Mishael o Asaria; neaku eitasheito ninche te dukuya olaiguanani.

English: And in all matters of wisdom and understanding, that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers that were in all his realm.
Masaai: Naa ore te pooki bae e ng'eno o eyiolounoto naipirta enaikilikuana olaiguanani ninche, nedol ajo kelang ninche katitin tomon ilkuyantik pooki o lasakutok ootii atua enkitoria enye pooki.

English: And Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus.
Masaai: Neton Daniel o metabau olari le dukuya lo laiguanani Sairos.

English: And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep brake from him.
Masaai: Ore to lari li are le nkitoria e Nebukadnesa, neidetidet Nebukadnesa nenyamalu oltau lenye, neimin ninye njo.

English: Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the astrologers, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, for to shew the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.
Masaai: Neitanapisho ilo aiguanani nchere ore ilkuyantik, o lasakutok o loas inenking'asia o Lkaldayo neiturrurruni te nebo pee etum aatoliki olaiguanani enkidetidet enye. Nejing'u ninche nepuonu aaitashe te dukuya olaiguanani.

English: And the king said unto them, I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit was troubled to know the dream.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani ninche, “Aidetideta duoo, netanyamala oltau lai eyieu neyiolou ina kidetidet.”

English: Then spake the Chaldeans to the king in Syriack, O king, live for ever: tell thy servants the dream, and we will shew the interpretation.
Masaai: Nejoki Ilkaldayo olaiguanani, “Lo aiguanani, tobiko ntarasi! Toliki isinkan linono enkidetidet, pee kintodol iyie enkibalakinoto enye.”

English: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, The thing is gone from me: if ye will not make known unto me the dream, with the interpretation thereof, ye shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.
Masaai: Newaliki olaiguanani Ilkaldayo ajoki, “Ore ilo rorei opuku ti atua nanu naa kedede; te nimikintayiololo intae nanu enkidetidet o empukunoto enye, nedung'udung'i intae aaitaa ndung'udung'ot, neidaikieki nkajijik inyi.

English: But if ye shew the dream, and the interpretation thereof, ye shall receive of me gifts and rewards and great honour: therefore shew me the dream, and the interpretation thereof.
Masaai: Kake te nintodolulu intae ina kidetidet o empukunoto enye, niyookiki aang'amu te nanu nkishorot, o nchuneti o enkanyit kitok. Metaa entoduaaki nanu ina kidetidet o enkibalakinoto enye.”

English: They answered again and said, Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will shew the interpretation of it.
Masaai: Newalu ninche aaigil eni are, “Nchoo olaiguanani eliki isinkan lenyena enkidetidet, pee kintodolu iyiook enkibalakinoto enye.”

English: The king answered and said, I know of certainty that ye would gain the time, because ye see the thing is gone from me.
Masaai: Newalu olaiguanani ajo, “Ayiolo aitisip nchere, erishata intae ing'oruru, enkaraki nitoduaa intae aajo aauno nanu olomoni,

English: But if ye will not make known unto me the dream, there is but one decree for you: for ye have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, till the time be changed: therefore tell me the dream, and I shall know that ye can shew me the interpretation thereof.
Masaai: nchere ti nimimbalunyenye intae ina kidetidet te nanu, naa ena nabo ake endung'okinoto inyi e nkiguana. Itoning'okinote intae pee iroro elejare o lemeitoriori te dukuya nanu o meibelekenyata nkatitin. Metaa entolikioki nanu enkidetidet pee ayiolou nchere eikindimidimi aatoliki enkibalakinoto enye.”

English: The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is not a man upon the earth that can shew the king's matter: therefore there is no king, lord, nor ruler, that asked such things at any magician, or astrologer, or Chaldean.
Masaai: Newaliki Ilkaldayo olaiguanani aajoki, “Meetae hoo oltung'ani te nkop oidim aitabai ena yieunoto o laiguanani; amu meetae aekata olaiguanani kitok aashu ogol oikilikuanua embae naaijo ena too loibonok pooki o too lasakutok, o too Lkaldayo.

English: And it is a rare thing that the king requireth, and there is none other that can shew it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.
Masaai: Ore ena bae naikilikuanu olaiguanani naa kegol, nemeetae likae oidim aitoduaa ninye olaiguanani meteleku ake nkaitin, naa ore emanyisho enye neme te nebo iloata seseni loo nkiri.”

English: For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ena negoro olaiguanani nerasu oleng te ngoro neitanapisho nchere ore lelo tung'ana pooki ang'eni le Babilon neidaikieki.

English: And the decree went forth that the wise men should be slain; and they sought Daniel and his fellows to be slain.
Masaai: Neaku eibulayie ina kitanapata nchere ore lelo tung'ana ang'eni naa keari metuata, neing'oru ninche Daniel o lelo le ncholiek enye, pee ear ninche metuata.

English: Then Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom to Arioch the captain of the king's guard, which was gone forth to slay the wise men of Babylon:
Masaai: Newaliki Daniel Ariok, ilo kitok le rripore o laiguanani, to losek o tenkarriyiano, laa ninye apa oshomo aar metuata iltung'ana ang'eni le Babilon;

English: He answered and said to Arioch the king's captain, Why is the decree so hasty from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
Masaai: nejoki ninye Ariok, ilo kitok le rripore o laiguanani, “Kainyoo pee errish oleng ena kitanapata o laiguanani?” Neitayiolo taa Ariok Daniel ina bae.

English: Then Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would give him time, and that he would shew the king the interpretation.
Masaai: Nelo Daniel atua aji nesai olaiguanani meishoo ninye enkata pee etum aitoduaa olaiguanani enkibalakinoto.

English: Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:
Masaai: Neitoki Daniel alo atua enkaji enye, neitayiolo ina bae Hanania, o Mishael o Asaria, lelo le ncholiek enye,

English: That they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his fellows should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Masaai: nejoki ninche meing'oru olng'ur le Nkai e shumata ti alo ena kisudoroto, pee meidaaya ake Daniel o lelo le ncholiek enye te nebo lelo ang'eni le Babilon.

English: Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Masaai: Neboluni taa ina kisudoroto aaitodol Daniel te nduaata e kewarie. Neisis Daniel Enkai e shumata.

English: Daniel answered and said, Blessed be the name of God for ever and ever: for wisdom and might are his:
Masaai: Nejo Daniel: “Meisisi enkarna e Nkai ntarasi o ntarasi, amu enenye eng'eno o enkidimata.

English: And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding:
Masaai: Eibelekeny ninye nkatitin o rishat; eiwuang'ie ninye ilaiguanak neput ilaiguanak; neisho ninye eng'eno nagut lelo ng'eni o eyiolounoto;

English: He revealeth the deep and secret things: he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.
Masaai: eitodolu ninye mbaa naagut oo nkisudorot; neyiolo ninye ina natii atua enaimin, naa ninye ebikie ewang'an.

English: I thank thee, and praise thee, O thou God of my fathers, who hast given me wisdom and might, and hast made known unto me now what we desired of thee: for thou hast now made known unto us the king's matter.
Masaai: Iyie, Enkai o loo papa, aaisho nanu enashe o enkisisa, amu kinchoo nanu eng'eno o engolon, nikintayiolo nanu nena nikinkilikuanutua te iyie, amu ntayiolo iyie iyiook ina bae naipirta olaiguanani.”

English: Therefore Daniel went in unto Arioch, whom the king had ordained to destroy the wise men of Babylon: he went and said thus unto him; Destroy not the wise men of Babylon: bring me in before the king, and I will shew unto the king the interpretation.
Masaai: Nelo taa Daniel atua ine netii Ariok, laa ninye etegelua olaiguanani meidaikie lelo tung'ana ang'eni le Babilon, nelo ajoki ninye nji, “Mindaikie iyie lelo tung'ana ang'eni le Babilon; torikoki nanu mashomo dukuya olaiguanani, pee alo aitodol olaiguanani ina kibalakinoto.”

English: Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste and said thus unto him, I have found a man of the captives of Judah, that will make known unto the king the interpretation.
Masaai: Neriku Ariok Daniel aitasieku aitijing'u meitasho te dukuya olaiguanani nelo ajoki ninye nji: “Anoto nanu ti atua lelo yarunoto ooing'uaa Yuda oltung'ani oidim aitayiolo olaiguanani ina kibalakinoto.”

English: The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, Art thou able to make known unto me the dream which I have seen, and the interpretation thereof?
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Daniel, laa keji apa enkarna enye Belteshasa, “Eikindim iyie aitayiolo nanu ina kidetidet natoduaa o enkibalakinoto enye?”

English: Daniel answered in the presence of the king, and said, The secret which the king hath demanded cannot the wise men, the astrologers, the magicians, the soothsayers, shew unto the king;
Masaai: Newaliki Daniel olaiguanani ajoki, “Meetae iltung'ana ang'eni, anaa iloontaleng'o, anaa ilkuyantik, aashu laaing'urak loo lakir ooidim aaitoduaa olaiguanani ina kisudoroto naikilikuanua,

English: But there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these;
Masaai: kake etii Enkai e shumata naa ninye nabolu nkisudorot neitayiolo ninye olaiguanani Nebukadnesa ina nayooki aaku too nkolong'i e siadi. Ore ina kidetidet ino o nena duaat e lukunya ino ina kata irragita te ndapash naa ninche kuna:

English: As for thee, O king, thy thoughts came into thy mind upon thy bed, what should come to pass hereafter: and he that revealeth secrets maketh known to thee what shall come to pass.
Masaai: Ore te iyie, lo aiguanani, ina kata irrag te ndapash, nepuonu ndamunot oo naaidim aataa te siadi; naa ore ilo oibalunye nkisudorot nikintayiolo iyie ina nayooki aaku.

English: But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but for their sakes that shall make known the interpretation to the king, and that thou mightest know the thoughts of thy heart.
Masaai: Kake ore te nanu, mme te nkaraki eng'eno ai naata alang pooki ooishu pee eibalunyeki ena kisudoroto te nanu, kake pee etumi aaitayiolo olaiguanani enkibalakinoto enye, pee itum atayiolo indamunot o ltau lino.

English: Thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image. This great image, whose brightness was excellent, stood before thee; and the form thereof was terrible.
Masaai: “Itoduaa iyie, lo aiguanani, naa ng'ura, enkitanyaanyukoto kitok. Ore ena kitanyaanyukoto kitok oleng neeta ewang'an nawang oleng, neitashe te dukuya iyie, naa tenidol keitureisho.

English: This image's head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass,
Masaai: Ore endukuya ena kitanyaanyukoto naa ene sahabu nasila, ore olgoo lenye o nkaik naa ine nkosholai, ore enkoshoke enye o nkupesir naa ino suyai,

English: His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.
Masaai: ore nkejek enyena naa ine sekenkei, ore ndapi enyena oo nkejek naa olkuroti oshula esekenkei o enterit.

English: Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.
Masaai: Ore anaa enitoduaa etebeluaki osoit neme te nkaina e tung'ani nesulakino aosh ina kitanyaanyukoto nena kejek enyena naashula esekenkei o esarng'ab nebel ninche aitaa mbelibelat.

English: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
Masaai: Neaku ore ina sekenkei, o ina sarng'ab o ilo suyai, o ina osholai o ina sahabu nerrarra pooki aaku mbelibelat netiu anaa suut ewueji neidong'ieki enkurma te nkata e nkirowuaj, neya ninche olkutati o metaa medoli ninye enkiti enye. Kake ore ilo soit otoosho ina kitanyaanyukoto neaku oldoinyo sapuk neiput enkop pooki.

English: This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.
Masaai: “Ena apa ina kidetidet; naa eikiliki naa taata iyiook olaiguanani enkibalakinoto enye.

English: Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory.
Masaai: Ore iyie, Laaiguanani, nira olaiguanani loo laiguanak, laa iyie eishoo Enkai e shumata enkitoria, o engolon, o enkidimata, o enkitoo;

English: And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold.
Masaai: naa atua nkaik inono etipika ninye, eneba anaa enemanya tung'ani, o ng'uesi e ong'ata, o ntaritik o loing'ang'e, nikintaa iyie olaitoriani te shumata ninche pooki - iyie ina dukuya e sahabu.

English: And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.
Masaai: Ore te siadi iyie nedumunye ae kitoria nemegol anaa enino, o enkae e uni o suyai naa kelo aitore enkop pooki.

English: And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things: and as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise.
Masaai: Naa kelotu enkitoria e ong'uan, nagol anaa esekenkei, amu kebel esekenkei ntokitin pooki neitaa empunyua; naa ore anaa esekenkei napurdisho kebel nepurd kuna pooki.

English: And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters' clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the iron mixed with miry clay.
Masaai: Naa ore anaa enitoduaa ndapi enyena oo nkejek o lkimojik aa esarng'ab, o laitobirani eshula o esekenkei keaku enkitoria naoro; kake ore embata ndapai e sekenkei keaku ketii atua ninye, anaa ake enitoduaa esekenkei eshula o enterit.

English: And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.
Masaai: Naa ore anaa enitoduaa lelo kimojik loo nkejek aa esekenkei nashula o enterit neijia etiu ina kitoria kegol ti ae alo neshal ti ae alo.

English: And whereas thou sawest iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.
Masaai: Ore anaa enitoduaa iyie esekenkei eshula o esarng'ab neijia etiu eshula maate aayama, kake meibung'a maate aaku nabo, anaa ake enemeibung'a esekenkei o enterit.

English: And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.
Masaai: Ore ti atua nkolong'i e lelo aiguanak neun Enkai e shumata enkitoria merruoyo ae kata, ore enkitoria enye meya ae kata kulikae tung'ana, naa kerrar ninye nkitoriat pooki neiting'ie ninche, neitashe ninye ntarasi;

English: Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.
Masaai: anaa ake enitoduaa nchere etebeluaki osoit to ldoinyo neme te nkaina e tung'ani nerrar ina sekendei, o suyai, o enterit, o enkosholai o ina sahabu. Enkai kitok naitayiolo olaiguanani ina nayooki atiu te siadi. Kedede ina kidetidet nesipa enkibalakinoto enye.”

English: Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an oblation and sweet odours unto him.
Masaai: Nebatata olaiguanani Nebukadnesa te nkomom enye, neserem ninye Daniel, neitanapisho pee ei taikini ninye olasar nepejokini enkorropil.

English: The king answered unto Daniel, and said, Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, seeing thou couldst reveal this secret.
Masaai: Nejoki olaiguanani Daniel, “Esipa ore Enkai ino naa Enkai oo nkaitin naa Olaitoriani loo laiguanak, naa olaitodolunoni loo nkisudorot, amu indima iyie atabolu ena kisudoroto.”

English: Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.
Masaai: Neisho ilo aiguanani Daniel enkitoo e shumata o nkishorot kumok sapuki neisho ninye meitoria olosho e nkop e Babilon pooki, neitaa sii ninye olkitok loo lang'eni pooki le Babilon.

English: Then Daniel requested of the king, and he set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon: but Daniel sat in the gate of the king.
Masaai: Neikilikuanu Daniel to laiguanani, negelu ninye Shadrak, o Meshak o Abednego metaa ninche ooing'or mbaa e nkop e Babilon; kake etobiko ninye Daniel to lgoriet te nkaji o laiguanani.

English: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
Masaai: Neitobir olaiguanani Nebukadnesa enkitanyaanyukoto e sahabu, naa ore enkadoro enye naa ntemat e nkaina ntomoni ile naa ntemat e nkaina ile neitasheiyie ninye enkong'ata e Dura, to lkerenket e Babilon.

English: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the princes, the governors, and the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
Masaai: Neitoki Nebukadnesa airriwaa ilkiliku meiturrurruni ilkituaak o laitasheikinok sunash ogelema o lbalusuni o ilaiguanak o ilashumak loo mpisai o ilkituaak loo nkitanapat o lkituaak pooki loo loshon pee epuonu enkitisinyata ina kitanyaanyukoto natesheta olaiguanani Nebukadnesa.

English: Then the princes, the governors, and captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together unto the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Masaai: Neiturrurro lelo kituaak, o laitasheikinok sunash ogelema, o lbalusuni, o lautarok o lashumak loo mpisai, o ilkituaak loo nkitanapat, o iladung'ok loo nkiguanat o lelo kituaak loo lkerenket, tenkaraki enkitisinyata e ina kitanyaanyukoto natesheta olaiguanani Nebukadnesa; neitashe ninche te dukuya ina kitanyaanyukoto natesheta Nebukadnesa.

English: Then an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages,
Masaai: Ore ilo kilikuai, neibalunye to ltoilo sapuk ajo, “Eitanapaki intae, loo rere, nakuapi, o lng'ejepa,

English: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
Masaai: nchere ore ti nining'ining'i oltoilo le mowuo, o endule, o lwulul loo usin, o enkinanta nanyaanyukie olwulul, o enkawuo oo sinkolioitin, o lbene olkuti te ndule, o pooki pukunoto o sinkolio, nirrugogo aabaiki enkop, aaserem ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu naitasheyie olaiguanani Nebukadnesa.

English: And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.
Masaai: Naa ore pooki ng'ae lemebatata aserem nepuoi nabo kata aanang'aki atua olkokuet le nkima oyupuyup.”

English: Therefore at that time, when all the people heard the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and all kinds of musick, all the people, the nations, and the languages, fell down and worshipped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
Masaai: Neaku ore ake pee ening iloreren ilo toilo le mowuo o lwulul loo usin, o enkinanta nanyaanyukie olwulul, o enkawuo oo sinkolioitin, o lbene okuti te ndule, o pooki pukunoto o sinkolio, ore iltung'ana pooki, o loreren o lng'ejepa nebatata pooki te dukuya ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu naitasheyie olaiguanani Nebukadnesa.

English: Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews.
Masaai: Neaku ore apa teina kata nepuonu kulikae Kaldayo dukuya neitang'or lelo Yahudi.

English: They spake and said to the king Nebuchadnezzar, O king, live for ever.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche olaiguanani Nebukadnesa, “Laaiguanani, tobiko ntarasi!

English: Thou, O king, hast made a decree, that every man that shall hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, shall fall down and worship the golden image:
Masaai: Ore iyie, laaiguanani, intobira enkitanapata, nchere ore pooki tung'ani oning oltoilo le mowuo, o endule, o lwulul loo usin, o enkinanta nanyaanyukie olwulul, o enkawuo oo sinkolioitin, o lbene okuti te ndule, o pooki pukunoto o sinkolio naa kebatata aserem ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu;

English: And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth, that he should be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.
Masaai: ore oloba anaa olemebatata aserem nenang'akini atua olkokuet le nkima oyupuyup.

English: There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
Masaai: Etii kulikae Yahudi litegelua iyie meitasheiki mbaa olkerenket le Babilon: Shadrak, o Meshek o Abednego. Eji ore kulo tung'ana, laaiguanani, mikishilaa ninche iyie; meisiaai ninche nkaitin inono aashu eserem ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu nintasheyie.”

English: Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. Then they brought these men before the king.
Masaai: Neitanapisho Nebukadnesa te ngoro napi meyauni Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego. Neyauni kulo tung'ana dukuya olaiguanani.

English: Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, do not ye serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up?
Masaai: Nejoki Nebukadnesa ninche, “Kesipa doi, Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego, nchere misiaayiayia intae nkaitin aainei aashu iserememe ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu naitasheyie nanu?

English: Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?
Masaai: Ore naa taata ti niterretenate, ti nining'ining'i oltoilo le mowuo o le ndule o lwulul loo usin o enkinanta nanyaanyukie olwulul, o enkawuo oo sinkolioitin o lbene okuti te ndule, o pooki pukunoto o sinkolio, naa nibatatata aaserem ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu naitobira nanu, naa aisidai ina. Kake tinimiserememe intae, nenang'akini intae nabo kata atua olkokuet oyupuyup; naa kaa ai ina naidim atokordu intae aitayu too nkaik aainei?”

English: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter.
Masaai: Newaliki Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego olaiguanani nejoki, “Oo Nebukadnesa, mikiaata iyiook tipat pee kiwaliki iyie tena bae.

English: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
Masaai: Naa tenaa neijia, ore Enkai ang naa ninye kisiaai naa keidim atokordu iyiook aitayu ti atua ilo kokuet oyupuyup; naa kekordu ninye iyiook aitung'uaa enkaina ino, laaiguanani.

English: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
Masaai: Kake te neitu, tayiolo iyie, laaiguanani nchere, mikisiaai iyiook nkaitin inono aashu kiserem ina kitanyaanyukoto e sahabu nintasheyie iyie.”

English: Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated.
Masaai: Neiput Nebukadnesa engoro napi, ore enkomom enye neibelekenya arruoyo ti alo Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego. Neitanapisho ninye meinoki ilo kokuet le nkima aaitulusoo katitin naapishana tena duoo kijukujuk e kiyupuyup.

English: And he commanded the most mighty men that were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Masaai: Neitanap kulikae tung'ana magil le njore enye meteena Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego, nenang'aki ninche atua ilo kokuet oyupuyup le nkima.

English: Then these men were bound in their coats, their hosen, and their hats, and their other garments, and were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Masaai: Neeni kulo tung'ana eishopito nkilani enye e atua o nioriong, o nkopiyiani enye o kulikae kilani lenye, nenang'akini ninche atua olkokuet le nkima oyupuyup.

English: Therefore because the king's commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding hot, the flame of the fire slew those men that took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki narrish apa ina kitanapata o laiguanani neirowua oleng ilo kokuet le nkima, etang'amayie olng'ejep le nkima anya lelo tung'ana ootudumutua Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego.

English: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Masaai: Ore kulo tung'ana okuni, Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego, nesulakini eena atua ilo kokuet le nkima oyupuyup.

English: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king.
Masaai: Neing'asia olaiguanani Nebukadnesa nedumunye nabo kata. Nejoki ninye ilarikok lenyena, “Keitu iyiook kinang'aki iltung'ana okuni eena atua enkima?” Newaliki ninche olaiguanani ejo, “Esipa, Laaiguanani.”

English: He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.
Masaai: Newaliki ninye ajo, “Kake adolita nanu iltung'ana oong'uan lemeena oopuoito te mpolos e nkima, neitu eiseyieki; ore eliooto e ilo li ong'uan nenyaanyukie enkerai oo nkaitin.”

English: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, came forth of the midst of the fire.
Masaai: Nelotu Nebukadnesa anyiku enkutuk e ilo kokuet le nkima nayupuyup nejo, “Shadrak o Meshak o Abednego, isinkan le Nkai natii shumata aisul, wootu elepu, naa wootu ene!” Neipang'u Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego ti atua enkima.

English: And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king's counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.
Masaai: Ore lelo kituaak, o laitasheikinok sunaishi oogelema o lbalusuni o laikook lo laiguanani neiturrurro te nebo nedol aajo eitu etum enkima ai golon too seseni le lelo tung'ana; ore ilpapit loo lukuny enye eitu ninye eisui, ore nkilani enye neitu eikoni ae, nemetii olng'usil le nkima ninche.

English: Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.
Masaai: Nejo Nebukadnesa, “Meisisi Enkai e Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego, nairriwua ninye olmalaika lenye netokordua isinkan lenyena, lelo ooisiliga ninye, neitu eitaa toki enkitanapata o laiguanani, neitayu iseseni lenye alang te neisiaai neserem ae neme ina Ai enye maate.

English: Therefore I make a decree, That every people, nation, and language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill: because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.
Masaai: Ore naa kaitayu enkitanapata: Ore pooki orere, o pooki kop, o pooki ng'ejep oiro inaapaashare Enkai e Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego nedung'i aaitaa ndung'udung'ot, ore nkajijik enye neidaikieki; amu meetae ae Ai naidim atokordu tena pukunoto.”

English: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, in the province of Babylon.
Masaai: Neilepie olaiguanani aisho enkitoo Shadrak o Meshek o Abednego to lkerenket le Babilon.

English: Nebuchadnezzar the king, unto all people, nations, and languages, that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.
Masaai: Olaiguanani Nebukadnesa oigeroki iltung'ana pooki, o loreren, o lng'ejepa oomanya enkop pooki: Metoponikini intae eseriani!

English: I thought it good to shew the signs and wonders that the high God hath wrought toward me.
Masaai: Atoduaa nanu ajo eisidai te naitodolu ilmonek o nenking'asia naataasaka Enkai natii shumata aisul tialo nanu.

English: How great are his signs! and how mighty are his wonders! his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
Masaai: Kebaa esapuko oo lmonek lenyena le nking'asia, kebaa enkidimata oo mbaa enyena e nking'asia! Ore enkitoria enye naa enkitoria oo ntarasi, ore enkitoo enye nebaiki iishoritin o ishoritin.

English: I Nebuchadnezzar was at rest in mine house, and flourishing in my palace:
Masaai: Ore nanu Nebukadnesa kaisikarra apa ti atua enkaji ai natudupe ti atua enkaji ai natudupe ti atua enkaji ai e nkitoo.

English: I saw a dream which made me afraid, and the thoughts upon my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
Masaai: Anoto apa nanu enkidetidet naaituria; ore airragita te ndapash naaitanyamal ndamunot o nduaat e ndukuya ai.

English: Therefore made I a decree to bring in all the wise men of Babylon before me, that they might make known unto me the interpretation of the dream.
Masaai: Neaku aitanapishe nanu meyauni lelo tung'ana pooki ang'eni le Babilon meyauni dukuya nanu, pee aatum ninche aaitayiolo nanu enkibalakinoto eina kidetidet.

English: Then came in the magicians, the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers: and I told the dream before them; but they did not make known unto me the interpretation thereof.
Masaai: Nepuonu ilkuyantik o loo ntaleng'o o Lkaldayo, o laing'urak loo lakir atua ine natii; naliki nanu ninche ina kidetidet, kake maaidim ninche aatoliki nanu enkibalakinoto enye.

English: But at the last Daniel came in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods: and before him I told the dream, saying,
Masaai: Ore te siadi nelotu Daniel dukuya nanu - ilo apa oji enkarna Belteshasa aaipotie enkai ai, naa atua ninye etii enkiyang'et oo nkaitin sinyat naliki nanu ninye ina kidetidet, ajoki,

English: O Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in thee, and no secret troubleth thee, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and the interpretation thereof.
Masaai: “Iyie Belteshasa, olkitok loo lkuyantik, ore enkaraki nayiolo nanu ajo etii enkiyang'et oo nkaitin sinyat atua iyie nemeetae enkisudoroto nagol te iyie, ena kidetidet nanu atoduaa; tolikioki nanu enkibalakinoto enye.

English: Thus were the visions of mine head in my bed; I saw, and behold a tree in the midst of the earth, and the height thereof was great.
Masaai: Ore nena duaat e ndukuya ai ina kata airragita te ndapash naa kuna: Atoduaa nanu, naa ng'ura, olchani te mpolos e nkop; ore enkadoro enye naa eikitok.

English: The tree grew, and was strong, and the height thereof reached unto heaven, and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth:
Masaai: Nebulu ilo shani negolu ore enchumata enye nebaiki keper, naa kelioo te neiting'ie enkop pooki.

English: The leaves thereof were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it.
Masaai: Ore mbenek enyena naa eisidain naa kumok ilng'anayio lenyena, ore ilo shani netii endaa e pooki toki. Netum ing'uesi e ong'ata oloip ti abori ninye ore ntaritik o loing'ang'e nemany ilng'osil lenyena, ore pooki toki naishu neitoti te ilo shani.

English: I saw in the visions of my head upon my bed, and, behold, a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven;
Masaai: “Atoduaa nanu te nena duaat e ndukuya ai ina kata airragita te ndapash, naa ng'ura, olarriponi, ilo osinya, nelotu adou eing'uaa shumata.

English: He cried aloud, and said thus, Hew down the tree, and cut off his branches, shake off his leaves, and scatter his fruit: let the beasts get away from under it, and the fowls from his branches:
Masaai: Neyietu aishir nejo nji, ‘Entudung ilo shani meturori, nisulaa ilng'osil lenyena, nidung'oo mbenek enyena nisardakiekie ilng'anayio lenyena; nchoo ng'uesi eisik aapuo te ntonata enye neisik ntaritik too lng'osil lenyena.

English: Nevertheless leave the stump of his roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts in the grass of the earth:
Masaai: Kake entung'uai enkobei o ntona enyena te nkop, eena te sekenkei o to suyai te mpolos oo nkujit naanana e ong'ata. Nchoo ninye eshalu te nkoliolio e shumata; nchoo erishata enye eaku te nebong'uesi ti atua nkujit e nkop;

English: Let his heart be changed from man's, and let a beast's heart be given unto him; and let seven times pass over him.
Masaai: nchoo eibelekenya endamunoto enye e tung'ani naa nchoo eishori ninye endamunoto e ng'ues naa nchoo nkatitin naapishana egiroo ninye.

English: This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.
Masaai: Ore ina dung'okinoto e nkiguana ene lelo arripok, embae natudung'oki to rorei le lelo sinyat, pee eyiolou ilooishu pooki nchere ore ilo otii shumata aisul ninye oitore enkitoria oo ltung'ana, neisho ninye ilo oyieu, nepik shumata ninye ilo oshal.’

English: This dream I king Nebuchadnezzar have seen. Now thou, O Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation thereof, forasmuch as all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known unto me the interpretation: but thou art able; for the spirit of the holy gods is in thee.
Masaai: Ore ena kidetidet, nanu olaiguanani Nebukadnesa, otadua. Naa ore iyie Belteshasa, mbalunye enkibalakinoto, enkaraki ore lelo tung'ana pooki ang'eni le nkitoria ai maaidim aaitayiolo nanu enkibalakinoto, kake indim iyie, amu etii enkiyang'et oo nkaitin sinyat atua iyie.”

English: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was astonied for one hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king spake, and said, Belteshazzar, let not the dream, or the interpretation thereof, trouble thee. Belteshazzar answered and said, My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies.
Masaai: Neitoki Daniel, apa oji enkarna enye Belteshesa, aing'asia te nkiti rishata neitanyamal ndamunot enyena ninye. Nejo olaiguanani, “Belteshesa, mincho kintanyamal ina kidetidet aashu enkibalakinoto.” Newalu Belteshasa ajo, “Olkitok lai, metaa ina kidetidet ene lelo likimba iyie ore enkibalakinoto enye neaku enoo lmang'ati linono!

English: The tree that thou sawest, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached unto the heaven, and the sight thereof to all the earth;
Masaai: Ore ilo shani litodua iyie, otubulua negolu, o metabaiki enchumata enye keper, naa dapash ninye abaiki enkop pooki;

English: Whose leaves were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all; under which the beasts of the field dwelt, and upon whose branches the fowls of the heaven had their habitation:
Masaai: laa eisidan mbenek enyena naa kumok ilng'anayio lenyena, naa ninye etii endaa e pooki toki; naa abori ninye etumie ng'uesi e ong'ata oloip, naa ilng'osil lenyena emanya ntaritik o loing'ang'e

English: It is thou, O king, that art grown and become strong: for thy greatness is grown, and reacheth unto heaven, and thy dominion to the end of the earth.
Masaai: iyie, ilo laaiguanani, itubula nigolu. Etubulua enkitoo ino o metabaiki shumata ore enkitoria ino netabaikia lubot e nkop.

English: And whereas the king saw a watcher and an holy one coming down from heaven, and saying, Hew the tree down, and destroy it; yet leave the stump of the roots thereof in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts of the field, till seven times pass over him;
Masaai: Ore ina natoduaa olaiguanani olarriponi, ilo sinyati, edou eing'uaa shumata ejo, ‘Entudung entuuroi olchani ninyalinyala ninye, kake entung'uai enkobei o ntona enyena te nkop, eena te sekenkei o to suyai, too nkujit naanana e ong'ata; naa nchoo erubata enye eaku te nebo ng'uesi e ong'ata, o metaba anaa negiroo ninye nkatitin naapishana;’

English: This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree of the most High, which is come upon my lord the king:
Masaai: ena ninye enkibalakinoto enye, laaiguanani: Enkitanapata e ilo otii shumata aisul, ninye shumata olkitok lai olaiguanani,

English: That they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field, and they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and they shall wet thee with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass over thee, till thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.
Masaai: nchere eikipuoi aaraa iyie aaitung'uaa iltung'ana, ore emanyisho ino naa keaku te nebo ing'uesi e ong'ata; eikinchori iyie inosa nkujit anaa olkiteng, naa eishalu iyie te nkoileelio e shumata, naa eikigiroo iyie nkatitin naapishana o metaba anaa niyiolounchere ilo otii shumata aisul oitore enkitoo e tung'ana, neisho ninye ilo oyieu.

English: And whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the tree roots; thy kingdom shall be sure unto thee, after that thou shalt have known that the heavens do rule.
Masaai: Naa ore anaa enaitanapishoteki pee eing'uari enkobei o ntona e ilo shani, naa kelo enkitoria ino adedeyu obaiki ina kata niyiolounye nchere keper naitoreisho.

English: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquility.
Masaai: “Metaa naa laaiguanani nchoo enkikoo ai eng'amaroyu te iyie; nturrai ing'ok inono te asata e sipata, o ntorrok inono te nkitodolunoto o lng'ur too looitorogonyaki, pee ebaiki neponari nkolong'iinono e seriani.”

English: All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar.
Masaai: Eeuo ena pooki shumata olaiguanani Nebukadnesa.

English: At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ilapaitin tomon o are neloito ninye te nchumata e nkaji e nkitoo e Babilon,

English: The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?
Masaai: nejo olaiguanani, “Aimekitok ena Babilon natesheta nanu te ngolon ai kitok metaa enkaji e nkitoo nairragie o te nkitoo e nkitoria ai.”

English: While the word was in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee.
Masaai: Ore eton epuku kulo rorei te nkutuk o laiguanani, nedou oltoilo oing'uaa shumata, “Olaiguanani Nebukadnesa, kirorieki iyie: Kishomo enkitoria aing'uaa iyie,

English: And they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field: they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and seven times shall pass over thee, until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.
Masaai: naa aikiarari iyie aaitung'uaa iltung'ana, ore emanyisho ino naa keaku te nebo ing'uesi e ntim; naa keaku inos iyie nkujit anaa olkiteng; naa eikigiroo iyie ilarin naapishana, o metaba anaa niyiolou nchere ilo otii shumata aisul oitore enkitoo etung'ana, neisho ninye ilo oyieu.”

English: The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.
Masaai: Ore ina kata ake neitabari ilo rorei to laiguanani Nebukadnesa. Nearari ninye aaitung'uaa iltung'ana, neinos nkujit anaa olkiteng, neshalu osesen lenye, te nkoileelio e shumata o metubulu ilpapit lenyena te nkadoro anaa nkopir o lkurragos, netiu iloisotok lenyena anaa loo lmotonyi.

English: And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:
Masaai: Ore te siadi nena olong'i, nashumu nanu Nebukadnesa nkonyek aainei aing'or shumata, naarrinyokino nanu ndamunot aainei, naisis nanu ilo otii shumata aisul, naisis nayanyitu ilo oishu ntarasi; amu ore enkitoria enye naa enkitoria oo ntarasi, ore enkitoo enye nebikoo too ishoritin o ishoritin

English: And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing: and he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?
Masaai: ore lelo pooki oomanya enkop neikenaki aajo pesho; neas ninye te risioroto e yieunoto enye to lorora le shumata o ti atua lelo oomanya enkop; nemeetae oloidimaa enkaina enye, aashu ejoki ninye, “Kaa iasita iyie?”

English: At the same time my reason returned unto me; and for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me; and my counsellors and my lords sought unto me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent majesty was added unto me.
Masaai: Ore te ina kata ake naarrinyokino nanu endamunoto ai; ore te nkaraki enkitoo e nkitoria ai naarrinyokini enkisisa o enkishiaa. Naaing'oru ilaikook o lkituaak laainei, naapiki nanu atua enkitoria ai, naaponikini nanu enkitoo sapuk.

English: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.
Masaai: Ore nanu Nebukadnesa naisis naserem nayanyitu ilo Aiguanani le shumata; amu ore isiaaitin enyena pooki naa neitoriori. Ore nkoitoi enyena nesipa. Naa ore lelo oopuo to lwuasa eidim ninye aitadou.

English: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.
Masaai: Neitobir apa olaiguanani Belshasa osirua kitok te nkaraki ilkituaak lenyena enkalifu nabo, neok ninye enaisho oo sabibu te dukuya lelo enkalifu nabo.

English: Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eishamisham Belshasa enaisho, neitanapisho nchere ore nena masaa e sahabu o nenkosholai apa naaitayio Nebukadnesa papaai lenye ti atua enkaji e Nkai te Yerusalem meyauni, pee etum olaiguanani o lkituaak lenyena o nkituaak enyena o nkapiak enyena aatookishore ninche.

English: Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of the house of God which was at Jerusalem; and the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, drank in them.
Masaai: Neyau ninche nena masaa e sahabu o nenkosholai apa naaitayioki ti atua enkaji e Nkai, te ina aji e Nkai te Yerusalem. Neokishore olaiguanani ninche, o lkituaak lenyena, o nkituaak enyena o nkapiak enyena.

English: They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
Masaai: Neok ninche enaisho oo sabibu, nerrep nkaitin nena aitin e sahabu, o nenkosholai, o nosuyai, o nesekenkei, o enosoit.

English: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
Masaai: Ore nabo kata neliooyu ilkimojik le nkaina e tung'ani neiger enturoto naelare esuntai e nkaji o laiguanani enkipirakinoto oiket lo ltaa; nedol olaiguanani ina aina eigerisho.

English: Then the king's countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another.
Masaai: Neibelekenya emua o laiguanani, neitanyamal ninye ndamunot enyena, nelepori irubat osesen lenye neikirikira nkung aaosho.

English: The king cried aloud to bring in the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. And the king spake, and said to the wise men of Babylon, Whosoever shall read this writing, and shew me the interpretation thereof, shall be clothed with scarlet, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Masaai: Neyietu olaiguanani abuaku pee eyakini iloibonok, o Lkaldayo o laduaak. Nejoki olaiguanani lelo tung'ana ang'eni le Babilon, “Ore oloba anaa oloisoma ele sirata nelimu enajo ninye, naaitodol nanu enkibalakinoto enye neishopokini olkila sintet nepiki olpisiai le sahabu aaitaman emurt enye, nelo ninye aaku oloitoreisho liokuni te nkitoria.”

English: Then came in all the king's wise men: but they could not read the writing, nor make known to the king the interpretation thereof.
Masaai: Nejing'u lelo ang'eni pooki lo laiguanani, kake meidim ninche aaisoma ilo sirata aashu eitayiolo olaiguanani enkibalakinoto.

English: Then was king Belshazzar greatly troubled, and his countenance was changed in him, and his lords were astonied.
Masaai: Nenyamalu oleng ilo aiguanani Belshasa neibelekenya emua enye, neiputukuny lelo kituaak lenyena.

English: Now the queen, by reason of the words of the king and his lords, came into the banquet house: and the queen spake and said, O king, live for ever: let not thy thoughts trouble thee, nor let thy countenance be changed:
Masaai: Ore enkitok o laiguanani, te nkaraki irorei lo laiguanani o lelo kituaak lenyena, nelotu olgilata oitoomonishoreki, nejo ina kitok olaiguanani, “La aiguanani, tobiko ntarasi! Mincho ndamunotinono kintanyamal aashu emua ino eibelekenya.

English: There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of thy father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him; whom the king Nebuchadnezzar thy father, the king, I say, thy father, made master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;
Masaai: Etii atua enkitoria ino oltung'ani otii atua ninye enkiyang'et oo nkaitin sinyat. Ore apa too nkolong'i e papaai lino, nenotoki ti atua ninye ewang'an, o eyiolounoto o eng'eno natiu anaa eng'eno oo nkaitin, ore apa olaiguanani Nebukadnesa, papaai lino, neitaa ninye olkitok loo lkuyantik, oloo ntalengo, Ilkaldayo o laing'urak loo lakir,

English: Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar: now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.
Masaai: enkaraki naa ore oltau sidai, o eng'eno, o ening'unoto nalimunye enkibalakinoto oo nkidetidetat oo iloyiotiaa neiwuang'ie inyamalitin nenotoki tele tung'ani oji Daniel, apa oishoo olaiguanani enkarna ajo Belteshasa. Nchoo naa Daniel eipotuni pee eitodolu ninye enkibalakinoto ele sirata.”

English: Then was Daniel brought in before the king. And the king spake and said unto Daniel, Art thou that Daniel, which art of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Jewry?
Masaai: Neitijing'uni Daniel meeu dukuya olaiguanani. Nejoki olaiguanani Daniel, “Ira iyie lido Daniel, apa ora obo loo yarunot le Yuda, apa oyaua olaiguanani papa lai te Yuda.

English: I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.
Masaai: Atoning'o ilomon linono nchere etii enkiyang'et oo nkaitin sinyat atua iyie nenotoki sii ewang'an, o eyiolounoto o eng'eno nagut ti atua iyie.

English: And now the wise men, the astrologers, have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing, and make known unto me the interpretation thereof: but they could not shew the interpretation of the thing:
Masaai: Etorikuoki taata ilang'eni o loo ntalengo meetu dukuya nanu pee eisom ele kigeroto naaitayiolo nanu enkibalakinoto enye; kake meidim ninche aaitodolu enkibalakinoto ena bae.

English: And I have heard of thee, that thou canst make interpretations, and dissolve doubts: now if thou canst read the writing, and make known to me the interpretation thereof, thou shalt be clothed with scarlet, and have a chain of gold about thy neck, and shalt be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Masaai: Kake atoning'o nanu nchere indim iyie atolimu nkibalakinot niwuang'ie enyamali. Ore naa taata ti nindim iyie aisoma ele kigeroto nikintayiolo nanu enkibalakinoto, nikinchopokini olkila sintet, nikipiki olpisiai le sahabu aaitaman emurt ino, niaaku oliokuni oitoreisho te nkitoria.”

English: Then Daniel answered and said before the king, Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
Masaai: Newal Daniel te dukuya olaiguanani ajo, “Nchoo nkishorot inono eaku nkuninono, naa nchoo nena kishorot inono likae; ore ake eyia kaisomaki nanu olaiguanani ilo kigeroto naitayiolo ninye enkibalakinoto e ilo kigeroto.

English: O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour:
Masaai: la aiguanani, eishoo Enkai kitok oleng Nebukadnesa, papaai lino enkitoria o enkisisa o esikar;

English: And for the majesty that he gave him, all people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him: whom he would he slew; and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he set up; and whom he would he put down.
Masaai: naa ore enkaraki ina kitoo naishoo Enkai ninye eikirikirate iltung'ana pooki, o loreren, o lng'ejepa neureishoyu te dukuya ninye; ore oloyieu near metua near metua; ore oloyieu neitopok neitopok; ore ilo oyieu neilepie, neilepie, ore oloyieu neitadou neitadou.

English: But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him:
Masaai: Kake ore ake pee eilepunye oltau lenye neitagol oltau metaa keasisho to lwuasa neiwuang'ieki ninye te ilo orika lenye le nkitoo, neyae enkitoo enye aaitung'uaa ninye;

English: And he was driven from the sons of men; and his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: they fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven; till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men, and that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.
Masaai: nerei ninye aitung'uaa iltung'ana, neitotiuni ndamunot enyena anaa ineng'ues, ore emanyisho enye neaku te nebo isirkon le ntim; neitoti ninye too nkujit anaa olkiteng, neshalu osesen lenye te nkoliolio e shumata, o metaba anaa neyiolou ninye nchere Ina Ai natii shumata aisul naitore enkitoria e tung'ana, nepik shumata ninye ilo oyieu ninye.

English: And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this;
Masaai: Naa ore iyie, olayioni lenye, Belshasa, eitu intobor oltau lino hoo niyiolo kuna pooki,

English: But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified:
Masaai: kake ilepunye kewan nigilunore Olaitoriani le shumata; ore nena masaa e nkaji enye neitijing'uaki aayau dukuya iyie, ore iyie o lkituaak linono, o nkituaak inono o nkapiak inono nitookie ninche enaisho oo sabibu, nirrepirrepe intae nena aitin e nkosholai o nesahabu o nosuyai, o nesekenkei, o nenchata, o nosoit, nena nemedolisho aashu ening'isho aashu eyiolo, kake ore ina Ai naa enkaina enye etii enkiyang'et ino netii inkoitoi inono pooki neitu iyie iyanyit.

English: Then was the part of the hand sent from him; and this writing was written.
Masaai: “Neaku te ine netii ninye eirriwuaki ina aina, nesiri ele kigeroto.

English: And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
Masaai: Naa ele kigeroto otisiraki: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, o PARSIN.

English: This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.
Masaai: Ena enkibalakinoto ena bae: MENE, eikena Enkai nkolong'i e nkitoria ino neyau ninye enkiting'oto;

English: TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
Masaai: TEKEL, kineneng'aki iyie te ntemet naineneng'ishoreki nedoli aajo ing'or.

English: PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.
Masaai: PERES, etooroki enkitoria ino neishori ile Mede o le Parsia.”

English: Then commanded Belshazzar, and they clothed Daniel with scarlet, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made a proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Masaai: Neitoki Belshasa aitanapisho neishopokini Daniel olkila sintet o lpisiai le sahabu oitamanaki emurt enye, nelimuni aaibalunye naaipirta ninye, nchere keaku ninye o liokuni oitoreisho te nkitoria.

English: In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain.
Masaai: Ore ina kewarie ake neari Belshasa ilo aiguanani loo Lkaldayo metua.

English: And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.
Masaai: Neng'amu Darius le Mede enkitoria, aa oloo larin oobaya ntomoni ile oare.

English: It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes, which should be over the whole kingdom;
Masaai: Eitishipa apa Darias pee epik ilbalusuni iip o tikitam meitoreisho ti atua enkitoria enye pooki;

English: And over these three presidents; of whom Daniel was first: that the princes might give accounts unto them, and the king should have no damage.
Masaai: ore shumata ninche naa ilkituaak okuni, laa Daniel apa obo, aa ninye eyaki kulo balusuni ilomon, pee metum ake olaiguanani eng'orikinoto.

English: Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
Masaai: Ore apa ilo Daniel nening'oyu oleng alang lelo kituaak pooki o lbalusuni, amu etii apa enkiyang'et sidai atua ninye. Neitobir olaiguanani pee epik ninye shumata enkitoria pooki.

English: Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Masaai: Ore lelo kituaak o lbalusuni neing'oru enaitang'orie Daniel ti alo enkitoria; kake eitu ninche etum enaitang'orie aashu eleyiata, amu keisiligayu apa ninye, nemeetae enkitadiaata aashu eleyiata nanotoki te ninye.

English: Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Masaai: Neitoki kulo tung'ana aajo, “Mikitum ae kitang'oroto aashu eniking'unyung'unyakinye ele Daniel meteleku ake ti niking'oru ti alo nkitanapat e Nkai enye.”

English: Then these presidents and princes assembled together to the king, and said thus unto him, King Darius, live for ever.
Masaai: Nening'okino kulo kituaak o lbalusuni embae nayaki olaiguanani, nepuonu aajoki ninye, “Olaiguanani Darias, tobikoi ntarasi.

English: All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Masaai: Ore iyiook pooki oosiaisho te nkitoria ino - ilaitasheikinok, o lbalusuni, o laitasheikinok loo lkerenketi, o lkulikae arikok, nikitoning'okinote nchere pee eitobir olaiguanani enkitanapata, neitirrishi oleng, nchere ore pooki ng'ae oserem ae ai aashu tung'ani too nkolong'i tomon uni, metelekuake iyie lo aiguanani nenang'akini ninye eululu oo lng'atunyo.

English: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Masaai: Ore naa taata, la aiguanani, intobira ina kitanapata nipik olmishire ina natoning'okinoteki pee meidimi aaibelekenya, anaa enatiu nkitanapat oo Lmedi o Lparsian, nena nemeidimi aaibelekenya.”

English: Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.
Masaai: Neaku etipika apa olaiguanani Darias olmishire ina palai neimie.

English: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Masaai: Ore ake pee eyiolou Daniel nchere etipikaki olmishire ina naimieki nelo ninye enkaji enye ebolo ildirishani le nkaji e shumata eing'orita Yerusalem; negil ninye kung katitin uni te nkolong neomon neishooyo enashe te dukuya Enkai enye, anaa apake enataasa.

English: Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.
Masaai: Neitoki kulo tung'ana aapuonu te ning'okinoto neinepu Daniel esaisho neomon te dukuya Enkai enye.

English: Then they came near, and spake before the king concerning the king's decree; Hast thou not signed a decree, that every man that shall ask a petition of any God or man within thirty days, save of thee, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered and said, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Masaai: Neitoki ninche aapuonu aanyiku nejo te dukuya olaiguanani, “Amaa, ti alo enkitanapata, la aiguanani! Keitu iyie ipik olmishire ina natoning'okinoteki; nchere ore pooki tung'ani osaisho tiae ai aashu te tung'ani ti atua nkolong'i tomoni uni meteleku ake te iyie, la aiguanani, nenang'akini atua eululu oo lng'atunyo?” Newal olaiguanani ajo, “Keuno ina bae, anaa enatiu enkitanapata oo Lmedi o enoo Lpasi, nena nemeidimi aaibelekenya.”

English: Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
Masaai: Neitoki ninche aawal te dukuya olaiguanani ejo, “Ore lido Daniel ora obo loo yarunot ooitung'uari Yuda, mikishilaa ninye iyie, laaiguanani, aashu ina naimieki nitipika olmishire, kake keomon ninye asaisho katitin uni te nkolong.”

English: Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening olaiguanani kulo rorei, neing'oru eneiko pee ekordu Daniel; nenyamalu o metadoi enkolong pee ekordu ninye.

English: Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed.
Masaai: Neitoki kulo tung'ana aapuonu te nkiguanakinoto enetii olaiguanani, nejoki olaiguanani, “Tayiolo, laaiguanani, nchere enkitanapata ena oo Lmede o Lpasi naa nchere meetae enatudung'o olaiguanani aashu enkitanapata naidimi aaibelekenya.”

English: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani aitanapisho, neyauni Daniel nenang'akini atua eululu oo lng'atunyo. Nejoki olaiguanani Daniel, “Inchoo Enkai ino, ina nisiaaita anaake kikordu iyie!”

English: And a stone was brought and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Masaai: Neyauni osoit aairragie te nkutuk e ina ululu nemishir olaiguanani to lmishire lenye o to lmishire loo lkituaak lenyena, nchere meetae embae naidimi aaibelekenya ti alo Daniel.

English: Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting: neither were instruments of musick brought before him: and his sleep went from him.
Masaai: Nelo olaiguanani enkaji enye e nkitoo, neen kewan ina kewarie pee menya endaa, nemeetae nkinantani naayakaki ninye, nelau ninye njo.

English: Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions.
Masaai: Ore enamanarie enkakenya nedumunye olaiguanani neisarrisar alo eululu oo lng'atunyo.

English: And when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?
Masaai: Ore pee elotu ninye ataaniki ina ululu natii Daniel neyietu aishir to ltoilo lo sina nejoki Daniel, “Oo Daniel, osinka le Nkai naishu, eikindima duoo Enkai ino ina nisiaai anaake atokordu too lng'atunyo?”

English: Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
Masaai: Nejoki Daniel olaiguanani, “La aiguanani, tobiko ntarasi!

English: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
Masaai: Eirriwua Enkai ai olmalaika neiken nkutukie oo lng'atunyo, neitu ninche aainyal, amu aatoduaki aajo maata entioto te dukuya ninye, o te dukuya iyie sii, laaiguanani, eitu aas entorrono.”

English: Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
Masaai: Neng'idayu ilo aiguanani oleng, neitanapisho meitayuni Daniel ti atua eululu. Neaku eitayioki apa Daniel ti atua eululu nemetii hoo olkordata le nkinyalata onotoki te ninye, enkaraki apa naisiliga ninye Enkai enye.

English: And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
Masaai: Neitanapisho olaiguanani, ore lelo tung'ana apa ooitang'oro Daniel neyauni, nenang'akini atua eululu oo lng'atunyo, ninche, o nkera enye o nkituaak enye; naa ore eitu ninche ebaiki abori ina ululu neng'amaa ilng'atunyo ninche negiligil iloik lenye.

English: Then king Darius wrote unto all people, nations, and languages, that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.
Masaai: Neitoki olaiguanani Darias aigeroki iloreren pooki, o nkuapi pooki o nkutukie pooki naatii enkop pooki ajo: “Metoponikini intae eseriani.

English: I make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
Masaai: Aitobira nanu enkitanapata nchere ore ti atua enkitoria ai pooki neikirikira iltung'ana te nkuretisho te dukuya Enkai e Daniel, Amu Enkai naishu ninye, nebik ntarasi; meidak ae kata enkitoria enye, naa enoontarasi enkitoo enye.

English: He delivereth and rescueth, and he worketh signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who hath delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
Masaai: Kekordu ninye nesaru, neas ninye nkitoduaat e nking'asia te shumata o te nkop, ilo laa ninye oitajeuo Daniel aitung'uaa engolon oo lng'atunyo.”

English: So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
Masaai: Neaku etubula apa ele Daniel te nkata e nkitoria e Darias o enkitoria e Sairos ilo le Parsian.

English: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed: then he wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters.
Masaai: Ore to lari le dukuya le Belshasa, olaiguanani le Babilon, netum Daniel enkidetidet o nduaat e ndukuya enye ina kata apa eirragita te ndapash enye. Neiger ninye ina kidetidet, nelimu esiana e ina bae.

English: Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.
Masaai: Nejo Daniel, “Atoduaa nanu te nduaata ai kewarie, naa ng'ura, ore lelo kutat oong'uan le shumata nekut te ngolon enaiposha kitok.

English: And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
Masaai: Neipang'u ing'uesi ong'uan aapuku ti atua enaiposha, nemeetae ake enemepaashare enkae.

English: The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings: I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man's heart was given to it.
Masaai: Ore ene dukuya nenyaanyukie olng'atuny neeta inaipuko o lkurragos. Ore aing'orita nanu nedotuni inaipuko enyena, neilepieki ninye te nkop neishori ninye meitasho too nkejek are anaa oltung'ani, neishori ninye endamunoto e tung'ani.

English: And behold another beast, a second, like to a bear, and it raised up itself on one side, and it had three ribs in the mouth of it between the teeth of it: and they said thus unto it, Arise, devour much flesh.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, enkae ng'ues e are, naikununo anaa olng'arurumi. Neilepieki ninye te nkalo nabo; neeta ninye ilaras okuni te nkutuk enye, too rishat oo lala lenyena; netiaakaki apa ninye, ‘Tudumunye inosa nkiri oleng.’

English: After this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena naing'orisho nanu, naa ng'ura, enkae, nanyaanyukie olowuaru keri, neeta inaipuko ong'uan e motonyi te nkoriong enye; neeta ina ng'ues ilukuny ong'uan neishori ninye enkitoria.

English: After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ena nadol nanu too nduaat e nkewarie, naa ng'ura eng'ues e ong'uan, torrono neitureisho negol oleng; neeta ilala sapuki le sekenkei; kenyaisho ninye negiligilisho, neituny ilekunottoo nkejek enyena. Nepaashare ninye nena ng'uesi pooki apa naatii dukuya ninye, neeta mowuarak tomon.

English: I considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another little horn, before whom there were three of the first horns plucked up by the roots: and, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of man, and a mouth speaking great things.
Masaai: Atisipua nanu nena mowuarak, naa ng'ura etupukuo ti atua ninche enkae mouo, enkiti, naa te dukuya ninye etadotuoki imowuarak uni oo naduoo e dukuya, naa ng'ura ena mouo netii nkonyek naanyaanyukie nkonyek o ltung'ani o enkutuk nairo mbaa sapuki.

English: I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.
Masaai: “Ore aing'orisho nanu, neirragieki ilorikan le nkitoo ore obo otobikoyie ilarin kumok netonie olorika lenye; ore ikilani lenyena neibor anaa soito le nchan, ore ilpapit le ndukuya enye neikununoanaa ilpapit loo nkerra; ore ilo orika lenye le nkitoo naailng'ejepa le nkima ooyupuyup, ore nkejek oo ngarrin enyenanaa enkima nayupuyup.

English: A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
Masaai: Nepuku olkeju le nkima nelo aim dukuya ninye; neisiai ninye nkalifuni o nkalifuni, ore te dukuya ninye neitashe nkalifuni tomon katitin nkalifuni tomon; neton enkiguana eiguanare, neboli mbukui.

English: I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.
Masaai: “Naing'orisho taa nanu te nkaraki ilo toilo le lelo rorei sapuki ooiroro ina mouo. Naa ore aing'orita, neyieng'i ina ng'ues, neinyali osesen lenye neishoori metapeji te nkima.

English: As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time.
Masaai: Ore nena kulie ng'uesi neoruni enkitoria enye, kake ore enkishui enye neitoodoroki te rishata o te nkata.

English: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
Masaai: Atoduaa to nduaata e kewarie, naa ng'ura, ore too nkatampo e shumata nelotu obo onyaanyukie enkerai e tung'ani, nelotu enetii Ilo otobikoyie ilarin kumok neitarasari te dukuya ninye.

English: And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
Masaai: Neishori ninye enkitoria o enkitoo o enkitoria, pee etum iltung'ana pooki, o nkuapi, o lng'ejepa aaisiaayia ninye. Ore enkitoria enye naa enkitoria oo ntarasi nemeish aekata, Ore enkitoo enye naa enkitoo oo ntarasi, nemeish aekata, naa nabo enkitoria enye nemeidimi aaidaikie.

English: I Daniel was grieved in my spirit in the midst of my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.
Masaai: “Ore ti alo nanu, Daniel, nelimana oltau lai ti atua nanu ore nena duaat e ndukuya ai naaitanyamal.

English: I came near unto one of them that stood by, and asked him the truth of all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
Masaai: Atataanikia nanu obo le lelo ooitashe te ine naikilikuan esipata naipirta kuna pooki, neaku aatolikio ninye, naaibalakinye nanu enkibalakinoto e kuna tokitin.

English: These great beasts, which are four, are four kings, which shall arise out of the earth.
Masaai: ‘Ore kuna ng'uesi pokira ong'uan kituaak naa ilaiguanak oong'uan ooyooki aaipang'u te nkop.

English: But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.
Masaai: Kake ore lelo sinyat le ilo Otii Shumata Aisul naa keng'amu enkitoria, neaku enkitoria enenye ntarasi, o ntarasi o ntarasi.’

English: Then I would know the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass; which devoured, brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with his feet;
Masaai: “Naitoki ayieu nayiolou esipata naipirta ina ng'ues e ong'uan napaashari ninye too nkulie, naitureisho oleng, neeta ilala lenyena le sekenkei o loisotok lo suyai; nenyaisho negiligilisho neituny ilekunot too nkejek enyena;

English: And of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell; even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things, whose look was more stout than his fellows.
Masaai: o naaipirta nena mourak tomon naatii endukuya enye, o ina ae mouo naa te dukuya ninye etigilari uni enye, ina mouo naata nkonyek o enkutuk nairo mbaa sapuki neeijo ninye kitok te nena naaboitare.

English: I beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;
Masaai: Ore aing'orisho nanu neitayunye ena mouo olarrabal lelo sinyat, nemir ninche,

English: Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.
Masaai: o metaba anaa nelotu Ilo Otobikoyie, neiguanareki lelo sinyat le Ilo Otii Shumata aisul, nebau ina kata pee eishori lelo sinyat enkitoria.

English: Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.
Masaai: “Nji etejo ninye, ‘Ore ti alo ina ng'ues e ong'uan, kelotu enkitoria e ong'uan enkop, naa kepaashari ninye too nkitoriat pooki, naa kemut ninye enkop, pooki, neituny, negiligil.

English: And the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise: and another shall rise after them; and he shall be diverse from the first, and he shall subdue three kings.
Masaai: Ore nena mowuarak tomon, ore ti atua ena kitoria neipang'u ilaiguanak tomon, naa kedumunye likae te siadi ninche; naa kepaashari ninye te kuldo le ndukuya, naa keiwuang'ie ninye ilaiguanak okuni.
