Masaai: Neiteleikiaki taata entolu intana oo lkeek naa ore pooki shani lemeiu lng'anayio sidain, nedung'i aanang'aki enkima.

English: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:
Masaai: “Aibatisa nanu intae te nkare pee eitodolu nchere irridutua ng'ok; kake ore olaasujita, naa kegol ninye, aalang nanu, maaishiaakino hoo nanu te nanapaki inamuka enyena, naa ninye oibatisa intae te Nkiyang'et Sinyati o te nkima.

English: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
Masaai: Neeta esilet enye te nkaina enye, naa keor asip olkurroto lenye oidong'ishoreki, nesotoki enkano enye empeche ore isuut nepej te nkima nemearayu.”

English: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
Masaai: Ore te siadi ina nelotu Yesu eing'uaa Galilaya enetii Yohana te Yordan meibatisae ninye.

English: But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?
Masaai: Neyieu Yohana neany eibatisa, nejoki, “Keishiaakino naa iyie likimbatisa nanu, pa nilotu iyie enatii?”

English: And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Tonyorrai taata iyie, amu te ina eishiakino nikintabaya naayieu Enkai pooki.” Nenyorraa Yohana.

English: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
Masaai: Ore pee eidipi aaibatisa Yesu, neilepu nabo kata aing'uaa enkare; ng'ura, nebolokino shumata nedol ninye Enkiyang'et Sinyati e Nkai edou anaa enturkulu, elotu shumata ninye;

English: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Masaai: naa ng'ura, nepuku oltoilo te shumata nejo, “Enkerai ai ena nanyor, natishipe te ninye.”

English: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.
Masaai: Ore ina kata neilepie Enkiyang'et Sinyati Yesu arik ong'ata metetema shetani.

English: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip atupukoi nkolong'i artam dama o kewarie.

English: And when the tempter came to him, he said, If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
Masaai: Nelotu olatemani nejoki, “Te naa ira iyie Enkerai e Nkai, tiaaki kulo soito metaa mukateni.”

English: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
Masaai: Kake newaliki ajoki, “Etisiraki, ‘Meishuyie oltung'ani emukate ake, kake eishuyie pooki rorei opukunye enkutuk e Nkai.’ ”

English: Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple,
Masaai: Neitoki shetani arik enkanasa sinyati neitoton ninye te ntopij e nkaji e Nkai.

English: And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
Masaai: Nejoki. “Te naa ira iyie Enkerai e Nkai, tusulai kewan enkop; amu etisiraki aajo: ‘Keitanap ninye ilmalaika lenyena te nkaraki iyie, eikinap ninche too nkaik enye, pee mikinkob osoit enkeju ino.’ ”

English: Jesus said unto him, It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Etisiraki sii aajo, ‘Mitem iyie Olaitoriani Enkai ino.’ ”

English: Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
Masaai: Neitoki shetani arik ninye oldoinyo oado oleng, neitodol ninye nkitoriat pooki e nkop o enkitoo enye.

English: And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Ekaaisho nanu iyie kuna tokitin pooki ti nikigilaki kung aserem.”

English: Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Shomo shetani amu, etisiraki aajo, ‘Teserema Olaitoriani Enkai ino naa ninye ake openy isiaai.’ ”

English: Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
Masaai: Neing'uaa shetani ninye te ina kata; naa ng'ura, nepuonu ilmalaika aaisiaai ninye.

English: Now when Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee;
Masaai: Ore pee ening ninye ajo eteenaki Yohana neibelekenya alo Galilaya.

English: And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:
Masaai: Neing'uaa Nasaret nelotu abik te Kapernaum, enkang natii embata e naiposha te nkop e Sebulon o Naftali,

English: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
Masaai: pee ebaya enatejoki to loiboni le Nkai oji Isaya pee ejo,

English: The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
Masaai: “Enkop e Sebulon o enkop e Naftali ineeshepita enkoitoi nalo enaiposha, lido kekun le Yordan Galilaya oo loreren,

English: The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
Masaai: etoduaa ewang'an kitok olorere otonita ti atua enaimin, ore lelo ootonita te nkop o to loip lee keeya, ekenyikia ewang'an.”

English: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Masaai: Ore ebaiki ina kata neiteru Yesu alikioo ororei le Nkai nejo, “Erridutu amu etinyikua enkitoria e shumata.”

English: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
Masaai: Ore eloito te mbata e naiposha e Galilaya nedol ilalashera oare, Simon oji Petero o lalashe lenye Anterea, enang'aki o rreshet atua enaiposha, amu ilarreshok apa loo sinkir.

English: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Wootu, erukurukoreki, naa kaitaa intae ilarreshok loo ltung'ana.”

English: And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
Masaai: Neing'uaa nabo kata irresheta lenye neirukurukore.

English: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
Masaai: Ore pee eigutaa penyo nedol kulikae alashera oare. Yakobo le Sebedayo, o Yohana olalashe lenye, ti atua empeut eboitare papaai lenye Sebedayo, eripita irresheta lenye neipot ninche.

English: And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.
Masaai: Neing'uaa nabo kata empeut o papaai lenye neirukurukore.

English: And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.
Masaai: Nemanaa Yesu te Galilaya pooki eiteng'enisho too nkajijik enye e ntumo, nelikioo ilomon Supati le ina kitoria, neishiunye pooki keeya o emueyian ti atua olorere.

English: And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatick, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them.
Masaai: Neibulu olning'o lenye enkop pooki e Siria; neyakini ninye iltung'ana pooki oomueyiaa ooibung'a nkeyaitin oo mpukunot kumok o looata loiriruani o looata emuoyian e nkiterria o lmaiman o looidimua emion; neishiunye ninye ninche.

English: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judaea, and from beyond Jordan.
Masaai: Nesuj ilororani kituaak ooing'uaa Galilaya o Dekapoli o Yerusalem o Yudea o lido kekun le Yordan.

English: And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him:
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu isiamon neilepaki oldoinyo: ore pee eton nepuonu ilooiteng'eni lenyena enetii.

English: And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying,
Masaai: Neiteng'en ninye ninche nejo:

English: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Masaai: “Emayiana ilaisinak too ltauja; amu enenye enkitoria e keper.

English: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
Masaai: “Emayiana ilooishir; amu ninche eilejileji.

English: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
Masaai: “Emayiana iloobor; amu ninche oojung enkop.

English: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
Masaai: “Emayiana ilooata esumash o enkure eing'oru enayieu Enkai; amu ninche eitaraposhi.

English: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
Masaai: “Emayiana iloata olng'ur amu ninche eing'urrieki.

English: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
Masaai: “Emayiana ilooitukuo ltauja; amu ninche oodol Enkai.

English: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
Masaai: “Emayiana lelo ooitayu osotua; amu ninche eji inkera e Nkai.

English: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Masaai: “Emayiana lelo ooisilisili te nkaraki enayieu Enkai amu enenye enkitoria e keper.

English: Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
Masaai: “Imayianana intae te nesukeny ninche intae, neisilisil, neiteeniki intae imbaa pooki torrok e lejare te naa nkaraki nanu.

English: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.
Masaai: Enting'idata nishipapa oleng; amu kitok olerrinyore linyi te shumata; amu eisilisilo ninche aaiko neijia iloibonok le Nkai ootii apa te dukuya intae.

English: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.
Masaai: “Irara intae emunyan e nkop; kake te netuyiatuyu emunyan, ainyoo eshukokinyeki enkisuisho? Meitoki aata tipat katukul, kake kenang'ari boo meitunyoi iltung'ana too nkejek.

English: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
Masaai: “Irara intae ewang'an e nkop. Meisudoroyu enkanasa natii oldoinyo.

English: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Masaai: Nemeinok sii ltung'ana oltaa nepising to ltoo, kake eiteleiki olperere; neitawang'aki pooki ootii aji.

English: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
Masaai: Neijia sii enchoo ewang'an inyi metawang'a te dukuya iltung'ana pee edol iasat inyi supati, pee eyanyituni Papa linyi otii shumata.

English: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
Masaai: “Emijo kaewuo aitarruoo Nkitanapat aashu loibonok le Nkai, eitu alotu aitarruoo kake pee aitabaya.

English: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
Masaai: Amu esipa ajoki intae, ore o metaba anaa nelusoo shumata o enkop, melusoo osirata obo anaa oltipoto obo loo Nkitanapat eitu eitabari.

English: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae ogil enkitanapata nabo e kuna kutiti, hoo te naa enkinyi, neitayiolo ilkulikae metigila, naa keipoti ninye aajo olkini te pooki te nkitoria e keper; kake ore oloas nena neitayiolo sii ilkulikae metaasa, naa keipoti ilo aajo olkitok te nkitoria e keper.

English: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
Masaai: Amu ajoki intae te naa melusoo esupatisho inyi alang enoo laiteng'enak loo nkitanapat o enoo Lfarisayo, nimijing'ijing'i enkitoria e keper.

English: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:
Masaai: “Itoning'o aajo etiaakaki iltung'ana li apa, ‘Miar metua; naa ore oloar metua neishiaakino enkiguana.’

English: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae, ore pooki ogorokino olalashe, naa keishiakino enkiguana; ore olosurdaany olalashe, neishiaakino, nerikokini ilkituaak; ore olodekisho ajo ‘Lo modai!’ keishiaakino olbalbal le nkima.

English: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;
Masaai: Naa ti niyau enkishoroto ino olperere lo lasar, nidamu te ine olalashe lino likiaatakinore,

English: Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
Masaai: tung'uai teine enkishoroto te mbata o lperere lo lasar, shomo; tang'asa toning'ore olalashe lino, pee intoki ashukunye aitayu enkishoroto ino.

English: Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.
Masaai: “Tasioki toning'ore olintarrikinore eton iriamariri te nkoitoi; pee mikirik enetii oladung'oni le nkiguana nikirikoki oladugoni le nkiguana esikari, nikinang'akini korokoroni.

English: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.
Masaai: Esipa aajoki, mipuku te ine katukul o metaba anaa nilak empisai nabayie.

English: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
Masaai: “Itoning'o aajo etejoki, ‘Miloloito.’

English: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae, ore oloing'or eng'oruoi neng'uar eidipa atololoito to ltau lenye.

English: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
Masaai: Ti nikintasur enkong'u ino e tatene, tukurtu, inturrai, amu enaikash te neimin erubata nabo alang te nenang'akini osesen lino pooki olbalbal le nkima.

English: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut if off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
Masaai: Naa ti nikintasur enkaina ino e tatene, tudung'u inturrai; amu eikash erubata ino nabo te neimin, alang osesen lino pooki te nenang'akini olbalbal le nkima.

English: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
Masaai: “Etejoki sii, ‘Ore oloorore enkitok enye, inchoo eisho ninye empalai naorore.’

English: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae, ore pooki ng'ae oorore enkitok enye, neme te nkaraki e loloito ake, etipika ninye atua eloloito; ore oloyam ina natoororeki, etololoite ninye.

English: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:
Masaai: “Itoning'o sii iltung'ana li apa enatiaakaki, ‘Minya olmumai le lejare, kake intabai ilmuma linono to Laitoriani.’

English: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne:
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae minos ilmuma katukul hoo te shumata, amu olorika le nkitoria e Nkai;

English: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.
Masaai: aashu te nkop, amu olorika loo nkejek enyena; aashu te Yerusalem, amu enkang o laiguanani kitok.

English: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.
Masaai: Niminos olmumai te ndukuya ino, amu mindim aiborrie olpapita obo anaa aitoroka.

English: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
Masaai: Kake enchoo irorei linyi metaa ee, neaku ee, aashu mme, neaku mme, amu ore enalusoo te nena naa ilo torrono eing'uaa.

English: Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
Masaai: “Itoning'o aajo etejoki, ‘Enkong'u o te nkong'u, o olalae to lalae.’

English: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae, migilunore olikintaas entorrono kake ore olikiosh eseder e tatene, imbelekenyaki sii enkae.

English: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani pooki oyieu nikirik enkiguana, eyieu nikioru olkila li atua, inchoo meewa sii oli oriong.

English: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.
Masaai: Ore olikiaraki, shomo kilomita nabo, shomo are.

English: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
Masaai: Ore olikiomon, inchoo; ore olikisilen, mimitiki.

English: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.
Masaai: “Itoning'o aajo etejoki, ‘Tonyorra ole latia ino, nimbayu olmang'atinta lino.’

English: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
Masaai: Kake ajoki nanu intae, entonyor ilmang'ati linyi, niomonokiki lelo ooisilisil intae;

English: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
Masaai: pee itumutumu intae aataa inkera e Papa linyi otii keper; amu eilepakinye enkolong enye iltorrok o supati neirriwaki enchan iloota sipat o ile meeta.

English: For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?
Masaai: Amu ti ninyorrinyorro iloonyor intae, kaa shunet itumutumu intae? Ai meiko neijia oshi ilasotok le kodi?

English: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?
Masaai: Naa te naa ilalashera linyi ake irorokiki, kaa yasata naa italang'ie ilkulikae? Ai meiko oshi neijia ilkulikae oreren?

English: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
Masaai: Entaa naa bayarot anaa Papa linyi otii keper laa bayaroti.

English: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
Masaai: “Eng'ura pee miasiaasa isupati inyi te dukuya inkonyek oo ltung'ana ijojo pee edol ninche intae; amu ti ninkoko neijia nimitumutumu shunet te Papa linyi otii keper.

English: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
Masaai: “Ore ti nintayu iyie enkishoroto ino o lng'ur nimiosh emowuo, anaa enaiko isunkuro too nkajijik e ntumo o too nkoitoi, pee errep iltung'ana. Esipa ajoki intae, eidipa ninche aanoto enchunet enye.

English: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
Masaai: Kake ti nintayu iyie enkishoroto ino o lng'ur nimincho enkaina ino e kedienye metayiolo enaas ene tatene;

English: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.
Masaai: pee eaku intokitin ninchooyo, inoo nkisudorot; naa ore Papa lino odol too nkisudorot, nikincho ninye olerrinyore.

English: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
Masaai: “Naa ti niomonono nimitiuwu anaa isunkuro, amu enyor ninche aatoomon eitashoo too nkajijik e ntumo o too lojat oo nkoitoi naalala e nkanasa, pee etum aatodol iltung'ana. Esipa ajoki intae, eidipa ninche aanoto shunet enye.

English: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
Masaai: Kake ti niomon iyie, tijing'a olgilata lino, ore pee indip aikeno kutuk aji niomon Papa lino too nkisudorot, ore Papa lino odol too nkisudorot naa aikilaaki iyie.

English: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
Masaai: “Naa tiniomonono, emintaa irorei kumok anaa enaas iloreren, amu edamu ninche aajo kening'i ninche te nkumoi oo rorei lenye.

English: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
Masaai: Emitiu anaa ninche, amu eyiolo Papa linyi iniyieuwu eton eitu iomonunu intae.

English: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
Masaai: Naa inji entejo: ‘Papa lang otii shumata meitisinyi enkarna ino

English: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Masaai: meeu enkitoria ino, metaasi eniyieu te nkop anaa enatiu te shumata.

English: Give us this day our daily bread.
Masaai: Inchoo iyiook ena olong endaa ang e anaake.

English: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
Masaai: Nipalaki iyiook isilen ang, anaa ti nikipalaki iyiook ilooata isilen ang.

English: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
Masaai: Nimirik iyiook atua intemat, kake intajeu iyiook tiaatua ilo torrono.’

English: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
Masaai: “Amu tinipalakiki intae iltung'ana inkitarruorrot enye, naa kepalaki sii ninye intae Papa linyi otii shumata.

English: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
Masaai: Kake ti nimipalakiki intae iltung'ana inkitarruorrot enye, nemepalaki sii intae Papa linyi inkitarruorrot inyi.

English: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
Masaai: “Naa ti nieniene ate aapukoo, emitiu anaa isunkuro oosot inkomomi, amu keidisie ninche inkomomi enye, pee edol iltung'ana aajo etupukoitie. Esipa ajoki intae, eidipa aanoto shunet enye.

English: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;
Masaai: Kake ore ti nipukoo iyie, iela endukuya ino nisuj enkomon ino;

English: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.
Masaai: mikidol iltung'ana inchere itupukoiyie, kake edol Papa lino otii inkisudorot; ore Papa lino odol too nkisudorot nikimputaki.

English: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
Masaai: “Emishumaki ate te nkop masaa kiroteti, eneinosie olasai o endoron, negil ilapurrok, nepurroo,

English: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
Masaai: Kake entushumaki ate te shumata masaa inyi kiroteti, te nemeinosie olasai, anaa endoron, nemegil ilapurrok nemepurroo;

English: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Masaai: amu ore enetii masaa inono kiroteti, naa ine eyooki atii oltau lino.

English: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
Masaai: “Ore oltaa lo sesen naa enkong'u, metaa te neikishiaan enkong'u ino, neiput osesen lino pooki ewang'an.

English: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!
Masaai: Kake te naa torrono enkong'u ino neiput osesen lino pooki enaimin. Amaa te neaku ewang'an natii iyie enaimin: kebaa esapuko e ina aimin!

English: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
Masaai: “Metii oltung'ani oidim aaisiaayia ilkituaak oare amu eibayu obo nenyorru olikae; aashu eibung'are obo nemenu olikae. Mindimidimi aaisiaayia Enkai o Mamon, enkai oo masaa.

English: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
Masaai: “Enkaraki ina pe ajoki intae, eminyamaliki enkishui inyi, aajo ainyoo inyanya, anaa ainyoo iokioko, anaa too seseni linyi aajo ainyoo inchopishopo. Ai melusoo enkishui alang endaa, nelusoo osesen alang nkilani?

English: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Masaai: Eng'ura intaritik o loing'ang'e inchere, meunisho nemeisampu, nemeiturrurroki impechen; neitoti Papa linyi otii shumata ninche. Ai mirara intae kiroteti aalang ninche?

English: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
Masaai: Ai ng'ae te intae oidim te neitanyamaluo atoponai enkadori enye entemata nabo?

English: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
Masaai: “Ainyoo naa pee inyamalakiki inkiliani? Entadamu intapuka e ong'ata enaikununye te nebulu; amu measisho ninche nemepiyaisho;

English: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
Masaai: kake ajoki nanu intae eitu eishopi ninye Solomon te sikar enye pooki anaa nabo e kuna.

English: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?
Masaai: Amaa te neishop Enkai inkujit e ong'ata aiko neijia, naatai taata neyookini aanang'aki enkima taaisere, ai meitulusoo oleng aishop intae, lo tung'ana ooti enkirukoto?

English: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?
Masaai: “Eminyamalu ijojo, ‘Ainyoo kinya?’ anaa, ‘Ainyoo kiok?’ ana, ‘Ainyoo kinchop?’

English: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
Masaai: Amu nena pooki eing'oru iloreren lemeyiolo Enkai; amu eyiolo Papa linyi le shumata ajo iyieuu nena pooki.

English: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Masaai: Kake entang'as eng'oru enkitoria enye o sipat enyana; naa keponikini intae nena pooki.

English: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
Masaai: Metaa eminyamalaki ine taaisere amu enyamalaki taaisere kewan. Eidip enkolong intorrok enyena.

English: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
Masaai: “Eminguanare pee meinguanareki intae.

English: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.
Masaai: Amu ore enkiguana ninguanarere, naa ninye eiguanareki intae; ore enintorisiokiki ilkulikae, naa ninye eitorisiokini intae.

English: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
Masaai: Ainyoo pee ing'uraa esuama natii enkong'u o lalashe lino, nimidol olchata otii enkong'u ino makewan?

English: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?
Masaai: Anaa kaji inko ti nijoki olalashe lino, ‘Inchooki maitayu esuama te nkong'u ino;’ naa, ing'ura etii olchata atua enkong'u ino makewan?

English: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.
Masaai: Lo sunkuroi, tang'asa intayu ilo shata te nkong'u ino makewan pee itumoki atoduaa oleng, aitayu ina suama te nkong'u o lalashe lino.

English: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.
Masaai: “Emincho ildiein entoki nasinya, niminang'akiki ilului inyi ilbitiro pee meituny too nkejek enye, neibelekenyakino intae aakij.

English: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
Masaai: “Entoomonu pee eishori intae; eng'oru naa itumutumu entooshiosh kutuk aji pee eboluni intae.

English: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
Masaai: Amu ore pooki oomonu neng'amaa, ore olooshiosh neboluni.

English: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?
Masaai: Anaa kalo tung'ani te intae laa, te neomon e nkerai emukate, keisho ninye osoit?

English: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?
Masaai: Aashu ae te neomon osinkirri, keisho olasurai?

English: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
Masaai: Aiti niyiololo intae oora torrok aaishoo inkera inyi inkishorot sidain, kebaa eitulusoo naleng Papa linyi otii shumata aisho intokitin sidain lelo oomon ninye?

English: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
Masaai: Metaa ore pooki niyieuwu neitaas intae iltung'ana entaasa sii intae ninche nena, amu kuna nkitanapat o loibonok le Nkai.

English: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
Masaai: “Entijing intae te nkishomi napirik amu dapash kishomi nelala enkoitoi nalo enkiminata, naa kumok iloojing ina.

English: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
Masaai: Amu kepirik kishomi naa ronkai enkoitoi nalo enkishon, naa ilkuti ootum ina.

English: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.
Masaai: “Entorrip ate too loibonok le lejare oopuonu enitii eishopito inkilani oo ntare, kake ore atua ninche, naa isuyian ooata enkarri.

English: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?
Masaai: Too lng'anayio lenye iyiolouu. Keitayuni sabibu too lkiku anaa ilng'abolo too lkikarreta?

English: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.
Masaai: Neijia etiu, eiu pooki shani sidai ilng'anayio sidain, neiu pooki shani torrono ilng'anayio torrok.

English: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
Masaai: Meidim olchani sidai atoiu ilng'anayio torrok, nemeidim sii olchani torrono atoiu ilng'anayio sidain.

English: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
Masaai: Ore pooki shani lemeiu ilng'anayio sidain, nedung'i aauroo nenang'akini enkima.

English: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
Masaai: Neijia naa etiu, too lng'anayio lenye iyiolouu ninche.

English: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.
Masaai: “Mme pooki tung'ani laajo ‘Olaitoriani, Olaitoriani,’ ojing enkitoria e Nkai, kake ilo oas enayieu Papa lai otii shumata.

English: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?
Masaai: Aayooki aajoki ilkumok te ina olong, ‘Olaitoriani, Olaitoriani, keitu kimbonisho te nkarna ino, nikiaraa iloiriruani te nkarna ino, nikiaas ine nking'asia te nkarna ino?’

English: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
Masaai: Naa kashirraki ina kata ajoki ninche, ‘Eitu ae kata ayiolou intae, enchom entung'uayoki intae, ilaasak loo ntorok.’

English: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
Masaai: “Metaa ore pooki ng'ae oning lelo rorei laainei neas, neitanyaanyukieki oltung'ani oteshetaka enkaji enye endapidapoi,

English: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
Masaai: nesha enchan, nenang'unye enkare, nekut olkutati, neosh ina aji, neitu euroo; amu etuunokoki olkitamanyunoto lenye shumata endapidapoi.

English: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:
Masaai: “Na ore pooki ng'ae oning kulo rorei laainei nemeas, neitanyaanyukieki oltung'ani omoda oteshetaka enkaji enye shumata osinyai;

English: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
Masaai: nesha enchan nenang'unye enkare, nekutu olkutati, neosh ina aji, neurori neaku kitok euroroto enye.”

English: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:
Masaai: Ore pee eidip Yesu kulo rorei, neing'asia siamon te nkiteng'enare enye;

English: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Masaai: amu eiteng'ena ninche anaa oloata enkidimata nemetiu anaa ilaiteng'enak lenye loo nkitanapat.

English: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
Masaai: Ore pee edou ninye to ldoinyo, neirukurukore siamon kituaak.

English: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, nelotu enetii oloata enkeeya oo lbolot, negil kung aserem, nejoki, “Lo kitok, ti niyieu kindim atisika.”

English: And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Masaai: Neitorioo enkaina enye neiseyie nejo, “Ayieu; tisikayu.” Nesikari nabo kata enkeeya enye.

English: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Ng'ura, miliki oltung'ani; kake shomo intoduaa kewan olapolosani, nintayu enkishoroto naitanapishe Musa, metaa shakenisho te ninche.”

English: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
Masaai: Ore pee ejing ninye Kapernaum, nelotu olkitok le sikari enetii asai ninye,

English: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
Masaai: ejo, “Lo kitok, eirrag olaisiaayiani lai ti aji, etaa olmaima, neitabayie oleng.”

English: And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Kalotu aishiunye.”

English: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
Masaai: Newaliki ilo kitok le sikari ajoki, “Lo kitok, kaamakua nanu ti nijing'u enkaji ai, kake tejo ake ororei, naa keishiu olaisiaayiani lai.

English: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
Masaai: Amu ara sii nanu oltung'ani otii abori enkitoo, naata nanu sikarini laatii ti abori, te najoki obo, ‘Shomo,’ nelo; najoki likae, ‘Wou,’ nelotu; naa te najoki osinka lai, ‘Taasa ena, neas.’ ”

English: When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Yesu nena, neing'asia nejoki lelo oosujita, “Esipa ajoki intae, eitu ae kata adolie likae ti atua Siraeli enkirukoto sapok naba inji.

English: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
Masaai: Najoki nanu intae, epuonu ilkumok ooing'uaa oloo saen o loontoluo aatoni te nebo Abraham o Isaak o Yakobo ti atua enkitoria e shumata;

English: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Masaai: kake ore lelo laa ninche naaji ile ina kitoria nenang'akini atua enaimin e auluo; neaku enkishirata o eonyoto oo lala.”

English: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ilo kitok loo sikarini, “Shomo ang; metotiwuo te iyie anaa ina niruko.” Neishiunyeki olaisiaayiani lenye te ina kata ake.

English: And when Jesus was come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother laid, and sick of a fever.
Masaai: Ore pee ejing Yesu enkaji e Petero, nedol enkaputani enye eirrag emuei oloirobi.

English: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them.
Masaai: Neiseyie enkaina enye neing'ueki oloirobi, neinyototo aisiaai ninye.

English: When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick:
Masaai: Ore pee eaku teipa, neyakini ilkumok ooata iloiriruani nearaa iloiriruani to rorei, neishiunye lelo pooki oomuei.

English: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
Masaai: Pee etum atabai enairoroki to loiboni le Nkai oji Isaya pee ejo, “Ewa ninye openy imuoyiaritin ang, netanapa inkeyaitin ang.”

English: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu esiamo kitok emanita, neitanap metalang'a aapuo lido kekun.

English: And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
Masaai: Nelotu olaiteng'enani loo nkitanapat nejoki, “Lo Aiteng'enani, kaasuj pooki weuji nilo.”

English: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Eeta imbariak ingumot, neeta intaritik o loing'ang'e sinkin kake meeta Enkerai e Tung'ani eneiteleiki endukuya enye.”

English: And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
Masaai: Nejoki likai loo looiteng'eni lenye, “Lo kitok, inchooki matang'asa alo anukaa papa.”

English: But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Yesu ninye, “Tusujuaki; inchoo ilmeneng'a metunukai ilmeneng'a lenye.”

English: And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him.
Masaai: Ore pee ejing Yesu empeut, nesuj ilooiteng'eni lenyena.

English: And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.
Masaai: Ng'ura, neinyototo olkutati kitok te naiposha, metaa keimisie ilopir le nkare empeut; kake keirura ninye.

English: And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.
Masaai: Nepuo enetii ilooiteng'eni lenyena, neinyeyie, nejoki, “Intajeu iyiook, Lo Kitok, amu kindaaitie.”

English: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Aainyo pee iureishoyuyu intae ilooti enkirukoto?” Neinyototo neisikong olkutati o enaiposha; nelotu enkitirring'ata kitok.

English: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
Masaai: Neing'asia lelo tung'ana nejo, “Kaa pukunoto o ltung'ani ele oning olkutati o enaiposha?”

English: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.
Masaai: Ore pee ebaiki lido kekun le nkop oo Lgadaren, nenang'are iltung'ana oare oaata iloiriruani oopi oleng ooing'uaa inkuraren o metaa meidim oltung'ani aima ina oitoi.

English: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, nebuak ninche aajo, “Ainyoo iatakinore iyie iyiook Enkerai e Nkai? Amaa iewuo iyie aitame iyiook eton eng'or enkata?”

English: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.
Masaai: Netii eluaata oo lbitiro nalakuaniki ninche nadaa.

English: So the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.
Masaai: Nesai lelo oiriruani aajoki, “Te naa iaraa iyiook aipung'ie, inchoo iyiook maape aajing enda boo oo lbitiro.”

English: And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Enchom.” Ore pee eipung ninche, nepuo aajing ilbitiro; naa ng'ura! nekuet emboo pooki, nesulari te marti aajing enaiposha, neye ti atua enkare.

English: And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils.
Masaai: Neilanyisho ilchekuti aapuo inkang'itie enye nelikioo imbaa pooki o nena naatotiwuo te lelo ooata iloiriruani.

English: And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura! nepuku enkanasa pooki aapuo aanang'are Yesu; ore pee edol nesai metung'uai ilo kirine lenye.

English: And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city.
Masaai: Neked empeut nelang alo enkanasa enye.

English: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura neyakini oltung'ani maima, eirrag te rruat; ore pee edol Yesu enkirukoto e lelo tung'ana, nejoki ilo maima, “Na kerai, ntagoluoyu to ltau amu kitapalakaki ng'ok inono.”

English: And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura nejo kulikai aiteng'enak loo nkitanapat ti atua ate, “Enkai emor ele tung'ani.”

English: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
Masaai: Neyiolou Yesu ndamunot enye nejoki, “Aainyo pee mbirribirrirri ntorrok too ltauja linyi?

English: For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?
Masaai: Kaa nalelek, te neji ‘Kitapalakaki ng'ok inono.’ Ana te neji, ‘Inyoo shomo?’

English: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.
Masaai: Kake ore pee itumutumu aatayiolo aajo, eeta Enkerai e Tung'ani engolon te nkop napalakinye iltung'ana ng'ok,” nejoki ilo maima, “Inyo, tudumu erruat ino, shomo ang.”

English: And he arose, and departed to his house.
Masaai: Neinyototo, nelo ang.

English: But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.
Masaai: Kake ore pee edol siamon neureishoyu neisho Enkai enkitoo naishoo ltung'ana engolon naaijo ina.

English: And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
Masaai: Ore eim Yesu ine nedol oltung'ani oji Matayo, eton te neitainyeki kodi nejoki, “Tusujuaki,” neinyototo asuj.

English: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.
Masaai: Neaku ore eton te ina aji enye ainos endaa, ng'ura, nepuonu ilasotok le kodi o laing'okok kumok netoni te nebo Yesu o looiteng'eni lenyena.

English: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?
Masaai: Ore pee edol Ilfarisayo ina, nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Aainyo pee eng'arie Olaiteng'enani linyi endaa ilasotok le kodi laing'okok?”

English: But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
Masaai: Kake ore pee ening, nejo, “Meyieu ilememuei olabaani, kake iloomuoi ooyieu.

English: But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Masaai: Enchom enteng'ena ate eneikununo ele rorei, ojo, ‘Olng'ur ayieu mme olasar;’ amu eitu alotu aipot isupati kake ilaing'okok.”

English: Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?
Masaai: Nepuonu ina kata ilooiteng'eni le Yohana enetii nejoki, “Aainyo pee kipukoo oleng iyiook o Lfarisayo, nemepukoo ilooiteng'eni linono?”

English: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Keidim ilchorueta lo loyamishe aaishira eton eboitare oloyamishe? Kake kepuonu nkolong'i naayae olayamishe aaitung'uaa ninche, ina kata kenya epukoo.

English: No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.
Masaai: “Meetae oltung'ani opik erashe ng'ejuk enkila musana; amu ore ina natipikaki epolos enkila, neponari apolosa.

English: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.
Masaai: Nemepik sii iltung'ana enaisho ng'ejuk oo sabibu ilbenia musan; naa te nepik nepolosa ilbenia, neibukori enaisho oo sabibu nepolosa sii Lbenia; kake ilbenia ng'ejuko epiki pee erripi pokira are.”

English: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.
Masaai: Ore eton eliki ninche kuna baa, ng'ura, nelotu oltung'ani oitore enkaji e ntumo negilaki kung nejoki, “Etua te na kata entito ai, kake wou inteleiki enkaina ino pee epiu ninye.”

English: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples.
Masaai: Neinyototo Yesu o looiteng'eni lenyena nesuj ninye.

English: And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment:
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, nelotu enkitok te siadi ninye, naruko osarge larin tomon o are, neiseyie olcholoi lo lkila lenye; amu etejo to ltau lenye,

English: For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.
Masaai: “Te naiseyie ake olcholoi lo lkila lenye naishiu.”

English: But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.
Masaai: Neibelekenya Yesu nedol ninye, nejoki, “Naito, intagoluoyu amu kinchiunye enkirukoto ino.” Neishiu ina kitok aiteru te ina kata ake.

English: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise,
Masaai: Ore pee elotu Yesu enkaji e ilo oitore enkaji e ntumo nedol ilookut indulen o lorere eilepilep oleng,

English: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.
Masaai: nejoki, “Ewuang'a amu eitu eye entito, keirura.” Nekueniyie ninche aayiet.

English: But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.
Masaai: Ore pee eidipi aaipung'ie olorere, nejing neibung enkaina enye, neinyototo entito.

English: And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land.
Masaai: Neibulu kulo omon ilo kerenket pooki.

English: And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.
Masaai: Ore egiroo Yesu aing'uaa ine nesuj iltung'ana aare modook ooishiraki aajoki, “Ing'urrie iyiook enkerai e Daudi.”

English: And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They said unto him, Yea, Lord.
Masaai: Ore pee ebaiki aji, nepuonu ilmodook enetii, nejoki Yesu ninche, “Irukuruku aajo kaidim ataasa ena?” Nejoki, “Ee lo kitok.”

English: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it unto you.
Masaai: Neiseyie nkonyek enye ejo, “Inchoo etiu anaa enkirukoto inyi.”

English: And their eyes were opened; and Jesus straitly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.
Masaai: Neboloyu nkonyek enye. Neitanap Yesu nereiki ajoki ninche, “Entodol emincho hoo oltung'ani obo eyiolou.”

English: But they, when they were departed, spread abroad his fame in all that country.
Masaai: Kake eipung'o nepuo aaibulunye ilomon lenyena ilo kerenket pooki.

English: As they went out, behold, they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a devil.
Masaai: Ore pee eipung lelo, ng'ura, neyakini ninye oltung'ani lemeiro otijing'a oloirirua.

English: And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spake: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.
Masaai: Ore pee eitupuku oloirirua, neiro ilo lemeiro apa, neing'asia esiamo nejo, “Eitu ae kata edoli ena ti atua enkop e Israel.”

English: But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.
Masaai: Kake etejo Lfarisayo, “Engolon oo loiriruani eararie ninye loiriruani.”

English: And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every disease among the people.
Masaai: Neman Yesu inkang'itie pooki sapuki o nkutiti, neiteng'enisho too nkajijik enye e ntumo, nelikioo ilomon supati le nkitoria e keper, neishiunye pooki keeya o pooki pukunoto e mueyian.

English: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
Masaai: Ore pee edol ninye olorere netum olng'ur te ninche amu eteekate ninche, nelepori neidapashari netiu anaa ntare nemeeta olchekut.

English: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Esipa aisapuk enkisampuare kake kuti ilaisiaayiak.

English: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
Masaai: Kaae, entoomon naa Olaitoriani le nkisampuare meirriu ilaisiaayiak atua enkisampuare enye.”

English: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
Masaai: Neipot lelo ooiteng'eni lenyena tomon o aare, neisho meitoria nearaa iloiriruani ooiduruk, neishiunye sii mpukunot pooki oo mueyiaritin o nkeyaitin.

English: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Masaai: Naa kuna nkarn oo looiteng'eni lenyena pokira tomon o aare; ole dukuya Simon oji Petero, o Andrea olalashe lenye; Yakobo le Sebedayo o Yohana olalashe lenye;

English: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
Masaai: Filipo, o Bartolomayo; Tomas o Matayo olasotoni le kodi; Yakobo le Alfayo, o Tadayo;

English: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
Masaai: Simon onyor olosho lenye o Yudas Iskariot laa ninye oishooyie Yesu.

English: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:
Masaai: Kulo pokira tomon o aare eirriwayie Yesu neitanap ajoki, “Emipuo nkoitoi oo Loreren, nimijing'ijing'i enkang hoo nabo oo ltung'ana le Samaria

English: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Masaai: kake enchom enetii ntare kiminat e nkaji e Siraeli.

English: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Masaai: Ore ipuopuo, entolikioi entejo ‘Etinyikua enkitoria e shumata.’

English: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.
Masaai: Enchiunye iloomuei, entopiu ilootuata enchiunye iloota enkeeya oo lbolot, entaarai iloiriruani. Eishooki intae pesho, enchooi sii intae pesho.

English: Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses,
Masaai: Emishoroo sahabu anaa mpesai too nkimeitani inyi,

English: Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat.
Masaai: nimishoroo embene te lototo inyi, anaa nkilani maare, anaa namuka, anaa eng'udi, amu eishiaakino olaisiaayiani endaa enye.

English: And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence.
Masaai: Ore pooki ang sapuk o enkiti nijing'ijing'i, enkilikuanisho tenaa ketii oltung'ani supat atua, nitonini tenebo ninye o metaba anaa nidumunyenye aapuo.

English: And when ye come into an house, salute it.
Masaai: Na ti nijing'ijing'i enkaji eroroki.

English: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.
Masaai: Naa te neishiaakino intae ina aji, nejing osotua linyi shumata ninye, naa te nemeishiaakino, neshukokino intae osotua linyi.

English: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ai lemeng'amaa intae, anaa olemening ororei linyi, ore pee ipukuku aaing'uaa ina aji, anaa ina ang, nimpiripiroo enterit natii nkejek inyi.

English: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
Masaai: Esipa ajoki intae, keikashieki Sodom o Gomora te ina ang te nkolong enkiguana.

English: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
Masaai: “Eng'urai airriwayie intae anaa nkerra atua suyian, enteng'enita anaa lasuriaa, niborrurru anaa nturkuluni.

English: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues;
Masaai: Kake entodol ate too ltung'ana amu keishooyo intae meiguanareki neidong intae ti atua nkajijik enye e ntumo.

English: And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.
Masaai: Naa keriki intae dukuya ilbalosini o laiguanak te nkaraki nanu, pee iakuku shakeni te ninche o too Loreren.

English: But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak.
Masaai: Kake ore ina kata te nerik intae, eming'aeng'ae aajo, ‘Kaa kijo’, amu keishori intae te ina kata enijojo.

English: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.
Masaai: Amu mme intae ooiro, Enkiyang'et e Papa linyi nairo ti atua intae.

English: And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.
Masaai: “Naa keishooyo olalashe olikae, metaari metua, neishooyo menye enkerai, nedumakino nkera ntoiuo enye neishooyo ninche metaari metuata.

English: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
Masaai: Naa keibayu intae iltung'ana pooki, enkaraki enkarna ai, kake ore olong'iri metabaiki enkiting'oto nejeu.

English: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.
Masaai: Naa te nearari intae te na ang, esikaki enkae, amu esipa ajoki intae, miishushu nkang'itie e Siraeli pooki eitu elotu Enkerai e Tung'ani.

English: The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.
Masaai: “Melang oloiteng'eni oloiteng'en ninye, nemelang osinka oloitore ninye.

English: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?
Masaai: Eidip oloiteng'eni te netiu anaa oloiteng'en ninye, netiu osinka anaa oloitore ninye. Asa taa etejo olopeny enkaji Beelsebul, kebaa eitulusoo aajo neijia lootii enkaji enye!

English: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.
Masaai: “Metaa emiure ninche amu, meetae embae naisudoyioki nemeyiolouni.

English: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.
Masaai: Ore enajoki nanu intae te naimin embalunye te wang'an, ore enining'ining'i te nkiok, entolikioi too nchumarot oo nkajijik.

English: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Masaai: Emiureyu ilooar osesen nemeidim aatar enkiyang'et, enare ti niureyuyu ilo oidim aidaikie pokira are enkiyang'et o sesen ti atua olbalbal le nkima.

English: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.
Masaai: Ai meinosieki ntiitiini are esenti nabo, kake mesulunye nabo aosh enkop, meyiolo Papa linyi.

English: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
Masaai: Ore ninche intae, eikenaki o metabaiki lpapit loo lukuny inyi.

English: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki e ina emiureishoyu amu, inkashikasha aalang intiitiini kumok.

English: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
Masaai: “Ore naa pooki laaibalie te dukuya ltung'ana, naa kaibalie sii ninye te dukuya Papa lai otii shumata.

English: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
Masaai: Ore pooki laamiki te dukuya ltung'ana naa kamiki sii nanu ninye te dukuya Papa lai otii shumata.

English: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.
Masaai: “Emidamu nijojo kaewuo ayau osotua enkop; eitu alotu ayau osotua, kake olalem ayawua.

English: For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
Masaai: Aewuo nanu airriki oltung'ani o menye nairriki entito o ng'otonye, nairriki entito o enkaputani.

English: And a man's foes shall be they of his own household.
Masaai: Ore lmang'ati lo ltung'ani keaku lelo le nkaji enye.

English: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
Masaai: “Ore olonyor menye anaa ng'otonye aitalang nanu, anaa olonyor olayioni lenye anaa entito enye pee aaitalang nanu, nemaishiaakino nanu.

English: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.
Masaai: Ore olemenap osalaba lenye naasuju nemaaishiakino nanu.

English: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.
Masaai: Ore ologolie enkishui enye neiminie, ore oloiminie enkishui enye enkaraki nanu negolie.

English: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
Masaai: “Ore olong'amaa intae, nanu etang'amayie, ore olaang'amaa nanu naa ilo lairriwua etang'amayie.

English: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man's reward.
Masaai: Ore olong'amaa oltung'ani supat te nkaraki naa supat, netum olerrinyore lo ltung'ani supat.

English: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
Masaai: Ore oloitook obo le kulo ooti, enkikompe e nkare nairobi enkaraki naa oloiteng'eni lai, esipa ajok intae, meimin olerrinyore lenye.”

English: And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip Yesu aitanapa ilooiteng'eni lenyena tomon o are, neing'uaa ine nelo aiteng'enisho, nelikioo ororei too nkang'itie naamanita ine.

English: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples,
Masaai: Nening Yohana eena te korokoroni nkiasin e Kristo, neirriwaki ilooiteng'eni lenyena nejoki,

English: And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?
Masaai: “Ai yie elde olotu ana keetae likae likiaanyu?”

English: Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Enchom entoliki Yohana imbaa nining'itoto o nidolitata.

English: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.
Masaai: Etodolishote ilmodook, nepuo ilmaiman, neishiunyeki le nkeeya oo lbolot, nening'ishoyu lming'anta, neitopiuni ilootuata, ore ilaisinak, nelikini Ororei Supat le Nkai.

English: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
Masaai: Nemayiana olemetum olkob te nanu.”

English: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
Masaai: Ore pee epuo ninche neimaki Yesu Yohana to lorere ajoki, “Ainyoo ishomo intae aadol ti ong'ata? Kolperesi oyuk enkijape?

English: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses.
Masaai: Kake aainyo pee impang'a aapuo? Ko ltung'ani oishopito nkilani naapuyiapui ishomo aadol? Ng'ura, ore ilooishop inkilani naapuyiapui nkajijik oo laiguanak etii.

English: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.
Masaai: Kake ainyoo pee impang'a aapuo? Ko loiboni le Nkai ishomo aadol? Ee pae olkitok olang oloiboni le Nkai.

English: For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
Masaai: Amu ninye eimakaki pee etisiraki aajo, ‘Ng'urai airriwaa olkipaaret lai aiturukie te iyie, likintobiraki enkoitoi ino.’

English: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
Masaai: Esipa ajoki intae, eitu etumi ae kata too ltung'ana ooiu nkituaak, olkitok olang Yohana Olaibatisani. Kake ore oloti aisul te nkitoria e shumata naa kitok te ninye.

English: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
Masaai: Ore ebaiki nkolong'i e Yohana Olaibatisani o taata eisimitai te ngolon enkitoria e keper, neisimaa iloogol.

English: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
Masaai: Amu eibonishote loibonok pooki le Nkai nkitanapat o metabaiki Yohana;

English: And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
Masaai: naa te naa iyieuwu ning'amumu ena, ele doi Eliya, olapa olotu.

English: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Oloata nkiyiaa toning'o.

English: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows,
Masaai: “Ainyoo aitanyaanyukie ltung'ana le na kata? Etiu anaa nkera naatoni too neemirishoreki, neipot inkulie nejoki,

English: And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented.
Masaai: ‘Kitooshokitio intae ndulen neitu iranyiranya; nikinchirakita intae neitu nchirishiri.’

English: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil.
Masaai: Amu eewuo Yohana nemedaa, nemeokisho, nejo ltung'ana, ‘Keeta oloirirua.’

English: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
Masaai: Ore Enkerai e Tung'ani neewuo nedaa, neokisho, nejo ninche, ‘Eng'ura oltung'ani oulu, olaokoni le naisho naa olchore loo loosotu kodi o laing'okok!’ Kake too nkiasin etokorduaki kulo ti atua ltung'ana, pee eaku ilng'anayio le dukuya le Nkai o lo Lkuoo le Ker.

English: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:
Masaai: Neiteru aisikong nkang'itie naataasie siaitin enyena e nking'asia, amu eitu eirridu ng'ok enye,

English: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
Masaai: “Ee kake ayia Korasin, ee kake ayia Betsaida, amu te naa ketaasaki inenking'asia naataasaki ti atua intae, te Tiro o te Sidon anaata erridutua apa moitie, nepika ilkuniyiani o nkuruon.

English: But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.
Masaai: Kake ajoki intae, keikashieki Tiro o Sidon te nkolong e nkiguana aaitalang intae.

English: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
Masaai: Oi iyie Kapernaum aa ijo eikisisi aailepie shumata? Ae kintadouni tabaiki enemeneng'a. Amu ore isiaaitin naataasaki ti atua iyie, te naa ketaasaki apa te Sodom anaata eton eetae ina ang o tene.

English: But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.
Masaai: Amu esipa ajoki intae, keikashieki enkang e Sodom te nkolong e nkiguana aaitulusoo te iyie.”

English: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
Masaai: Neitoki Yesu ajo te ina kata, “Aaisho iyie enashe, Papa Olaitoriani le shumata o enkop, amu isudorie kuna baa iltung'ana ng'eni niboloki nkera.

English: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.
Masaai: Ee neijia etiu Papa amu ina nikintishipa iyie.

English: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
Masaai: “Aaishoo Papa pooki toki, nemeetae hoo obo oyiolo ina Kerai leme Papa ake, nemeetae hoo obo oyiolo Papa leme ina Kerai ake o pooki ng'ae ogelu Enkerai aboloki.

English: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Masaai: “Wootu enatii intae pooki oonyamal niatata ilolan ooiroshi, pee ayeng'iyeng'ie intae.

English: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Masaai: Enteleiki ate enchata ai oo murto, enteng'ena ate te nanu, amu kabor nemawuasa to ltau, naa itumutumu intae enkiyeng'iyeng'ata ti atua nkorroki inyi;

English: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Masaai: amu kelelek enchata ai oo murto naa keneneng olola lai.”

English: At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.
Masaai: Ore te ina kata nelo Yesu te nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata aim atua nkurman e nkano, netir esumash ilooiteng'eni lenyena, neitayu enkano aainos.

English: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Ilfarisayo nejoki, “Ng'ura enaasita ilooiteng'eni linono, nemebara te neasi te nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata.”

English: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;
Masaai: Nejoki, “Keitu isomama enataasa apa Daudi o looboitare etotiro esumash?

English: How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?
Masaai: Etijing'a enkaji e Nkai neinos emukate enkitoduaaroto nemeishoruno too nkitanapat meinosa ninye o lelo ooboitare, ilapolosak ake ooinos.

English: Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
Masaai: Ana keitu isomama too nkitanapat inchere kegil ilapolosak le nkaji e Nkai enkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata nemeikeni aajo eisarkionie ninche nemeikoni aajo eitarruoitie ninche?

English: But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.
Masaai: Kake ajoki intae, etii ene entoki kitok alang enkaji e Nkai.

English: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
Masaai: Kake te naa itayioloito eneikununo ele rorei ojo, ‘Olng'ur ayieu mme olasar.’ Naa anaata mipikipiki entioto ilemeeta.

English: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.
Masaai: Amu Olaitoriani le nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata Enkerai e Tung'ani.”

English: And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:
Masaai: Nelo ninye aing'uaa ine alo ajing enkaji e ntumo

English: And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.
Masaai: Netii ine oltung'ani tasat aina. Neikilikuan ninche aajoki, “Inyorriki keishoruno too nkitanapat te nebakishoi te nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata?” Aa kejo taa pee etum aaitang'oro ninye.

English: And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Kalo tung'ani linyi oata enker nabo, naa te nedoiki ina ker engumoto te nkolong e kiyeng'iyeng'ata, nemeibung aitayu?

English: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
Masaai: Kebaa naa elusoo oltung'ani te nker! Te nkaraki e ina keishoruno metaasi mbaa supati te nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata.”

English: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo tung'ani, “Intorioi enkaina ino!” Neitorioo neishiu atiu anaa enkae.

English: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.
Masaai: Kake eipang'a ake Ilfarisayo nepuo aaiguanare aaing'oru eneiko pee ear ninye metua.

English: But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all;
Masaai: Neyiolou Yesu ilo rorei nelo te ine, nesuj iltung'ana kumok neishiunye ninche pooki.

English: And charged them that they should not make him known:
Masaai: Neitanap ajoki, pee melikioo,

English: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
Masaai: ejo pee etum atabai enatejoki te nkutuk o loiboni le Nkai oji Isaya pee ejo,

English: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.
Masaai: “Osinka lai ele, lategelua, olanyor lai, oshipakino oltau lai; naa kapik Enkiyang'et shumata ninye, olaa ninye odung'oki loreren enkiguana;

English: He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.
Masaai: nemeilepilep ninye nemebuakita; nemening'i oltoilo lenye too nkoitoi oo nkaulelie,

English: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
Masaai: nemegil olperesi oilenye, nemear olkilang'ilang'et oiliilari, o manaa neisulie enkiguana.

English: And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.
Masaai: Naa enkarna enye eyooki Loreren aaisilig.”

English: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.
Masaai: Nerikokini ina kata oltung'ani oata oloirirua; naa modooni nemeiro, neishiunye, Yesu ninye neiro nedolishoyu.

English: And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David?
Masaai: Neing'asia olorora pooki nejo, “Keidim ele ataa ninye Enkerai e Daudi?”

English: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Ilfarisayo ina nejo, “Mearaa ele tung'ani iloiriruani mme te ngolon e Beelsebul olkitok loo loiriruani.”

English: And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:
Masaai: Neyiolou ndamunot enye nejoki, “Ore enkitoo pooki naoro ti atua nerruoyo; anaa enkang ake pooki, anaa enkaji naoro aara maate, meitashe.

English: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?
Masaai: Amaa teniaraa Shetani, Shetani, neoro ninye makewan kaji naa eiko enkitoria enye teneitashe.

English: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.
Masaai: Amaa te naa te Beelsebul aaraa nanu iloiriruani, ai ng'ae eararie ninche nkera inyi? Ninche maate ooyooki aairrash intae.

English: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.
Masaai: Kake amaa te naa te Enkiyang'et e Nkai aaraa nanu iloiriruani, enkitoria e Nkai naa naewuo atua intae.

English: Or else how can one enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.
Masaai: “Keidim oltung'ani atijing'a enkaji o ltung'ani ogol neya ntokitin enyena, eitu eng'as aen ilo tung'ani ogol? Pee etum aawa ntokitin e nkaji enye?

English: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.
Masaai: “Ore olemaaning'ore naa olmang'atinta lai ore olemeiturrur te nebo nanu, keisardaikie.

English: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.
Masaai: Enkaraki ena ajoki intae, epalakini ltung'ana ng'ok pooki o emoroto namor Enkai, kake ore emoroto namor Enkiyang'et Sinyati, nemepalakini.

English: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.
Masaai: Ore olomor Enkerai e Tung'ani, kepalakini, kake ore pooki ng'ae omor Enkiyang'et Sinyati, nemepalakini tele porror o to lolporor olotu.

English: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.
Masaai: “Entaa olchani sidai, nesidanu ilng'anayio lenyena, aashu entaa olchani torrono, netorronu lng'anayio lenyena amu too lngayio lenyena eyiolouni olchani.

English: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
Masaai: Naishoi oo lasuriaa, kaji nkoko pee ndimidimi aairoro irorei supati irara intae torrok? Amu inaabore oltau eiro enkutuk.

English: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani supat neitayu supati ti atua olchumati lenye sidai, ore oltung'ani torrono, neitayu ntorrok to lchumati lenye torrono.

English: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
Masaai: “Ajoki naa intae, ore pooki rorei lemeeta tipat oiro iltung'ana, eikenu kenya ake te nkolong e nkiguana.

English: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.
Masaai: Amu to rorei lino kinkenakini isupati, naa to rorei lino kinkenakini ntorrok.”

English: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.
Masaai: Nejoki ilaiteng'enak loo nkitanapat o Lfarisayo, “Olaiteng'enani, kiyieu nikidol olmonekie te iyie.”

English: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, “Eyieu kulo tung'ana lena kata torrok oololoito olmonekie nemeishori, pooki o lmonekie oishori naa olo loiboni le Nkai oji Yona.

English: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
Masaai: Ore anaa apa etii Yona enkoshoke e ntiamasi o sinkirri ndamaritin uni o nkewarieitin uni, neijia sii etiu Enkerai e Tung'ani, kelo aton ndamaritin uni o nkewarieitin uni ti atua enkop.

English: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.
