Masaai: Naa te nebaiki ele rorei nkiyiaa o lbalusui, nikirorie iyiook pee kintung'uaa intae enyamali.”

English: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.
Masaai: Neya ninche impesai neas anaa enatiaakaki. Neibulunyeki ele rorei Ilyahudi o metabaiki taata.

English: Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.
Masaai: Nepuo lekua ooiteng'eni tomon o obo Galilaya o metabaiki oldoinyo otiaaka Yesu enchom.

English: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.
Masaai: Ore pee edol neserem ninye; kake eing'asha kulikae.

English: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
Masaai: Nelotu Yesu enetii neirorie ajoki, “Aaishooki enkidimata pooki te shumata o te nkop.

English: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
Masaai: Enchom entaa loreren pooki ilooiteng'eni laainei, nimbatisasa te nkarna e Papa o ene Nkerai o ene Nkiyang'et Sinyati:

English: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
Masaai: ninteng'ening'ene meibung'a inaitanapa intae pooki; naa ng'ura, atii te nebo intae nkolong'i pooki o metabau enkiting'oto e nkop.”

English: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;
Masaai: Enkiterunoto oo lomon supati le Yesu Kristo Enkerai e Nkai.

English: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
Masaai: Anaa enaigero oloiboni le Nkai oji Isaya pee ejo, “Ng'ura, airriwaa olkilikuai lai dukuya enkomom ino, oitobir enkoitoi ino.

English: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Masaai: Etii oltoilo obuaku ti ong'ata, ‘Entobiraki Olaitoriani enkoitoi, entobiraki irrekiei ooitoriori.’ ”

English: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
Masaai: Neipang'u ti ong'ata Yohana Olaibatisani, nelimu enkibatisa naitoduaaya enkirridunoto nayau empalakinoto oo ng'ok.

English: And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
Masaai: Nepuo enetii ninye iltung'ana le nkop pooki e Yudea, o le Yerusalem, neibatisae ninche to lkeju le Yordan eirridu ng'ok enye.

English: And John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
Masaai: Naa enkila oo lpapit le ntames eishopito Yohana neeta enkimeita e nchoni te mpolos enye, naa lmaat o naishi e ong'ata enya.

English: And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.
Masaai: Nelikioo ninye ejo, “Elotu te siadi nanu ologol laalang nanu olaa kaamakua te nairrugokino alak enkeene e namuke enye.

English: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
Masaai: Aidipa nanu aibatisa intae te nkare kake te Nkiyang'et Sinyati eibatisa ninye intae.”

English: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.
Masaai: Nelotu Yesu te nena olong'i eing'uaa Nasaret e Galilaya neibatisa Yohana ninye te Yordan.

English: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:
Masaai: Ore nabo kata pee eilepu ninye te nkare, nedol pee ebolo shumata nedou Enkiyang'et Sinyati eikununo anaa enturkulu adoiki ninye;

English: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Masaai: nelotu oltoilo oing'uaa shumata ojo, “Ira iyie Oinoti lai lanyor; atishipe te iyie.”

English: And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.
Masaai: Ore nabo kata nereu ninye Enkiyang'et e Nkai ong'ata.

English: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
Masaai: Nebik ti ong'ata nkolong'i artam, etemita shetani; neboitare ng'uesi e ong'ata; neisiaai ilmalaika ninye.

English: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
Masaai: Ore eidipaki aateen Yohana, nelotu Yesu Galilaya, alikioo lomon Supati le Nkai;

English: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
Masaai: ejo, “Etabaua enkata, netinyikua enkitoria e Enkai; erridutu, naa eruko ele rorei supat.”

English: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
Masaai: Ore eshepita enaiposha e Galilaya, nedol Simon o Andrea olalashe le Simon enang'aki orreshet atua enaiposha; amu ilarreshok loo sinkir ninche.

English: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Entusujuaki pee aitaa intae ilarreshok loo ltung'ana.”

English: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.
Masaai: Neing'uaa nabo kata irresheta lenye nesuj ninye.

English: And when he had gone a little farther thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
Masaai: Ore pee enyikaa peno, nedol Yakobo le Sebedayo o Yohana olalashe lenye, etii atua empeut eripita irresheta.

English: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.
Masaai: Neipot nabo kata; neing'uaa Sebedayo menye lenye te mpeut eboitare ilaisiaayiak nesuj ninye.

English: And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.
Masaai: Nepuo aabaya Kapernaum; ore ake pee eaku enkolong e sabato nejing enkaji e ntumo neiteng'enisho.

English: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.
Masaai: Neing'asiae te nkiteng'enare enye, amu eiteng'ena ninye ninche anaa oloitore enajo, nemetiu anaa lasirak.

English: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,
Masaai: Netii te ina kata ake te nkaji enye e ntumo oltung'ani oata oloirirua oiduruk;

English: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
Masaai: nebuaku ajo, “Ainyoo iatayie iyie iyiook, Yesu le Nasaret? Iyewuo aidaikie iyiook? Kaayiolo ajo ira ng'ae, ira iyie ilo Sinyati le Nkai.”

English: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
Masaai: Kake eisikong'a Yesu ninye ajoki, “Tigirayu, tupuku tung'uai ninye!”

English: And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.
Masaai: Nediding'unye oloirirua aiterreyie, nebuaku to ltoilo sapuk, nepuku aing'uaa.

English: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.
Masaai: Neing'asia pooki, o meikilikuanata aajo, “Ainyoo ena? Enkiteng'enare ng'ejuk! Eji keitore te ngolon iloiriruani ooiduruk, nening ninche ninye.”

English: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee.
Masaai: Ore ina kata ake, neibulu olning'o lenye pooki wueji te nene neemanita Galilaya.

English: And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Masaai: Nepuku ake te nkaji e ntumo, nejing enkaji e Simon o Andrea, eboitare Yakobo o Yohana.

English: But Simon's wife's mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.
Masaai: Neirrag enkaputani e Simon emuoi oloirobi, neinosakini te ina kata.

English: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.
Masaai: Nelotu neibung enkaina nedumu, neing'ueiki oloirobi, neinyototo aisiaai ninche.

English: And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.
Masaai: Ore pee eaku teipa, etadoyie enkolong, nerikokini iltamueyia pooki o lelo ooata loiriruani.

English: And all the city was gathered together at the door.
Masaai: Nesotokino enkanasa pooki enkalo e kutuk aji.

English: And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him.
Masaai: Neishiunye ilkumok ooata mueyiaritin oo mpukunot kumok, nearaa iloiriruani kumok; neitu eisho iloiriruani meiroro amu keyiolo ninche ninye.

English: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Masaai: Ore enasirie, te niosowuani, neinyototo ayok alo ewueji neliyio neomon te ine.

English: And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.
Masaai: Neing'oru Simon o lelo ooboitare.

English: And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek for thee.
Masaai: Ore pee etum nejoki, “King'oru ltung'ana pooki.”

English: And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Emaape kunda kulie ang'itie, pee aliki sii ninche, amu ina doi pee aewuo enkop.”

English: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils.
Masaai: Neibulu Galilaya pooki, alikioo ilo rorei too nkajijik enye e ntumo nearaa loiriruani.

English: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
Masaai: Nelotu oltung'ani oata enkeeya oo lbolot esai, negilaki kung ajoki, “Tiniyieu eikindim aishiunye matisikayu.”

English: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
Masaai: Neing'urrie, neitorioo enkaina aiseyie, nejoki, “Ekayieu, tisikayu.”

English: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
Masaai: Neing'uaa enkeeya oo lbolot nabo kata, nesika.

English: And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;
Masaai: Neing'ode areiki nereu nabo kata,

English: And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
Masaai: nejoki, “Toduaa ake miliki likae tung'ani; kake shomo intoduaai kewan to lapolosani; ninchooyo entoki apa naitanapishe Musa te nkisujata, pee intadedeyie to lorere.”

English: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.
Masaai: Kake etupukuo ake neiteru ainosaa, aibalie ilo omoni, neaku eitu eitoki Yesu aidim atijing'a enkang eduaakini, neaku ti ong'ata eton; nepuonu ltung'ana aayiaya eing'uaa nkaloli pooki.

English: And again he entered into Capernaum, after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.
Masaai: Ore pee errinyo, Kapernaum eishari nkuti olong'i, nening'i aajo etii ang.

English: And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.
Masaai: Neiturrurrokino iltung'ana kumok o metaa meetae empaash ebaiki te kutuk aji, einosaki Yesu ninche ilomon.

English: And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.
Masaai: Nepuonunui neyakini oltung'ani tarrush oilenye onapita ltung'ana oong'uan.

English: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
Masaai: Ore pee elau eneimu te nkumoi o lorere, nebol aadede shumata enkaji, ine neipirare. Ore pee eidip aatabol neitadou erruat napetita ilo oilenye.

English: When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu enkirukoto enye, nejoki ilo oilenye, “Enkerai ai, kitapalakaki ng'ok inono.”

English: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
Masaai: Netoni te ine ilasirak nedamisho aajo too ltauja lenye,

English: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?
Masaai: “Ainyoo pee ejo ele tung'ani inji? Eijo kemorisho! Ai ng'ae oidim atapalaki ng'ok, leme Enkai ake?”

English: And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
Masaai: Neyiolou nabo kata Yesu ina to ltau lenye nchere, edamu ninche nena too ltauja lenye, neikilikuan ajoki, “Kaji etiu pee nkilikuanana ate nena too ltauja linyi?

English: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
Masaai: Kaa nalelek, ai te najoki ele oilenye, ‘Kitapalakaki ng'ok inono,’ ana ai te najoki, ‘Inyo, tudumu erruat ino shomo’?

English: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)
Masaai: Kake ore pee itumutumu aatayiolo nchere keeta Enkerai e Tung'ani enkidimata te nkop napalakinye ng'ok.” Nejoki ilo oilenye,

English: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.
Masaai: “Aajoki, inyo, tudumu erruat ino shomo ang.”

English: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.
Masaai: Neinyototo, nedumu nabo kata erruat enye, neipung te dukuya ninche pooki; o meing'asiata pooki neisis Enkai, ejo, “Eitu ai kata kidol embae naaijo ena!”

English: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.
Masaai: Neitoki apuku te ine nelo embata e naiposha, nesotokino olorora pooki ninye neiteng'en ninye ninche.

English: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
Masaai: Ore ina kata eloito nedol Lawi ole Alfayo eton te nkapisi oo mpesai e kodi nejoki, “Tusujuaki.” Neinyototo asuj ninye.

English: And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.
Masaai: Ore eton anya endaa te nkaji enye, netoni lasotok kumok loo mpesai e kodi o looata ng'ok te nebo Yesu o looiteng'eni lenyena; amu ai kumok iloosujita.

English: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?
Masaai: Ore pee edol ilasirak lo Lfarisayo eng'arie ninye endaa looata ng'ok o lasotok le kodi, nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Kaji etiu pee eng'arie ninye ilasotok le kodi o looata ng'ok endaa?”

English: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Yesu, nejoki ninche, “Meyieu ilememuei olabaani, iloomuei ake ooyieu neitu alotu aipot isupati, kake looata ng'ok aewuo aipot.”

English: And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?
Masaai: Neaku enkata naitupukoo ate ilooiteng'eni le Yohana o loo Lfarisayo; nepuonu ltung'ana enetii ninye nejoki, “Kaji etiu pee eitupukoo ate ilooiteng'eni le Yohana o loo Lfarisayo, nemeitupukoo ate ilinono?”

English: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Keitupukoo ate ilchoreta lo loyamishe eton eisiritore? Ore eton eisiritore oloyamishe, nemeidim aaitupukoi ate.

English: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
Masaai: Keyooki aapuonu nkolong'i, naayae oloyamishe aaitung'uaa ninche, neitupukoo taa ate ina olong.

English: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.
Masaai: Meetae oltung'ani oripaki erashe nemenota enkila musana; amu te neripaki, neng'erunye ina ng'ejuk te idia musana, nejarari eng'erata.

English: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.
Masaai: Nemeetae oltung'ani opik enaisho ng'ejuk atua lbenia musan; naa te nepik, nedany ina aisho ilbenia. Ilbenia ng'ejuko ake epiki enaisho ng'ejuk.”

English: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.
Masaai: Ore egira eim inkurman te nkolong e sabato ore epuoito neiteru ilooiteng'eni lenyena aagilu lukuny e nkano.

English: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?
Masaai: Nejoki Ilfarisayo ninye, “Ng'ura, kaji etiu pee easita enemeishoruno too nkitanapat metaasi te nkolong e sabato?”

English: And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Keitu ai kata isomama enataasa Daudi, etanyamala netir esumash, ninye o lelo ooisiritore:

English: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
Masaai: eneikuna pee ejing enkaji e Nkai enapa kata aa Abiatar olapolosani, kitok, nenya emukate enkitoduaaroto nemeishoruno too nkitanapat meinosa likae leme olapolosani, nenya ninye neisho sii lelo ooboitare?”

English: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Eitayioki enkolong e sabato te nkaraki oltung'ani, eitu eitaini oltung'ani te nkaraki enkolong e sabato;

English: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Masaai: netaa enkerai e tung'ani olaitoriani le nkolong e sabato.”

English: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.
Masaai: Neitoki Yesu ajing enkaji e ntumo, netii ine oltung'ani oikaolo enkeeya enkaina.

English: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.
Masaai: Neing'or ninche te naa keishiunye ilo te nkolong e sabato, pee etum aaitang'oro ninye.

English: And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilo tung'ani oikaole enkaina “Wou ene.”

English: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Kaa naishoruno too nkitanapat mataas te nkolong e sabato, metaasi isupati anaa metaasi intorrok, meitopoki ana metaari metua?” Kake etigirate ninche.

English: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
Masaai: Nekurraki ninche pooki nkonyek te ngoro, eisinanuo te nkaraki narook oishuaa, nejoki ilo tung'ani “Intorioi enkaina ino!” Neitorioo, neishiu, enkaina.

English: And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
Masaai: Neipang Ilfarisayo, nepuo nabo kata aainos enkiguana eboitare esirit oo le Herode, pee egilunore ninye eing'oru olosek oarie ninye metua.

English: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,
Masaai: Nerrinyo Yesu te ine te nebo looiteng'eni lenyena aapuo enaiposha, nesuj olorora kitok oing'uaa Galilaya; o looing'uaa Yudea

English: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.
Masaai: o Yerusalem o Ldumea o lido kekun le Yordan o lorora kitok oing'uaa Turo o Sidon; etoning'o nena pooki naataasa, nepuonu enetii ninye.

English: And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena meitobirakini empeut te nkaraki olorere, pee merratanyi ninye;

English: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.
Masaai: amu eidipa aishiunye lkumok, metaa keiding'akino lelo pooki oomueiaa ejo maiseyie.

English: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.
Masaai: Naa ore ake pee emaniki iloiriruani ooiduruk, nerriaa te dukuya ninye ebuaku aajo, “Ira iyie Enkerai e Nkai!”

English: And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.
Masaai: Nekurraki areiki ajoki pee melikioo.

English: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
Masaai: Neilepaki ninye oldoinyo, neipotu lelo ooyieu ninye openy nepuonu enetii ninye.

English: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
Masaai: Negelu tomon o aare, ooisiritore ninye, pee etum airriwai metolikioi ororei le Nkai;

English: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
Masaai: neaku eeta enkitoria naararie iloiriruani;

English: And Simon he surnamed Peter;
Masaai: Neisho Simon enkarna ajo Petero;

English: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
Masaai: Yakobo le Sebedayo, o Yohana olalashe Yakobo, neisho lelo enkarna ajo Boanerge, aa keji Ilenkikurrukur:

English: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
Masaai: Andrea, o Filipo, o Bartolomayo, o Matayo, o Tomas, o Yakobo le Alfayo o Tadayo, o Simon olkanaani,

English: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Masaai: o Yudas Iskariot, laa ninye otakaldayie. Nelo ang.

English: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
Masaai: Neitoki ake esiamo aasoto, metaa metumoki ninche aainosa endaa.

English: And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.
Masaai: Ore pee ening iltung'ana lenyena le sotua, nepuo pee epuo aaibung, amu kejo, “Etarruoyie elukunya.”

English: And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.
Masaai: Nejo laiteng'enak loo nkitanapat ootadoutuo eing'uaa Yerusalem, “Beelsebul eeta, naa oloitore loiriruani eararie loiriruani.”

English: And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
Masaai: Neipotu enetii ninye, nejoki too nkitanyaanyukot, “Kaji eiko pee eidim shetani ataarai shetani?

English: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
Masaai: Te neoro enkitoria ti atua, nemeidim ina kitoria aitasho.

English: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
Masaai: Naa te neoro enkaji ti atua kewan, nemeidim ina aji aitasho.

English: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.
Masaai: Naa te netudumakine shetani kewan aoro, meitashe, kake keiting.

English: No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.
Masaai: Meetae oltung'ani oidim atijing'a enkaji o ltung'ani ogol nearaa masaa enyena, eitu eng'as aen ilo ogol, pee etumoki taa ataara enkaji enye.

English: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
Masaai: Esipa ajoki intae, epalakini ltung'ana ng'ok pooki, o emorore pooki namorisho ake;

English: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:
Masaai: kake ore oloba anaa olomor Enkiyang'et sinyati, meeta empalakinoto aikata, kake etaa eng'oki ntarasi.”

English: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
Masaai: Amu ketejo ninche, “Oloirirua oiduruk eeta ninye.”

English: There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him.
Masaai: Nelotu ng'otonye o lalashera lenyena; ore eeitashe ninche te boo neirriwaa enkutuk meipoti.

English: And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.
Masaai: Netoni esiamo aamanita ninye; nejokini, “Etii ng'utunyi o lalashera linono boo kinkilikuanu.”

English: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, “Ai ng'ae yieyio o lalashera laainei?”

English: And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!
Masaai: Ore pee eitaman inkonyek lelo oomanita ninye, nejo, “Noolo yieyio o lalashera laainei!

English: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae oas enayieu Enkai, ninye olalashe lai, o enkanashe ai o yieyio.”

English: And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.
Masaai: Neitoki aiteru aiteng'enisho te mbata e naiposha. Neiturrurrokino olorora kitok oleng, o metijing'a atua empeut aton ti atua te naiposha; neton ilo orora te nkop natoyio te mbata e naiposha.

English: And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,
Masaai: Neutaki ninche mbaa kumok too nkitanyaanyukot nejoki,

English: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:
Masaai: “Entoning! Ng'ura, eshomo olaunoni aunisho.

English: And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.
Masaai: Ore eunisho nedoiki kulikae anterera embata e nkoitoi, nepuonu ntaritik aanya.

English: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae enkop oo soito nemetii nkulupuok kumok, nesioki aabulu, naa ore ake pee ebulu amu megut nkulupuok;

English: But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
Masaai: ore pee eilepu enkolong nepej, naa ore amu meeta ntana netoyu.

English: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae anterera atua lkiku nebulu lelo kiku negor, metaa eitu eiu ilng'anayio.

English: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae anterera atua nkulupuok sidain nebulu neiu ilng'anayio, neponari aaiu maa tomoni uni, maa ntomoni ile, maa iip.”

English: And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Nejo, “Oloata nkiyiaa naaning'ishore, toning'o.”

English: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable.
Masaai: Ore etaa ninye ake, neikilikuan lelo ooboitare te nebo ilooiteng'eni lenyena enajo nena kitanyaanyukot.

English: And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:
Masaai: Nejoki, “Eishooki intae entayiolo mbaa nemeibala e nkitoria e Nkai, kake ore te lelo ootii auluo, etiu mbaa pooki anaa nkitanyaanyukot;

English: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.
Masaai: pee te neing'or, neing'or nemedol, naa te nening, nening nemejing'aa, pee meibelekenyakino ake Enkai, nepalakini.”

English: And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Aimining'ung'u ena kitanyaanyukoto? Kaji naa inkoko pee ining'ung'u nkulie kitanyaanyukot pooki?

English: The sower soweth the word.
Masaai: “Ore olaunoni, ororei eun.

English: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
Masaai: Naa kulo ilootii embata e nkoitoi, ine neunieki ororei; ore pee ening; nelotu shetani nabo kata aya ilo rorei otuunoki ti atua ninche.

English: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;
Masaai: Naa inji etiu lelo ootuunoki te nkop oo soito, lelo laa, ore pee ening ororei, neng'amu nabo kata te ng'ida;

English: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.
Masaai: nemeeta ntana ti atua ate, kake ebikie enkiti kata; kake ore pee elotu osina anaa enkisilisilore te nkaraki ilo rorei, nerrorro nabo kata.

English: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,
Masaai: Ore lelo ootunokoki atua lkiku; naa lelo ooning ilo rorei,

English: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.
Masaai: kake ore pee ejing'aki nyamalitin e nkop, o eng'ida oo masaa, o eng'uarrata e kulie tokitin, negor ilo rorei, metaa meisho etum ilng'anayio.

English: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.
Masaai: Kake ore lelo ootuunokoki enkulupuoni sidai, naa lelo ooning ilo rorei neiruk nepik iltauja neiu ilng'anayio maa tomoniuni, maa ntomoni ile, maa iip.”

English: And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Keyauni oltaa nepising'ari to ltoo, aashu epiki orunku le erruat? Mme eneiperere epiki?

English: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.
Masaai: Amu meetae entoki naisudoyioki neme keji ake pee eibalunyeki; nemeetae entoki natunukaki neme keji ake pee eibalayu.

English: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Oloata nkiyiaa naaning'ishore, toning'o.”

English: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Eng'urai ena nining'itoto; amu ore emborei ninchooyo iyie naa ninye kinchori sii iyie, nikiponikini.

English: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.
Masaai: Amu keponikini ilo oata aaisho kulie; ore ilo lemeeta, neoruni ina naata.”

English: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Etiu enkitoria e Nkai anaa te neisuaaki oltung'ani lanterera enkop.

English: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.
Masaai: Neirura neinyototo dama o kewarie, nerumishoyu lanterera nebulu, nemeyiolo ninye eneikununye.

English: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
Masaai: Enkop naitubulu openy, neng'asunye mbenek, neitoki ntapuka neitoki lanterera aajing elukunya.

English: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
Masaai: Kake ore pee eku lanterera, neitayu oltung'ani olalem adung'u amu etabawua enkisampuare.”

English: And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?
Masaai: Nejo ninye, “Ainyoo kintanyaanyukie enkitoria e Nkai anaa kaa kitanyaanyukoto kiaasishore te ninye?

English: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:
Masaai: Etiu anaa empeu e karadali, enaa ore euni te nkop, ninye enkini aisul ilanterera le nkop;

English: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.
Masaai: kake ore pee euni nebulu, aisul inkeek e ntim, neitayu lng'osil, o metaa kepuonu ntaritik e shumata aapik sinkin oloip lenye.”

English: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.
Masaai: Neinosaki ilo rorei aiko neijia too nkitanyaanyukot kumok, anaa enaidima ninche aatoning;

English: But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.
Masaai: neitu eirorie metii enkitanyaanyukoto, kake ore pee eaku ninye ake o looiteng'eni lenyena neibalakinye ninche pooki toki.

English: And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.
Masaai: Ore ina olong pee eaku teipa, nejoki ninye ninche, “Ematalang aapuo lido kekun.”

English: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.
Masaai: Neing'uaa olorere nerik ninche ninye, etiu anaa duoo ake, te ina peut. Netii kulie peuti ine te nebo ninye.

English: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
Masaai: Nedumunye olkutati kitok, nedam ilopir le nkare ina peut, o metaa keiput enkare.

English: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
Masaai: Kake etii ninye siadi empeut, eirura epetita enkirishet e lukunya; neinyeyie ninche ninye nejoki, “Olaiteng'enani, ai mme toki te iyie te nikindaaya?”

English: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
Masaai: Neinyototo nebuaaki osiwuo, nejoki enaiposha, “Tigirayu! Ntirring'ayu.” Neish osiwuo, negira enkare oleng.

English: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Ainyoo pee itureishote?”

English: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
Masaai: Neiputukuny ninche, nejokino, “Ai ng'ae doi ele? Olaa kening ninye osiwuo o enaiposha?”

English: And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
Masaai: Nebaiki ninche olikae kekun le naiposha, nebaiki enkop oo Lgerasene.

English: And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
Masaai: Ore pee edou te mpeut, nenang'are nabo kata oltung'ani otamanya nkuraren, eeta oloirirua oiduruk:

English: Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:
Masaai: nemeetae oltung'ani oidima ateena ninye too lpisia.

English: Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
Masaai: Amu eteenaki katitin kumok too lgoteta; nemeeta hoo obo oidimua aitoborro.

English: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
Masaai: Naa kebuakita ake dama o kewarie too nkuraren o to o ldoinyo, near kewan too soito.

English: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu te nelakua, nekuet aserem ninye.

English: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
Masaai: Nebuaku to ltoilo sapuk, ejo, “Ainyoo kiatayie nanu, Yesu, Enkerai e Enkai natii Shumata Aisul? Aatasayia te Nkai, mikisilisil.”

English: For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.
Masaai: Amu ketiaaka, “Tupuku tung'uai ilo tung'ani, lo oirirua oiduruk!”

English: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
Masaai: Neikilikuan Yesu ajoki, “Aikiji ng'ae?” Newaliki ajoki, “Kaaji empuoto; amu aikira kumok.”

English: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
Masaai: Nesai ninche ninye oleng pee mearaa teina kop.

English: Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.
Masaai: Netii eluaata oo lbitiro nadaa te ine te mbata o ldoinyo;

English: And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.
Masaai: nesai iloiriruani Yesu aajoki, “Irriwai iyiook maape aajing kuldo bitiro, nchoo iyiook matijing.”

English: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.
Masaai: Neisho ninche meshomo. Nepuku lelo oiriruani ooiduruk nejing lelo bitiro; ore ina luaata, nabaya nkalifuni are, neipirri aadoyio to loshong'ishong'i nengorokino enaiposha, neimis te naiposha.

English: And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
Masaai: Neisik ilchekuti lenye, nepuo aalikioo te ina anasa o te ina kop. Nepuonu ltung'ana aadol enatotiwuo.

English: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
Masaai: Nepuonu enetii Yesu, nedol oladuoo oata oloirrirua eton te ine, eishopo naa biyoto enkorrok enye, oladuoo otang'asa aata empuoto loo loiriruani: neureishoyu ninche.

English: And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootoduaa ina nelikioo nena naatotiutuo te ilo apa otang'asa aata iloiriruani o too lbitiro.

English: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
Masaai: Neiteru aaomon Yesu metung'uai ina latia enye.

English: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.
Masaai: Ore ejing'ita empeut, neomon ilo apa otang'asa aata iloiriruani eji pee eisiritore.

English: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
Masaai: Kake etanya Yesu nejoki, “Shomo ang enetii ilchoreta linono, toliki ninche eneba enikintaasa Olaitoriani, o eneikuna pee king'urrie.”

English: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.
Masaai: Nelo neiteru alikioo te Dekapoli nena naaitaasa Yesu ninye; neing'asia ltung'ana pooki.

English: And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.
Masaai: Ore pee eitoki Yesu alang'aki olikae kekun, neiturrurrokino olorora kitok; etii ninye embata e naiposha.

English: And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,
Masaai: Nelotu ina kata obo le lelo ooitore enkaji e ntumo, oji enkarna Yairo; ore pee edol ninye, nebatata too nkejek enyena.

English: And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.
Masaai: Nesai, ajoki, “Etaa keye entito ai kiti. Wou inteleiki nkaik, pee eishiu, nepok.”

English: And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.
Masaai: Neiriamariyie ninye. Nesuj esiamo kitok, neiding'akino.

English: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,
Masaai: Netii enkitok naturuke larin tomon o aare,

English: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
Masaai: netanyamala oleng eruk ilabaak kumok, netumuta ntokitin pooki apa naata, nepal enaikashu, neponari arrishu.

English: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.
Masaai: Netoning'o eimakini Yesu, neimu te siadi ti atua olorere neiseyie olkila lenye.

English: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.
Masaai: Amu etejo, “Te naiseyie ninye olkila lenye, naishiu.”

English: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.
Masaai: Negem nabo kata erukoto enye, nening to sesen lenye nchere eishiunyeki emueyian enye.

English: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?
Masaai: Ore Yesu, etayiolo ajo Eshomo engolon aing'uaa ninye, neibelekenya nabo kata ti atua olorere, nejo, “Ai ng'ae naaiseyie lkilani laainei?”

English: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Idolita esiamo kinding'akino, nintoki ajo, ‘Ai ng'ae laaiseyie?’ ”

English: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
Masaai: Neing'orisho ninye pee edol olotaasa ina.

English: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
Masaai: Kake eishoo ina kitok pee edol enaitaasaki, nelotu te nkuretisho eikirikira, nebatata te dukuya ninye, neliki sipat pooki.

English: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Na kerai, kinchiunye enkirukoto ino; shomo te seriani, ninchiu emuoyian ino.”

English: While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?
Masaai: Ore eton eirorita, nepuonu ilooing'uaa enkaji e ilo oitore enkaji e ntumo nejo, “Etua entito ino. Oo pee intoki aitanyamal Olaiteng'enani?”

English: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
Masaai: Kake eitu eshilaa Yesu ina natejoki, nejoki oloitore enkaji e ntumo, “Miureishoyu, iruko ake iyie.”

English: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
Masaai: Neitu eisho likae tung'ani metusuja ninye leme Petero ake o Yakobo o Yohana olalashe Yakobo.

English: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
Masaai: Ore pee abaiki ninche enkaji e ilo oitore enkaji e ntumo, nedol olorere o ltung'ana ooishirita oobuaku aaishir oleng.

English: And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.
Masaai: Ore pee ejing atua, nejoki ninche, “Ainyoo pee nchirishiri aabuakita? Eitu eye enkerai keirura.”

English: And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.
Masaai: Nekueniyie ninche ninye. Kake eitupukuo ninye lelo pooki boo, nerik menye enkerai o ng'otonye o lelo ooiriamunore, nejing ine netii enkerai.

English: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
Masaai: Neibung enkaina nejoki, “Talita kumi;” eji, “Entito kinyi, aajoki inyo.”

English: And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.
Masaai: Neinyototo nabo kata entito aitashe nelo, amu enoo larin tomon o aare embotoro enye. Ore nabo kata nenum ninche enking'asia.

English: And he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.
Masaai: Nereiki aitore ajoki meliki hoo likae tung'ani ena bae nejoki ninche meishoo ninye endaa nanya.

English: And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.
Masaai: Neing'uaa ine nelotu enkop enye; nesuju ilooiteng'eni lenyena.

English: And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e sabato neiteru aiteng'enisho te nkaji e ntumo; ore ilkumok ootoning'o ninye neing'asia, ejo, “Kaji enotie ele tung'ani kuna pooki. Kaa ng'eno eishooki ninye? Ebaa kuna baa e nking'asia naas inkaik enyena!

English: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
Masaai: Mme olaguetani loo nkeek doi ele, olayioni le Mariamu, naa olalashe Yakobo o Yosef Yudas o Simon, naa ai metii nkanashera enyena atua iyiook?” Nerikare ninye.

English: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Melaikini oloiboni le Nkai enkanyit mme te nkop enye, o ti atua enkaji enye.”

English: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
Masaai: Nelaikino ataasa inenking'asia te ine; ilkuti tung'ana ake oomuei eiteleikia nkaik neishiunye.

English: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
Masaai: Neing'asia ninye te nkaraki nemeeta ninche enkirukoto. Nemanaa too nkang'itie eiteng'enisho.

English: And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;
Masaai: Neipotu ninye lelo tomon o aare, neisho meitoria iloiriruani torrok.

English: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
Masaai: Neitanap ajoki, “Emishoroo toki te lototo inyi, eng'udi ake; naa emiya mukateni, aashu olbene, aashu mpesai too nkimeitani inyi.

English: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
Masaai: Enchopoi inamuka kake eminchopoo lkilani maa are.”

English: And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Ore ake enkaji nijing'ijing'i, entotoni te ine o entung'uai ine wueji.

English: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
Masaai: Naa te neitu eng'amu intae dikae wueji, nemening intae, ore ipuopuo, empiripiroi enterit niaatata too nkejek inyi metaa shakeni te ninche.”

English: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.
Masaai: Nepuo aalikioo nchere keishiaakino neirridu ltung'ana.

English: And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.
Masaai: Nearaa ninche iloiriruani kumok, neelie eilata iltamueyia kumok neishiunye.

English: And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.
Masaai: Nening olaiguanani oji Herode ina; amu etayioloki enkarna e Yesu. Nejo kulikae, “Eitopiwuoki Yohana Olaibatisani too lootuata; ina pee easisho ena golon ti atua ninye.”

English: Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
Masaai: Nejo kulikae, “Eliya doi.” Nejo sii kulikae, “Oloiboni le Nkai otiu anaa loibonok le Nkai li apa.”

English: But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.
Masaai: Kake ore pee ening Herode nejo, “Yohana, olapa latudung'oyie elukunya eitopiwuoki.”

English: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife: for he had married her.
Masaai: Amu eirriwayie Herode ltung'ana meibung'i Yohana, neen apik korokoroni te nkaraki Herodias, enkitok o lalashe lenye oji Filipo amu eyama apa ninye.

English: For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife.
Masaai: Amu etiaaka Yohana Herode, “Mikinchoro too nkitanapat iyama enkitok o lalashe lino.”

English: Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:
Masaai: Neilap Herodias ninye neaku keyieu near metua. Kake etalaikine,

English: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
Masaai: amu keure Herode Yohana, eyiolo ajo oltung'ani supat naa sinyati, nerrip eserian. Ore pee elo neinining nemilo; eji neng'ida sii te nening.

English: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;
Masaai: Kake eewuo erishata to lkekun otoinieki Herode neitoomonisho ninye neipot ilkituaak lenyena o ltung'ana arikok le Galilaya.

English: And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu entito e Herodias aranyaki, neitiship Herode o lomon lenyena; nejoki olaiguanani ina tito, “Toomonoki entoki ake pooki niyieu, naa kaaisho.”

English: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
Masaai: Neinosaki olmumai ajo, “Ore entoki ake pooki nikiomon, kaaisho o te naa ematua e nkop naitore.”

English: And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
Masaai: Neipung nelo ajoki ng'otonye, “Ainyoo aomonu?” Nejoki, “Elukunya e Yohana Olaibatisani.”

English: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
Masaai: Nejing'u nabo kata asieku enetii olaiguanani, neomon ejo, “Ayieu nikincho nabo kata elukunya e Yohana Olaibatisani te mbesen.”

English: And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath's sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
Masaai: Neisinanuo naleng olaiguanani; kake ore te nkaraki lmuma lenyena o lelo omon lenyena neaku, meyieu nedot ina natiaaka.

English: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
Masaai: Neirriwaa olaiguanani nabo kata osikari le rripore, neitanap ninye meyau elukunya e Yohana. Nelo ilo nedung'u elukunya te korokoroni,

English: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
Masaai: neyau ina lukunya te mbesen, neisho ina tito; neisho entito ng'otonye.

English: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
Masaai: Ore pee ening ilooiteng'eni lenyena, nepuonu aaya osesen lenye, neirragie te nkurare.

English: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
Masaai: Nerrinyunye ilkipaareta enetii Yesu, neliki ninye nena pooki naataasa o naaitengenishote.

English: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Wootu oopeny emaape eneliyio, eyeng'iyeng'ata enkiti kata.” Amu aikumok iloopuonu epuo, neaku meeta ninye erishata nainosie endaa.

English: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.
Masaai: Nepuo te mpeut ewueji neliyio aa ninche ake oopeny.

English: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.
Masaai: Netoduaaitie ltung'ana kumok, neyiolou, neipirri aapuo too nkejek ine eing'uaa nena ang'itie pooki, neng'asie ine wueji.

English: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
Masaai: Ore pee edou te mpeut nedol olorora kitok, neing'urrie ninche, amu etiu anaa ntare nemeeta olchekut; neiteru aiteng'en mbaa kumok.

English: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:
Masaai: Ore pee emutu, nepuonu ilooiteng'eni lenyena enetii nejoki, “Keliyio ene wueji, nemuto;

English: Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.
Masaai: intanapa ninche, meshomo nkurman o kuna ang'itie naamanita ene aainyang'aki ate entoki nanya.”

English: He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?
Masaai: Kake etawalikia ninye ajoki ninche, “Enchoo intae ninche entoki nanya.” Nejoki ninche ninye. “Aikipuo aainyiang'u mukateni oo ndinarii iip are, pee kincho meinosa?”

English: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Kaja mukateni niatata intae? enchom eng'urai.” Ore pee eing'oraa neyiolou, nejoki, “Imiet o sinkir aare.”

English: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
Masaai: Neitanap meitotona olorere too nkujit naanyori, anaa ltimito.

English: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.
Masaai: Netoni aaitayu ltimito maa iip, anaa onom.

English: And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
Masaai: Ore pee edumu Yesu nena mukateni imiet o sinkir aare neraposhu nkonyek aing'or shumata, nemayian, nebel imukateni neisho ilooiteng'eni lenyena meishoo lelo tung'ana; neoriki lelo sinkir aare ninche pooki.

English: And they did all eat, and were filled.
Masaai: Nenya pooki neraposho.

English: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
Masaai: Nesotu mbelat naatelekuaki o noo sinkir sii neiput nkikapuni tomon o aare.

English: And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.
Masaai: Ore lelo ooinosa nena mukateni nera nkalifuni imiet ilewa.

English: And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena nabo kata meshomo nejing empeut neituruk aapuo lido kekun, aapuo Betsaida eitanapare ninye esiamo.

English: And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.
Masaai: Ore pee eorore, nelo aomon te nena doinyo.

English: And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.
Masaai: Ore etaa teipa, eidipa empeut ashomo empolos e naiposha, netii ninye openy enkop natoyio.

English: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
Masaai: Nedol ajo keekenya earare enkurtoroto e mpeut amu kenang'are osiwuo ninche. Ore te rripore e ong'uan e nkewarie nelotu enetii ninche, elo eporito enkare. Neyieu negiroo.

English: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:
Masaai: Kake etoduaa ninche ninye elo te shumata e nkare nejo ke nkukuu, nebuaku aaishir;

English: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.
Masaai: amu etoduaa pooki ninye, neiputukuny. Kake eirorie nabo kata nejoki, “Entagoluoto, nanu doi, emiureisho.”

English: And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
Masaai: Nejing ninye atua empeut te nebo ninche negira osiwuo. Neirriang pooki,

English: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.
Masaai: amu eitu ejing'aa enapa kias oo mukateni, kake etagolo iltauja lenye.

English: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
Masaai: Ore pee elang ninche lido kekun, nepuonu enkop e Genesaret, neen empeut te mbata e naiposha.

English: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
Masaai: Ore pee epuku te mpeut neyiolou iltung'ana ninye te ina kata ake.

English: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.
Masaai: Nekuet aaman ina kop pooki, neiteru aariku ltung'ana pooki oomuei too rruatin enye aaya ewueji ake pooki nening'oki aajo etii.

English: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.
Masaai: Neaku ore pooki wueji nelo, too nkang'itie, too nkanas kituaak, o te ina kop, nerikokini iloomueyiaa aairragie too wuejitin neemirishoreki, nesai Yesu meisho eiseyie ninye olcholoi lo lkila lenye; ore lelo pooki ooiseyie neishiunyeki.

English: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee eiturrurrokino Ilfarisayo enetii Yesu, eboitare ninche ematua oo lasirak, ooetuo eing'uaa Yerusalem,

English: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
Masaai: nedol aajo keinos kulikae ooiteng'eni lenyena endaa eiduruk inkaik, eji meisuja.

English: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.
Masaai: (Amu ore Lfarisayo, naa neijia etiu Ilyahudi pooki, menya endaa eitu eisuj inkaik enye, pee eitabaya nkoon oo lpayiani.

English: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
Masaai: Naa te nepuonu eing'uaa ineemirishoreki; menya endaa eitu eng'as aaisuj ate. Naa keeta kulie koon naaitabaya ninche, anaa enkisujata oo nkikompeni o motioo o ntokitin oo suyan.)

English: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?
Masaai: Neikilikuan Ilfarisayo o lasirak aajoki, “Ainyoo pee mesuj ilooiteng'eni linono nkoon oo lpayiani metaa kenya endaa too nkaik naaiduruk.”

English: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Esipa enotoko Isaya pee eibonisho ajo ti alo intae isunkuro, anaa enaigero, ‘Too nkutukie ake, aayanyit, kulo tung'ana, kake kaalakuaniki ltauja lenye nanu,

English: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
Masaai: naa pesho aaserem nanu, aa nkoon oo ltung'ana eiteng'enare.

English: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
Masaai: Itapalaitie intae inkitanapat e Nkai, nikurrakiki aaibung inkoon oo ltung'ana.’ ”

English: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Inotito intae olosek lianyienyie nkitanapat e Nkai, pee itumutumu aaitabai nkoon inyi.

English: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
Masaai: Amu etejo, Musa ‘Iyanyita minyi o ng'utunyi,’ nejo sii, ‘Ore olomor menye anaa ng'otonye, neiririkino keeya.’

English: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.
Masaai: Kake nijojo intae, ‘Te nejoki oltung'ani menye aashu ng'otonye, Ore entoki duoo nikitumie nanu etaa korban (aa taa enaishori Enkai)

English: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
Masaai: nimintokiki aaisho ilo meitaasa menye anaa ng'otonye toki.’

English: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
Masaai: Ore te ina nintaa pesho ororei le Nkai te nena koon inyi nintarasakinono. Niasiasa doi kulie kumok neeijo nena.”

English: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:
Masaai: Neitoki aipotu olorere nejoki, “Entoning'oki intae pooki, naa enchoo ejing'aa intae.

English: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
Masaai: Meetae entoki e oriong oltung'ani naa te nejing ade atua neidim aisarkionie ninye; kake mbaa naapuku ti atua oltung'ani naaitaa ninye torrono.

English: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Te neeta oltung'ani nkiyiaa naaning'ishore toning'o.”

English: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
Masaai: Ore pee ejing aji, neing'uaa olorere, neikilikuan ilooiteng'eni lenyena enajo ina kitanyaanyukoto.

English: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Aimejing'aa sii ninche intae? Aimidolidolo aajo ore pooki toki natii oriong oltung'ani, te nejing nemeidim aitarruoi;

English: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
Masaai: amu te nejing, mme oltau lenye ejing kake enkoshoke, neipung ade ake?” (Ore pee ejo neijia neitisiny indaiki pooki.)

English: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
Masaai: Nejo, “Ore inaapuku ti atua oltung'ani, ninche naaitarruoo oltung'ani.

English: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Masaai: Amu atua oltung'ani eing'uaa indamunot torrok, enkiborra oo nkonyek, empurrorre, earata metua, eloloito,

English: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:
Masaai: ng'uarrat torrok, enkarrueisho, olosek torrono, enkipororonkos, olom, esulare, olwuasa, emodai.

English: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
Masaai: Atua oltung'ani eing'uaa kuna torrok pooki, naa kuna naaisarkionie oltung'ani.”

English: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
Masaai: Ore pee epuku te ine nelo olkirine le Turo o Sidon. Nejing enkaji nabo, nemeyieu neyiolouni aajo etii ine; kake etalaikinoteki aaisudoi.

English: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
Masaai: Kake ore nabo kata netii enkitok, naibung'a entito enye kiti oloirirua oiduruk, nening ajo etii ine, nelotu, nebatata too nkejek enyena aserem.

English: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
Masaai: Ore ina kitok naa enoo Lyunani, o losho le Sirofoinike te inoto. Neomon metaarai oloirirua te ina tito enye.

English: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ina kitok, “Inchoo eng'asi aaitoti nkera, amu meishiaakino teneyae mukateni oo nkera aanang'aki ldiein.”

English: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs.
Masaai: Kake etawalikia ninye nejoki, “Ee itisipa lo kitok; kake ore sii ninche ndiein naalutoo emisa nesotu rrarrat ooitadoyio nkera.”

English: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Ore te nkaraki ina nitejo, shomo ang; etung'uayie oloirirua entito ino.”

English: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
Masaai: Nelo ang, neinepu enkerai eirrag te rruat, neshomo oloirirua.

English: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
Masaai: Nerrinyunye Yesu aing'uaa ilo kirine le Turo, neimaa Sidon alo enkalo e naiposha e Galilaya, nepolos aimaa atua Dekapoli.

English: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
Masaai: Nerikokini oltung'ani ming'ani laa penyo sii neiro, nesai meiteleiki enkaina.

English: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;
Masaai: Nerik aitung'uaa atua olorere arik aa ninye ake openy, nepik ilkimojik nkiyiaa enyena, nenotu nkamulak neiseyie olng'ejep lenye;

English: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
Masaai: neing'or shumata, neitadoiyie oltau, nejoki ninye, “Efafata,” nchere, “Taboloyu.”

English: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
Masaai: Nebolo nkiyiaa enyena, nelaa eneta o lng'ejep lenye, neiro aitobiraki.

English: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;
Masaai: Neitanap pee meliki likae tung'ani; kake ore anaa pee eitanap ajoki melikioo, neitulus ninye eitadaraa ina.

English: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
Masaai: Nelus enking'asia enye neaku keji, “Etaasa mbaa pooki aitobiraki ore ninye ilming'anta o lemeiro, neidimie aisho meiroro.”

English: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,
Masaai: Ore te nena olong'i, enyaaka olorora kitok asoto, nemeeta entoki nanya, neipotu ilooiteng'eni lenyena nejoki ninche,

English: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
Masaai: “Kaata olng'ur te le orere, amu nkolong'i uni taata aaisiritore nanu nemeeta entoki nanya.

English: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.
Masaai: Naa te najoki meshomo nkang'itie enye, neiterriaa te nkoitoi; neetuo kulikae eing'uaa enelakua.”

English: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?
Masaai: Newaliki ilooiteng'eni lenyena aajoki, “Kaji eiko oltung'ani te neitoti kulo tung'ana too mukateni te ne ti ong'ata?”

English: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
Masaai: Neikilikuan ajoki, “Kaja mukateni niatata intae?” Nejoki, “Naapishana.”

English: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.
Masaai: Neitanapisho metotona ltung'ana te nkop, nedumu nena mukateni naapishana, ore pee eishooyo enashe nebelibel neisho ilooiteng'eni lenyena meitarasaki olorere. Neitarasaki ninche ilo orora.

English: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.
Masaai: Neeta sii lkuti sinkir ooti. Ore pee emayian, neitanapisho meitarasari sii ninche lelo aaisho olorere.

English: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.
Masaai: Nenya, neraposho. Nesotuni lmong'oishi ootelekutua, nkikapuni naapishana naabore.

English: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
Masaai: Nebaya lelo tung'ana nkalifuni ong'uan.

English: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
Masaai: Neitanap meshomo ang; nejing ninye nabo kata atua empeut te nebo ilooiteng'eni lenyena, nepuo enkalo o Dalmanuta.

English: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
Masaai: Nepuonu Ilfarisayo aaishankarrarre ninye, aayie olmonekei oing'uaa keper aatem.

English: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
Masaai: Neitadoiyio oltau te nguton, nejo, “Ainyoo pee eing'oru kulo tung'ana le na kata olmonekie oing'uaa shumata? Esipa, ajoki intae, meetae hoo olmonekie oishori ltung'ana le na kata.”

English: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.
Masaai: Neing'uaa Yesu ninche, neitoki ajing empeut nelo olikae kekun.

English: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.
Masaai: Netorikine ninche eitu eyau mukateni; neaku emukate nabo ake eeta tiatua empeut.

English: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.
Masaai: Neitanap Yesu ninche ajoki, “Entorrip ate te nkisuijo oo Lfarisayo o te nkisuijo e Herode.”

English: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.
Masaai: Neiguana maate ejo, “Mukateni mikiaata.”

English: And when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?
Masaai: Neyiolou Yesu ina, nejoki ninche, “Ainyoo pee ijokinono eji miatata mukateni? Keton ake mejing'aa intae naa aimining'ung'u? Kaji etiu pee egol intae ilukuny?

English: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
Masaai: Aimidolidolo niatata nkonyek? Niatata nkiyiaa aimining'ishosho? Aimidamumu?

English: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.
Masaai: Amaa pee abel imukateni imiet abelaki ltung'ana nkalifuni imiet, kaja nkikapuni oo lmong'oishi oobore litasotutuo?” Nejoki, “Tomon o aare.”

English: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
Masaai: “Oo napa naapishana natebelaka nkalifuni ong'uan: kaja nkikapuni naabore oo lmong'oishi litasotutuo?” Nejoki, ‘Naapishana.”

English: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Neton ake intae mining'ung'u?”

English: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.
Masaai: Nepuonu Betsaida. Nerikokini olmodooni, aaomon meiseyie.

English: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.
Masaai: Nerik ilo modooni aibung enkaina, neipung'ie te ina ang. Ore pee enotaki nkonyek enyena, neiteleiki nkaik, neikilikuan ajoki, “Idol toki?”

English: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
Masaai: Neshumu nkonyek nejo, “Kadol iltung'ana; kake etiu anaa lkeek, epuoito.”

English: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
Masaai: Neitoki ake Yesu aiteleiki nkonyek enyena nkaik, neing'orisho ninye oleng neishiu, nedolishoyu abaraki,

English: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.
Masaai: Neisho elo ang, nejoki, “Nimirrinyo ake ajing ena ang.”

English: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
Masaai: Nelo Yesu o looiteng'eni lenyena, nkang'itie e Kaisarii e Filipi. Ore epuo te nkoitoi neikilikuan Yesu ilooiteng'eni lenyena ajoki, “Kejo iltung'ana kara nanu ng'ae?”

English: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “Yohana Olaibatisani, nejo kulikae, Eliya; nejo sii kulikae ira obo loo lapa oibonok le Nkai.”

English: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
Masaai: Neikilikuan ajoki, “Kake amaa intae, nijojo kara ng'ae?” Newaliki Petero ajoki, “Ira iyie Kristo.”

English: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
Masaai: Neitanap ninche pee meliki likae tung'ani.

English: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
Masaai: Neiteru aiteng'en ajoki meeta nchere pee meisilisili Enkerai e Tung'ani too mbaa kumok neanyi ilpayiani o lapolosak kituaak o lasirak, neari metua, ore pee elusoo nkolong'i uni neitoki apiu.

English: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
Masaai: Nelimu ina aibalunye. Nerik Petero ninye neiteru aikok.

English: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
Masaai: Kake eibelekenye Yesu ore pee edol ilooiteng'eni lenyena, neing'ode Petero, nejoki, “Shomo kurum ai shetani! Amu mitii iyie enkalo e Nkai, kake enoo ltung'ana itii.”

English: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
Masaai: Neipotu olorere te nebo ilooiteng'eni lenyena meetu enetii ninye, nejoki ninche, “Te neyieu oltung'ani naasuj nanu, nchoo metanya inaayieu oltau lenye, nedumu osalaba lenye naasuj nanu.

English: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's, the same shall save it.
Masaai: Amu ore olojo aitopok enkishui enye neiminie; ore oloiturraa enkishui enye te nkaraki ele rorei supat, neitajeu.

English: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
Masaai: Amu ainyoo edupore oltung'ani, te netum enkop pooki neiturraa enkishui enye?

English: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
Masaai: Anaa ainyoo einosie oltung'ani enkishui enye?

English: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
Masaai: Amu ore olodol isora te naaimaki nanu aashu ororei lai tena ishoi oo ng'ok naloloito nedol sii ninye enkerai e Tung'ani isora eimaki ninye te ina olong elotu te nkitoo e Menye eiriamunore ilmalaika sinyat.”

English: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Esipa, ajoki intae, etii doi ilooitashe tene lemeinyorrinyor keeya katukul o metaba anaa nedol enkitoria e Nkai eewuo te ng'olon.”

English: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
Masaai: Ore pee eishunye nkolong'i ile nerik Yesu Petero o Yakobo o Yohana, neilepie enchumata o ldoinyo oado aa ninche ake; newala emua enye edolita ninche.

English: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
Masaai: Neitintilu lkilani lenyena, aaiborru oleng, enaa meetae olaisujani te nkop oidim aiborrie metotiwuo neijia.

English: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
Masaai: Neliooyu Eliya o Musa te dukuya ninche; eirorie Yesu.

English: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
Masaai: Newalu Petero nejoki Yesu, “Olaiteng'enani, aisidai kitii ene; nchoo iyiook kishetu ilng'oborri okuni, olino obo o le Musa obo o le Eliya obo.”

English: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
Masaai: Naa aimeyiolo enajoito, amu eiputukunyo oleng.

English: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
Masaai: Neitemoo enkatampoi nejo, “Nele Oinoti lai lanyor, ninye entoning.”

English: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
Masaai: Ore nabo kata ake, ejo maing'orisho neitu eitoki aadol likae otii te nebo ninche. Yesu ake openy.

English: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.
Masaai: Ore edou to ldoinyo, neitanap amitiki einosaki likae tung'ani nena naatoduaa ninche, o metaba naa nepiu Enkerai e Tung'ani aing'uaa ilootuata.

English: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
Masaai: Neibung ninche ilo rorei, neikilikuana maate aajo. “Ainyoo doi ena najo ake, kepiu aing'uaa ilootuata?”

English: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?
Masaai: Neikilikuan ninche Yesu aajoki, “Ainyoo pee ejo ilaiteng'enak loo nkitanapat eji meeta nchere meng'as Eliya alotu?”
