Masaai: Neliki ilooiteng'eni le Yohana. Yohana nena baa pooki.

English: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
Masaai: Neipot Yohana aare le lelo kipaareta lenyena neirriwaki Yesu ejo, “Aa iyie doi apa olotu? Anaa ai likae kiaanyu?”

English: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
Masaai: Ore pee epuonu lelo tung'ana enetii Yesu nejoki, “Yohana Olaibatisani oirriwua iyiook enitii ejo, ‘Aa iyie doi apa olotu anaa ai kianyu likae?’ ”

English: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.
Masaai: Ore te ina kata ake neishiunye Yesu ltung'ana ooata nkeyaitin o mueyiaritin kumok, nearaa loiriruani; ore lmodook kumok nebol inkonyek nedolishoyu.

English: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ninche nejoki, “Enchom entoliki Yohana kuna nitoduaa o nitoning'o; etodolishote ilmodook, nepuo lmaiman, neishiunyeki aasik iloota enkeeya oo lbolot, nening'ishoyu lming'anta, neitopiuni ilootuata, nelikini laisinak ororei supat,

English: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
Masaai: nemayiana ilo tung'ani lemetum olkob te nanu.”

English: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
Masaai: Ore eidipa aashom ilooirriwuaki le Yohana neiteru Yesu ainosaa Yohana to lorere nejo, “Ainyoo nawa intae enchom entodol ti ong'ata? Kolperesi oyuk enkijape?

English: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings courts.
Masaai: Mme ninye? Ainyoo naa ishomo intae aadol? Koltung'ani oishopito nkilani naapuyiapui o naaitintil? Nkang'itie oolooitoreisho etumieki lelo ooishop nkilani naapuyiapui o ne nkuso.

English: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
Masaai: Kake ainyoo doi ishomo aadol? Koloiboni le Nkai? Ee pae naa kelang ninye oloiboni le Nkai.

English: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
Masaai: Ninye doi eimakita lkigerot aajo, ‘Nele olkilikuai lai laiturukie te iyie, olaa ninye likintobiraki enkoitoi ino.’

English: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
Masaai: Ajoki intae, kitok Yohana alang pooki tung'ani oiu enkitok kake ore eyia, ore olobayie te nkitoria e Nkai naa kitok alang ninye.”

English: And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
Masaai: Ore pee ening iltung'ana pooki o loosotu kodi neitadedeyie Enkai amu eibatisaki te nkibatisare e Yohana.

English: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.
Masaai: Kake etanyaita ninche Lfarisayo o laiteng'enak loo nkitanapat enayiewuaki Enkai amu etanyaita ninche maate eibatisa Yohana.

English: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
Masaai: Nejo Olaitoriani, “Ainyoo atemaki kulo tung'ana le kuna olong'i? Kainyoo enyaanyukie?

English: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
Masaai: Enyaanyukie nkera naatoni te nemirishoreki, naaipotuno ejo, ‘Kitooshokito intae ndulen, neitu iranyishosho; nikinchirakita intae, neitu nchirishiri.’

English: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.
Masaai: Amu eewuo Yohana Olaibatisani eitupukoo kewan, nemeok enaisho oo sabibu; nijojo intae, ‘Keeta oloirirua.’

English: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
Masaai: Eewuo Enkerai e Tung'ani nedaa neokisho; nijojo, ‘Eng'ura oltung'ani olubo, naa olamerani, naa olchore loo loosotu kodi o laing'okok!’

English: But wisdom is justified of all her children.
Masaai: Ore naa eng'eno e Nkai, neitadedeyie pooki oora inkera enyena.”

English: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house, and sat down to meat.
Masaai: Neipot oltung'ani obo loo Lfarisayo Yesu pee eitoomon te nkaji enye. Nejing enkaji e ilo Farisayoi neton anya endaa.

English: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, etii enkitok ina anasa, naa enkaasani oo ng'ok; ore pee iyiolou ajo einosita Yesu endaa te nkaji e ilo Farisayoi, neyau oltulet lo soit oji alabasta le ilata narropil,

English: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
Masaai: neitashe te siadi ninye too nkejek enyena, neiter aituku nkejek enyena too lkiyio, nejut too lpapit le ndukuya enye, neng'utut nkejek enyena, neelie ina ilata.

English: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
Masaai: Ore pee edol ilo Farisayoi oitoomono nejo to ltau, “Te naa koloiboni le Nkai ele tung'ani anaata etayiolo ajo aing'ae anaa kaa pukunoto e nkitok ena naibung ninye!”

English: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Master, say on.
Masaai: Neirorie Yesu nejoki, “Simon, aata embae naaliki.” Nejoki, “Ee Olaiteng'enani.”

English: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Eisilenoko oltung'ani aisilenoni ltung'ana aare indinari enyena, neisho obo indinari iip imiet, neisho olikae onom.

English: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
Masaai: Ore pee elau pokira aare entoki nalakie, nepalaki pokira aare. Amaa te pokira aare, kalo onyorru ninye oleng?”

English: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.
Masaai: Newaliki Simon ajoki, “Amen ajo, elde otapalakaki nkumok.” Nejoki Yesu, “Etisipa ewalata.”

English: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
Masaai: Neibelekenyakino enkitok, nejoki Simon, “Dol ena kitok? Aewuo enkaji ino neitu kincho enkare oo nkejek; kake aaitashala ena kitok inkejek aainei too lkiyio nejut too lpapit lenyena.

English: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.
Masaai: Eitu king'utut; ore ninye, anaa duoo pee ajing'u eitu aapal maangutut inkejek aainei.

English: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.
Masaai: Eitu kiel endukuya te ilata, kake aaela ninye nkejek te na ilata.

English: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
Masaai: Aajoki naa te nkaraki ina, etapalakaki ng'ok enyena, aa kumok, amu etonyorrishe oleng, amu ore doi olopalakini nkuti naa kiti enyorrata enye.”

English: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ina kitok, “Kitapalakaki ng'ok inono.”

English: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
Masaai: Ore lelo ootoni aadaa te nebo ninye neiter aajo maate, “Ai ng'ae ele eji opalaki oltung'ani ng'ok?”

English: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
Masaai: Nejoki ina kitok, “Kintajewuo enkirukoto ino; shomo te seriani!”

English: And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him,
Masaai: Neaku ore eidipayu nena, neruk nkanas sapuki o nkutiti elikioo ilo rorei neyaki lomon supati le nkitoria e Nkai. Neiriamariyie ilooiteng'eni lenyena tomon o aare ninye,

English: And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,
Masaai: o nkituaak naaishiunyeki loiriruani o nkeyaitin: Mariamu Magdalena, nataarayioki loiriruani oopishana metung'uai,

English: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.
Masaai: o enkitok e Kusa osinka le Herode naji Yoana, o Susana, o kulie kumok naaitoomono ninche Yesu o looiteng'eni too masaa enye.

English: And when much people were gathered together, and were come to him out of every city, he spake by a parable:
Masaai: Ore pee etumo esiamo kitok aaiturrurro, nesotokino lelo le nena ang'itie pooki, neiro alimu enkitanyaanyukoto,

English: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
Masaai: “Etupukuo olaunoni alo aun ilaanterera lenyena: ore eunisho, nedoiki kulikae embata e nkoitoi; neitunyori too nkejek, nenya motonyi e shumata.

English: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae enkop o soit, nejo matubulu, netoyu amu meeta enkare naok.

English: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae atua lkiku, neiriamunore lkiku, negor ninche.

English: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Nedoiki kulikae enkop sidai, nebulu, neiu ilng'anayio iip nabore.” Ore ejoito neijia, nebuak ajo, “Oloata nkiyiaa, toning'o!”

English: And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?
Masaai: Neikilikuan ilooiteng'eni lenyena ninye enalimu ena kitanyaanyukoto.

English: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Eishooki intae entayiolo nkisudorot e nkitoria e Nkai; kake eishori lkulikae too nkitanyaanyukot, pee eing'or nemedol, nening ninche nemejing'aa.

English: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
Masaai: “Naa inji eikununo ina kitanyaanyukoto: Ore ilanterera naa ninche ororei le Nkai.

English: Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootadoikitio embata e nkoitoi naa lelo ooning ororei; nelotu Shetani aitayu too ltauja lenye arishie pee meiruk neitajeuni.

English: They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
Masaai: Ore lanterera ootadoikitio enkop o soit naa lelo ooning ororei neng'amu te ng'ida. Kake eitu ejing'aa atua ninche; neiruk te nkiti kata ake, ore pee epuonu ntemat nebatata aaitiak.

English: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootadoikitio atua lkiku naa lelo ooning;

English: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
Masaai: kake nepuo neitirrishaki enyamali oo masaa o esikar e na kishon nemeitabaya aaiu ilng'anayio.

English: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.
Masaai: “Meetae oltung'ani oinok oltaa neitoki aitoip to ltoo anaa epik orunku le rruat, kake epik enerupa neitasheyie pee edol iloojing' ewang'an.

English: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.
Masaai: Amu meetae entoki naisudoro, nemeibalunyeki; nemeetae enoo nkurrat nemeibalunyeki te wangan.

English: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.
Masaai: Enteng'enuoto too mbaa nining'ining'i amu ore oloata, naa keishori, ore olemeeta neoruni ina najo ninye keeta.”

English: Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come at him for the press.
Masaai: Nelotu ng'otonye Yesu o lalashera lenyena neitu eidim aatabaiki ninye te nkiding'a o lorere.

English: And it was told him by certain which said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
Masaai: Neyakini olkilikuai aajoki, “Etii ng'utunyi o lalashera linono boo, eitashe, kiyieu nikitumore.”

English: And he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, “Ore yieyio o lalashera laainei naa, lelo ooning ororei le Nkai neibung.”

English: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples: and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.
Masaai: Ore nabo olong; nejing empeut ninye o looiteng'eni lenyena: nejoki ninche, “Ematalang aapuo lido kekun le naiposha,” nedumunye aapuo.

English: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water, and were in jeopardy.
Masaai: Ore epuoito neirura ninye. Nedumunye olkutati te naiposha, neaku keiput empeut enkare, nejing bata.

English: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.
Masaai: Nepuo aainyeyie ajoki, “Lo Kitok! Lo Kitok! Kindaaitie!” Neinyototo nebuaki osiwuo o enkilugo e nkare; negira, nelotu enkitirring'a.

English: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Koree enkirukoto inyi?” Neureishoyu, neing'asia, nejokino maate, “Kaing'ae taa ele laa keitore osiwuo o enkare, nening?”

English: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.
Masaai: Nebaya lido kekun loo Lgeraseni, oipirare Galilaya.

English: And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the city a certain man, which had devils long time, and ware no clothes, neither abode in any house, but in the tombs.
Masaai: Ore pee edoiki enkop natoyio nenang'are oltung'ani obo le ina anasa oota iloiriruani; oshomo nkolong'i kumok meishopo, nemejing ang, too nkuraren eton.

English: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu, nebuak, nebatata te dukuya ninye, nejo to ltoilo sapuk, “Kainyoo aatayie nanu iyie Yesu, Oinoti le Nkai Natii Shumata Aisul te pooki? Aatasayia mikisilisil.”

English: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)
Masaai: Amu ketaarayie ninye ilo oirirua torrono otii ilo tung'ani metupuku. (Amu eibung'a nkolong'i kumok, neteenaki aarrip, nerridi too sekenke naairoishi o too munyororoni; ore pee eitirrie pooki nearaa oloirirua ninye ong'ata.)

English: And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him.
Masaai: Neikilikuan Yesu ajoki, “Ai kiji ng'ae?” Nejo, “Kaaji, Empuoto;” amu loiriruani kumok ootijing'a.

English: And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.
Masaai: Nesai pee mearaa ninche meshomo olodo le nkop.

English: And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them.
Masaai: Netii ine emboo oo lbitiro, nadaa to losho; nesai meishoo pee epuo aajing lelo bitiro. Neisho meshomo.

English: Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.
Masaai: Nepuku lelo oiriruani te ilo tung'ani, nejing ilbitiro; nekuet ina luaata oo lbitiro to loshong'ishongi neimis te naiposha neya enkare.

English: When they that fed them saw what was done, they fled, and went and told it in the city and in the country.
Masaai: Ore pee edol lchekuti le lelo bitiro inaatotiwuo, eisik aapuo aalikioo te ina anasa o te ina kop.

English: Then they went out to see what was done; and came to Jesus, and found the man, out of whom the devils were departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
Masaai: Nepuku iltung'ana aapuo aadol enatotiwuo; nepuonu enetii Yesu, neinepu ilo tung'ani otooruoki loiriruani aaraa, eton, neishopo, nenyakua oltau lenye biyoto, etonita too nkejek e Yesu; neureishoyu ninche.

English: They also which saw it told them by what means he that was possessed of the devils was healed.
Masaai: Nelikioo lelo apa ootoduakita ilo tung'ani eoruni loiriruani aaraa neaku biyoto, enaikuna pee eishiunyeki.

English: Then the whole multitude of the country of the Gadarenes round about besought him to depart from them; for they were taken with great fear: and he went up into the ship, and returned back again.
Masaai: Ore lelo tung'ana pooki le nkop oo Lgeraseni o neemanita, nesai metung'uai ninche amu etureishote oleng. Nejing ninye empeut ashuko.

English: Now the man out of whom the devils were departed besought him that he might be with him: but Jesus sent him away, saying,
Masaai: Nesai oladuoo oishiunyeki meturubare, kake eitanapa ajoki,

English: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee. And he went his way, and published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him.
Masaai: “Tushukoyu enkang inyi, imbalakinye enaba ina nikintaasa Enkai.” Nelo aing'uaa, einosaa te ina anasa pooki nena e nking'asia naaitaasa Yesu ninye.

English: And it came to pass, that, when Jesus was returned, the people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.
Masaai: Ore pee eitu Yesu, neitoomon olorere te nchipai amu keanyita ake pooki.

English: And, behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at Jesus' feet, and besought him that he would come into his house:
Masaai: Nelotu oltung'ani oji Yairo naa olkitok le nkaji e ntumo; nebatata too nkejek e Yesu nesai meshomo enkaji enye,

English: For he had one only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she lay a dying. But as he went the people thronged him.
Masaai: amu esila nabo ake eeta, oo larin tomon o aare, neirrag etaa keye. Kake ore ejo alo neiding'akino olorere.

English: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, which had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed of any,
Masaai: Netii enkitok naruko osarge larin tomon o aare; neishang'itie masaa enyena kumok too labaak, neitu eishiunye hoo obo.

English: Came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.
Masaai: Neimu te siadi, neiseyie olcholoi lo lkila lenye, negem nabo kata osarge.

English: And Jesus said, Who touched me? When all denied, Peter and they that were with him said, Master, the multitude throng thee and press thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
Masaai: Nejo Yesu, “Ae ng'ae naatoshoroyie?” Neitolilo olorere, nejoki Petero, “Lo Kitok, kironyita olorere likinturrurrokinote!”

English: And Jesus said, Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yesu, “Etii oltung'ani laatoshoroyie, amu atayiolo ajo etii engolon natupukuo te nanu.”

English: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him and how she was healed immediately.
Masaai: Neisho ina kitok, pee edol ajo meekure eidim aisudori, nekuetu eikirikira, nebatata te dukuya ninye, neibalakinye mbaa pooki te dukuya olorere, ajo aainyo pee etaasa ina, o eneikuna pee eishiwuo.

English: And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ina kitok, “Naito, kinchiunye enkirukoto ino. Shomo te seriani.”

English: While he yet spake, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue's house, saying to him, Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Master.
Masaai: Ore ejo neijia, nelotu oltung'ani oing'uaa enkaji e ilo kitok le nkaji e ntumo, nejoki, “Etua esila ino; mintoki aintanyamal olaiteng'enani.”

English: But when Jesus heard it, he answered him, saying, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Yesu ina, newaliki ajoki ninye, “Miureishoyu: iruko ake iyie, naa keitaae biyoto.”

English: And when he came into the house, he suffered no man to go in, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and the mother of the maiden.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu ina aji, neitu eisho likae tung'ani ejing'u, Petero ake o Yohana o Yakobo, o menye o ng'otonye ina kerai.

English: And all wept, and bewailed her: but he said, Weep not; she is not dead, but sleepeth.
Masaai: Ore aa kitok olkiyioi eishirita ltung'ana nejoki Yesu ninche, “Eminchir amu eitu eye, keirura.”

English: And they laughed him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.
Masaai: Nekueniyieki oleng, amu eyiolo aajo eidipa atua.

English: And he put them all out, and took her by the hand, and called, saying, Maid, arise.
Masaai: Kake ore ninye, neibung, neipot ajoki, “Nakerai, inyo!”

English: And her spirit came again, and she arose straightway: and he commanded to give her meat.
Masaai: Neshukokino ninye enkiyang'et enye, neinyototo nabo kata, neitanapisho meishori endaa.

English: And her parents were astonished: but he charged them that they should tell no man what was done.
Masaai: Neing'asia ntoiwuo e ina kerai kake eitanapa meliki hoo tung'ani enataase.

English: Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases.
Masaai: Neipot lekua ooiteng'eni tomon o aare, neisho engolon, o enkidimata naitoreyie loiriruani pooki, neishiunye mueyiaritin.

English: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
Masaai: Neirriwaa metolikioi enkitoria e Nkai, neishiunye iloomueyiaa.

English: And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Emiya hoo toki te lototo inyi, aa eng'udi, aashu embene, aashu endaa, aashu mpesai, nimiyaya nkilani maa are.

English: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.
Masaai: Ore enkaji pooki nijing'ijing'i, entotoni te ine o entupuku te ina ang.

English: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
Masaai: Ore ilemeitoomon intae, entung'uai ina ang nimpiripiroo enterit natii nkejek inyi metaa shakeni te ninche.”

English: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.
Masaai: Nepuo aamanaa te nena ang'itie, pooki elikioo lomon supati, neishiunye ltamueyia too wuejitin pooki.

English: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said of some, that John was risen from the dead;
Masaai: Ore Herode laa ninye oitore Galilaya, nening nena pooki naasitae; neiputukuny amu ejo kulikae tung'ana, “Yohana otopiwuo too lootuata.”

English: And of some, that Elias had appeared; and of others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.
Masaai: Nejo kulikae, “Eliya oipang'aka.” Nejo kulikae, “Obo loo loibonok li apa otopiwuo.”

English: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
Masaai: Nejo Herode, “Atudung'oyie taa ninye Yohana elukunya, ae ng'ae naa ele laning mbaa enyena?” Neing'oru eyieu nedol ninye.

English: And the apostles, when they were returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.
Masaai: Ore pee eshukunye ilkipaareta, neinosaki Yesu mbaa pooki naataasa. Nerik nepuo enkilepata, o metoriko enkanasa naji Betsaida.

English: And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.
Masaai: Ore pee eyiolou olorora, nesujaa; neitoomon neirorie aliki ninche mbaa e nkitoria e Nkai, neishiunye ilooyieu neishiunyeki.

English: And when the day began to wear away, then came the twelve, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.
Masaai: Ore pee eaku kedoiyo enkolong, nepuonu ilooiteng'eni lenyena enetii nejoki, “Intanapa olorere meshomo kuna kurman o nkang'itie naataana aairrag neing'oru endaa amu ong'ata ene nikitii.”

English: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy meat for all this people.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Enchoo doi intae endaa.” Nejoki ninche, “Mikiaata ae toki neme mukateni miet o sinkir aare, aashu te naa aikipuo aainyang'aki ele orere pooki endaa.”

English: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.
Masaai: Amu ebaya lewa ootii, nkalifuni miet. Nejoki Yesu ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Entotona olorere too intukusi maa onom.”

English: And they did so, and made them all sit down.
Masaai: Neas ina, neitoton iltung'ana pooki.

English: Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.
Masaai: Nedumu mukateni pokira miet, o sinkir are, neing'or shumata nemayian nebel, neisho ilooiteng'eni lenyena meitoomonie olorere.

English: And they did eat, and were all filled: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them twelve baskets.
Masaai: Nenya, neraposho pooki. Nesotuni lmong'oitie loo lekunot, neiput inkikapuni tomon o aare.

English: And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
Masaai: Ore eomonito Yesu openy, netii ilooiteng'eni lenyena, neikilikuan ajoki, “Kejo olorere kara ng'ae?”

English: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say, Elias; and others say, that one of the old prophets is risen again.
Masaai: Newaliki aajoki, “Ejo Yohana Olaibatisani, nejo kulikae, Eliya; nejo kulikae ira obo loo loibonok li apa otopiwuo.”

English: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Nijojo intae kara ng'ae?” Nejoki Petero, “Iyie Kristo le Nkai.”

English: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;
Masaai: Neitanap ninye ninche neitore pee meliki hoo oltung'ani ilo rorei.

English: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Meeta nchere pee meinyali Enkerai e Tung'ani too mbaa kumok, neany ilpayiani o lapolosak kituaak o lasirak neari metua, neitopiuni te nkolong e uni.”

English: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche pooki, “Te neyieu oltung'ani naasuj, nanu, inchoo emenaa kewan, nenap osalaba lenye inkolong'i pooki, naasuj.

English: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
Masaai: Amu ore oloyieu neitajeu enkishui enye, neiminie; kake ore pooki oiturraa enkishui enye enkaraki nanu neitajeu.

English: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
Masaai: Amu ainyoo dupoto o ltung'ani tenetum enkop pooki neiturra enkishui enye.

English: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father's, and of the holy angels.
Masaai: Amu ore olodol anyit te nanu o too rorei laainei, neduaaki sii ninye Enkerai e Tung'ani ninye anyit te nelotu te nkitoo enye o ene menye o enoo lmalaika sinyat.

English: But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Kake ajoki intae too sipat nchere etii kulo ooitashe te ne ilemeishamisham enkeeya katukul, eitu eng'as aadol enkitoria e Nkai.”

English: And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
Masaai: Ore too nkolong'i naabaya isiet eidipate nena baa nerik Petero o Yohana o Yakobo neked oldoinyo aaomon.

English: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
Masaai: Neaku ore eomonito, neibelekenya emua e nkomom enye, o nkilani enyena, neiborru neimerlelu.

English: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, neirorie ninye Musa o Eliya

English: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
Masaai: etalioote te nkitoo e keper neirorie Yesu eimaki eneyooki aiko eitabaya eyieunoto e Nkai aye te Yerusalem.

English: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
Masaai: Ore Petero o looboitare neiliara njo, kake edolisho ake nedol enkitoo e Yesu, o lelo tung'ana pokira aare ooitashe te nebo ninye.

English: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
Masaai: Ore epuo lelo tung'ana aaing'uaa Yesu, nejoki Petero Yesu, “Lo Kitok, sidai kitii ene, maitobira lng'oborri okuni, obo lino, o obo le Musa o le Eliya.” Nemeyiolo enajoito.

English: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
Masaai: Ore ejo neijia nedou enkatampoi neitoip apik oloip; neureishoyu pee ejing atua ina atampoi.

English: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
Masaai: Nepuku oltoilo te nkatampoi nejo, “Ena Enkerai ai Gelunoti, entoning ninye.”

English: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
Masaai: Ore pee egira ilo toilo, nedoli Yesu aa ninye ake. Negira ninche, eitu eliki ltung'ana te nena olong'i inaatoduaa.

English: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.
Masaai: Ore taaisere pee edou to ldoinyo, netumore olorora kitok Yesu.

English: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, nebuaku oltung'ani obo tiatua ina siamo ejo, “Olaiteng'enani, aatasayia ng'urai enkerai ai amu ninye ake aata;

English: And, lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him.
Masaai: naa kenang'aa oloirirua, nebuak, neiterreyie o meitayu labur nemeing'uaa asioki, near oleng.

English: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.
Masaai: Natasayia ilooiteng'eni linono meitayu netalaikinote.”

English: And Jesus answering said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Oi ena ishoi nemeeta enkirukoto, kaboitare intae naitaas intae o anu? Iyau enkerai ino ene.”

English: And as he was yet a coming, the devil threw him down, and tare him. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.
Masaai: Ore eyau, nenang'aa oloirirua neiterreyie, nebuaaki Yesu ilo oirirua torrono, neishiunye ina kerai, neshukoki menye.

English: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they wondered every one at all things which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,
Masaai: Neing'asia lelo pooki ootoduaa engolon magilani e Nkai. Ore eton eing'asia pooki too mbaa naataasa, nejoki ninye ilooiteng'eni lenyena,

English: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men.
Masaai: “Emincho ake erikino intae kuna taata naliki intae! Keishoori Enkerai e Tung'ani aaitarasaki inkaik oo ltung'ana.”

English: But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.
Masaai: Kake eitu ejing'aa ina natiaaka; eton eisudoro te ninche, metaa mening'u tipat enye, nemeitieu sii aaikilikuana.

English: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.
Masaai: Neiteru enchankar tiatua ninche maate ejo kalo lenye olkitok te pooki.

English: And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,
Masaai: Neyiolou Yesu ina nadamu ninche, nedumu enkerai neitataaniki kewan aitasheyie;

English: And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.
Masaai: nejoki ninche, “Ore pooki ng'ae ong'amu ena kerai te nkarna ai, nanu etang'amua, ore oloisul te nkitisho ti atua intae, naa ninye oisul te nkitoo.”

English: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.
Masaai: Neng'amaa Yohana ajoki, “Lo Kitok, kitoduaa oltung'ani earaa loiriruani te nkarna ino nikimitiki, amu mme ole ncholiek ang.”

English: And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Emimitiki, amu ore olemekes intae, naa ole nkalo inyi.”

English: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
Masaai: Netaanu nkolong'i pee eilep alo shumata, nemut nabo ajo kelo Yerusalem.

English: And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
Masaai: Neirriwaa ilooiteng'eni meituruko dukuya ninye aajing ang oo Samaria, pee eitobiraki enejing.

English: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Kake eitu eitoomon ilopeny enkaraki naipirta Yerusalem.

English: And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
Masaai: Ore pee edol ilooiteng'eni lenyena, Yakobo o Yohana, nejo, “Olaitoriani, iyieu nikimpotu enkima te keper metapejoi?”

English: But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
Masaai: Neibelekenyakino aing'ode nejoki, “Miyiololo aajo kaa pukunoto oo ltauja iatata,

English: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
Masaai: amu eitu doi elotu Enkerai e Tung'ani amut iltauja loo ltung'ana, kake pee eitajeu.” Nepuo ae ang.

English: And it came to pass, that, as they went in the way, a certain man said unto him, Lord, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
Masaai: Ore epuo te nkoitoi, nejoki oltung'ani obo Yesu, “Ekaasuj nanu iyie pooki wueji nilo.”

English: And Jesus said unto him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Eeta mbariak ngumot enye, neeta motonyi sinkin. Kake meeta Enkerai e Tung'ani eneirishaki elukunya enye.”

English: And he said unto another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
Masaai: Nejoki likae, “Tusujuaki nanu.” Kake etiaka, “Lo Kitok, nchooki ang'as alo anukaa papa.”

English: Jesus said unto him, Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Inchoo lmeneng'a, metunukai, ilmeneng'a kake shomo iyie tolikioi ilomon le nkitoria e Nkai.”

English: And another also said, Lord, I will follow thee; but let me first go bid them farewell, which are at home at my house.
Masaai: Nejoki sii likae, “Olaitoriani, aasuj kake, nchooki ang'as alo aitanapare iltung'ana to lmarei lang.”

English: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Ore oltung'ani otonyorra enturore neitoki anang silig, nemeishiaakino enkitoria e Nkai.”

English: After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.
Masaai: Ore te siadi nena, negelu Olaitoriani kulikae ntomoni naapishana neirriwaa maare, meturuko nena ang'itie o pooki wueji neyieu openy nelo.

English: Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Sapuk enkisampuare, kake kuti laisiaayiak entoomon naa olopeny enkisampuare meirriu laisiaayiak meetu enkisampuare enye.

English: Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.
Masaai: Enchom! Airriwaa intae anaa lkuoo le kerra ooirrikini atua suyian.

English: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.
Masaai: Emiya embene, aashu nkilani, aashu namuka, nimirorokiki hoo oltung'ani te nkoitoi.

English: And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
Masaai: Ore enkaji pooki nijing'ijing'i entang'as entejo, ‘Metijing'a eseriani ena aji.’

English: And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.
Masaai: Naa te netii oltung'ani le seriani ine netum ninye eseriani inyi, naa te nemetii, neshukokino intae eseriani inyi.

English: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.
Masaai: Entotoni te ina aji ninosinoso, niokioko entoki naba anaa enaishori intae, amu enare olaasani le siaai olekoisiaayio lenye; emipuo aarukurukoo nkajijik.

English: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:
Masaai: Ore enkang pooki nijing'ijing'i neitoomon intae, entam endaa naishooki intae;

English: And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
Masaai: ninchiunyenye iloomuei ootii nijokiki etinyikua enkitoria e Nkai.

English: But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,
Masaai: Ore enkang nijing'ijing'i nemeitoomon intae, enchom inkoitoi enyena naalala nijojo,

English: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
Masaai: ‘Ore ninye enterit e nkang inyi nikiaata too nkejek ang, kimpiripiroki intae, kake entayiolo nchere, etinyikua enkitoria e Nkai.’

English: But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.
Masaai: Esipa ajoki intae, ore te ina olong e nkiguana, Sodom eikashieki alang enaitaasi ina ang!

English: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
Masaai: “Ee kake ayia iyie Korasin! Ee kake ayia iyie Betsaida! Amu te naa ketaasaki apa te Tiro o Sidon nena e nking'asia naatasaki tiaatua intae, anaata eirridutua apa moitie, neishop lkuniyiani, neelare nkuruon.

English: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
Masaai: Kake Tiro o Sidon eikashieki te nkolong e nkiguana aaitalang intae.

English: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
Masaai: Oi iyie Kapernaum, eijo shumata kilepieki, kintadouni shomo enemeneng'a.”

English: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Ore pooki oning intae, nanu ening, ore oloany intae, nanu eany, ore olaany nanu, naa ilo laairriwua etanya.”

English: And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.
Masaai: Neshukunye lekua ntomoni naapishana o aare te ng'ida. Ejo, “Olaitoriani, ore ebaiki loiriruani, etoning'o iyiook kiaaraa te nkarna ino!”

English: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu nejoki, “Atoduaa Shetani esulunye anaa enkiwuang'ata eing'uaa shumata.

English: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
Masaai: Enining'o! Aishoo intae enkidimata, metaa indimidimi aaitunyoi ilasuriaa o nkulupani, o engolon pooki e ilo mang'atinta, nemeeta enaiko intae.

English: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.
Masaai: Kake eming'idare ina naning intae iloiriruani; kake enting'idata amu eigero nkarn inyi te shumata.”

English: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.
Masaai: Ore ina kata ake neshipayu Yesu eiganya Enkiyang'et Sinyati, nejo, “Ashe Papa Olaitoriani le keper o enkop! Amu isudorie kuna baa ilang'eni o looata eyiolounoto niboloki inkera naanana, amu ina eyieunoto e mpiris ino.

English: All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.
Masaai: Nanu eishoo Papa pooki toki, nemeetae oloyiolo Oinoti leme Papa ake, nemeetae oloyiolo Papa leme Oinoti lenye ake, o lelo pooki ngae ake ogelu enkerai aboloki ninye.”

English: And he turned him unto his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:
Masaai: Neibelekenyakino ilooiteng'eni lenyena, neirorie too nkurrat nejo, “Emayiana nkonyek naadol kuna nidolitata intae.

English: For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.
Masaai: Amu ajoki intae, eyieu apa loibonok o laiguanak, nedol kuna nidolidolo, kake eitu hoo edol; neyieu apa nening kuna nining'ining'i kake eitu hoo ening.”

English: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, neinyototo olang'eni obo aikilikuanishore, eyieu netem, nejoki, “Lo Aiteng'enani, kaji aiko pee ajung enkishui nemeish?”

English: He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Kakua baa naaigero too nkitanapat e Nkai? Kejo aa enisoma iyie?”

English: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, “Tonyorra Olaitoriani Enkai ino to ltau lino pooki, o te nkiyang'et ino pooki, o te ng'eno ino pooki, o te ngolon ino pooki, ninyorru o le latia ino anaa eninyor kewan.”

English: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Itawala aitobiraki, taasa ina pee iton inchu.”

English: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?
Masaai: Neyieu ninye neitaa kewan asipani, nejoki Yesu, “Ai ng'ae doi ole latia ai?”

English: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Etadowuo oltung'ani eing'uaa Yerusalem alo Yeriko, neinepu ilaisimak neoru nkilani, near neing'uaa etaa keye.

English: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
Masaai: Nelotu olapolosani aim ina oitoi, ore pee edol nepaash, nelo.

English: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
Masaai: Nelotu sii ninye ole Lawi aim ine ore pee edol nepaash, nelo.

English: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
Masaai: Kake ore pee elotu Osamariyiai olo sii ninye nkang'itie, ore pee edol neing'urrie.

English: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
Masaai: Nebaiki neen ilbaa lenyena nebukoki eilata neisho enaisho oo sabibu, neitoki aitaked esikiria enye, nerik enkaji naitoomonishoreki neitobir te ine.

English: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
Masaai: Ore taaisere, neitayu dinari are aisho olopeny ina aji nejoki, ‘Ing'ura taa ele tung'ani, ore pooki toki nanya nalusoo te nena, nalotu alak te nashukunye.’

English: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?
Masaai: Kaa idol iyie te lelo tung'ana pokira okuni, kalo otaa ole latia te ilo otara ilaisimak?”

English: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
Masaai: Nejo ninye; ilo oing'urrie ninye. Nejoki Yesu Ninye shomo sii iyie taasa ina.

English: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
Masaai: Ore epuo neimaa Yesu enkang namanya enkitok naji Marisa neitoomon te nkaji enye.

English: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.
Masaai: Neeta enkanashe naji Mariamu, nelotu ina aton too nkejek e Yesu, aton aainining inkiteng'enat.

English: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
Masaai: Nenyamalu Marisa too siaaitin enyena kumok, nelotu enetii nejoki, “Olaitoriani, ai midol ajo emakua te naasisho openy, naapalaki enkanashe ai? Tiaaki naa maaeu aret.”

English: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:
Masaai: Kake etawalikia Olaitoriani ajoki, “Marisa, Marisa, intanyamaluo nimposha too mbaa kumok;

English: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
Masaai: kake nabo bae ake naata tipat, ena bae natudutayie Mariamu naisul; nemeyae aaitung'uaa ninye.”

English: And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.
Masaai: Neaku ore eomonito te dikae wueji, ore pee eidip, nejoki obo loo looiteng'eni lenyena, “Olaitoriani, inteng'ena iyiook enkomono anaa enaiteng'ena Yohana ilooiteng'eni lenyena.”

English: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Ti niomonono entejo: Papa meitisinyi enkarna ino, meeu enkitoria ino.

English: Give us day by day our daily bread.
Masaai: Inchoo iyiook anaa ake endaa nabaiki iyiook.

English: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.
Masaai: Nipalaki iyiook ing'ok ang, anaa te nikipalaki sii iyiook ilooinyal iyiook. Nimirik iyiook atua ntemat.”

English: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves;
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Kalo linyi oota lchore laa te nelo ainyeyie eitorite enkewarie, ajoki, ‘Olchore, isilenokoki mukateni uni;

English: For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him?
Masaai: amu eewuo olchore lai eing'uaa nkang'itie nemaata entoki naisho.’

English: And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee.
Masaai: Kejoki ilo otii aji, ‘Mikintanyamal, amu eikeno kutuk aji, neirurate nkera, kirurate pooki. Meekure aidim ainyo pee aaisho?’

English: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.
Masaai: Ajoki ntae, te nemeisho duoo te nkaraki naa olchore lenye, kake ore enkaraki naitirrishaka olikae, einyototo ake aisho naaba anaa naayieu.

English: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Masaai: Najoki naa ntae, entoomonu pee eishori ntae, eng'oru pee itumutumu; entooshiosh kutuk aji pee eboluni ntae.

English: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
Masaai: Amu ore pooki oomonu netum; ore oloing'oru netum; ore olooshiosh kutuk aji neboluni.

English: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?
Masaai: “Kalo te ntae oisho enkerai enye osoit etoomonuo emukate? Aashu te neomonu osinkirri, keisho olasurai?

English: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?
Masaai: Aashu te neomonu olmosori, keisho enkulupa?

English: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
Masaai: Asa taa doi iyiololo ntae iltung'ana torrok, aaisho nkera inyi ntokitin sidain, kebaa na aitulus Papa linyi otii keper aisho Enkiyang'et Sinyati lelo oomon ninye?”

English: And he was casting out a devil, and it was dumb. And it came to pass, when the devil was gone out, the dumb spake; and the people wondered.
Masaai: Nearaa oloirirua lemeiro. Neaku ore pee epuku ilo oirirua lemeiro, neiro ilo tung'ani apa oonyo kutuk, neing'asia olorere.

English: But some of them said, He casteth out devils through Beelzebub the chief of the devils.
Masaai: Kake etejo kulikae lenye, “Beelsebul, olkitok loo loiriruani, oishoo engolon naararie loiriruani.”

English: And others, tempting him, sought of him a sign from heaven.
Masaai: Netem sii kulikae eing'oru osapiipiyiet oing'uaa keper.

English: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.
Masaai: Kake ore pee eirrash ndamunot enye, nejoki, “Ore enkitoria ake ninye pooki naoro aara oopeny neidaaya, ore enkaji naara openy neurori.

English: If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub.
Masaai: Kaji eiko Shetani te neoro aara makewan, keitoki enkitoria enye auno? Amu ijojo naa te ngolon e Beelsebul aaraa loiriruani?

English: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.
Masaai: Naa omaa te naa kengolon e Beelsebul aararie nanu loiriruani, kengolon e ng'ae doi aararie ninche nkera inyi loiriruani? Ninche naa ooyooki aaiguanare ntae.

English: But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.
Masaai: Kake te naa ai to lkimojino le Nkai aaraa loiriruani, enkitoria e Nkai naewuo atua ntae.

English: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace:
Masaai: Ore te nerrip oltung'ani ogol otanape enkaji enye, neserian imasaa enyena pooki.

English: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.
Masaai: Kake te nerasaki ologol alang ninye nemir, neoru masaa o larrabal duoo naawuasare, nelo aor iyarunot naatarua.

English: He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.
Masaai: “Ore pooki leme ole nkalo ai, nau ekesh, ore ole maaret osotu, naa keisardaikie.

English: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he saith, I will return unto my house whence I came out.
Masaai: “Ore te neidur oloirirua oiduruk to ltung'ani nelo aimaa iwuejitin nemetii enkare, eing'oru eneyeng'iyeng'are; ore pee elau, nejo, ‘Kashukokino enkaji ai apa natung'uayie.’

English: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau, neinepu etooroki neikodi,

English: Then goeth he, and taketh to him seven other spirits more wicked than himself; and they enter in, and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
Masaai: neito ninye alo aipot kulikae oiriruani oopishana torrok aalang ninye, meetu aamany ine; nerruoyo empukunoto e ilo tung'ani enatiu apa te dukuya.”

English: And it came to pass, as he spake these things, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo neijia, nebuaku enkitok nabo ti atua olorora nejoki, “Emayiana sii ake enkoshoke nikitoiwuo o lki likintanaaki.”

English: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.
Masaai: Newaliki Yesu ajoki, “Ee paa emayiana aaisul, ilooning ele rorei le Nkai neibung.”

English: And when the people were gathered thick together, he began to say, This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.
Masaai: Ore pee eiturrurrokino esiamo Yesu neiter ajoki, “Arruok sii ake ltung'ana lena kata, embae eing'oru; kake meetae naa embae enking'asia naishori neme e Yona.

English: For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.
Masaai: Amu ore anaa enataa Yona embae enking'asia too ltung'ana le Ninawi, neijia sii etiu Enkerai e Tung'ani too ltung'ana le na kata.

English: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
Masaai: Eyooki enkaiguanani e kopikop adumunye te nkiguana oo ltung'ana lena ishoi nedung'oki ninche enkiguana, amu eewuo ninye too neeiting'ie enkop elotu ainining eng'eno e Solomon, naa ng'ura, etii ene olkitok olang Solomon.

English: The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.
Masaai: Eyooki ltung'ana le Ninawi aaitasheiki neitang'or ltung'ana le na ishoi, te nkolong e nkiguana, nedung'oki enkiguana, amu eirridutua ninche etolikio Yona ororei le Nkai, naa ng'ora, etii taa ene olkitok olang Yona.

English: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.
Masaai: “Meetae oltung'ani oinok oltaa nepik orunku aashu epising to ltoo, kake epik eneiperere pee eitawang'aki iloojing'u.

English: The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.
Masaai: Etiu nkonyek inono anaa oltaa lo sesen lino, naa te naa biyot nkonyek inono, newang osesen lino pooki; kake ore pee kira torrok nkonyek nerip enaimin osesen lino pooki.

English: Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.
Masaai: Toduaa naa pee miaku ewang'an niata enaimin.

English: If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.
Masaai: Amu te nebore osesen lino pooki ewang'an, nemeeta enemisimis, newang'u pooki wueji, atiu anaa te nikilang oltaa owang.”

English: And as he spake, a certain Pharisee besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.
Masaai: Ore eirorita Yesu, neipot Olfarisayoi obo meshomo anya endaa te nkaji enye, nelo, neton anya endaa.

English: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled that he had not first washed before dinner.
Masaai: Neing'asia ilo Farisayoi pee edol ajo eitu eng'as aisuj inkaik eitu enya endaa.

English: And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Olaitoriani ilo farisayioi, “Intukuku ntae Lfarisayo oriong enkikompe o esaani, kake ore atua ntae ebore enkowuarisho o enkarruoisho.

English: Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?
Masaai: Lo moda! Ai me ele obo oitobira oriong o atua?

English: But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.
Masaai: Kake enchoru to lng'ur nena tokitin naatii atua, naa ng'ura, kesinyayu pooki toki te ntae.

English: But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
Masaai: “Kake ee kake aiyia ntae lo Farisayo! amu nchoruru ematua e tomon oo ntasimi oo mbenek pooki nipalaa enkiguana oo sipat o enyorrata e Nkai, naa eishiaakino nitaasa nimipalaa nena kulie.

English: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
Masaai: Ee kake aiyia ntae Ilfarisayo! Amu inyorrinyorro lorikan sidain too nkajijik entumo, ninyorrinyorro lng'asak too wuejitin neemirishoreki.

English: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.
Masaai: Ee kake aiyia ntae! amu itiuu anaa nkuraren nemelioo, naaitunyoo ltung'ana meyiolo.”

English: Then answered one of the lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also.
Masaai: Newaliki obo loo laiteng'enak loo nkitanapat ajoki, “Olaiteng'enani, te nijo nji, iyiook sii iyiet.”

English: And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Ee kake ayia sii ntae ilang'eni loo nkitanapat! amu intanapinapa ilkulikae ilolan ooiroishi lemenapayu, ore ntae maate nimiseyieyie too lkimojik linyi.

English: Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
Masaai: Ee kake ayia! Amu ishetishete nkuraren oo iloibonok le Nkai laa papaai linyi ootaara metuata.

English: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.
Masaai: Metaa, itaa shakeni, nitonyorraitie nkiasin oo loo minyi, amu ninche ootaara metuata, nishetakiki ntae nkuraren.

English: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:
Masaai: “Ore enkaraki ina, etejo, eng'eno e Nkai, ‘Kairriwaki ninche loibonok o lkipaareta, near kulikae metuata, nearaa kulikae’,

English: That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
Masaai: paa ore ilo sarge loo loibonok le Nkai, oibukoyioki ebaiki apa pee eitamanyuni enkop, neitalakuni ltung'ana le na ishoi;

English: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.
Masaai: ebaiki osarge le Abel o metabaiki osarge le Sakaria, oitanang'aki erishata olperere lo lasar o ewueji sinyati ee ajoki intae keitalakuni too ltung'ana lena ishoi.

English: Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
Masaai: “Ee kake aiyia lang'eni loo nkitanapat! Amu iwaita embolet najing'ieki ewueji e ng'eno; neitu ijing'ijing'i ntae maate nirishieshie lelo oojing'ita.

English: And as he said these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things:
Masaai: “Ore eing'uaa ine, neiteru lasirak o Lfarisayo aaitirrishaki oleng, nerrumoki meimaki imbaa kumok

English: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.
Masaai: erreshu enaitang'orie te nena naajo ninye.

English: In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Masaai: Ore etiu neijia, pee eiturrurro olorora kitok metaa keitunyoro, neiteru aiturukie ilooiteng'eni lenyena ajoki, “Entodol ake ate te nkisuijo oo Lfarisayo nchere esunkureisho.

English: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.
Masaai: Meetae enaimulumularo nemeibalunyeki, aashu enaisudoro nemeyiolouni.

English: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.
Masaai: Ore embae pooki nitejo ntae te naimin neyookini aalikioo te wang'an, ore nena nipuopuo aaing'omingo'makino too lgilat loo nkisudorot neyookini aalikioo too nchumarot oo nkajijik.

English: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
Masaai: “Ajoki ntae, loshoreta laainei, emiure lelo ooar osesen, nemeitoki aata ai naaidim aataas eidipa ina.

English: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.
Masaai: Kake aikok intai aliki olonare niurere; entureita ilo laa ore eidipa atara metua, neitoki aata engolon nanang'akinye Yehanum; ee ajoki ntae, ilo enturiata!

English: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?
Masaai: “Ai mme elai are ake enya ntiitiini miet? Nemelang ninye Enkai hoo nabo e nena.

English: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
Masaai: Oo naa ntae ilaa keikena ninye lpapit loo lukuny inyi. Emiureisho; iatata pae tipat aalang ntiitiini kumok.

English: Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:
Masaai: “Najoki nanu ntae, ore pooki laaibalie te dukuya ltung'ana, neibalie sii ninye Enkerai e Tung'ani ninye te dukuya ilmalaika le Nkai.

English: But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.
Masaai: Kake ore ilo laamiki te dukuya ltung'ana nemikini sii ninye te dukuya lmalaika le Nkai.

English: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.
Masaai: Ore oltung'ani pooki osukeny Enkerai e Tung'ani kepalakini, kake ore olomor Enkiyang'et Sinyati nemepalakini.

English: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:
Masaai: Naa te neyae ntae nkajijik e ntumo o laitoriak o enkitoo, eming'aing'ai aajo ai jojo aa anaa aiwalulu aajo aa;

English: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
Masaai: amu keutaki ntae Enkiyang'et Sinyati te ina saa enijojo.”

English: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.
Masaai: Nejoki oltung'ani obo otii atua ilo orere, “Olaiteng'enani, tiaaki olalashe lai maatooriki enjung'ore ang.”

English: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
Masaai: Kake etiaka, “Lo tung'ani, ai ng'ae laaitaa nanu olarishani anaa olooriki ntae?”

English: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
Masaai: Neitoki ajoki ninche, “Entodol ake ate, entodol ate to lng'uarra; amu ore enkishui neme nkumoi oo masaa naata.”

English: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:
Masaai: Neitoki aliki enkitanyaanyukoto, nejoki, “Eetae apa olkarsis neisho enkurma enye oleng,

English: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?
Masaai: nejoki kewan enye, ‘Kaa taa aas, amu maata enapik endaa ai?’

English: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.
Masaai: Nejo, ‘Inji aiko, kaar impechen aainei nashetu naalala naalang kuna; pee ashumie endaa ai o masaa aainei.

English: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.
Masaai: Naa kajoki oltau lai, lo tau! iata masaa kumok nikitushumakaki too larin kumok; isikarrayu tadaayu niokisho nishipa.’

English: But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?
Masaai: Kake nejoki Enkai, ‘Lo modai! Ena kewarie kiyieki oltau lino; paa omanaa nena tokitin ninteng'ela keaku pasa nkuneng'ae ninche?’

English: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.
Masaai: Neijia etiu oloshumaki kewan imasaa neme karsis ti alo Enkai.”

English: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Ajoki naa ntae, emintanyamaluo te nkaraki enkishon inyi, te ntoki ninyanya, o too seseni linyi te ntoki ninchopishopo.

English: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.
Masaai: Amu kitok enkishui alang endaa, naa kitok osesen alang inkilani.

English: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?
Masaai: Ing'ura lkurruki; meunisho, nemesotisho, nemeeta sitooni anaa mpechen, neitoki ake Enkai sii ninche. Kebaa naa elang tipat inyi ntae enoo motonyi!

English: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?
Masaai: Naa kalo obo linyi oidim atoponiki kewan entemata nabo e nkaina te nkishui enye?

English: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?
Masaai: Amaa naa te nimindimidimi aataas enkiti bae anaa ina, oo pee intanyamaluoluo too nkulie pooki?

English: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
Masaai: Ng'ura ntapuka, eneiko te nebulu, nemeekenya nemepiyaisho; kake ajoki ntae, ore ninye Solomon te sikar enye pooki nemeikodo anaa enatiu nabo e kuna.

English: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?
Masaai: Kake pasa taa eishop Enkai aiko nji olkujita obulu taata ti ong'ata ore taaisere nenang'akini enkima, kebaa eitulus aishop intae, lo tung'ana kulo ooti enkirukoto!

English: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.
Masaai: Naa eming'oruru entoki ninyanya anaa eniokioko, naa emisinanuo.

English: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.
Masaai: Amu kuna tokitin eing'oru loreren pooki le nkop; neyiolo Papa linyi ajo nkolati inyi nena.

English: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Masaai: Ore enaikash naa eng'oru enkitoria enye, naa keaku sii nkuninyi nena kulie.

English: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Masaai: “Emiureisho, lo turrur oti, amu Papa linyi otonyorra aisho ntae enkitoria enye.

English: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
Masaai: Entimir imasaa inyi, enchoo laisinak; engoraki ate lbenia lememusanu, ooata olchumati te shumata lememuta, ine nemenyikaki olapurroni nemeinosie oriri.

English: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Masaai: Amu ore ine netii olchumati lino naa ine etii oltau lino.

English: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;
Masaai: “Enterreten impolosi inyi, naa enchoo etoni eyupuyup ltaai linyi

English: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.
Masaai: nitiuu anaa ltung'ana ooanyita olkitok lenye elotu eing'uaa osirua le nkiyama, pee te nebau neipotisho nesioki aabolu nabo kata.

English: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.
Masaai: Emayiana ake lelo aisiaayiak laa te nebau olkitok lenye neinepu erripisho. Esipa ajoki ntae, kerretena ninye openy neisho ninche metotona te mesa, nelotu aitoti ninche.

English: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.
Masaai: Naa te neewuo te rripore e are, aashu te ne uni, neinepu etiu neijia, nemayian ake lelo aisiaayiak!

English: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.
Masaai: Kake entayiolo nchere, te naa keyiolo olopeny enkaji esaa nalotunye olapurroni, anaata etorripishe naa anaata eitu eisho metigili enkaji enye.

English: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.
Masaai: Entashololoto sii ntae; amu elotu Enkerai e Tung'ani te saa niminteikiki.”

English: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?
Masaai: Nejoki Petero, “Olaitoriani, aiyiook ake iliki ena kitanyaanyukoto ena ei pooki ng'ae?”

English: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani, “Kalo pasa abarani ilo supat naa ng'en otung'eikia olopeny enkaji, meitotio lootii too rishat enye?

English: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.
Masaai: “Emayiana ake sii ilo aisiaayiani oinepu olkitok lenye easita ina naitanapa.

English: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.
Masaai: Esipa ajoki ntae, keisho meitoria masaa enyena pooki.

English: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;
Masaai: Kake oo te nejo ilo aisiaayiani openy, ‘Eimutie olkitok lai,’ neiteru aidong nkaisiaayiak, nedaa ninye neokisho amera,

English: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.
Masaai: neyooki alotu olkitok le ilo aisiaayiani to lkekun, lemeiteikini o te saa nemeyioloi, neitame neitaboitaki ilemening'isho.

English: And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.
Masaai: Ore ilo aisiaayiani apa oyiolo enayieu olkitok lenye, neitu eas aitabaya aashu ina nanyor, neidong'i oleng.

English: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.
Masaai: Kake ore ilo lemeyiolo, netaasa enaishiaakino enkidong'oto, eari penyo. Ore pooki oishooki nkumok, neyieki ninye nkumok; ore ilo laa ninye eitanap iltung'ana nkumok neyieki ninye nkumok oleng.

English: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I if it be already kindled?
Masaai: “Aewuo aisuroki enkop enkima; naa oi sii ake duoo te naa keidipa atudupai!

English: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!
Masaai: Kake kaata enkibatisa naaibatisae; nebaa enaaitirrishita o meitabari kenya!

English: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:
Masaai: Aijojo pasa kaewuo ayaki enkop osotua? A'a, ajoki eoro ayaki;

English: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
Masaai: amu ore ebaiki taata eoro enkaji nara miet; nepong'ore uni are, nepong'ore are uni;

English: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
Masaai: nepong'o enkerai o menye, nepong'o entito o ng'otonye, nepong'ore enkaputani enkitok o layioni lenye, nepong'ore esiankiki enkaputani.”

English: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.
Masaai: Nejoki sii olorere, “Te nidolulu oshi enkatampoi eilepa te nkalo e ndoyioroto, nijojo nabo kata, ‘Kelotu asha’; netiu neijia.

English: And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.
Masaai: Ore pee idolidolo osiwuo oing'uaa moikuape nijojo, ‘Kelotu airowuaju’; netiu neijia.

English: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time?
Masaai: Lo sunkuro! Kulo iyiololo intae aatolimu eliooto enkop o loing'ang'e; kake kaji nkoko pee miyiololo aaing'ura nilimumu enatiu ena kata?

English: Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?
Masaai: “Naa kaji etiu pee mirishushu oopeny enasipa?

English: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.
Masaai: Ore eton iriamariri te nkoitoi o ilo likintang'or to larishani, tetema toning'ore ninye eton ipuopuo, pee mikiyeataki enetii olaiguanani, nikintarasaki olaiguanani osikari, nikipik osikari korokoroni.

English: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.
Masaai: Aajoki, mipuku aikata te ine mme italaa empisai nabayie.”

English: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
Masaai: Netii apa kulikae ootii ine ina kata ootolikitio Yesu eneikuna Pilato Ilgalilaya ootara metuata neitushulaki osarge oloo lasarri lenye.

English: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?
Masaai: Newaliki ninche ajoki, “Ijojo pasa ai lelo Galilaya oota ng'ok aalang ilkulikae Galilaya pooki, eji amu neijia eikunaki enkitamioto?

English: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
Masaai: Ajoki ntae, mme neijia; kake te neitu iridudu sii ntae nindaayaya aaiko neijia.”

English: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
Masaai: Aashu doi lapa oora tomon o isiet ootuurokine enkaji naado te Siloam near metuata, ijojo pasa ninche larruok aalang ilkulikae pooki oomanya apa Yerusalem?

English: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
Masaai: Ajoki ntae mme neijia; kake te neitu irridudu sii ntae nindaayaya aaiko neijia.

English: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.
Masaai: Neinosaki ena kitanyaanyukoto: “Eeta apa oltung'ani olng'aboli ouno te nkurma enye oo lng'anayio nelotu aing'orunye lng'anayio neitu etumie.

English: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?
Masaai: Nejoki oloramat ilng'anayio, ‘Eji larin okuni taata alotu ake aing'orunye ele ng'aboli lng'anayio, nematumie, tudung'o tuuroi; oo pee etumuta enkop?’

English: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, ‘Tapala, lo kitok, te le ari sii taata, matuturoki napik entulugumi.

English: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.
Masaai: Ore pee etoiwuo lng'anayio te le ari olotu naa sidai; kake te neitu, nidung auroo.’ ”

English: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
