Masaai: Neaku eiteng'enisho apa ninye te nkaji nabo te nkolong e sabato.

English: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.
Masaai: Netii enkitok naata oloirirua le lepori too larin tomon o isiet; neaku keirrugori meidim ataraposhunye.

English: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.
Masaai: Ore pee edol Yesu ninye, neipot, nejoki, “Na kitok, kitooruoki entasato ino.”

English: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
Masaai: Neiteleiki nkaik enyena, neraposhunye te ina kata. Neisis Enkai.

English: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.
Masaai: Kake etagore olkitok le nkaji e ntumo enkaraki naishiunye Yesu olorere te nkolong e sabato nejoki olorere, “Eetai nkolong'i ile naaishiaakino neasieki esiaai; wootu te nena olong'i meishiunyeki ntae, neme te nkolong e sabato.”

English: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
Masaai: Newaliki taa Olaitoriani nejoki, “Lo sunkuro! Keetae obo linyi lemelaku olkiteng anaa osikiria lenye to lale te nkolong e sabato, nerik aitook enkare?

English: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
Masaai: Paa ai meishiaakino ninye ena kitok, entito e Abraham nateena shetani larin tomon o isiet ai meishiaakino netalakuaki te nkolong e sabato.”

English: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo neijia, nekurru lelo pooki ooing'orunore; neshipa olorere pooki too mbaa pooki e nkisisa naataasa ninye.

English: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?
Masaai: Neitoki taa ajoki, “Kaji eikununo enkitoria e Nkai? Naa ainyoo pasa eitanyaanyukieki?

English: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.
Masaai: Etiu anaa enkantererai e karadali natuuno oltung'ani te nkurma enye; nebulu aaku olchani, nemany intaritik ilng'osil lenyena aapik isinkin.”

English: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?
Masaai: Neitoki ake Yesu ajoki, “Ainyoo pasa aitanyaanyukie enkitoria e Nkai?

English: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
Masaai: Etiu anaa enkisuijoi natudumua enkitok neitushulaki mboreitin uni e nkano, o metaba anaa neisuijoyu pooki.”

English: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
Masaai: Neimaa nkang'itie sapuki oo nkutiti neiteng'enisho eloito enkalo e Yerusalem.

English: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,
Masaai: Nejoki oltung'ani obo, “Olaitoriani, ai kuti pasa lelo oojeu?” Nejoki ninche,

English: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
Masaai: “Entonyok eimu kutuk aji napirik; amu ajoki ntae, eyooki lkumok aaing'oru pee eimu nelaikino.

English: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:
Masaai: Ore ake pee eaku einyo olopeny enkaji aiken kutuk aji, ninteruru aaitashoo te boo ioshiosho kutuk aji ijojo, ‘Olaitoriani, tabolu iyiook.’ Newaliki ninye ntae ajoki, ‘Mayiolo nanu ajo kaji ng'uaa.’

English: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
Masaai: Nintokiki taa aajo, ‘Kitadaate nikitookishote o iyie, ninteng'enishe too nkoitoi ang naalala enkanas.’

English: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
Masaai: Kake kejoki ninye ntae, ‘Ajoki ntae, mayiolo nanu kaji ng'uaa; entalamaki nanu, intae pooki oora laasak loo ntorrok?’

English: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
Masaai: Ore te ine ninchirishiri nionyionyo lala, idolidolo Abraham o Isaak o Yakobo o loibonok le Nkai pooki etii enkitoria e Nkai nimanikiki ate etanang'ayioki ntae auluo.

English: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Naa kepuonu ltung'ana ooing'uaa enkilepunoto o endoyioroto, o looing'uaa kopikop o moikuape aatoni te mesa ti atua enkitoria e Nkai.

English: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, ketii ile siadi ooaku le dukuya, netii ile dukuya ooaku le siadi.”

English: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
Masaai: Ore te ina saa ake nepuonu embata oo Ilfarisayo, nejoki, “Inyo shomo te ne amu keyieu Herode nikiaar tua.”

English: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ninche, “Enchom entiaaki ilo barie, ‘Ng'ura, aaraa nanu loiriruani naishiunye iltamuoyia taata o taaisere o te nkolong e uni; naidip inkolati aainei.

English: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.
Masaai: Kake ore etiu neijia enkoitoi ai ake asuj taata o taaisere o idia olong; amu meidimayu metaa kenang oloiboni le Nkai dikae neme Yerusalem.’

English: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
Masaai: Ooi Yerusalem, Yerusalem naar iloibonok le Nkai ninang too soito lelo likirriwakini. Aikat aja pasa ejo aiturrur inkera inono te nebo anaa enkuku naiturrur inkuoo enyena ti abori inaipuko enyena nimiyieu.

English: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
Masaai: Ng'ura eitaa Enkai enkaji ino mijooni. Naajoki meekure kintoki ae kata adol o tejo, ‘Emayiana ilo olotu te nkarna o Laitoriani!’ ”

English: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.
Masaai: Ore apa te sabato nabo nelo ninye ainos endaa te nkaji o Lfarisayoi obo kitok, te nkolong e nkiyeng'iyeng'ata, neing'or ninche aajur.

English: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.
Masaai: Naa ng'ura, etii oltung'ani dukuya ninye otejia osesen.

English: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
Masaai: Neirorie Yesu lang'eni loo nkitanapat o Lfarisayo, ajoki, “Keishoruno pasa too nkitanapat meishiunyeki oltung'ani te nkolong e sabato anaa ai meishoruno?”

English: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;
Masaai: Kake etigirate ninche. Neibung ilo tung'ani neishiunye, neisho meshomo.

English: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Ai ng'ae te ntae laa te neeta enkurrarru anaa olkiteng otusulakine olkesumet lemesaru nabo kata aitayu, oi aa te nkolong e sabato.”

English: And they could not answer him again to these things.
Masaai: Nelaikino aatawaliki ina.

English: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,
Masaai: Neitoki aliki enkitanyaanyukoto lelo ooitoomoni, etoduaa eneiko tenegelaki ate iwuejitin lorikan ooilepie, nejoki ninche,

English: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;
Masaai: “Te nikimpotokini osirua le nkiama, mitonie ake ewueji enkanyit, melotu ake likae oipoto kitok likilang;

English: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.
Masaai: nelotu ilo oipoto ntae, pokira oare, nikijoki, ‘Nchoo sii iyie ele tung'ani enetonie,’ nintoki iyie adou te nkurruna alo ewueji e abori.

English: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.
Masaai: Kake ore iyie pee kimpoti, totona te wueji nebayie tukul, paa te nelotu ilo oitoomonisho nikijoki, ‘Olchore, ilepa sii iyie;’ nikiyanyitu esiamo pooki niboitare te mesa.

English: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
Masaai: Amu ore pooki oilepie kewan neitadouni, ore oloitadou kewan neilepieki.”

English: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.
Masaai: Nejoki sii ninye ilo oitoomonisho, “Te nincho ltung'ana endaa aashu ntobiraki osirua, mimpot lchoreta linono o lalashera linono o lelo lo lmarei lino aashu lkarsisi le latia ino, pee mikiyooki sii ninche aaitoomon, nikilaaki enda apa nintaasa.

English: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:
Masaai: Kake ore ti nintobir iyie osirua, mpoto laisinak, o ltarrushi o lng'ojiniaa o lmodook,

English: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
Masaai: naa eikimayiani amu mikindim ninche aatalaaki iyie. Aikilaakini kenya ake te mpiunoto e lelo supati.”

English: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Ore pee ening ina obo le lelo ootoni te mesa, nejoki, “Emayiana ilo oyooki adaa te nkitoria e Nkai.”

English: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:
Masaai: Kake etiaka ninye ilo, “Etii apa oltung'ani oitobira osirua kitok, neipot iltung'ana kumok,

English: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.
Masaai: ore pee ebau enkata e ilo sirua neirriwaa olaisiaayiani lenye metiaaki lelo ooipotoki, ‘Wootu; amu eirrag pooki toki!’

English: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.
Masaai: Kake eiterutua pooki aaitaakuuk. Nejo ole dukuya, ‘Ainyang'ua enkurma, naa kalo ake adol; aatasayia tung'ueikiaki nanu.’

English: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.
Masaai: Nejo likae, ‘Ainyang'ua nanu lmong'i tomon naa kalo pee alo asipu; aatasayia tung'ueikiaki nanu.’

English: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.
Masaai: Nejo likae, ‘Enayamie enkitok, nemaidim naa aeu.’

English: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
Masaai: Kaae, nelotu olaisiaayiani aliki olkitok lenye nena. Negoro olopeny enkaji nejoki olaisiaayiani lenye, ‘Tasiooi shomo nkoitoi oo nkaulele e ina anasa, toriku laisinak o ltarrushi o lmodook o lng'ojiniaa.’

English: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo aisiaayiani, ‘Lo kitok, eidipaki aataas ina natejo, neton ake meiputa enkaji.’

English: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
Masaai: Nejoki olkitok ilo aisiaayiani lenye, ‘Shomo nkoitoi sapuki o nkutiti, o lkirinen taaru ltung'ana meetu, o meiputayu enkaji ai.

English: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.
Masaai: Amu ajoki ntae, meishiamisham hoo obo le lelo apa ooipotokoki endaa ai.’ ”

English: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,
Masaai: Ore eiriamariyie olorora kitok, neibelekenyakino nejoki,

English: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
Masaai: “Ore pooki ng'ae olotu enatii lemeibayu menye o ng'otonye, o enkitok enye o nkera, o lalashera o nkanashera, ee o ebaiki enkorrok enye, nemeidim ataa oloiteng'eni lai.

English: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
Masaai: Ore pooki lemenap osalaba lenye naairukurukore, nemeidim ataa oloiteng'eni lai.

English: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
Masaai: Amu kalo pasa linyi, laa te neyieu neshetu oltalet, lemeng'as aton aikenisho pee eyiolou te naa keidip intokitin naata?

English: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
Masaai: Pee meaku ake, ore eidipa aitamanyu nelaikino aidipa, nesukeny pooki ng'ae odol,

English: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
Masaai: ejo, ‘Eiterua ele tung'ani ashetisho, neitu eidip.’

English: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
Masaai: Anaa kalo aiguanani oyieu nerasaki likae aiguanani to larrabal, eitu eng'as aiguana te naa keirish ilenyena iip tomon, iip tikitam le lido oarare?

English: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.
Masaai: Naa te nemeirish, ore eton eitu enyiku olikae, neirriwaki lkiliku aikilikuanu mbaa naaitayu osotua.

English: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
Masaai: Neijia naa etiu, ore ake olinyi lemeibayu pooki toki naata nemeidim ataa olaiteng'eni lai.

English: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?
Masaai: “Ai sidai emunyan; kake amaa te netuyiatuyu emunyan kerrinyokinoyu enkisukut enye?

English: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Masaai: Meitoki aata tipat te nkurma nemeeta to lchala; keiturrarri ake. Oloata nkiyiaa naaning'ie inchoo ening.”

English: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.
Masaai: Ore lasotok le kodi o laasak loo ng'ok neaku kepuonu aanyikaki aainining.

English: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
Masaai: Neing'unyung'uny Ilfarisayo o lasirak ejo, “Keitoomon ele tung'ani ilaasak loo ng'ok neng'arie endaa.”

English: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki ina, neliki ninche ena kitanyaanyukoto:

English: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
Masaai: “Kalo te ntae laa te neeta intare iip pee eimin nabo, lemeing'uaa kunda ntomoni naaudo ti ong'ata, alo aing'oru ina nabo naimina, o menoto ade?

English: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Masaai: Ore pee etum, neiteleiki oloililai, eshipa.

English: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau ang, neiturrurru ilchoreta lenyena o elatia enye ajoki ninche, ‘Matishipata, amu anoto enaduoo ker ai naimina.’

English: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
Masaai: Ajoki ntae, neijia etiu, ai kitok oleng enchipai natumi te shumata to laasani loo ng'ok obo oirridu alang iltung'ana ntomoni naaudo o naaudo supati lemeetayie ninche tipat enkirridunoto.

English: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?
Masaai: “Anaa kaa kitok ina, naa te neeta impisai tomon e nkosholai, pee eimin nabo, nemeinok oltaa neor enkaji neing'oru ade o menoto?

English: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
Masaai: Ore pee etum, neiturrurru nchorueta enyena o elatia ajoki, ‘Matishipata amu anoto enkosholai ai naimina.’

English: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
Masaai: Ajoki ntae, neijia etiu, keshipa sii lmalaika le Nkai to laasani loo ng'ok obo oirridu.”

English: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
Masaai: Nejoki, “Etii apa oltung'ani oata layiok aare;

English: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
Masaai: nejoki oloti menye, ‘Papa, nchooki nanu masaa naaku inaainei.’ Neoriki pokira masaa enyena.

English: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
Masaai: Ore pee elusoo nkuti olong'i, neiturrurru ilo oti masaa pooki naata nemir newalu mpesai nelo enkop nalakua, nelo aishang'itie masaa enyena te ine te nkiwushuush.

English: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip atumuta pooki toki, nelotu olameyu sapuk te ina kop, neiteru atir esumash.

English: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki ina nelo aibung'are olkarsis obo le ina kop, neirriwaa ilo shoo meshomo airrita lbitiro.

English: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
Masaai: Neaku nena kinyat naanya lbitiro eng'uar pee enya; nemeetae oloisho toki.

English: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
Masaai: Kake ore pee eirrash kewan nejo, ‘Kaja pasa laisiaayiak le papa ooata endaa nanya neleku, kake eji nanu ele oya olameyu te ne!

English: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
Masaai: Kainyototo alo enetii papa, najoki, “Papa, ataasa engoki te Nkai o te dukuya iyie,

English: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
Masaai: meekure eishiaakino naaji kara enkerai ino; ntaaki anaa abo le kulo aisiaayiak linono.” ’

English: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
Masaai: Neinyototo nelotu enetii menye. Kake ore eton elakua, nedolu menye neing'urrie, nekuetiki aibung ang'utut.

English: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
Masaai: Nejoki olayioni menye, ‘Papa, ataasa eng'oki te Nkai o te dukuya iyie; meishiaakino naaji kara enkerai ino.’

English: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
Masaai: Kake etiaaka menye laisiaayiak lenyena, ‘Entasieku olkila oisul, enchopoki; naa entipik olgisoi enkaina enye, ninchopokiki namuka nkejek enyena;

English: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
Masaai: entereu olkiteng opir enteyieng, ematishipata emating'idata;

English: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
Masaai: amu ore ena kerai ai ketua apa, nenyaaka apiu.’ Neimina apa, nenyaakaki aatum.

English: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.
Masaai: “Netiooyo ina kata olayioni lenye botor te nkurma; ore pee elotu anyikaki ina aji, nening'oo osinkolio eranyishoi.

English: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
Masaai: Neipot olaisiaayiani obo aikilikuan enaasitai.

English: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.
Masaai: Nejoki, ‘Eewuo olalashe lino, neyiang'aki papaai lino olashe opir, amu enoto menye eserian.’

English: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
Masaai: Kake negoro neany ejing'u. Nepuku menye ailejilej.

English: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
Masaai: Kake etawalikia ninye menye ajoki, ‘She, aaisiaayia nanu iyie kulo arin kumok, neitu ai kata aany aas enikijoki, neitu ai kata kincho nanu olkuoo ninye, pee atum atishipayu tenebo ilchoreta laainei.

English: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
Masaai: Kake ore pee elotu ele ayioni lino, otumutaka masaa inono mulayoni, niyieng'aki olkiteng opir.’

English: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.
Masaai: Nejoki, ‘Enkerai ai, itii oshi ake iyie ene natii naa enino entoki pooki naata.

English: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
Masaai: Keishiaakino pae duoo niking'ida, nikishipa amu ketua apa ele alashe lino, neishu taata, eimina apa nenotoki.’ ”

English: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.
Masaai: Neitoki Yesu ajoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Etii apa oltung'ani karsis oata olaing'urani le nkaji, neitang'ori ilo aing'urani aajo keishang'itie intokitin olkitok lenye.

English: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.
Masaai: Neipotu ninye nejoki, ‘Kaa bae ena natoning'o nikimpirta iyie? Inkenakaki intokitin pooki aainei ning'orita.’

English: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.
Masaai: Nejo olaing'urani ti atua kewan, ‘Kaji aiko, netaa aaoru olkitok lai enking'urata e siaai? Nemaata engolon naturishore, nemaaisho isura aomonisho.

English: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
Masaai: Atayiolo enaas, pee aang'amu ltung'ana too nkajijik enye te naaoruni enking'urata e siaai.’

English: So he called every one of his lord's debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?
Masaai: Kaae, neipot lelo pooki ooatayie olkitok lenye silen maa obo, nejoki oloiturukuo, ‘Kebaa esile niata o lkitok lai?’

English: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
Masaai: Nejo, ‘Iltuleta iip le ilata.’ Nejoki ninye ilo, ‘Tudumu empalai ino e sile, totona tasioki ngero onom.’

English: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.
Masaai: Neitoki ajoki likae, ‘Kebaa esile niata iyie?’ Nejo, ‘Mboreitin iip e nkano.’ Nejoki ninye ilo, ‘Tudumu empalai ino e sile ngero ntomoni isiet.’

English: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
Masaai: Neisis olkitok ilo aing'urani aimonkoni amu kalamas; amu ng'eni nkera e na kop too mbaa enye aalang nkera e wang'an.

English: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
Masaai: “Najoki intae entaiki ate lchoreta te kuna masaa enkop nemesinya, paa kore pee emuta neng'amari intae te nenen neebikieki ntarasi.

English: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
Masaai: “Ore ilo oisiligayu too nkuti neisiligayu sii too nkumok ore olemeisiligayu too nkuti nemeisiligayu too nkumok.

English: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
Masaai: Amaa naa te nimisiligayuyu too masaa nemesinya, aing'ae pasa likintoki aisiligie imasaa e dede?

English: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man's, who shall give you that which is your own?
Masaai: Naa amaa te neitu iaku oloisiligayu too neeiking'a, ai ng'ae likincho nena naara ninono?

English: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
Masaai: Meetae osinka oidim aisiaayia lkituaak aare; eibayu ake obo nenyorru olikae, aashu eibung'are obo nemenaa olikae. Mindimidimi sii intae aaisiaayia Enkai o masaa.”

English: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Ilfarisayo, iloonyor naa masaa neikordod Yesu.

English: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Yesu, “Ntae lelo ooitaakuno irara asipak too ltung'ana, kake eyiolo Enkai ltauja linyi; amu ore ina nailepie ltung'ana naa olminong too nkonyek enyim Enkai.

English: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
Masaai: “Eetae nkitanapat e Musa o loibonok o metabaiki Yohana; ore ebaiki ina kata nelikiori lomon supati le nkitoria e Nkai, nediding'akino pooki ng'ae te ngolon.

English: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
Masaai: Kake elelek pee eish shumata o enkop alang te nelau tipat o ltipoto obo loo nkitanapat e Nkai.

English: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.
Masaai: “Ore oltung'ani ake pooki oituraa enkitok enye neyam ai keloloito. Ore oloyam enkitok natung'uayie olmoruo lenye naa keloloito.”

English: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
Masaai: Nejoki, “Etii apa oltung'ani karsis, oishop olkila onyokie o loibor, nenya olkar nkolong'i pooki.

English: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
Masaai: Neirrag te kutuk aji e nkaji enye oltung'ani aisinani oomonisho oji Lasaro, oata mpaldakani

English: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
Masaai: oyieu neitaraposh kewan too mbelat naasulunye te mesa o lkarsis; neaku kepuonu ldiein aamej mpaldakani enyena.

English: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
Masaai: Neye ilo aisinani nenap ilmalaika aaya olgoo le Abraham. Neye sii ninye olkarsis nenukari;

English: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
Masaai: ore etii Yehanum, eitamei, nedumu nkonyek, nedol Abraham elakua netii Lasaro olgoo lenye.

English: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
Masaai: Neipotisho ajo, ‘Papa Abraham, ing'urrieki, irriu Lasaro meitadoiki olkimojino lenye enkare naaitong'aki olng'ejep lai; amu aainosita ena kima.’

English: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
Masaai: Kake etiaka Abraham, ‘Nakerai, tadamu nchere inoto olkar loo mbaa pooki inchu te nkop, ore Lasaro nenoto sii ninye osina, kake ore taata neitishipi etii ene, nitii iyie osina.

English: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
Masaai: Naa ore etii kuna pooki, etipikaki eng'erem narish iyiook o intae, pee melang'u ole naalo ine nemelang'u oleine alotu ene nikitii.’

English: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house:
Masaai: Nejoki, ‘Aatasayia naa, papa, irriwai ninye metaa olkilikuai te nkang e papa,

English: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
Masaai: amu imiet ilalashera laata, metoliki pee mepuonu sii ninche ene wueji o somit.’

English: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Abraham, ‘Eeta Musa o loibonok le Nkai inchoo ninche ening lelo.’

English: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.
Masaai: Nejoki, ‘A'a papa Abraham mme neijia; te netum olkilikuai loolooinguaa ilootuata, neirridu.’

English: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, ‘Te nemening Musa o loibonok le Nkai, nemening sii ninye oloing'uaa lootuata.’ ”

English: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Meeta nchere mepuonu ntemat e nkarrueisho; kake ee kake aiyia ilo laa ninye eimu!

English: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.
Masaai: Enaikash te neenikini ninye osoit oiutuutishoreki emurt nenang'akini atua enaiposha, alang te neitapong'oo nabo e kuna kutiti.

English: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
Masaai: Entodol ate; te neitarruoo olalashe lino, irorie, ore pee eirridua, tapalaki;

English: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
Masaai: naa te nikinyala nabo, olong kat naapishana, nikingil kat naapishana ajoki, ‘airridua’, nipalaki ake.”

English: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni, “Olaitoriani, toponiki iyiook enkirukoto!”

English: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani, “Te naa iatata napaji enkirukoto naba anaa enkantererai e karadali, indimidimi aatiaaki ele ng'aboli, ‘Tadotunye, tuunokinoyu enaiposha.’ nening intae.

English: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?
Masaai: “Keetae obo linyi oata osinka oturisho aashu oloirritisho, ojoki te nelotu eing'uaa enkurma, ‘Wou nabo kata totona tadaayu?’

English: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
Masaai: Anaa keng'as ake ajoki, ‘Tang'asa taa ntobirakaki endaa, nirretena nikiyaki, ore aidipa atadaayu naokisho; nilo sii iyie adaa niokisho?’

English: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.
Masaai: Ijojo pasa keisho ilo sinka enashe enkaraki nataasa enaitanapaki?

English: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
Masaai: Neijia itiuu sii intae, ore pee ndipidipi aataas inaaitanapaki intae pooki, entejo, ‘Mikira sinkan le tipat; kitaasa ake iyiook enaishiaakino nikiaas.’

English: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
Masaai: Neaku ore te nkoitoi elo Yerusalem neim erishata e Samaria o Galilaya.

English: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
Masaai: Ore ejing enkang nabo, nenang'are ltung'ana tomon ooata enkeeya oo lbolot neitashe ninche te nelakua

English: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
Masaai: nebuaku aajo, “Olaitoriani, Yesu, ing'urrie iyiook.”

English: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
Masaai: Ore pee edol ninye ninche nejoki, “Enchom entoduaai ate too lapolosak.” Ore epuoito neishiu nesika.

English: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
Masaai: Ore pee edol obo lenye ajo eishiunyeki, neshukunye eisisita Enkai to ltoilo sapuk;

English: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
Masaai: neirrabalakino enkop too nkejek e Yesu, ejoki ashe. Naa Osamariyiai ninye.

English: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu, “Ai mme tomon duoo ilaishiunye metisikata? Koree lkulikae pokira ooudo?

English: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
Masaai: Kaji etiu pee eitu etumi obo oshukunye aisho Enkai enashe meteleku ele leeiking'a?”

English: And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye ilo, “Inyo shomo; kintajewuo enkirukoto ino.”

English: And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:
Masaai: Ore pee eikilikuan Ilfarisayo enkata nalotu enkitoria e Nkai, newaliki ajoki ninche, “Melotu enkitoria e Nkai too lmonek oolioo;

English: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
Masaai: nemeyookini aajo, ‘She, nena natii ene!’ aashu ‘Neidia!’ amu ng'ura, etii enkitoria e Nkai atua intae.”

English: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ilooiteng'eni lenyena, “Kepuonu inkolong'i naa ing'uarring'uarra te ni idolidolo enkolong nabo e Nkerai e Tung'ani, nimidolidolo.

English: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
Masaai: Naa kejokini intae, ‘Ng'ura ende!’ aashu, ‘Ng'ura ene!’ Emipuo ake emirubare.

English: For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.
Masaai: Amu ore enatiu enkiwuang'ata naimerlelu neitawang embata nabo e shumata o metabaiki enkae, neijia etiu Enkerai e Tung'ani te ina olong enye.

English: But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation.
Masaai: Kake ore eitu ebau ine eng'asi ake aainyal too nkumok neany iltung'ana le na kata.

English: And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
Masaai: Ore anaa enatiu apa too nkolong'i e Noah, neijia etiu too nkolong'i e Nkerai e Tung'ani.

English: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
Masaai: Kedaai apa, neokishoi, neyamishoi, neishoori meyami, o meeu ina olong natijing'a Noa atua emeli, nelotu oloirrag le nkare nemut ninche pooki.

English: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
Masaai: Neijia sii apa etiu too nkolong'i e Lot aa, kedaae apa, neokishoi, neinyiang'ishoi, nemirishoi, neunishoi, neshetishoi,

English: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Masaai: kake ore ake ina olong natupukuo Lot aing'uaa Sodom neshau enkima oo soito le nkima eing'uaa shumata neidaikie ninche pooki.

English: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
Masaai: Neijia sii etiu ina olong naibalunyeki Enkerai e Tung'ani.

English: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
Masaai: Ore te ina olong, inchoo ilo otii shumata enkaji, oata ntokitin ti atua, milotu ake ajo aya; ore sii ilo otii enkurma mirrinyo ake.

English: Remember Lot's wife.
Masaai: Entadamu enkitok e Lot.

English: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae ojo agolie enkishui enye neiminie, kake ore pooki oiturraa enkishui enye neitopoki.

English: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
Masaai: Ajoki intae, “Ore te ina kewarie keirrag ltung'ana aare erruat nabo; neyai obo, neing'uari olikae.

English: Two women shall be grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
Masaai: Neiutuutisho nkituaak are te nebo to soit obo; neyai nabo neing'uari enkae.

English: Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
Masaai: Netii ltung'ana aare enkurma; neyae obo neing'uari olikae.”

English: And they answered and said unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “Olaitoriani, ae ti aji?” Nejoki, “Enetii empopok, eiturrurrokino lmotonyi.”

English: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
Masaai: Neliki Yesu ninche enkitanyaanyukoto; eitodol inchere eishiaakino ake neomon anaa ake nemenauru.

English: Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man:
Masaai: Nejoki, “Eetae apa te nkanasa nabo olaiguanani lemeure Enkai nemeshilaa tung'ani;

English: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.
Masaai: neetae enkoliai te ina anasa nalotu anaa ake enetii ajoki, ‘Tomituoki sii ake te le mang'atinta.’

English: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;
Masaai: Neng'as aany; ore te siadi nejo openy, ‘Ore hoo nemaure Enkai nemaikenu tung'ani,

English: Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.
Masaai: kake ore amu aateeka ena oliai, kamitu pee maaitoki aisomit te na lotunoto enye.’ ”

English: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.
Masaai: Ejo Olaitoriani, “Entoning enajo ilo aiguanani arruoni.

English: And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?
Masaai: Paa aijojo memitu ninye Enkai ilgelunot lenyena, ooishiraki dama o kewarie? Ijojo keimutie ti alo ninche?

English: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
Masaai: Ajoki intae kemitu asioki. Kake amaa eyia, keinepu pasa Enkerai e Tung'ani te nelotu, eetai enkirukoto te nkop?”

English: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:
Masaai: Etolikio sii ena kitanyaanyukoto lelo ooisilig ate aajo supati te Nkai nemen ilkulikae,

English: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
Masaai: “Eilepa ltung'ana aare aapuo aaomon te nkaji e Nkai, naa Olfarisayoi obo naa olasotoni le kodi olikae.

English: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
Masaai: Neitashe Olfarisayoi neomon te nkorrok enye makewan ejo nji, ‘Na Ai, aaisho enashe amu matiu nanu anaa ikulikae tung'ana, matiu anaa laikonyak ilaimonkok, iloololoito, nematiu sii anaa ele osotu kodi.

English: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
Masaai: Kat are aen kewan aitupukoo te wiki, naishooyo ematua e tomon e pooki toki natum.’

English: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
Masaai: Kake eitasho ninye olasotoni le kodi, te nelakua nemeshumu ninye nkonyek enyena aing'orie shumata kake olgoo eoshiosh, ejo, ‘Na Ai, ing'urrieki nanu olaing'okoni!’

English: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
Masaai: Ajoki intae, etadoyie ele tung'ani alo enkaji enye eishooki esipata alang ilo likae; amu ore pooki ng'ae oilepie kewan neitadouni, ore oloitadou kewan neilepieki.”

English: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
Masaai: Neyakini sii ninche nkera kutiti pee etum aiseyie, ore pee edol ilooiteng'eni ina neisikong ninche.

English: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Kake eipotuo Yesu enetii nejoki, Enchoo nkera epuonu enatii emimitiki; amu enoo naatiu anaa kuna enkitoria e Nkai.

English: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.
Masaai: Edede, ajoki intae, ore pooki ng'ae lemeng'amu enkitoria e Nkai anaa enang'amu enkerai nemejing katukul.

English: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
Masaai: Neikilikuan oltung'ani obo oitoreisho ajoki, “Laai teng'enani supat, kaji aiko pee ajung enkishui oo ntarasi?”

English: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Ainyoo pee kijo kara supat? Meetae hoo obo supat leme Enkai ake.

English: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.
Masaai: Iyiolo iyie nkitanapat. ‘Miloloito, miar likae metua, mipurrisho, minteeniki likae elejare iyanyita minyi o ng'utunyi.’ ”

English: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up.
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, “Aibung'a kuna pooki ebaiki apa ara oti.”

English: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
Masaai: Ore pee ening Yesu ina, nejoki, “Kitong'orikia nabo toki. Timira pooki toki niaata tooriki laisinak, naa itum olchumati te shumata; wou taa tusujuaki.”

English: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.
Masaai: Kake ina ake etoning'o neisinanuo oleng, amu karsis apa naleng.

English: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
Masaai: Neing'or Yesu ninye nejo, “Egol taa duoo to ltung'ani oata imasaa pee ejing enkitoria e Nkai!

English: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Amu elelek te ntames pee eim enaudoto o ltidu alang oltung'ani karsis te nejing enkitoria e Nkai.”

English: And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved?
Masaai: Nejo lelo ootoning'o, “Ai ng'ae naa doi eitajeuni?”

English: And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.
Masaai: Kake etejo, “Ore enemeidimayu too ltung'ana keidimayu te Nkai.”

English: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.
Masaai: Nejo Petero, “Ng'ura, kitung'uaitie iyiook inkang'itie ang nikisuj iyie.”

English: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God's sake,
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Edede, ajoki intae, meetae oltung'ani otung'uayie enkaji, aashu enkitok aashu, lalashera, aashu ntoiwuo aashu nkera, te nkaraki enkitoria e Nkai,

English: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.
Masaai: lemetum nkatitin kumok taata te na kata, ore te idia kata nalotu netum enkishui oo ntarasi.”

English: Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.
Masaai: Nerik lelo tomon o aare enkilepata, nejoki, “Ng'ura, Yerusalem kilep aapuo, naa ore mbaa pooki naatisiraki naaipirta Enkerai e Tung'ani too loibonok le Nkai naa keitabari.

English: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on:
Masaai: Amu keitarasakini ninye Iloreren nesurdaanyi neitaasi enesulare nenotakini;

English: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
Masaai: neoshi ninye neari metua, ore te nkolong e uni nepiu.”

English: And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.
Masaai: Kake eitu hoo ening'u embae nabo e kuna; keisudoro ena bae te ninche, neaku eitu ening'u enajoki.

English: And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:
Masaai: Ore pee enyikaki Yeriko, netii oltung'ani modooni oton te mbata e nkoitoi aomonisho;

English: And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant.
Masaai: ore pee ening olorere egiroo aapuo, neikilikuanisho ajo ainyoo ina.

English: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.
Masaai: Nejokini, “Yesu le Nasaret oimita ene.”

English: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
Masaai: Nebuaku ajo, “Yesu, olayioni le Daudi, ing'urrieki nanu!”

English: And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootii dukuya ninye nebuaaki metigirayu; kake etabuakua ninye aitulus oleng, “Ara Daudi, ing'urrieki!”

English: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,
Masaai: Neitashe Yesu nejo metorikuni enetii; ore pee enyikaki, nejoki,

English: Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
Masaai: “Kaa iyieu naaitaas?” Nejo, “Olaitoriani, kayieu nadolishoyu.”

English: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Todolisho; kinchiunye enkirukoto ino.”

English: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.
Masaai: Nedolishoyu nabo kata nesuj ninye, eisisita Enkai; ore lelo tung'ana pooki, pee edol ina, neisis Enkai.

English: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
Masaai: Ore pee ejing Yesu Yeriko, nepolos alo.

English: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
Masaai: Netii oltung'ani oji Sakayo; naa olkitok loo lasotok le kodi, naa karsis.

English: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
Masaai: Neing'oru eneiko pee edol Yesu ajo ai ng'ae, nelaikino, te nkaraki olorere, amu dorrop ninye.

English: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
Masaai: Neipirri aituruk neked o lng'aboli pee edol, amu ine wueji, eim Yesu.

English: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
Masaai: Ore pee ebaiki Yesu ine neraposhu nkonyek nejoki, “Sakayo, tasieku tadou; amu enkaji ino ade taata ajing.”

English: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
Masaai: Nesieku taa nedou neng'amu te ng'ida.

English: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
Masaai: Ore pee edol ninche neing'unyung'uny pooki ejo, “Eshomo meitoomoni te nkaji o ltung'ani aing'okoni.”

English: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
Masaai: Neinyototo Sakayo nejoki Olaitoriani, “Ng'ura, Olaitoriani, aitorit aor imasaa aainei naisho laisinak naa te neetae hoo oltung'ani latooruo toki enye, te nkeleekisho, nalaaki katitin ong'uan.”

English: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninye, “Eewuo taata ena olong enjeunoto ena aji, amu ole Abraham sii doi ninye.

English: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
Masaai: Amu eewuo Enkerai e Tung'ani aing'oru pee eitajeu ilooimina.”

English: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.
Masaai: Ore einining'ito ltung'ana nena, neitoki Yesu aliki ninche enkitanyaanyukoto, amu etinyikaka ninye Yerusalem naa kejo ninche etaa keibalunyeki enkitoria e Nkai te ina kata.

English: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki ina, nejoki, “Eshomo olaiguanani obo kitok enkop nalakua meishori enkitoria neshukunye.

English: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.
Masaai: Neipot isinkan lenyena tomon, neisho ake obo empisai e sahabu nejoki, ‘Etaasishore o maeu.’

English: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.
Masaai: Kake ore enkaraki naiba ltung'ana le ina kop enye ninye, neitusuj olkilikuai ejo, ‘Mikiyieu neitore iyiook ele tung'ani.’

English: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
Masaai: Ore pee eitu, eidipa atang'amai enkitoria, neipot lelo sinkan lenyena apa ootung'eikia impesai, meetu, pee eyiolou dupoto nanoto te nkinyang'a.

English: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.
Masaai: Neituruku ole dukuya, ejo, ‘Olaitoriani, enoto ropiyiani inono tomon kulie katitin tomon.’

English: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
Masaai: Nejoki, ‘Intobira, osinka supat! Ore enkaraki nitaa oloisiligayu too nkuti oleng, iyooki aitore nkanas tomon!’

English: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.
Masaai: Nelotu ole aare, ejo, ‘Olaitoriani, enoto ropiyiani inono kulie tomon katitin imiet.’

English: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.
Masaai: Nejoki ilo, ‘Intore sii iyie nkanas imiet.’

English: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:
Masaai: Neitoki alotu likae sinka ejo. ‘Olaitoriani, nena empisai ina e sahabu naisudoyie apa te nkarasha;

English: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.
Masaai: amu iyie aturia, amu ira oltung'ani ogol pukunoto; odumu ineitu irragie, nidung neme iyie otuno!’

English: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:
Masaai: Nejoki ninye, ‘Ekaadung'oki naa enkiguana te nkiroroto ino makewan, lo sinka torrono! Iyiolo apa ajo kara oltung'ani ogol pukunoto, odumu ineitu airragie, nasotu ineitu aun?

English: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?
Masaai: Kaji naa etiu pee eitu ishum impesai aainei te mbenki, pee te na lotu, natum nena aainei o naaiu?’

English: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.
Masaai: Nejoki lelo ooitashe te ine, ‘Entooru ina pisai e sahabu naata ninye enchoo elde oata tomon.’

English: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)
Masaai: (Nejoki ninche ninye, ‘Olaitoriani, keeta ninye ropiyiani tomon katitin tomon!’)

English: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, ‘Ajoki intae, ore pooki ng'ae oata keponikini aaisho; kake ore elde lemeeta, keoruni ninye ina kiti naata.

English: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.
Masaai: Kake ore ninche kulo mang'ati laainei, apa lemeyieu naitore, eyau entaar metuata tene natii.’ ”

English: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip atejo neijia, negiroo alo ailepaki Yerusalem.

English: And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
Masaai: Neaku ore pee enyikaki Betfage o Betania, to ildoinyo oji oloo Loirienito, neirriwaa ilooiteng'eni lenyena aare,

English: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.
Masaai: ejo, “Enchom enda ang naipirare intae, ore pee ijing'ijing'i nidolidolo enkurrarru naena, neitu ae kata eked oltung'ani; ore pee ilakuku nireuu ene.

English: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.
Masaai: Naa te neikilikuani intae aajoki, ‘Oo pee ilakuku?’ Entejo nji, ‘Olaitoriani oata enadung'ie.’ ”

English: And they that were sent went their way, and found even as he had said unto them.
Masaai: Nepuo lelo ooirriwayioki neinepu etiu anaa ina natiaaka.

English: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?
Masaai: Ore elaku olkurrarru, nejoki lopeny, “Kaji etiu pee ilakuku olkurrarru?”

English: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.
Masaai: Nejo ninche, “Olaitoriani oata enadung'ie.”

English: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus thereon.
Masaai: Nerewaki Yesu, ore pee eirotoki enkurrarru nkilani enye, neitaked Yesu,

English: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
Masaai: ore elo ekedito osikiria, neisalaash ninche nkilani enye te nkoitoi.

English: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;
Masaai: Ore pee enyiku, to loshong'ishong'i lo ldoinyo loo Loirienito, neiteru aang'ida olorora pooki oo looiteng'eni neisis Enkai to ltoilo sapuk too nkiaasin e ngolon naatoduaa,

English: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
Masaai: ejo, “Emayiana Olaiguanani olotu te nkarna o Laitoriani, Eseriani te keper naa enkitoo te Nkai!”

English: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.
Masaai: Nejoki kulikae loo Lfarisayo ootii atua olorere, “Olaiteng'enani, intigira ilooiteng'eni linono.”

English: And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.
Masaai: Newaliki ajoki, “Ajoki intae, ore te negira kulo nebuaku ninche kulo soito.”

English: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
Masaai: Ore pee enyikaki ina anasa nedol neishiraki;

English: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
Masaai: ejo, “Ooi te naa iyiolo sii ake te le kekun imbaa naayau eseriani! Kake ore taata keisudoro medol inkonyek inono.

English: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
Masaai: Amu kepuonu nkolong'i, nikintamuat lmang'ati linono oolkerenket, nikipunyaki too nkaloli pooki,

English: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
Masaai: nikinang'ie enkop, iyie taa, o nkera niata ti atua, nemeetae osoit obo ti atua iyie oing'uari eiteleikino olikae; amu eitu iyiolou olkekun likibaikinye Enkai.”

English: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;
Masaai: Nejing enkaji e Nkai neiteru aaraa lelo oomirisho

English: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.
Masaai: ejoki ninche, “Etisiraki aajo, ‘Ore enkaji ai keaku ene nkomono;’ kake intaa intae enkapune oo laisimak.”

English: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,
Masaai: Neiteng'enisho anaa ake te nkaji e Nkai. Neing'oru ilapolosak kituaak, o lasirak o ltung'ana kituaak le ilo orere pee eidaikie ninye;

English: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.
Masaai: kake etalaita enaas, amu eteenikinote ltung'ana pooki irorei lenyena.

English: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,
Masaai: Ore nabo olong, eiteng'enita ltung'ana nelikioo lomon supati te nkaji e Nkai, nepuonu lapolosak kituaak o lasirak o lpayiani enetii

English: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?
Masaai: nejoki ninye, “Toliki iyiook ae te ngolon e ng'ae ias iyie kuna baa, ae ng'ae likincho ena golon?”

English: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:
Masaai: Newaliki ninye ajoki, “Kaikilikuan sii nanu intae embae nabo; entolikioki,

English: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?
Masaai: amaa apa enkibatisa e Yohana ai shumata eing'uaa, anaa ltung'ana?”

English: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?
Masaai: Neiguana maate ejo, “Amaa tenikijo, ‘Shumata eing'uaa’, nejoki iyiook, ‘Oo naa pee eitu irukuruku?'

English: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.
Masaai: Kake ti nikijo, ‘Iltung'ana eing'uaa,’ nenang iyiook kulo tung'ana pooki too soito; amu eyiolo too ltauja aajo oloiboni le Nkai Yohana.”

English: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.
Masaai: Newaliki aajoki, mikiyiolo eneing'uaa.

English: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Maliki sii nanu intae eneing'uaa engolon naasie kuna baa.”

English: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
Masaai: Neiter aliki olorere ena kitanyaanyukoto, “Etuno oltung'ani enkurma oo lng'anayio, neisho laramatak meisilenoi nelo ai kop nebik enkata naado.

English: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau enkata, neirriu osinka airriwaki ilaramatak, meishoo ematua oo lng'anayio le ina kurma; kake eidong'o lelo ooisilenoitie ninye nerriny too nkaik naarook.

English: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
Masaai: Neirriwaa likae sinka; near sii ilo nesul, nearaa too nkaik naarook.

English: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.
Masaai: Neitoki ake airriwaa oli okuni. nepik ilbaa ilo nearaa ong'ata.

English: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.
Masaai: Nejo olopeny enkurma ina oolng'anayio, ‘Kaji aiko? Olayioni lai kirotet airriwaa; kebaiki neyanyit ninye.’

English: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
Masaai: Kake ore pee edol lelo ooisilenoitie ninye, nejokino maate, ‘Ele doi olajung'oni, mataar pee eaku enaang enjung'ore.’

English: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?
Masaai: Nearaa auluo enkurma near metua. Kaa pasa kenya eitaasi ninche olopeny enkurma?

English: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.
Masaai: Kelotu aidaikie lelo ooisilenoitie neisho kulikae ina kurma.” Ore pee ening ninche ina nejo, “Taba meiwuang'a!”

English: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?
Masaai: Kake eing'ura Yesu ninche nejo, “Kaa naa ena nasira, ‘Ilo soit otanyaita lashetak otaa ole lukunya o lmairroto'?

English: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
Masaai: Ore pooki ng'ae osulakino ilo soit negiligil aitaa mpurdat; kake ore ake olourokino ninye nerrar tukul.”

English: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.
Masaai: Neiteru lasirak o lapolosak kituaak aajo matipik inkaik te ina saa, kake etureita olorere; amu etoduaa aajo ninche eipirie ina kitanyaanyukoto.

English: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.
Masaai: Metaa neing'or ninche ninye neirriwaki ilaikeernok ooitaakuno supati te Nkai, pee etum aawaita kuna naajo, netum aaitarasaki enkitoria o enkiguana o lbalusui.

English: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any, but teachest the way of God truly:
Masaai: Neikilikuan ninche aajoki, “Olaiteng'enani, kiyiolo aajo iro iyie ninteng'enisho too sipat, metii enyorrakino, kake iutu iyie enkoitoi e Nkai te sipata.

English: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?
Masaai: Keishiaakino neishori Kaisari kodi ana aimeishiaakino?”

English: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?
Masaai: Kake etayiolo ninye enkeleekisho enye, nejoki,

English: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Caesar's.
Masaai: “Entoduaaki empisai. Ai ng'ae esirakino naa kole ng'ae olkigeroto oata?” Nejoki, “Ole Kaisari.”

English: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Enchoo naa Kaisari inaara ine Kaisari, ninchosho Enkai inaara ine Nkai.”

English: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.
Masaai: Nelaikino aaibung'a ninye etii olorere te nena naatejo; kake eing'asiate ninche te nena naawalu negira.

English: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there is any resurrection; and they asked him,
Masaai: Nepuonu Sadukayo enetii, lelo apa oojo meetae empiunoto,

English: Saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man's brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
Masaai: neikilikuan embae nabo, aajo, “Olaiteng'enani, etisiraka iyiook Musa nchere te neye olalashe oltung'ani, oata enkitok nemeeta nkera, neya ake ilo tung'ani ina kitok pee eiki olalashe nkera.

English: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
Masaai: Eetae apa ilalashera oopishana; neyam ole dukuya enkitok, neye meeta nkera;

English: And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.
Masaai: neiko neijia oli aare,

English: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: and they left no children, and died.
Masaai: neyam sii oli okuni, neiko neijia pokira oopishana neitu eing'uaa nkera neye.

English: Last of all the woman died also.
Masaai: Ore te siadi neye sii ninye enkitok.

English: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.
Masaai: Amaa kenya te mpiunoto, etiu neijia, keaku ene ng'ae ina kitok? Amu eyama pokira oopishana ninye.”

English: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
Masaai: Nejoki Yesu ninche, “Eyamisho neishoori meyami nkera e na kata;

English: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:
Masaai: kake ore lelo oishiaakino nebaiki ina kata nebaiki sii empiunoto oo lootuata meyamisho nemeyami,

English: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
Masaai: amu metiooyo eitoki aaye, amu etiu anaa lmalaika neaku nkera e Nkai, aaku nkera e mpiunoto.

English: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
Masaai: Kake ore nchere epiu ilootuata, ketuutua ninye Musa, te ine neigerore mbaa osanag teine neipotie ninye Olaitoriani ajo Enkai e Abraham naa Enkai e Isaak, naa Enkai e Yakobo.

English: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.
Masaai: Mme naa Enkai oo lootuata, kake enoo looishu; amu ninye eishuyie pooki.”

English: Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.
Masaai: Newal embata oo lasirak aajo, “Olaiteng'enani, iroro aitobiraki.”

English: And after that they durst not ask him any question at all.
Masaai: Amu eitu eitoki aaitieu aaikilikuana ae bae.

English: And he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David's son?
Masaai: Kake etiaka ninye ninche, “Kaji etiu pee eji Kristo enkerai e Daudi?

English: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
Masaai: Amu etejo Daudi openy te mbuku e Olkerempe le Nkai, ‘Etiaka Olaitoriani Olaitoriani lai, Totona te nkaina ai e tatene

English: Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.
Masaai: o metaba anaa naitaa ilmang'ati linono olorika loo nkejek inono.’

English: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?
Masaai: Metaa eipoto Daudi ninye ajo Olaitoriani; kaji eiko pee eitoki aaku enkerai enye?”

English: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,
Masaai: Nejoki ilooiteng'eni lenyena ening'ito olorere pooki,

English: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;
Masaai: “Entorrip ate too lasirak, oopuaya eishopito lkilani ooado, nenyor neirorokini too neeimishoreki nenyor ilorikan sidain aaisul ti atua nkajijik e ntumo, o wuejitin enkanyit too mashoi,

English: Which devour widows' houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.
Masaai: oonya aamut nkajijik oo nkolia neitaakuno neitoodor enkomono e Nkai. Etum ninche enkiguana narrish oleng.”

English: And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.
Masaai: Neshumu Yesu nkonyek nedol ilkarsisi eitadoiki nkishorot enye osanduku oshumishoreki;

English: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
Masaai: nedol sii enkoliai aisinani eitadoiki ielai are naanyokie.

English: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
Masaai: Nejo, “Edede ajoki intae, ena oliai aisinani natipika aisul too lkulikae pooki;

English: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.
Masaai: amu eishorutua pooki te nkumoi oo naata, kake eishorua ninye to sina lenye pooki toki naata.”

English: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,
Masaai: Ore eimaki kulikae enkaji e Nkai, eneikunaki teneikodi too soito sidain o too nkishorunot, nejoki,

English: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
Masaai: “Ore anaa kuna tokitin nidolitata, kepuonu nkolong'i nemeitokini aata osoit obo oiteleikino olikae lemesulakini enkop.”

English: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?
Masaai: Neikilikuan aajoki, “Olaiteng'enani, kanu eaku kuna baa, naa ainyoo olmonekie outu ajo etaa ebau?”

English: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.
Masaai: Nejo, “Entodol meitapong'ori intae; amu kepuonu lkumok te nkarna ai, ejo, ‘Nanu ilo? Etinyikua enkata!’ Emisuj intae ninche.

English: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.
Masaai: Naa ore pee ining'ining'i njorin o long'oling'oli, emiureisho, amu eituruku ake nena aatiu neijia, kake melotu enkiting'oto e nkop nabo kata.”

English: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Kedumakino olosho likae osho, nedumakino enkitoria enkae kitoria;

English: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.
Masaai: nelotu olokirikiri le nkop too wuejitin kumok, nelotu olameyu o olmeitai too wuejitin kumok, naa kepuonu ntabo naaitureisho o lmonek ooing'uaa shumata,

English: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake.
Masaai: kake ore eton eitu ebau nena pooki keibung'i intae, neinyali, neitarasakini intae nkajijik e ntumo e korokoroni, nerikokini intae laiguanak o lbalusuni te nkaraki enkarna ai.

English: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.
Masaai: Neaku te intae enkata nimbalielie enkirukoto inyi.

English: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:
Masaai: Entumut ena nabo too ltauja linyi nchere, emidamu eitu ebau enkata aajo kaa kiwal;

English: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.
Masaai: amu nanu oisho intae enkutuk o eng'eno, nemeetae hoo obo le lelo mang'ati linyi oidim airisha aashu ewal.

English: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.
Masaai: Keitarasaa intae intoiwuo o lalashera o ltung'ana lo lmarei o lchoreta, naa keari kulikae linyi metuata;

English: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake.
Masaai: neibayu intae pooki te nkaraki enkarna ai.

English: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.
Masaai: Kake meimin ninye olpapita obo loo lukuny inyi.

English: In your patience possess ye your souls.
Masaai: Kake te ng'iriata inyi itumutumu enkishui.

English: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.
Masaai: “Kake ore pee idolidolo Yerusalem etamana mpuot, entayiolo aajo etinyikua emutata enye.

English: Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
Masaai: Ore ina kata lootii Yudea esikaki ldoinyo, ore lelo ootii atua ina anasa nepuku aapuo, nemejing'u lelo ootioyo ti ong'ata;

English: For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
Masaai: amu nkolong'i e nkitamioto kuna, naabaya mbaa pooki naatisiraki.

English: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
Masaai: Woi nena naanuta o naaitanakisho te nena olong'i! Amu keaku kitok osina o engoro e Nkai nadoiki kulo tung'ana;

English: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
Masaai: kedung'ori aauroo too lalema, neriki atua loreren pooki meshomo sinkaisho; neitiamie Yerusalem Iloreren, o metaba anaa neitabari nkatitin oo Loreren.

English: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;
Masaai: “Naa kepuku ntabo e nkolong o lapa o lakir, ore te nkop neinepu osina loreren o enking'aing'ai neikurrukur enaiposha o lopir le nkare,

English: Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.
Masaai: neiterriaa ltung'ana te nkiputukuny 3 nena baa naapuonu enkop; amu keigirigiro engolon pooki e shumata.

English: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
Masaai: Ore te ina kata nedoluni Enkerai e Tung'ani elotu te ngolon te nkatampoi o te nkisisa kitok.

English: And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.
Masaai: Ore taa pee eng'as aabau kuna baa eng'ura shumata entushumu lukuny inyi, amu etinyikua esarunoto inyi.”

English: And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;
Masaai: Neliki enkitanyaanyukoto ajoki. “Eng'ura olng'aboli o lkeek pooki;

English: When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.
Masaai: ore ake pee eiteru aaitayu mbenek, niduaakiki ate nchere etinyikua olodalu.

English: So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.
Masaai: Neijia naa etiu, ore pee idolidolo eaku kuna baa, entayiolo entejo etinyikua enkitoria e Nkai.

English: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.
Masaai: Edede, ajoki intae, meishari ena ishoi eitu eitabari nena pooki.

English: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
Masaai: Keish shumata o enkop, kake meish ororei lai hoo obo.

English: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
Masaai: “Kake eng'ura ate pee meaku ltauja linyi biitia o emerai o nkolati e na kop, neirrashu intae ina olong neluam intae anaa orreshet;

English: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Masaai: amu neijia etiu kedoiki lelo pooki, oomanya enkop pooki.

English: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
Masaai: Kake enchololoto intae inkatitin pooki, niomonunu meishori intae engolon nipaashieshie nena naapuonu, pee intasheshe te dukuya Enkerai e Tung'ani.”

English: And in the day time he was teaching in the temple; and at night he went out, and abode in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.
Masaai: Neiteng'enisho dama nkolong'i pooki te nkaji e Nkai, kake ore kewarie neipang alo airrag oldoinyo oji oloo Loirienito.

English: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, for to hear him.
Masaai: Ore enasirie neyooki ltung'ana pooki aapuo aainining ninye te nkaji e Nkai.

English: Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
Masaai: Nenyiku osirua loo Mukateni neitu oji Pasaka.

English: And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people.
Masaai: Neing'oru ake lapolosak kituaak o lasirak eneiko pee ear metua; paa olorere eure.

English: Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
Masaai: Nejing Shetani Yudas oji Iskariot, olaa obo le lelo tomon o aare;

English: And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.
Masaai: nedumunye alo aning'ore lapolosak kituaak o sikarini, aitoriak eneiko pee ekaldaa Yesu te ninche.

English: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.
Masaai: Neshipa ninche nejoki keisho mpesai.

English: And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.
