English: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
Masaai: Kake etiaaka Paulo ninche, “Etaara iyiook te dukuya olorere, eitu eiguanareki iyiook, nikira sii ile Roma, netanang'akita iyiook korokoroni; neyieu taata neitupuku iyiook too nkurrat? Mme neijia; kake enchoo epuonu ninche maate aaitupuku iyiook.”

English: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
Masaai: Nepuo lelo sikarini aainosaki iladung'ok le nkiguana lelo rorei, neureishoyu, etoning'o aajo ile Roma ninche.

English: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
Masaai: Nepuonu aasai ninche; ore pee eitupuku, neikilikuan te naa kepuo aaing'uaa ina anasa.

English: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
Masaai: Nepuku ninche te korokoroni, nepuo enkaji e Lidia: ore pee eidip aatodol ilalashera, neilejilej ninche nepuo.

English: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
Masaai: Nepuo aaimaa Amfipoli o Apolonia o meetu Sesalonike, netii ine enkaji oo Lyahudi e ntumo.

English: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
Masaai: Nelo Paulo nejing ine anaa olkuaak lenye. Ore te rishata oo wikii uni neishankarrarre too lkigerot,

English: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
Masaai: eliki enajo neitadedeyie ti atua ninche nchere meeta apake kata nemeinosieki Kristo osina, neitoki ake apiu too lootuata. Nejoki, “Naa ele Yesu laliki intae, ninye doi Kristo.”

English: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
Masaai: Nenyorraa kulikae lenye nena neaku ile nkalo e Paulo o Sila, naa neijia etiu Lyunani kumok ooserem Enkai, neme kuti sii ninche nkituaak arikok naairuko.

English: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
Masaai: Kake eishoo ninche Lyahudi te nkaraki olom nepuo aasotu ilarruok olwushuush too neemirishoreki, nesotu esiamo neliman ina anasa pooki; nerasaki enkaji e Yason, ejo pee erikoki ninche lelo tung'ana.

English: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
Masaai: Ore pee elau, neikurtutaa Yason o kulikae le lelo alashera aayaki ilaitoriak le ina anasa, ebuakita aajo, ore “Kulo tung'ana ooijulujulo enkop aing'orie shumata abori neetuo sii ene;

English: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
Masaai: naa Yason otang'amua arik enkaji enye: neetuo pooki aas inemeishoruno aakesh Kaisari, ejo eji eetae likae aiguanani oji Yesu.”

English: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
Masaai: Neng'uyan ninche ilo orere o lelo aitoriak le ina anasa pee ening ilo rorei.

English: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
Masaai: Ore pee eya te Yason o te lelo kulikae mpesai naaisiligieki, neishori meshomo.

English: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
Masaai: Ore ake pee emutu neisikie nabo kata lelo alashera Paulo o Silas kewarie meshomo Berea. Ore pee ebaya ninche ine nepuo aajing enkaji oo Lyahudi e ntumo.

English: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
Masaai: Neaku kening'isho ninche lelo metiu anaa ile Sesalonike, amu etang'amutua ilo rorei eyieu to lokiyo sapuk, nejur ilkigerot anaa ake pee edol te naa ai neijia etiu kuna baa.

English: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
Masaai: Neaku eiruko lkumok lene te nkaraki ina, o meiruko sii ninche nkituaak neme kuti naa nkarikok o Lyunani, o lewa leme kuti sii ninche.

English: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
Masaai: Ina ake etoning'o Lyahudi le Sesalonike nchere etolikioyie Paulo ororei le Nkai te Berea, neitoki ake aapuonu ine, neing'oling'ol olorere aaitanyamal.

English: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
Masaai: Nerik nabo kata lelo alashera Paulo meshomo o meitabaiki enaiposha: neng'as ninche Silas o Timoteo aabik te ine.

English: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
Masaai: Ore lelo ootoriko Paulo neitabau Atene. Ore eitanap Paulo ninche aisho olkilikuai oyaki Silas o Timoteo metasieku ine, nerrinyo aapuo.

English: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
Masaai: Ore eanyita Paulo ninche te Atene, nenyamalu naleng te kewan enye etoduaa eneba enkumoi oo nkitanyaanyukot naaitaai nkaitin te ina anasa.

English: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
Masaai: Neishankarrarre Lyahudi o lkulikae tung'ana ooserem Enkai te nkaji e ntumo, o te nemirishoreki anaa ake, ilooba anaa lootumore.

English: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
Masaai: Neetae sii kulikae ang'eni te ine, ooji ile Epikureo looji ile Stoiko oonotore ninye. Nejo kulikae lenye, “Kejo aa ele shoshoroi?” Nejo kulikae, “Ketiu anaa nkaitin eeiking'a elimu;” naa enkaraki natolimuo Yesu o empiunoto.

English: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
Masaai: Metaa ninche ootudumutua nerik olkiu te wueji neji Areopago, ejoito, “Kaa kiteng'enare ng'ejuk ena nilimu amu eikiyieu nikiyiolou?

English: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
Masaai: Amu eijo keitu ae kata kining kuna baa nilimu: kiyieu naa nikiyiolou enajo kuna baa.”

English: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
Masaai: (Naa ore lelo tung'ana pooki le Atene o lomon ootii ina anasa, meeta ai naas neme ketoni ake aairo, einosakino aashu einining'u embae ake pooki ng'ejuk.

English: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
Masaai: Metaa neitashe Paulo te dukuya ilo kiu le Areopago, nejo, “Lo lewa le Atene, adolita ajo ore te pooki oitoi irara ilaseremak oleng.

English: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
Masaai: Amu ore aloito, nadol olperere lo lasar oigero ajo nji, ‘ENE ENKAI NEMEYIOLOI.’ Ore naa ina Ai niserememe miyiololo ninye ena naliki nanu intae.

English: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
Masaai: Ore ina Ai naitobira enkop o ntokitin pooki, aa ninye taa Olaitoriani le shumata enkop, mme nkajijik naaitobiri too nkaik emany ninye.

English: Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
Masaai: Neme too nkaik eisiaai ninye, anaa keeta ae toki nayieu, naa ninye sii doi oisho pooki ng'ae enkishui, o enkiyang'et, o pooki toki.

English: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
Masaai: Naa te ilo obo eitobira iloreren pooki te nkop, metamanya oriong e nkop. Naa ketang'asa te dukuya aitaiki rishat o lpolosien oorish ineemany.

English: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
Masaai: Neitaa ninche peyie etum aaing'oru Enkai, pee ebaiki ake neirrapirrapu, nebaiki netum. Hoo nemelakuaniki ninye hoo obo lang,

English: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
Masaai: amu, ‘Ninye kinchuyie, naa ninye kipuoyie, naa ninye pee kira.’ Anaa enatejo likae aranyani linyi otejo, ‘Kira sii iyiook eishoi enye.’

English: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device.
Masaai: Te nikira naa eishoi e Nkai, emikintoki naa ake aajo eji ketiu empukunoto e Nkai anaa saabu, anaa enkosholai, anaa osoit oguetu enkarriyiano arashu endamunoto olosek le tung'ani.

English: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
Masaai: Enkaraki ina pee eimula Enkai enkong'u te nena katitin e modai; kake ore taata eitanapa ajoki ltung'ana te pooki wueji, ‘Embelekenyata entung'uai nkoitoi inyi e nkarruoisho.’

English: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
Masaai: Amu eidipa ninye atuuno enkolong, nayooki aiguanare enkop too sipat, te ilo tung'ani otegelua. Naa ninye eitadedeyie ninye too ltung'ana pooki, eitopiwuo ilo aitung'uaa ilootuata.”

English: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.
Masaai: Ore pee ening ninche eimaki empiunoto oo lootuata neikordod kulikae; kake etii kulikae lenye ootejo, “Kintoki ake aainining iyie te likae kekun.”

English: So Paul departed from among them.
Masaai: Metaa nepuku Paulo alo aing'uaa.

English: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
Masaai: Kake etii kulikae ootaa le nkalo enye neiruk: ilootii Dionisio, obo le lelo le Areopago, o enkitok naji Damaris, o kulikae ake.

English: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
Masaai: Ore pee elusoo kuna nedumunye Paulo te Atene, nelotu Korinto.

English: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
Masaai: Netum Olyahudi obo oji Akuila, laa oinoti le Ponto, naa enalotunye det eing'uaa Italia te nebo enkitok enye Prisila, enkaraki naitanapishe olaiguanani kitok Klaudius meshomo Lyahudi pooki aaing'uaa Roma. Nelo Paulo enetii ninche;

English: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
Masaai: naa ore amu keng'ar enkarriyiano e siaai enye, nebik te nebo ninche, neasisho; amu ilaitobirak loo emai ninche.

English: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
Masaai: Neiguana anaa ake te nkaji e ntumo too nkolong'i e sabato ejo ayietu Ilyahudi o Lyunani meiruko.

English: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
Masaai: Ore pee edou Sila o Timoteo te Makedonia, nesheikino ninye Paulo elikioroto o rorei neishakenoki too Lyahudi nchere Kristo Yesu.

English: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
Masaai: Ore pee egilunore ninche maate ninye nemor, neipiripiroki Paulo ilkilani lenyena nejoki, “Meeu osarge linyi shumata lukuny inyi. Maata nanu entioto; ore ebaiki taata iltung'ana loo Loreren alo enetii.”

English: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man's house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
Masaai: Nelo aing'uaa lelo, nejing enkaji o ltung'ani oji Tito Yusto, oserem ninye Enkai, otashare enkaji enye ene ntumo.

English: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
Masaai: Ore Krispas laa ninye oitore ina aji e ntumo, neiruk Olaitoriani, neiruk sii enkaji enye pooki; ore pee ening Ilkorintio kumok neiruk neibatisae.

English: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
Masaai: Nejoki Olaitoriani Paulo nabo olong kewarie eirura, “Miureishoyu, iroro, nimigira;

English: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
Masaai: amu atii nanu te nebo iyie. Nemeetae oltung'ani likibaiki aitaas entorrono: amu kumok iltung'ana laainei te na anasa.”

English: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
Masaai: Nebik Paulo te ine olari obo o lapaitin ile, eiteng'enita ninche to rorei le Nkai.

English: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
Masaai: Ore pee eitaai Galio olbalusui loo Roma te Akaia, nedumakino Lyahudi pooki Paulo te nebo, nerik olorika le nkiguana,

English: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
Masaai: ejoito, “Keyiataki ele tung'ani olorere pee eserem Enkai te nkoitoi nemeishoruno too nkitanapat.”

English: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
Masaai: Kake ore ejo Paulo abol enkutuk, nejoki Galio Lyahudi, “Te nesipa naaji ajo kembae e ntorroni aashu ene karrueisho, lo Yahudi, naa anaata iatata esipata nang'iri ainining intae.

English: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
Masaai: Kake te na kenchankar oo rorei o nkarn o nkitanapat inyi, eng'urai oopeny; mayieu nanu naaku olarishani loo mbaa neeijo nena.”

English: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
Masaai: Nearaa aitung'uaa olorika le nkiguana.

English: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
Masaai: Nesar pooki aaibung Sostene, ilo apa oitore enkaji e ntumo oo Lyahudi, neidong te nkalo o lorika le nkiguana. Neitu hoo eshilaa ninye Galio nena baa pooki.

English: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
Masaai: Ore te siadi kuna, enyaaka abik nkolong'i kumok etulusoitie nena, neitanapare lalashera, neked emeli alo Siria, neiriamariyie Prisila o Akuila. Netabarnoki te Kenkrea: amu einosa olmumai.

English: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
Masaai: Nepuonu ninche Efeso, neing'uaa ninche te ine. Kake eshomo Paulo ajing enkaji e ntumo neishankarrarre Lyahudi.

English: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
Masaai: Ore pee eji maiboo metobiko oleng, neany;

English: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
Masaai: kake etudumunye nejoki ninche, “Kaitoki ake ashukunye, te neyieu Enkai.” Neked emeli alo Efeso.

English: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
Masaai: Ore pee elang'aki Kaisaria, neilep airoroki esirit, neitoki adoyio alo Antiok.

English: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
Masaai: Ore pee ebik nkuti olong'i te ine, nedumunye alo neimaa olkirine le Galatia, o Prigia aruk nenen, eitagol ilooiteng'eni pooki.

English: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
Masaai: Neetae Olyahudi oji Apolo, laa te Aleksantria eini, nelotu elo Efeso; naa arriyia to rorei naa magilani too lkigerot.

English: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
Masaai: Neiteng'enaki apa ilo tung'ani te nkoitoi e o Laitoriani; naa ore amu oltung'ani oisusunkat oleng, neiro neiteng'enisho abaraki mbaa e Yesu, hoo naa enkibatisa e Yohana ake eyiolo

English: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
Masaai: neiteru airo te mpijan te nkaji e ntumo. Kake ore pee einining Prisila o Akuila, nerik enkaji enye, neibalakinye Enkoitoi e Nkai aabaraki.

English: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
Masaai: Ore pee eyieu ninye, nelang alo Akaia, neitagol ilalashera ninye nesiraki ilooiteng'eni empalai metang'amu ninye: ore pee ebaya Akaia neretu naleng lelo laa te nkaraki empiris e Nkai pee eiruko:

English: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
Masaai: amu etigilua ninye Ilyahudi te ng'olong naa te dukuya ltung'ana eitoduaayie too lkigerot inchere ore Yesu ninye Kristo.

English: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
Masaai: Neaku ore etii ninye Apolo Korinto, neimayie Paulo ina kop oo ldoinyo nelotu Efeso, neinepu kulikae ooiteng'eni te ine.

English: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
Masaai: Nejoki lelo, “Itang'amaitie apa Enkiyang'et Sinyati pee irukuruku?” Nejoki ninche ninye, “A'a, keitu ninye ai kata kining aajo keetae Enkiyang'et Sinyati.”

English: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche, “Kaa kibatisare naa apa eibatisaki intae?” Nejoki ninche, “Enkibatisa e Yohana.”

English: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
Masaai: Nejoki Paulo, “Eibatisishe Yohana enkibatisa e nkirridunoto, nejoki olorere, meiruko ilo olotu te siadi ninye, naa, Yesu taa ilo.”

English: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Masaai: Ore pee ening ina, neibatisae te nkarna o Laitoriani Yesu.

English: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
Masaai: Ore pee eiteleiki Paulo nkaik enyena, nedoiki Enkiyang'et Sinyati ninche: neiro kulie kutukie neibonisho.

English: And all the men were about twelve.
Masaai: Nera lelo tung'ana pooki tomon o aare.

English: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
Masaai: Nejing enkaji e ntumo neshirraki airo te rishata oo lapaitin okuni, neishankarrarre nesayieki ninche mbaa naaipirta enkitoria e Nkai.

English: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
Masaai: Kake ore pee eikirnyanya kulikae neitagol onyek, nemor ena oitoi te dukuya olorere, nelo aing'uaa ninche, negelu ilooiteng'eni, nelo aiteng'enisho anaa ake te nkaji naisumareki.

English: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
Masaai: Neidikidik aas ina te rishata oo larin aare; o metaa ore lelo pooki oomanya Asia aa Lyahudi o Lyunani, nening ororei lo Laitoriani.

English: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
Masaai: Neas Enkai e nking'asia too nkaik e Paulo:

English: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
Masaai: o metaa kenapakini ltamueyia nkarash, o nkitampaani o nkarash o sesen le Paulo o nkarash naaisiaaishore, nepuo nkeyaitin aaing'uaa, nepuku loiriruani aapuo.

English: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
Masaai: Kake enotoki sii kulikae Yahudi oopuaya, ooaraa loiriruani, nedumunye aaku enkarna o Laitoriani Yesu ejokinye lelo oiriruani, “Aainosie olmumai te nkarna e ilo oji Yesu olikioo Paulo.”

English: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
Masaai: Neetae ilayiok oopishana le likae, apolosani kitok, oji Skewa ooikuna ninche neijia.

English: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
Masaai: Newaliki oloirirua ajoki ninche, “Kayiolo Yesu, nayiolo Paulo; kake airara doi intae iloo ng'ae?”

English: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
Masaai: Neipidoki ilo apa tung'ani ooata oloirirua lelo pooki, neidimu ninche aare, negilu aar, neisikie te ina aji meishopo neeta lbaa.

English: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
Masaai: Neyiolou pooki ng'ae ina ebaiki Lyahudi o Lyunani oomanya Efeso; nedoiki enkuretisho ninche pooki nerrepi enkarna o Laitoriani Yesu.

English: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
Masaai: Nepuonu sii lkumok le lelo ooiruko, neirridu, neibalunye nkiaasin enye.

English: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
Masaai: Ore esiana e lelo apa ooasishore ilosekin le naibon neyau mbukui enye aaiturrur: nepejoo edolita pooki ng'ae: neikeni esiana oo mpesai naainosieki neaku ropiyiani naaibor naabaya nkalisuni onom.

English: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
Masaai: Neijia eikuna ororei lo Laitoriani te magilanisho neponari te ngolon.

English: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
Masaai: Ore pee eiting kuna baa, nemut Paulo openy te Nkiyang'et Sinyati ajo, ore pee eidip aimai Makedonia o Akaia, neitoki alo Yerusalem, nejo, “Ore pee aidip ashomo ine, meeta nchere eitu alo Roma.”

English: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
Masaai: Ore pee eirriwaa aare le lelo aretok lenyena Makedonia, aa taa Timoteo o Erasto, neng'as ninye makewan abik te Asia te nkiti rishata.

English: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
Masaai: Ore ake te nena, katitin nedumunye oloilole leme oti ti alo ena Oitoi.

English: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
Masaai: Amu eetae oltung'ani oji Demetrus, kunoni loo sekenke oo mpesai, oidong'u too sekenke oo mpesai Artemis* naatudupore oleng lelo kunono.

English: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
Masaai: Nesotu ilo kulikae kunono ooitobir sii ninche nena tokitin, nejoki, “Lo kituaak, iyiololo aajo ena siaai ang oshi kidupore.

English: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
Masaai: Nidolitata, nining'itoto aajo mme te Efeso ake, kake etaa ore ninye Asia pooki, eibelekenye eilejileja ilo oji Paulo ltung'ana kumok aitapong'oo, ajoki eji mme hoo nkaitin kuna naa too nkaik eitobiri.

English: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
Masaai: Mme taa doi ena siaai ang ake etarrikio eyookini aamenaa; kake taaisere doi neaku ore ninye enkaji e nkai ng'oruoi kitok naji Artemis neitaai pesho, nebaiki doi ninye nesuluni te sikar enye, ina naa ninye eserem Asia neserem enkop pooki.”

English: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
Masaai: Ore ake pee ening ninche ina neiput engoro, nebuak aajo, “Kitok ake Artemis oo Leefeso.”

English: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
Masaai: Neiput olmilo ina anasa; nekuet pooki te nebo aapuo eor e nkiguran eikurtutaa Gayo o Aristako, oora ninche ltung'ana le Makedonia, ooiriamunore Paulo pee elotu.

English: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo Paulo ajing atua lelo tung'ana, nemitiki ilooiteng'eni.

English: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
Masaai: Ore sii kulikae loo laitoriak le Asia, laa lchoreta lenyena, neirriwaki enkutuk esai pee metem ninye makewan alo ina aji e nkiguana.

English: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
Masaai: Nebuaku kulikae ejo ena nebuaku kulikae ejo ai: amu eing'oling'ole ina tumo: naa aimeyiolo esejata sapuk ajo aainyo pee eiturrurroteki te nebo.

English: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
Masaai: Neitupukuni Aleksanta ti atua olorere, naa Lyahudi ooturrumoitie. Neyuk Aleksanta ninche te nkaina, eyieu newaliki olorere.

English: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
Masaai: Kake ninye ake etayioloito aajo Olyahudi; nebuaku pooki to ltoilo obo neidikidik aaiko neijia te rishata oo saai are ejoito, “Kitok ake Artemis oo Leefeso.”

English: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
Masaai: Ore ade pee eitigir olasirani kitok le ina anasa olorora, nejo, “Lo lewa le Efeso, keetae pasa oltung'ani lemeyiolo ajo ena anasa e Efeso oshi enkarriponi e nkaji naomonieki Artemis kitok o ilo soit sinyati apa odou eing'uaa te shumata?

English: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
Masaai: Ore naa amu iyiololo aajo meetae oltung'ani oishankarru kuna baa, keishiaakino naaji nigirara, pee miwuapakinono ake aas ai bae namurtana.

English: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
Masaai: Amu iyautua kulo tung'ana ene, neme ketupurro nkajijik naaomonishoreki neitu sii emor enkai ang.

English: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
Masaai: Te neeta Demetrus, aashu kulo kunono ooiriamunore embae naatakinore likae tung'ani, ebolo nkajijik e nkiguana neetae ilbalusuni: enchoo epuonu aaiguana olikae o likae.

English: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
Masaai: Kake te niaatata kulie ning'oruru, epuonunui aaiguanare nena te noshi ake kiguana.

English: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
Masaai: Amu kebaiki doi neiguanareki iyiook te le ongolingoli le na olong, amu ai meeta duoo tipat nadumunyeki; naa te neikilikuani iyiook nikilau enikijo te nkaraki ele oilole.”

English: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip atejo nejia, neidapasha ina tumo.

English: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
Masaai: Ore pee eishunye ina liman, neipotisho Paulo aiturrur ilooiteng'eni neikok, neitanapare, nelo aing'uaa eyieu Makedonia.

English: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
Masaai: Ore pee eimaa nene wuejitin, neikok ninche oleng nelotu enkop oo Lyunani.

English: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
Masaai: Ore etobiko lapaitin okuni te ine, neiguanare Lyahudi ejo pee ear metua, enoshi kata ejo pee elo aked emeli alo Siria, nerrinyo etumuta ajo keimaa ake pookata Makedonia.

English: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
Masaai: Neiriamariyie Sopater olayioni le Pirro, le Berea o meitabaiki Asia; o kulo le Sesalonike, Aristako o Sekunto; o Gayo le Derbe, o Timoteo; ore ile Asia naa Tikikos o Trifimo.

English: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
Masaai: Kake eituruko apa kulo, nepuo aanyu iyiook te Troas.

English: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
Masaai: Nikiked emeli te Filipi eishari osirua loo mukateni Nemeisuijieki, nikibau Troas too nkolong'i miet; nikibik nkolong'i naapishana te ine.

English: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e dukuya e wiki, kitoni te nebo aagil emukate, neikok Paulo ninche ejo pee eyooki alo te ntaaisere; neitoodor ororei o meitoritoyu enkewarie.

English: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
Masaai: Naa kumok ilkilang'eta te ilo gilata le shumata, likitumore.

English: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
Masaai: Neton oloti barnoti oji Yutikas te lusie, neimug eiroshiutuo njio. Ore eton ake eitoodorita Paulo ororei, neidimutua olbarnoti njio nesulunye te nkaji e uni te shumata, nedumuni eji ketua.

English: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
Masaai: Nedou Paulo, nepetaa nedumu amuataki nkaik nejo, “Emimputukuny amu eton eishu.”

English: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
Masaai: Ore pee eilep, nebel emukate, nedaa, neitoki ake airorie kata naado, o mekenyu, nelo taa aing'uaa.

English: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
Masaai: Nerikuni oladuoo barnoti eishu neme kiti enkilejilejata nanoto ninche.

English: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
Masaai: Kake kinturuko iyiook aapuo enetii emeli, nikiked nikilang aapuo Aso, kijo pee kipuo aang'amu Paulo te ine, amu ninye otejo neijia eyieu ninye nelo aimaa enkop natoyio.

English: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu anang'are iyiook te Aso, nikintaked emeli, nikipuonu mitelene.

English: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
Masaai: Ore pee kidumunye te ine, nikiyooki aapuonu te ntaaisere o maipirare Kios, ore te nkolong nasuju nikintashe peno te Samo, ore te nkae olong nikipuonu Mileto.

English: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
Masaai: Amu etumuta Paulo ajo kegiroo Efeso te meli, pee meya enkata te Asia; eyieu nesiooyo, ejo te neidimayu neyieu netii Yerusalem te nkolong e Pentekoste.

English: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
Masaai: Ore kitii Mileto, neirriwaa Paulo olkilikuai Efeso, aipot ilpayiani le ina sirit.

English: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
Masaai: Ore pee epuonu enetii ninye nejoki ninche: “Iyiololo maate ebaiki enapa olong nang'as are Asia, eneikununo entonata ai ti atua intae te ina kata pooki;

English: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
Masaai: aisiaaita Olaitoriani te mborron pooki o te ng'eno, o too lkiyio, o too ngolot nanoto te nkaraki losekin loo Lyahudi.

English: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
Masaai: Niyiololo aajo eitu ai kata aing'ash aibalunye intae embae ake pooki naret intae, naiteng'en intae te dukuya ltung'ana, naruk inkajijik,

English: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
Masaai: aishakenoki ndung'ot pokira aa Lyahudi o aa Lyunani meirridu ti alo meirridu ti alo Enkai, neiruk Olaitoriani lang Yesu Kristo.

English: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
Masaai: Ore naa taata, ng'ura, Yerusalem aloito aaena oltau mayiolo mbaa naapuo aatum te ine:

English: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
Masaai: meteleku ake Enkiyang'et Sinyati ake naaishakenoki nanu te pooki anasa inchere inkeenta naanyita o inkitamiot.

English: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
Masaai: Kake maikenaa enkishui ai ajo keeta tipat, anaa keeta dupoto te nanu, aa kajo pee aitabaya elototo ai, o esiaai natang'amua to Laitoriani Yesu, aishakenoki ororei supat le mpiris e Nkai.

English: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
Masaai: Ore naa taata ng'ura, ayiolo ajo meekure intokiki ai kata aadol enkomom ai, intae kulo laisiritore alikioo enkitoria e Nkai.

English: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina, aishakenoki taata intae ajo maata eng'oki to sarge lo ltung'ani ake pooki.

English: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
Masaai: Amu maata enatelekua eitu aibalakinye intae lulung'ata e nkikoo e Nkai neitu aliki intae.

English: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
Masaai: Entagolie ate maate o ina luaata pooki naitaa intae Enkiyang'et Sinyati ilaing'urak lenye, aaitoti esirit e Nkai nainyiang'aka ninye kewan to sarge lenye.

English: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
Masaai: Kayiolo ajo nanu ake olo nejing atua intae isuyian ooata enkarri, lemeing'urrie ena luaata;

English: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
Masaai: naa keinyiototo ltung'ana ti atua intae, oojo mbaa e nkiushoto, pee eyiataa looiteng'eni laa ninche esujaa.

English: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
Masaai: Enchololoto naa nidamumu aajo ore te rishata oo larin okuni eitu agira aikokito intae pooki dama o kewarie too lkiyio.

English: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
Masaai: Ore naa taata inkaik e Nkai aitarasaki intae, o ele rorei le mpiris, oidim atesheta intae neisho intae enjung'ore te nebo lelo pooki ooitengelaki.

English: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.
Masaai: Eitu ang'uar enkosholai aashu saabu o enkila e likae tung'ani.

English: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
Masaai: Iyiololo maate aajo kuna aik naaisiaayiakita nkolati aainei makewan o ne lelo laisiritore.

English: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Masaai: Aitoduaa intae pooki toki, nchere ti nisiaaishosho aaiko neijia niretirete ilooshal, idamumu irorei lo Laitoriani Yesu anaa enatejo openy inchere, ‘Enkishooroto namayiana alang eng'amaroto.’ ”

English: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip atejo neijia, negil kung neomon te nebo ninche pooki.

English: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,
Masaai: Neishiraki pooki ninye oleng, nemuataki Paulo nkaik neng'utut ninye,

English: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
Masaai: neisina oleng te nkaraki ilo rorei otejo eji, meitoki ae kata aadol enkomom enye. Neitarioo ninche ninye aaitabaiki enetii emeli.

English: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
Masaai: Ore kitung'uaitie ninche nikiked emeli, nikintoriounye aapuonu Kos, ore te nkolong nasuju nikibau Rodos, nikidumunye te ine nikipuonu Patara.

English: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
Masaai: Ore pee kitum emeli nalang alo Foenike, nikiked aapuo.

English: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
Masaai: Ore pee kidol Kipros, nikincho kedienye aaporoo aapuo Siria o maetu Tiro, amu te ine eitadou emeli lolan.

English: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore king'orutua ilooiteng'eni, nikibik nkolong'i naa pishana te ine. Nejoki lelo Paulo te Nkiyang'et nchere pee melo ake Yerusalem.

English: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
Masaai: Ore pee kiishu nena olong'i, nikidumunye aapuo enapake lototo ang; neitarioo iyiook ninche pooki o nkituaak o nkera, o maetu auluo e ina anasa, nikigil kung te mbata e naiposha nikiomon nikinchoro ole sere.

English: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
Masaai: Nikintoki aaked emeli, nerrinyo ninche aapuo ang.

English: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
Masaai: Ore kindipa elototo ang king'uaa Tiro, nikibau Tolemai; nikiroroki ilalashera nikibik nabo olong te nebo ninche.

English: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
Masaai: Ore te ntaaisere nikidumunye o maetu Kaisaria; nikijing enkaji o lalikioroni Filipo, obo loo lapa oopishana, nikitoni te nkaji enye.

English: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
Masaai: Neeta ninye ntoyie ong'uan nemeayama, naaishoro enaibon e Nkai.

English: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
Masaai: Ore kitobiko nkuti olong'i, nelotu oloiboni le Nkai oing'uaa Yudea oji Agabo.

English: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
Masaai: Nelotu ine nikitii nedumu enkimeita e Paulo neen kewan inkejek o nkaik, nejo, “Inji ejo Enkiyang'et Sinyati, ‘Inji epuo aaiko Lyahudi te Yerusalem aaen olopeny ena kimeita neitarasaki nkaik oo Loreren.’ ”

English: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee kining ina nikisai iyiook o lelo tung'ana ninye pee meilep alo Yerusalem.

English: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
Masaai: Newal Paulo nejo, “Kaa ena niaasitata, kinchirakiki nikintashalishala oltau? Mme doi enkeene ake aitieu naaeni kake te naa kaye te Yerusalem naye te nkaraki enkarna o Laitoriani Yesu.”

English: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
Masaai: Ore pee elaikinoi aaiboo, nikigira nikijo, “Metotiwuo naa anaa enayieu Olaitoriani.”

English: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee eishunye nena olong'i nikinapa pee kilep aapuo Yerusalem.

English: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
Masaai: Neiriamariyie iyiook kulikae ooiteng'eni oing'uaa Kaisaria, nerik iyiook enkaji e likae oji Mnason le Kipros, olaa oloiteng'eni musana ninye, paa ninye kirragaitie.

English: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
Masaai: Ore pee kipuonu Yerusalem, neng'amu iyook ilalashera te nchipai.

English: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
Masaai: Ore te ntaaisere neeiriamunore iyiook Paulo kipuo enetii Yakobo; nelulung'a ilpayiani pooki te ine.

English: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip airoroki ninche, neinosaki aa maa nabo nena baa pooki naataasa Enkai ti atua Loreren ooisiaaishore ninye.

English: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
Masaai: Ore pee ening ninche, neisis Enkai. Nejoki ninche ninye, “Olalashe, idolita eneba nkalifuni oo Lyahudi ooiruko; neeta pooki olokiyo too nkitanapat.

English: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
Masaai: nikietuoki aakur te ninche nchere ishomo aiteng'en Ilyahudi pooki ootii Loreren metung'uai Musa, eji nepal memurat inkera enye nemesuj lkerreti lang.

English: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
Masaai: Kaa naa easi? Nemeeta nchere eitu ening aajo iewuo.

English: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
Masaai: Taasa ena nikijoki iyie. Kiaata ltung'ana oong'uan ooata olmumai;

English: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
Masaai: tudumu kulo tung'ana pokira oong'uan mikintukui te nebo ninche nilaaki ninche nena tokitin naaitalakishoi, pee ebarni. Ina eyiolounye pooki ng'ae nchere meeta tipat kunda baa naatiaakaki ti alo iyie amu isujita iyie makewan nkitanapat e Nkai te nkishon ino.

English: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
Masaai: Kake ore ltung'ana loo Loreren ooiruko, kirriwakita apa empalai nayakita enkiguana ang nchere pee erishie ate ntokitin naapolosakini nkitanyaanyukot neme Enkai o sarge o ntokitin naagori o eloloito.”

English: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
Masaai: Nedumu taa Paulo lelo tung'ana pokira oong'uan te nkolong nasuju, neitisiny kewan, tenebo ninche nejing atua enkaji e Nkai, alikioo eneiting'ie nkolong'i e ina kitukuoto, neishooyo sii ntokitin naaitukuyieki ninche pokira.

English: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
Masaai: Ore etaa keidipayu nena olong'i pokira naapishana, netii Ilyahudi ooing'uaa Asia, ootoduaa ninye te nkaji e Nkai, neing'oling'ol esiamo, neitabaiki ninye nkaik aaibung,

English: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
Masaai: ebuakita aajo, “Lo lewa le Israel, entaret iyiook! Ele tung'ani doi oiteng'enita ltung'ana te pooki wueji meibai ele orere neibayu nkitanapat e Nkai o ene wueji; nenyaaka ayau Iyunani aitijing enkaji e Nkai, neewuo aisarkionie ene wueji sinyati.”

English: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
Masaai: Naa Trofimo etoduaaki ae olong eiriamariyie Paulo te ina anasa, nejo ninche ketoriko Paulo aitijing enkaji e Nkai.

English: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
Masaai: Neing'oling'ola taa enkanasa pooki, nekuetu ltung'ana aaiturrurro te nebo; neibung'i Paulo neikurtutari in aji e Nkai, neikeni kutuk aji nabo kata.

English: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
Masaai: Ore eji matar metua, nebaiki ororei olkitok loo sikarini loo ltimito nchere einyio oloilole te Yerusalem pooki.

English: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
Masaai: Nedumu ninye isikarini o lkituaak le lelo timito, nekuetu adoiki ninche: ore pee edoluni ilo kitok o sikarini, nepal eitu eitoki aar Paulo.

English: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
Masaai: Nenyikaki ilo kitok loo sikarini, neibung arik ninye, neitanapisho meteeni too munyororoni are, neikilikuan ajoki aira ng'ae neikilikuan enataasa.

English: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
Masaai: Nebuaku kulikae ti atua ilo orora ae bae, nejo kulikae ai; ore pee edol ajo meeta ae natum te nkaraki olodoo; neitanapisho meyauni atua emanyata oo sikarini.

English: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
Masaai: Ore enoshi naitabaikini inkedeta e kishomi, neaku te shumata eya isikarini aaing'atie enkop te nkaraki olong'oling'oli le ilo orora egorokinoi;

English: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
Masaai: amu esujita ake ilo orere ebuakita aajo, “Ewaita ninye!”

English: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
Masaai: Ore etaa keitabaikini Paulo ina manyata, nejoki ilo kitok loo sikarini, “Eikincho pasa maairorie?” Nejoki ninye, “Iyiolo doi enkutuk oo Lyunani?

English: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
Masaai: Metaa mira doi olanaarri Misiri oirrikia olorere meitarrikinore sirkali nerik ilapa tung'ana asesesekuanak nkalifuni ong'uan ong'ata?”

English: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
Masaai: Newaliki Paulo ajoki, “Kara nanu Olyahudi, oing'uaa Tarso e Kilikia, metaa mme misil enkanasa naing'uaa; aatoomono naa nchooki mairorie ele orere.”

English: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
Masaai: Ore pee eisho, neitashe Paulo te nena kedeta e kishomi, neyuk olorere te nkaina; ore pee egira aajo tim, neirorie te nkutuk oo Lhebrania, nejoki:

English: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
Masaai: “Ilalashera laainei o loo papa, entoning'oki te kuna namitunye kewan te dukuya intae.”

English: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
Masaai: Ore pee ening'i aajo enkutuk oo Lhebrania eirorie, neitirring'a oleng aagira. Nejo,

English: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
Masaai: “Ara Olyahudi, naa te Tarso e Kilikia aaini, kake te na anasa aaitubuluni too nkejek e Gamaliel, naaiteng'eni te risioroto oo nkitanapat oo loo papa naarrish, naata olokiyo te Nkai anaa ena nitiuwu pooki te le kekun.

English: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
Masaai: Ainosie nanu ena Oitoi osina o metuata naen anang'aki korokoroni ilewa o nkituaak,

English: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
Masaai: naa shakeni lai olapolosani kitok naa neijia etiu olkiaama pooki loo lpaiyiani. Ninche laaishoo mpala nayaki lalashera, pee adumunye alo Dameski aibung lelo ootii ine ayau Yerusalem eena pee eitamei.

English: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
Masaai: “Ore aloito atinyikaka Dameski, etaa enaipirie enkolong newang'u nabo kata ewang'an naing'uaa shumata naaman.

English: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
Masaai: Nabatata te nkop naning oltoilo laajoki, ‘Saulo Saulo aainyo pee kisilisil?’

English: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
Masaai: Nawaliki ajoki, ‘Olaitoriani, aira ng'ae?’ Naajoki ninye, ‘Ara Yesu le Nasaret lisilisilito!'

English: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
Masaai: Ore lelo laairiamariyie nanu nedol ina wang'an kake eitu ening oltoilo le ilo laairorie.

English: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
Masaai: Najo, ‘Olaitoriani, kaji aiko?’ Naajoki Olaitoriani, ‘Inyo, shomo tijing'a Dameski, paa te ine kilikini nena pooki nikitegelakaki taasa.’

English: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
Masaai: Ore amu meekure adolisho te nkaraki ina wang'an, naariki aaibung enkaina lelo ootii te nebo nanu, o maetu Dameski.

English: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
Masaai: “Netii ine oltung'ani obo oji Ananias, oserem ninye Enkai anaa enajo nkitanapat, ooilet Ilyahudi pooki te supatisho, laa ine nemanya ninye.

English: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
Masaai: Nelotu ilo enatii, neitashe ti alo nanu naajoki, ‘Olalashe lai Saulo, todolisho.’ Ore te ina saa ake nadolishoyu nadol ninye.

English: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
Masaai: Nejo ninye, ‘Enkai oo loo papa nikitegelua tayiolo yieuna enye, nikincho toduaa ilo obo Asipani nining oltoilo te nkutuk enye;

English: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
Masaai: amu iaku shakeni lenye too ltung'ana pooki te nena nitoduaa o nitoning'o.

English: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
Masaai: Ainyoo naa taata ianyita? Inyo mikimbatisai, intukuoi ing'ok inono, impoto enkarna enye.’

English: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
Masaai: “Ore pee aidip atushukunye Yerusalem aomonito te nkaji e Nkai, naainepu enduaata

English: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
Masaai: nadol aajoki ninye nanu, ‘Isarisara tasiooi tung'uai Yerusalem, amu meng'amaa hoo ninche shakenisho ino ti alo nanu.’

English: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
Masaai: Najo, ‘Olaitoriani, eyiolo ninche maate enaikuna meeta enkaji e ntumo neitu ajing napik korokoroni naar lelo likiruko.

English: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
Masaai: Naa ore pee eibukori osarge le Stefano olchakeni lino, aitashe sii nanu atonyorrayie, naa nanu oitasheikio nkilani e lelo ootara.’

English: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
Masaai: Naajoki ninye, ‘Shomo, amu nanu laairriwaa enelakua shomo enetii Loreren.’ ”

English: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
Masaai: Neinining lelo tung'ana Paulo o metejo ele rorei; nejo ake neijia, neilepie pooki ltoiloishi nejo, “Ewuang'ie ele tung'ani te nkop! Amu meishiaakino neishu!”

English: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
Masaai: Ore ebuakita neisuaakita ilkilani lenye nekur enterit aaisuaaya,

English: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
Masaai: neitanapisho ilo kitok loo sikarini meyauni ninye atua emanyata enye, nejo metaari meiroro, pee eyiolouni enatabuaakinye ninche Paulo.

English: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
Masaai: Ore eidipaki aateen too nkeenta, nejoki Paulo osajini oitasheiki, “Keishiaakino pasa neidong'i oltung'ani loo Roma, leitu eng'asi aaiguanare?”

English: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
Masaai: Ore pee ening ilo sajini ina nelo enetii olkitok loo sikarini nejoki, “Kaa bae ena nijo aas? Amu oloo Roma ele tung'ani.”

English: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
Masaai: Metaa nelotu ilo kitok enetii nejoki, “Tolikioki sii iyie japa, eji ira doi oloo Roma?” Nejoki, “Ee.”

English: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
Masaai: Newaliki ilo kitok loo sikarini ajoki, “Kainyiang'ua nanu ina kiela too ropiyiani kumok oleng.” Nejoki Paulo, “Kaikino nanu.”

English: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
Masaai: Metaa nepuo nabo kata aalam lelo apa oojo pee epuonu aajur; neureshoyu sii ninye ilo kitok loo sikarini amu etayiolo ajo oloo Roma Paulo neidipaki aateen.

English: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
Masaai: Kake ore taaisere, neyieu ninye ake neyiolou enaitang'orie Lyahudi Paulo pee eisitaaitie, neen ninye, nejoki lapolosak kituaak o lkiaama pooki menototo, neriku Paulo neitasheyie te dukuya ninche.

English: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
Masaai: Neing'or Paulo ninche akurraki olkiaama nkonyek, nejo, “Ilalashera laainei, aitasho te dukuya Enkai o metabau ele kekun aata oltau sidai.”

English: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
Masaai: Nejoki olapolosani kitok oji Ananias lelo ooitashe aatashare Paulo metooshi enkutuk.

English: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
Masaai: Nejoki Paulo, “Enkai nikiyooki aosh iyie, oleeijo esuntai naiborrieki! Aiton pee kinguanare too nkitanapat e Nkai nintoki apaash enajo nena kitanapat ajo maatooshi?”

English: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?
Masaai: Nejoki lelo ooitashe te ine, “Kolapolosani kitok le Nkai imor?”

English: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
Masaai: Nejo Paulo, “Enkaraki naa ai mayiolo lalashera laainei, ajo ninye olapolosani kitok, amu etisiraki aajo, ‘Mijo ake ine nkarrueisho ti alo oloitore olorere linyi.’ ”

English: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
Masaai: Kake ore pee edol Paulo ajo Isadukayo enchoto nabo naa Lfarisayoi enkai, nebuaku ajo to lkiama, “Ilalashera laainei, ara nanu Olfarisayoi naa Lfarisayoi laaiu; olapa siligi o empiunoto oo lootuata doi pee aaiguanareki.”

English: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo neijia, nepuku empong'o oo Sadukayo o Lfarisayoi, neoro olkiaama.

English: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
Masaai: Amu ejo Sadukayo meetae empiunoto, nemeetae ilmalaika, nemeetae enkiyang'et; kake enyorraa ninche Lfarisayo nena pooki.

English: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
Masaai: Nepuku olodoo kitok; neinyiototo kulikae aiteng'enak loo nkitanapat Farisayo neiguana nejo, “Eitu hoo kitum iyiook entioto te le tung'ani. Oo doi te naa kenkiyang'et aashu olmalaika oirorie?”

English: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
Masaai: Ore pee eaku keibelekenya empong'o aaku olarrabal, nedol ilo kitok loo sikarini, neureyu ajo kepolosi Paulo aaitaa ng'urrot, neirriwaa sikarini metadoi aayau ninye te ngolon aaitung'uaa ninche neyau emanyata.

English: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
Masaai: Ore te nkai kewarie natusujua ina, neitashe Olaitoriani ti alo ninye nejo, “Intagoluoyu, amu ore anaa ina nikinchakenoko nanu te Yerusalem, neijia kiyooki aiko aishakenoki te Roma.”

English: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
Masaai: Ore pee ekenyu neiguana Lyahudi nenya olmumai pee menya endaa nemeok ae toki o metaba anaa near Paulo metua.

English: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
Masaai: Negiroo artam ilooinosa ina kiguana o kiguan enkarruesho.

English: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
Masaai: Nepuo lelo enetii ilapolosak kituaak o lpayiani; nejo, “Kiteena ate katukul to lmumai nchere mikinchamisham endaa o metaba anaa nikiaar Paulo metua.

English: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
Masaai: Enyeito intae, o lkiama, entiaaki taata olkitok loo sikarini meitadou ninye, entaakunoto keeta eniyieuu nisipunyenye, aabaraki. Amu kitanapate iyiook pee kiar metua eton eitu enyikaki intae.”

English: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
Masaai: Nening olayioni le nkanashe Paulo ina rreshoto enye nelo ajing emanyata neliki Paulo.

English: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
Masaai: Neipot Paulo obo le lelo sajinini nejo, “Toriko ele barnoti enetii olkitok loo sikarini, amu keeta enajoki.”

English: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
Masaai: Nerikoki olkitok loo sajinini nejo, “Paulo oloshi oena laaipoto naajoki maatorikoki ele barnoti, amu keeta enikijoki.”

English: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
Masaai: Neibung ilo kitok enkaina nerik enkilepata neikilikuan too nkurrat ajoki, “Kaa kiyieu nikijoki?”

English: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Eiguanate Ilyahudi pee kipuonu aaikilikuan tayooki taaisere intadoi Paulo meshomo enetii olkiaama, anaa keeta enayieunye pee epuo aajur oleng.

English: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
Masaai: Kake minyorraa ina nayieu ninche; amu artam nadooyo iltung'ana lenye ootii olnukata aaresh ninye, eteena ate to lmumai aajo menya endaa nemeok toki mme keidipa aatar ninye metua; neidipa taata aatanapata, iyie eanyita tonyorrai ina.”

English: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
Masaai: Neisho ilo kitok loo sikarini olbarnoti elo neitirrishaki ajo, “Nimiliki ake likae tung'ani ajo kitolikio ena bae.”

English: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
Masaai: Neitoki ilo aipot isajinini aare nejoki, “Ore te saa uni e nkewarie enchoo enapa sikarini iip are te nebo intomoni naapishana loo mbartan o loo remeta iip are oopuo aabaya Kaisaria.

English: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
Masaai: Naa sii erotoki Paulo embarta naked, entorikoki olbalusui Feliks.”

English: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
Masaai: Neiger empalai ajo nji:

English: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
Masaai: “Nanu Klaudius Lisia laairoroki, Oloyanyiti Olbalusui Feliks.

English: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
Masaai: Ele tung'ani eibung'a Lyahudi, naa anaata etara metua, neaku ainepua aata sikarini nasaru, atayiolo ajo oloo Roma.

English: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
Masaai: Ore ajo pee ayiolou embae naisitaarieki nariku aitadoiki olkiaama lenye.

English: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
Masaai: Nayiolou ajo mbaa oo nkitanapat enye eisitaarieki, kake meeta enataasa nairirikino keeya anaa eenata.

English: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
Masaai: Ore pee aarojakini nchere einosaki enkiguana pee eari ele tung'ani metua, nairriu nabo kata enitii iyie, naitanap lelo ooisitaaya meetu aalimu te dukuya iyie enaatakinore ninye.”

English: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
Masaai: Neaku etoriko isikarini Paulo anaa enaitanapaki nerik kewarie o meitabaiki Antipatri.

English: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
Masaai: Neyooki taaisere aashukunye emanyata, neing'ueikini iloo mbartan metoriko aapuo.

English: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
Masaai: Ore pee epuonu Kaisaria neitarasaki olbalusui empalai, neitodol Paulo etii dukuya ninye.

English: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
Masaai: Ore eisom empalai, neikilikuan ajoki koliaalo osho. Ore pee eyiolou ajo ole Kilikia

English: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.
Masaai: nejo, “Kaayooki ainining te nebau lelo likintang'or.” Neitanapisho metorripi te nkaji e Herode e nkitoo.

English: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
Masaai: Ore etulusoitie nkolong'i miet nedou Anania olapolosani kitok o kulikae payiani o ltung'ani olotu airo, oji Tertulo. Nepuonu aainosaki olbalusui nena baa naaitang'orie Paulo;

English: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
Masaai: ore pee eipoti neiteru Tertulo aitang'or Paulo ejo: “Ore amu iyie pee king'idare ena seriani kitok, naa te leng'on ino, Oloyanyiti Feliks, pee eibelekenyitai mbaa aaitang'ejuk te le orere,

English: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
Masaai: niking'amaa nena te nashe too nkoitoi pooki o te pooki wueji.

English: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
Masaai: Kake ore pee mikintoki aaibok iyie, naaomon to lng'ur lino toning'o iyook too ndorropu.

English: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
Masaai: Amu kinoto aajo serseri ele tung'ani naa oltang'oroi too Lyahudi pooki te nkop pooki, naa ninye obo loo larikok le na kiteng'enare kilaut naji eno Lnasarayoi.

English: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
Masaai: Ketetema doi ninye ajo aisarkionie enkaji e Nkai paa iyiook ooibung'a. Eikijo apa iyiook pee kinguanare too nkitanapat ang,

English: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,
Masaai: kake Lisia olkitok loo sikarini oewuo newuapaa aoru iyiook te ngolon oleng.

English: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
Masaai: Neitoki ake Lisia aitoreisho nejo meetu lelo ooitang'or dukuya iyie. Te nijur ele tung'ani, te ninye iyiolou iyie openy esipata e nena nikintang'orie.”

English: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
Masaai: Neirukoki Ilyahudi ina kitang'oro, neitisip aajo neijia etiu.

English: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
Masaai: Ore pee eyuk olbalusui meiroro, newal Paulo nejo: “Ore amu kayiolo ajo kumok ilarin intore ele orere, kashipa amitu kewan.

English: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
Masaai: Te niyieu naa indim aitadedeyie nchere, eitu egiroo tomon o aare nkolong'i anaa nailep alo aserem Enkai te Yerusalem;

English: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
Masaai: neitu aainepu ninche aishankarrarre likae tung'ani aashu aing'oling'ol esiamo, te nkaji e Nkai, aashu too nkajijik e ntumo aashu te ina anasa.

English: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
Masaai: Nemeidim doi ninye aaitadedeyie kuna naapuonu aaitang'orie.

English: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
Masaai: Kake anyorraa ena nabo te dukuya iyie, nchere te na Oitoi, najo ninche enkiteng'enare kilaut aserem nanu Enkai oo loo papa, airukito mbaa pooki naalimuno too nkitanapat anaa too naaigero too loibonok le Nkai.

English: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
Masaai: Naata osiligi te Nkai naanyorra sii ninche kulo nchere kelotu empiunoto e lelo ooata esipata o lemeeta.

English: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
Masaai: Metaa anyokita oshi ake pee aata oltau sidai ti alo Enkai o ti alo ltung'ana.

English: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
Masaai: Ore det etulusoitie lkuti arin nalotu ayaki olorere lang nkishorunot naaretieki laisinak nkishorunot e nashe.

English: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
Masaai: Ore aa ina aasita, naainepu aaitisinyaki te nkaji e Nkai, neitu adumu aashu aliman. Kake eetae Lyahudi le Asia

English: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
Masaai: laa keishiaakino napaji netii ene pee aapuonu aaitang'or, te naa keeta enaatakinore.

English: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
Masaai: Aashu doi elimu ninche kulo maate aajo kaa torroni apa aanotie pee aitashe te dukuya olkiaama,

English: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
Masaai: neme ena nabo ake natabuakua aitashe te dukuya ninche ajo, ‘Enkaraki oo lootuata pee aitashe te dukuya intae maaiguanareki te le kekun.’ ”

English: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
Masaai: Kake ore ninye Feliks, amu ketiu anaa ketabaraka ayiolou ena Oitoi, neilitilit, ajoki, “Ore pee edou Lisia, olkitok loo sikarini naadung'oki enkiguana.”

English: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
Masaai: Neitanap osajini metorripi kake meitirrishi sii, nememitikini lchoreta lenyena epuonu aaret anaa enayieu.

English: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
Masaai: Ore eshomo nkuti olong'i nelotu Feliks oe enkitok enye naji Drusila, naa Eyahudi ninye; nejo meipoti Paulo meinining'o eimaki enkirukoto nairuki Yesu Kristo.

English: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
Masaai: Ore pee eishankarrarre too mbaa naaipirta enkiguana oo sipat o enkibooroto naaibooyo oltung'ani kewan arishie ntorrok, o enkiguana kenya nalotu, neureishoyu Feliks nejo, “Shomo taata; ore pee atum erishata naaipot.”

English: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
Masaai: Ore eyia neijia naa kejo apa kebaiki neisho Paulo mpesai. Neaku keirriwaa lkiliku nkatitin kumok neinosie lomon.

English: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
Masaai: Kake ore pee elusoo larin aare, neirriuni Porkio Festo meibung'a erishata e Feliks; ore ninye Feliks ejo pee eitiship Ilyahudi, neing'uaa Paulo te korokoroni.

English: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
Masaai: Ore pee ebau Festo, ina kop naitore, nkolong'i uni ake naatulusoitie, nedumunye te Kaisaria ailep alo Yerusalem.

English: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
Masaai: Neitang'or ilapolosak kituaak o larikok loo Lyahudi Paulo te ninye nesai aaitirrishaki,

English: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
Masaai: aajoki meitobiraki ninche mbaa aisho ilo tung'ani meewai Yerusalem, aa kejo pee erresh aasesekuan te nkoitoi.

English: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
Masaai: Newaliki Festo ajoki te Kaisaria erripi Paulo, netaa etataana pee elo sii ninye ine.

English: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
Masaai: Nejoki, “Metaa, enchoo ltung'ana ooata enkitoria te intae edou mairiamari, naa te neetae enatapong'e te ilo tung'ani, nepuo aaitang'or.”

English: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
Masaai: Ore etobiko nkolong'i naabaya isiet anaa tomon te nebo ninche, nedoyio alo Kaisaria; ore te nkolong nasujita ina nelo aton to lorika lenye le nkiguana neitanapisho metorikuni Paulo.

English: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
Masaai: Ore pee elotu ninye, neisho Lyahudi ootadoutuo eing'uaa Yerusalem neitashe aaman Paulo neitang'or too mbaa kumok torrok kake etalaikinote aaitadedeyie.

English: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.
Masaai: Nejo Paulo emitu kewan, “Maata tukul enaitorruoyie too Lyahudi, nemaata te nkaji e Nkai te Kaisari.”

English: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
Masaai: Kake eishoo ninye Festo, ejo pee eitiship Ilyahudi, nejoki Paulo, “Iyieu nilep alo Yerusalem, pee kipuoi aaiguanare te ine te dukuya nanu te nkaraki kuna baa?”

English: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
Masaai: Kake etejo Paulo, “To lorika le Kaisari le nkiguana aitashe, naa te ne eishaakino naaiguanareki; maata doi entorrono naitaasa Ilyahudi, naa esipata ina niyiolo iyie aitorioki.

English: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.
