Masaai: Te naa kara olkiminchali, aashu te naa kaata enataasa nairirikino keeya, maing'oru ajo ailanyaa keeya; kake te nemeetae esipata te nena naaitang'orieki, nemeetae likae laaidim aitarasaki ninche. Atejo Kaisari eyakini enkiguana ai.”

English: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.
Masaai: Ore Festo, etang'asa aikilikuanishore olkiaama lenye newaliki ajoki, “Kaisari itejo meyakini enkiguana ino, ilo naa ake enetii Kaisari.”

English: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.
Masaai: Ore etulusoitie nkolong'i naaje, nebau olaiguanani Agripa o Bernike Kaisari aairoroki Festo.

English: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
Masaai: Ore etobiko nkolong'i kumok te ine, neinosaki Festo olaiguanani enkiguana e Paulo, nejoki, “Eetae oltung'ani otung'uayie Feliks eena.

English: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
Masaai: Ore atii Yerusalem naainosaki lapolosak kituaak o lpayani loo Lyahudi mbaa enyena, eyieu nadung'oki ninye enkiguana.

English: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
Masaai: Nawaliki ajoki ninche, mme olkerreti lang Iroma ilo oishoori oltung'ani eitu etumo nkomomi e lelo ooitang'oro, ooisitaare, netum oloitang'oroki erishata namitunye kewan newalu nena naaisitaarieki.

English: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
Masaai: Ore taa pee etumo tene, eitu aimutie, amu ore pee ekenyu naton to lorika le nkiguana naitanapisho metorikuni ilo tung'ani.

English: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
Masaai: Ore pee einyiototo aaitashe lelo ooitang'or, eitu eyau e nkarrueisho anaa apa enajo nanu;

English: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
Masaai: kake eji enchankar eeta o ninye naipirta nkoon enye neipirta oltung'ani oji Yesu, otua apa, neitadedeyie ninye Paulo ajo eishu.

English: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
Masaai: Ore amu katala enaikonakino pee atum atujurro kuna baa, naikilikuan ninye tenaa keyieu nelo Yerusalem paa te ine epuoi aaiguanare te nena.

English: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
Masaai: Kake ore pee einyaku Paulo ajo metorripi paa Kaisari olo aiguanare, naitanapisho metorripi o manoto enaikunaa airriwaki Kaisari.”

English: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
Masaai: Nejoki Agripa Festo, “Kayieu o nanu nainining ilo tung'ani.” Nejoki, “Taaisere iyiooki aning ninye.”

English: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.
Masaai: Neaku ore te nkolong nasujita ina nelotu Agripa o Bernike eisikarrate, nejing ina aji e nkiguana te nebo lkituaak loo sikarini o ltung'ana kituaak le ina anasa, neitanapisho metorikuni Paulo.

English: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
Masaai: Nejo Festo, “Olaiguanani Agripa, o intae pooki ootii ene te nebo iyiook, ele tung'ani doi aaetuo olorere pooki loo Lyahudi aaitang'or, te idie te Yerusalem o te ne sii, eilepilep aajo meishiaakino neitoki aishu.

English: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
Masaai: Ore nanu makewan, natisipua ajo eitu eas ai bae nairirikino keeya, kake ore pee ejo ninye lido Aiguanani Kitok ake olo aiguanare, najo kareu naa.

English: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
Masaai: Nemaata embae enye nauno najo aigeroki Olaiguanani Kitok. Ina pee atorikuo dukuya iyie, Olaiguanani Agripa, peyie aa ore pee eidipi aatujur natum enaiger ajo.

English: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
Masaai: Kadol nanu aa kemakua te nairriwaa oloena nemaitoduaaya mbaa naaitang'orieki.”

English: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
Masaai: Nejoki Agripa Paulo, “Kinchoro iroro te kewan ino.” Neitorioo Paulo enkaina neiteru airishisho nejo:

English: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
Masaai: “Kajo nanu kamunyak aa te dukuya iyie Olaiguanani Agripa, airishisho te le kekun te nkaraki nena pooki naaitang'orie Lyahudi,

English: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
Masaai: amu iyiolo pae iyie lkerreti o enchankar oo Lyahudi; naa ina pee aaomon ting'iria inining'okoki.

English: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
Masaai: “Keyiolo Ilyahudi enkishon ai abaiki keraisho, neyiolo nkiterunot atii atua ele orere lang te Yerusalem.

English: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
Masaai: Aayiolo te nkata naado, te naa napaji keyieu neishakenoki, nchere olkerreti orrish aisul te seremata e Nkai ataa Olfarisayoi.

English: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
Masaai: Naa ore pee aitashe taata maaiguanareki te ne, enkaraki osiligi oinosie olmumai Enkai iloo papa,

English: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
Masaai: olaa ninye eisiligita lelo oshon pokira tomon o aare ejo pee etum, naa ina pee eitirrish aaserem Enkai dama o kewarie. Naa te nkaraki ele siligi, Olaiguanani, pee aaitang'oro Lyahudi!

English: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
Masaai: Aainyo doi pee ijojo meirukoyu te intae nchere keitopiu Enkai ilootuata?

English: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
Masaai: “Kajo apa nanu makewan keishiaakino te naas mbaa kumok agilunore enkarna e Yesu le Nasaret.

English: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
Masaai: Naiko doi neijia te Yerusalem; neme taa kaikenoyie ake lelo sinyat kumok te korokoroni, ekaaishoo lapolosak kituaak enkidimata, ore ninye pee eari metuata katii esiana e lelo ooyiewuaki ina.

English: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
Masaai: Nainosie ninche osina nkatitin kumok too nkajijik pooki e ntumo natem ajo aitamor ninche Enkai; naa te ina goro napi, atusujaka nkanas oo loreren.

English: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
Masaai: “Ina pee atudumunye alo Dameski aaitanapa lapolosak kituaak naata sii mpala enye.

English: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
Masaai: Ore enaipirie enkolong, lo aiguanani, nadol te nkoitoi ewang'an naing'uaa keper, nawang alang enkolong, newang'u aamanita o lelo apa laairiamariyie.

English: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
Masaai: Ore pee kibatata te nkop, naning oltoilo laajoki te nkutuk oo Lhebrania, ‘Saulo, Saulo, aainyo pee kisilisil? Iyie doi omeyu te niroro ljipeta!'

English: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
Masaai: Najo, ‘Aira ng'ae Lo Kitok?’ Nejo Olaitoriani, ‘Ara Yesu lisilisilito.

English: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
Masaai: Kake inyo ntasho too nkejek inono; amu kaatayie enkolat pee aaipang'aka, aategelua iyie taasisho ninchakenoki nena baa nitoduaa o nena naaitoki aitaliorie te iyie.

English: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
Masaai: Naa kaaitajeu te kulo tung'ana o too Loreren laa ninche aairriwaki

English: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
Masaai: pee ibol inkonyek enye, pee eibelekenya aaing'uaa enaimin aapuonu ewang'an, neing'uaa engolon e sheitani aapuonu enetii Enkai, pee eng'amu ampalakino oo ng'ok netum ewueji ti atua lelo ooitisinyaki amu nanu eiruko.’

English: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
Masaai: “Ore te nkaraki ina, Olaiguanani Agripa, eitu agolong'aki ilo otaliee te keper,

English: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
Masaai: kake aibalakinye lelo ootii Dameski, o lootii sii Yerusalem o atua enkop pooki e Yudea, o Loreren sii ninche, nchere pee eirridu neibelekenyakino Enkai neas nkiaasin naairirikino enkirridunoto enye.

English: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
Masaai: Enkaraki ena pee aaibung'a Ilyahudi te nkaji e Nkai naajo matar matua.

English: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
Masaai: Ore ebaiki ena olong aata eretoto naa Enkai eing'uaa, naa ina pee aitashe aishakenoki too looti o too lkituaak, maata ae najo neme napa naajo iloibonok le Nkai nejo Musa keaku:

English: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
Masaai: nchere meeta kata apa nemeitamei Kristo, o sii nchere ninye ong'as apiu to lootuata, pee eibalakinye ewang'an iltung'ana o loreren.”

English: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
Masaai: Ore eirishisho ajo neijia, nejo Festo to ltoilo sapuk, “Paulo, oloirirua iata, eng'eno ino kitok nikioshoo elukunya.”

English: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
Masaai: Kake etejo Paulo, “Maata nanu oloirirua, Oloyanyiti kitok Festo, isipat naaishiaakino airorita.

English: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
Masaai: Amu keyiolo ninye olaiguanani kuna baa, naa ninye ashirraki airorie; amu majo keeta hoo embae nabo e kuna nemeyiolo ninye, amu mme too nkurrat etaasaki kuna.

English: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
Masaai: Olaiguanani Agripa, isiligita doi iyie loibonok le Nkai? Ayiolo ajo isiligita.”

English: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
Masaai: Nejoki Agripa Paulo, “Ijo sa eikintaa olkiristianoi te nkiti kata.”

English: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
Masaai: Nejo Paulo, “Te naa ai te nkiti aashu te naado, kayieu napaji te Nkai neme iyie ake kake o kulo pooki laaning'ito te na olong netiu anaa enatiu nanu metii taa kulo pisia.”

English: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
Masaai: Neinyiototo taa Olaiguanani aitashe, o ilo balosi o Bernike o lelo ootoni te nebo ninche,

English: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
Masaai: ore pee epuo, nejokino maate, “Meeta ele tung'ani enaasita nairirikino keeya anaa eenata.”

English: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
Masaai: Nejoki Agripa Festo, “Keidimi napaji aatalaku ele tung'ani te neme ketoomonuo meyakini Kaisari enkiguana enye.”

English: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.
Masaai: Ore pee edung'i aajo kiked emeli aapuo Italia, neitarasakini Paulo o kulikae ooteenaki olkitok loo sikarini oji Yulio, lo ltim le Augusto.

English: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
Masaai: Nikiked emeli e Adramitio nairoto pee edumunye alo nena ang'itie e mbata e naiposha te Asia, nikipuo, neiriamariyie iyiook Aristako Olmakedoniai le Sesalonike.

English: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong nasujita ina niking'eliki Sidon; neing'urrie Yulio Paulo, neisho meshomo abaiki lchoreta lenyena meitoomoni.

English: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
Masaai: Ore te enaiposha neigara iyiook Kipros, amu ketaa keibooyo iyiook olkutati.

English: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
Masaai: Ore kitalang'a enaiposha naipirare Kilikia o Pamfilia, nikibau Mira, enkanasa e Likia.

English: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
Masaai: Ore te ine netum ilo sikari kitok emeli e Aleksantria nalang alo Italia neitaked iyiook ina.

English: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
Masaai: Nikipuo aa kutiti too nkolong'i kumok aa te ngoloto kitabautua enetaaniki Nido; ore amu meisho iyiook olkutati kipuo, nikiporoo kingura Krete o maipirare Salmone.

English: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
Masaai: Nikipuo te ngoloto kingara ine, o maetu ewueji neji Enkutoto Sidai, nenyikita enkanasa naji Lasea.

English: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
Masaai: Ore amu eiturrayioki enkata sapuk, netasuro elototo amu eidipa atulusoi enkata e mpukoroto, neiguan Paulo ninche,

English: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
Masaai: nejoki, “Lo kituaak, kadol ajo keaku kearisho ena lototo e meli neimin intokitin kumok, kake bata sii enkishui ang iyiook maate.”

English: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
Masaai: Kake etoning'o olkitok le ina meli loo sikarini, o lopeny emeli nening sii olopeny ina meli aitalang ina natejo Paulo.

English: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
Masaai: Naa ore amu mme sidai ina kutoto oo melin ebikieki te nkata e nkirobi, nejo lkumok lenye ai sidai te neporoo aapuo te ine, ejo te neidimayu nebaya Foinike, naa enkutoto ina oo melin te Krete, naipirta enkalo e nkilepunoto e kopikop o erishata e nkilepunoto e moikuape, peyie ebik te ine te nkata e nkirobi.

English: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
Masaai: Ore pee ekutu maa kutiti olkutati le moikuape, nejo ninche kenoto ina nayieu, nedotu eenet e meli neporoo aashep Krete, enyikita embata e ina kop.

English: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
Masaai: Kake ore te nkiti kata nelotu osiwuo oji ole rishata e nkilepunoto e kopikop, adoku teina kop;

English: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
Masaai: ore pee eibung osiwuo ina meli nelaikino emeli aitoriokinore, nikipalaa meterewa iyiook.

English: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
Masaai: Ore ekuetie yiook kigira aagiroo enkiti lemankale naji Kauda, te ngoloto kinotokito eenata e mpeut;

English: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
Masaai: ore ina kata pee eyietu, etureita aajo ebaiki nepuoi aaitar isinya le Sirti, neitadou olkarasha kitok oreu emeli, nerei etiu neijia.

English: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
Masaai: Ore eiposhita iyiook olkutati, neiteru te nkolong nasuju ina aaitadooyo ilolan oonapita emeli.

English: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
Masaai: Ore te nkolong e uni, neitadooyo ntokitin naagolieki emeli too nkaik enye maate.

English: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
Masaai: Ore etulusoitie nkolong'i kumok eitu ae kata eliooyu enkolong anaa lakir, neme kiti olkutati opetita iyiook, neish iyiook osiligi nikijo ebaiki ake neitajeuni iyiook.

English: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
Masaai: Ore amu etupukoitie kata naado, neipang'u Paulo ti atua ninche nejo, “Lo lewa, keishiaakino apa te naa eikitoning'o naa anaata eitu idumunyenye te Krete nipuonunu metobori intae aaiko nji neimina imasaa naaba nji.

English: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.
Masaai: Ajoki naa taata intae, entagoluoto; amu meetae hoo obo oye ti atua intae, kake eye emeli.

English: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
Masaai: Amu ore duoo te na kewarie neitashe olmalaika le Nkai nara nanu olenye naa ninye aserem,

English: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
Masaai: nejo, ‘Paulo miureishoyu, amu meeta nchere pee mintashe ake te dukuya Kaisari, naa ng'ura, kinchoo Enkai pooki likiriamariyie te meli.’

English: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
Masaai: Metaa, entagoluoto, lo lewa, amu kaata enkirukoto te Nkai nchere ketiu anaa ina ake naatiaakaki.

English: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
Masaai: Kake keetae ole mankale likikuetiki aaiponyakino.”

English: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
Masaai: Ore pee ebau enkewarie e tomon oong'uan, Kipuoito ake te naiposha e Adria, o metaa keitorito enkewarie, nemusu lelo tung'ana arewak le meli aajo kitinyikakita ae kop.

English: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
Masaai: Neitadooyo entemet netum ntemeta tomon o miet.

English: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
Masaai: Ore pee eureishoyu ejo ebaiki neitooshi iyiook emarti oo soito, neitadooyo ienet oong'uan te dukuya emeli, nesaisho mekenyu.

English: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
Masaai: Ore eing'oru lelo arewak le meli eneiko pee eluaya aaing'uaa emeli neidipa doi ninye aaitadoiki empeut enaiposha, eitaakuno keeta kulikae eenata ooitadooyo te dukuya e meli,

English: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
Masaai: nejoki Paulo olkitok loo sikarini o sikarini lenyena, “Te neitu etoni ltung'ana ti atua emeli meitajeuni intae.”

English: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
Masaai: Nedung'oo sikarini nkeenta e ina peut, neisho meshomie ina.

English: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
Masaai: Ore etaa kekenyu, nejoki Paulo ninche pooki meinosa endaa, nejoki, “Ene tomon o oong'uan ade taata ena olong isirng'ang'ate miatata endaa, eitu inyanya toki.

English: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
Masaai: Asayiaki naa intae ajoki enosa endaa; ekeisho intae engolon amu medoyio hoo ninye olpapita le lukunya e likae obo linye.”

English: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo neijia nedumu emukate, ore pee eisho Enkai enashe etii pooki, negil neiter anya.

English: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
Masaai: Negolu pooki oishuaa nenya sii ninche maate endaa.

English: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
Masaai: (Nikira pooki iltung'ana oobaya iip are o ntomoni naapishana o ile ti atua ina meli.)

English: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
Masaai: Ore pee edaa aaraposho, neiteneneng emeli, nenang'aki enkano atua enaiposha.

English: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
Masaai: Ore pee ekenyu, eitu eyiolou ninche ina kop, kake etoduaa enkutoto naata osinyai oisiasha, neiguana te naa keidim aaitabaiki ina meli ina kop natoyio.

English: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
Masaai: Metaa neiturraa ieneta lenyena nelaku nkeenta naaenita lkurteta ooboinieki emeli; neitoki taa alaaki olkarasha kitok osiwuo neitoriokino ilo sinyai oisiasha.

English: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
Masaai: Kake neikob likae sinyai oitemoro neing'irtit emeli enkop neuno olkidong'oe le meli metaa meekure edotunoyu, negilita ilopir le naiposha dukuya emeli.

English: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
Masaai: Neiguanare isikarini pee ear lelo tung'ana ooena metuata, pee mepor ake neisik aapuo;

English: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
Masaai: kake ore ilo kitok loo sikarini te nkaraki nayieu neitajeu Paulo, nerishie amitiki ninche eas ina nayieu. Neitanap ilooba anaa ilooidim aatapor enkare meituruko aadoyo te meli nepor enkare aapu enkop natoyio,

English: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
Masaai: ore lkulikae ooleku nepororie lkeek aashu mbelat e ina meli. Metaa neaku etasarutua pooki enkop natoyio.

English: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
Masaai: Ore kitajeutuo, nikipuonu aayiolou aajo keji ilo lemankale Malta.

English: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
Masaai: Ore ilopeny ina kop neitoomon iyiook to lng'ur otuluso, amu einuaa enkima neng'amaa iyiook pooki, amu eiterua asha naa keirobi.

English: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
Masaai: Netasotuo Paulo looti keek nepik enkima, nepuku olasurai te nkaraki enkirowuaj neirinakino enkaina enye.

English: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
Masaai: Ore pee edol lelo oopeny ine eililio ina ng'ues te nkaina enye nejokino maate, “Meeta nchere mme olarani ele tung'ani. Ore hoo netajeuo te naiposha, meeta esipata naishuyie.”

English: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
Masaai: Ore ninye, neipiripiroki ina ng'ues enkima nemeeta enaitaasa ninye.

English: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
Masaai: Neanyu ninche ejo ebaiki nejeyu aashu ebatata aosh enkop etua; kake ore pee eanyu te nkata naado neitu eduaaki ninye ae napiak, neibelekenya neaku kejo enkai ninye.

English: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
Masaai: Ore embata e ine wueji naa ninye etii olopololi lo laiguanani oitore ilo lemankale, neji ninye Publio, neng'amu ninye iyiook aitoomon osupatei inkolong'i naara uni.

English: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
Masaai: Neaku emuei menye Pubilio eeta oloirobi nerotu sii osarge; nelo Paulo abaiki neomon, neiteleiki nkaik neishiunye ninye.

English: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
Masaai: Ore pee etiu nejia, ore lkulikae tung'ana pooki le ilo lemankale ooata mueyiaritin, nepuonu sii ninche meishiunyeki.

English: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
Masaai: Neisho iyiook nkishorot kumok; naa ore pee kidumunye, nepikaki iyiook emeli ntokitin pooki nikiaatayie enkolat.

English: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
Masaai: Ore etulusoitie lapaitin okuni nikiked emeli, netobiko ninye te ilo le mankale te nkata e enkirobi, emeli e Aleksantria, naa nkaitin mao naasirakino elukunya enye.

English: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
Masaai: Nikipuo aang'eliki Sirakusa, nikibik nkolong'i uni te ine.

English: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
Masaai: Te ine kitudumunye nikimanaa o metabau Regio; enkolong nabo ake nashomo nedumunye osiwuo le moikuape ore te nkolong e are nikipuonu Puteoli.

English: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
Masaai: Nikitum lalashera te ine, neitoomon iyiook nikibik nkolong'i naapishana. Metaa nikipuonu Roma.

English: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii Forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
Masaai: Ore ilalashera ootii ine, pee ening'oo iyiook, nepuonu o metabau Sokoni e Apio o Mukaonini Uni aanang'are iyiook. Ninche ake etoduaa Paulo neisho Enkai enashe negolu oshoke.

English: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
Masaai: Ore pee kibau Roma, neishori Paulo eton openy, te nebo ilo sikari oirrita ninye.

English: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
Masaai: Ore pee elusoo nkolong'i uni neipotu Paulo larikok loo Lyahudi te nebo; ore pee eiturrurro nejoki ninye ninche, “Ilalashera laainei, ore hoo nemaata enaitaasa iltung'ana lang, aashu ilkerreti loo loo papa, kake aaishooyioki aena te Yerusalem aaisho nkaik oo Roma.

English: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
Masaai: Ore pee aajur ninche nanu, neyieu naalaku mashomo, amu maata apa ae naaitanang'i pookata.

English: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
Masaai: Kake ore pee eany Ilyahudi, naamiraki matasaru Kaisaria hoo nemaata ae naaipotoki olorere lang.

English: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
Masaai: Te nkaraki ina pee atejo kayieu nadol intae nairorie intae, amu enkaraki ilo ora osiligi le Israel pee aena te le pisiai.”

English: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
Masaai: Nejoki ninche ninye, “Mikiaata iyiook mpala nikitang'amaitie eing'uaa Yudea nikimpirta iyie, nimikiaata too lalashera lang ooetuo ene oloinosua aashu eliki iyiook ae torroni ti alo iyie.

English: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
Masaai: Kake kiyieu pae nikining enijo iyie o nena nilimu; amu pooki enikiyiolo ti alo ena kiteng'enare ng'ejuk napaashari, keimakini te pooki wueji eibai.”

English: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
Masaai: Ore pee egelaki ninye olkekun, nepuonu enetii te nkaji natijing'a aa kumok oleng. Neinosaki ena bae te nkakenya o memuto, eishakenoki enkitoria e Nkai netem ajo aitijing'aa ninche mbaa e Yesu too nkitanapat e Musa, o too loibonok le Nkai.

English: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
Masaai: Nejing'aa kulikae nena naatejo ninye kake eitu eiruk kulikae.

English: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
Masaai: Ore pee egela ninche maate, nepuo pee eidip Paulo atejo ena bae: “Etisipa apa Enkiyang'et Sinyati pee ejoki iloo minyi to loiboni le Nkai oji Isaya,

English: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
Masaai: ‘Shomo enetii kulo tung'ana, tiaaki, ining'ining'i doi kake mejing'aa hoo intae, ning'oring'oro doi kake midolidolo hoo intae,

English: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
Masaai: amu eikang'ate ltauja le kulo tung'ana, naa ming'anta nkiyiaa mening, neikeno nkonyek enye; pee medol ake too nkonyek enye, nening too nkiyiaa enye, nejing'aa ltauja lenye, neibelekenya maishiunye nanu ninche.’

English: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
Masaai: Entayioloito naa intae inchere, ore ena jeunoto e Nkai, eirriwakaki Loreren; ekeinining'u ninche.”

English: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
Masaai: Ore pee ejo neijia nepuo ninche Ilyahudi eishankarra maate.

English: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
Masaai: Nebik ilarin aare oolulung'a te ine, te nkaji enye naisilenuo, neng'amu lelo pooki ooetuo enetii ninye.

English: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
Masaai: Nelikioo enkitoria e Nkai neiteng'enisho too mbaa o Laitoriani Yesu Kristo aibalie nemeetae olomitiki.

English: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
Masaai: Paulo osinka le Yesu Kristo, oipotoki metaa olkipaaret, negeluni te nkaraki ororei supat le Nkai

English: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
Masaai: otolimuo apake te dukuya too loibonok le Nkai lenyena tiatua ilkigerot,

English: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
Masaai: naa ilo rorei supat oipirta ilo Inoti lenye, le ntalipa e Daudi ti alo osesen

English: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
Masaai: netolimuoki neitadedeyieki ninye te ngolon inchere Enkerai e Nkai to rrekie le Nkiyang'et Sinyati pee eitopiuni too lootuata, naa Yesu Kristo Olaitoriani lang,

English: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
Masaai: laa ninye kinotie iyiook empiris o kipaaretisho nikiyaunye enkirukoto naning'isho too loreren pooki te nkaraki enkarna enye,

English: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:
Masaai: nitii sii intae ilooipotoki te nebo ninche entaa le Yesu Kristo.

English: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Masaai: Airoroki intae lelo pooki oonyor Enkai ti atua Roma, ooipotoki entaa sinyat. Meeu empiris o eseriani atua intae eing'uaa Enkai Papa lang o Laitoriani lang Yesu Kristo.

English: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
Masaai: Ore enaituruk, ang'as aisho Enkai ai enashe ti atua Yesu Kristo tenkaraki intae pooki, enkaraki netaa kelikiori enkirukoto inyi te nkop pooki.

English: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;
Masaai: Amu Enkai shakeni lai, naa ninye aisiaai te nkishui ai ti alo ilo rorei supat lo Inoti lenye nchere eitu apal maimaki intae anaa ake te nkomono ai,

English: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.
Masaai: ajo oi kenya eishoru Enkai te yieunoto enye manoto erishata nabaikinye intae.

English: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;
Masaai: Amu ayieu naleng nadol intae, pee atum atang'arie intae enkishorunoto e nkiyang'et, natum aitagolo intae;

English: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
Masaai: ajo pee kiretutu intae te nkirukoto inyi naretu sii nanu intae te naai.

English: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.
Masaai: Kayieu niyiolouu ilalashera laainei nchere kumok inkatitin nayieu oshi nalotu abaiki intae, (kake eitu aaishori ebaiki taata,) peyie atum embata e nkisampuare tiatua intae o too loreren.

English: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.
Masaai: Aata nanu esile too Lyunani o too leme Lyunani, too looiteng'enaki o leitu.

English: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
Masaai: Ina pee ayieu oleng naliki sii ninche intae Ilomon Supati ti atua Roma.

English: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
Masaai: Amu makurru nanu te lelo Omon Supati; amu ninche engolon e Nkai nayau enjeunoto te pooki ng'ae oiruk, neituruk too Lyahudi neitoki too Lyunani.

English: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
Masaai: Amu te ninche eibalunyeki te lelo omon supati nchere ore enkiterunoto o enkiting'oto e nkoitoi naitopokie Enkai oltung'ani naa enkirukoto. Anaa enajo ilkigerot, “Ore oltung'ani oisho Enkai esipata te nkoitoi e nkirukoto nepok.”

English: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
Masaai: Amu eibalunyeki taata e ngoro e Nkai eing'uaa shumata eiba entorroni pooki o enkarruoisho oo ltung'ana ooibooyo te esipata.

English: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.
Masaai: Amu ore mbaa naayiolounoyu ti alo Enkai keibala te ninche, amu Enkai naitoduaa ninche.

English: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
Masaai: Ore anaa apa pee eitaini enkop netayioloki ake ina pukunoto enye nemelioo, aa taa enkidimata enye oo ntarasi o ina nara ninye Enkai, netaliee te nena tokitin naaitayioki. Metaa meeta hoo ninche eneitolonyaki;

English: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
Masaai: amu ore hoo neyiolo Enkai, eitu eyanyit aaitaa ninye Enkai aashu eisho ninye enashe, kake eirriirrana too ndamunot enye, neirriirrana nkorroki enye nemisimisu.

English: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
Masaai: Ore ejo ninche ai ng'eni neaku lmoda,

English: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
Masaai: neitawal enkitoo e Nkai nemeye ninye ntarasi newalunye inkitanyaanyukot neeijo oltung'ani oye ake, aashu imotonyi aashu ng'uesi, aashu ng'uesi naaikurtutari.

English: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina etung'uayie Enkai ninche neisho ing'uarrat oo ltauja lenye oonyor iloirerioni, o metaa kelaiki enkanyit iseseni lenye maate,

English: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
Masaai: amu etawalunye emonkoi isipat e Nkai nesai neisiaai entoki naitobiruaki nepal Ilo Oitobira, omayiana ninye intarasi. Esai.

English: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina etung'uayie Enkai ninche metang'uarra imbaa e sulare. Eibelekenyate ng'oruo enye aaing'uaa orrekie oishiaakino nepuo ilo lemeishiaakino,

English: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.
Masaai: nepal sii ninche ilewa aaku meing'oru nkituaak neinuaakino ng'uarrat maate, neas ilewa o lewa mbaa e nkurruna neng'amu too seseni lenye maate nena naaiu ina torroni nataasa.

English: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;
Masaai: Naa ore amu eitu edol ninche aajo keishiaakino neyanyit Enkai, neing'uaa Enkai ninche metaa, keriata indamunot enye netum olkuaak torrono.

English: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
Masaai: Iloobore empukunoto ake pooki e nkarruoisho, o entorroni, o ing'uarrat, ilaa ntorrok ake edol, iloobore olom, o ilooitayu loikop enchankar, olosek torrono, esayiet, enkurrare,

English: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
Masaai: o enkisuro, ilooiba Enkai, ilooilash, iloonya kutukie, ilooipiru ntorrok, iloogolong'aki ntoiwuo,

English: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
Masaai: ilmoda lemedamisho, ilemeisiligayu, ilooiba ilkulenye, ilemeeta olng'ur.

English: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.
Masaai: Ore hoo neyiolo enatundung'o Enkai ajo ore lelo ooas nena neiririkino keeya, neme ake duoo keas ninche kake kening'okino o lelo ooas.

English: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki nena, miaata enintolonyaki, lo tung'ani ira toki nira, te ninguanare likae; amu ore pee inguanare iyie likae naa kewan inguanare, amu ore iyie, ira oloiguanare olikae, niaasita sii iyie nena.

English: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.
Masaai: Nikiyiolo aajo edoiki enkiguana e Nkai lelo ooas nena baa.

English: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
Masaai: Ijo pasa, lo tung'ani, te ninguanare lelo ooas nena niaasita sii iyie openy, eijo pasa ilany iyie enkiguana e Nkai?

English: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
Masaai: Ana aimenaa iyie enkitoo o lng'ur lenye o eanyunoto o eng'iriata enye? Aimiyiololo aajo kejo Enkai pee kirikoki olng'ur lenye enkirridunoto?

English: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
Masaai: Kake engolon o ltau lino lemeirridu nikintaany iyie engoro e Nkai kenya te neboluni.

English: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:
Masaai: Amu kelaaki ninye pooki tung'ani aitorisioki isiaaitin enyena:

English: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
Masaai: ore lelo oong'iri aas isupati eing'oru enkitoo o enkanyit o empuaan nemeish, neisho ninye lelo enkishui nemeish.

English: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
Masaai: Kake ore lelo oonyor ate lemeiruk ina sipata, laa ntorrok esuj nening ninche, netum lelo engoro o erasakinoto.

English: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;
Masaai: Keaku osina o emion to ltung'ani pooki oas intorrok, neituruk to Lyahudi naa neijia etiu to Lyunani,

English: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:
Masaai: kake keaku enkitoo o enkanyit o eseriani te pooki ng'ae oas isupati, neituruk to Lyahudi naa neijia etiu too Lyunani.

English: For there is no respect of persons with God.
Masaai: Amu meeta Enkai olkep.

English: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;
Masaai: Ore lelo pooki ooas ing'ok meeta nkitanapat naa keimin meeta nkitanapat ore lelo ootaasa ng'ok eeta nkitanapat neiguanareki te nena kitanapat.

English: (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.
Masaai: Amu mme lelo ooning ake nkitanapat, isupati ti alo Enkai, kake lelo ooitabaya nkitanapat eishori isipat.

English: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:
Masaai: Te neas iloreren lemeeta nena kitanapat to lkerreti lenye oopeny nena naajo Inkitanapat, netaa ninche meeta nkitanapat, hoo nemeeta ninche nekua kitanapat.

English: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
Masaai: Keitoduaaya aajo keigero nena naajo nkitanapat ti atua iltauja lenye, neaku too nkorroki enye shakeni, ore ndamunot enye eiguanare ti ai kata, ore ti ai kata nemitu ninche,

English: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.
Masaai: te ina olong kenya anaa enalimu nanu te kulo omon laainei supati, te ina olong kenya eiguanare Enkai inkisudorot oo ltung'ana te Yesu Kristo.

English: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,
Masaai: Kake ti nikiji ira Olyahudi naa Nkitanapat ingarakino niwuasare osotua lino o Enkai,

English: And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;
Masaai: niyiolo iyie eyieunoto enye ninyor ina naikishiaan, amu kituutakaki ti atua nkitanapat,

English: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,
Masaai: naa te naa kesipa nchere ira iyie olarikoni loo lmodook, nira ewang'an e lelo ootii enaimin,

English: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
Masaai: nira oloutaa ilmoda, nira oloiteng'en inkera, amu iata eyiolounoto e sipata oo nkitanapat

English: Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
Masaai: amaa naa iyie oloiteng'en ilkulikae, oo pee minteng'en kewan? Amaa ilikioo ajo mipurrisho, ipurrisho pasa iyie?

English: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
Masaai: Oo iyie olojo miloloito, iloloito pasa iyie? Oo iyie oloiba nkitanyaanyukot naaitaai nkaitin, ipur pasa iyie inkajijik enye naasaishoreki?

English: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?
Masaai: Ore iyie olowuasare nena kitanapat, intukurru pasa Enkai apaashare nkitanapat?

English: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
Masaai: Amu ore anaa enatisiraki, “To lbae linyi emori enkarna e Nkai ti atua Loreren.”

English: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
Masaai: Amu esipa eeta emurata tipat te nimbung inkitanapat; kake te nigil inkitanapat netiu imurata anaa eimimurata.

English: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
Masaai: Metaa, te neibung oltung'ani lememurata nena naajo nkitanapat, aimetiu ole memurata anaa olomurata?

English: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?
Masaai: Ore naa lelo lememurata ooibung nena kitanapat ninche ooiguanare intae iloota nkitanapat naasira niaatata emurata kake nitapaashare nena kitanapat.

English: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
Masaai: Amu mme Olyahudi odede pooki ng'ae ake odoli etiu ti oriong, neme pooki ake emurata naa olodung'o ake osesen.

English: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.
Masaai: Olyahudi odede olora ti atua kewan, ore emurata nara naa embae o ltau naa ene nkiyang'et mme enasira ake. Ore enkisisa e ilo neme enoo ltung'ana kake ene Nkai.

English: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?
Masaai: Amaa naa, kaa dupoto eeta Olyahudi? Amaa ainyoo tipat e murata?

English: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.
Masaai: Eeta tipat naleng too rrekiei pooki. Neituruk inchere, Ilyahudi eitanapa Enkai ilkiliku lenyena.

English: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?
Masaai: O etaa meisiligayu kulikae lenye? Keidim ina aibelekenya metaa meisilgayu Enkai?

English: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.
Masaai: Mme neijia ina katukul! Nchoo eaku Enkai asipani hoo naa aimonkoni pooki tung'ani, anaa enatisiraki nchere, “Kintadedeyieki iyie Enkai too rorei linono, nimirisho ake te nikinguanareki.”

English: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man)
Masaai: Kake amaa te naa kenkarruoisho ang naibalie esipata e Nkai, te nkiguana, eikijo aa naa? Eikijo mme asipani Enkai te neyau engoro enye (Kairorita taa doi anaa naajo ltung'ana.)

English: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?
Masaai: Mme neijia! Amu te neaku neijia etiu, kaji naa eitoki Enkai aiko te neaku ninye olaiguanani le nkop?

English: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
Masaai: Naa amaa te naa kelejare ai naibalie oleng isipat e Nkai, neyaki ninye enchunet nalusoo oleng, oo naa pee aaitokini aaiguanare eji ataasa ng'ok?

English: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.
Masaai: Oo naa pee mikiaas ntorrok pee epuonu isupati? Amu ina doi eiteenikitia kulikae iyiook aajo neijia kijo. Ore endung'okinoto e nkiguanan natum ninche lelo naa keishiaakino.

English: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;
Masaai: Ainyoo naa? kitalang'ie iyiook Ilyahudi ilkulikae? Meeta katukul, amu kindipa iyiook aatejo nchere etii Ilyahudi, naa neijia etiu Ilyunani; abori engolon oo ng'ok.

English: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
Masaai: Anaa enatisiraki nchere: “Meetae hoo oloota esipata, netaa hoo obo Enkai

English: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.
Masaai: nemeetae hoo olojing'aa, nemeetae hoo obo oing'oru Enkai.

English: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
Masaai: Etapong'ori pooki, netaa te nebo: nemeetae obo oas isupati, meetae hoo obo.”

English: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:
Masaai: “Enkurare nang'a ilgoso lenye, neasishore ilng'ejepa lenye aalejishore.” “Esayiet o lasuriaa nanuka too nkutukie enye.”

English: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
Masaai: “Nebore nkutukie enye ildeketa o enduaran.”

English: Their feet are swift to shed blood:
Masaai: “Neten inkejek enye epuo aaibukoo osarge,

English: Destruction and misery are in their ways:
Masaai: ore irrekiei lenye naa enkidaaroto o sinaitin,

English: And the way of peace have they not known:
Masaai: nemeiyiolo ninche inkoitoi e seriani.”

English: There is no fear of God before their eyes.
Masaai: “Nemetii olturiaki le Nkai dukuya nkonyek enye.”

English: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.
Masaai: Neaku kiyiolo iyiook aajo ore pooki najo nkitanapat naa lelo ejoki ootii abori nena kitanapat, pee eitigiri ake pooki kutuk, neaku Enkai eikenaki enkop pooki imbaa enye.

English: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.
Masaai: Amu meetae oltung'ani hoo obo oikenakini esupatisho ti alo ninye to lbae loo nkiasin oo nkitanapat, amu nkitanapat eimu eyiolounoto oo ng'ok.

English: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
Masaai: Kake eibalunyeki taata esupatisho e Nkai neitu eimu nena kitanapat, hoo neishakenokito inkitanapat o loibonok le Nkai,

English: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:
Masaai: esupatisho e Nkai to rrekie le nkirukoto ti atua Yesu Kristo, te lelo pooki ooiruk. Amu meeta enepaashare;

English: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
Masaai: etaasa pooki ng'ok neitong'oro enkitoo e Nkai,

English: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:
Masaai: neikenakini esupatisho te mpiris enye metaa enkishorunoto pesho, te lakunoto natii atua Kristo Yesu,

English: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;
Masaai: ilo oishorua Enkai metaa olkipoket to sarge lenye, ongamaroyu te nkoitoi e nkirukoto. Ore apa ena naa enaitodolu esipata e Nkai, amu ore teng'iriata e Aisho enye, netogiroyie ninye ing'ok naatulusoitie;

English: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.
Masaai: pee etum aitadedeyie makewan neitusupat sii ilo oota enkirukoto ti atua Yesu.

English: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.
Masaai: Kaji naa etii olwuasa lang? Eiwuang'ieki. Ti aa kitanapata? Ai te nkitanapata oo nkiasin? Mme neijia, kake te nkitanapata e nkirukoto.

English: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
Masaai: Amu kimbung'a iyiook nchere te nkirukoto eitaae oltung'ani supat metii easata oo nkitanapat.

English: Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:
Masaai: Ana ketaa Enkai ke Nkai oo Lyahudi ake? Ai mme Enkai ninye oo Loreren sii ninche leme Ilyahudi? Ee pae, enoo Loreren sii ninche.

English: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
Masaai: Amu nabo Enkai, naa ninye oitusupat iloomurata te nkitanapata e nkirukoto enye o lelo lememurata te nkirukoto enye.

English: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.
Masaai: Ketaa naa iyiook ooibelekeny nekua kitanapat te na kirukoto? Mme neijia! Ore enatii, nkitanapat kintudupaa.

English: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
Masaai: Kaa naa kijo enoto papa lang Abraham to rrekie lo sesen?

English: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.
Masaai: Amu te naa napaji ei te nyuaata enye enotoko Abraham kewan esipata naa enaata eeta enawuasare. Kake mme te dukuya Enkai.

English: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
Masaai: Amu kejo aa ilkigerot? “Eiruko Abraham Enkai ore enkaraki ina neikenaki Enkai ninye esupatisho.”

English: Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.
Masaai: Ore naa oloisiaaisho nemeikenakini olekoisiaayio lenye anaa kenkishoroto kake anaa enenye naisiayua.

English: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
Masaai: Ore naa ilo leitu eisiaayu toki kake neiruk ilo oikenaki isipat oleme supat, neikenaki Enkai enkirukoto enye nchere esupatisho.

English: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,
Masaai: Neijia sii eikuna Daudi aimaki emayianata o ltung'ani oikenaki Enkai esupatisho neme te nkaraki isiaaitin ejo:

English: Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
Masaai: “Emayiana lelo ootapalakaki enkarruoisho neitoipori ng'ok enye;

English: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.
Masaai: nemayiana ilo tung'ani lemeikenaki Olaitoriani eng'oki enye.”

English: Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.
Masaai: Amaa ena mayianata ei loo murata ake ootum, anaa ketum sii ninche ilememurata? Kijo iyiook, eikenakaki Abraham esupatisho te nkirukoto.

English: How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
Masaai: Kaji naa eikuna pee eikenakaki ninye? Eidipaki aatumurat anaa etiu. Mme eidipaki aatumurat, anaa eitu. Mme eidipaki aatumurat, kake eton eitu emurati.

English: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:
Masaai: Ketumurataki pee eaku ina olponoto anaa olmishire le supatisho naata apa te nkirukoto eton memurata. Eikonaki neijia pee eaku ninye menye le lelo pooki ooiruk memurata laa te ina eikenakini esupatisho,

English: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.
Masaai: neaku sii menye le lelo oomurata leme kemurata ake, kake esuj ina kirukoto naata apa papa lang Abraham eton memurata.

English: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
Masaai: Ore ina kisiligata naishooki Abraham o eishoi enye, nchere keyooki aajung enkop eitu eishori te nkaraki nkitanapat kake te nkaraki esupatisho e nkirukoto.

English: For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:
Masaai: Te naa napaji ilasujak loo nkitanapat oaku ilajung'ok, pesho naa enkirukoto naa pesho ina kisiligata.

English: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.
Masaai: Amu eyau nkitanapat engoro kake ore enemetii nkitanapat nemetii engilata oo nkitanapat.

English: Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,
Masaai: Enkaraki e ina paa enkirukoto eitasheyie peyie aa empiris eigarakino ina kisiligata, neitadedeyieki te ishoi enye pooki, neme te lelo asujak loo nkitanapat aa ninche ake, kake o te lelo oong'arie Abraham enkirukoto, amu ninye menye iyiook pooki.

English: (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.
Masaai: Anaa enatisiraki aajo, “Aaitaa nanu iyie menye loo loreren kumok.” Te dukuya Enkai etang'amua ninye ina kisiligata, ina Ai nairuko ninye, naa ninye naisho ilootuata enkishui, neipotu intokin nemeetae neaku.

English: Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations; according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be.
Masaai: To siligi eiruko neisilig melioo entoki naisiligu pee etum ataa menye loo loreren kumok; anaa enapa natiaakaki eji, “Inji ebayu eishoi ino.”

English: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb:
Masaai: Eitu eshalu enkirukoto enye pee eing'or osesen lenye makewan, ototiwuo anaa olotua amu etinyikaka ilarin iip te moruao enye, aashu pee eing'or enguset e Sara ajo olupi.

English: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;
Masaai: Meetae olng'ash oidima aigusugusie enkisiligata naisiliga Enkai kake etagolo ninye te ina kirukoto anaa pee eishoo Enkai enkitoo.

English: And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.
Masaai: Etonyorrayie tukul inchere keidim Enkai aitabai ina naisiligie.

English: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.
Masaai: Ina pee eikenakaki enkirukoto enye nchere esupatisho.

English: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;
Masaai: Kake ore ilo rorei ojo “Eikenakaki”, mme enkaraki ninye ake pee etisiraki;

English: But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;
Masaai: kake enkaraki sii ninche iyiook ilooiruk ilo oitopiwuo Yesu Kristo Olaitoriani lang too lootuata,

English: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.
Masaai: olotaraki te nkaraki eanyata ang, neitopiuni pee eikenakini iyiook esupatisho.

English: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina, amu te nkirukoto eikenakaki iyiook isipat, kiaata iyiook eserian te Nkai ti atua Olaitoriani lang Yesu Kristo.

English: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
Masaai: Te ninye sii kinoto enyikakinoto e mpiris nikintasheyie, naa eiking'ida to siligi kitok likiaata te Nkai.

English: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience;
Masaai: Ore enalusoo te ina, eiking'ida o ti atua sinaitin lang, kiyiolo aajo osina oiu eng'iriata,

English: And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
Masaai: neiu eng'iriata olkuaak nadupa, neiu entonata nadupa osiligi,

English: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.
Masaai: nemeitukurru iyiook ilo siligi, amu etubukokoki enyorrata e Nkai atua iltauja lang te Nkiyang'et Sinyati naishooki iyiook.

English: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.
Masaai: Ore apa eton mikiaata eretoto, ore te nkata naishiakino neye Kristo te nkaraki ltorrok.

English: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.
Masaai: Amaa, ei mme egol pee enang likae oltung'ani oikenakaki isipat, hoo nebaiki neitieu likae atua te nkaraki oltung'ani supat.

English: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Masaai: Kake eitodolua Enkai eneba enyorrata nanyor iyiook amu ore apa eton kira iloo ng'ok, netua Kristo te nkaraki iyiook.

English: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.
Masaai: Ore naa, enkaraki ina, naikenakini taata iyiook isipat to sarge lenye, neisul naa eyooki ninye aitajeu iyiook te ngoro e Nkai.

English: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
Masaai: Amaa te naa ore apa kira iyiook ilmang'ati neitoning'oki iyiook o Enkai te nkeeya o Inoti lenye, elusoo oleng, taata kitoning'ote, eitajeu iyiook enkishui enye.

English: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.
Masaai: Neme ina ake, eiking'ida sii te Nkai ti atua Olaitoriani lang Yesu Kristo, laa te ninye kinoto ilo sotua.

English: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:
Masaai: Ore etiu neijia, enkaraki oltung'ani obo pee etijing'a ng'ok enkop, neitijing'u ng'ok enkeeya. Neaku eibulua enkeeya enkop pooki amu eitarruoitie ltung'ana pooki.

English: (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law.
Masaai: Ore doi ninye eton meetae inkitanapat, ekeetai apake ng'ok te nkop, kake ore te nemeetae nkitanapat nemeikenakini oltung'ani ng'ok.

English: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.
Masaai: Kake ore ake etiu neijia, ore ebaiki enkata e Adam o metabaiki Musa, neitoria ake enkeeya pooki o metabaiki lelo lemeeta enkitanapata natanyaita anaa pee etanya Adam. Ore Adam apa nenyanyukie lido olotu.

English: But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many.
Masaai: Paa meing'ura tukul enkiaas e mpiris e Nkai o idia apa kitarruorroto nabo e Adam. Eyaka eng'oki o ltung'ani obo iltung'ana pooki keeya, kake ore empiris e Nkai o enkishorunoto enye te ilo tung'ani obo oji Yesu Kristo neyaka pooki ng'ae emayianata nabor.

English: And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification.
Masaai: Meing'ura tukul enkishorunoto e Nkai o nena naayawua enkitarruorroto e ilo tung'ani obo, amu ore enaiguanaka Enkai ina kitarruorroto nabo naa mutata, kake ore enkishorunoto enye e mpiris neitayio inkitarruorrot kumok neyau empalakinoto.

English: For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)
Masaai: Amu eyawua eng'oki o ltung'ani obo enkitoria e keeya, te ilo tung'ani obo. Kebaa elusoo empiris e Nkai ayaki olning'o o ninye neidimie lelo oong'amu ina te mborei pooki meitoreisho te nkishui ti atua Yesu Kristo.

English: Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life.
Masaai: Ore anaa ina nayaka enkias nabo torrono mutata pooki tung'ani, neyaki sii ninye enkias nabo supat o ltung'ani supat, iltung'ana pooki elakunoto.

English: For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.
Masaai: Ore anaa ina naitaaki lkumok ilaitarruorrok te nkaraki engogong'i o ltung'ani obo, neijia eitaae lkumok supati.

English: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:
Masaai: Eetuo nkitanapat aaponaa ianyat, kake ore ine netoponariyie ing'ok te ine etuluso empiris aboreyu oleng.

English: That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.
Masaai: Neaku ore ina nayau enkitoria oo ng'ok keeya too ltung'ana, neyau ninye empiris olning'o o Enkai, olning'o oriku enkishui oo ntarasi ti atua Yesu Kristo Olaitoriani lang.

English: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
Masaai: Aikijo aa naa? Aikienikino atua ng'ok pee eponari empiris?

English: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?
Masaai: Mme neijia pae! Kaji iyiook kinko ilootuata ti alo ng'ok ti nikintoki aaenikino atua?

English: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?
Masaai: Aimiyiololo aajo ore iyiook pooki ooibung'are Yesu Kristo ti atua enkibatisa ang nikimbung'are ninye, nikitaa nabo o ninye te ina te nkaraki enkeeya enye?

English: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
Masaai: Naa ore anaa ina nikitaa nabo o ninye te nkeeya enye te nkibatisa ang, netaa ina ketunukayioki iyiook te nebo ninye, neaku ina naitopiwuo Papa ninye too lootuata te nkias e nkitoo, neaku ina enkishui ng'ejuk te iyiook.

English: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:
Masaai: Amu te neitaaki iyiook nabo o ninye te nkeeya naaijo enenye, nesipa pae keyookini aaitaa iyiook nabo o ninye te mpiunoto naaijo enenye.

English: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.
Masaai: Nikiyiolo aajo etashoki enkorrok ang musana te nebo ninye peyie eitarruorri osesen loo ng'ok pee mikintoki aaku rrindiki loo ng'ok.

English: For he that is dead is freed from sin.
Masaai: Amu ore olotua netalakuaki too ng'ok.

English: Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:
Masaai: Kake te naa eikituata iyiook te nebo Kristo, nikiruko aajo eikinchu sii te nebo ninye.

English: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.
Masaai: Amu eikiyiolo aajo ore Kristo eitopiwuoki too lootuata nemeitoki ae kata aigil aye. Meekure eitore keeya ninye.

English: For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
Masaai: Ore keeya natua ninye naa ng'ok etanang'a, nabo kata ake. Kake ore enkishui naishu ninye naa te Nkai eishu.

English: Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Masaai: Enkenai sii intae ate nchere ituata ti alo ng'ok ninchushu ti alo Enkai ti atua Kristo Yesu.

English: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.
Masaai: Emincho naa ng'ok eitoreisho ti atua iseseni linyi ooyooki aaye, metaa kearaki intae entoning ing'uarrat enye.

English: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.
Masaai: Emincho rubat oo sesen linyi eaku entoki naasishore tenkarruoisho, kake enchoo ate Enkai anaa ltung'ana ooitopiwuoki aaitung'uaa enkeeya meetu empuaan, ninchosho Enkai rubat oo seseni linyi metaa ntokitin naaisiaaishore esupatisho.

English: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
Masaai: Amu meitoki eng'oki aitore intae, amu meekure itii abori nkitanapat kake abori empiris.

English: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.
Masaai: Kaa naa ae? Eikias ng'ok amu meekure kitii abori nkitanapat kake abori empiris kitii? Mme neijia pae!

English: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
Masaai: Aimiyiololo aajo ore ake olinchosho meitoria intae niakuku rrindiki lenyena, nitaa rrindiki le ilo lining'ining'i, aa too ng'ok naa ore pee aa ng'ok isiayiayia neiting'oki keeya; ore pee aa Enkai ining'ining'i, neiting'oki esupatisho.

English: But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.
Masaai: Kake ashe te Nkai amu ore intae oora apa rrindiki loo ng'ok nitaa ilooning'isho too ltauja, aaning ina kiteng'enare naishooki intae.

English: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.
Masaai: Naa ore pee elakuni intae too ng'ok niakuku rrindiki le supatisho.

English: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.
Masaai: (Airo anaa naajo ltung'ana enkaraki e nchalan inyi e tung'ani.) Amu ore anaa ina apa ninchooitie ate aaku irrindiki loo loirerioni o enkarruoisho, etaa taata inchooitie ate aaku rrindiki le supatisho pee itumutumu aatubulu te sinyatisho.

English: For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.
Masaai: Ore apa irara rrindiki loo ng'ok, nemeeta enabaikinore intae esupatisho.

English: What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.
Masaai: Naa ainyoo lng'anayio linoto te ina? Inoto mbaa naaitukurru taata intae amu keeya eiting'oki.

English: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.
Masaai: Kake eidipaki aatalaku intae entaa rrindiki le Nkai, niaatata ilng'anayio lenyena laa embolunoto te sinyatisho, neiting'oki ina enkishui oo ntarasi.

English: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Masaai: Amu ore olekoisiayio loo ng'ok naa keeya; kake ore enkishorunoto e Nkai e pesho naa enkishui oo ntarasi ti atua Kristo Yesu Olaitoriani lang.

English: Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?
Masaai: Eimiyiololo intae ilalashera laainei amu ltung'ana sii doi ooyiolo nkitanapat airorie nchere eitore ake nkitanapat oltung'ani eton eishu?

English: For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.
Masaai: Etiu anaa te neeniki nkitanapat enkitok olpayian lenye eton eishu. Kake ore pee eye olpayian nelakuni enkitok te nena kitanapat te nkaraki enkeeya o lpayian lenye.

English: So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina, keji ake keloloito te nelo meewa likae lee eishu olpayian lenye. Kake te neye olpayian netalakuaki te ina kitanapata, naa te neyam likae lee nemeji keloloito ninye.

English: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.
Masaai: Neijia sii itiuu intae, ilalashera laainei, ituata intae ti alo nkitanapat to rrekie lo sesen le Kristo, pee iakuku ile likae, naa ilo oitopiwuoki too lootuata pee kitum iyiook aatoiki Enkai ilng'anayio.

English: For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.
Masaai: Ore apa aa osesen kinchuyie, ore ng'uarrat ang oo ng'ok, etupututuo nkitanapat, neasisho ti atua rubat ang neiu ilg'anayio le keeya.

English: But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.
Masaai: Kake ore taata, netalakuaki iyiook ti alo nena kitanapat, nikituata iyiook ti alo ina apa nateena iyiook, nemeekure aa nena kitanapat naaigero naaitore iyiook kake ena kishui ng'ejuk e Nkiyang'et kinchuyie.

English: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.
Masaai: Eikijo naa taa? Ketaa ng'ok inkitanapat? Mme neijia pae! Paa kake te neme nena kitanapat, anaata mayiolo nanu ajo ainyoo ng'ok. Anaata mayiolo ng'uarrat ajo ainyoo te neme nena kitanapat naatejo, “Ming'uar.”

English: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.
Masaai: Kake ore ng'ok, pee eisho nkitanapat erishata, neputu ti atua nanu impukunot pooki oo ng'uarrat. Ore te nemeetae nkitanapat netuata ng'ok.

English: For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.
Masaai: Eetae apa enkata naishu ake maata nkitanapat, kake ore pee elotu ina kitanapata, neinyototo ng'ok naye nanu.

English: And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death.
Masaai: Ina kitanapata kewan naji apa aayaki enkishui nataa keeya te nanu.

English: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.
Masaai: Amu ng'ok naatijing'a ina rishata naayautua nkitanapat. Naalej nanu ng'ok naa ore tiaraki ina kitanapata naar nanu matua.

English: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.
Masaai: Neaku sinyat ninche nkitanapat nesinya sii ina kitanapata, nesipa naa supat.

English: Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.
Masaai: Ketaa ina apa naji aaret naanyaaka aar matua? Mme ninye. Ore enatiu, eng'oki, pee elioyu naa duoo eng'oki, nataasishore embae naji apa pee aaret aa nanu ear matua eji, eng'oki nataasishore enkitanapata pee etum aitodolu entorroni enye nemeeta eneiting'ie.

English: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.
Masaai: Kiyiolo doi aajo ore Nkitanapat naa ne nkiyang'et, nematiu nanu neijia. Kake ara nanu oltung'ani otimiraki mataa orrindik loo ng'ok.

English: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.
Masaai: Eimayiolo doi iasat aainei makewan, amu maas enayieu naas, kake ina naiba ninye aas.

English: If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.
Masaai: Neaku te eina aas, netiu anaa nkitanapat ake atonyorrayie ajo supati.

English: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.
Masaai: Kake ore enatii meekure aa nanu oas inaas, kake ina ng'oki natii atua nanu.

English: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.
