Masaai: Naa ore te dukuya ninye, meetae hoo toki te nena naaitayioki naisudoro kake keibala pooki neboluni te dukuya nkonyek e ilo likiyaki imbaa ang.

English: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
Masaai: Ore naa amu kiaata olapolosani kitok oilepa shumata, Yesu, Oinoti le Enkai, ematukurraki aaibung elimunoto ang.

English: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Masaai: Amu mme olapolosani likiaata olemeidim atayiolo enchalan ang, kake ore ilo obo likiata naa oloidipaki apa aatetem anaa enatemitae iyiook kake eitu eas ninye ng'ok.

English: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
Masaai: Ematinyikaki naa ilo orika le mpiris kintieu, pee king'amu olng'ur nikitum empiris naretu iyiook te nkata e ngoloto.

English: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
Masaai: Amu ore olapolosani ake pooki ogeluni ti atua olorere negeluni metaasisho te nkaraki olorere tiaalo Enkai, neitayu nkishorot o lasarri te nkaraki ng'ok.

English: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
Masaai: Neidim ninye ataretu te mborron ilmoda o lwushuush, enapita ninye makewan enchalan enye.

English: And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki ena meeta nchere meng'as aitayu olasar loo ng'ok enyena makewan neitayu sii noo ilkulikae tung'ana.

English: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
Masaai: Nemeetae oloisho kewan ina kitoo, kake Enkai naipot, anaa apa pee eipot Aron.

English: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
Masaai: Neaku ore sii ninye Kristo eitu eilepie kewan meitaae olapolosani kitok, kake ketegeluaki ilo otiaaka ninye, “Ira iyie Oinoti lai taata aatoiwuo iyie,”

English: As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Masaai: anaa pee ejo te dikae wueji, “Ira iyie olapolosani ntarasi, to lkerreti le Melkisedek.”

English: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
Masaai: Ore too nkolong'i enyena o sesen etoomonuo Yesu esaisho, nebuaku oleng too lkiyio, esai ilo apa oidim aitajeu te nkeeya, netoning'oki ninye te nkaraki naure ninye Enkai.

English: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
Masaai: Amu ore hoo naa Oinoti ninye, eitamoo kewan enkirukoto te ina mion nanoto,

English: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;
Masaai: naa ore amu eitabayioki, etaa ninye enjeunoto oo ntarasi te lelo pooki ooning ninye,

English: Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
Masaai: neitaa Enkai ninye olapolosani kitok to lkerreti le Melkisedek.

English: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
Masaai: Ore te na bae keetae nkumok naaji naagol elimunoto, amu eijo ketagolo intae ilukuny mining'ung'u.

English: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
Masaai: Amu ore aa intae napaji taata ilaiteng'enak, neton eiririkino te nelotu likae aigilie intae nkiterunot o rorei le Enkai. Eton aa kule naairirikino intae, mme endaa nagol;

English: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
Masaai: amu ore pooki ng'ae laa kule ake eishuyie naa alani to rorei le supatisho, amu eton aa enkerai ninye.

English: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
Masaai: Kake ore endaa nagol naa enoo ltung'ana botoro, ene lelo ooiteng'enaki to lmoo metayiolo aatirishu isupati o ntorrok.

English: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
Masaai: Ore naa ematogiroi nkiterunot oo nkiteng'enat e Kristo emaape dukuya aabulu, meaku eikintoki aaitamanya enkirridunoto niking'uaa isiaaitin naatuata, o enkirukoto nikiruk Enkai,

English: Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
Masaai: o enkiteng'enata e nkisuja o enkiteleikinoto oo nkaik, o empiunoto oo lootuata, o enkiguana oo ntarasi.

English: And this will we do, if God permit.
Masaai: Naa aikiaas kuna pooki eishorua Enkai.

English: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
Masaai: Amu meidimayu neitokini aitasheyie te nkirridunoto lelo ooidipaki aaitawang'a, neishamishama enkishorunoto e shumata, netang'arieki Enkiyang'et Sinyati,

English: And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
Masaai: neishamishama esupatisho o rorei le Enkai o engolon e ina kata nalotu,

English: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
Masaai: teneitoki ninche etii nena, aaibelekenya neany eiruk, amu ilo Inoti le Nkai eigil aashe maate nepik enkurruna metalioyu.

English: For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
Masaai: Amu ore enkop naok enkare nashaiki nkatitin kumok, nebulaki endaa naret lelo ooturokini, netum emayianata naing'uaa Enkai.

English: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.
Masaai: Kake te neiu ilkiku o endiati, neaku pesho nenyikaki oldeket; naa empejoroto eiting'oki.

English: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
Masaai: Ore hoo naa neijia ti nikiro, ore te intae, ilanyor laainei, kesipa nchere kiaatayie intae osiligi loo mbaa naaikash e njeunoto.

English: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
Masaai: Mme Enkai neme asipani metaa kerikino enkisiaayiare inyi enyorrata nintoduaaitie ti alo lelo sinyat ooisiaaisho, neton ake isiaaitata.

English: And we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:
Masaai: Nikiyieu neitoduaaya pooki ng'ae linyi enyuaata naikununo neijia pee itumutumu emborei oo sipat osiligi o meiting'o,

English: That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
Masaai: pee miaakuku yietuti, kake ilooduaaya lelo laa te nkirukoto enye o te ng'iriata etujung'o nkisiligat.

English: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
Masaai: Amu ore pee eisho Enkai Abraham enkisiligata naa ore amu meetae likae kitok olang oinosie olmumai, neinosie kewan olmumai,

English: Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
Masaai: nejo, “Esipa kaamayian nanu iyie naaponaa.”

English: And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
Masaai: Neaku ore Abraham, etobiko neng'iri, netum enkisiligata.

English: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
Masaai: Oltung'ani kitok alang kewan einosie oltung'ani olmumai naa ore te nchankar ake pooki aa olmumai oitadedeyie.

English: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
Masaai: Neaku ore apa pee eyieu Enkai neitoduaya tukul nchere meibelekenya enkiguana enye, nepik olmumai,

English: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
Masaai: peyie aa too mbaa are nemeibelekenya, naa te nena meidimayu pee eaku Enkai olalejani, kinoto iyiook ilooisikakita aasaru eretoto nagol nikimbung'ie ilo siligi otipikaki dukuya iyiook.

English: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
Masaai: Kiata iyiook ena ng'ape nauno naenikino oltau, naa osiligi ojing agiroo oliatua lo lkarasha orish enkaji e Enkai,

English: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Masaai: ine neshomo Yesu aituruk te nkaraki iyiook, eidipa ninye ataa olapolosani kitok intarasi to lkerreti le Melkisedek.

English: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
Masaai: Amu ore ele oji Melkisedek, olaiguanani le Salem, naa olapolosani le Enkai, netii shumata te pooki, netanang'are ninye Abraham eshukunye aing'uaa enjore natimirie laiguanak, nemayian ninye;

English: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
Masaai: naa ninye etoorikia Abraham ematua e tomon e pooki toki. Eituruk ninye, te newaluni enkarna enye, aa olaiguanani le supatisho, naa olaiguanani le Salem, eji Olaiguanani le seriani.

English: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
Masaai: Meeta ninye menye anaa ng'otonye, nemeeta entipat, nemeeta eneiting'ie enkishui enye, kake etiu anaa ilo Oinoti le Nkai, ora olapolosani ntarasi.

English: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
Masaai: Ng'ura eneba enkitoo enye! Eishoo papa lang Abraham ninye ematua e tomon oo yarunot.

English: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:
Masaai: Naa ore lelo le ishoi e Lawi oong'amu empolosare neetae naitanapaki ti atua nkitanapat meishoo olorere ninche ematua e tomon, naaton lalashera lenye, hoo naa le ishoi e Abraham sii ninche.

English: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
Masaai: Kake ematua e tomon naishoo Abraham nemayian ninye ilo apa otang'amua nkisiligat.

English: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
Masaai: Metii enchankar inchere olkitok ake omayian oloti,

English: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
Masaai: ore te ne, iltung'ana ooyooki aaye, oong'amu ematua e tomon, ore te ine, naa ilo obo oitadedeyieki aajo keishu.

English: And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
Masaai: Keidim doi ninye oltung'ani atejo ore ninye Lawi makewan, oishoro metang'amu ematua e tomon, eishooyie ematua e tomon te Abraham,

English: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
Masaai: amu eton apa etioyo too sapo too sapo e nkakuyiaa lenye pee enang'are Abraham Melkisedek.

English: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
Masaai: Ore taata te naa ketumoyu apa bayaroti te mpolosare oo le Lawi, amu te ninye etang'amutua ilo orere nkitanapat, ainyoo eitokini aayieunye likae apolosani olotu to lkerreti le Aron?

English: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
Masaai: Amu te neibelekenyi lapolosak neibelekenyi sii ninche nkitanapat.

English: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
Masaai: Amu ore ele oimaki kuna baa naa ole likae osho lemeeta ninche ae kata oltung'ani lenye otopolosishe to lperere lo lasar.

English: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
Masaai: Amu eibala olosho le Yuda etoikioki Olaitoriani lang, naa ore te ilo osho, neitu ejo Musa ae naipirta ilapolosak.

English: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
Masaai: Keitoki ena bae awang'u oleng te neinyototo likae apolosani lo rreikie le Melkisedek,

English: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
Masaai: ajo eitaaki olapolosani neme to rrekie loo nkitanapat anaa te ntipat o sesen ake eeta engolon, kake te nkidimata enkishui nemeidimi aaishie.

English: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Masaai: Amu eitaikiaki ninye shakenisho nchere, “Iraiyie olapolosani ntarasi to rrekie le Melkisedek.”

English: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
Masaai: Ore te nabo alo, eiwuang'ieki enapa kitanapata naituruku te nkaraki nashal nemeeta dupoto,

English: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
Masaai: amu meetae entoki naiputakine te nkaraki nkitanapat, ore te nkae alo, eyawuaki osiligi oikash, laa te ninye kinyikaki iyiook Enkai.

English: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:
Masaai: Neitu easi ina metii olmumai.

English: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
Masaai: Ore lelo apa ooitera aaku ilapolosak netaa metii olmumai, kake ore ele netolimuoki to lmumai, “Einosa Olaitoriani olmumai nemeibelekeny enatejo inchere, ‘Ira iyie olapolosani intarasi.’ ”

English: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
Masaai: Ena naishoo Yesu meitadedeyie osotua olusoo to likae.

English: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
Masaai: Ore lapa apolosak ooiturukutuo naa kumok esiana enye, amu etomitikio enkeeya ebikoo te mpolosare;

English: But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
Masaai: kake eibung'ita ninye empolosare enye nemeiting, amu ebik ninye intarasi.

English: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
Masaai: Ina pee eidim ninye aitajeu nkatitin pooki lelo ooimu ninye epuonu aanyikaki Enkai, amu eishu oshi ake ninye netumoki atoomonoki ninche.

English: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
Masaai: Amu eikash te iyiook, ti nikiata olapolosani kitok oba nji osinyati, lemeeta entiyoto, nemeeta entibili, olotirishuaki too laing'okok neilepieki aaitogiroo shumata.

English: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
Masaai: Meetayie ninye tipat, anaa enatiu apa lelo kulikae apolosak, meeta tipat napolosishore anaake, to lbae loo ng'ok enyena makewan, neitoki apolosisho to lbae loo ng'ok o lorere, eitabayie ninye ina nabo kata ake apa pee eishooyo kewan.

English: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
Masaai: Esipa nchere nkitanapat naaitaa ltung'ana ooshal lapolosak kituaak, kake ore ilo rorei lo lmumai, otusujua nkitanapat, netegelua ilo Inoti bayaroti obik intarasi.

English: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
Masaai: Ore embae sapuk te kuna naaji naa ena: eikiaata doi iyiook olapolosani kitok oba neijia. Olotonita te tatene e Nkitoo e Shumata,

English: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
Masaai: olaisiaayiani le ine wueji sinyati o le ilo ng'obor osipa leme oltung'ani oitasheyie kake Olaitoriani.

English: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
Masaai: Amu ore olapolosani ake pooki netegeluaki meishooi nkishorot neitayu lasarri, naa keishaakino apa neeta sii ninye ele apolosani entoki naishooyo.

English: For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:
Masaai: Ore te naa kena kop etii, nemeaku hoo olapolosani, amu keetae naa lelo kulikae apolosak ooishooyo nkishorot anaa enajo nkitanapat.

English: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
Masaai: Neisiaai ninche nyaanyukie o loip le ine wueji sinyati te shumata; amu ore pee eaku keun Musa olng'obor, netuutaka Enkai ninye nejoki, “Toduaa taa ntobira pooki toki nturubare lelo sirat likintoduaaki to ldoinyio.”

English: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
Masaai: Kake ore anaa enatiu, enoto ninye Kristo enkisiaayiare naikishiaan ele sotua oyau ninye, amu eitabayioki too nkisiligat naalusoo te nekua.

English: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
Masaai: Amu tene meeta apa ilo sotua ntiyot, naa anaata meetae ae nayaunyeki likae liaare.

English: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
Masaai: Amu ntiyot etoduaa te ninche pee etejo: “Kepuonu nkolong'i, Olaitoriani ojo, naa kayooki aitayu osotua ng'ejuk o enkaji e Israel o enkaji e Yuda.

English: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
Masaai: Lemetiu anaa olapa sotua laitayio o loo menye enapa olong pee aibung ninche te nkaina ariku aitung'uaa enkop e Misiri; amu eitu ninche etoni ti atua osotua lai, naa ina pee eitu aitoki ashilaa ninche Olaitoriani ojo.

English: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
Masaai: Nele osotua laitayu o enkaji e Israel te nelusoo nena olong'i, Olaitoriani ojo. Kapik nkitanapat aainei atua lukuny enye, naiger ninche ti atua iltauja lenye, naa kaaku Enkai enye, neaku ninche iltung'ana laainei.

English: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
Masaai: Nemeitoki pooki ng'ae aiteng'en ole latia enye aashu eiteng'en pooki ng'ae olalashe lenye, ajoki, ‘Tayiolo Olaitoriani,’ amu kaayiolou pooki nanu, eiteru to loti te pooki o metabaiki olkitok te pooki.

English: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
Masaai: Amu katum kenya ake olng'ur ti alo ntorrok enye, nemaitoki ae kata adamu ng'ok enye.”

English: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
Masaai: Ore eimaki ninye osotua ng'ejuk neitaa musana ole nkiterata. Ore ilo omusanu aaku moruo netinyikaka enkiishata.

English: Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
Masaai: Ore doi ninye ilo sotua le dukuya neeta apa irrekiei le seremare o ewueji sinyati e nkop.

English: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
Masaai: Amu eitobiraki olng'obor li oriong, laa atua ninye etii olkilang'et o emesa omukateni e nkitoduaaroto; neji ine Ewueji Sinyati.

English: And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
Masaai: Ore ti oriong olkarasha li aare neitashe olng'obor oji Sinyati Oleng,

English: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
Masaai: netii olperere lo lasar le nkorropil le sahabu o ilo sanduku losotua omura pooki alole te sahabu, netii atua ilo moti e sahabu natii mana, o enapa ng'udi e Aron natubulakita mbenek, o lapa soito lo sotua;

English: And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
Masaai: netii ilkerubi le nkitoo ooitushurita ilo orika lo lng'ur. Ore kuna tokitin nimikindim aaimaki taata nikisipu.

English: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.
Masaai: Ore pee eidipi aaitabai kuna kitobirat, neaku kejing ilapolosak anaake atua ilo ng'obor aaitabaya empolosare enye;

English: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
Masaai: kake ore ine e are, olapolosani kitok ake ojing, ore ninye naa kata nabo to lari, nemejing meetae osarge oishooyo te nkaraki kewan enye o te nkaraki inkitarruorrot e ilo orere.

English: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
Masaai: Te na bae eitodolu Enkiyang'et Sinyati inchere eton mebolo enkoitoi najing'ieki ine wueji sinyati eton ake eitashe ilo ng'obor lioriong,

English: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
Masaai: naa ina enkitanyaanyukoto e na kata taata. Ore te risioroto ele rrekie neishoori inkishorunot, o lasarri lemeidim aaitaa supati indamunot elelo oosaisho,

English: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
Masaai: kake endaa ake eipirta o enaoki o enkitukuore oo mpukunot kumok, naa imbaa naaitore osesen naatuunoki o metabau enkata enkibelekenyata.

English: But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
Masaai: Kake ore eewuo Kristo anaa olapolosani kitok loo mbaa supati naapuonu, neaku ore to lng'obor kitok obaya, leme inkaik naaitobira, inchere, ime olena kitayunoto,

English: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
Masaai: etijing'a ninye nabo kata Ewueji Sinyati, neme osarge loo lkineji o lasho etoshoroyie kake osarge lenye makewan, neitadedeyie te ina elakunoto oo ntarasi.

English: For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
Masaai: Amu amaa te naa ore iltung'ana ooiduruk naa keituku enkisuaakinoto o sarge loo lkineji o loo loing'ok o nkuruon e ntawuo te nkipooto o lo sesen,

English: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
Masaai: kebaa naa elusoo osarge le Kristo, laa te ina Kiyang'et oo ntarasi eishoo kewan Enkai meeta entiyoto, aituku indamunot inyi neitung'uaa isiaaitin naatuata esiaayia Enkai naishu.

English: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
Masaai: Ore te nkaraki nena, ninye olaidikidikoni lo sotua ng'ejuk, paa ore lelo ooipotoki netum inkisiligat e njung'ore oo ntarasi, amu enotoki enkeeya ng'ejuk nalaku too nkitarruorrot lelo ootii abori lido sotua le dukuya.

English: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
Masaai: Amu ore te neetae empalai e njung'ore, neng'asi ake aaitadedeyie enkeeya eilo oitujung'ishe.

English: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
Masaai: Amu pooki ake pee ejung'ishoi naa te neetae olotua, amu mejung'ishoi eishu oloitujung'ishe.

English: Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.
Masaai: Naa ina pee eitu apa eitabari olapa sotua musana metii osarge.

English: For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
Masaai: Amu ore apa, keimaki ake Musa enkitanapata ake pooki enena aliki olorere nedumu osarge loo lasho o loo lkineji, te nebo enkare olpapit oonyokie loo ntare o lchani oji hisop, neisuaaki embuku kewan o lelo tung'ana pooki,

English: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
Masaai: ejoito, “Osarge ele lo sotua oitanapa intae Enkai.”

English: Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
Masaai: Neiko sii neijia ilo sarge eisuaaki kunda pokira are, ilo ng'obor o ntokitin pooki naasishoreki te seremare.

English: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.
Masaai: Esipa nchere, ore to lkerreti loo nkitanapat o sarge apake eipoki pooki toki to sarge, naa ore eitu eibukori osarge nemeetae empalakinoto oo ng'ok.

English: It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
Masaai: Neaku meeta apake kata nemeitukui kuna tokitin naa inkitanyaanyukot ake e nekua e shumata aaipokie kulo asarri, kake ore nena tokitin maate e shumata neipokieki lasarri oolang kulo.

English: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
Masaai: Amu eitu eitijing'i Kristo, ewueji sinyati naitobiraki too nkaik naa enkitanyaanyukoto ake e idia nasipa, kake atua shumata kewan, paa keitashe taata te dukuya Enkai terishata ang.

English: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;
Masaai: Neme keitoki ninye aigiligil aishooyo kewan, anaa enaiko ilo apolosani kitok ejing atua ine Wueji Sinyati anaake to lari eeta osarge leme o lenye;

English: For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
Masaai: amu te naa neijia etiu, naa anaata eigilieki ninye emion ana apa moitie pee eitamanyuni enkop. Kake ore enatiu, etaliee ninye nabo kata ake te pooki eiting'o enkata pee eiwuang'ie ng'ok eitaa ninye kewan olasar.

English: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
Masaai: Naa ore anaa enaitanapishoteki metuata iltung'ana nabo kata ake, ore pee elusoo ina nelotu enkiguana,

English: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
Masaai: neijia sii etiu Kristo, ore eidipaki aaitarasai ena nabo newa ng'ok oo lkumok, keliooyu eni are, neme ng'ok elotu aararr kake kelotu aitajeu lelo ooanyita ninye te yieunoto sapuk.

English: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
Masaai: Ore amu oloip ake le nena sidain naapuonu eeta nena kitanapat neme nekua tokitin naasipa naara nemeidim aekata, te lelo asarri ooitaini to lari ake osuju olikae, imeidim aaitaa bayarot lelo oonyikaki.

English: For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
Masaai: Amu te naa keidim anaata apa meekure eitaini. Te naa keitukuoki lelo aseremak, anaata meitoki aayioloiki ate ng'ok.

English: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
Masaai: Kake ore ti atua lelo asarri netii enkitadamunoto oo ng'ok anaa ake te pooki ari.

English: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
Masaai: Amu meidimayu metaa osarge loo loing'ok o lkineji ooya ng'ok.

English: Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
Masaai: Enkaraki nena, ore apa pee elotu Kristo enkop, nejo, “Ore ilasarri o nkishorunot imiyieu iyie kake osesen kintobiraka nanu;

English: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
Masaai: ore ilasarri oopeji o nkishorunot oo ng'ok neitu ishipakino iyie.

English: Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.
Masaai: Ina pee tejo, ‘Ng'ura nele nanu, oewuo pee aas eniyieu, eyieunoto ino, Na Ai ai!’ anaa enatisiraki tialo nanu ti atua olpiyayati le mbuku.”

English: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law;
Masaai: Ore pee ejo to ine te shumata, “Eitu iyieu iyie neitu ishipakino ilasarri o nkishorunot naapeji o nkishorunot oo ng'ok.” Neishooyioki kuna te risioroto anaa enajo nkitanapat,

English: Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
Masaai: nenyaaka aponaa ajo, “Nele nanu, aewuo paa aas enyieunoto ino.” Keiwuang'ie ninye idia e dukuya peyie etum aitasheyie eniare.

English: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Masaai: Naa ina eitukuyieki iyiook te nkishorunoto o sesen le Yesu Kristo nabo kata ake te rishata e pooki.

English: And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
Masaai: Neitashe olapolosani ake pooki anaake te siaai enye, eigil aitayu iloshi ake asarri, lemeidim ae kata aawaita ng'ok.

English: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;
Masaai: Kake ore pee eidip Kristo aitayu olasar loo ng'ok obo ake loo nkatitin pooki, neton ninye te nkaina e tatene e Enkai,

English: From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
Masaai: Paa te ine eton o metaba anaa neitaae ilmang'ati lenyena olorika loo nkejek enyena.

English: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
Masaai: Amu to lasar obo eitabayie ninye te nkata pooki lelo ooitukuoki.

English: Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,
Masaai: Neitaiki sii ninye enkiyang'et Sinyati iyiook shakeni; te nkata nasuju ejo,

English: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
Masaai: “Nele osotua laitayu nanu o ninche te siadi nena olong'i, Olaitoriani ojo, naa kapik inkitanapat aainei iltauja lenye, naiger ninche too ndamunot enye.”

English: And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.
Masaai: Neitoki aponaa nejo, “Ore ing'ok o nkitarruorrot enye nemaitoki adamu ae kata.”

English: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
Masaai: Ore enetii empalakinoto e kuna, nemeitoki atii olasar loo ng'ok.

English: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
Masaai: Ore enkaraki nena, ilalashera, ore naa amu eikiaata iyiook enkitieunoto nikijing'ie ine wueji sinyati to sarge le Yesu,

English: By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
Masaai: te ina oitoi ng'ejuk naishu nataboloko ninye iyiook te ilo karasha, aa taa to sesen lenye,

English: And having an high priest over the house of God;
Masaai: nikiaata sii olapolosani kitok oitore enkaji e Enkai;

English: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
Masaai: ematinyikaki to ltau osipa ti atua emborei e nkirukoto, neisuaakaki iyiook aaisuj ltauja lang metaa mikiaata ileeni too ltauja lang neisujaki iseseni lang te nkare nasila.

English: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)
Masaai: Emaibung'a aakurraki elimunoto o siligi lang mikingusugus, amu keisiligayu ilo oishorua ina kisiligata;

English: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
Masaai: naa ematadamu enikinkunakino olikae olikae enkisusunkat o enyorrata o siaaitin sidain,

English: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
Masaai: nimikipalaa entumo, anaa enatiu olkuaak le kulikae, kake intagolo olikae olikae neisul idolitata aajo etinyikua ina Olong.

English: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
Masaai: Amu ti nikiaas ing'ok aaotiki kindipa aatang'amu eyiolounoto e sipata, nemeitokini aata olasar loo ng'ok,

English: But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.
Masaai: kake enkuretisho e anyunoto e ndung'okinoto e nkiguana, o engoro e nkima namut lelo mang'ati.

English: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
Masaai: Ore apa oltung'ani ogil nena kitanapat e Musa neye metii olng'ur te neetae shakenisho oo ltung'ana aare aashu okuni.

English: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
Masaai: Ijo kebaa elusoo enkitamioto nayaki kewan oltung'ani oany Oinoti le Enkai, neisarkionie osarge lo sotua laa ninye eitukuyieki neitagor ina Kiyang'et e mpiris?

English: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
Masaai: Amu eikiyiolo ilo otejo, “Enaai elap, nanu oitalaku.” Nejo sii, “Olaitoriani oiguanare iltung'ana lenyena.”

English: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Masaai: Entoki naitureisho ti nibatatakino inkaik e Enkai naishu.

English: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
Masaai: Kake entadamu sii intae napa olong'i e dukuya ina kata apa eidipaki aaitawang'aki intae, ing'iriri enkitirrishakinoto nagol te nebo emion,

English: Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.
Masaai: neaku kebolori intae metamori te dukuya olorere neisilisili intae, nitaa ti ae kata encholiek e lelo ooikunaki neijia.

English: For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
Masaai: Amu iutata apa olng'ur too looena, nitonyorraitie te nchipai meishang'itieki masaa inyi, amu eiyiololo apa aajo iatata intae maate entoki nalang naa enabikoo.

English: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina eminturraa naa enkitieunoto inyi, naata olerrinyore kitok.

English: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
Masaai: Amu meeta nchere pee miaatata eng'iriata, pee itumutumu aataas enayieu Enkai, ning'amumu ina kisiligata natolimuoki,

English: For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.
Masaai: “Amu eng'or enkiti kata, pee elotu ilo olotu nemeimutie;

English: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
Masaai: Kake enkirukoto eishuyie osinyati lai, naa te nerrinyo siadi, nemeshipakino oltau lai ninye.”

English: But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.
Masaai: Kake mikira iyiook ile lelo oorrinyo siadi nemuti, kake kira ile lelo ooata enkirukoto negolie iltauja lenye.

English: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
Masaai: Ore enkirukoto naa ninye naitadedeyie intokitin naaisiliguni, naa ninye enkitisipata e nena tokitin nemelioo.

English: For by it the elders obtained a good report.
Masaai: Amu te nkirukoto etonyorrarrie Enkai iltung'ana li apa.

English: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto kiyiolo aajo eitayioki enkop te nkiroroto e Enkai, neaku ore kuna naadolitai naa too nemelioo eitobiraki.

English: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto eyaka Abel Enkai olasar ong'amaroyu alang ole Kain, laa ninye etonyorrarrie Enkai ninye ajo supat, etaa Enkai shakeni amu etang'amayie olasar lenye; etua ninye kake ore te nkirukoto enye neton eirorita.

English: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto ewaki Enok aailepie pee medol keeya; neitu etumi, amu Enkai nawa ninye. Naa ore eton eitu eilepieki neitisipaki nchere eitishipa ninye Enkai.

English: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
Masaai: Naa ore metii enkirukoto nemeidimayu peyie eitishipi ninye. Amu ore pooki ng'ae oyieu nenyikaki Enkai naa ore ake meiruko inchere keetae ninye naa ninye oisho inkishorot lelo ooing'oru ninye.

English: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto eitatala Enkai Noa nena baa apa neton melioo nening ninye neitobir esafina pee esaru enkaji enye; te na bae etudong'oko enkop enkiguana neaku ninye olajung'oni le supatisho natumi te nkirukoto.

English: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etoning'ishe Abraham pee eipoti metupuku alo ewueji nelotu atum nejung; nepuku ninye nelo, nemeyiolo enelo.

English: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etobiko aa omoni te ina kop naisiligieki, anaa te neeiking'a naa ilng'oborri emany o Isaak o Yakobo, oora sii ninche ilajung'ok le ina kisiligata te nebo ninye.

English: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
Masaai: Amu ina anasa eanyita naata enkitamanyunoto enaa ore oloshetu o loitobir naa Enkai.

English: Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto enoto Sara enkidimata nemenayu te ishoi etaa moruo, netulusoitie ilarin lenyena, etoduaa ninye ajo keisiligayu ilo oishoo enkisiligata.

English: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
Masaai: Enkaraki nena paa oltung'ani obo, etiu apa ninye anaa olotua enotoki eishoi naba te nkumoi anaa ilakir le shumata nemeikenayu etiu anaa osinyai le mbata e naiposha.

English: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
Masaai: Etuata kulo pooki etii atua enkirukoto, neitu eng'amu ninche enapa naisiligieki, kake etoduaa neirorokita, te nelakua, netolimutuo inchere ilomon ninche naa inkisikat te nkop.

English: For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
Masaai: Amu ore lelo tung'ana oojo neijia neibalunye inchere enkop apa nabikie eing'oru.

English: And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.
Masaai: Te naa kenkop apa natung'uaitie edamu ninche, anaata apa enoto erishata nashukore.

English: But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.
Masaai: Kake ore anaa enatiu, ae kop eyieu sidai te ina, naa ene shumata, Enkaraki e ina pee mekurru Enkai te neji ninye Enkai enye, amu eitobiraka ninye ninche enkanasa.

English: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
Masaai: Te nkirukoto eitayio Abraham, Isaak, enapa kata pee etemi, aishooyo oinoti lenye obo,

English: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
Masaai: oloimakaki aajo, “Isaak eipotieki eishoi ino.”

English: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
Masaai: Etoduaa ninye ajo keidim Enkai aitopiu iltung'ana ebaiki ilootuata; te ina kitanyaanyukie aajo, enoto ang'amu.

English: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etamayiana Isaak Yakobo o Esau too naapuonu.

English: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto, etaa keye, etamayiana Yakobo ilayiok le Yosef, eigarakino ninye elukunya e ntirma enye eirrugo aseremisho.

English: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etaa eiting'o Yosef, eimaka enaidurra oo Siraeli neutaki eneikunaa enukaroto enye.

English: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto, pee eini Musa, eisudoyioki lapaitin okuni intoiwuo enyena, amu etoduaa ninche aajo aisidai ina kerai; neitu eureyu ninche ina naitanapishe olaiguanani.

English: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
Masaai: Te nkirukoto, etanya Musa, etubulua, eipoti aajo ole ntito e Farao,

English: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Masaai: nedutaa meinosieki osina te nebo iltung'ana le Enkai alang te neton aitumurru olkar loo ng'ok.

English: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
Masaai: Etoduaa ajo emoroto namori te nkaraki Kristo naikash alang enkarsisisho o masaa kiroteti e Misiri, amu keanyita idia kishorunoto.

English: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto eshomo aing'uaa Misiri, neitu eiureyu engoro e ilo aiguanani; amu eting'iria anaa olodolita ilo lemelioo.

English: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto, eitayio Pasaka neisuaaya osarge, pee, mear ninche ilo Arani loo lkikaunot.

English: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etalang'a lelo tung'ana enaiposha nanyokie anaa enkop natoyio; kake ore Ilmisiri pee etem aajo maikuna neijia, neya enkare.

English: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto etuurori isunta e Yeriko etamanaki too nkolong'i naapishana.

English: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
Masaai: Te nkirukoto pee eitu eari Rahabu ina mulayoi, te nebo lelo apa kulikae lemening'isho, amu etang'amua ninye lelo aikitalak to sotua.

English: And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
Masaai: Naa kakua kulie naitoki aajo? Amu maata enkata naimakinye Gideon, Barak, Samson, Yepta, Daudi o Samuel o lelo oibonok le Enkai

English: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
Masaai: ilaa te nkirukoto etimira inkitoriat, neitabaya te ngolon enkiguana oo sipat, neng'amu nkisiligat, neibooyo nkutukie oo lng'atunyo,

English: Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
Masaai: near olkutati le nkima, neilany enepi o lalem enkidimata ti atua enchalan, neaku magil te njore, nemir injoreitin oo lmang'ati.

English: Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
Masaai: Etang'amutua inkituaak ilootuata lenye eitopiwuoki, Einosieki kulikae osina, etanyaita elakuni, ejo pee eyooki aapiu te mpuaan nalang ina.

English: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
Masaai: Eting'iria kulikae imorot o oshot, o metabaiki ilpisia o korokoroni.

English: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;
Masaai: Eirruyaki too soito, nedung'i te musumeno aitaa are, neari to lalem nepuaya eishopito ndapan oo nkerra oo noo nkineji, ilaisinak o looisilisili neinyali

English: (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
Masaai: ilemeishiakino enkop te netii nepuaya too lpurkel o too ldoinyo, o too ldoinyio, o too rrumati o too nkapuniaa e nkop.

English: And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
Masaai: Ore kulo pooki, hoo neitadedeyieki te nkirukoto enye, neitu eng'amu ina kisiligata,

English: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.
Masaai: amu etasioko apa Enkai adol embae naikash te iyiook, inchere ore mikitii iyiook nemeitabari ninche.

English: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
Masaai: Ore enkaraki nena, amu etaa emanita iyiook enkatampoi kitok e lelo shakenini, emaiturrai sii iyiook enkiroishi ake pooki, o eng'oki naonyikino iyiook oleng, emaipirrio te ng'iriata te ina kuetata natipikaki dukuya iyiook.

English: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Masaai: Emaimariria Yesu olaa ninye olaiturukoni naa oloitabaya enkirukoto ang, olaa ore enkaraki eng'ida natipikaki dukuya ninye neting'iria osalaba, nemenu ina kurruna, neton taata te nkaina e tatene o lorika le nkitoo e Enkai.

English: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
Masaai: Entadamu intae ilo oting'iria enkiba naba neijia oo laing'okok eiba kewan enye, pee minaururu intae nemidukenyanya ti atua iltauja linyi.

English: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.
Masaai: Ore te nkesha inyi iararere ing'ok neton eitu igilunorere o meibukori osarge.

English: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
Masaai: Anaa ketorikine intae ina naikokieki intae anaa nkera? “Enkerai ai, nimimenu earata nikiaar Olaitoriani, nimilepori ti nikiosh ninye!

English: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
Masaai: Amu olonyor eosh Olaitoriani, neitame enkerai ake pooki nang'amu ninye.”

English: If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
Masaai: Enkaraki naa ioshot e nkikoo pee ing'iriri. Eitaasa intae Enkai enaitaas inkera enyena anaa kaa kerai eetae nemeosh menye arere?

English: But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
Masaai: Te nemeoshi intae aarere, anaa enaitaasaki ilkulikae pooki, nitaa nkera naadumuni nimirara inot.

English: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
Masaai: Ore etii ena, nikiaata loo papa lang te nkop oosh aarere nikiyanyita ninche. Paa eimikiyanyit naa oleng ilo Papa loo nkiyang'eta pee kinchu?

English: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
Masaai: Amu etoosho ninche iyiook aarere te nkiti rishata anaa enayieu ninche, kake keosh ninye iyiook arere amu eisidai ina te iyiook pee kitum esinyatisho esupatisho enye.

English: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
Masaai: Ore te ina rishata eoshoto pooki narere oltung'ani imemelok; ore te siadi neiu ilng'anayio le seriani e supatisho te lelo ootarerioki te ina.

English: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina entarrapu nena aik naalepori naa entagolo nena kung inyi naashal,

English: And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.
Masaai: naa entobiraki inkejek inyi inkoitoi naaitoriori, paa ore ilo ng'ojine nemeburukusha kake pee etumi aaishiunye.

English: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
Masaai: Entonyok eng'oru osotua too ltung'ana pooki, o esinyatisho naa ore te nemeetae nemetumi hoo olodol Olaitoriani.

English: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;
Masaai: Entodol ake pee meetae hoo obo olau empiris e Enkai; inchere pee metumi “entonai e nduaran” nabulu neyau entorroni, neaku te ina ilkumok te ina eisarkionieki ilkumok;

English: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
Masaai: niminchosho etumi oltung'ani hoo obo ololoito aashu olemeserem Enkai anaa Esau, otimira enjung'ore e ikinet enye neinosie endaa e nabo kata.

English: For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
Masaai: Amu iyiololo aajo ore te siadi, pee eitoki aayieu nejung ina mayianata, netanyaki ninye, amu eitu etum erishata pee eirridu, hoo neing'orua too lkiyio.

English: For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
Masaai: Amu mme doi entoki naiseyieki ietuo enetii, enkima nayupuyup, o enaimin o entoki naitureisho, o lkutati,

English: And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:
Masaai: o ltoilo le ntarumpeta o ltoilo laa ore nkirorot enyena neitureita lelo apa ootoning'o metasaisho aajo pee meitokini aaigilie kulie kirorot.

English: (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:
Masaai: Amu meitieu apa ninche aating'iria enkitoria naishooki, “Te neiseyie ninye eng'ues ele doinyio, neari too soito.”

English: And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)
Masaai: Eituria ina naitoduaaki o metejo Musa, “Kaikirikira nanu te nkuretisho.”

English: But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,
Masaai: Kake Oldoinyo le Sion ietuo intae o enkanasa e Enkai naishu, Yerusalem e keper, o enetii ilmalaika lemeikenayu ooiturrurro eikodoki,

English: To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
Masaai: nietuo eumata oo lkikaunot ooigero te shumata, nietuo enetii olarishani laa ninye Enkai e pooki; o enetii inkiyang'eta oo ltung'ana sinyat ooitabayioki,

English: And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.
Masaai: o enetii Yesu, ilo Aitutumoni lo sotua ng'ejuk, o enetii ilo sarge oisuaayioki neiro te mpiris nalang eno sarge le Abel.

English: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:
Masaai: Entodol ake emiaany ele olimu kuna. Amu amaa te neitu eilanyisho lelo ootanyaita ninye te nkop, mikiaata sii iyiook enikilanyie ilo oirorie iyiook etii shumata.

English: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
Masaai: Eikirikirie oltoilo lenye enkop ina kata apa; kake eitayio taata enkisiligata ajo, “Eton aigil ena nabo neme enkop ake aikirikirie kake o shumata sii.”

English: And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
Masaai: Ore ena bae najo ‘aigil ena nabo,’ neitodolu inchere keiwuang'ieki ina apa naikirikirieki, neitodulu ena entoki naitobiraki, pee eing'uari ina nemeikirikirieki.

English: Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:
Masaai: Enkaraki ina emanoto iyiook enashe kitang'amutua enkitoria nemeidimi aaigusugusie, naa emaishoo Enkai eseremata nang'amaroyu, natii enkanyit o lturiaki;

English: For our God is a consuming fire.
Masaai: amu ore Enkai ang naa enkima namutisho.

English: Let brotherly love continue.
Masaai: Enchoo enyorrata oo lalashera ebikoo.

English: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
Masaai: Emintololoiki enkitoomono oo lomon amu te ina eitoomono apa kulikae ilmalaika meyiolo.

English: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
Masaai: Entadamu lelo ootii korokoroni, anaa eitii korokoroni te nebo ninche, o lelo ooinyali, amu itii sii intae atua ilo sesen.

English: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
Masaai: Enchoo eyanyiti enkiyama ti atua iltung'ana pooki naa emincho ina rruat e nkiyama eisarkionieki; amu Enkai naiguanare lelo ooibor onyek o loololoito.

English: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
Masaai: Torripo enkishui ino ti alo enyorrata oo mpesai aa nchoo kibaiki entoki niaata; amu etejo ninye, “Maapal maadamu nemaaing'uaa.”

English: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
Masaai: Neaku eikintieu aatejo, “Olaitoriani olaretoni lai, maureishoyu, kaa aaidim oltung'ani aitaasa?”

English: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.
Masaai: Entadamu ilaiturukok linyi, lelo ooinosakita intae ele rorei le Enkai, entoduaai enkiting'oto e mpuaan enye, naa enturubare enkirukoto enye,

English: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
Masaai: ore Yesu Kristo ninye ake olang'ole taata o ntarasi.

English: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.
Masaai: Emincho eitapong'ori intae too nkiteng'enat naapaashaa; amu keishiaakino naa empiris naitagol oltau, neme indaiki, neitu eret lelo ooitudupita.

English: We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.
Masaai: Eikiaata iyiook olperere lo lasar lemeng'arie iyiook lelo ooisiaaisho teilo ng'obor.

English: For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.
Masaai: Amu ore nkiri e nena kishu naayau olapolosani ine wueji sinyati aitaa olasar loo ng'ok naa ti auluo enkang oo lng'oborri epejori.

English: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
Masaai: Neaku ore sii ninye Yesu naa ti auluo kishomi einosieki osina pee etum aitisinya iltung'ana lenyena to sarge lenye makewan.

English: Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
Masaai: Ore enkaraki ina emainyeito aapuo auluo enkang oo lng'oborri, nikinapaki nena morot.

English: For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.
Masaai: Amu mikiaata iyiook enkanasa nikibikie te ne, kake ae anasa king'oru nalotu.

English: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.
Masaai: Ti atua ninye naa maitaiki Enkai anaa ake olasar le nkisisa, aa inchere, ilng'anayio loo nkutukie naalimu enkarna enye.

English: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
Masaai: Emintololoiki easata oo supati, o eng'arata oo ntokitin niaatata, amu ore ilasarri laaijo lelo naa keitiship Enkai.

English: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.
Masaai: Entoning ilarikok linyi niyanyititi, amu iltauja linyi eirrita, anaa iltung'ana ooyookini aikilikuan, enchoo naa eiko ninche neijia te ng'ida, neme to sina, amu meeta ina dupoto te intae.

English: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.
Masaai: Entoomonoki iyiook, amu king'idare ena nchere mikiaata ileeni ti atua iltauja lang, eikiyieu nikiaasisho to rrekie sidai too mbaa pooki.

English: But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
Masaai: Atukunyaki intae naleng enkuna neijia pee aasiokini aarrinyoki intae.

English: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
Masaai: Ore naa taata Enkai e seriani nanyaaka ashuku Olaitoriani Yesu aitung'uaa ilootuata, ilo shekut kitok loo nkerra, te ilo sarge lo sotua loo ntarasi,

English: Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Masaai: meishopoki intae pooki toki sidai pee itumutumu aataas ina nayieu ninye, neas ina naitiship ninye ti atua intae; ti atua Yesu Kristo, olaa enenye enkitoo ntarasi o ntarasi. Esai.

English: And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words.
Masaai: Asai intae ilalashera, emisi tele rorei lai le nkikoo, amu too ndorropu atisiraka intae.

English: Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.
Masaai: Entayiolo inchere etalakuaki olalashe lang Timoteo, naa kayooki adol intae te nebo ninye te netasiekuo.

English: Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.
Masaai: Eroroki ilarikok linyi pooki o lelo sinyat pooki. Eiroroki intae ilooing'uaa Italia.

English: Grace be with you all. Amen.
Masaai: Metaa empiris te nebo intae pooki. Esai.

English: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
Masaai: Yakobo, osinka le Enkai o lo Laitoriani Yesu Kristo, Enkirorokino, too loshon tomon o aare ooisardakino inkuapi pooki.

English: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
Masaai: Ilalashera laainei, enkenai inchere eng'ida, te nitumutumu intemat oo mpukunot kumok,

English: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
Masaai: amu iyiololo nchere ore entemata natemi enkirukoto inyi eyau eng'iriata.

English: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
Masaai: Ning'iriri metabaiki enkiting'oto pee iakuku ilooiputakinote nelulung'a neitu eng'oriki toki.

English: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
Masaai: Naa te netii olinyi otong'orikia eng'eno, inchoo ninye metoomonu te Enkai naisho iltung'ana pooki te leng'on metii enkisikong'akinoto naa keishori sii ninye.

English: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
Masaai: Kake inchoo ninye eikilikuanu te nkirukoto meeta olng'ash katukul; amu ore oltung'ani oing'ash netiu anaa ilopir le naiposha ooreu osiwuo nekutaa.

English: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.
Masaai: Mincho oltung'ani laaijo ilo edamu ajo ketum toki to Laitoriani,

English: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Masaai: oltung'ani oata mbaa are to ltau lemeuno too rrekiei lenyena pooki.

English: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:
Masaai: Inchoo olalashe oshal metishipayu te nkaraki nailepieki ninye,

English: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.
Masaai: ore olalashe karsis inchoo sii ninye metishipayu te nkaraki neitadowuoki, amu etiu anaa intapuka e ntim kelusoo.

English: For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.
Masaai: Amu eilepu enkolong eirowua, nepej intapuka nemugut, nedoiyio, nerruoyo empukunoto e sidano enye. Neijia ake etiu oltung'ani karsis, kerruoyo eitoritote mbaa enyena pooki.

English: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
Masaai: Emayiana oltung'ani ong'iri too ntemat, amu ore pee eidip ating'iria entemata neng'amu ninye enkopiyia e nkitoo e nkishui naisiligie Enkai, lelo oonyor Ninye.

English: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
Masaai: Emincho ake oltung'ani te netemi, ejo, “Enkai naatetema;” amu metem Enkai too ntorrok, nemetem sii ninye Enkai oltung'ani.

English: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.
Masaai: Kake etemi pooki tung'ani, te nkaraki eng'uarrata enye torrono; neyiataa aitalamaa neitasur.

English: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
Masaai: Ore pee eidip ina ng'uarrata anoto intona neiu ing'ok. Ore pee ebaya ng'ok, neiu enkeeya.

English: Do not err, my beloved brethren.
Masaai: Ilalashera laainei lanyor, eminchosho eleji intae.

English: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
Masaai: Ore entoki pooki sidai o enkishoroto pooki nemeeta entiyoto edou eing'uaa shumata enetii Papa loo wang'aritin, nemeibelekenya Ninye, aashu etii enetii Ninye oloip le nkibelekenyata.

English: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
Masaai: Te nkaraki eyieunoto enye, etoiwuo Ninye iyiook to rorei loo sipat, pee eaku iyiook ilng'anayio le dukuya loo nkitobirat enyena.

English: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
Masaai: Entayiolo ena lalashera laainei lanyor. Inchoo pooki tung'ani metaa olosioki aning, nemesioki airo, nemesioki sii agoro.

English: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
Masaai: Amu ore engoro o ltung'ani nemeas isipat e Enkai.

English: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
Masaai: Entalama ate olduruk pooki o enkumoi oo ntorrok, ning'amaa te mborron Ororei otuunokoki atua intae oidim aitajeu iltauja linyi.

English: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Masaai: Kake entaa ilaasak lo rorei, mme laning'ok ake ilejileje ate.

English: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
Masaai: Amu te neaku ake oltung'ani olaning'oni lo rorei, mme olaasani, netiu ninye anaa oltung'ani oing'or enkomom enye te nking'uret.

English: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.
Masaai: Amu eing'or ninye enkomom enye, ore pee elo, nerikino nabo kata enaikununo.

English: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
Masaai: Kake ore olojur asipu inkitanapat bayarot, inkitanapat e lakunoto, nesheikino, nemetiu anaa elde ake oning nerikino, kake olaasani ooata nkiaasin, ore ilo nemaiyiani ti atua iyasat enyena.

English: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.
Masaai: Te nedamu oltung'ani ajo olaseremani le Enkai, nemeitore olng'ejep lenye, kewan elej ore eseremare enye naa pesho.

English: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
Masaai: Ore eseremare sidai nemeeta entiyoto te nkomom e Enkai, Papa, naa ena: embaikinoto oo ltung'ana okishin o nkolia, ti atua isinaitin lenye nerrip kewan pee metum entibili te nkop.

English: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
Masaai: Ilalashera laainei, emiaaku iloota olkep imbung'itata enkirukoto o Laitoriani lang Yesu Kristo, Olaitoriani le nkisisa.

English: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;
Masaai: Amu te nelotu naaji oltung'ani oata ilgiso le sahabu, neishopito inkilani sidain atua enkaji inyi e ntumo, nelotu sii ninye ine oltung'ani aisinani oishopito siapird.

English: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:
Masaai: Ning'oring'oro intae elde oishopito inkilani sidain, nishilaa aajoki, “Totona te ne,” nijokiki elde aisinani, “intasho te nde,” aashu, “Isukudoyu te mbata oo nkejek aainei.”

English: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?
Masaai: Aimidol ajo itipikate olgelati maate, niaakuku ilooiguenare too ndamunot torrok?

English: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
Masaai: Entoning, ilalashera laainei lanyor. Keitu egelu Enkai laisinak te nkop metaa karsisi te nkirukoto o lajung'ok le nkitoria naisiligieki lelo oonyor ninye?

English: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?
Masaai: Kake eitu iyanyititi intae ilo tung'ani aisinani. Aime ilkarsisi doi ooibooki intae enkop?

English: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
Masaai: Aime ninche doi ooiyietaki entai inkajijik e nkiguana? Aime ninche doi oomor ina arna sidai nayanyiti?

English: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:
Masaai: Te nintabayaya inkitanapat o Laitoriani anaa enajo isirat, “Tonyorra olelatia ino anaa kewan,” itaasa esupat.

English: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.
Masaai: Kake te nintodolulu olkep, nitaasa eng'oki, neiguanare intae inkitanapat inchere irara ilagilak loo nkitanapat.

English: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
Masaai: Amu ore pooki ng'ae oibung inkitanapat pooki neitapong te nabo, netaa eitarruoyie te pooki.

English: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
Masaai: Amu ore olotejo, “Miloloito,” netejo sii, “Miaar metua.” Metaa te neitu iloloito, kake itaara metua, itaa naa olagilani loo nkitanapat.

English: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
Masaai: Eroro, niaasishosho, anaa iloopuoi aaiguanare too nkitanapat e lakunoto.

English: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
Masaai: Amu meeta enkiguana olng'ur, te ilo leitu eitodolu olng'ur, kake emir olng'ur enkiguana.

English: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?
Masaai: Kaa dupoto, ilalashera laainei, eeta, te nejo oltung'ani keeta enkirukoto nemeeta siaaitin? Keidim enkirukoto enye aitajeu?

English: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,
Masaai: Amaa te nemeishopo anaa te nemeeta endaa olalashe anaa enkanashe,

English: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
Masaai: nejoki obo linyi ninche. “Enchom te seriani, erowuaja, niraposhosho,” neitu eisho ninche nkolati o sesen, kaa dupoto eata?

English: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
Masaai: Neijia etiu enkirukoto openy, te nemeeta siaitin, ketua.

English: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
Masaai: Kake eidim oltung'ani oje atejo, “Iata iyie enkirukoto naata nanu siaitin.” Intoduaaki naa enkirukoto ino aa ninye ake, metii isiaitin inono, ore naa too siaitin aainei naaitodol enkirukoto ai.

English: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.
Masaai: Iruk iyie ajo nabo Enkai, itaasa esidai. Eiruk sii ninche iloirriruani neikirikira.

English: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
Masaai: Iyieu iyie nikintodoli lo tung'ani omoda inchere ore enkirukoto nemeeta siaitin naa koolupi?

English: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Masaai: Amaa papa lang Abraham keitu eikenakini sipat te nkaraki siaitin, pee eitayu oinoti lenye Isaak to olperere lo lasar?

English: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
Masaai: Aimidol ajo ore enkirukoto o nkiaasin enyena easisho te nebo? Neitabayioki enkirukoto enye too nkiaasin.

English: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.
Masaai: Pee ebaya osirata ojo, “Eiruko Abraham Enkai, ore te nkaraki enkirukoto neikenaki Enkai ninye esupatisho,” neipoti aajo olchore le Enkai.

English: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
Masaai: Idol taa ajo eikenakini oltung'ani sipat too siaitin mme to lbae le nkirukoto ake.

English: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
Masaai: Aime te ina oitoi ake sii oo nkiaasin eikenakaki Rahabu ina naibor onyek isipat pee eng'amu lelo aikitalak, neipung'ie ti ae oitoi?

English: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
Masaai: Ore anaa enatua osesen te nemetii enkiyang'et neijia etiu enkirukoto nemetii siaitin etua.

English: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
Masaai: Emincho ilkumok te intae ilalashera laainei eaku ilaiteng'enak, amu iyiololo aajo ore iyiook pooki ooiteng'enisho naa keiguanareki enagol te nikintadiak.

English: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.
Masaai: Amu ore iyiook pooki nikintadiak too nkumok naa te netii obo lemeitadiak too naajo, oltung'ani aa o lemeeta entiyoto ilo, oidim sii aitoria osesen lenye pooki.

English: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
Masaai: Ing'ura ti nikipik mbartan isenkenke inkutukie naarewueki, nening iyiook, nikindim aaboin iseseni lenye pooki anaa enikiyieu.

English: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
Masaai: Eng'urai sii imelin, hoo naa sapuki oleng, nerrumoo olkutati ogol oleng, eutaa ninche enkiti toki aipirie enkalo ake ninye naba anaa enayieu olarewani.

English: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
Masaai: Neijia etiu olng'ejep enkiti rubata to sesen, kake ejo sapuki oleng. Tadamu eneba esapuko e ntim, naidim oloti tiili atapejo?

English: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.
Masaai: Ore olng'ejep enkima, enkop nebore intorrok ti atua irubat ang, nepik osesen pooki intibil, neinuaaki enkima enkishui o sesen olulung'a te nkima naing'uaa Yehanum.

English: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:
Masaai: Amu eidim iltung'ana aaidondorra neidipa aidondorra pooki pukunoto oo ng'uesi o motonyi o noo ng'uesi naaiserpepiari oo noo ng'uesi e naiposha,

English: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
Masaai: kake metii oltung'ani oidim aidondorra olng'ejep, entorroni nemeitirring'a, ebore esayiet nayaisho.

English: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.
Masaai: Te ilo ng'ejep kimayian Olaitoriani o Papa, naa ninye kidekie iltung'ana, lelo ooitobiraki te nkitanyaanyukoto e Enkai.

English: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.
Masaai: Ina kutuk ake eimu emayian o ldeket. Ilalashera laainei, aime neijia duoo eishiaakino netiu.

English: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?
Masaai: Keimu enkong'u nabo e nchorro enkare namelok o e naisukut?

English: Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.
Masaai: Amaa ilalashera laainei, keidim olng'aboli atoiu ilosiyio anaa sabibu ilng'abolo? Meidim sii ninye enchorro naisukut aishoru enkare namelok.

English: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.
Masaai: Kaing'ae te intae olng'en neeta endamunoto? Nchoo eitoduaaya te nkishon enye sidai o to lkuaak lenye inkiaasin enyena te mborron e ng'eno.

English: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.
Masaai: Kake ti niatata olom odua o enyorrata e ate ti atua iltauja linyi, eminya kutukie nimilejishosho aaibooyo esipata.

English: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.
Masaai: Ore ena ng'eno eitu edou eing'uaa shumata, kake ene nkop, o enoo ltung'ana, o enoo loiriruani.

English: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
Masaai: Amu ore enetii olom o enyorrata e kewan, netii olong'oling'oli o empukunoto pooki suuji.

English: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
Masaai: Kake ore eng'eno nagut naing'uaa shumata nesila neeta eseriani, nebor, netemaa mbaa, nebore olng'ur, neiu ilng'anayio sidain, nemeeta olng'ash anaa esunkureisho.

English: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.
